500003|2026-03.headline: Aegis Logistics FY26 PAT rose 41% to INR1,107 crore and Q4 PAT rose 43% to INR455 crore, led by LPG distribution margins of about INR7,000 per ton.
500003|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 23% to INR8,333 crore, normalized EBITDA rose 36% to INR1,599 crore, and PAT crossed INR1,000 crore for the first time. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 52% to INR2,594 crore and normalized EBITDA up 54% to INR670 crore. The LPG segment drove the result, with distribution volumes up 45% in FY26 and 71% in Q4, while the Liquid segment was flat on revenue and EBITDA fell 5% for the year. Management outlined a large capex pipeline (about $1.2 billion to March 2027, about INR5,000 crore in FY28, about $5 billion through 2030/31) and said it expects to maintain FY27 momentum.

segments.name: LPG
segments.commentary: FY26 terminal throughput reached 5.15 million tons (+14%), distribution volumes 7.54 lakh MT (+45%) and sourcing sales 6.07 lakh MT (+2%). Q4 LPG revenue INR2,410 crore (+65%) and EBITDA INR549 crore (+136%), with Q4 distribution volume at a record 2.34 lakh MT (+71%).

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR644 crore and EBITDA INR472 crore (-5%), reflecting phasing of capacity additions and no major take-or-pay contribution versus last year. Q4 revenue INR184 crore and EBITDA INR126 crore.

guidance_outlook: Distribution margin guided at about INR7,000 per ton, which management expects to sustain through FY27 and beyond; FY26 average was about INR7,000 versus about INR4,000 in FY25.

Cumulative capex of about $1.2 billion by March 2027; about INR5,000 crore capex in FY28; about $5 billion pipeline through 2030/31 (management clarified the target is December 2030 and that heavy spending falls in FY29-FY31).
Long-term EPS CAGR guidance of about 25% reiterated; management said it is conservative and that it has beaten its own guidance.
Target of about 2 million tons of gas distribution (LPG plus ammonia) by FY28.

Ammonia: expected utilization about 25% in year one, then growing 30-40% a year; ammonia throughput margin INR2,500-3,000 per ton; distribution about 200,000 tons initially, growing 20-30% a year, margin up to INR5,000 per ton.
LPG supply shortfall improved from about 50% in April to about 30% in May; management expects normalcy around Q2 FY27 but declined to forecast precisely.
risks_watch: Distribution margin sustainability: the INR7,000 per ton level is tied to elevated energy prices and the war; management says it expects scale-driven procurement gains from FY28 but offered no quantified path.
LPG supply normalization: shortfall still about 30% in May; management expects normalcy around Q2 FY27 with no firm date.
Execution timing: JNPT, Mumbai, Kandla CRL 4, Pipavav jetty and ammonia terminal, and Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline are all targeted for H1 FY27 or year-end FY27; slippage would delay volumes.
Capex step-up from about INR800 crore in FY26 to about $1.2 billion by March 2027 and about $5 billion by 2030; funding mix and gearing (about 0.6x) to watch.
Vadhavan port (about INR20,000 crore) remains a nonbinding MoU subject to approvals and land allocation; its inclusion in the capex pipeline is uncertain.
Ammonia economics are new and unproven for the company; utilization and margin targets are management estimates.
500003|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on growth and the energy-transition opportunity, but conservative on numbers: management declined to raise the 25% EPS CAGR guidance and said it prefers to under-promise. Evasive on exact timing of LPG normalization and on precise FY28-30 ammonia volumes.
key_quotes: We are a very conservative company and I think 25% CAGR growth is not small.
Going forward, we feel the INR7,000-odd margins should be sustainable as beyond '26, '27, we would see our distribution volumes really of a scale that brings procurement efficiencies.
So, we are very bullish. We have a partner, Itochu, along with us.
our sort of philosophy here at Aegis is really to not to overpromise, always to under promise, and hopefully overdeliver.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Q4 jump in gas segment profitability per ton, was there a one-off, and what is the normalized level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin averaged about INR7,000/MT vs INR4,000 in the prior year, with volume surge also contributing; it expects INR7,000-odd to be sustainable as scale brings procurement efficiencies, and full-year effects of Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic terminals will add to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: When will LPG supply fully normalize, and what is the FY27 and FY28 capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: LPG shortfall fell from about 50% in April to about 30% in May; normalcy is expected sometime in Q2. Capex is about $1.2 billion by March 2027 and about INR5,000 crore in FY28, both organic and inorganic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vadhavan MoU included in the capex pipeline, and what is the exact capex split of FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Vadhavan could be included in the $5 billion pipeline depending on land allotment and permits, but not all of it. The $5 billion is through December 2030 (not FY30), with heavy spend in FY29-FY31.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ammonia economics for utilization and margins, and does ammonia distribution reach INR5,000/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilization is expected at about 25% in year one, then growing 30-40% a year; throughput margin INR2,500-3,000/MT; distribution starts at about 200,000 tons, growing 20-30% a year, with margin up to INR5,000/MT depending on the market.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from volumes versus price, and how will revenue trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of the rise from about INR4,000 to INR7,000 comes from volume-led procurement efficiencies (volumes went from about 5.2 lakh to 7.5 lakh MT) and part from margin improvement; it expects revenue to grow year on year as volume offsets price normalization.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the 25% EPS CAGR guidance, and what are the FY30 ammonia and LPG volume targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is conservative, has beaten its own guidance, and achieved 32% EPS CAGR over five years; EPS has moved from INR6 to INR26 with the CAGR guidance unchanged. It declined to give a precise FY30 ammonia volume, citing dependence on terminals commissioned and locations secured, but pointed to a 3 million ton ammonia supply-demand gap by 2029 per CRISIL.

500003|2026-06.headline: Aegis Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 212% YoY to INR545 crore and normalized EBITDA 184% to INR727 crore, driven by a record LPG distribution quarter.
500003|2026-06.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 results, with PAT of INR545 crore (up 212% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR727 crore (up 184%). The Gas division posted its highest-ever EBITDA of INR591 crore (up 296% YoY), with distribution volumes of 2.77 lakh MT (up 91% YoY, up 19% QoQ). Liquids EBITDA rose 28% to INR136 crore on INR178 crore revenue. Management announced several port and capacity milestones, including commissioning of a 36,000 MT ammonia terminal at Pipavav and a Board-approved 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Logistics
segments.commentary: Throughput held steady at 1.124 million MT. Sourcing volumes rose marginally 1% YoY to 1.21 lakh MT.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Distribution
segments.commentary: Record 2.77 lakh MT volume. Management cites a distribution margin of INR7,000+ per MT as sustainable, versus INR4,000 historically.

segments.name: Liquids
segments.commentary: Highest-ever Q1 EBITDA of INR136 crore, with five consecutive quarters of EBITDA growth. Mangalore liquid capacity of 193,000 CBM is fully utilized after a 75,000 CBM addition.

guidance_outlook: Cumulative capex of about $1.2 billion targeted in FY27.
Capex pipeline of about $5 billion through FY2030-31; funding via equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting gearing of about 0.6.
Distribution volume: management aims for 2 million MT, now expected to cross 1 million MT this year and possibly 1.5 million MT next year; growth rate closer to 50% per management.
Logistics throughput: worst-case growth of about 25% a year, with step-up growth possible as Pipavav and KGPL enablers are used.
Mumbai 64,000 CBM liquid storage (INR125 crore) targeted for commissioning in H1 FY27.
JNPA first phase of about 100,000 CBM liquid storage targeted for Q3 FY27; Kochi additional 49,577 CBM expected early next fiscal year; Kandla CRL 4 (94,148 CBM) targeted next year.

JNPA: 101,900 CBM liquid today; about 318,100 CBM liquid, 77,236 MT LPG and a 35,000 MT bottling plant under a roughly INR1,675 crore program. Board also approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank.

Pipavav: LPG capacity now 70,800 MT after a 48,000 MT terminal commissioned June 2025; 36,000 MT ammonia terminal commissioned; VLGC-compliant jetty due this year; liquid rail gantry with 0.5 million MT/yr take-or-pay due by year-end; Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline connection expected in H1 FY27. Jamnagar-Loni LPG pipeline complete.
Kandla: 952,000 CBM liquid and 48,000 MT LPG; VLGC-compliant; CRL 4 expansion targeted next year.
Kochi: 82,545 CBM liquid today, rising to 132,122 CBM after a 49,577 CBM addition.
Mangalore: 82,000 MT LPG terminal commissioned June 2025; LPG rail gantry and bottling plant at INR52.5 crore; liquid capacity 193,000 CBM; evaluating 60,000 CBM more.
Haldia: about 25,000 MT LPG terminal under HPCL terminaling agreement to 2038; 226,890 CBM liquid storage; 3 acres of land acquired for expansion.
Vadhavan port: non-binding MoU for a potential INR20,000 crore investment, subject to approvals.
demand_pricing: Management says distribution volume growth reflects new customers, wider geography and ullage added from Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic terminals, not only the war.

Blended distribution margin was about INR7,000/MT in FY26 and Q1 FY27. Management says the margin should be INR7,000+ going forward, supported by shipping savings from VLGC carriers (freight of about $15 vs $50 on MGCs).
Management states margins were not INR5,000 in Q4 or Q1 and said blended FY margin matters more than quarterly figures.
Ammonia: distribution to industrial customers starts within weeks of commissioning; no cylinders or gas stations. Margins not disclosed.
Management says it is a distributor, not a trader, and does not take inventory or price positions.
Morbi demand has partly restarted; management says Morbi is no longer the core of the business.
Logistics tariffs are uniform across ports; no port-wise split given.

qa_highlights.question: Is distribution volume growth ahead of expectations, and are the customer contracts sticky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2 million MT aim predates the war and reflects infrastructure build-out; new cryogenic terminals at Pipavav and Mangalore have added ullage and geography.

qa_highlights.question: How should EBITDA per ton be viewed near term and structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR7,000+ per MT is sustainable. It expects the margin not to fall back to INR4,000, citing procurement gains from VLGC shipping as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the per-unit margins for sourcing, logistics and distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquids EBITDA is divided by capacity (about 2 million CBM). Logistics throughput gives close to INR1,000/MT EBITDA. Sourcing is a low contributor, at about $85-90/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth outlook beyond 25% CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: 25% is the benchmark for logistics; anything above depends on the enablers. Distribution growth is expected to be higher, closer to 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not fill more storage given the ITOCHU partnership and the LPG supply deficit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not take inventory or price positions and will distribute on a monthly basis, rather than act as a trader.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash across subsidiaries fund the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: AVTL is self-funded through equity, and ITOCHU is planned to rise to 25% over three years. Standalone cash is around INR2,700 crore, and consolidated liquidity exceeds INR5,940 crore. Management will hold cash until it finds opportunities.

risks_watch: Distribution margin sustainability: management guides INR7,000+/MT for FY27-28 on VLGC freight savings, but Q1 and Q4 margins were not INR5,000 and no quarterly margin disclosure is given; track blended FY27 margin.

Execution timelines: Mumbai 64,000 CBM (H1 FY27), JNPA first ~100,000 CBM phase (Q3 FY27), Pipavav jetty and rail gantry (year-end), Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection (H1 FY27), Kandla CRL 4 (next year), Kochi 49,577 CBM (early next FY).

Geopolitical dependence: management links distribution volume and margin gains partly to Middle East war disruption and says normalization would change the mix; the 2 million MT aim now looks like 1 million MT this year and 1.5 million MT next year.

Capital deployment: roughly $1.2 billion capex in FY27 and a $5 billion pipeline through FY2030-31, funded by equity, accruals and debt at about 0.6 gearing; cash is spread across subsidiaries and AVTL depends on ITOCHU equity rising to 25% over three years.
Ammonia: Pipavav 36,000 MT terminal commissioned with a 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc; ammonia distribution margins not disclosed and management asked to wait a quarter.
key_quotes: We believe the margin of INR7,000 looks sustainable.
We expect this INR7,000 not to come down to INR4,000 again when everything is normalized, say, in '27, '28 onwards.
We are distributors. We get material where we see demand and then we distribute it or reach out to those customers.
We believe that year-on-year, we would always clock a worst-case scenario growth in the logistics volume of around 25%.

500008|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 15-16% to INR3,530 crore, with lead-acid margin near 12% despite raw-material inflation.
500008|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR3,530 crore, up close to 15% YoY, with about 92% from Lead Acid Batteries and about INR280 crore from New Energy. Lead-acid revenue grew about 12% and 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler OEM volumes grew more than 30%, while aftermarket grew 5-6%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 11%, and lead-acid operating margin was about 11.6% after adjusting for lithium pack trading, with management citing raw-material and alloy cost spikes linked to the geopolitical conflict. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR13,814 crore (up about 7.5%) with a 10.8% consolidated margin; the company guided FY27 capex of INR1,500-1,700 crore, mostly in New Energy.

financial_highlights.change: up close to 15% YoY (16% per management later)

financial_highlights.metric: Lead Acid Battery revenue growth Q4 FY26
Lead Acid operating margin Q4 FY26 (ex lithium trading)

segments.name: Lead Acid Battery (Automotive and Industrial)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 12% YoY in Q4; 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler OEM volumes up more than 30%, aftermarket up 5-6%, other industrial segments up 3-4%, telecom lead-acid declining as it shifts to lithium. Price hikes of 5-6% taken in domestic automotive in Q4 in tranches.

segments.name: Tubular batteries and Home UPS
segments.commentary: Tubular battery volumes grew more than 35% in Q4; in-house share is 70-75% with 20-25% now traded from other manufacturers. Home energy demand described as sustained.

segments.name: Lubes
segments.commentary: Lubes business has reached a run-rate of about INR50 crore revenue per quarter.

Management is still aiming for a 13-14% EBITDA margin on a standalone basis over time, despite lead prices around INR210,000-220,000 per tonne, but gave no timeline.
Another 2-3% price increase expected, with the company saying this may not fully recover cost pressure; no price hike taken yet in the current quarter.
FY27 capex planned at INR1,500-1,700 crore: about INR400 crore for Lead Acid and INR1,100-1,200 crore for New Energy.
BESS integration facility at Divitipally targeted to start production at end of calendar 2026 with 5 GWh initial capacity, expandable to 10 GWh; BESS operating margin initially 6-7%.
Giga 1 (2 GWh cell line, 2170 cylindrical) expected to start production in June 2027; LFP products expected 2028 or later; 16 GWh Divitipally target unchanged.

CQP in final commissioning; commercial samples expected to customers in the next couple of months; full-scale operations expected in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is equipment for the 2 GWh cell line ordered, and what are the commissioning constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment has been ordered; the constraint is limited visas for Chinese engineers to commission it, with a few visas issued and engineers on ground at CQP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Gotion partnership and LFP plant timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology licensing from China is being discouraged by Beijing; management says product development is now largely India-driven. The Gotion tie-up was corporate-to-corporate with no government approval sought. First capacity next year will be NMC; LFP is 2028 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS margins once stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial operating margin about 6-7%, with upside as scale improves; the BESS plant is seen as a strategic lever for ESS cell manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 outlook for replacement and industrial segments, and Q4 growth by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM 2W and 4W grew more than 30%, aftermarket 5-6%, other industrial 3-4%, telecom declining; FY27 growth guided at mid to high single digit.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material inflation and price hikes should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead and alloys about 70% of RM; plastics about 10% with possible 40% increase; another 2-3% price increase likely, possibly insufficient to offset full cost pressure.

500031|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Electricals Q4 FY26 was modest: Lighting Solutions EBIT margin 8.7% in Q4 and record 8.5% for the year, while Consumer Products posted a loss on deleverage.
500031|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a modest quarter, hit by a delayed summer, geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruption and input cost inflation. Lighting Solutions grew 16% in Q4 with an 8.7% EBIT margin, and annual turnover rose 9.5% with EBIT up 28% and a record 8.5% annual margin. Consumer Products bore the brunt: fans and coolers declined, kitchen appliances grew about 30%, and the vertical reported a loss from operating deleverage. The company entered wires in February 2026, ended FY26 with INR 934 crore of cash, and kept negative working capital, with about INR 400 crore of operating cash flow in the quarter. A final dividend of INR 3 per share (150% of face value) was recommended.

500031|2026-06.headline: Bajaj Electricals Q1 FY27: revenue up 2.3% YoY while EBIT margin rose to 6.6% from 2.5%, led by consumer products margin recovery to 3.9%.
500031|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 2.3% YoY in Q1 FY27, with consumer products up 1.7% (after multiple quarters of decline) and lighting solutions up 4.4%. Consolidated EBIT margin expanded to 6.6% from 2.5%, with consumer products EBIT margin at 3.9% versus negative 1.7% a year earlier, driven by gross margin gains and operating leverage. Fans remained the weak spot, with management attributing share loss to operational issues including gas and PCB shortages. Management guided to 8-10% growth on a blended basis (described as a non-binding aspiration) and a 6-7% margin stabilisation for the next two years before a move toward 10% in consumer products. Cash flow from operations was negative in the quarter, mainly due to tax payments linked to the Morphy Richards acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Market share trend and rural performance?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and operating cash flow?

qa_highlights.question: Cost inflation and pricing outlook?

500034|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Finance Q4 FY26: AUM crossed INR 5 lakh crore (up 22.4% YoY), PAT up 26.7%, and FY27 credit cost guided lower at 1.45%-1.60%.
500034|2026-03.overview: Management reported a strong Q4 FY26 on core metrics: AUM reached about INR 510,000 crore (up 22.4% YoY), PAT grew 26.7% and PBT 26%, before one-time items. A revised presentation moved recoveries on written-off loans into loan losses, lowering loan loss to average AR to 1.65% from 1.75% and raising opex to NTI to 33.8% from 33.2%, with no PBT or PAT impact. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 20-24%, 15-17 million new customers, opex to NTI down 25-40 bps, ROA of 4.4-4.6% and ROE of 19-20%. The call was heavily framed around geopolitical contingency, AI transformation and a "cruise mode" posture after an aggressive post-COVID period.

Management said guidance excludes any adverse geopolitical impact, with some conservatism built in; CFO noted that the old 165-175 bps range converts to 145-170 bps on the new presentation.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no NIM expansion is needed; ROA of 4.6% in FY26 core is the base, supported by 22-24% growth, opex to NTI improvement and lower loan loss to AR. Management cites 4 levers: growth, margin, opex and credit costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PCR so high and will it unwind next year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ECL is now a quarterly bottom-up exercise, PCR should stay in the current corridor, and management intends to keep building provisions for balance-sheet resilience.

qa_highlights.question: Will profit growth reach 35-40% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said profit growth may be faster than balance sheet growth but did not validate a 35% figure; management described tailwinds from credit cost and cost efficiency, subject to geopolitical stability.

qa_highlights.question: How does 20-24% AUM growth compare with the long-term 20%+ target?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the long-term commitment is 20%-plus per year. Management aims to grow at about 2x system credit growth, targeting a top 5-6 lender position within 5-7 years.

500038|2026-03.headline: Balrampur Chini raises PLA project cost by INR230 crore to INR3,080 crore and approves INR450 crore preferential equity plus INR200 crore debentures.

500042|2026-03.headline: BASF India FY26 PBT before exceptionals rose to Rs 564 crore from Rs 600 crore equivalent comparison; Q4 PBT Rs 90 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.
500042|2026-03.overview: Management presented FY26 (year to 31 March 2026) consolidated results, including the coatings business and discontinued operations, with sales around Rs 3,900-4,000 crore per quarter and volumes up 6-7% for the year but prices down 5-6%. Q4 showed volume-led growth (about 12-15% volume growth YoY, sales up about 10%) and PBT before exceptionals of Rs 90 crore against Rs 25 crore in March 2025. Working capital rose about Rs 600-800 crore, pushing FY26 operating cash flow to about minus Rs 110 crore versus Rs 370 crore last year. Management flagged the West Asia conflict, feedstock inflation, rupee depreciation and a possible demand softening in the coming months, and said no plants were shut down.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited erratic monsoons, soft commodity prices (chilli acreage and intensity down), and high channel inventories. It said the 12 launches in four years are about 25% of ag sales and carry higher margins, and that channel inventory is healthy. It gave no view on normalised margins.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material cost increases being passed on, and is demand responding?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through starts upstream and is uneven by segment; management has been successful in some cases. It expects a slight softening of demand as customers wait and see and pre-buying fades.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY21 is not comparable due to restructuring, including the sale of the construction chemicals business. 500043|2026-03.headline: Bata India posted a second straight quarter of 5%+ value growth in Q4 FY26; like-to-like PBT grew about 11% after excluding four non-cash items.
500043|2026-03.overview: Management reported a second consecutive quarter of accelerating, volume-backed growth of 5%+ in value, with broad-based growth across channels and categories. Reported PBT fell about 94% due to exceptional items, mainly a plant closure (VRS) cost and a INR220 million FX impact on a licensing liability. Excluding four non-cash items, like-to-like PBT grew about 11% and cash flow from operations grew about 18%. Inventory fell 13% YoY and 28% over two years while availability rose about 1,000 bps, and ZBM stores were scaled to about 700 by May 2026.

segments.name: Retail (COCO/ZBM)
segments.commentary: Volume-led DOS growth; ZBM stores at about 550 last quarter with about 50-55% of COCO sales, rising to about 700 stores (about 70% of sales) by end-May 2026. Target of 800-850 stores by quarter end.

segments.name: Franchise (FOFO)
segments.commentary: Franchise stores crossed 700 with double-digit growth and higher overall profitability; franchise share is close to double digit of revenue. Management targets nearing 1,000 stores in the next 12 months.

segments.name: Multi-brand distribution (MBO)
segments.commentary: Expanded to about 1,670 towns; channel is showing early signs of growth after pressure in towns below 1,000. Distribution is about 10-12% of revenue.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing channel across B2B, B2C and dot-com; about 8-10% of revenue per CFO, about 12-13% per CEO. Over 700 stores fulfil online orders.

segments.name: Brands: Hush Puppies and Power/HP premium
segments.commentary: Hush Puppies is about 18-20% of turnover and the fastest-growing brand. Premium HP and Power portfolio is outpacing overall growth.

segments.name: Under INR1,000 MRP segment
segments.commentary: About 35-40% of revenue; declined for about 3 years but has stabilised and is now growing roughly in line with the overall ~5% top line.

guidance_outlook: Inventory is about 70-75% of the way through the reduction programme, with a target turn of about 3 versus about 2.7 currently, without compromising availability.
Full-price sales are growing about 2x overall growth; management is 'reasonably hopeful' of gross margin improvement going forward.
Raw material inflation is about 5-6% blended as of the last review; price increases of 5-6% are planned but not yet rolled out.
Franchise store count to approach 1,000 within about 12 months; ZBM stores to reach about 800-850 by the current quarter end.
Management declined to give forward-looking guidance on bata.com or overall D2C growth for FY27.
capex_capacity: One manufacturing facility closed in the quarter, with a related VRS exceptional cost; management is removing legacy factories and consolidating to a few large suppliers.
Store network is about 2,000 EBOs (COCO plus franchise), with about 1,150 COCO stores.
Marketing spend is about 1.5x prior levels, with digital about 80-85% of the spend.
Sneakers proposition under development to target younger consumers; details to be shared later.
demand_pricing: March was better than January, and management sees no tangible change in consumer sentiment as of now, but will not give forward-looking statements.
Brand consideration rose to 66, its highest level; Ballerina campaign drew a strong response.
Full-price sales are growing faster, with markdowns lower; gross margin optics are diluted by franchise mix and a one-off INR60 million provision reversal in the base quarter.
Trade receivables rose about 65% YoY, attributed to channel mix (wholesale, franchise, B2B e-commerce) and base effect; management says provisions for doubtful debts show no deterioration.
Minimum wage hikes in Haryana, UP and Karnataka are seen as structural; the company is spread across 30 states and only 3-4 are affected so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory at a desirable level, and why is lower discounting not showing in gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Turns are about 2.7 against a target of about 3. Gross margin optics are diluted by the shift to franchise (lower GM%, accretive to EBIT) and a INR60 million provision reversal in base Q4 FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What raw material and minimum wage impact is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended raw material inflation is about 5-6% and is being covered by inventory, hedges and price elasticity-led pricing. Management sees no direct impact yet, and wage hikes are structural but partly offset because many stores already pay above minimum wage.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Bata brand's revenue growth been stagnant, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to inventory simplification, which had deteriorated and is now recovering, along with franchise expansion, SIS, digital, and product and marketing levers.

qa_highlights.question: How long will vendor and store revamps take to reach the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees underlying operating leverage coming through from store revamp, inventory decluttering and supplier consolidation, with benefits in coming periods.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise about 65% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Due to channel mix, with more credit in wholesale, franchise and B2B e-commerce, plus a base effect. Management says the quality is fine and doubtful-debt provisions are steady.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between below and above INR1,000 products, and what is Hush Puppies' contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Below INR1,000 is about 35-40% of revenue and has stabilised. Hush Puppies is about 18-20% of turnover. Management will provide the exact split offline, and it could not give FY25/FY26 volume growth on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: COCO is about 65% and non-COCO about 35%. Within non-COCO, franchise is close to double digit, e-commerce about 8-10% and distribution about 10-12%.

500043|2026-06.headline: Bata India Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 4% to INR979 crore, with underlying PBT up about 22% and gross margin up 130 bps.
500043|2026-06.overview: Bata reported Q1 FY27 turnover of INR979 crore, up about 4% YoY, with volume and price contributing roughly equally to growth. Underlying PBT grew about 22%, and the company crossed 2,000 EBO stores. Management flagged raw material cost push of 5-6% (mainly crude-linked synthetics), which it plans to offset through price increases that reach shelves from around September. Monsoon-related deferral of revenue in the prior quarter was expected to reverse in July and early August. The call was an Ambit-hosted post-earnings session, with management declining forward guidance.

segments.commentary: Ladies category was the lead driver within Bata brand, supported by the Taapsee Pannu campaign and the Everyday Essential range. Bata grew despite the adverse trend.

segments.name: Hush Puppies
segments.commentary: Led growth alongside Floatz, with strong sequential and YoY growth; no figure was disclosed.

segments.name: Floatz
segments.commentary: Continued strong sequential and YoY growth; no figure disclosed.

segments.name: Power / NorthStar (sneakers)
segments.commentary: Power grew well; NorthStar was a drag as lines are being rationalised ahead of a stronger collection over the next couple of quarters.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: Broad-based growth across ZBM stores (close to 800 stores, about 80% of business), franchise (about 750 stores), e-commerce and multi-brand outlets. Franchise and e-commerce carry lower gross margin but are EBIT-accretive.

Price-hiked stock expected to reach markets at scale around September 2026.
Product funnel reimagination expected to show more impact in H2 FY27 and H1 FY28; significant portfolio change by March 2027.
Gross margin levers cited: premiumisation and higher full-price sales; channel mix (franchise/e-commerce growth) a partial offset.

Vendor consolidation: from about 100-120 partners 2.5-3 years ago to below 70 (about 60) now; target of 15 core plus 15 satellite partners over 3-5 years, with total margin benefit about 200 bps over that period.
Elevated marketing spend expected to continue for the next couple of years; ZBM 2.0 (Project Elevate) results to be shared next quarter.
capex_capacity: Store network: about 2,000 EBO stores crossed, of which about 1,250 COCO/DOS (incl. about 125 Hush Puppies DOS) and about 750 franchise; management aspires to 3,000 stores over time.

Franchise partner ROI cited at 18-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin not expand more despite higher full-price sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix (franchise and e-commerce growing faster) diluted gross margin by about 100 bps. Without it, gross margin expansion would have been about 230 bps versus 130 bps reported; EBIT per pair is the benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores, and what is the ZBM contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1,250 COCO/DOS and about 750 franchise stores. About 775 ZBM stores generate about 80% of COCO retail revenue; management sees ZBM near saturation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost flat for five quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: VRS was part of the business case; a 24-month organisational restructuring, Blue Yonder merchandising platform and manpower reallocation drove savings. Store manpower broadly unchanged; franchise growth required added manpower.

qa_highlights.question: Franchise store economics and SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise like-for-like growth close to high single digits for about four quarters. Partner ROI about 18-24%. Revenue per sq ft not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: A&P trajectory and timing of revenue payback?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P at about 3-3.5% of sales vs about 2.5% a year ago; management said it will not move to 7-8%. Revenue payback expected 'as early as possible'.

500049|2026-03.headline: BEL FY26 revenue rose 16% to INR27,480 crore with EBITDA margin at 30%; FY27 guidance is revenue growth above 15% and EBITDA margin above 28%.
500049|2026-03.overview: BEL reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR27,480 crore (up 16%), PBT of INR8,075 crore (up 14%) and PAT of INR6,048 crore (up 14%), with EBITDA margin of 30% versus 29% in FY25. Order book stood at INR73,882 crore as on 1 April 2026, against FY26 order inflow of INR30,045 crore. Management said all FY26 guidance parameters were met. The call flagged QRSAM contract signing expected by June 2026 as the key near-term order event, with FY27 order inflow guided above INR55,000 crore.

segments.name: Defence electronics (about 90% of revenue, FY27 mix guidance)
segments.commentary: Management guides defence at 90% and non-defence at 10% of revenue for FY27, plus or minus 1%. Non-defence is currently 8-10% of turnover, targeted at 15-20% over time.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports are 4-5% of turnover, with a target of more than 10% over 4-5 years; near-term increase expected only 1-2%. Export order book is about USD96 million for this year and subsequent years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of more than 15%.
FY27 EBITDA margin of more than 28%.
FY27 order inflow expected above INR55,000 crore, including QRSAM.
FY27 R&D investment target of about INR2,200 crore.
FY27 capex target of more than INR1,200 crore, with 20%-plus growth; FY26 capex was about INR900 crore.
Defence to non-defence revenue mix of 90:10 (plus or minus 1%), with any change to be updated mid-year.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR900 crore; FY27 target is more than INR1,200 crore, with larger projects planned over three years at Palasamudram, Chitrakoot and Vellore, alongside Ghaziabad and Bangalore.
Management sees no capacity choking for the next 3-5 years, and continues adding capacity to avoid constraints over 10-15 years.

Computing infrastructure (CPU/GPU) already exists at CRL Ghaziabad, CRL Bangalore, the software SBU and PDIC; a separate high-performance computing facility is planned soon. Compute investment was INR100-plus crore over the last two years, with INR100-200 crore more in approval.
AMCA: BEL and L&T (consortium, L&T lead) expected to receive the RFP within about 15 to 45 days; investment will rise only after selection as successful bidder.
demand_pricing: QRSAM contract: management expects signing by end-June 2026, with a 5-10% chance of slipping to July and a worst case of one more month. First production model is due within 18 months of signing; margins are not yet quantified and are expected to be similar to existing business.

Submarine P-75I: BEL expects more than 50-60% of electronics content, with about six subsystems. Electronics are typically 25-30% of submarine value (plus or minus 5%). Execution is expected over about 5 years, aligned to MDL's schedule.

Order book breakdown: electronic fuses about INR4,300 crore (over 7 years), LRSAM about INR3,500 crore, LCA about INR3,200 crore, BMP-II upgrade about INR2,800 crore, Ashwini about INR2,460 crore, Mi-17 V5 EW about INR2,200 crore, spares and miscellaneous about INR2,500 crore.

Big-ticket pipeline for FY26-28 includes NGC corvette subsystems (about 50% expected this year), Shatrughat and Samghat EW, HAMMER, Shakti Phase IV and MFR-X naval radar. Management expects one or two items above INR20,000-25,000 crore in the next 2-3 years.
Data centre: current orders are a few hundred crore; an indigenous end-to-end solution with C-DAC could yield INR2,000-10,000 crore, with a first segment of INR1,000-5,000 crore.
Semiconductors are 17-19% of material cost and are fully imported today; management says price increases are absorbable and indigenisation will offset them.
Indigenous content is 80-85% on average, 90% for DRDO-driven products, and 55-65% for older TOT programs; semiconductors remain the main constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will the submarine (P-75I) programme add to BEL's business, and how big is its electronics share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BEL would supply more than 50-60% of electronics, about 25-30% of submarine value is electronics (plus or minus 5%), and execution could take about 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: When will the QRSAM contract be signed and how soon will execution start?
qa_highlights.answer: Signing is expected before June-end 2026 (5-10% chance of slipping to July). First production model is due 18 months after signing; margins are too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-off in other expenses, which rose about 36% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the rise reflects regular provisions tied to scale, such as performance warranty and LD-related items; total provisions as a percentage of sales were similar to FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the cash flow and working capital changes, including receivables rising about 30 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose because customer payments of about INR were delayed past the previous year-end and received in April-May 2026. Receivable days have been around 140-150 for four to five years. Management did not explain the low FY26 operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion.

qa_highlights.question: How much supply chain disruption came from the Middle East crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Some LRSAM sub-components from the Middle East were delayed about 1-1.5 months, but management sees no major FY26 revenue impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins after the wage revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance already reflects the wage revision due 1 January 2027, with some higher employee cost expected in Q4 FY27, and that the margin outlook is based on indigenisation and product mix.

risks_watch: QRSAM contract signing timing (June vs July 2026) and final pricing and advance terms, which drive FY27 order inflow.
Order book flat near INR74,000 crore against revenue of INR27,480 crore; FY27 growth above 15% depends on big-ticket orders arriving.

Semiconductor import dependence and the Middle East supply disruption.

500049|2026-06.headline: BEL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25.27% to INR 5,533 crore and PAT 8.17% to INR 1,048 crore; order book INR 72,258 crore.
500049|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 25.27% YoY to INR 5,533 crore, while PBT rose 8.81% to INR 1,403 crore and PAT rose 8.17% to INR 1,048 crore. Cumulative Q1 EBITDA margin was 25.83% and EPS was INR 1.43 versus INR 1.33. Order inflow was lean at INR 3,754 crore, which management attributed to timing, since FY26 year-end orders spilled into April. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 15% revenue growth, 21-23% EBITDA margin (with a 28% year-end claim), and over INR 55,000 crore order inflow including QRSAM.

segments.name: Defence platforms by service
segments.commentary: Army, Navy and Air Force each about 30% of the order book, with defence at roughly 90% of the total. Major order book items include Electronic Fuze (Army), LRSAM (Navy), LCA LRUs, Ashwini Radar and Mi-17 V5 EW suite (Air Force), and BMP-2 upgrade.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export order book about USD 465 million; internal FY27 export guidance around USD 300 million; target 10% of revenue from exports within five years.

segments.name: Counter-drone / DEW
segments.commentary: Focus on high-power laser and microwave DEW hard-kill systems; about 80% of 2 kW laser DEW orders from the last three years already supplied. Microwave DEW prototype ready with DRDO, still under evaluation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15%, which management said it is confident to meet or exceed.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 21-23% in the closing remarks; management also said year-end margin will cross 28%. Quarterly margin may vary between 25% and 31% on product mix.
FY27 order inflow guidance of over INR 55,000 crore including QRSAM (about INR 30,000 crore QRSAM, about INR 15,000 crore platform orders, rest base orders).
R&D spend above INR 2,200 crore and capex above INR 1,200 crore for FY27.
Defence to non-defence business mix of about 90:10.
Employee cost to turnover expected to stay around 12% in coming years despite wage revision from January 2027; provision for January-March 2027 in FY27.
Indigenisation target of zero import of modules and sub-modules within five years.
capex_capacity: Capex of over INR 1,200 crore planned for FY27, mainly production infrastructure and capacity enhancement.
R&D budget above INR 2,200 crore allocated for FY27 for niche technology, indigenisation and collaborative R&D.
AMCA: RFP submission date moved by two months to 27 August 2026; response with L&T to be ready by mid-August.
Indigenous content about 78-80% of turnover.
demand_pricing: Order inflow was lean in Q1 because FY26 year-end orders slipped into April; management said Q1 inflow of about INR 307 crore was in line with its plan.
QRSAM (Army and Air Force, about INR 30,000 crore) expected by September 2026, pending CCS approval; procedural delays acknowledged.
Project Kusha: BEL expects an order of INR 40,000 crore-plus for the program, with a minimum of INR 28,000-29,000 crore for BEL; RFP for commercial activity still a long way off after DRDO testing.

Platform orders of around INR 15,000 crore expected in FY27 (NGC or P75I, with more than 50% probability of both); Shatrughat and Samaghat about INR 9,000 crore, Shakti Phase 4 about INR 2,000 crore, HAMMER about INR 2,500 crore, expected in 3-6 months.
Netra Mk2: BEL lost the system integrator role to Adani Defence (L1), but expects subsystem supply (radar, EW, data links).
Management attributed the Q1 margin decline to product mix, not input cost; material cost typically 50-59% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 order inflow lean YoY and when will QRSAM come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 year-end orders spilled into April, Q1 inflow was in line with plan, and QRSAM is expected by September 2026 pending CCS approval, with all BEL inputs complete.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables, cash flow and margin decline drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell to about 140 from 176 at March 2026. Margin variation was attributed to product mix, not input costs; full-year EBITDA margin of 28% was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Tejas LRU delivery timing on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LRU supply is ahead of HAL's contract schedule; any HAL slowdown could shift INR 200-300 crore of turnover by a few months, below 1% of the INR 30,000 crore plan.

qa_highlights.question: LRSAM execution and FY27 revenue contributors?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 3,000 crore LRSAM balance remains, of which about INR 2,100 crore is planned for FY27. Other FY27 contributors include Akash Army (about INR 1,200 crore), D-29 EW, MPR Arudhra, BMP-2 upgrade and LCA LRUs (INR 500-1,000 crore each).

qa_highlights.question: Pay commission impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Wage revision due from 1 January 2027; FY27 will carry a three-month provision. Employee cost to turnover expected to stay around 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold with higher R&D and what is indigenisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects R&D rising towards 8% of revenue to support margins through indigenisation; it targets zero import of modules within five years.

500067|2026-03.headline: Blue Star Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 1.3% to Rs 4,072 Cr, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin up to 8%; management guides FY27 UCP margin to 8-8.5% despite cost pressure.
500067|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 1.3% YoY to Rs 4,072 Cr, the highest ever quarterly revenue, and EBITDA excluding other income rose to Rs 326.3 Cr (8% margin vs 7% a year ago). FY26 revenue grew 3.6% to Rs 12,402 Cr while net profit fell to Rs 527.3 Cr from Rs 591.3 Cr, with the Labour Code gratuity and leave encashment charge taken as an exceptional item. Summer demand set in only from 13 April 2026, so channel inventory and the timing of the 13% price increase are the main near-term swing factors. Management said FY27 margins will be under pressure from raw material and petrochemical costs, and it declined to give FY27 revenue growth guidance.

Management expects margin pressure through FY27 from commodity, copper, petrochemical (styrene, polystyrene) and FX costs; it said margins will be under pressure until 2030 as the market expands.

Price increase of about 13% warranted: about 8% realised to date and roughly 5% more to come in May-June billings. The 13% covers the desired margins but excludes further post-war input cost increases.
Segment 1 (projects and commercial AC) margin target of 7% to 7.5%; commercial AC growth outlook of 8% to 10% for FY27, with data centre MEP revenue potentially more than doubling in about 3 years.
Annual capex of about Rs 250 to 350 Cr including maintenance, R&D and IT. Decision on one more RAC assembly line expected by October 2026.
Management said it was too early to guide FY27 revenue growth; it is cautiously optimistic and depends on how the summer plays out.

Management said RAC and commercial refrigeration plants are operating close to 100% capacity this year if growth is good.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken since January including the BEE norm change, and how much more is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5% from the energy label change and about 8% in total including raw material and FX; about 8% of a warranted 13% has been realised, with roughly 5% more coming in May-June billings.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company see margin pressure in Q1 from the price increase timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin pressure will persist through the year; the extra price increase took effect in May, and 8% to 8.5% UCP margin remains the outlook for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory level in RACs compared with January, and will price hikes cause demand destruction?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is reasonable at about 45 to 60 days; management does not expect a sharp demand drop from the net 3% increase, but a fuel price shock could hit sentiment.

qa_highlights.question: Why are project margins stuck at 7% to 7.5% despite data centre growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are a blended business (buildings, infra, factories, data centres); margins have run at 7% to 7.5% and management will not commit to 8% to 8.5% yet.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q4 margins affected by, and was there a provision reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 17.5 Cr labour code provision reversal was in exceptional items and does not affect segment results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre MEP market and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Market estimated at about Rs 3,500 to 4,000 Cr; Blue Star's MEP business is about Rs 1,000 Cr a year with an order book of about Rs 1,500 Cr at any time. Equipment content is minimal, mainly electrical and mechanical items.

500086|2026-06.headline: Exide Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 17.6% and EBITDA rose 19.5% to INR655 crores, with margin at 12.4%.
500086|2026-06.overview: Management reported broad-based double-digit growth across automotive OEM, replacement, home inverter, solar, industrial and exports, helped by a strong summer and a low base. EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps YoY and about 70 bps QoQ despite higher input costs from West Asia disruption and rupee weakness. Price increases of 4-6% YoY across categories were taken, with further hikes to be decided case by case. In lithium-ion, all four Bangalore lines are installed, the NCM cylindrical and LFP prismatic lines have started customer samples, and revenue is expected to start during FY27. Management declined to give full-year guidance.

segments.name: Automotive OEM
segments.commentary: Grew about 25% YoY for a third straight quarter; 4W OEM volume up 21% and 2W OEM up 20%, on a low base. Management expects percentage growth to slow in H2 against a strong Q3/Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Replacement (2W/4W)
segments.commentary: 4-wheeler replacement volume grew about 10%; all replacement businesses reported double-digit revenue growth.

segments.name: Home inverters and solar
segments.commentary: Both grew over 20% YoY on summer demand; solar volume grew about 12-14% and solar posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR400+ crores. Inverters are 15-25% of revenue depending on season.

segments.name: Industrial infrastructure (ex-telecom)
segments.commentary: Maintained double-digit growth, supported by industrial UPS and traction. Government tenders were muted in the quarter, with an H2 pick-up expected.

segments.name: Lithium-ion (Exide Energy Solutions)
segments.commentary: Bangalore plant: 4 lines installed; NCM cylindrical and LFP prismatic lines are shipping samples. Lithium pack business is small (INR100-200 crores in FY26 per management) and management does not expect it to be profitable with imported cells.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 revenue guidance; management cited poor visibility on market and H2 base effects, though Q2 benefits from a low base.
Bangalore plant revenue expected to commence during FY27 shortly; utilisation of 25-30% of the factory in the first year, which management reaffirmed.
FY27 lithium-ion capex approved by Board at INR1,400 crores, with INR100 crores spent in July; may be reviewed.
Phase 1 (6 GWh) has no PLI support; Phase 2 capex is lower than Phase 1 as land and utilities for 12 GWh are already built, but total could exceed the earlier INR7,000 crore plan.

Phase 1 capacity is 6 GWh, with provision to expand to 12 GWh in the next few years. Pack capacity in-house is 1.5 GWh.

Lead-acid: INR500 crores is set aside every year for the core business, for bottleneck debottlenecking, automation and capacity expansion, mainly in 4W. Exide has 5 SLI plants with brownfield headroom.
Pilot line for R&D expected at end of calendar 2026; more than 100 R&D engineers are in Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was double-digit in most businesses: 4W replacement about 10%, 4W OEM 21%, 2W OEM 20%, solar 12-14%.

Management said 2W/3W/telecom lithium demand is a switch from imported cells, not new demand, and that the 3W market is about 70-75% aftermarket retrofits.

Chinese export VAT rebate on cells fell from 9% to 6%, and management expects the removal from 1 January 2027 to affect imported-cell landed costs. China export controls on raw materials are deferred to around November.

qa_highlights.question: Split of volume vs pricing growth, and whether any new contracts contributed?

qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no full-year guidance. It flagged H2 percentage slowdown in auto OEM due to the high base from Q3/Q4 FY26, though absolute volumes remain high (passenger vehicles up from 1.2 to 1.4 million).

qa_highlights.question: Cell yields and early learnings from the giga factory?

qa_highlights.question: Are there PLI and pricing views for the imported-cell competition?

qa_highlights.question: Inverter share of revenue?

500087|2026-03.headline: Cipla Q4 FY26 revenue INR 6,541 crore; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 18.5%-20% excluding Lanreotide, with US $1 billion run-rate target by FY27 end.

Quarterly EBITDA margin was 15.2% (21% for the year, excluding other income), and quarterly PAT was INR 555 crore (8.5% of sales). North America reported quarterly revenue of USD 155 million and annual revenue of USD 780 million, with the generic Ventolin AB-rated approval from the US facility as the key milestone. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin of 18.5%-20%, weighted to H2, and a US run-rate of USD 1 billion by end-FY27, both excluding Lanreotide.

500087|2026-06.headline: Cipla Q1 FY27 revenue INR7,119 crore (+2% YoY reported, ~4% adjusted); EBITDA margin ex-other income 16.7%, FY27 18.5–20% guidance kept.
500087|2026-06.overview: Cipla reported its highest-ever Q1 revenue of INR7,119 crore, up 2% YoY, but a new accounting presentation (certain marketing and promotional expenses now netted from revenue from 1 April 2026) depresses reported growth; management says adjusted growth is about 4%. EBITDA margin excluding other income was 16.7% and reported gross margin after material cost was 62.5%, hit by product mix, war-related costs, and higher-than-normal inventory write-offs. Management kept the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5–20% and reiterated a US$1 billion North America exit run-rate, contingent on launches of Ventolin, three respiratory assets (including generic Advair) and one large peptide. The company is moving into a new CFO transition, with Dinesh Jain succeeding Ashish Adukia as Global CFO.

segments.name: North America

segments.commentary: Private-market secondary sales grew 6.5% vs market 5.7% (IQVIA MAT); reported rupee revenue fell about 5% largely due to presentation change and loss of a tender whose supply plan continues to weigh this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin (ex-other income) guidance of 18.5–20% broadly unchanged; management says it is predicated on new launches and margin improvement.

Ventolin: exclusivity for about six months; management expects to capture generic share until competition enters, and sees Advair facing three or four competitors so not a US$100 million product.

500087|2026-09.headline: Cipla Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR 7,404 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.7%, while the $1 billion US exit run-rate guidance was reiterated.
500087|2026-09.overview: Cipla reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 7,404 crore, up 4% QoQ, with One India posting its highest-ever quarterly revenue and 12% YoY growth. EBITDA margin excluding other income was 18.7%, up 200 bps QoQ, and PAT was INR 878 crore (11.9% of sales). North America revenue was $172 million, up $10 million QoQ, and management kept its exit-FY27 run-rate target of $1 billion and FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5% to 20%. Key US launches (generic Advair DPI, Ventolin ramp) depend on supply ramp-up and three pending approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What bridges US revenue from about $170 million to the $250 million (about $1 billion annualised) exit rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to ramp-up of Ventolin and Advair plus four respiratory and one peptide launch expected this year; said there are multiple pathways and kept guidance. Ventolin was described as a big driver, and Lanreotide is excluded from the exit rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the three pending US approvals be needed to hit the exit rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ventolin alone covers much of the gap and that the combination of new and existing products gives confidence. It declined to split contribution by product and said approval timing depends on FDA review.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA and Q4 margin expected to improve sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Jain said the expected US ramp-up drives sequential improvement; the company guided to an improvement from Q3 to Q4, bucking typical Q4 seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Q2 other expense jump include one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Jain said there was no one-off; Q2 expense base is seasonally higher than Q1 and reflects launch-related investment ahead of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the South Africa reported decline despite secondary outperformance?
qa_highlights.answer: Achin Gupta cited an accounting change that restates top line but keeps EBITDA unchanged, plus a lost tender that is being contested; a favourable court ruling has come through.

qa_highlights.question: Is R&D going to remain at 6% to 7% of revenue, and do biosimilars need Phase III trials?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 R&D stays at 6% to 7% of revenue and that the FDA is generally waiving Phase III for biosimilars; the lead programme received FDA consultation supporting this.

500092|2026-03.headline: Crisil Q1 FY26 revenue rose 30.1% YoY, helped by a timing-driven USD4.5 million renewal pull-forward and INR14.4 crore FX gain.

Research, Analytics and Solutions (RAS) segment income rose 34.9% to INR735.6 crore with margin expansion to 22.7%, aided by a full quarter of PriceMetrix. Ratings grew about 20.2% YoY on surveillance fees and new ratings, while management said bond issuance fell 12% YoY in Q1 CY26 amid West Asia-driven yield hardening. 500096|2026-06.headline: Dabur Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 10.6%, with India FMCG up 9.5% on 5% volume growth and international up 15.5% in INR.
500096|2026-06.overview: Consolidated business grew 10.6% in Q1 FY27 with India FMCG at 9.5% (5% volume) and international at 15.5% in INR terms. HPC grew 12.3% led by hair care, where hair oil grew about 18% (roughly half volume, half price). Operating margin rose 11% and PAT rose 15%, both ahead of revenue. Management guided to sequential acceleration in revenue growth and double-digit consolidated revenue growth for the full year, while flagging that volumes will be under pressure from inflation and Middle East war-linked crude costs.

500101|2026-03.headline: Arvind acquires 61% of Dalco-GFT (via AAML) at 7.75x CY25 EBITDA; transaction valued at $136M EV.
500101|2026-03.overview: Arvind Limited announced the acquisition of a 61% economic stake in Dalco-GFT, a US needle-punch nonwovens maker, through its subsidiary Arvind Advanced Materials Limited (AAML), at 7.75x CY2025 reported EBITDA. Management said the deal is EPS and margin accretive at consolidated level and that financing has closed. The call was restricted to the transaction because FY26 results were yet to be announced, so no FY26 financials were discussed. Management guided to Dalco-GFT growing mid-teens on a $5M-per-year capex run rate, versus about 10% historically. Full target financials and goodwill figures were deferred to Q1 FY27, with headline balance sheet numbers promised separately.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation, and does capex need to rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 85%. Planned capex of about $5M per year is to be funded from internal accruals, with surplus cash used to pay down debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why do sellers exit now and how is management retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has rolled over a large part of its equity and holds about 39% in total; the founder holds about 16-17% for the 4-year period. Performance-linked long-term incentives were redone, and the financial sponsor is the main seller.

qa_highlights.question: How is the $136M EV funded given the $110M debt raised?
qa_highlights.answer: The EV of about $136M, plus about $16-17M net debt, implies about $84-85M of outlay for the stake. Sellers roll about $35-36M of equity into AAML, which explains the 61% stake and the debt split.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Dalco growing at only 10% historically?
qa_highlights.answer: The PE owners focused on efficiency and profitability (high-teen EBITDA margins) rather than capacity and new business development; the new plan lifts capex to about $5M per year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk in the US expansion and integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans a low-touch model with no change to the operating team; it says the workforce is under 150 with 70-80 blue-collar staff. Products are said to be broadly fungible across 3-4 end markets, and automotive is protected in the US.

qa_highlights.question: Cost inflation and supplier/customer bargaining power?
qa_highlights.answer: The only inflation is in polymer raw materials, which are petroleum-linked; some cost increases have been passed on and management sees no derailment risk. Sole sourcing reflects deep specification into vehicle platforms.

segments.commentary: About 90-92% of product is sold to Indian Oil under a long-term agreement at refinery transfer price (RTP). Around 300 retail outlet licences were obtained, with commissioning expected in FY27; the retail project is about INR400 crore.

guidance_outlook: No planned major M&I in the first six months of FY27; a scheduled M&I of one crude/refinery unit is expected around September-October 2026, which will affect throughput.
Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project (250 KTPA capacity, INR1,600 crore) has all approvals and execution is under way; IRR-based and aimed at higher realisations.
About INR2,000 crore (LOBS INR1,600 crore plus retail INR400 crore) to be spent over 2-3 years, plus about INR500 crore per year normal capex.
Low-cost debottlenecking and secondary capacity study with EIL expected to complete in FY27; capex not yet frozen and not in current plan.
Management expects momentum to continue into FY27; net debt ratio stated as comfortable and capacity to borrow for projects is available.
Bonus issue to be considered by the Board at the appropriate time.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR856 crore versus INR673 crore in FY25.
Group 2/3 LOBS unit of 250 KTPA (INR1,600 crore); execution started, approvals in place.
Retail outlet programme of about 300 outlets (INR400 crore), with bulk of commissioning in FY27.

Export duties on diesel and ATF were imposed from 26 March 2026; management said export is optional, and it is not booking exports under compulsion.

Crude mix in FY26 (approximate): India about 10%, Russia 25-30%, Middle East the majority (including Iraq), Africa and US 5-10%. Around 30-40% of Middle East term volumes were disrupted briefly, with suppliers assuring make-up cargoes.

Management said LPG maximisation (447 TMT vs 404 TMT) did not hurt margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will throughput stay at 110-111% in H1 FY27?

qa_highlights.question: What is the core versus reported Q4 GRM, and what was the forex loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Core GRM is US$10.3/bbl versus reported US$13.75/bbl. Forex loss was about INR200 crore in Q4 and about INR350 crore for FY26, per the call (later cited as INR400 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Is net GRM after export duty and RTP adjustment still healthy for diesel and ATF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the net GRM on realised RTP is close to long-term averages, around US$13/bbl, and that the monthly view is what counts. It declined to comment on media reports of OMC discount demands.

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics and capex of the LOBS project and low-cost debottlenecking?
qa_highlights.answer: LOBS is IRR-based, shifting volumes from Group 1 to Group 2/3 lube feedstock. Debottlenecking is at study stage with EIL, expected to complete in FY27, with capex not in current plan.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise mainly to forex losses booked in other expenses: INR634 crore in Q4 and INR2,001 crore for FY26. A separate note was not provided due to disclosure classification norms.

risks_watch: Crude supply disruption: Strait of Hormuz closure for over 50 days and 30-40% short-term disruption to Middle East term volumes; make-up cargoes assured but not yet confirmed.
Export duty and RTP mechanics on diesel and ATF; management declined to confirm any OMC discount arrangement.
Forex losses (INR350-400 crore in FY26) flowing through other expenses; watch for further INR-denominated impact.
Scheduled M&I around September-October 2026 could pull down throughput from above-100% levels.
Execution of INR2,000 crore growth capex (LOBS and retail) and commissioning of about 300 outlets in FY27.
Management did not quantify profit foregone from RTP-based sales to IOCL when asked.

500112|2026-06.headline: SBI Q1 FY27 net profit hit a record ₹21,121 crore; domestic NIM held at 3%, with full-year 3% guidance reiterated.
500112|2026-06.overview: SBI reported record Q1 FY27 net profit of ₹21,121 crore and operating profit growth of 9.77% YoY, with domestic NIM at 3%. Total business crossed ₹110 trillion, deposits exceeded ₹60 trillion and advances crossed ₹50 trillion. Gross and net NPA ratios were at their lowest in over two decades, though absolute GNPA/NNPA and fresh slippages (₹7,046 crore vs ₹5,500 crore in Q4) rose sequentially. Management attributed much of the quarter-on-quarter noise in expenses and income to bulk Q4 booking and said it will amortise some bulk expenses over three quarters going forward. Credit growth guidance was kept at 14-15% for FY27, and the bank said ECL impact details would come in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: Cost of deposits down; cost of resources up ~7 bps (as stated)
Q1 business growth 1.33% (analyst calculation from quoted QoQ figures)
0.32% growth (as quoted by analyst); ~18% YoY per analyst

segments.commentary: Retail term deposits grew 14%; savings bank deposits of ₹17.5 lakh crore grew 10%. Gold loans (personal ₹1.25 trillion, agri ₹1.85 trillion) crossed ₹3.1 trillion as of 30 June, with yields of 8.5-8.9%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book is about 33% of total advances; management said corporate growth was lower sequentially due to T-bill-linked pricing shifts. Corporate pipeline including undisbursed loans and working capital exceeds ₹9 lakh crore.

segments.commentary: SME loan limit for MSME Dream business rule engine raised to ₹10 crore from ₹5 crore; SME fresh slippages ₹2,300 crore in Q1.

segments.commentary: About $6 billion FCNR(B) mobilised plus $1 billion OFCB and $300 million ECBs (~$7.3 billion total), funded mostly via foreign offices; management expects ~$10 billion FCNR(B) and ~₹1 trillion total mobilisation.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: SBI Funds Management listed; management said NSE value unlocking is possibly in Q3 and mutual fund value unlocking in the current quarter.

FY27 credit growth guidance of 14-15% reiterated (corporate revised to 14-15% per webcast answer); management views 18% as difficult and industry growth at 15-16%.

ECL: numbers to be given in Q2; ECL data to be pushed into IT systems by around 18 August; no major impact expected, with capital augmentation from mutual fund listing and planned divestments plus transitional regulatory dispensation.

SBI General Insurance is the next listing candidate, with no timeline given.

Centre of Excellence and CHAKRA initiative being set up to build capability to fund emerging sectors such as data centres, GPU, hydrogen and solar; early stage with a few assessments done.

Excess SLR of ₹3.06 lakh crore as of 30 June, rising to ~₹4 lakh crore currently.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth managed against liquidity; wholesale/bulk deposit rates rising and bank not willing to pay them; bulk deposit proportion not disclosed but said to be coming down.
CASA: savings deposits grew 10%; non-government current account deposits grew 14%; government current account balances declining.
Corporate pricing expected to be driven by CP and NCD rates; management does not expect major deviation from its pricing expectations.
Xpress Credit growing at about 8% QoQ, held back by gold loan substitution (~3% rate arbitrage). Gold loan yield is 8.5-8.9%; average ticket size ₹2.5-3 lakh; LTV below 55-56%; risk weight near zero.
Forex fee income of ~₹500 crore in Q1 affected by the war-driven volatility and RBI NOP limit of $100 million effective late March.
Analyst observed NBFCs growing personal loans at 20-25% vs banks at 10-11%; management cited collection capability as a constraint on self-employed lending.
Government business fee income boosted about ₹500 crore QoQ, around half from accounting change to accrual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did deposits (0.5%) and advances (0.32%) grow slowly QoQ, and why did slippages, SMA-2, and other provisions rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deposit growth is managed against liquidity and rising wholesale rates; Q1 slippages are seasonally high, ₹7,046 crore with ~₹1,400-1,500 crore pulled back, and there is no concern on GNPA/NNPA/SMA. Other provisions of ₹1,269 crore are mostly PLI provisions spread over four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL affect run-rate credit cost and net worth, and will it be passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: No numbers yet; to be given in Q2. Management expects no major impact given capital augmentation and transitional dispensation, and does not expect pass-through to borrowers in year one.

qa_highlights.question: Is 18% credit growth sustainable, and when does SBI become the most valuable bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 18% reflects base effect, but 14-15% guidance is anchored on nominal GDP plus 2-3%; industry estimated at 15-16%. Market-cap question was not directly answered.

qa_highlights.answer: Domestic impact not significant given small bulk proportion; overseas NIM impact neutral as foreign offices reduce lower-yielding trade finance and supply chain assets to fund leverage.

qa_highlights.answer: Personal gold loans ₹1.25 trillion and agri ₹1.85 trillion; yields 8.5-8.9%. Management said no scope to move to double-digit yields; treated as opportunistic and ROE-accretive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of deposits and pension trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits improved, supporting NIM stability; pension costs declining with significant reduction expected post-2035, supported by actuarial revaluations (MTM gain ₹935 crore vs ₹1,125 crore a year ago).

500113|2026-03.headline: SAIL Q4 FY26: PAT up 43% YoY on higher NSR and volumes; FY27 sales volume target 22 mn tons and capex guided to INR15,000 crore.
500113|2026-03.overview: SAIL reported Q4 FY26 crude steel output of 4.9 mn tons (up 4% YoY), sales volume of 5.3 mn tons (up 4%) and turnover of INR30,541 crore (up 5%). PBT rose 48% and PAT 43% YoY in the quarter, and management said Q4 borrowings fell by INR3,200 crore. For FY26, record sales volume of 19.9 mn tons (up 11%) and a roughly 1 mn ton inventory reduction drove borrowings down about INR8,150 crore, and management said the FY26 balance sheet carries no audit qualifications for the first time in many years. Management said NSR rose about INR4,000/t from Q4 to April-May, while coking coal cost is also rising, with a stated impact of INR1,400-1,500/t in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, no rail price arrears in FY26 vs ~INR1,800 crore in FY25
management hopes to lower it in FY27

segments.name: Long products
segments.commentary: Q4 NSR INR53,400/t; April NSR INR57,600/t and mid-May about INR57,800/t. March long-product price increase was about INR1,500/t.

segments.name: Flat products
segments.commentary: Q4 NSR INR51,000/t; April INR56,700/t and mid-May about INR56,000/t. Flat price increase in March was about INR1,400/t. A safeguard duty on flat imports is in place.

segments.name: Bokaro Steel Plant
segments.commentary: EBITDA recovered sharply in H2 FY26 after FY25 breakdowns and a Hot Strip Mill repair that ran 2 months beyond plan. Better flat-product NSR and SMS fixes also helped, and management expects further improvement in FY27.

segments.name: Salem (stainless)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making. CR mill yield is 83-84% against a 90% target, and LPG has been replaced with PNG. Management plans to feed imported stainless slabs to idle CR and SR mill capacity.

segments.name: NSL / RINL volumes
segments.commentary: NSL total volume was 1.12 mn tons in FY26, with Q4 near 0.1 mn tons. Sales of RINL products began in February, at about 48,000-50,000 tons in Q4, and are guided at 0.6-0.7 mn tons in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume target of 22 mn tons (about 22.5 mn tons including RINL products), up from 19.9 mn tons in FY26.
FY27 crude steel production target of 22.5 mn tons against stated capacity of 21 mn tons, to be reached through debottlenecking and operational efficiency.

Capex guidance: INR15,000 crore in FY27, INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28, and INR20,000-25,000 crore per year after that, to be funded mainly from internal accruals with incremental long-term borrowings.
Coke rate target to fall by about INR20/kg in FY27 after the earlier reduction; management aims for a further drop in coke rate.

Employee strength is 49,752 as of 1 April 2026, with a further reduction of 3,400-3,500 expected in each of FY27 and FY28. A VRS targeting 500-1,000 exits is under way. Pay revision from 1 January 2027 is not yet in the guidance and will be provided for in Q4 FY27.

Q1 FY27 inventory: management aims for no build-up in Q1 and expects Q2 to be sluggish with inventory reduction in Q3 and Q4. Coking coal cost is up about INR2,000/t to about INR21,500/t, implying a cost impact of INR1,400-1,500/t on production cost.
capex_capacity: Crude steel capacity is 21 mn tons; FY26 output was 19.43 mn tons. FY27 target is 22.5 mn tons through debottlenecking and operating beyond rated capacity.

New capacity expansion projects at IISCO (about 4.5 mn tons, INR35,000-36,000 crore), Bhilai (about 3.5 mn tons, about INR30,000 crore, yet to be announced) and Bokaro (about 3 mn tons, about INR18,000 crore) are the three cleared expansions.

IISCO packages are tendered and groundwork is starting, with spending rising from FY28 and some spending in Q4 FY27. Bokaro and Bhilai spending is mainly expected from FY29; new capacity is expected from FY30-31.
Capex in FY27 covers debottlenecking, AMR (asset modernisation/replacement) and expansion projects.
Iron ore: FY26 production was 38 mn tons with a 56 mn ton target for FY27 and 80 mn tons as the longer-term ramp-up goal. The Chiria mine is a new lease, not a renewal.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew about 8% in FY26 while production grew 11%. India became a marginal net exporter, with exports of 6.5 mn tons and imports of 6.6 mn tons.
Q1 demand is expected to be muted, with destocking, then a pickup from Q3. Rupee depreciation and firmer international prices support landed cost and selling prices.

Cost pressure: the Middle East situation pushed up limestone/flux costs (CFR from about $23-24 to about $35/t), with an impact of only INR100-200/t on saleable steel. Fuel constraints were managed through PNG and LPG banks.
Rail freight prices: FY25 arrears were about INR1,800 crore; FY26 provisional rates are lower, and the FY25 rate finalisation could affect FY27. Management said the direction is unclear.
Flat safeguard duty and cheaper import blends are limiting import volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 volume guidance and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 sales target of 22 mn tons (vs 19.9 mn in FY26); FY27 capex INR15,000 crore against about INR9,100 crore in FY26; FY28 about INR18,000-19,000 crore; then INR20,000-25,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Realisations in Q4 and April-May, and cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 blended NSR about INR52,000/t; April about INR57,000/t. Coking coal rose from INR18,200/t in Q4 to about INR21,000 in April and INR21,800 in May. Q1 consumption cost impact is smaller because of about 30 days of inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity and the path to 22.5 mn tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 21 mn tons. Growth to 22.5 mn tons comes from debottlenecking and efficiency gains, with new capacity only from FY30-31. Management said output could reach 23 mn tons later.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q3 to Q4 EBITDA bridge explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Input prices were a INR272 crore headwind, offset by a INR429 crore gain from better raw-material usage (higher PCI, more oxygen, better iron ore use).

qa_highlights.question: Can 100%+ utilisation be sustained given the capacity figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DPR capacity is not a hard limit for blast furnaces and SMS; productivity can exceed design, citing examples of 2.3 going to 3 and the operations of peers.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and what is the leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects internal accruals to cover most of FY27 capex, with incremental long-term borrowings beyond that. Net debt to equity is 0.37 and is expected to fall further in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital rise with the monsoon season?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for no inventory build in Q1 but said Q2 will be challenging, with inventory reduction planned for Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Wage revision from 1 January 2027: the impact is not yet in guidance and may be booked in Q4 FY27; past revisions were about 15%.
Coking coal and imported coal costs are rising, with the Q1 cost impact estimated at INR1,400-1,500/t against a NSR tailwind.
Q1 and Q2 demand softness and destocking; inventory build risk.
Rail freight price finalisation for FY25 could go either way in FY27.
Middle East supply disruption affecting fuel, flux and raw material routes (Strait of Hormuz).
Salem Steel Plant losses and BISL disinvestment status; the Chiria mining lease is still pending.
Achieving 22 mn tons on the 21 mn ton stated capacity and funding INR15,000 crore capex in FY27.
