rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY30-31 for new capacity; debottlenecking to 22.5 mn t in FY
rows.why: Crude capacity is 21 mn t against 19.43 mn t output (92% utilisation) and the FY27 target of 22.5 mn t, but the three cleared expansions (IISCO 4.5 mn t, Bhilai 3.5 mn t, Bokaro 3 mn t) only arrive FY30-31, so new capacity within the window rests on debottlenecking, not new plants.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 sales target of 22 mn t vs record 19.9 mn t in FY26 (+11%), with RINL products guided at 0.6-0.7 mn t; Q1-Q2 expected to be sluggish, so the growth is back-loaded.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 92% with 21 mn t rated capacity and FY27 capex of INR15,000 crore, stepping up to INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28 and INR20,000-25,000 crore a year after; Bhilai (about INR30,000 crore) is yet to be announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 PAT up 51% and Q4 PAT up 43% with NSR up about INR4,000/t into April-May, but the 22 mn t target depends on Q1-Q2 destocking and the rail-freight outcome is unclear.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coking coal rising to INR21,800/t in May (cost impact INR1,400-1,500/t in Q1), Q2 expected sluggish with inventory build risk, and FY25 rail arrears (about INR1,800 crore) could go either way.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: RINL products began selling in Feb 2026 at about 48,000-50,000 t in Q4 and are guided at 0.6-0.7 mn t in FY27; no other new product launch was discussed.

rows.label: Coke rate cut of INR20/kg in FY27
rows.why: Management commits to a further INR20/kg coke-rate reduction after the earlier cut, and the Q3-to-Q4 EBITDA bridge already showed a INR429 crore gain from better raw-material usage.

rows.label: Net debt to equity down from 0.37
rows.why: Borrowings fell about INR8,150 crore in FY26 (INR3,200 crore in Q4) and management expects net debt to equity to fall further in FY27, with capex of INR15,000 crore mostly funded from internal accruals.

rows.label: Salem stainless turnaround
rows.why: Salem is still loss-making with CR mill yield at 83-84% against a 90% target, and management plans to feed imported stainless slabs to idle CR and SR capacity.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 record volume, profit growth, debt reduction and the FY27 22 mn t target and capex path; it was cautious on Q1-Q2 demand, coking coal cost, the wage revision and rail price outcome, and analysts pressed on whether 100%+ utilisation on 21 mn t capacity is sustainable.

500113|2026-06.headline: SAIL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose over 50% to INR4,356 crore (16.7% margin) despite 4.8 Mt crude steel output, aided by advanced capital repairs and better NSR.
500113|2026-06.overview: SAIL reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA of INR4,356 crore versus INR2,925 crore a year earlier, with margin of 16.7% and EBITDA per tonne of INR10,464. PBT and PAT rose to INR2,159 crore and INR1,636 crore from INR890 crore and INR685 crore. Crude steel output fell to 4.8 Mt (4.9 Mt CPLY) and sales volume dropped about 7-8% to 4.2 Mt, as major capital repairs at IISCO, Durgapur and Bokaro were advanced into Q1 by design. Average NSR was INR57,100/t, up about INR5,000/t from Q4 FY26, and borrowings were flat at INR21,729 crore versus INR21,663 crore at 1 March 2026.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Flats about 52.7% and longs about 34.8% of sales; semis fell to about 11-12.5% from 14% in Q1 FY26. Finished steel share rose to 89% from 86%.

segments.commentary: NMDC Steel marketing sales were nil vs 3.73 lakh t CPLY; RINL semis sales were about 93,000 t (new this year). NSL plus RINL combined was about 2.76 lakh t CPLY.

Gap between primary and secondary TMT narrowed to about INR5,000/t.
June to July long-product prices fell about INR2,000-3,000/t; recent upward momentum of INR500-1,000/t expected. Flat product prices fell about INR1,000/t between June and July.
Safeguard duty of 11.5% remains in place (second year of three-year term). Anti-dumping investigation has been initiated and may bring relief.

Rail price: provisional FY27 price about INR74,000/t, which management expects to be revised upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q1 NSR vs Q4, and how do July prices and Q2 NSR look?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 NSR was INR57,100/t vs Q4 INR52,000/t. Monsoon-driven seasonal decline expected in Q2, with Q2 NSR about INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1; longs more affected than flats.

qa_highlights.question: Is full-year volume guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management maintained full-year volume guidance and expects growth over last year by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for coal costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported coal was INR21,300/t in Q1 vs INR18,100/t in Q4. Index fell from about 235 to 220; coal cost expected to fall INR1,000-2,000/t from August.

qa_highlights.question: Is third-party iron ore sales growth sustainable, and what about subgrade inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Mines sales more than doubled YoY, adding about INR400 crore turnover and INR150 crore profit. Target of about 8 Mt for captive mines; subgrade inventory about 32 Mt with 3 Mt first auction in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target INR15,000 crore; FY28 above INR20,000 crore; later years INR25,000-26,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-reduction plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,000/t cost cut in FY27 from Q2; by FY29 IISCO expansion cuts variable cost INR3,000-4,000/t, with fixed cost up INR1,500-2,000/t, net about INR2,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the Gulf conflict affect input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel impact limited due to in-plant gas use; flux cost up on freight but offset by lower usage, saving about INR25 crore. Limestone and imported coal costs rose; coal up about INR3,500/t YoY.

500113|2026-09.headline: SAIL Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR1,774 crore on 5.2 MT sales and EBITDA of INR4,561 crore, despite higher imported coking coal costs.
500113|2026-09.overview: SAIL's Q2 FY27 sales volume rose 24% QoQ to 5.2 MT and turnover reached INR31,766 crore (+20% YoY), with EBITDA of INR4,561 crore and PAT of INR1,774 crore. Imported coking coal rose about INR1,700/t QoQ to INR22,930/t, compressing margins, though volume, inventory reduction and high-end mix offset it. Borrowings fell to INR20,583 crore and inventory dropped to 1.59 MT, while management guided to about 21 MT FY27 sales (cut from 22 MT) and a capex step-up to INR15,000 crore this year and over INR1.2 lakh crore over FY27-FY31. Management said Q3 and Q4 prices and technical parameters should improve, with October NSR up about INR4,000/t over the Q2 average.

segments.name: Iron ore fines (external sales)
segments.commentary: H1 sales about 2.5 MT vs 0.9 MT last year (+167%), with profit of INR388 crore vs INR124 crore CPLY. FY27 target is 7-8 MT vs internal 10 MT target.

segments.name: Rails and bars
segments.commentary: Rails were about 8% of volume and bar and rod about 22% of production volume; rails hold a larger share of turnover. Rail sales expected at 1.2-1.3 MT this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 saleable steel sales guidance cut to about 21 MT from 22 MT, with H1 at 9.33 MT; includes about 0.5 MT of RINL volume and no NMDC sales.

FY27 capex guidance INR15,000 crore (H1 INR5,500 crore; Q3+Q4 INR9,000-10,000 crore); FY28 above INR20,000 crore, FY29 about INR25,000 crore; about INR1.2 lakh crore over FY27-FY31.
Imported coking coal guided at about INR23,500/t in Q3 and about INR22,000-23,000/t in Q4; Q3 average around INR23,800-23,900/t (about INR1,000 above Q2).
Inventory target of 1.2-1.3 MT by year-end (15 days at 30 Sep vs 17.5 days at 31 Mar); plants and ports target 30-35 days.
Employee count expected at about 46,000 by FY27 year-end and 26,000 by 2031; separations of 3,000-4,000 a year plus VRS.
Interest cost may rise in H2 after a 25 bp repo hike; management expects debt to rise from FY28 as capex ramps.
capex_capacity: Expansion from 20 MT to 35 MT across IISCO, Bokaro, Bhilai and Rourkela; IISCO packages already ordered and work started, Bokaro in advanced tendering, Bhilai tendering to start shortly, Rourkela DPR ready for in-principle approval.
Rowghat iron ore mine: interim mining at about 3 MT under EC; ramp-up path 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 14 MT over 3-4 years after MDO main mining starts (1+ year away).
Tasra coking coal mine to start production from January 2027, expected to lower imported coking coal dependence.
Gua mines to expand from 4 MT to 10 MT via MDO appointment; 2 MT RSP pellet plant on course and in advanced stage.
Long-term aspiration of 100 MT iron ore by FY31-32 (80-85 MT is the fallback); excludes Chiria.
demand_pricing: Q2 average NSR was about INR54,400/t long and INR57,000/t flat (average INR55,500/t); October NSR is INR58,700/t long and INR61,700/t flat, about INR4,000/t above Q2.
Imported coal index (Platts) peaked at $290/t in August and stabilised at $266-267/t.
Q2 EBITDA hit by rainy-season furnace and raw material issues in Jharkhand and Odisha; technical parameters improved in October.
Rail price revision had about INR300 crore positive impact in Q1 and nil in Q2.
Q2 EBITDA per tonne about INR8,170 vs H1 about INR9,561; management targets INR11,000-12,000/t levels in Q3-Q4.
Management cited WSA forecast of 1.7% global steel demand growth in CY27 and India consumption growth of about 8% in CY26 and CY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity upfront when capex spans 4-5 years, given single-digit return ratios?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed timing matters and said the FPO will be timed to investor confidence; capex will be funded through about INR50,000 crore of internal accruals over 4 years, with debt and FPO later.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 volume still be 22 MT and does it include RINL and NMDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is now about 21 MT given H1 of 9.33 MT; it includes RINL (H1 184,000 t, Q2 88,000 t, full-year up to 0.5 MT) but excludes NMDC.

qa_highlights.question: Imported coal price outlook, given earlier guidance of a INR1,000-2,000 decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 average was INR22,930/t, Q3 expected about INR23,500 and Q4 about INR22,000-23,000; management said there was no change in accounting policy and the earlier view assumed prices would fall.

qa_highlights.question: Capex ramp-up and annual spend trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex guided at INR15,000 crore, FY28 above INR20,000 crore, FY29 INR25,000 crore; about INR1.2 lakh crore spend over FY27-FY31, confirmed as FY27-FY31.

qa_highlights.question: Labour code provision of INR198 crore in Q2 (INR350 crore cumulative)?
qa_highlights.answer: Booked under other expenses (repairs and maintenance line) on best estimate using infrastructure rates; final industrial rates are not yet notified, so plus or minus adjustments are possible.

qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was about 1.0-1.1 MT and Q2 about 1.1-1.2 MT (management estimates); constraints are permits and pricing in Jharkhand, with Rowghat and Dalli-Rajhara as sources for Chhattisgarh.

500114|2026-03.headline: Titan Q4 FY26: management guides 15-20% jewellery growth as a 3-5 year CAGR, not FY27; buyer growth returned to 8% and Damas/Middle East losses weighed on Q4.
500114|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 top-line growth as its best in the recent past, with all businesses growing. Jewellery buyer growth recovered to 8% in Q4 after being roughly flat for the prior nine months, helped by wedding buying, gold price-led urgency, the exchange campaign and the Festival of Diamonds activation. Profitability was pressured by a ₹82 crore loss at the international subsidiary (largely Middle East, incl. Damas), a ~₹80 crore transfer-pricing adjustment in standalone books, and a ~₹100-120 crore employee special reward booked in unallocated costs in Q4. Management declined to give FY27 numerical guidance and deferred margin outlook to an investor day in the first week of June 2026.

500117|2026-03.headline: DCW Q4 FY26 PAT rose 60% YoY to Rs.18 crore and FY26 EBITDA rose 11% to Rs.240 crore, with net debt cut to Rs.71 crore.
500117|2026-03.overview: Q4 revenue was Rs.609 crore (+13.2% YoY, +17% QoQ) and Q4 EBITDA including other income was Rs.70 crore (+14% YoY, +40% QoQ). FY26 revenue was Rs.2,144 crore (+7.2%) and EBITDA Rs.240 crore (+11.2%), with PAT up 60% to Rs.48 crore, helped by lower finance cost. Management said profit growth came from volumes, utilisation and cost gains rather than price, since realisations fell across most products, with C-PVC down more than 20%. Specialty EBITDA fell 6.5% to Rs.177 crore on C-PVC–PVC spread compression, while basic chemicals EBITDA rose to Rs.54 crore from Rs.19 crore. Management withheld FY27 EBITDA guidance and cited pricing volatility from the West Asia conflict; the earlier Rs.400 crore target looks derailed.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (C-PVC, SIOP)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA Rs.177 crore (-6.5%) and margin about 30%, down about 6 points, as C-PVC realisations fell over 20% against unchanged PVC input prices. Q4 EBITDA Rs.39 crore, down 16% YoY and 22% QoQ. SIOP margin is still 35-40%, per management.

segments.name: Basic chemicals (caustic soda, soda ash, chlorine-neutral)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA Rs.54 crore vs Rs.19 crore, with margin 3.5% vs 1.3%, helped by fixed-cost absorption and solar power substitution. Q4 EBITDA Rs.30 crore vs Rs.14 crore a year earlier. Caustic realisation was about $350/t in Q4 and above $400/t in Q1 FY27 per management.

segments.name: Synthetic rutile
segments.commentary: Record FY26 sales volume and reduced inventory. Management guided that the spread should stay elevated vs last year on a better mix from ex-China long-term contracts. It is reported within basic chemicals, and no quarterly realisation was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 EBITDA guidance. CFO said the Rs.400 crore target communicated earlier is 'derailed' by pricing pressure in commodities and specialty; a Rs.300 crore figure could not be confirmed.
Scheduled term loan repayment of about Rs.130 crore in FY27; with Rs.71 crore net debt, the company expects to be net cash positive by end-FY27.
Finance cost for FY27 is guided to fall by about Rs.12-13 crore to around Rs.50 crore, or slightly below, if working-capital credit lines are not used heavily.
The 10 kt final C-PVC phase was completed in late March 2026; benefits are expected from Q1 FY27 and are expected to be annualised over the year.
Management expects caustic and soda ash prices to stay elevated for a couple of quarters; VCM/PVC spreads may be under pressure due to the West Asia conflict.
capex_capacity: C-PVC capacity was raised from 20 kt to 50 kt: 30 kt was added this year, with the final 10 kt completed in late March 2026. C-PVC volumes rose to about 37-38 kt from about 22 kt.
SIOP debottlenecked from 18 kt to 28 kt; output reached 24 kt last year and is now near capacity. Future SIOP spend is aimed at value-added grades, not volume.
Commodity capex will focus on efficiency, not volume. Growth capex will go into specialty or niche chemistries. New capex announcements are on hold until the geopolitical situation clears.
Renewable (solar) project was commissioned in FY26 and substitutes about 25% of power from TNEB. Further solar investment is on hold pending clarity on Tamil Nadu banking rules.
Management said incremental C-PVC payback is about 2-2.5 years at current prices; ROC is 8.56% (slide 20), and management said it would be above 14-15% at 2023-24 commodity prices.
demand_pricing: C-PVC realisations fell more than 20% in FY26 with unchanged PVC input prices, compressing the PVC–C-PVC spread. Management said spreads have returned to pre-war levels, and a pass-through lag in March is expected to normalise in the coming quarter.

Caustic soda operating rates fell in Southeast Asia due to petrochemical feedstock shortages, tightening supply. Demand from paper and textile dipped, but alumina demand is strong, and there has been no production curtailment.
Soda ash import price is about $250/t, and prices are supported by the loss of Iran and Russia imports and higher freight.
Synthetic rutile realisation depends on the export mix; ex-China customers pay better prices. Management is building long-term ex-China contracts.

Management said Epigral, Lubrizol and other new C-PVC capacity still leaves room for imports, so it does not expect a domestic glut. It also noted that dumping cases on PVC and soda ash were not implemented, and that China and Korea C-PVC duties were applied earlier.

PVC feedstock VCM is sourced largely from the Middle East. Supply was disrupted by the Gulf war, so the company is buying at higher cost, which it cannot fully pass through. Management said two European PVC plants (about 2 lakh t, including Vinnolit) closed in 2025, before the conflict.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the caustic soda price firming: cost push or end-user demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to supply disruption: Southeast Asian petrochemical feedstock shortages cut caustic operating rates. It expects this to last until the situation normalises. Q4 realisation was about $350/t and Q1 is above $400/t.

qa_highlights.question: Will the power cost savings from solar be Rs.40-50 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the original target was about Rs.40 crore and later guidance was Rs.25-30 crore. Adjusting for coal prices and volume, savings are about Rs.23-24 crore, and power cost is about Rs.7-8 crore lower in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: What finance cost should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost should fall by Rs.12-13 crore to about Rs.50 crore, or slightly less, as the company keeps about Rs.200 crore in FDs. Negative carry from working-capital lines could push it up if the war continues.

qa_highlights.question: Are we on track for Rs.2,500 crore revenue, Rs.400 crore EBITDA and net debt-free status by FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-free by FY27 is on track given Rs.130 crore of repayments, and the company should be net cash positive. The Rs.400 crore EBITDA target is derailed by price erosion, and no EBITDA guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROC and steps to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: ROC is 8.56%. Management said it will rise with commodity prices and that new investment will focus on high-margin, low-capex projects. It said ROC would be 14-15% or more at 2023-24 commodity prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a glut risk in C-PVC from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic demand still exceeds combined capacity of DCW, Epigral, and Lubrizol, so it sees no mismatch. Imports would fill any gap.

qa_highlights.answer: Supply moved from a single Qatar producer to a global distributor sourcing across Asia. Management ruled out backward integration at current scale; storage expansion would add only about 10-15 days of inventory.

500124|2026-06.headline: Dr Reddy's halts semaglutide injectable API commercial supply after impurity out of spec in scale-up batch; 6-7 million pens now expected Nov-March.
500124|2026-06.overview: Dr Reddy's disclosed on July 9, 2026 that an impurity from a scaled-up synthetic semaglutide API process was out of specification in finished drug product testing, halting API dispatch to long-term partner OneSource. Management says the issue is a process/reaction problem requiring parameter tweaks and repeat validation (three validation batches), with no equipment change expected. Commercial supply is now targeted to resume in October, with 6-7 million pens expected from November to March FY27 versus the earlier plan that assumed sales from July to October. Management says no recall, no regulatory filing change, no patient safety impact on product already supplied, and no penalties expected, though some customer down-payment arrangements may need renegotiation. The company said oral semaglutide is unaffected because it uses a different API source.

segments.commentary: Commercial API supply halted pending validation; resumption targeted for October with 6-7 million pens from November to March. Management says no penalties are anticipated, though some down-payment arrangements may need renegotiation.

segments.name: Semaglutide oral tablets
segments.commentary: Management said there is no impact, as oral tablets use a different API source.

guidance_outlook: Validation timeline: root cause in days to a week or two, validation batches and testing (sterility up to three weeks) through end-September, then commercial API to OneSource in October, and market supply from late October or early November.
Management reiterated the 20%-plus EBITDA margin target is unchanged, but acknowledged lost sales in the coming months versus what was discussed at the May and June investor meetings.
Captive manufacturing plans remain valid but will shift by a few months, since in-house facility API supply depends on post-validation output.
Backup injectable API supplier is about a year away because it needs a pre-approval supplement.
Management said demand exceeds supply and it is confident in demand going forward.
capex_capacity: Scale-up of synthetic API process at the API facility was intended to increase API output for growing global semaglutide demand; the scale-up batch failed the impurity specification at finished product testing.
The in-house fill-finish facility is being built and will eventually be used for semaglutide and other products; management said plans shift by a few months.
Management said that, if the issue were not solved, the halt would last through September, with the backup supplier not available for about a year.
demand_pricing: Management said demand exceeds supply: 'if we had 15 million, we could supply that also.'
Competition from Sandoz, Aspen and others was raised; management said some of these names are also being supplied by Dr Reddy's.
Partners in Canada (Sandoz, Torrent) and India were updated; some have alternatives. Canadian supply already shipped is unaffected, but future Canadian supply will be impacted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for resolving the impurity issue, and how is supply affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects validation completion around September, supply to OneSource in October and market supply from late October or early November; a halt is in effect until then. Management noted a risk of further delay.

qa_highlights.question: Will re-validation need new regulatory submissions?
qa_highlights.answer: No; validation is a scale-up step with no specification or filing change, so no prior agency approval is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is any inventory at risk or any recall needed?
qa_highlights.answer: No recall, since scale-up batches were never shipped. Inventory held at OneSource is company-owned; management said it may need to be written down, with details in about two weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Does the issue affect the 20%-plus EBITDA margin target and the 12 million pen first-year target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said plans are unchanged beyond the lost sales; FY27 volume now expected at 6-7 million pens in addition to units already sold, which is below the earlier plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is the impurity from raw material, process or equipment?
qa_highlights.answer: The impurity is from the API process and reaction, not raw material; management said parameter changes should fix it without equipment change.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be penalties to partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no penalties are anticipated, though some down-payment arrangements may need renegotiation.

risks_watch: Validation risk: a further failure would push supply beyond the current October and November timeline.

Renegotiation of customer down-payment arrangements and potential loss of partners (Canada, India) who may choose alternatives.
Competitive intensity from new entrants (Sandoz, Aspen and others) during the supply gap.
Captive fill-finish facility timeline, which now shifts by a few months.
Q1 FY27 results (silent period) to show the financial impact of the disclosure.

It was firm that there is no recall, no regulatory filing change and no patient safety impact, and reiterated long-term commitment to OneSource.

There is no impact on the product's existing global regulatory filings, whether approved or currently under review.
Nothing has changed. Unfortunately, if we had 15 million, we could supply that also.
It has nothing to do with the cost here. It's about GMP.

qa_highlights.question: Nutra: how much growth comes from US Valensa versus India, and what EBITDA margin is achievable at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is largely from Valensa with new launches. Steady-state EBITDA margin is 12-15%. India is about 20% of consolidated Nutra turnover; Europe certification issues in India business were not entirely company fault and have been resolved.

qa_highlights.question: What KPIs will management track by March 2027 to judge the disciplined approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on working capital efficiency, leveraging debt cost, monetising non-core assets, cost reduction and improving current ratio; aiming for a stronger balance sheet by March 2027 and March 2028 and over the next 4-6 quarters. Standalone debt: about Rs. 150 crore long-term and Rs. 800-900 crore short-term, with CPG margin KPIs set for breakeven in 4-5 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh crush fall, and is TN sugar still viable or in need of restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Cane availability in TN and AP is a macro concern as farmers shift to other crops; crush in these geographies expected flat to about 5% lower in SY 2026-27, with Karnataka the only make-up source. Management is running tight cost control in these states and says further restructuring discussions continue, with no specific plan announced.

qa_highlights.question: PSRIPL: what is the cash outgo versus the non-cash impairment and reversal, and is there more to fund?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs. 610 crore was infused (already in public domain); Rs. 55 crore loan given in Q1, totalling Rs. 665 crore. The Rs. 591 crore reversal relates to remeasured guarantee liabilities and is non-cash; about Rs. 18 crore fresh impairment in Q1. Of the Rs. 130 crore envisaged, Rs. 65 crore remains, to be given over time as required. Asset sales expected but no value quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone debt as of 30 June and seasonal rise in short-term debt once crushing starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term debt about Rs. 980 crore at 30 June versus about Rs. 1,250 crore at 31 March 2026; long-term about Rs. 150 crore. Short-term debt is linked to working capital and will rise when crushing starts; management aims to reduce feedstock imports and improve the position.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise from about Rs. 51 crore to Rs. 59 crore YoY, and is it a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase due to VSS (voluntary separation scheme) in legacy plants, not CPG capability building. One-off in one plant so far, with more VSS intended to cut fixed costs.

qa_highlights.question: Sugar: will the company favour sugar over ethanol given high sugar prices, and what is ethanol capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said producing more sugar makes sense at current prices, with a base sugar volume maintained for customers. Distillery capacity is 582 KLPD (about 18 crore litres), of which about 120 KLPD is grain-based. Switching is margin-driven, but OMC supply commitments carry penalties per litre if undelivered.

risks_watch: Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh cane availability and recovery: crush expected flat to about 5% lower; Karnataka monsoon yields in late August and September are critical for the season.

Short-term debt will rise again when crushing starts; working capital discipline and feedstock import timing are key to the March 2027 debt reduction target.

500126|2026-03.headline: P&G Health FY26 sales rose 16% to close to ₹1,400 crore and PAT rose 30% to ₹327 crore, with volume growth at mid-single digits.

Growth was attributed to the Integrated Growth Strategy, three FY26 innovations (Livogen Iron Gummies, Neurobion Nerve Pain Relief Cream, Evion L5000), and expanded pharmacy coverage of about 30,000 added pharmacies and HCPs. qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew in FY26, with Nepal at 3X and Sri Lanka at high single digits, driven by consumption, availability, detailing and launches such as Neurobion Forte and Evion Forte. No export figure in rupees was given.

The Board cut the dividend payout from 140% to 90%, subject to shareholder approval. Management guided to about 7 lakh tons of pipe dispatches and 13-14% EBITDA margin in FY27, with recovery expected from Q3 FY27.

EBITDA rose 17.2% with margin at 20.2%, and PAT excluding exceptional items rose about 1%, while full-year PAT grew 15%. Beauty & Cosmetics grew 30% and Oral Care recovered to 10% growth. Management said the Middle East crisis is raising raw material and logistics costs, which it expects to fully pass through, and it announced a proposed merger with Indovida.

500135|2026-06.headline: EPL Q1 FY27 revenue grew 25.3% (20% underlying ex pass-through) with EBITDA margin at 18.8%; revenue guidance raised to high teens.
500135|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue growth of 25.3%, or 20% underlying excluding pass-through of higher raw material prices, with EBITDA up 15.2% and margin at 18.8% (19.6% underlying). Reported PAT fell 1.4% while PBT rose 10%, which management attributed to a low base-year effective tax rate and phasing. Working capital rose roughly INR 180 crore in the quarter, mainly inventory, which management linked to raw material price inflation and safety stock. Revenue growth guidance was raised from early double digits to high teens for the next few quarters, with the 20% underlying EBITDA margin target held. Europe margins contracted on operational issues and transitional costs, and the Indovida merger received CCI approval but is still pending final approval.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~15.5% adjusted EBITDA margin sustainable, and what is steady-state margin?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ELITe contribution and timing?

500136|2026-06.headline: Ester Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA up 103% to INR58.9 crore, margin 13.3% vs 8.3%, PAT INR18.6 crore vs loss INR7.2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 run-rate be sustained for the remaining three quarters, and were there one-off gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged an other income component and said it was one-time; it expects sustainable good earnings for the next 6 to 8 quarters on supply-demand balance and stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will drive the INR2,000-2,200 crore revenue goal and how will margins evolve over 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are price (global prices expected to hold above the last 2-3 years), higher utilisation in films, specialty polymers and rPET, a rising share of high-priced specialty products, and operational efficiency. Management said it should reach the target in 2 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 spreads and the premium on value-added products; will spreads hold through year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads for 12-micron corona commodity film were INR28-30 per kg in Q1. VAS products carry a premium of INR25 or more, with offline coated products higher; spreads are holding in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What VAS contribution can be expected by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said VAS could reach up to 35% of the portfolio by the exit quarter of FY27, versus 29% in Q1 and a 50-60% target over 2 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did rPET volumes fall sequentially and when will external sales pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it temporary: internal rPET demand for packaging films rose, so external sales dipped. External sales are expected to recover from September, with a larger effect in October to December.

qa_highlights.question: Will ELITe face competition, given other players are already building textile-to-textile capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued the market is large, that its technology handles polyester-cotton blends and low-cost feedstock that competitors cannot, and that Loop has more than 10 years of work and contracts 1.5 years ahead of commissioning. All ELITe output is to be exported, and management agreed a premium is likely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Specialty Polymers and its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to flat to single-digit growth in FY27, with a pipeline maturing in H2, and a 20% plus CAGR over 3 to 5 years. Margins may normalise in percentage terms, but absolute EBITDA and EBIT should grow from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the other income split, cash balance, debt repayment and JV funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of about INR9.8 crore comprised treasury income of about INR3 crore, FD and investment interest of about INR3.5 crore, and FX gain of about INR1 crore, with the rest balance. Gross debt is INR720-722 crore, targeted to fall by INR100 crore to about INR620 crore by year-end. Cash is about INR235 crore, of which about INR140 crore is earmarked for the JV. ELITe debt will sit at JV level.

500144|2026-06.headline: Finolex Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR 2,013 crore and PAT 59% to INR 221 crore, helped by a temporary communication-cable margin spike near 30%.
500144|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR 2,013 crore, with PBT of INR 277 crore (up about 62%) and PAT of INR 221 crore (up about 59%). PBT margin expanded to 13.4% from 11.8% and PAT margin to 10.7% from 9.6%. Electrical cables drove growth on volume and price, while communication cables margins were lifted by low-cost opening fiber inventory that management said will normalise. Copper rod revenue collapsed to INR 8 crore as the rod plant shut on LPG shortage.

segments.name: Electrical cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,767 crore, up about 47%. Automotive, battery, flexible, solar and agricultural cables grew high double digits in volume; building wire grew low single digits in volume as channel destocked. Management said domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable.

segments.name: Communication cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 176 crore, up about 62% from INR 109 crore, with margin close to 30%. Volumes up about 30%; INR 30-40 crore of the revenue was exports to the US and Europe. Management expects margins to normalise to low double digits by year-end as opening inventory is consumed.

segments.name: Copper rod
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 8 crore vs INR 403 crore a year ago; rod plant shut for the quarter due to continued restriction on LPG availability.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Described as a weak link: fans were short of commercial LPG and conduit pipes short of PVC. Target of INR 5 billion FMEG revenue by FY28 reiterated, though the season was largely lost.

guidance_outlook: Communication cable margin expected to normalise; management still sees double-digit margins, likely low double digits, at year-end if demand holds.
Fiber draw capacity to rise from 4 million km to 8 million km by September 2026 (end of Q2), directly rather than in two phases.
Cabling capacity to rise from 8 million to 10 million km, with a longer timeline than the draw expansion.
Preform (100 metric ton) plant expected to stabilise in the next couple of months; management expects it to be fully functional from the September quarter. Phase 2 preform doubling under review.
FY27 capex unchanged at about INR 300 crore.
FMEG target of INR 5 billion by FY28 still intact per management.
capex_capacity: Fiber draw capacity: moving from 4 to 8 million km in one phase, completion by September 2026; original plan was 4 to 6 then 6 to 8.
Preform plant of 100 metric tons, equivalent to about 4 million km of fiber; the balance of 8 million km requires bought-in preform. Phase 2 expansion will be decided later.
Cabling capacity: one plant full, the other about three-quarters utilised; expansion to 10 million km.
FY27 capex about INR 300 crore, unchanged.
Management confirmed R&D and capex steps for data-centre-grade cables, with no details given.
demand_pricing: Fiber prices (G.652.D): about USD 5-6/km in December 2025, peaked at USD 17-18, now settling at USD 11-13/km; premium fiber sold up to USD 50/km.
Communication cable demand is driven by data-centre and AI build-outs; long-term contracts are over half of communication revenue and were repriced in late June 2026.
Electrical cables: about 60% construction, with automotive cables above 14% of the mix in Q1; LV and HV cables about 7-8% of the mix.
Electrical cable price hike of about 3% taken in May 2026 amid copper at about INR 14,000 per kg level; channel inventory was lower at quarter end.
Domestic fiber consumption about 25 million km per year vs China at 400 million km plus; management sees 50-60 million km potential.
Germanium tetrachloride supply is restricted with long lead times; supply covers the calendar year, with no multi-year contracts available.
BharatNet: no update; winners waiting given high prices.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are EBITDA margins, and how much of the expansion is one-off versus mix or copper pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gains came from optic fiber opportunities that may not recur, so management is conservative on them. Domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable; communication margins will fall as old raw material is used up, to low double digits by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What fiber prices are prevailing and how do they compare with December 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: G.652.D went from USD 5-6/km in December 2025 to USD 17-18, and is now settling at USD 11-13/km. Management declined to forecast further movement.

qa_highlights.question: How much of communication cable revenue is exports and to which geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 35-40 crore of the communication revenue was exports, mainly to the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 100 MT preform plant lift margins by about 100 bps once it is fully functional?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see margins improving from here and called 100 bps stretching it, given that elevated prices may not last.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach about INR 300 crore per quarter from fiber?
qa_highlights.answer: At USD 11/km on 8 million km a year, fiber-only sales would be about USD 88 million, or about INR 250-260 crore; cabling adds 20-30% value on top, so INR 300 crore is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG outlook and does the INR 5 billion FY28 target still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed LPG shortages for fans and PVC shortages for conduit pipes; the target of INR 5 billion by FY28 remains.

risks_watch: Communication cable margin of about 30% is temporary; normalisation to low double digits as low-cost inventory runs out.
Fiber supply is tight: preform and germanium are restricted, with preform sourcing still partly external and contracts about a year long.
Input cost volatility from LPG, helium, PVC and fuel after Middle East disruption; supply chain risk to the copper rod plant.
Export revenue depends on episodic opportunities; management cannot give a repeatable export mix.
Preform contract repricing could raise raw material costs once older contracts reset.
FMEG remains weak; catching up on the lost fan and pipe season is uncertain.

500147|2026-03.headline: Standalone revenue rose 162% YoY to INR2,000 million in Q1 CY26 with EBITDA of INR114 million, while consolidated EBITDA margin was only 1.4%.
500147|2026-03.overview: John Cockerill India reported its first quarter of consolidated results, including China, Belgium and Germany entities from January 2026. Standalone revenue grew 162% YoY to INR2,000 million and standalone EBITDA turned positive at INR114 million (about 5.7% margin), but management attributed margin pressure to hiring costs, a mix shift toward large projects, and one-off integration expenses. Consolidated revenue was INR3.4 billion (+56% YoY) with EBITDA of INR49 million (1.4% margin). Consolidated order book was about INR33 billion and standalone order book about INR13 billion (+101% YoY). Management targets a consolidated EBITDA margin of around 3% now and more than 10% over three years, while fundraising and USA consolidation timing remain undecided.

segments.name: Standalone (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,000 million and EBITDA INR114 million in Q1 CY26; margin dented by hiring upfront costs, a shift to large projects from value-added services, and consolidation one-offs. Management expects margin improvement from next quarter as Q1 and H2 FY25 orders convert.

segments.name: Consolidated (incl. China, Belgium, Germany)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3.4 billion and EBITDA INR49 million (1.4% margin) in first consolidated quarter, hit by integration costs and consolidation adjustments. Order book about INR33 billion, mostly executable over about three years; value services portion 12-18 months.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin currently around 3%, to rise step by step; management aims for more than 10% over the next three years, with mid-path progress expected by start of next year.
Cost restructuring from West to East (India/China) planned over 18 months; benefits expected over 12-18 months.
Margin improvement expected from next quarter as recently won orders start converting.
Value services targeted at 30-35% of mix over the next three to five years.
Management expects new technology (JVD, Volteron) revenue in coming quarters; Volteron has no revenue yet and its commercial strategy is being reshaped.
Rolls coating facility at Taloja expected to be commissioned shortly; capex described as limited for an engineering company.
capex_capacity: Rolls coating facility at Taloja expected to be commissioned shortly, introducing coating capabilities in India with faster turnaround.
Capex described as limited because JCIL is an engineering company; main P&L effect is R&D and new-technology costs, not capex.
Old machines dismantled at Taloja last year to create space for the coating line, generating asset-sale income.
JVD technology still being fine-tuned; revenue expected in coming quarters. Volteron commercialisation expected on a medium-term horizon.
demand_pricing: JSW Steel CGL project order won in the quarter, valued at approximately INR4.4-4.7 billion.
Management expects positive order trend over 24 months, led by India (capacity doubling by 2030) and China, plus growing interest in JVD green-steel technology.

Europe described as a standby market; management expects new EU import quotas to drive demand next year. US seen as a market with the best steel price per ton, with consolidation and Nippon Steel's US Steel purchase expected to drive investment.
Relationship with SAIL under an MoU signed a little over a year ago; management would not disclose details, saying projects are being built up.
Consolidated order book executable mainly over about three years; value services over 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating leverage not show despite record revenue, and why did employee costs rise 34% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited three factors: upfront hiring and organisational realignment costs, a mix shift toward large projects (JSW, Tata) versus value-added services, and one-off consolidation/integration expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated order book executability?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the approximately INR33 billion is executable over about three years; a smaller value services portion runs 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Post-consolidation margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated EBITDA about 3% currently; target above 10% over three years, with mid-path progress by the start of next year, via a West-to-East cost shift over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Fundraise deferred? Promoter stake and USA consolidation timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Board still exploring funding options with another board meeting planned in 2-3 weeks. Promoter stake to stay at current level for now. USA consolidation faces technical issues; target by end of year or a slight postponement.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition price versus revenue for the European, Chinese and US businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total SPA price is around EUR50 million including USA; the analyst's arithmetic was disputed and the discussion was taken offline.

qa_highlights.question: Composition of other income of about INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly interest income plus sale of old assets and scrap; Q1 other income stated as INR93 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone and consolidated margins converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects convergence through moving activity to India/China, converting R&D into orders, and structural streamlining over 12-18 months; iron and steel (upstream) has no contract in hand yet.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 1.4% versus standalone margin of about 5.7%; delivery of the targeted ~3% and later 10%+ depends on cost realignment.
JVD and Volteron R&D costs are running ahead of revenue; Volteron IP sits with the promoter and strategy is under discussion.
Fundraise plan deferred; board decision expected in 2-3 weeks. Promoter stake change possible.
USA business consolidation timing uncertain (end of year or postponement) with technical issues.
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and European energy costs may cause short-term volatility.
Transcript shows analyst disputes over acquisition pricing and other income, taken offline; watch for disclosure follow-up.

500147|2026-06.headline: John Cockerill India Q2 CY26 standalone revenue up 82% YoY to ~INR149 crore; consolidated INR299 crore (+18% YoY), order book ~INR4,500 crore.
500147|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 82% YoY to about INR149 crore and consolidated revenue reached about INR299 crore, up 18% YoY, but both fell sequentially as Q1 benefited from closing older projects. Management attributed weaker Q2 margins to upfront costs on newly started projects, organisation-building spend and one-time consolidation costs after the China, Germany and Belgium entities were brought under the listed company. Order wins of about INR1,200 crore in the quarter lifted the consolidated order book to about INR4,500 crore (standalone about INR2,200 crore). Management expects revenue and margins to build in H2 as new projects ramp, though it gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Expected marginally lower in next two quarters

segments.commentary: Service revenue in Q2 about one-third of Q1; management says lower because project progress was slower, not lack of orders, and services margins remain strong.

rows.why: Utilisation is about 95% overall and JNPT is near 100%, so a further 60,000 kL JNPT phase (combined capex about INR100 cr) is planned for next year and ammonia/LPG bullets (INR450-500 cr) are under discussion with 5-6 acres of JNPT land set aside.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not raise guidance; no exceptional rental demand was taken from the war-related supply disruption, and the JNPT rental reset compresses LST margins for 2-3 years.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Expansion timing has slipped-risk noted by management (conflicting statements on timing), receivables over 6 months are rising on EPC credit terms, and the Goa terminal is near zero utilisation with INR10-12 lakh/month holding cost.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Goa petroleum modification (blended petrol approvals, capex about INR2 cr) is set to start after monsoon and finish by 31 March 2027, but no contract is signed yet; Singapore chemical-basket subsidiary is at a preliminary stage.

rows.label: JSW port EPC order INR175 cr
rows.why: Engineering is complete on the INR175 cr JSW order with margins described as higher single digit, though executed value was not disclosed and groundwork only starts after monsoon.

rows.label: Receivables over 6 months rising on EPC credit terms
rows.why: Management says retention money is paid only after one year and there is no bad debt issue, but the receivables build-up is a drag on working capital.

rows.label: Visakhapatnam LOI on hold
rows.why: Progress is on hold due to a dispute between a prior plot holder and the Visakhapatnam port, so no new terminal is expected in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on the JNPT expansion and 5-6% annual rental escalation but defensive on the margin compression, receivables and Goa; analysts pushed on margin recovery, utilisation and Goa, and several answers were vague or conflicting on timing.

500153|2026-09.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast to divest JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms plus Daund rail for INR1,154 crore, with INR500 crore due around January 2027.
500153|2026-09.overview: Management, on an investor call held October 7, 2026, outlined the sale of the LST (liquid storage tank) businesses at JNPA, Goa and Cochin, together with the JNPA-linked Daund rail business, for INR1,154 crore plus an exit-linked consideration. Payment is staged: about INR500 crore by January 2027, about INR300 crore by March 2027, and the balance INR354 crore over 12 to 18 months tied to port approvals and tank commissioning. Of the first INR500 crore, about INR190-200 crore goes to tax and bank-limit closure and about INR200 crore to a buyback and special dividend, with INR100 crore for chemical expansion and EPC book growth. Management guided chemical PAT to about INR18 crore in FY26 rising to INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years, and EPC PAT to about INR150 crore by around FY30. Much of the Q&A probed the rationale for exiting the higher-margin LST business and the lack of quarter-wise numbers.

financial_highlights.metric: Divestment consideration (JNPA, Goa, Cochin LST + Daund rail)
financial_highlights.change: plus further consideration linked to investor exit valuation (not quantified)

financial_highlights.metric: Planned shareholder return from first tranche (buyback + special dividend)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR5 crore PAT in FY24 (full year)
management says profit up ~1,000% over last 2 years
management now expects above INR200 crore

segments.name: LST (liquid tank farm) – divested
segments.commentary: JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms and JNPA-linked Daund rail are being sold for INR1,154 crore. JNPA expected in books until about Dec 2026/Jan 2027, with Cochin and Goa removed gradually over the next calendar year. Company retains a small stake in a Kandla terminal, described as insignificant; a non-compete applies.

segments.name: Chemical (benzoic acid, sodium benzoate)
segments.commentary: Two plants, each about 1,000 tons/month; utilisation about 70-80%. One plant is being doubled, with completion expected July 2027. REACH certification obtained for UK and EU; orders over 600 tons received, expected to reach about 2,000 tons/year. Management targets chemical PAT of INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years.

segments.name: EPC (tankage, pipeline, petroleum)
segments.commentary: Order book expected to be about INR500-600 crore next year, with EPC revenue of about INR250 crore per annum from FY28 onward per management. Targeted 5% share of a INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum-related EPC opportunity implies about INR150 crore PAT. EBITDA margin assumption 7-8% on a conservative basis, PAT margin basis not clearly specified.

guidance_outlook: Chemical PAT expected to be INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years (from INR18 crore in FY26); management says chemical profitability to rise 3-4x in 4-5 years.
EPC PAT of about INR150 crore targeted by around 2030, assuming 5% share of INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum EPC pipeline.
Total PAT target of about INR210 crore in 3-5 years versus about INR70 crore currently; FY28 PAT growth target of 15-20% YoY.
Chemical revenue to rise about 20-25% in the year after capacity commissioning and about 70-80% in the following year, per management.
Debt expected to stay at minimum; company does not expect to need significant bank debt, although bank limits are needed for guarantees.
Further tranche proceeds to be used for expansion or shareholder returns, decided by the board based on capex visibility.
capex_capacity: Chemical capacity doubling at one plant (of two, about 1,000 tons/month each), targeted completion July 2027.
Stage 1 capex across chemical and EPC of not more than about INR150 crore.
New agro and specialty derivative plants planned with technology and licence partners; to be funded later, with back-to-back buyback arrangements with customers under discussion.
Management says no balance capex remains on the JNPA port asset, and that about 43 tanks are under construction at JNPA (per management answer on LST growth capex).
Capex to continue over the next 1-2 years; first stage expected to be complete by FY28.
demand_pricing: REACH certification enabled UK and EU exports; over 600 tons of orders received.
Management says the chemical business profit grew from INR5 crore (FY24) to INR15-16 crore (FY25), INR18 crore (FY26) with turnover broadly flat.
Crude-linked raw material costs: management says it passes through fluctuations to customers but cannot rule out margin impact at high crude prices.
Chemical EBITDA margin cited by analyst at 11-12%; management expects to sustain or improve it without a firm number.
EPC contract wins include KKR (about INR300 crore), GACL/NALCO JV pipeline, ANA Oleo, Allana, Adani MPL and Jindal projects.

qa_highlights.question: Deepesh Sancheti (Maanya Finance): what is the timeline for the next INR300 crore tranche, and how will EPC working capital be funded after debt is repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance INR354 crore spread over 12-18 months, milestone-linked to port approvals and tank commissioning. Bank guarantee lines used for EPC will be temporarily replaced with deal funds and reinstated; management says sufficient cash will come from tranches and PAT for EPC working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Romil Savaliya (CJ Shah Family Office): why has chemical top line been flat for years, and what is changing in EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on profitability, not turnover: chemical PAT went from INR5 crore in FY24 to about INR15-16 crore in FY25 and INR18 crore in FY26 on similar turnover. EPC is being moved from a support role for LST to an independent division targeting about INR150 crore PAT in 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Nishita (Sapphire Capital): what is the rationale for divesting the higher-margin LST business, and what is chemical capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rationale cited as projected cost increases and market movement over 2-3 years, plus the value offered by the buyer, which management said it judged fair. Chemical has two plants of about 1,000 tons/month each; one is being doubled by July 2027; utilisation is about 70-80%. Q1 chemical PAT of INR6 crore is chemical only, and EPC quarterly turnover was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavesh Patel (Patel Investments): will the 40-45% shareholder return apply to later tranches, and what is FY28 PAT expectation and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The buyback and special dividend apply to the first tranche only; later tranches depend on capex visibility and board decisions. Management targets 15-20% PAT growth YoY into FY28 from about INR70 crore. No significant bank debt is expected, though bank limits are needed for guarantees.

qa_highlights.question: Saurabh (Mangalam): is there a non-compete, will the company re-enter LST, and how exposed is chemical margin to crude?
qa_highlights.answer: A standard non-compete applies; the Kandla stake is a carve-out and insignificant; no plan to return to LST near term. Crude pass-through is attempted but margin impact cannot be ruled out at high crude.

qa_highlights.question: Prateek Kothari (CRK Stock Broking): what is the first tranche's use of funds and what is the chemical top-line ballpark?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the first INR500 crore, about INR200 crore goes to shareholders, about INR190-200 crore to tax and bank-limit closure, and the balance to chemical and EPC growth. Chemical FY26 revenue was about INR180 crore, now expected above INR200 crore; revenue expected to rise 20-25% in the year after commissioning and 70-80% in the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Krupa Sanjay Desai (Electrum Capital): what EPC revenue and margin are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: EPC revenue this year about INR50-60 crore given seasonality; about INR250 crore per year from next year with KKR and other contracts. Management cited a general expectation of about 10% margin but planned at 7-8%, specified as PAT; the INR150 crore EPC PAT is expected by about 2030.

risks_watch: Timing of the INR500 crore (about January 2027) and INR300 crore (March 2027) tranches depends on port approvals and shareholder approval; the INR354 crore balance is milestone-linked with no fixed date.
Q1 FY27 chemical PAT of INR6 crore (about 10% margin on INR60 crore revenue) is well above the FY26 run-rate; management says it aims to sustain it, but gave no firm guidance.
Loss of JNPA LST earnings from around the March 2027 quarter, with Cochin and Goa rolling off over the next calendar year; the group's profit base will shift to chemical and EPC.
Chemical capacity doubling at one plant targeted for July 2027; execution and ramp-up timing is key to the 20-25% and 70-80% revenue step-ups.
Crude-linked raw material costs could compress chemical margins; management cannot rule this out.

EPC targets (order book INR500-600 crore next year, INR2,500-3,000 crore in 4-5 years, 5% of INR70,000 crore pipeline) are unquantified attempts; working capital needs post-debt repayment are unclear.
Quarterly EPC turnover and profit were not provided; management will share on request, so segment disclosure remains limited.
key_quotes: So, combined with the chemical PAT of about INR60 crores and the EPC PAT about INR150 crores, you're looking at your company going in the next 3 to 4, 5 years to about INR210 crores of PAT, which is currently at 70.
And one important thing of about the buyback that you should know is that the promoters will not be participating in it.
But I cannot commit or I cannot speculate that no margins will ever be hit on how crude behaves suddenly, but we have -- I believe, enough systems in place to sustain any reasonable fluctuations.
So, capex will keep happening through the next 1 or 2 years continuously.
500153|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the growth outlook for chemical and EPC, with an emphasis on shareholder returns. Cautious and evasive on specific numbers and timelines: management repeatedly declined to speculate on future figures, gave port-approval timing only as "expected", and did not answer the ownership question about CJ Shah family stake.

500165|2026-03.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 7.6% and PBDIT up 21%; management guides to 13-14% margin and high-single-digit decorative price increases.
500165|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 7.6% with PBDIT up 21% and PBT before exceptional items up 12.8%, while full-year standalone revenue rose 3.2% and PBDIT 1.2%. Consolidated Q4 PBDIT rose 30.6%. Management attributed the quarter's margin resilience to better mix in both decorative and industrial, and to lower other expenses. Price hikes totalling roughly 2% in March and 5-6% in each subsequent round were taken amid a crude and rupee shock tied to the West Asia crisis. The company said demand has held so far with no volume impact seen, but visibility for FY27 is "wait and watch."

segments.commentary: Management said the decorative volume-value gap was not significant, as low-profit items were deliberately curtailed. Growth in the decorative business was described as mid-single-digit or lower, and new products and super premium emulsions drove better mix. Decorative projects are now about 10%+ of sales, and new businesses (waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finish) are also 10%+ and slightly higher than projects.

segments.name: Industrial - Automotive
segments.commentary: Auto coatings grew close to double digits in Q4, with passenger vehicle demand healthy and a long waiting list cited by customers. Two-wheeler demand grew at high double digits, and commercial vehicles and tractors grew at double digits.

segments.name: Industrial - General and Powder
segments.commentary: Overall industrial grew slightly higher single digits in Q4 per management. Powder coatings returned to mid-single-digit growth with a good channel sales performance.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated the historical EBITDA margin band of 13-14% for FY27 on both consolidated and standalone bases, with an endeavour to reach the higher end. FY26 was said to have been within that range.

Decorative price increases: about 2% in late March, then 5-6% each on 10 April, 21 April and 11 May, for a net higher-single-digit increase as of now. Aniruddha Joshi's question put the cumulative effective hike in the low teens; management did not dispute it.
Industrial channel prices were revised effective mid-April. OE price increases have been granted in part, with negotiation timing slightly delayed but effective-from dates protecting margins.

Management said a crude price of about USD 100 would be manageable with current price hikes. It expects to live with the inflation for about 6 months, with a possible second-half reversal if conditions improve.
Price increases could be scaled back through schemes if deflation arrives. Management said dealer incentives were adjusted in line with the price hikes.
capex_capacity: Capex is described as normal and in line with prior years.
Powder and industrial liquid coatings are running at about 70-75% utilisation, with sufficient capacity.
Management aims to grow performance coatings at double digits, tied to infrastructure spend and the expansion plan outlined at the February strategy session.
Paint Plus retail format has replaced NXTGEN Shoppe and Shop-in-Shop, with about 250+ stores opened.
Paint-as-a-service is present in more than 250 cities; the Illuminati architect and designer programme in 45+ cities; the painter programme covers more than 1.2 lakh painters.
demand_pricing: Decorative demand has improved since November, with an uptick across the last five months. Management said there was no volume impact from the price hikes so far.

Management said the market has seen a constant uptick since November, and that new entrants and unorganised players also took price hikes in January and February. Management expects unorganised-player impact to show up over 3-6 months, mainly in low-end products such as primers.
Management said that for the Q4 mix improvement, new products were a large contributor and super premium emulsions performed well. Market share was gained in focused T2 and T3 towns across India.
Dealer incentives are typically higher in April as a stocking month. Management said they are being adjusted with the price increases, in line with normal industry practice.
Auto demand is strong, with OEMs reporting long waiting lists. Demand in infrastructure, appliances and other industrial segments is described as standard and normal.
Management said the company is not chasing market share at any cost, and is focusing on profitable growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth came from decorative versus industrial, and what was the volume and mix contribution in decorative?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto was up close to double digits and industrial overall was up slightly higher single digits. Decorative was mid-single digits or lower. Mix improved in both segments, which lifted contribution and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes will sit in Q1, and how are B2B and industrial price negotiations going?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative hikes were about 2% in March, then 5-6% each on 10 April, 21 April and 11 May, for a net higher-single-digit increase. Industrial channel prices were revised effective mid-April. OE price increases have been granted in part, with a slight delay in timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is 13-14% margin guidance for FY27 achievable, and does it assume current raw material costs persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 13-14% band as the endeavour, with an aim for the higher end. It expects raw material prices to stabilise after a temporary panic-driven spike, and believes conditions should improve in the second half.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall about 150 bps as a percentage of sales year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a drop in fuel costs and fixed-cost leverage, plus ongoing cost and spend efficiency. It said there was no full-year true-up in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for decorative and industrial demand, and what would happen if crude corrects or stays high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said auto demand is strong and deco trends are stable through April. If inflation persists, further price increases are possible. If deflation arrives, schemes would be adjusted first, with price cuts only if the softening is sustained. It said a crude price of about USD 100 would be manageable with current hikes.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales do decorative projects and new businesses represent?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative projects are about 10%+ of sales. New businesses (waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finish) are also 10%+, slightly higher than projects.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation from crude and rupee depreciation. Management said price hikes will lag, so near-term margin pressure is possible; the sensitivity to 5-10% input cost increases was not quantified.
Management expects demand to be a wait-and-watch as the West Asia crisis and supply-chain disruption continue. A prolonged crisis could hit consumption through fuel and other costs.
Possible volume impact from price increases in the coming quarters, and inventory-led sales in April distorting secondary numbers.
Competitive intensity from new entrants and a delayed price increase among B2B and industrial customers.
Diwali timing is late this year, which could shift advertising and promotional spend across Q1 and Q2.
Other expenses fell about 150 bps as a percentage of sales YoY, which may not be sustainable if fuel costs normalise.
500165|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on execution and pricing discipline, with management stressing profitable growth and deliberately avoiding market-share chasing. It was cautious and evasive on FY27 demand, auto price quantum, and the timing of raw-material relief, repeatedly calling forecasts "very difficult" and "a crystal guessing" exercise.

500165|2026-06.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 10.2% with PBDIT up 7.7%; management targets 13-14% margins for FY27 despite input cost pressure.
500165|2026-06.overview: Standalone net revenue grew 10.2% YoY, PBDIT 7.7% and PBT 5.1%; consolidated revenue rose 9.8%, PBDIT 8.3% and PBT 5.8%. Decorative value growth was high single digit with volume growth low single digit, as the company deliberately shed low-margin volume. Industrial coatings grew double digit in value, but price increases lagged, with about 5% realised so far at customer level. Management announced a INR601 crore capacity expansion across automotive, powder coating and resin, spread over about 2 to 2.5 years, and kept its margin ambition intact.

financial_highlights.metric: Industrial price hike achieved so far
financial_highlights.change: Still under negotiation; effective ask from 1 April

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth high single digit; volume growth low single digit as premium mix was prioritised over low-margin, high-volume products. Economy grew mid-single digit and super premium grew double digit. Margins were stable YoY despite higher ad spend.

segments.name: Industrial (Automotive, Performance Coatings, Powder)
segments.commentary: Value growth double digit. Automotive and powder coating saw strong growth; liquid performance coatings led by construction equipment, drums and coil coating. Gross contribution fell about 1.3% as price increases lagged cost inflation.

segments.name: Auto Refinish
segments.commentary: Growth was flat. Management cited notable premium PU body shop wins and a transition from solvent-borne to waterborne systems that is on plan.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and premium wood finish
segments.commentary: Construction chemicals grew double digit; premium wood finish grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 margin ambition of 13-14% is retained, subject to the geopolitical situation not worsening.
Q2 decorative price increase of about 3% expected to flow through; industrial price increase of another 3-5% expected in Q2.

Q2 will carry high-cost inventory and a seasonally weaker quarter, but management expects to maintain margins versus last year's same quarter, helped by sourcing, value engineering and formula optimisation.
Medium term, aim to reach the higher end of the 14%+ margin range within 2-3 years through premiumisation, industrial growth and fixed-cost leverage.
Expected ROCE on incremental capex is towards 18%, with per-KL capex on new capacity lower than the current programme.
Management expects a slightly better festive season, with Diwali in November giving October more painting days in Q3.
capex_capacity: INR601 crore capex for automotive, powder coating and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur.
Capacity addition of 66,000 KL per year plus resin capacity of close to 10,000 metric tons per year.
The INR601 crore outlay is spread over about 2 to 2.5 years; normal annual capex is INR150-200 crore.
Part of the spend is front-loaded infrastructure, so future incremental capacity will be cheaper per KL.
Industrial capacity is expected to be full in about 2 years, requiring the addition.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity in decorative remains high, with new entrants still testing the market; no change in pricing discipline, dealer incentives or scheme intensity versus last year or Q4 exit.
Network expansion: 1,700 dealers added in Q1; network additions targeted at 5-10% a year.
Industrial price hike to date about 5%, with more discussions expected to add in Q2.
Solvent inflation was sharp, but solvent inventory is only about 15 days, which made it hard to hedge.
Some free-product schemes continue in certain markets, not specific to the company's focus towns.
Input cost inflation peaked in June and has since eased slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Is decorative volume growth in line with the market, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is not below competitors, but the company is deliberately avoiding low-margin, high-volume products. Competitive intensity remains high and is expected to persist through this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat YoY when the market leader expanded margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial price increases lag by 1-2 quarters, so the price-cost gap hit industrial gross contribution by about 1.3%. Ad spend rose in Q1 but was offset by mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value growth split in decorative and industrial?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative value growth is high single digit and industrial is double digit. Q1 mix is heavier on decorative, and the mix changes each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the capex and what returns are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: INR601 crore over about 2-2.5 years on top of normal capex of INR150-200 crore per year. Management expects ROCE towards 18%, with lower per-KL capex on new capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing growth in Q1 and Q2 on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated pricing was about 4-5% in Q1. Q2 adds about 3% in decorative and another 3-5% in industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new resin capacity is backward integration for automotive paint, but raw material integration is not on the card. The Kansai Group's global network can supply intermediates as needed.

Rupee depreciation may lift import costs; industrial price negotiations may still be incomplete in Q2.
Decorative volume growth is low single digit, and the company is ceding share in low-margin segments.
Ad and dealer investment is rising, and margin benefit depends on whether premium mix gains come through.
