tone.note: Management was confident on pig iron pricing, castings demand and capacity additions, but cautious and wait-and-watch on tubes given Chinese dumping; analysts probed the other-expenses jump, green-power savings, Q1 margin trajectory, and the pass-through on alloy steel, which management left vague.

500249|2026-06.headline: KSB H1 FY27 revenue INR 12,920 mn with weak Q1 sales (2–3% growth); management targets double-digit FY growth on H2 export recovery.
500249|2026-06.overview: Management presented at an institutional investor meet (held 19 Aug 2026) covering H1 FY27 (April–June 2026 quarter as described in the call). H1 revenue from sales was INR 12,920 mn, EBITDA INR 1,465 mn and PBT INR 1,279 mn. Management attributed the subdued quarter to Middle East export shipments held up by the geopolitical situation, supply-chain constraints on castings after gas availability issues, a delayed KUSUM 2.0 solar scheme, and slow project-pump order inflow. Management expects a much better H2 and aims for double-digit growth, though it flagged NPCIL test-bed delays on nuclear and continued fixed-price margin pressure.

financial_highlights.change: Management said Q1 sales grew only 2–3% over the prior period
Well below plan due to KUSUM 2.0 delay
Down from mid-teens levels the analyst cited; management called it temporary

segments.name: Order intake mix
segments.commentary: Standard 51%, Engineered 14%, SupremeServ 16%, Valves about 19% of order intake, per management.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order on hand INR 1,235 crore covering GHAVP 1 and 2, Kaiga 5 and 6 and the Kudankulam safety package; Shirwal nuclear capacity at 80–90% utilisation with a new shed adding about 7,000 sq m (about 20% plant capacity).

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Margin fell to single digits in H1 on commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales; management expects a return to double-digit margins.

segments.name: SupremeServ
segments.commentary: Management targets 25–30% aftermarket share in India (group target 35%); business growing about 15% per annum.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar pumps are 5–7% of current order book versus a 10–12% target; Maharashtra tender orders expected to help in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Goal is double-digit growth for the full year; management said 15–17% average growth over time is achievable (10–15% volume, about 15% value).
H2 expected to be much better, with export shipments recovering from Middle East disruption and supply chain now around 85–90% stable.
Nuclear GHAVP testing expected to start in September 2026 once NPCIL resolves test-bed issues; first pump needs about 500 hours of testing (2–3 months), with up to six pumps a year possible.
EBITDA target of 13–14% reiterated; gross margin under pressure on fixed-price project business, partly offset by internal cost reduction.
Export order book about 15% of sales, with a target of 20%.
S/4HANA implementation in H1 of next year, with group cost allocation expected in FY28 OpEx; amount not yet decided.
Capex of about INR 80–120 crore per year (sustenance plus growth).
capex_capacity: Shirwal plant is about 115,000 sq m (15,000 sq m added with recently bought land); a new shed of about 7,000 sq m adds about 20% capacity.
Shirwal capacity about 1,200–1,300 pumps across energy, oil and gas and nuclear combined.
Nuclear: first indigenous pump made in 2025, under testing at NPCIL test bed in 2026; ISO-19443 certified.
Reciprocating pumps being developed under BP&CL technology; EIL approval in process, requiring a running pump supplied within 12 months.
Split-case pump of 10,000 cubic metres per hour under development for export and river-linking projects.
demand_pricing: Management sees energy (thermal, nuclear, renewable) and water/wastewater infrastructure as main growth drivers; supercritical thermal boiler circulation pump win broke an import jinx.
Project market (oil and gas, petrochemical) slowed; Dangote refinery expected to contribute later.
Price increases: foundry costs up 12–15%; KSB standard market price hikes so far single-digit, being phased in.
Export demand hit by Middle East war and earlier US tariffs cancelling some orders; US boiler feed pump orders for gas plants noted.
Data centre: orders from KSB Germany's OEM customers and an international OEM in India for liquid cooling; no size quantified.
Pump content of projects estimated at 3–5% of total project value.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 performance subdued, and how much export was to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the war affecting exports (pumps ready but undelivered) and supply-chain constraints; sales grew only 2–3%, and H2 is expected to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is double-digit growth; nuclear test-bed delay is the main risk, which management sees as low risk. 20% top-line is possible but with peaks.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution and competition for the next primary coolant pump tender?
qa_highlights.answer: GHAVP testing delayed by NPCIL test-bed issues, with testing expected from September; a new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) expected in a few months, and KSB is the approved supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Why valves margin fell to single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales together, and called it temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order intake not improve materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard business growing but new-market entry takes time (fire-fighting, marine, mining); project market, especially oil and gas and petrochemical, slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard cycle is 24–36 months; deliveries to NPCIL around 48 months from order; management confirmed about 4 years from groundbreaking to first supply.

qa_highlights.question: BP&CL run-rate and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: On track but slow due to PSU referencing and tender requirements; medium-term potential INR 40–50 crore a year.

risks_watch: Nuclear: NPCIL test-bed issues delaying GHAVP testing, which could push back deliveries and revenue recognition.
Gross margin pressure from fixed-price project contracts and foundry cost pass-through lag of 3–6 months.
Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation and shipment clearances; export inventory still held at end-June.
Solar: KUSUM 2.0 delay; solar receivables and state-government payment cycle may keep receivable days elevated.
S/4HANA cost allocation from FY28 onwards; amount not yet quantified.
Q2 results should show whether H2 recovery materialises and whether valves margins return to double digits.
500249|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities but defensive on the weak H1; management repeatedly says it expects H2 to recover, with few hard numbers on timing or magnitude.
key_quotes: So, we are looking for a good outlook, not short-term, but long-term.

But we expect a much better half in the second half, because as of today, we see that the issues related to supply chain, of course, have not been fully solved, but it is much better that we have now a bit of consistency in the supply chain after having agreed with them on the revised prices.
Our goal is to have a double -digit growth. This is what we are aiming for.
So I see these as temporary variations.
So whatever you see investment of INR 80 crores, INR 100 crores, INR 120 crores annually, we intend to do that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterates 13-14% EBITDA margin and good double-digit valves margin, but valves fell to single digits in H1 and fixed-price project margins remain under pressure with foundry costs up 12-15% and pass-through lag of 3-6 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Shirwal nuclear capacity is at 80-90% utilisation and a new 7,000 sq m shed adds about 20% plant capacity, under construction, though no commissioning date was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 10-15% volume growth for FY27 but Q1 sales grew only 2-3% and H2 recovery rests on Middle East export shipments and supply stabilisation at 85-90%, with no quantified timeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at INR 80-120 crore a year, with Shirwal nuclear utilisation at 80-90%, but no new plant or board-level capex plan was announced on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 sales growth was 2-3% against a double-digit full-year goal, and management has offered few hard numbers on H2 recovery, so an upgrade looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 growth of 2-3% against a 10-15% volume goal, the NPCIL test-bed delay pushing GHAVP testing to September, and the KUSUM 2.0 delay (solar H1 revenue INR 50-60 crore) all put the double-digit target at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Reciprocating pumps under BP&CL technology await EIL approval needing a running pump within 12 months, and a 10,000 cu m/hr split-case pump is under development, but no launch dates were given.

rows.label: Nuclear primary coolant pump tender (about eight reactors)
rows.why: A new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) is expected in a few months and KSB is the approved supplier, against an order on hand of INR 1,235 crore.

rows.label: Order book growth from H1 order intake
rows.why: H1 FY27 order intake was INR 15,307 mn (excl. Nuclear) and the order book reached INR 27,445 mn in June 2026, with management citing a 14% intake CAGR.

rows.label: Standard market price hikes being phased in
rows.why: Foundry costs are up 12-15% and KSB standard price hikes so far are single-digit and being phased in, with a 3-6 month pass-through lag.

tone.note: Management was confident on nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities and on the double-digit full-year goal, but defensive on the 2-3% Q1 sales growth and vague on H2 timing; analysts pushed on the valves margin drop and nuclear test-bed delays.

500252|2026-03.headline: LMW Q4 FY26 revenue rose to ₹854 crore (vs ₹789 crore a year ago) and TMD order book reached ₹3,300 crore, with ~₹2,300 crore active.
500252|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue rose to ₹3,353 crore from ₹3,137 crore and consolidated profit to ₹195 crore from ₹151 crore, with standalone PBT up 42% to ₹221 crore. Q4 standalone revenue was ₹854 crore, up from ₹767 crore in Q3 and ₹789 crore a year ago. Management said textile machinery (TMD) order intake rose sharply in Q4 as cotton spinners' profitability improved, while the machine tool division grew strongly and ATC revenue reached ₹207 crore. Management flagged rising raw material, logistics and commodity costs across the industry, with no price hikes taken in MTD yet.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹767 crore in Q3 FY26 and ₹789 crore in Q4 FY25
vs ₹440 crore in Q3 and ₹493 crore in Q4 FY25
vs loss of ₹15.64 crore in FY25
one-time, related to new labour code and VRS outgo
vs ₹1,003 crore; ~10% foundry, balance machine tools
vs ₹146 crore; loss ₹32 crore vs profit ₹1.9 crore
vs ₹67 crore; breakeven vs loss ₹6.8 crore

segments.name: TMD (textile machinery)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹1,801 crore (down ~2%) and profit ₹9.75 crore; Q4 revenue ₹485 crore. Order book ₹3,300 crore (about ₹2,300 crore active), all booked in Q4. FY26 sales mix domestic:exports:spares 66:8:26.

segments.name: Machine tool division (MTD)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 25-28% in FY26 to ~₹1,205 crore for machine tools plus foundry (~10% foundry). Management cited ~11.5% margin in Q4 and no price hikes. Customer mix ~50-52% automotive, ~48% non-automotive; capacity headroom of ~20% and utilisation of 70-75%.

segments.name: ATC (aerospace and precision components)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹207 crore (vs ₹169 crore); Q4 revenue ~₹56 crore with segment result ~₹11 crore (close to 20% margin). Order book ~₹360 crore to be executed over 18 months. About 90% of sales are exports; mix is ~78% metallics and ~22% composites.

segments.name: LMW Global and LMW China
segments.commentary: LMW Global FY26 turnover ₹184 crore with ₹32 crore loss and ₹44 crore order book. LMW China FY26 turnover ₹130 crore, breakeven, and ₹120 crore order book.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a much larger offtake of textile machines as cotton spinners' margins improve, but said it is too early to call a hockey-stick recovery like FY22.
ATC capacity additions are expected to start yielding higher turnover in the second half of FY27.
Management expects MTD margins to continue as turnover grows, and said it will invest for growth once utilisation nears 90%.
Management plans a new, larger ATC facility outside the city centre; ATC capex of about ₹150 crore over five years was referenced for infrastructure only, excluding machinery.
Management aims to rebuild exports to about 23-25% of sales over the next three years, from ~8% in FY26 (per the sales mix).
capex_capacity: Textile machinery capacity utilisation is about 50-55%; machine tool utilisation is about 70-75%, with ~20% headroom in MTD even after Q4 shipments.
Capex of over ₹300 crore was spent in the last three years, mainly for machine tool capacity and modernisation; about 50% of FY26 capex went to ATC.
ATC composites utilisation is about 50%, with headroom to grow.
ATC capex is project-specific and tied to order wins; the new facility is planned to be larger than the current one.
The company is considering an investment of up to US$30 million via a UAE holding company, partly for working capital and partly for export growth (GCC presence for two years).
demand_pricing: Management said the textile industry has improved over the last two months, with good cotton yarn spreads, while crude-based synthetics face challenges. Demand is recovering from Bangladesh, China-linked yarn demand and Turkey.
TMD order book of ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4, versus the previous quarter's figure.
No price hikes taken in MTD; margin uplift attributed to operating leverage, with some forex income.
Raw material, logistics, steel, plastics and commodity costs are rising industry-wide; management did not disclose the size of planned price increases.
Import content in machine tools is about 50% of materials, mostly sourced locally in INR, with some USD-linked sourcing.
ATC is about 90% export-driven; customers are Tier-1 aerospace suppliers, and it also supplies ISRO, HAL and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the textile outlook and order pipeline, and the MTD growth and ATC order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Textile order book is ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4. MTD is continuing to grow with automotive at ~50-52%. ATC booked ₹195 crore; its order book of ~₹360 crore is to be executed over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is ATC's business, customer qualification cycle, and profit potential?
qa_highlights.answer: ATC has metallics and composites divisions covering engine parts, sheet metal, structures, assemblies and special processes. It is about 90% export-focused. Management said the ~19 certifications required include NADCAP, ISO and customer-specific ones. It does not disclose growth numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why invest up to US$30 million in a UAE holding company, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds are for working capital, which is under pressure because of geopolitics, and for export growth in GCC markets. It cited turning-centre exports of ~₹20 crore and a target of 23-25% exports over three years. No payback period was given.

qa_highlights.question: How can ROCE improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said textile machinery is cyclical with an ~8-year cycle and the business is at a low point. It said ATC has much better ROCE, MTD will improve, and capex is heavy in textile. Management said it will keep investing through downturns.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book 3,300 crore total with 2,300 crore active? What price hikes are needed to offset raw material costs, and what is the imported content?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: ₹3,300 crore total, ~₹2,300 crore active. Management would not share the size of price increases. Machine tool import content is about 50%, partly sourced locally in INR.

qa_highlights.question: Could ATC scale to ₹1,000 crore in five years, given a ~₹150 crore capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹150 crore figure covers infrastructure only, excluding machinery, and that the new facility could scale beyond ₹300 crore of revenue. It did not give a ₹1,000 crore target.

risks_watch: Volatile crude and geopolitics are hurting synthetic fibre producers and pressuring working capital; banks may limit funding.
Raw material and logistics costs are rising, and availability is a concern (e.g., LPG and some industrial gases); pricing pass-through is unclear.
ATC order book depends on long-term contracts subject to push-outs or pull-ins, and the business is working-capital intensive because raw materials are imported.
Textile recovery may be cyclical and not a sharp rebound; management has not committed to a timeline.
Export contribution fell to ~8% of sales in FY26, against a historical 23-25% target.
500252|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book, MTD margins and ATC growth, but cautious on textile recovery timing and evasive on pricing, customer names, ATC targets and payback. It described the textile cycle as still at a low point.
key_quotes: We have actually got a significant increase in order book compared to the last quarter.
Whether this again would be, you know, a hockey stick recovery kind of what we have seen in 21-22 that is too early to be mentioned.
So, what you're seeing is pure operational the margin which is coming through because of consistently doing upwards of 100 crores or 300 crores per quarter.
But customer names and the projects would be difficult.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: MTD margin was ~11.5% in Q4 and management expects margins to continue as turnover grows via operating leverage, with ATC at close to 20% segment margin, but rising raw material and logistics costs and no price hikes yet cap the upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ATC capacity additions are under construction and management expects them to yield higher turnover in the second half of FY27, with a new larger ATC facility outside the city centre planned, though its timing is not dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: TMD order book reached ₹3,300 crore (about ₹2,300 crore active), all booked in Q4, and management expects much larger textile machine offtake, while ATC order book of ~₹360 crore executes over 18 months; TMD FY26 revenue was down ~2% at ₹1,801 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Machine tool utilisation is only 70-75% with ~20% headroom and textile utilisation is 50-55%, so a near-term MTD capex is not required; however, ATC capex is ongoing (~50% of FY26 capex), a new larger ATC facility is planned, and a up to US$30 million UAE holding company investment is under consideration, so further capex announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Textile order book of ₹3,300 crore and MTD growth of ~25-28% support an upside, but management called the textile recovery too early to call a hockey-stick and gave no FY27 revenue growth figure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rising raw material, logistics and steel costs with no price hikes taken in MTD, plus crude-linked pressure on synthetic fibre customers and tight working capital from geopolitics, could squeeze margins or push out orders.

rows.label: TMD order book ₹3,300 crore (~₹2,300 crore active)
rows.why: Order book of ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4, versus TMD Q4 revenue of ₹485 crore, so roughly 6-7 quarters of revenue at the current run-rate is visible.

rows.label: Export rebuild to 23-25% of sales
rows.why: Exports were ~8% of FY26 sales versus the 23-25% target, and the proposed US$30 million UAE holding company is aimed at GCC export growth, but no payback or timeline was given.

rows.label: New labour code and VRS one-offs
rows.why: Exceptional items of ~₹11.5 crore and ₹1.68 crore were booked in FY26 for the new labour code and VRS, so these are one-time and should not repeat.

tone.note: Management was confident on the ₹3,300 crore TMD order book, MTD margins and ATC growth, but cautious on the timing of textile recovery and evasive on pricing, ATC targets and UAE investment payback; analysts pushed on pricing pass-through and ATC scale.

ATC revenue rose to ₹60 cr and margins improved, partly due to forex. LMW Global and LMW China losses narrowed QoQ, and China turnover fell sharply YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for expansion into six new divisions, including pharma and specialty chemicals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an enabling board resolution covering multiple options (including EV and an advanced technology centre). Nothing is decided yet. Significant decisions will be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How secure is the TMD order book and what is the domestic visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹3,200 cr is secured through 10% deposits. Demand is recovering gradually, with state policies and FTAs as triggers. Cotton spinning margins are good, while synthetics are under strain.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the order book by customer type and project versus unitary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose customer-level detail. The order mix is about 70% projects and 30% unitary machines, against 60:40 in good years.

qa_highlights.question: ATC capacity expansion, margin outlook, and whether forex helped?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~₹150 cr land and building plan is due over 18-24 months. Q1 margin was higher on mix (more assemblies). Forex was a positive, with the ATC margin range at 94-96% after a jump from 85 to 95 last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of USD and EUR appreciation on MTD costs and mitigation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the currency impact is real on MTD and textile costs. Mitigation includes India-sourced parts and price revisions, and ATC and foundry have contractual price-revision clauses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only ~4% YoY while revenue grew ~25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ongoing cost optimisation and a VRS cost booked in the last quarter, with a tight cost belt maintained as ATC, MTD and textile pick up.

qa_highlights.question: Path back to 12-14% MTD EBIT margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Requires turnover growth and higher utilisation on a much larger cost base; no timeline was given.

500252|2026-09.headline: LMW Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 30% to ₹1,153 crore and PBT reached ₹204 crore, with TMD order book near ₹3,400 crore.

PBT was ₹204 crore against ₹93 crore in the prior-year period. Textile Machinery Division (TMD) grew 38% YoY in Q2 to ₹639 crore, while the Machine Tool Division and Foundry H1 turnover rose to ₹794 crore from ₹555 crore. Management was cautious on textile demand because of input cost inflation and supply chain issues, and more positive on machine tools and ATC.

segments.commentary: H1 turnover ₹794 crore, of which Foundry is 9%. Utilisation 75-80%. Management expects around 50% growth this year and says it is adding capacity.

segments.commentary: H1 turnover ₹135 crore (+39%). Utilisation about 70%. Order book about ₹1,000 crore, roughly 70% metallics and 30% composites. Segment margin cited at about 22%.

segments.commentary: LMW Global H1 turnover ₹100 crore with order book about ₹163 crore; LMW China H1 turnover ₹36 crore with order book about ₹128 crore. Capex for the year is planned to be broadly in line with depreciation, with some assets to come in on lease.

Management said it will take only orders it can execute, adding capacity to match, because contracts carry penalty clauses.
capex_capacity: MTD: capacity expansion of about 10% on a base of 6,750 machines, with ₹10 crore investment; this is a repurposed existing unit for assembly and is described as a statutory third-unit filing. Management says it will expand further at 80-85% utilisation.
MTD mix: about 76% turning centres and 23-24% machining centres; machining centres are growing faster.
ATC: the ₹150 crore investment is yet to be deployed. Management cites an asset-turn rule of thumb of about 1:1 to 1:1.3 (turnover to investment).
TMD utilisation about 60%; ATC about 70%; MTD 75-80%.

TMD is on fixed-price contracts with no current price pass-through, though a price discussion is active and VAVE cost programmes are under way.
TMD order book about ₹3,400 crore; net order inflow up about ₹200 crore in the quarter; about 70% of orders are project orders.
MTD: order inflow is consistent. Demand is driven by China+1 and machine upgrades. Auto is still a little over 50% of MTD sales, with defence, EMS and tooling expanding.
Indian machine tool market about 17,000-18,000 machines and about $2-2.5 billion by value. Imports are about 40-45% by volume and 50-55% by value, and are declining as domestic makers grow.
Lakshmi Auto Winder: launched and sold to a few southern customers, with ramp-up expected next year. Market is roughly ₹1,500 crore-plus, since winding is about 25-30% of spinning mill capex.
Management said export markets like Bangladesh and Turkey are challenged, and overseas losses reflect low topline. ATC is 90% export historically; domestic defence is now being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: ATC capacity, peak revenue from current and planned capex, and commissioning timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 70%. The asset-turn rule of thumb is 1:1 to 1.3. No timeline has been given for the new investment, which will be announced at an appropriate time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for TMD EBITDA margin, given the textile tailwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tailwind is more apt for MTD. TMD is cautious because of cost inflation and supply chain issues. There is no price pass-through yet, and VAVE is under way.

qa_highlights.question: MTD capacity expansion of only 10% when demand grows about 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: The expansion is a repurposed unit and is statutory filing-driven, not a calibrated expansion. Management said it will keep adding capacity at 80-85% utilisation, and that the ₹10 crore figure understates the ecosystem.

qa_highlights.question: Overseas losses and LMW Holding investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas losses reflect weak topline in Bangladesh and Turkey, plus high-cost locations. Order books of ₹163 crore (Global) and ₹128 crore (China) will be executed over the next 6-12 months. The ~₹200 crore sent overseas was used to buy the China subsidiary and returned to India.

qa_highlights.question: What does the ATC defence order book look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name specific programmes. It said it covers structures, assemblies, special processes and machining, but not electronics. Management said it is not into forging.

qa_highlights.question: Fixed cost trend and capex for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cost control, digitisation and automation, and VAVE for better COGS. Capex will be broadly in line with depreciation, with some leased assets.

500257|2026-03.headline: Lupin Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% YoY to Rs 7,475 crore and EBITDA 68% to Rs 2,171 crore; FY27 guided to high-single-digit growth and ~25% margin.

500257|2026-06.headline: Lupin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 8,277 crore and EBITDA hit INR 2,464 crore (30% margin), but management guided to a sharper US slowdown ahead.
500257|2026-06.overview: Lupin reported a record quarter with revenue from operations of INR 8,277 crore (up 32% YoY) and EBITDA excluding forex and other income of INR 2,464 crore (up 50% YoY, 30% margin, up 340 bps). Growth was broad-based across the US, India, Other Developed Markets, Emerging Markets and GIB, with ex-US organic growth above 20%. Management said Q2 onwards the US will moderate on Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, with quarterly US sales of USD 250-280 million, and it trimmed full-year EBITDA margin guidance to 24-25% from around 25%. Net cash fell to INR 2,831 crore from INR 4,636 crore after the VISUfarma acquisition closed.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Sales of USD 366 million, up 30% YoY in constant currency, driven by base volumes and partly offset by Mirabegron competition. FY27 US guidance is USD 1.1-1.2 billion, with management expecting USD 250-280 million per quarter over the next couple of quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 2,380 crore, up 13.9% YoY; diabetes grew 31.8% (1.8x category) and cardiac 1.2x category, while respiratory grew 6.9% vs category 11.3%. Chronic share rose to about 67% from about 65% in FY26; volume growth was 6.1%.

segments.name: Other Developed Markets (Europe, Canada, Australia)
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 1,149 crore, up 48% YoY, with Europe up 83% YoY. VISUfarma consolidation began this quarter. Management guides 10-20% growth over the next couple of years.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 990 crore, up 52% YoY. Brazil grew 117% YoY in local currency on Dapagliflozin and Empagliflozin launches.

segments.name: GIB
segments.commentary: Grew 40% YoY in the quarter, per management; no further detail given on the segment's drivers.

500279|2026-06.headline: Onida Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.5% YoY to Rs 182.4 crore, but net loss widened to Rs 14.2 crore from Rs 12.5 crore.
500279|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 29.5% YoY to Rs 182.4 crore, led by LED TV (+56.8%) and AC (+39.2%) in the branded business of Rs 175 crore (+35.8%). Gross margin improved 100 bps to 17.3%, helped by mix and AC/LED realisations, partly offset by washing machine margin pressure from input costs and competitor pricing. Net loss widened to Rs 14.2 crore from Rs 12.5 crore YoY. Management declined to give revenue or EBITDA guidance or timelines, repeatedly pointing to revenue momentum as the first step and profitability only after scale is reached.

segments.commentary: Largest category, about 60% of Q1 turnover per CFO; grew 39.2% YoY on seasonal recovery and better realisations.

segments.name: LED TVs
segments.commentary: About 25-30% of Q1 turnover; grew 56.8% YoY on launches and promotions. 100-inch QD Mini-LED TV launched and going to market.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Low single-digit share of revenue; down 1.8% YoY on mix, with margins hit by input costs and aggressive competitor pricing. Wider semi-auto and fully-automatic top-load range planned for Diwali.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or EBITDA guidance given; management said it would not give forward-looking numbers on this call.
Management said Q1 revenue growth should continue through FY27 and into next year, with bottom line to follow once scale is reached.
When asked about PAT breakeven, CFO said another ~30% increase in revenue from current levels should start contributing to bottom line (ballpark, subject to input costs and competition).
Internal target of 800-1,000 retail-excellence outlets by end of FY27; aim to double retail reach in 6-12 months.
Net working capital benchmark of 30-45 days on an annual average basis; expects no pressing funding need over the next 3-6 months.
Investor PPT to accompany Q2 FY27 results; calls planned at quarter-end results.
capex_capacity: Capex limited to small tooling and mould investments, to be funded internally.
Compressor JV or in-house compressor manufacturing not planned currently because scale does not justify it.
Wada plant scaled down in production; management denied immediate closure but said space may be used for other purposes, with no immediate timeline.
Asset monetisation under review; nothing immediately on the table, though not off the table.
Asset-light model: contract manufacturing deprioritised in favour of own branded business; reliance on ODM/OEM partners, with imports largely minimised due to QCO norms.
demand_pricing: Management said it wants to stay competitive on price while protecting margins; product mix is the other lever.
Early customer response to launches described as encouraging, with conversion rising as retail reach and activation expand.
Offline remains the bulk of revenue; e-commerce is in the high single digits.
Presence through distributors and direct dealers estimated at about 4,000+ stores, stronger in Tier-2/3 and in Gujarat, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and West Bengal.
Institutional cooling is a new vertical that management says has a few good inquiries.
Washing machine pricing pressure from competitors; input costs rising continuously, making frequent price changes difficult.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company handle rising input costs: price competitively or protect margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to stay competitive on pricing while managing the value chain to protect margins, with product mix as an added lever.

qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. CFO said roughly a further 30% revenue increase would start contributing to bottom line, but that is a ballpark that may shift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment and channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: AC about 60% of turnover, LED 25-30%, washing machines low single digit. Online is high single digit, offline is the majority.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company shifting to contract manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract manufacturing is now second priority; the branded business is the focus, with own production and some capability maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and cash position and are non-core assets being sold?
qa_highlights.answer: Fund-based limits largely unused as of June; borrowings of about Rs 38 crore to be repaid over 18 months; some surplus parked in mutual funds. Asset monetisation under review, nothing immediate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital benchmark?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-45 net working capital days on an annual average is a good benchmark, with seasonal elevation expected.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: washing machine margins under competitor pricing; input costs rising with limited ability to pass on.
Loss widened YoY despite revenue growth; the path to PAT breakeven remains undefined.
Balance sheet described as slightly stressed by management; asset monetisation (Andheri office, Wada land and plant) not yet decided.
Execution of retail expansion (double reach in 6-12 months; 800-1,000 excellence outlets) and funding of marketing and GTM spend.
Festive season (Diwali/Dussehra) performance of new TV and washing machine launches.

Leadership transition: management says the team is fully in place but further changes are expected.

500280|2026-03.headline: Century Enka Q4 FY26 operating revenue Rs 484 crore (+9% YoY) with EBITDA margin up 948 bps YoY to 11.46%, aided by price pass-through and some low-cost inventory.
500280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp YoY profit recovery: volume grew 14% YoY to 20,711 MT and EBITDA rose to Rs 55 crore, with price increases passed through after the Iran-related raw material spike from March. For FY26, revenue fell 15% to Rs 1,705 crore on 6% lower volume, but EBITDA (+29%) and PAT (+52%) improved. Management said the company has raised its indicative operating margin band to 7-10% from 6-8%, though it declined to guide quarterly numbers. Management indicated part of the gain came from consumption of lower-priced raw material, which will fade, and said the Rs 100 crore FY27 capex and renewable power additions will help margins only from H2.

segments.commentary: Q4 sales Rs 229 crore, +3% YoY; FY26 sales Rs 828 crore, -14% YoY. Finished goods inventory was reduced healthily during the quarter.

Capacity addition from the FY27 project about 2-2.5 KT; other projects add value rather than capacity.

Renewable power: company holds 26% equity in a third-party group captive hybrid project; equity contribution under Rs 10 crore; Phase-1 about 15 MW installed, 6-7 MW average output per year; Phase-2 expected to start around Q3 FY27.
Overall capacity utilisation about 80% in FY26 and about 85% in Q4 FY26.

demand_pricing: Raw material (caprolactam) prices rose sharply from March 2026 after the Iran conflict; company says price increases were passed through across product lines, with some customers' orders booked at earlier rates honoured.
Management says it did not cut production during the conflict and still consumes some older, lower-priced raw material, which will taper and reduce the margin benefit.

Demand drivers were tractor (record FY26 sales after a good monsoon), two-wheelers (above pre-COVID retail levels) and truck/bus; management expects slower growth going forward and tracks monsoon and rural demand.
Radialisation in truck and bus at about 60%, now stabilising; management expects only 1-2% growth in nylon reinforcement demand.
PTCF market in India estimated at about 25 KT, with 80-85% imported.
Chinese imports at low prices persist in commodity yarn; imports are about 20-25% of domestic NFY demand.

Value-added products earn about 20% additional margin over commodity products after conversion costs; commodity nylon filament yarn is about 15-20% of volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA margin is from inventory gains versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split the margin, citing competitive reasons. It said the company actively reduced inventory during the volatile period, and sales volume was a main driver of the Q4 performance.

qa_highlights.question: With over Rs 400 crore in investments and Rs 100 crore capex, will the company consider buyback or higher dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board discussions focus on growth and possible new segments including textiles. It said the buyback request has been conveyed to the Board, which will decide on merits; no decision was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable once low-cost inventory is used up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that higher-priced inventory will flow through, but said the operating margin range is now 7-10% versus 6-8% earlier, given cost and power initiatives that phase in from Q3-Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: The company is at Stage 2 of four approval stages with tire companies, with commercial sales expected in H2 FY27. The 4 KT plant has been utilised at 75-80% for industrial yarn.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the duty to lift domestic prices, estimating the impact at 10-30% of current FOB value. It did not quantify the import decline given that the duty is not yet notified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 100 crore FY27 capex capacity-enhancing?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 2-2.5 KT of capacity will be added from the project; most spend is for value-addition, power efficiency and safety, which should improve margins but not add capacity.

Management said margins are expected to normalise, and it kept its normalised operating margin range at 7-10%.

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin target range of 7% to 10%; management said Q2 (5.88%) is below its normal operating range.
PTCF commercial sales to commence in Q4 FY27; ramp-up gradual given multi-stage passenger car tyre approvals.
Hybrid power capacity additions at Bharuch expected to start delivering from Q4 FY27, with rough annualised benefit of about Rs 10 crore from the additional hybrid capacity.
Mother Yarn expansion at Pune expected to be capitalised in FY28.
Value-added products (VAPs) share of nylon filament yarn expected to reach about 50% in the near term.
Management declined to give formal forward-looking revenue or volume guidance, citing demand and raw material uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity approximately 92,000 MT; utilisation about 85% in Q2 FY27, with management guiding a 80% to 90% range depending on demand.
Ongoing CWIP projects: Mother Yarn expansion at Pune, increase in VAP capacity at Bharuch, energy-saving capex at both locations, safety improvements and old asset replacement.
Capital WIP rose from about Rs 13 crore in FY26 to about Rs 38 crore in H1 FY27.
Nylon capacity expansion completed in the quarter to support higher-margin offerings; no further nylon capacity expansion needed per management.
Polyester capacity is available but awaiting customer approvals (pool process); utilisation expected from Q4 FY27 onwards and mainly in FY28.
Capital allocation: company is not constrained by cash; capex approved through board on merit criteria.
demand_pricing: OEM tyre demand described as robust through September, with tractor sales the exception; secondary/replacement market weaker per ATMA data, with monsoon a factor.
Festive-season demand and the GST reduction (since September last year) cited as demand supports.
Raw material volatility sharply higher in Q2 due to Iran war; caprolactam about USD 2,000 to 2,100/t and nylon chips about USD 2,100 to 2,200/t currently.
Management says price increases were passed through, with timing gaps; absolute Q2 profit said to be above prior-year level.
Import competition from China in base and low-grade nylon yarn pressured margins; imports in Q1 were booked by tyre companies as risk mitigation.
Exports only 4% to 5% of turnover; EU and UK FTAs seen as future opportunities. Nuenyl (recycled yarn) targeted at export brands; Enkalon remains a domestic premium brand.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 37% revenue growth and how sustainable are realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth to volume growth plus higher realisations driven by raw material prices (caprolactam and polymerised chips). It said future pricing is very hard to project given high Q1 and Q2 volatility, which was much higher in Q2 due to the Iran war.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hybrid power benefit and how much headroom is there in capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The additional hybrid power is expected from Q4 FY27 with a rough annualised benefit of about Rs 10 crore. Utilisation was about 85% in Q2 and is expected to range 80% to 90%, with sufficient headroom for short-term demand surges.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NTCF sales fall due to imports and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Tyre companies booked larger imports in Q1 as a risk-mitigation step amid gas and raw material uncertainty. Management expects normalisation in coming quarters, but import spikes could recur in a volatile quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin sustainable and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a normalised EBITDA margin of 7% to 10%. Q1 was exceptional due to low-cost opening inventory and Q2 was below normal range given rising raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added product share in yarn and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: VAP share is rising quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year and is expected to reach about 50% in the near term. Management said VAP growth is already contributing to yarn margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: How is inventory rising and how will working capital evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose to about Rs 313 crore at end-H1, mainly because of higher raw material prices; volumes in quantity terms were flat to lower. Working capital should normalise when raw material prices move.

risks_watch: Raw material (caprolactam, nylon chips) price volatility linked to crude and the Iran war; timing gaps in pass-through to customers.
Continued Chinese and other imports pressuring NTCF volumes and base nylon yarn margins.
Weaker secondary/replacement tyre demand if monsoon, inflation or interest rates worsen.
Bharuch grid power tariffs and LNG prices; hybrid power benefit timing from Q4 FY27.
PTCF approval timeline and ramp-up pace; polyester capacity awaiting customer approvals.
Q3 margin recovery toward the 7% to 10% target range; inventory and working capital unwinding.

500284|2026-03.headline: FY26 PAT rose 360.9% to INR28.49 crore on caustic soda volume up 29.7% to 84,690 MT; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.03% hit by grid power tariff revision.
500284|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as a step-up year: total income INR393.1 crore (+44.62% YoY), EBITDA INR66.38 crore (+159%) at a 16.89% margin (+747 bps). Q4 FY26 total income was INR97.75 crore (+22.3% YoY), EBITDA INR13.72 crore at 14.03% margin (up 247 bps QoQ), and PAT INR4.39 crore (+68.64% YoY). Q4 margins were below Q3's stated level of above 20% because the grid power rate revision effective 1 October 2025 persisted and one electrolyser was shut for renovation, raising power consumption. Management said a 21 MW solar plant in Rajasthan is due around mid-June 2026, with renewables expected to rise to 40-45% of power needs.

segments.name: Chlorinated paraffin wax (CPW)
segments.commentary: Contributed meaningfully to Q4 revenue. Capacity is being expanded from 50 to 100 TPD, and management cited it as converting chlorine into a value-added product that stabilises the mix.

guidance_outlook: 21 MW solar plant in Rajasthan expected to be commissioned around mid-June 2026; renewable share expected to rise from about 15-20% to 40-45% of power needs.

Total installed capacity to reach 360 TPD after the 100 TPD caustic expansion, with an old 40 TPD plant decommissioned (gross would have been 400 TPD).
Management expects the energy-cost benefit to ease margin pressure once renewables are running; expects Q4's power-cost headwind to recede.
Plans to raise about INR90 crore of additional long-term debt; cost of debt around 8% (total about 7.9%).
capex_capacity: Total capex outlay INR315 crore over FY24 to FY27-28; first phase of INR150 crore (90 TPD caustic expansion, 16 MW Bikaner solar, equity in 10 MW hybrid project) completed.
Second phase under execution: 21 MW captive solar, CPW expansion from 50 to 100 TPD, and a further 100 TPD caustic soda expansion. Capital WIP INR43.85 crore at year-end.
Caustic soda capacity to reach 360 TPD post-expansion; new caustic capacity comes online around end-FY27, per analyst's reading of management's timeline.
Sulfuric acid project deferred due to volatile global sulfur prices; management cited heat-recovery use for a planned flaking unit as the rationale.

Management said salt is contracted yearly at about 11-12% of production cost, with consumption of 1.61-1.62 t salt per t caustic; purification chemicals rose 20-30% but are only 1-2% of cost.
Caustic soda prices spiked 30-35% in March 2026 and have since eased to about 12-15% above pre-war levels, per management.

Management said Indian capacity additions of 2-2.5 million tonnes over three years are largely captive for PVC on the West Coast and expected to export; chlorine prices are currently negative in India.

qa_highlights.question: Shortfall of about 97 lakh units from the consortium: how is it accounted and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall reflected committed units not supplied under the power purchase agreement, that the credit taken in power expenses is not reversible, and that full units are expected from June 2026 as the wind project completes.

qa_highlights.question: With utilisation near 80% and new capacity only at end-FY27, how will quarterly growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation should reach 80-85% over the next year, with demand exceeding North India supply given no new regional capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sulfuric acid plant deferred?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfur supply has been volatile for six to nine months and the war began about three months ago, so the project is on the back burner pending stability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margin fall versus Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Grid tariff revision applied in both quarters; caustic prices eased QoQ, and an electrolyser shutdown for membrane and electrode renovation raised power consumption in the last months of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net renewable savings and power cost without solar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure. It said the grid landed cost rose from about INR7 to INR8.2-8.3 per unit (a 15-18% rise) and that renewables are about 15-20% of power today.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of debt and FY27 interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is a little under 8% (about 7.9%) and INR90 crore of additional long-term debt is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is further renewable capex planned beyond current projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating more opportunities, pausing until the 21 MW project is done and domestic cell mandates settle, with a stated aim of maximising renewable share within regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Will new South and West Coast capacity cause oversupply in the domestic market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that new capacity is PVC-linked and export-oriented, that chlorine-caustic (ECU) pricing offsets, and that the North India market is small and fragmented.

500292|2026-03.headline: HeidelbergCement India FY26 EBITDA rose 19.8% to a per-ton figure of INR584 (up 10%) as volumes grew 8.8%; company now debt-free.
500292|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed higher EBITDA (up 19.8% YoY), PAT up 25.5%, and sales volume up 8.8%, with EBITDA per ton rising from INR530 to INR584. Q4 was weaker on price: gross realisation fell about INR105/ton QoQ, with INR53 raw material and INR25 other cost headwinds, only partly offset by power, fuel and freight. Management expects H1 FY27 cost pressure of INR100-160/ton (fuel and packaging), which it says it can pass on, though it expects prices to stay under pressure through the monsoon. The company repaid INR687 million of interest-free loans, is fully debt-free, and proposed a INR7 dividend per share.

segments.name: Premium and trade mix
segments.commentary: Premium products are 52% of trade volumes, up 9% YoY. Trade sales are 81% of total, with B2B at 19%.

Q1 FY27 cost increase expected at INR100-150/ton (fuel mix, diesel, packaging); total H1 pressure INR100-160/ton, which management says can be passed on.

Gujarat plant: still awaiting government clearance; capacity figure of 2.5-4 million tons mentioned earlier, not finalised.
Karnataka: 3 million ton integrated plant under construction (not part of the listed entity).

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 clinker production and what is the utilisation headroom and cement-to-clinker ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinker production was about 3.05 million tons in FY26, with cement capacity about 6 million tons and utilisation about 90-95%. Clinker ratio is about 60-61%, targeted to fall 50-100 bps; a new composite cement uses about 17% less clinker.

qa_highlights.question: What cost increase is expected next quarter and what levers exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a cost increase of INR100-150/ton next quarter. It sees INR100-160/ton as passable to customers. Fuel mix optimisation (petcoke to coal) could limit the impact to about INR150/ton versus the industry's about INR300.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Central India pricing weak, and can cost push be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new capacity (JK, a cement plant that came online, UltraTech ramp-up). It is confident of passing on cost increases with a lag but declined to forecast structural pricing beyond one year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the blending and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Khandwa blending unit adds about 0.35 million tons, costs about INR130 crore over two years, and is back-loaded. Total capex is about INR100 crore in FY27 and about INR120 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Clinker debottlenecking and capacity approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiln debottlenecking is complete, raising clinker capacity to about 3.23 million tons, but the government capacity approval is still pending. Grinding capacity is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for merger with Zuari and clinker sales volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a merger of group entities is planned eventually, but it would not set a timeline. Management declined to disclose clinker sales volume separately.

FY27 standalone capex planned at INR500 crores: about INR350-400 crores maintenance and replenishment, and INR100-150 crores for mining equipment.

Government clients (central, state, PSUs, agencies) about 95% of order book; private about 5%. No private client pressure or cancellations reported.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give FY27 guidance on revenue, margin and order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance for FY27 on any parameter given the uncertain environment; management will revisit after Q1 FY27 once there is more clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Is execution slowing and are clients asking to slow down work?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said all orders in the INR80,000-83,000 crore book have clearances and are fully available for execution, with no holdups.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and payment status for JJM (UP) projects?
qa_highlights.answer: UP JJM receivables fell to INR3,015 crores (incl. unbilled), with trade receivables at INR695 crores vs about INR1,700 crores in December; about INR1,000 crores collected in Q4 and INR400-450 crores in April.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone order book split and smart meter book?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the FY26 finance cost jump and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 finance cost INR645 crores (3.7% of revenue): loan interest INR220 crores, mobilisation advance interest INR154 crores, BG/LC commissions INR162 crores, other bank charges INR109 crores. Net of interest income INR554 crores (3.18%). Management would not estimate forward finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to subsidiaries and smart-meter funding?

Material availability risk; company is buying materials just-in-time.

Execution pace over the next quarter; management said no FY27 view until Q1 results.
Pending arbitrations and sub judice Jubilee Hills project; Oman impairment INR21.3 crores booked as exceptional item and all international receivables now fully impaired.

500294|2026-06.headline: NCC Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose 12% to INR 5,842 crore with EBITDA margin of 9.38%; FY27 guidance issued (8-10% revenue growth, 8.5-9% margin).
500294|2026-06.overview: Consolidated turnover grew 12% YoY to INR 5,842 crore, the highest Q1 and overall consolidated turnover in company history, while standalone turnover rose 12% to INR 4,952 crore. Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 9.38% from 8.81%, but PAT margin was 3.7% and consolidated PAT fell to INR 216.4 crore from INR 192.1 crore only on a reported basis (standalone PAT fell 1.4% YoY). Order book closed at INR 81,214 crore after INR 3,889 crore of inflows in the quarter, and management issued its first FY27 guidance. Debt rose sharply, with consolidated net debt at INR 3,513 crore, driven by smart-meter project loans.

Subsidiaries hold INR 9,902 crore of the total; standalone INR 71,312 crore.

segments.commentary: Total contract value INR 3,390 crore with about INR 116 crore executed so far; site fully mobilised with equipment received.

segments.commentary: Holding company for two Maharashtra SPVs and one Bihar project; about 45% of an estimated 7-8 million meters installed; cumulative smart-meter debt INR 1,461 crore; capex to finish by March 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow guidance INR 22,000-25,000 crore.
FY27 revenue growth guidance 8-10%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 8.5-9%.
Capex for FY27 maintained at INR 500 crore.
Standalone debt at March 2027 expected to be roughly flat YoY near INR 2,250-2,400 crore, depending on collections.
Orders booked in Q1 (INR 3,889 crore) expected to contribute turnover from Q3 FY27 onward.
Vizag Urban receivables of INR 271 crore expected by December 2026; AP Capital City old-project receivables of INR 142 crore expected this or early next quarter.
Smart-meter projects expected to finish capex by March 2027, after which O&M revenue accrues at about INR 1 crore per one lakh meters commissioned; TBM depreciation to start from Q3 FY27.
Management declined to give FY28 guidance or multi-year debt outlook.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex INR 170 crore against INR 500 crore FY27 budget.
Ken-Betwa site fully mobilised; monsoon may slow progress.
Smart meters: about 45% of 7-8 million meters installed (Maharashtra above 50%, Bihar lower); about INR 460 crore equity invested with no further equity needed.
TBM (tunnel boring machine) expected to start functioning, with depreciation rising from Q3 FY27.
Management said it has mobilised resources to complete smart-meter projects by March 2027.

Prospective bid pipeline about INR 2.5 lakh crore, not revised quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 12% revenue growth and ~9% margin in Q1 imply slower growth and margins for the rest of FY27 versus the new 8-10% and 8.5-9% guidance; could growth reach 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was encouraging but the environment is uncertain, and guidance was shared after a detailed exercise. Execution capability is unchanged; the performance depends on client funding, approvals and right-of-way, so no upside figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Quantum Technologies (smart meter) holding company and its equity investment?
qa_highlights.answer: It is the holding company for two Maharashtra smart-meter SPVs. About INR 460 crore equity has been invested, with no further equity required.

qa_highlights.question: JJM collections, outstanding and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 collections were about INR 610 crore against INR 2,771 crore UBR, with INR 413 crore more received in July. UP outstanding is INR 1,043 crore and the total JJM order book is INR 5,881 crore (groundwater 3,524, surface water 2,358). Management expects to substantially complete JJM projects this year if payment flow continues.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity price impact and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel and cement prices are stable, but petroleum-linked items, aluminium, copper and OFC cable are rising. About 81% of contracts have price escalation clauses that partly compensate. Q1 material costs were already in turnover, and prices are expected to stabilise in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is payment cycle from state governments better than a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payments are generally improving but vary by state, department and project, so no single generalisation applies.

qa_highlights.question: BharatNet fixed-price OFC exposure and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance BharatNet order is about INR 6,500 crore on a fixed-price contract. Management said current cable prices would mean lower profit rather than a loss, and it is pursuing resolution with the client and ministry.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the sharp rise in consolidated debt Y-o-Y?
qa_highlights.answer: Smart-meter project loans account for INR 1,461 crore of cumulative debt; holdco capex loans of about INR 160-170 crore were also raised. Management said the balance was about INR 4,020 crore gross and INR 3,513 crore net at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue ballooning faster than revenue; will conversion be lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 780-800 crore of the INR 7,414 crore unbilled revenue was certified in early July. Management expects unbilled to smooth over two quarters as BharatNet billing starts; the CFO said conversion moves revenue from unbilled to billed, not into the revenue line.

qa_highlights.question: Ken-Betwa status and effect of local protests?
qa_highlights.answer: Total contract value is INR 3,390 crore with about INR 116 crore executed. The site is fully mobilised with equipment received; management said the protest site is 20-30 km away and monsoon may slow progress.

qa_highlights.question: Mission Bhagiratha receivable of about INR 180 crore under High Court proceedings?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 50 crore has been received, with the balance expected at about 15% per month. Management said the matter is sub judice and declined further comment.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and finance cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: TBM depreciation is expected to start from Q3 FY27 once it begins functioning. Finance cost is expected to stay around 3% of revenue if collections continue.

risks_watch: Client funding, fund allocation and approval timing; management says performance depends on these and the environment is uncertain.

BharatNet fixed-price OFC exposure (balance INR 6,500 crore) with rising cable prices; margin compression is possible if prices stay high.
Unbilled revenue at INR 7,414 crore (38% of annualised revenue) and mobilisation advances of INR 3,163 crore (60% interest-bearing at 9.1%).
Receivable recovery from JJM (UP outstanding INR 1,043 crore), Vizag Urban (INR 271 crore by December 2026), AP Capital City (INR 142 crore) and Mission Bhagiratha (about INR 180 crore, sub judice).
Capex run-rate: only INR 170 crore spent against INR 500 crore budget in Q1; Ken-Betwa monsoon slowdown and TBM depreciation from Q3 FY27.

There is not an iota of change in our capability, our ability to execute the projects.
Yes, the entire INR 81,000 crores of orders are up and running now. All are executable orders.
So, by and large, we could say that things seem to be improving.

500300|2026-03.headline: Grasim Q4 FY26: Birla Opus revenue up 52% YoY like-to-like, Pivot revenue more than doubled; paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27 on crude-linked input cost spike.
500300|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a record year, with consolidated revenue of INR1,75,431 crores and standalone revenue of INR41,039 crores. Birla Opus grew 52% YoY like-to-like in Q4 and crossed 10% revenue market share in March 2026 on its own, while Birla Pivot's Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY and is close to its INR8,500 crore annual guidance. Raw material costs linked to crude derivatives rose sharply, with management citing up to 20-25% of COGS, prompting two further paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27. Cellulosic fibre and cement (UltraTech) contributed strong profit growth, and Grasim announced a INR10 final dividend.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue roughly doubled vs FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Caustic soda sales volume Q4 FY26

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Q4 like-to-like revenue +52% YoY; revenue market share up ~90 bps QoQ and 370 bps in FY26, now No.3 in organised decorative paints and crossed 10% share in March 2026. Installed capacity 1,332 MLPA (24% of industry); Kharagpur plant commercialised in Q3 FY26. Network at 11,500 towns, 50,000+ dealers, 1,200+ franchise stores; 218 products.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY; close to INR8,500 crore annual revenue guidance. Delivers to 5,000+ pin codes across 400+ cities. Management targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27, possibly sooner.

segments.name: UltraTech (cement, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed 200 MTPA grey capacity in April 2026, targeting 240+ MTPA by March 2028. UltraTech declared INR240 per share dividend, implying about INR4,000 crore cash inflow to Grasim before tax.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibre (VFY/Lyocell)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR4,614 crores (+14% YoY), EBITDA INR588 crores. Harihar Lyocell Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa under way within a total 110,000 tpa expansion. China operating rates at 92% in Q4 versus 87% a year ago.

segments.name: Chemicals (CFI)
segments.commentary: Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA moving to 1,530 KTPA. Specialty chemicals revenue +5% YoY, but higher ECH input prices hit profitability. Specialty chemicals 27% and chlorine derivatives 22% of revenue mix.

segments.name: Aditya Birla Capital (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Board approved a INR4,000 crore preferential equity raise; Grasim to invest INR2,880 crores to keep its 52.3% fully diluted stake.

segments.name: Insulators (within Others)
segments.commentary: Porcelain capacity held flat with productivity focus only; polymer long rods sold out after recent expansion; hollow composite expansion being evaluated. Sales and EBITDA no longer disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects industry paint growth to move from single-digit to double-digit in FY27, with Birla Opus targeting high double-digit growth.

Birla Opus priorities in order: become No.2 decorative paints player, reach INR10,000 crore revenue in the third year of full-scale operations (FY26 treated as year one), then profitability. Paint EBITDA losses to narrow quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.
Birla Opus dealer network to exceed 15,000 towns by end of FY27 from 11,500 currently.
Birla Pivot targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27.
Two further paint price increases announced April 2026, staggered into Q1 FY27; consumer impact expected in second half of Q1 and all of Q2 FY27.
Capex guidance for FY27 to be shared next quarter.
Grasim intends to keep above 50% stake in UltraTech and Aditya Birla Capital (current position, not a long-term policy).
capex_capacity: UltraTech above 200 MTPA grey capacity (April 2026); 240+ MTPA target by March 2028.
Harihar Lyocell: Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa in progress, total 110,000 tpa expansion; Phase 2 to be announced.
Birla Opus Kharagpur (sixth plant) commercialised Q3 FY26; average distance travelled per product down over 30%.
Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA to 1,530 KTPA; additional capacity under evaluation.
Insulators: no plans to add porcelain base capacity; incremental investment in polymer long rods and hollow composites.
demand_pricing: Paints: dealer price hikes of 2-6% in Jan-Feb 2026 were absorbed; primary and secondary sales stayed strong in Q4 and April 2026 primary sales were in line with March.
Paints: input costs rose to as high as 20-25% of COGS due to crude-linked raw materials, packaging and rupee depreciation; management says raw material prices remain unstable.
Paints: 10% free-paint consumer scheme continues despite price hikes; institutional channel grew 43% QoQ and 212% YoY, with a pipeline of 45,000 sites.
Paints premium and luxury products at 65% of value; 75% of products rated No.1 in blind tests by applicators (company claim).
Cellulosic fibre: management says cellulosic fibres are growing at roughly 2x the CAGR of other fibres in India; benign pulp prices supported margins.
Specialty chemicals: ECH input price increase compressed profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth in paints will come from distribution expansion and tinting machines versus throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth from both numerical dealer expansion (11,500 towns to 15,000+) and throughput gains by adding product ranges to existing dealers. Older dealers over 18 months show 25-50% higher counter share and throughput comparable to legacy players.

qa_highlights.question: Is paint profitability improving from scale, and is FY26 the first full year for the INR10,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY26 as the first full operating year internally. Fixed costs (sales and service force, brand spend) were front-loaded and should be covered by growth; variable-cost levers include better procurement, plant and logistics optimisation, and adding second and third raw material suppliers. Paint contribution improved significantly in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How close is Birla Opus to the No.2 position in decorative paints?
qa_highlights.answer: Birla Opus plus Birla White putty is roughly at the level of the current No.2 on a decorative-only basis for Q4 FY26. The ambition is for Birla Opus alone to become No.2 in decorative paints, excluding industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer throughput versus industry benchmarks?
qa_highlights.answer: Throughput is in line with market presence across A/B/C/D dealer classes. Top dealers stock 2-2.5x the bottom dealer and generate 4-5x its throughput. The market leader is estimated to have 20-25% more dealers and a richer A-class mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan after the UltraTech dividend, given about INR2,900 crores for ABC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the INR2,900 crore use (ABC stake maintenance) as a one-off for FY26. Cash is being used for Grasim's dividend, maintaining the ABC stake, and supporting the two new businesses. Capex guidance for FY27 will come next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Pivot profitability path and when will segment disclosure start?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot aims to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even and may get there sooner. Paints EBITDA losses are on a glide path to narrow each quarter. Management said segment reporting for paints and Pivot would start shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Will paint EBITDA losses (about INR300 crores per quarter) come down materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered 'Yes, it will come down' without quantifying the timing.

qa_highlights.question: Insulator capacity, sales and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Porcelain capacity is flat, with productivity focus; polymer long rods are sold out after expansion; hollow composite expansion is being evaluated. Insulator sales and EBITDA are no longer disclosed.

risks_watch: Paint input cost volatility: crude-linked raw materials and packaging rose to as high as 20-25% of COGS; management says prices remain unstable and could escalate further, so the staggered Q1 FY27 price hikes may not fully offset costs.

Demand elasticity: consumer and contractor impact of the price hikes expected in second half of Q1 and all of Q2 FY27; April 2026 primary sales were in line with March, and secondary sales are being tracked weekly.
Paints EBITDA losses (about INR300 crore per quarter per an analyst) are guided to narrow QoQ and YoY, but no quantified timeline was given; watch whether the glide path shows up in Q1 FY27.
Segment disclosure for Birla Opus paints and Birla Pivot is due to start shortly; the first disclosures will show the actual losses and Pivot's break-even progress.

500300|2026-06.headline: Grasim Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR48,716 crore, up 21% YoY, with standalone EBITDA more than doubling to INR1,094 crore.
500300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR48,716 crore (up 21% YoY), the 24th consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Standalone revenue rose 28% to INR11,795 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 107% to INR1,094 crore. Birla Opus revenue grew 64% YoY to INR1,661 crore after an 8.8% cumulative price increase to offset a raw material cost shock, and Birla Pivot grew 75% to INR2,548 crore. Management also disclosed a new 0.25% of standalone revenue brand royalty payable to Birla Holdings from June 2026, and a planned Renewables equity infusion below INR1,000 crore in FY27.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,548 crore (+75% YoY), annualised run rate above INR10,000 crore. Management reiterated EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27; private labels more than doubled YoY off a low base.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,530 crore (+12% YoY) on volumes down 4% YoY; specialty fibre rose to 27% of sales mix from 21%. EBITDA roughly doubled, helped by a low base and specialty mix.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,640 crore (+10% YoY); ECU realisation INR37,955/t (+6% YoY); caustic share of revenue fell to 49% and specialty chemicals rose to 30%. EBITDA INR491 crore (+16%). Volumes softer on plant maintenance.

segments.commentary: Sales volume 41.31 Mt (+12% YoY); gray capacity 205.5 Mt after adding 8.7 Mt in the quarter; EBITDA INR5,146 crore (+12%). Green power mix 45.6%; 5,802 retail outlets.

segments.commentary: Lending portfolio grew 32% to nearly INR2,20,000 crore; housing finance crossed INR50,000 crore (+50%). Grasim invested INR2,880 crore at INR356/share to maintain its fully diluted stake.

segments.commentary: Renewables revenue +59% YoY; textiles +26% YoY; insulators serving the power sector expansion.

500325|2026-06.headline: Reliance Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25% and EBITDA about 10% to over Rs 54,000 Cr, led by O2C spreads, with net profit near Rs 23,200 Cr (+6%).

Net debt was slightly lower than March at about Rs 1,23,000 Cr, with capex of about Rs 39,000 Cr; Moody's upgraded RIL to Baa1 and S&P is at A-.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Jio order book or a process for platform services revenue?

qa_highlights.question: Will the 168 MW Meta data centre be built on RIL's balance sheet, and what is the full-year capex plan?

500330|2026-03.headline: Raymond Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR85 crore (13.9% margin) from INR99 crore, while Engineering segments grew and a INR930 crore 5-year capex plan was announced.
500330|2026-03.overview: Consolidated total income rose 2% YoY to INR613 crore in Q4 FY26, but EBITDA fell to INR85 crore with a 13.9% margin versus INR99 crore and 16.4% a year earlier, as non-operating income dropped after INR600 crore was transferred to Raymond Realty post-demerger. For FY26, total income grew 10% to INR2,312 crore while EBITDA was flat at INR335 crore, with margin down to 14.5% from 15.9%. Aerospace & Defense revenue grew 26% for the year to INR392 crore, and Precision Technology & Auto Components grew 10% to INR1,667 crore with EBITDA up 34%, helped by synergies and a INR13 crore one-time land-sale gain. qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and capex phasing for the Andhra plant?

qa_highlights.answer: Cash includes liquid and some 2-3 year marketable investments. Management said the Engineering business is self-funding from cash flows, with the parent's liquidity as a backstop, and no parent capital infusion is planned for organic needs.
