rows.why: H1 FY27 UAE volume was about 2.1 mt with H2 expected similar and 4-5 mt annualised after the new mill ramps (about 30% utilisation in first year), though West Asia conflict is a demand risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40-41 mt FY27 volume guide, premium mix and the Meghalaya timeline, but cautious on fuel cost (Q3 guided INR2.15-2.20/kcal), freight savings sustainability and weak monsoon; it withheld granular disclosures such as pure cement cost, UAE revenue/EBITDA and clinker volu

500400|2026-03.headline: Tata Power Q4 FY26 PAT rose 8% to INR1,416 crores and FY26 PAT topped INR5,000 crores, with FY27 capex guided at about INR25,000 crores.
500400|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 EBITDA up about 10% to INR4,216 crores and PAT up 8% to INR1,416 crores, with full-year EBITDA up about 11% to INR16,090 crores and PAT above INR5,000 crores for the first time. Mundra was offline for nine months, and its SPPA with Gujarat is now signed, with four other states expected to follow in 4 to 6 weeks. FY26 capex came in well below the earlier guidance as transmission and right-of-way delays pushed projects out of the quarter. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR25,000 crores and about 2.5 GW of renewable commissioning, with roughly half of the 5 GW under-implementation pipeline due in FY27 and the rest by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up ~10% from INR3,829 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: Above INR5,000 crores (first full year above INR5,000 crores)

financial_highlights.metric: Solar cell and module manufacturing PAT (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: more than double the previous year

segments.name: Solar cell and module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR857 crores, more than double the prior year; plant stabilised with good yields. Captive demand from in-house utility-scale and rooftop projects is expected to absorb output.

segments.name: Odisha DISCOMs
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR809 crores vs INR439 crores in FY25. Management expects FY27 to be the best year for Odisha, with AT&C losses to fall about 2 percentage points a year to 12-13% over 4-5 years.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR499 crores with installations doubling; management targets 20% market share in 3 years and 50-60% rooftop market growth in FY27. Rooftop share was about 40% on 1.7 GW executed in FY26, per analyst.

segments.name: Utility-scale renewables / IPP
segments.commentary: Management expects about 2.5 GW commissioning in FY27 (solar 1.5-1.8 GW, remainder wind and hybrid/FDRE), with 5 GW under implementation, all in-house, and no third-party EPC work in FY27.

segments.name: Tata Projects
segments.commentary: Losses attributed to legacy projects (DFC and Barmer refinery), now largely complete. Management expects a return to profit in FY27.

segments.name: Mumbai Transmission and IEL
segments.commentary: Q4 PAT lifts of about INR50 crores (Mumbai Transmission) and INR63 crores (IEL) were attributed to asset capitalisation and deferred tax; Mumbai Transmission adds about INR1,000 crores capex a year on a 70:30 debt-equity structure.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex about INR25,000 crores, and similar capital outlay expected in FY28, covering solar, wind, pumped storage, pure hydro and transmission.
FY27 renewable commissioning about 2.5 GW (solar 1.5-1.8 GW), with a larger chunk from hybrid and FDRE projects.
Mundra SPPAs: Gujarat signed; remaining four states expected within 4-6 weeks; plant operating under Section 11 with billing per SPPA.
Odisha FY27 expected to be the best year yet, with AT&C losses falling toward 12-13% over 4-5 years.
Rooftop solar expected to grow 50-60% in FY27. Indian-made cell and module mandatory for government-subsidised rooftop from 1 June 2026.
Nuclear: 2 x 220 MW small modular reactor DPRs with NPCIL, some expected within about 6 months.

Current pipeline of 26.3 GW including existing capacity (16.7 GW operating): includes 2,800 MW Shirwata pumped hydro and Bhutan hydro (600 MW plus 1,125 MW, World Bank financing signed); Bhutan 1,125 MW expected around FY31-32.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR13,000 crores, below the guidance of about INR22,000 crores given in November; projects slipped due to right-of-way and TBCB transmission delays.
About 600 MW of large utility-scale projects being pushed to complete in Q1 FY27; deferred projects to be completed in FY27.
5 GW of renewable projects under implementation, all in-house; about 50% due in FY27 and the balance by FY28.
Company will not commission projects without permanent GNA and transmission certainty, which deferred some FY26 capex.
10 GW wafer and ingot plant to start in two phases, to supply Indian-made wafers from 1 June 2028.
Net renewable capacity: 16.7 GW operating; 26.3 GW including the current pipeline.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew about 2% in the last quarter but rose 5-6% from April; peak demand reached 256 GW and management expects it to exceed 270 GW in the next 1-2 months due to heatwave and El Nino.
Indonesian coal prices expected to stay within plus or minus 5%; coal and shipping costs have risen only slightly in the last two months.
Coal cost is a pass-through under the Gujarat SPPA, including FOB cost changes such as export duties or royalties.
Curtailment is intermittent and varies by location (evacuation allowed between 20% and 80%); cost reimbursed under GNA where curtailment occurs.
Solar and wind tenders: management says most of the current project pipeline bids with domestic cell and module requirements.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 capex well below the INR25,000 crore guidance from the November analyst meet, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance was closer to INR22,000 crores; projects slipped due to right-of-way and TBCB transmission delays. FY27 capex is about INR25,000 crores, with deferred projects completed this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full benefit of prior-period regulatory orders in Delhi distribution, and should FY27 reported numbers decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 regulatory approvals reflected INR783 crores vs INR333 crores in FY25. Further approvals are expected but are hard to quantify, as they relate to a pipeline of contested regulatory assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 IPP RE capacity addition and will the modules and cells be sourced in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 2 GW of commissioning in FY27, possibly slightly higher, of which solar is 1.5-1.8 GW. The in-house cell and module plant will supply the captive requirement, with about 1.4x module/cell content per MW.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the regulatory asset wind-down in Delhi is progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator has committed in an affidavit to amortise the regulatory assets over six years up to 2032, which is under monitoring by the Supreme Court and APTEL.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tata Power sacrifice coal profitability under the Gujarat SPPA, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said details will be shared once all five procurers sign, with no quantification given at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 5 GW renewable pipeline represent installed or contracted capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is on installed capacity; contracted capacity is lower (about 1,200 MW for FDRE and hybrid wind per the slide cited by the analyst).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR250 crore deferred tax asset and the Q4 PAT lifts at IEL and Mumbai Transmission?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the deferred tax was recognised in Q4 based on better profit visibility and carry-forward losses. IEL uplift was from a plant commissioning; Mumbai Transmission's recurring uplift is from about INR1,000 crores of annual capex.

risks_watch: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores is nearly double FY26 actual; slippage risk from transmission and right-of-way delays has already caused one shortfall.
Regulatory prior-period gains (INR783 crores in FY26) are lumpy and hard to forecast, so FY27 reported Delhi distribution profit could fall.
Four remaining Mundra SPPAs (states other than Gujarat) are not yet signed; billing is under Section 11 pending approvals.
Curtailment on solar projects and temporary GNA issues could hold back commissioning and PLF.
Coal monetisation remains open; management said a sale depends on valuation and signing all SPPAs.
Net debt to underlying EBITDA of 3.3x with a large capex programme; management says leverage discipline will be maintained.
Possible Indonesian coal export duty or royalty changes; coal cost is a pass-through under the SPPA.
500400|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating performance and growth, with cautious language on timing: management acknowledged FY26 capex shortfall and project slippage, and was evasive on quantifying regulatory gains, the coal monetisation and the Gujarat SPPA's profit-sharing terms.
key_quotes: We have now concluded the SPPA with Gujarat, and we are in the process of finalizing it with all the other 4 states, which we expect in next 4 to 6 weeks, we will complete.
Our leverage ratios are very stable. Our net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.3 and our net debt to equity is 1.2, which is very competitive for infrastructure and power industry.
We have fallen short because some of the projects that we were planning to execute in the last quarter could not happen.
So now we are being extra careful, and that is why some of our capex, which we had planned last year got deferred because we do not want to set up the plant and be on temporary GNA.
Mumbai transmission adds every year INR1,000 crores of capex. So, on a 70-30, you will have a return on equity on 30%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose about 10% to INR4,216 crores and FY26 EBITDA rose about 11% to INR16,090 crores, helped by Odisha DISCOM PAT of INR809 crores (vs INR439 crores) and rooftop PAT of INR499 crores, with the Mundra SPPA restoring coal pass-through earnings once all states sign.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (Q1-Q4 FY27), with about 600 MW pushed into Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management guides about 2.5 GW renewable commissioning in FY27 (solar 1.5-1.8 GW) from 5 GW under implementation, about half due in FY27, but FY26 capex was about INR13,000 crores against a INR22,000 crores guide, so slippage risk is material.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Rooftop installations doubled to about 1.7 GW executed in FY26 and management guides 50-60% rooftop market growth in FY27, with power demand up 5-6% from April and peak demand expected above 270 GW.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores and a similar outlay in FY28 is already guided, and a 10 GW wafer/ingot plant is planned to supply Indian-made wafers from 1 June 2028, though no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.why: Management expects Odisha FY27 to be its best year and further Delhi regulatory approvals are expected, but these are lumpy and hard to quantify, after FY26 regulatory approvals of INR783 crores vs INR333 crores.

rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores is nearly double FY26 actual, and FY26 regulatory gains of INR783 crores are lumpy, so reported Delhi distribution profit could fall; curtailment and transmission/GNA delays could also hold back commissioning.

rows.why: Indian-made cell and module become mandatory for government-subsidised rooftop from 1 June 2026, and the in-house cell and module plant (FY26 PAT INR857 crores, more than double) is set to supply captive demand.

rows.why: Gujarat SPPA is signed and the plant is operating under Section 11 with billing per SPPA, and management expects the remaining four states to follow in 4-6 weeks, though coal monetisation depends on signing all five.

rows.why: The regulator has committed in an affidavit to amortise regulatory assets over six years up to 2032, though the schedule is under Supreme Court and APTEL monitoring.

rows.label: Tata Projects return to profit
rows.why: Losses came from legacy DFC and Barmer refinery projects that are now largely complete, and management expects a return to profit in FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating performance, Odisha, rooftop and the FY27 capex and commissioning plan, but cautious on timing, acknowledging the FY26 capex shortfall and project slippage; analysts pushed on the lumpy Delhi regulatory gains, the Gujarat SPPA profit-sharing and coal monetisatio

500400|2026-06.headline: Tata Power Q1 FY27 PAT rose 11% to INR 1,401 crore and EBITDA 8% to INR 4,249 crore, the 27th straight quarter of growth.
500400|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 1,401 crore (+11%) and EBITDA of INR 4,249 crore (+8%), with revenue also up. Q1 capex was INR 5,300 crore, a first, against a FY27 plan of INR 25,000 crore. Odisha DISCOM collections were delayed by government payment timing and a heatwave-related disconnection pause, which management says is timing-related. Renewable capacity additions were 226 MW in Q1, with about 500 MW near commissioning and a FY27 target of 2,500-2,700 MW, taking installed capacity past 9 GW.

financial_highlights.change: first time quarterly spend at this level

financial_highlights.metric: Rooftop revenue (Q1, per analyst calculation from slides)
financial_highlights.change: revenue roughly doubled YoY per management

segments.name: Renewables (generation)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 6.7 GW, with 2.5 GW to be added in FY27 and capacity expected to cross 9 GW by year-end. Q1 commissioning was 226 MW; 500 MW is described as ready within weeks, with Q2 commissioning of 800-900 MW targeted.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: Management guides to 60-70% growth this year. Q1 revenue was about INR 1,350 crore on 371 MW installed, and Mundra-style battery storage is being added. Management says cumulative rooftop revenue could reach INR 30,000 crore by 2029.

segments.name: Transmission (Mumbai and TBCB)
segments.commentary: Mumbai transmission has about INR 10,000 crore of regulated investment over five years. Two TBCB projects are near commissioning (Jalpura-Khurja now, Bikaner-Neemrana by October); TBCB revenue so far is construction-revenue booking, not line-by-line EBITDA.

segments.name: Distribution (Odisha and Delhi)
segments.commentary: Odisha PAT grew about 6% and units sold rose 10.4%, but collections were delayed by government payments, the heatwave disconnection pause and billing lag. Management says the DISCOM should be judged on a 12-month basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing (TP Solar)
segments.commentary: Module output crossed 1,000 MW in Q1 for the first time, while cell output fell after a line change. Margins are around 25-26%, and management expects yield and efficiency to peak in Q2.

segments.name: Tata Projects / solar EPC
segments.commentary: Third-party solar EPC has been discontinued and no new orders are being booked; remaining legacy projects are in final stages, and losses were booked in Q1. Management expects one more quarter of impact.

segments.name: Mundra (coal and power)
segments.commentary: Mundra's PAT rose on a higher share of coal profits, while EBITDA fell. The plant runs under a supplementary PPA on cost-reflective terms with no equity return. The state cabinet approvals are expected in August-September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex plan of INR 25,000 crore, about 50% for renewables; Q2 capex expected above INR 6,000 crore, possibly INR 6,500 crore.
FY27 renewable additions of 2.5-2.7 GW, taking installed capacity past 9 GW by year-end.
Q4 is expected to be 4.5x-5x Q1 in profit terms, per management's trend comment.
Pumped storage: Shirwata 1,800 MW construction to start later in FY27; first 330 MW unit commissioning from early CY2029. Khorlochhu 600 MW Bhutan hydro expected in CY2030.
Rooftop: management expects cumulative revenue above INR 30,000 crore by 2029 and share rising from 12-13% to about 25%.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR 5,300 crore, the first time it has reached this level in a quarter.
Renewables: 226 MW commissioned in Q1, 500 MW near ready; Q2 commissioning target 800-900 MW.
Pumped storage: 1,800 MW Shirwata construction to begin later in FY27. Dorjilung 1,125 MW financial closure with PFC, IFC and other lenders expected in about two months.
Transmission: over 2,000 km of transmission in the pipeline; Mumbai transmission investment about INR 10,000 crore over five years.
Module capacity: 1,000 MW+ output in Q1; cell capacity still ramping after a line change.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew about 8.5% in Q1 (May about 11%, June 9.8%); July ran at 260-270 GW.
Rooftop realisation: analyst calculated about INR 36/Wp billed versus about INR 28/Wp in order inflow; management attributed the gap to product mix (ULA scheme, module size), not a price decline.
Coal prices up about 5-7%, with management expecting up to 5% more over the next nine months.
Renewable auctions are muted as central agency (SECI, NHPC, NTPC) PPAs give way to direct state bids and FDRE/RTC tenders.
ALMM-II continues; management says the proviso for behind-the-meter projects covers about 10% of demand and does not affect its business.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Odisha DISCOM growth muted, and why did Tata Projects losses widen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited delayed government payments for drinking water and street lighting, a heatwave-driven pause in disconnections until 15 June, and billing lag. It expects a recovery in Q2. Tata Projects is closing legacy loss-making projects, with about 10% in the final stage and one more quarter of impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Can curtailment losses be quantified, and when will transmission bottlenecks ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment across the industry was about 5% in Q1, which management says should settle over the next few quarters as evacuation lines are completed. Q2 commissioning should ramp up with about 500 MW near ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for renewable auction volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Central-agency auctions have slowed as states move to direct bids and customised FDRE/RTC tenders. Pumped storage and large C&I deals are the growth areas.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the TBCB EBITDA margin so low?
qa_highlights.answer: TBCB projects are still under construction, so revenue is recognised under lease accounting. Line-by-line EBITDA starts from Q2 as the two projects commission, with Q3 and Q4 to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TP Solar margins rise, and will third-party cell sales continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party cell sales were small. Some sales may continue for a few quarters for ALMM-exempt or open-access projects, but management does not expect large sales ahead. Margins reflect higher-efficiency products.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mundra PAT rise while EBITDA fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the PAT increase came from a higher share of coal profits. Under the supplementary PPA, the plant recovers coal costs and fixed costs on a normative basis but earns no equity return, so under-recovery is possible in some quarters.

risks_watch: Odisha and Delhi DISCOM collections are lagging and depend on timing; watch whether Q2 catches up.
Renewable commissioning is 500 MW away from the 2.5-2.7 GW FY27 target, and evacuation bottlenecks cause around 5% curtailment.
Rooftop growth (60-70% target) and falling module realisations as capacity rises across the industry; watch margins at TP Solar.
Net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.41x against a 3x-plus capex plan; watch leverage against the guardrails.
Tata Projects losses are expected for one more quarter; the Mundra supplementary PPA leaves the plant without an equity return; the nuclear plan awaits government rules.
500400|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, pipeline and rooftop, with repeated claims of consistency. It was defensive on Odisha collections, Tata Projects losses and the TBCB margin, attributing them to timing. It was brief on Mundra and EPC economics, and it deferred some detailed questions to Investor Relations.
key_quotes: This is the 27th consecutive quarter where we have seen increase in our PAT and EBITDA.
We will set up 2,500 megawatt to 2,700 megawatt.
We are at something like just 10% of the legacy projects in last stage there and cost to correction takes place because of that reason.
So in distribution, we should always look at 12 months rollover rather than seeing on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

rows.why: Q4 expected at 4.5x-5x Q1 profit per management trend comment, with TBCB line-by-line EBITDA starting Q2 and Tata Projects losses ending after one more quarter, though Odisha collections and coal cost up 5-7% are offsets.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: 226 MW commissioned in Q1, about 500 MW ready within weeks, and FY27 target of 2,500-2,700 MW taking installed capacity from 6.7 GW past 9 GW, with Dorjilung 1,125 MW financial closure expected in about two months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Renewable additions of 2.5-2.7 GW (about 38% of the 6.7 GW base), rooftop growth guided at 60-70% from 371 MW installed, and Odisha units sold up 10.4% in Q1, though no consolidated revenue growth figure was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (capex above INR 6,000 crore, possibly INR 6,500 cro
rows.why: Q1 capex of INR 5,300 crore was a first, against a FY27 plan of INR 25,000 crore, and Shirwata 1,800 MW PSP construction is set to start later in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 PAT rose 11% and EBITDA 8%, and management expects Q4 profit at 4.5x-5x Q1, but the Odisha collection delay and solar EPC losses cap near-term upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Renewable additions need 500 MW more than Q1 run-rate to hit 2.5 GW, curtailment is about 5% on evacuation bottlenecks, and net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.41x against a 3x-plus capex plan.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Rooftop battery storage is being added and Shirwata 1,800 MW pumped storage starts later in FY27, though the first 330 MW unit is not until early CY2029.

rows.label: TBCB transmission line-by-line EBITDA from Q2
rows.why: Jalpura-Khurja is near commissioning now and Bikaner-Neemrana by October, with line-by-line EBITDA starting Q2 and Q3-Q4 to follow, after Q1 TBCB EBITDA was low under lease accounting.

rows.label: Tata Projects solar EPC losses roll off
rows.why: Third-party solar EPC discontinued with no new orders, about 10% of legacy projects in final stage, and management expects one more quarter of loss impact.

rows.label: Mundra state cabinet approvals
rows.why: Approvals are expected in August-September, but the supplementary PPA gives no equity return and under-recovery is possible in some quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on renewables pipeline, rooftop growth and capex of INR 25,000 crore, but defensive on Odisha collections, Tata Projects losses and TBCB margins, attributing them to timing; analysts pressed on those areas and on curtailment.

500402|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 53% YoY to INR293.9 crores with PAT up 140% to INR28 crores, but FY26 revenue of INR868 crores missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance.
500402|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR293.9 crores, up 53% YoY and 27% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR25 crores at an 8.4% margin and PAT of INR28 crores. Management attributed the margin dip to one-time legal and arbitration costs, a non-cash expected credit loss provision and bank limit mobilisation costs. FY26 revenue of INR868 crores (up 13%), EBITDA of INR86 crores (9.7% margin) and PAT of INR76 crores (up 55%) fell short of the INR900-1,000 crore revenue guidance, which management blamed on fund-availability-linked execution pacing in March. Management guided to at least 25% growth in revenue and profit in FY27, and the company is building BESS manufacturing capacity alongside its water EPC business.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR299.55 crores; includes INR137 crores back-to-back debtors

financial_highlights.value: INR5,369 crores (about INR4,000 crores new, INR1,369 crores legacy)
INR380 crores against agreed INR700 crores

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Management said water is about 85-90% of revenue in the quarter and year; the company targets INR5,000 crores of total (incl. JV) order intake per year, with net share of INR2,500-3,000 crores. Recent wins include Kekri (Rajasthan, Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0), Indore (AMRUT) and Ranchi (NABARD).

segments.name: Power and BESS
segments.commentary: Power is a very small share of revenue. A 2.5 GWh BESS assembly line at Supa MIDC Pune is due to start by end-June 2026, expanding to 5 GW and 600 containerised units per year by end-2026. The NTPC BESS order is INR1,128 crores, of which INR96 crores is O&M; capex for BESS up to 5 GW plus containers is about INR200 crores plus INR35 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27: at least 25% growth in both top line and bottom line, with growth expected in every quarter; management said it will give annual numeric guidance at the annual call.
Shortfall in FY26 revenue (about INR50-100 crores of spillover) expected to be executed in Q1 and Q2 FY27; management said EPC orders execute over about 3 years.
EBITDA margin target of around 10%; new orders carry a minimum 10% margin, and management said the Q4 margin would have been about 10% without one-time costs.

NARCL: about INR45 crores minimum payment planned in FY27; surplus cash to be used for growth rather than NARCL repayment; arbitration awards in hand (about INR627-630 crores) expected to cover the balance.
Tax: accumulated losses and the new tax regime (no MAT) expected to keep tax payments low for a few years; management cited a tax shield of more than INR500 crores.
capex_capacity: 2.5 GWh BESS assembly line at Supa MIDC Pune to commence by end-June 2026, with expansion to 5 GW planned.
Container manufacturing of 600 units per year targeted by end-2026, for about INR35 crores.
Total BESS capex (up to 5 GW) about INR200 crores including about INR25 crores R&D; INR175 crores quoted for the 2.5 GW and 5 GW phases with INR125 crores for the first 2.5 GW.
Battery packs are about 35-40% of BESS EPC cost and containers about 8-10%, with battery packs and containers being manufactured in-house.
Peak revenue potential quoted as INR2,500 crores per 2.5 GW phase, about INR5,000 crores for both phases.
demand_pricing: Management cited government BESS targets of about 236 GW by 2031-32 and a 10% BESS mandate for renewables; it said 92 GW of BESS projects are in the pipeline.
All new contracts carry price variation clauses; management said it takes no order without PV and without clarity on funding.
Margin discipline: new orders are being taken at minimum 10% margin; OEM battery-pack orders also at minimum 10%.
Payment terms: NTPC and Power Grid BESS orders expected at 15-20 days; World Bank or bank-funded water projects 15-30 days.
Competition in BESS is rising; management pointed to its Energy Vault tie-up and power EPC experience as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue below the INR900-1,000 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution is linked to customer fund availability; March saw customer fund shortfalls on tenders such as RITES, so about INR50-100 crores of spillover moves into FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins dip in Q4 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited one-time legal and arbitration costs, an Ind AS expected credit loss provision and bank limit mobilisation costs, together adding about INR10 crores to other expenses; margin is expected to rise as new orders grow in the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net water order book and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is INR5,000 crores total order intake per year including JVs, with net share of INR2,500-3,000 crores; the analyst's net order book estimate was about INR3,300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Are Jal Jeevan Mission payment delays a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JJM payments were stopped for verification and are resuming, with the scheme extended to 2028; it has not taken new JJM projects recently and is focused on AMRUT and bank-funded projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will the NARCL dues be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR630 crores of awards are in hand, with about 75% payable to NARCL; the balance is expected to be funded from awards rather than operating cash flow, with about INR380 crores to be paid in total.

risks_watch: FY26 revenue missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance; the spillover of INR50-100 crores into FY27 must show up in Q1 and Q2 results.
Dependence on customer fund flows and government payments; JJM payment delays were acknowledged, and the company said it is avoiding orders without funding clarity.
NARCL repayment depends on arbitration awards, with about INR4,526 crores of claims pending and historical conversion of about 40%.

500402|2026-06.headline: SPML Infra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 74% YoY to INR286 crore and PAT 87% to INR22.7 crore, with EBITDA margin at 10%.

500403|2026-03.headline: Sundram Fasteners FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR 5,612 crore and PAT hit a record INR 580 crore, helped by Q4 EBITDA margin of 17%.
500403|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR 5,612 crore (up from INR 5,231 crore) and profit before exceptional items of INR 750 crore (up 12% from INR 668 crore). Exceptional items included a full reversal of a prior impairment provision, partly offset by an INR 11 crore gratuity provision under the new Labour Code. Q4 saw exports return to growth in both USD and INR terms, and EBITDA margin widened to 17% from 15.6% a year earlier. Management said April started well and that it targets double-digit growth over the next two years.

500403|2026-06.headline: Sundram Fasteners Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose 20% to INR1,618 crores from INR1,367 crores; standalone profit up ~10% to INR150 crores.
500403|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a very good start, with consolidated turnover up 20% YoY to INR1,618 crores and growth across OE, aftermarket and exports. Standalone profit rose from INR138 crores to INR150 crores, which management attributed to tighter control of fixed costs. Input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict was a pressure, with direct materials passed through to domestic OEMs and indirect/energy costs under negotiation. Management guided to margin expansion in Q2 once indirect cost recoveries are accounted for, and said the 20% run rate should hold through the festive period.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the cash conversion cycle stabilise?

500405|2026-03.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q4 FY26 standalone revenue INR 1,587 crore (+3% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 253 crore at 15.9% margin; ABS running at ~65% of design capacity.
500405|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 3% YoY to INR 1,587 crore on higher volumes (100,664 t, +5.4% YoY) and better spreads, with operating EBITDA up 75% YoY to INR 253 crore (15.9% margin) and PAT of INR 168 crore. The mass ABS plant restarted at ~65% of design capacity after an equipment failure, and EPS Phase-II (Amdoshi) lifted capacity to 115,000 tpa in April 2026. The company remains debt-free with INR 700 crore investable surplus.

500405|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR 1,693 crore, up 22% YoY, despite lower volumes, driven by higher raw material prices from the West Asia conflict. Operating EBITDA rose 88% YoY to INR 331 crore (19.53% margin) and PAT was INR 236 crore (13.96% margin), helped by wide global deltas between styrene monomer and downstream products. Manufactured volumes fell 24.5% YoY to 70,842 MT, with exports nearly absent and non-OEM demand down roughly 50%. Management declined to guide on volumes or margins, calling the situation fluid, and announced polystyrene and compounding expansions plus a new 80,000 TPA PS line totaling about INR 450 crore, funded from internal accruals.

500408|2026-09.headline: Tata Elxsi Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR 1,055.7 crore, up 2.3% in constant currency; EBITDA margin 21.9%, up 70 bps QoQ.
500408|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 1,055.7 crore, growing 2.3% in constant currency, with all three verticals up sequentially (transportation +2% QoQ, media and communication +3.4%, healthcare and life sciences +3.5%). EBITDA was INR 231.4 crore, up 7.1% QoQ and 19.7% YoY, with margin at 21.9%. Management attributed about 60-70 bps of the margin gain to currency and 10-20 bps to operating leverage and fading one-offs, which absorbed an annual wage revision. Europe automotive remained soft and the transportation outlook depends on it; management expects H2 to exceed H1 across businesses except the Europe-dependent part of transportation.

segments.name: Media and Communication
segments.commentary: Grew 3.4% QoQ in constant currency on ramp-ups of closed deals and AI-led wins, including a GenAI virtual assistant engagement with a global technology leader.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 3.5% QoQ in constant currency after bottoming last quarter; win with a global renal care leader for next-gen home dialysis systems.

500410|2026-03.headline: Ambuja Cements guided FY27 volumes to ~80 Mt (~8% growth) and cut capex to INR6,000-6,500 crore, with cost peaking at INR4,500/t and a INR250/t reduction targeted.
500410|2026-03.overview: Ambuja (consolidated, including ACC and Orient references) reported FY26 record volumes of 73.7 Mt (+16% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (+31%, INR887/t, +12%), with PAT of INR2,647 crore (+17%). Q4 was weak operationally: volumes were muted, cost per tonne rose to about INR4,500 in the quarter against an earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, and acquired assets (Sanghi at 57%, Penna at 46% utilization) lagged. Management reset its growth timeline, pushed capex out, and set a INR250/t cost reduction target for FY27. Pricing was flat-to-slightly-up at about INR254/bag, with industry realisations pressured by soft demand.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Grew both trade and non-trade, per management, with Mumbai and Gujarat margin-accretive. West is about 30% of volume.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Highest degrowth cluster as about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume was curtailed; channel build-out to take one to two quarters more.

segments.name: Central
segments.commentary: Volumes declined as the company shifted to blended cement offerings to improve margins.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth guidance of 8%; management says July trade volumes were up 8% YoY, implying a steep ramp needed for the rest of the year.
FY27 net operating cost target of INR4,250/t, with Q1 at INR4,241/t; a further INR250/t reduction targeted in FY28 to about INR4,000/t.
Identified savings of INR130-150/t from lead distance (INR35/t), fly ash and BCFC logistics (INR30/t), green power and heat rate (~INR50/t), and other items (INR10-15/t).
Q2 expected to see geopolitical-driven cost pressure of about INR100/t if conditions persist, which management says is mitigated by inventory (about 1 month clinker, about 3 months coal).
Capex of about INR6,500 crore in FY27 (about 25%, or INR1,500-1,600 crore, spent in Q1); FY28 capex run-rate of INR6,000-7,000 crore; capacity additions of 8-10 mtpa per year.

Capacity to reach 119 mtpa by end FY27 (Dahej, Salai Banwa, Bhatinda, Jodhpur already commissioned or in trials; Kalamboli and Warisaliganj expected Q2; Maratha clinker in Q1 FY28; Mundra in about 2029).
Green power target of 60% share by FY28 (48% on a revenue-plus-consumption basis versus 34% consumption-based today); RE capacity 973 MW, target 1,122 MW.
Targeted utilisation of 70-75% on a value-focused basis.
AFR (alternative fuel) share targeted at 12-15% in FY27 (currently about 7%) and 25% in the longer term.

RE capacity 973 MW (up about 500 MW over the year), with about 75 MW more commissioning; WHRS capacity 228 MW rising to about 376 MW by FY28.
Around 3.5 mtpa of old ACC plants temporarily suspended for about six months (Chaibasa, Marwar, Wadi, Lakheri cited by analysts); management says not permanent closures and no impairment expected.

Three coal blocks in pipeline, the first to be operational in about 30 months; investment payback 5-6 years.

Management cited Q1 disruptions from diesel shortages, packing material availability and geopolitical tensions as reasons for the YoY volume decline.
Brand pull and channel momentum in North, West, Central and East; South channel needs investment.
Capacity utilisation about 65% overall; management says value-focused utilisation target is 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company deliberately sacrificing volume for value, and will FY27 volume growth be muted or recouped in the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8% FY27 volume guidance holds, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY; it said market share was sustained or improved in trade while non-trade share was deliberately reduced.

qa_highlights.question: Where is green power heading, given 973 MW is already commissioned against a 1,122 MW target, and what is the economic benefit of captive use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 45 crore units were sold in Q1 and about 50% (~20 crore units) is expected to be consumed in Q2. The 34% share is consumption-based; on a revenue-plus-consumption basis it is about 48%, with a path to 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus green power cost in the range of INR3.3/unit per an analyst's arithmetic.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 cost outlook given geopolitical pressure, and is the FY27 INR4,250/t guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR100/t of potential cost rise in Q2 if geopolitical conditions persist, offset by INR130-150/t of identified savings and inventory of about 1 month clinker and 3 months coal. Net Q2 cost is expected slightly better than Q1 at INR4,241/t; FY27 INR4,250/t guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NSP lag peers and rise only about 1% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to accounting netting of certain expenses against NSP, Ex-works Incoterm shifts, and channel investment. It said NSP is market-driven and cost is the controllable lever.

qa_highlights.question: Which plants were temporarily suspended and is there any impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 mtpa of capacity is temporarily suspended for roughly six months, a mix of old ACC plants and one acquired-company plant across Central, East, North and South. Management said these are not permanent closures and no impairment is expected; the INR24 crore exceptional item relates to a VRS at a South India plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why did South and the acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi) see non-trade push and volume cuts, and how will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume in South was curtailed, with channel build-out needed for one to two quarters more. Orient runs at about 87% utilisation; Penna needs channel and trade investment; Sanghi is investing about INR600 crore in jetty expansion.

Green power grid connectivity for captive use (about 2-3 quarters) and the shift from sales to in-house consumption; the RMC EBITDA margin drop to about 7% from 14-15% needs explanation.
Status of the about 3.5 mtpa suspended capacity and the six-month restart, plus the Maratha clinker timeline slipping to FY28.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
Net operating cost reduced to INR4,241 per metric ton, a reduction of INR 206 PMT from the previous quarter.

500413|2026-03.headline: Thomas Cook (India) Q4 FY26 group revenue fell 10% YoY to INR 17,707 million as Middle East war hit DEI and Desert Adventures, while Sterling and India operations grew.
500413|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 in two phases: the first nine months were relatively stable (top line up 7%, EBITDA up marginally), while Q4 absorbed the Middle East conflict, airfare spikes and rupee weakness, with the Pahalgam/Operation Sindoor disruption earlier in the year. Full-year consolidated income rose 3% to INR 83,982 million (INR 85,578 million per closing remarks), but EBT fell 14% to INR 3,268 million. India operations grew EBT 16% in Q4, and Sterling posted record Q4 numbers. The board approved in-principle demerger of the resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts, with a timeline of Q1 FY28.

INR 1,701 million (31% margin) / INR 1,142 million (21% margin)

segments.commentary: FY26 turnover INR 27 billion (net basis) and revenue INR 1,541 million, +19% YoY; Q4 revenue +28%. Air volume +7.3% in Q4 and +4.8% for FY26.

segments.commentary: 78 resorts with about 3,800 rooms across 65 destinations; Q4 occupancy 64%, ARR +12% to INR 6,347, RevPAR +16%. Cash about INR 3,400 million and debt-free.

segments.commentary: About 50% of revenue from UAE; Q4 revenue INR 194 crore and EBIT negative INR 10 crore. Far East and APAC grew, and management expects Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did financial services top line and EBIT drop, and is margin being traded for share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 forex EBIT rose 17% and FY EBIT held at about INR 149 crore; the drop reflects mix shift and net revenue reporting with franchise revenue shares, not margin pressure. Float of about INR 16 billion was flat vs December, which management read as customers not spending.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sterling EBIT been flat at about INR 129 crore for two years despite rising room count?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani cited the end of membership acquisition revenue, a 2-3 month ramp-up lag for new resorts, and upfront costs. Krishna Kumar cited high ROU depreciation from leased resorts. EBITDA margin was 31% and EBIT margin 24%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DEI loss behind us and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram said the corrections are not done and the cost base will reduce over 30-60 days notice periods. He expects Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end and said FY26 will not match original plans. Debasis Nandy said top line depends on ground conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash and deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said net cash is close to INR 800 crore, to be used for technology capex, repayment of long-term loans over the next couple of years, and inorganic growth if returns criteria are met. An analyst's build-up gave about INR 730-740 crore, which was confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 outlook for Sterling and monsoon risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani said there are no headwinds so far in Q1; occupancy is expected to rise toward 65-70% over the year. Monsoon risk is being managed by asset protection and a geographically spread portfolio, with Q3 now the strongest quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said the process is on track for the 12-15 month plan, applications are with NSE and BSE, and completion is expected by Q1 FY28.

500413|2026-06.headline: Thomas Cook Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell 12% YoY to INR 21,530 million and PBT fell 21% to INR 885 million, driven by Middle East exposure.
500413|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income was INR 21,530 million, down 12% YoY, with PBT of INR 885 million, down 21%, mainly from Desert Adventures and DEI in the Middle East. Excluding the GCC subsidiaries, group EBIT grew 8%, and India businesses (forex, MICE, corporate travel, domestic) were stable to growing. Sterling Holidays reported its best quarter ever, with revenue up 21% and EBITDA up 21%. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, though it said H2 should be better than H1 if conditions hold.

segments.name: Foreign exchange
segments.commentary: Segment revenue +6% YoY, EBIT +8%, EBIT margin 45.3%. Retail turnover +8% YoY vs industry travel forex decline of ~8% (LRS Apr-May); education turnover +36%, digital penetration 23.5% vs 20.4%.

segments.name: Travel (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 17,106 million, -14% YoY; EBIT INR 405 million, -50%. Domestic +29%, short-haul +6% (+21% excluding Middle East), long-haul sales -28%. MICE +14% to INR 5,420 million; DMS -31% to INR 5,422 million with Desert Adventures revenue -89%.

segments.name: Sterling Holidays
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1.7 billion (+21%), EBITDA over INR 620 million (37% margin), PBT margin 28% (+200 bps). Occupancy 77% (+700 bps), ARR INR 7,809 (+10%), RevPAR +20%; net debt-free with cash above INR 3.7 billion.

segments.name: DEI (Digital Imaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,307 million vs INR 2,097 million; EBIT swung to INR -152 million from INR 106 million. About 50% of global business is in the Middle East; China site closures and Bahamas contract end added pressure. Net assets employed INR 243 crore.

segments.name: Desert Adventures (GCC)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 89% YoY; management estimated its EBIT impact at roughly INR 8-9 crore (about INR 90 million), not confirmed. Cost base did not flex as fast as volumes.

Long-haul deficit narrowed from about 28-30% to slightly lower levels in recent weeks; July and early August conversion better than Apr-Jun.

demand_pricing: Forex travel turnover declined alongside the industry, but education turnover grew 36% with NBFC partnerships and Study Buddy Card launch.

Sterling ARR +10% to INR 7,809 and occupancy +700 bps, indicating demand ahead of supply additions.
Short-haul ATV is 20-25% lower than long-haul, creating a mix headwind on revenue.
Management said margins are under pressure from higher airline costs and forex; tactical pricing used to keep capacity engaged.
TCS rate cut to 5% has had no visible impact on pricing; management called it a cash outflow, not a price change.

qa_highlights.question: How did underlying outbound leisure demand trend in July and early August, and do short-haul destinations carry comparable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said July and early August conversion was better than Apr-Jun but too early to call a shift. Short-haul margins are similar to long-haul, though short-haul ticket values are 20-25% lower.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thomas Cook pursue more airport forex counters over branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Airports are opportunistic, not a strategy; entry is made only at commercially rewarding terms, as with Delhi Airport.

qa_highlights.question: DEI: what are capital employed, normalised EBIT and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Net assets INR 243 crore; normal-year EBIT margin 6-7%; target 20% ROE. Major technology upgrade done, with periodic upgrades roughly every 10-12 years.

qa_highlights.question: Travel FY27 topline and EBIT margin outlook, and the TCS impact on pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 guidance. Internal EBIT margin range 4-5%. Management said it saw no clear TCS pricing benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the double-digit earnings growth guidance still achievable, and what is the split of GCC subsidiary impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not confirm double-digit growth. DEI EBIT moved from INR 10 crore profit to INR 15 crore loss (INR 25 crore delta). Detailed numbers to be obtained from Investor Relations.

qa_highlights.question: Will DEI cost optimisation show in Q2 results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visible benefits in Q2 and Q3 FY27; revenue recovery in the Middle East will determine earnings quality.

rows.why: Capex not discussed as a board plan; DEI ongoing capex is low with platform lasting 5-10 years on net assets of INR 243 crore, and Sterling expansion is asset-right (owned, leased, managed) rather than a large capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No FY27 guidance given and management could not confirm double-digit earnings growth; Q1 total income fell 12% and PBT fell 21%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Middle East recovery is sub-20% in Q1 and Desert Adventures revenue fell 89%, with its cost base not flexing as fast as volumes; Q1 PBT down 21% to INR 885 million and the full-year outlook remains unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Study Buddy Card launched in education, where turnover grew 36% with NBFC partnerships; no specific travel product launch date was given.

rows.label: DEI cost optimisation visible in Q2 and Q3 FY27
rows.why: Management expects visible DEI cost benefits in Q2 and Q3 FY27, against Q1 DEI EBIT of INR -152 million versus +INR 106 million a year earlier.

rows.label: Corporate travel and MICE pipeline
rows.why: Corporate gross turnover rose 15% to above INR 7 billion with 7 new accounts, and MICE revenue rose 14% to INR 5,420 million with over 110 groups booked.

rows.label: Sterling net debt-free with cash above INR 3.7 billion
rows.why: Sterling is net debt-free with cash above INR 3.7 billion, giving balance-sheet room for its pipeline of 2,000+ rooms.

500425|2026-03.headline: Ambuja FY26 volumes hit a record 73.7 Mt (+16%), but Q4 cost ran ~INR4,500/t and management reset FY27 guidance to ~80 Mt with capacity targets pushed out.
500425|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record volume year for Ambuja, with 73.7 million tonnes sold (up 16% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (up 31%, INR887/t). Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above the INR4,000 exit target, driven by acquired-asset underperformance (Sanghi 57%, Penna 46% utilization), freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management reset its growth plan: FY27 volumes ~80 Mt (~8%), capacity target 119 Mt by end-FY27 (vs earlier 140-155 Mt), FY27 capex INR6,000-6,500 crore, and a cost reduction of about INR250/t in FY27 plus INR250/t in FY28. Pricing has not offset cost inflation, with April-over-March hikes of about INR10/bag in a few areas.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 average cost per tonne

financial_highlights.value: about INR4,100/t normalized, INR4,500/t incl. escalation

financial_highlights.change: about INR1/bag QoQ; about INR255 a year ago

financial_highlights.metric: Premium cement share of trade sales

segments.name: Cement (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Capacity reached 109 Mt in FY26 after 10.7 Mt of new grinding and 7 Mt of clinker commissioning. Clinker capacity is 69 Mt, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).

segments.name: Sanghi Industries
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% for FY27. Turnaround is running behind schedule.

segments.name: Penna Cement
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% for FY27. Management said maintenance needs and breakdowns were higher than expected.

segments.name: Orient Cement
segments.commentary: Management said Orient is operating at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

segments.name: Green power
segments.commentary: Green power share rose to about 32% in Q4 from 26% earlier; INR150-200/t savings are expected from fly ash and green energy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume target of about 80 Mt, up about 8% from FY26; management described demand as soft, with industry growth of about 5-5.5%.
Cost reduction of about INR250/t on a full-year average in FY27 (target about INR4,250/t), with a further INR250/t reduction in FY28; Q1 FY27 cost expected flat at about INR4,500/t.
Capacity target lowered to about 119 Mt by end-FY27 from earlier 140-155 Mt; management said the FY28 capacity plan could slip by 1-2 years, to about FY30.
FY27 capex estimate of INR6,000-6,500 crore, with about INR4,000 crore already under execution; project IRR hurdle set at 18%.
Expected 10 Mt of capacity commissioning between now and September, including Salai Banwa and Warisaliganj; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) are planned for about 24-28 months out.
Management said it will not provide EBITDA/t guidance for now; the 15 Mt debottlenecking plan continues but timing may change.
capex_capacity: Capacity at 109 Mt; target 119 Mt by end-FY27 after about 10 Mt of ongoing additions including Salai Banwa and Warisaliganj.
Clinker capacity 69 Mt today; Maratha adds 4 Mt, and Mundra and Assam add 2 Mt each over about 24-28 months.

Management plans to shut some integrated-unit grinding capacity and move grinding closer to markets (North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat, Maharashtra); Bihar grinding to be set up, with Chhattisgarh becoming clinker-only.
Penna and Sanghi together hold 19 Mt of capacity; target is to raise their utilization by 5-10 points.
Efficiency capex (fly ash railway infrastructure and similar projects) is delayed by 3-6 months; benefits are expected from the coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand was muted, with volume growth of about 10% in the investor deck; excluding Orient, management acknowledged volumes were roughly flat YoY in the March quarter.
Industry prices rose about INR10/bag in March quarter, with INR15-20 gains in select pockets; April demand was described as subdued.
Premium cement is about 36% of trade sales; the gap to base product is about INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium.
Management said it would be happy with half of any industry price hike, given weak demand; price pass-through has not kept pace with cost.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth is flattish ex-Orient in Q4, yet FY27 guidance implies about 8-10% growth on softer industry demand. What drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited stabilizing Sanghi and Penna plus about 10 Mt of new capacity commissioning between now and September 2026, which will be needed to reach 80 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook given the INR4,000/t exit target versus the reported INR4,500/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for March exit; the March month was about INR4,100/t normalized, and INR4,500/t is the peak. A reduction of INR150-200/t is expected from fly ash and green energy, and INR250/t is the FY27 average target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Ambuja's fixed cost rising faster than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher branding (about INR70/t for FY26), repairs and maintenance at acquired assets, freight, lower government incentives and higher heat consumption. Acquired assets were said to drag EBITDA by about INR70-80/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is the reset of capacity and timelines a change in ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned but the timeline has moved; capacity was stepped back to 119 Mt by end-FY27. Capital will be deployed only after current projects are completed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 'core' versus 'non-core' working capital movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core working capital fell from 30 to 20 days; non-core rose, partly from incentives accounted on an as-received basis, and some of the increase could be accounting-driven. ACC's negative operating cash flow reflects receivables from Ambuja under the MSA, which are to be settled via an ICD.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any EBITDA/t guidance or an IRR target for new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA/t guidance was given. Karan Adani said the project IRR hurdle is 18% on all-equity funding.

risks_watch: Acquired assets (Sanghi, Penna) remain well below target utilization and have had breakdowns; FY27 volume depends on them.
Q4 cost of about INR4,500/t was higher than guided; West Asia-related packing and fuel inflation of about INR250/t is an open risk, and Q1 FY27 cost is expected flat.
Price realization of about INR254/bag is flat QoQ, with limited pricing power in soft demand.
Capex has been delayed (Maratha, Chhattisgarh), and project timelines have been pushed out; the FY28 capacity plan may slip to FY30.
Working capital and non-core receivables rose sharply, and management said the non-core figure was partly accounting-driven; follow-up needed.
Sanghi railway (Naliya) and marine logistics timelines; 7 vessels to be delivered from next year.
Pending JP assets; management declined to comment as the seller is a listed company.
500425|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and self-critical: management admitted under-delivery on cost, capex timelines and acquired-asset utilization, and reset guidance. Forward targets were framed as conditional on internal execution, with explicit caution on demand, pricing and fuel-cost volatility.
key_quotes: Ambuja delivered a resilient performance for the year, achieving its highest ever annual sales volume of 73.7 million tonnes, up 16% Y-on-Y
We are moving away from the time line.
It's capex -- I mean, the project IRR has to be 18%. this is all equity money.

rows.why: Q4 cost was ~INR4,500/t vs FY26 INR4,400/t; management guides a INR250/t cut in FY27 from fly ash, green power (share ~32% in Q4 vs 26%, INR150-200/t savings) and Sanghi/Penna fixes, but Q1 FY27 cost is flat at ~INR4,500/t and pricing (~INR254/bag, flat QoQ) is not keeping pace with cost, and no EBITDA/t guidance is given.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: FY27 capex is firmly set at INR6,000-6,500 crore against FY26 spend of ~INR7,500 crore, with Mundra and Assam clinker (2 Mt each) planned in ~24-28 months and capital to be deployed only after current projects complete; utilisation is 57%/46% at acquired assets, so near-term new capex is restrained.

rows.why: Guidance was reset down (capacity cut to 119 Mt from 140-155 Mt, FY28 may slip to ~FY30) and Q1 FY27 cost is flat at ~INR4,500/t against the INR4,000 exit aspiration.

rows.why: Volume target of ~80 Mt needs Sanghi/Penna utilisation gains and on-time commissioning, Q4 volume was roughly flat ex-Orient, April demand subdued, and West Asia packing/fuel inflation of ~INR250/t is an open risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Not discussed in the call beyond premium cement at ~36% of trade sales.

rows.why: Management plans to shut some integrated-unit grinding and set up Bihar grinding, with Chhattisgarh becoming clinker-only, targeting logistics cost savings against FY26 cost of INR4,400/t.

rows.label: Sanghi and Penna utilisation recovery
rows.why: Sanghi at 57% (target 65-70%) and Penna at 46% (target 55-60%), with the turnaround running behind schedule and maintenance and breakdowns above expectations; targets are conditional on execution.

500425|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA INR1,589 crore (16.7% margin, +331 bps QoQ), net cost INR4,241/t, down INR206/t QoQ; trade volumes -2% YoY.
500425|2026-06.overview: Management reported revenue of about INR9,500 crore, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crore, and PAT of INR660 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA per ton of INR931 (grey cement INR911). Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management says is on track for the INR4,250/t full-year guidance despite about INR110/t West Asia-related inflation. Volumes fell sharply: total volume was down about 7% YoY, trade down 2% and non-trade down 21%, as the company deliberately exited low-margin volumes, mainly in South and at acquired assets. Management guided to 8% trade volume growth for FY27 and said July trade volumes were up 8% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: down INR206/t QoQ; FY27 guidance INR4,250/t

financial_highlights.value: down about 7% YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

financial_highlights.change: trade share of sales 78% vs 74% prior quarter

financial_highlights.value: about 45 crore units; revenue about INR140 crore
financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26: about 24 crore units, about INR70 crore

financial_highlights.value: Lower in Q1 due to merger true-up; run rate to stay at Q4-level

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade share rose to 78% from 74%; premium products are 34% of trade sales. Trade volume -2% YoY, non-trade -21% YoY.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA cluster per management; trade volumes grew 2% YoY while low-margin non-trade fell sharply.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Trade and non-trade both grew positively per management; Mumbai and Gujarat carry higher-margin non-trade volumes.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Deliberate exit of about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume; highest decline in the region. Trade sales only recently started picking up.

segments.name: Central / East
segments.commentary: Central: volumes declined as blended cement was pushed for margin. East: trade volumes sustained with healthy margins.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: RMC EBITDA about INR33 crore in Q1, versus margins of about 14-15% in the prior four quarters; management cited raw material pricing and lease accounting.

guidance_outlook: FY27 net cost guidance INR4,250/t, reaffirmed; management expects INR130-150/t of savings from initiatives, against a possible INR100/t rise in Q2 from geopolitical pressure.
FY27 trade volume growth guidance of 8%, with trade expected to be upwards of 75% of sales; July trade volumes up 8% YoY.
Capacity to reach about 119 Mt by end FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt), then 8-10 Mt of organic additions per year; FY28 capex in a run rate of INR6,000-7,000 crore.
FY28 green power share targeted at 60% (about 48% on combined sales-plus-consumption basis); RE capacity 1,122 MW by FY28.
Target cost of INR4,000/t or below by end FY28 (about INR250/t further reduction).
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt today; trial runs at Dahej (1.2 Mt expansion) and Salai Banwa, UP (2.4 Mt) have started; Jodhpur (2 Mt commissioned, 3 Mt clinker trials) to stabilise in Q2 and be treated as commissioned in the September quarter.

Kalamboli, Mumbai (1 Mt) and Warisaliganj, Bihar (2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 (Warisaliganj likely September); Bhatinda (1.2 Mt) commissioned; Maratha clinker line moved to Q1 FY28; Mundra expected in about 18-24 months.
RE capacity 973 MW (about 1,122 MW target); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW; power cost reduced to about INR4.9/kWh from INR5.9.
About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily suspended for about six months; not permanent closure, per management.
Sanghi jetty and clinker expansion about INR600 crore; Penna AFR and WHRS investments INR100-150 crore; first coal block about 30 months away.
demand_pricing: Management said cement demand was stable in Q1, supported by infrastructure and housing; diesel shortages, packing material issues and East/West logistics disruptions hit Q1 volumes.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed this to Incoterm/ex-works changes and netting of certain channel costs, and said NSP is market-driven.
Analyst comparison: Ambuja NSP about INR100 below UltraTech's reported NSP in Q1, against an average premium of about INR50 over the prior quarters.
Management said Q2 net cost would be slightly better than the June-quarter level, after allowing for part of the geopolitical cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes be muted in FY27 given the value-over-volume approach, and can lost Q1 share be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of 8% trade volume growth on July momentum (+8% YoY); it said share was sustained or improved in trade and was deliberately reduced in non-trade.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of green power sales and when will it be consumed in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; management expects about 50% consumed in Q2 (about 20 crore units). Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus green power savings, and at most 10% will be sold going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR206/t cost decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fly ash sourcing, RE power, clinker factor (down about 2-3%), logistics (-INR10/t) and fixed cost optimisation; gross savings were about INR316/t after absorbing INR110/t of West Asia inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ASP up only marginally QoQ and below peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited accounting netting of certain expenses against NSP, ex-works Incoterm effects, and a Q1 disruption; it expects NSP to move in line with industry.

qa_highlights.question: Acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi, Orient): what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Orient at 87% utilisation with minimal investment; Penna needs about INR100-150 crore and a channel push in the South; Sanghi investing INR600 crore in a jetty and improving utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Ambuja-level ICD given to the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as part of the MSA arrangement, with Ambuja supplying about 3 Mt of cement to ACC; the ICDs are at 8% coupon and within approved limits, and merger is in advanced stages.

risks_watch: Trade volumes still negative YoY in Q1; the 8% FY27 growth target implies a steep ramp (about 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months per analyst math).
Q2 cost pressure from geopolitical escalation (possible INR100/t rise); clinker and coal inventories give about one month and three months of cover respectively.
Suspended capacity (about 3.5 Mt) and South volume exits (about 1 Mt); restart timing and the impact on fixed-cost absorption remain open.
Maintenance cost accounting: management is still engaging auditors on spreading O&M cost across four quarters; Q1 reflected actuals.
Green power consumption depends on grid connectivity for some plants, expected in two to three quarters; RMC margin fell to about 7% from 14-15%.
500425|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on cost and capacity delivery, with specific numbers for savings and commissioning, but noticeably defensive on volume decline and NSP gap versus peers, attributing both to one-off disruptions and accounting netting. Several answers on ICDs, RMC margin, cost reconciliation and the Orient valuation were deferred offline.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
And I would not shy highlighting that we are already seeing an 8% improvement on the trade volumes.
Having a sustainable performance matters more than anything.
Yes, you might be leaving the volume, but you're not leaving value on the table.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Net cost INR4,241/t, down INR206/t QoQ, is on track for INR4,250/t FY27 guidance, with INR130-150/t of further savings expected against a possible INR100/t Q2 geopolitical rise; EBITDA/t INR931 vs 16.7% margin up 331 bps QoQ.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity moves from 109 Mt to about 119 Mt by end FY27; Jodhpur 2 Mt commissioned (September quarter), Kalamboli 1 Mt and Warisaliganj 2.4 Mt due Q2, with Dahej 1.2 Mt and Salai Banwa 2.4 Mt already in trials.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 8% trade volume growth for FY27 with July trade up 8% YoY, but Q1 trade was -2% YoY and total volume about -7%, so the back-nine-months ramp of about 12-13% is steep and capacity utilisation is only about 65%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 65% with about 10.2 Mt of capacity already being added to reach 119 Mt, so a fresh capex push is not indicated; FY27 capex is held at about INR6,500 crore and FY28 run rate INR6,000-7,000 crore is already planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed the INR4,250/t cost, 8% volume and 119 Mt capacity guidance without raising it, and flagged a possible INR100/t Q2 cost rise from geopolitical pressure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade volume was -2% YoY in Q1 and the 8% FY27 target needs about 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months, while Q2 cost could rise by INR100/t and about 3.5 Mt of ACC capacity is suspended.

rows.label: NSP gap versus UltraTech narrowing
rows.why: Ambuja NSP is about INR100/t below UltraTech in Q1 versus an average premium of about INR50 earlier, and management says NSP is market-driven and expects it to move in line with industry.

rows.label: ACC intercompany loan (ICD) repayment under merger
rows.why: ICDs to the parent are at 8% coupon and within approved limits, with about 3 Mt cement supplied to ACC under MSA, but the treatment was deferred offline.

rows.label: Green power self-consumption and RE build-out
rows.why: About 50% of 45 crore units sold in Q1 expected to be consumed in-house in Q2 (about 20 crore units), power cost down to INR4.9/kWh from INR5.9, and RE capacity 973 MW rising toward 1,122 MW by FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost savings (INR4,250/t guide, INR130-150/t more savings) and commissioning dates, but defensive on the volume decline and the NSP gap to UltraTech; analysts pushed on the steep 8% volume ramp, NSP discount and RMC margin fall to about 7%, and several items were deferred

500440|2026-03.headline: Hindalco Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore on Oswego fire, but adjusted PAT rose 10% to INR5,796 crore.
500440|2026-03.overview: Consolidated business-segment EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR10,812 crore, while reported PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore due to exceptional items including the Novelis Oswego plant fire. India business segment EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR6,610 crore and PAT rose 11% to INR3,549 crore. Copper EBITDA hit a record INR907 crore on higher by-product (sulfuric acid) realisations, while Novelis adjusted EBITDA was about $498 million ($543/t). Management expects Novelis to recover in FY27 as Oswego hot mill restarts and Bay Minette ramps.

segments.name: India aluminium upstream
segments.commentary: Shipments +2% YoY, revenue +11% YoY, EBITDA INR5,448 crore at $1,756/t. Q4 cost rose about 2.4% QoQ; Q1 FY27 guided about 5% higher, mainly furnace oil.

segments.name: India aluminium downstream
segments.commentary: Shipments 124 KT (+18% YoY), EBITDA INR255 crore (+16% YoY), $226/t, driven by volume, mix and premiumisation.

segments.name: Copper (India)
segments.commentary: Record EBITDA INR907 crore (+48% YoY) on by-product realisations and efficiencies; metal shipments 128 KT (-5%), CCR volumes 91 KT (+11%).

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 917 KT (-4% YoY) excluding 73 KT Oswego loss; adjusted EBITDA $498 million ($543/t). Impacts: $53 million Oswego fire, $27 million tariffs, offset by $41 million Sierre flood insurance recovery.

guidance_outlook: Novelis: Oswego hot mill to restart in the next few weeks; current-year headwinds expected to substantially recover in FY27; long-term $600/t EBITDA target intact.
Novelis cost programme: FY26 exit run-rate savings raised to $200 million (from $125 million target); 3-year structural cost cut of $350-400 million by FY28 exit.

Novelis Bay Minette 600 KT greenfield plant: cold mill commissioning started, hot mill commissioning from next month, commercial coils in FY28, 18-24 month ramp; start-up costs of about $100-150 million annually expected below EBITDA.
India copper TC/RCs: more than 85% contracted at benchmark; expected close to zero or slightly negative for FY27.
India copper EBITDA: Q1 FY27 similar to Q4 (INR900 crore range) but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3.

India capex FY27 about INR12,000 crore (later framed as INR15,000-17,000 crore for the next year); Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, mainly Bay Minette; consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over next 2 years; net leverage around 2x.
Aluminium market: deficit now 1.5 million t for CY26 (from 0.3 million t), tightest in Q2-Q3 CY26.
Renewable capacity 470 MW at year end, rising to 523 MW by end Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Aditya smelter: first 180 pots by December 2027, next 180 pots by December 2028; management says timelines look firm.

Captive coal: Chakla box cut expected in next 2 months, first coal possibly Q4 FY27; Bandha box cut done but first coal only in FY28 due to high strip ratio; Meenakshi (strip ratio under 1) expected to add substantial volumes in FY29; Chakla Stage 1 forest clearance received.

Downstream: Aditya FRP ramping up; battery enclosure at full ramp-up; Aditya battery foil commissioned; Taloja AC fin facility commissioning; specialty alumina precipitate hydrate commissioned, under customer approval.

Copper: inner grooved tubes (35 KT) in customer qualification; 50 KT Pakhajan e-waste recycling plant to commission in August; copper smelter about 3 years out; battery grade copper foil scaled down to a smaller capacity in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Aluminium prices strengthened in the quarter; West Asia conflict disrupted supply; global market now seen in 1.5 million t deficit for CY26.
India Q4 FY26 aluminium demand about 1.6 million t, +9% YoY; India copper demand 402 KT, +10% YoY.
Q4 FY26 hedges: aluminium 64% at INR2,807/t; currency 26% at INR88/$. FY27 hedges: aluminium 29% at $3,013/t; currency 14% at INR90.13/$.
Sulfuric acid prices high due to Middle East conflict and China export restrictions; management expects Q1 FY27 to be slightly above Q4 but could correct if Strait of Hormuz reopens.
Global concentrate TC/RCs at record lows around -$0.21 to -$0.25/lb; expected to stay negative through FY27.
Alumina sales 211 KT in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY27 guided at about 170 KT.
Midwest premium at about $380/t due to 50% US tariffs; Japan premium up on supply tightness and freight. Domestic vs export realisation gap narrowed; exports may be slightly higher in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q4 copper EBITDA reflect the full sulfuric acid price surge, and how sustainable is the INR900 crore run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 expected in the same range given high sulfuric acid, but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3 and cautioned that Hormuz reopening could correct sulfur prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India and consolidated capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India FY27 capex about INR12,000 crore, rising to INR15,000-17,000 crore in the following year; Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, falling sharply in FY28 after Bay Minette. Consolidated capex expected to be lower than current levels; FY28 detail deferred to Q3/Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt breakdown and peak?
qa_highlights.answer: India gross debt INR12,200 crore, cash INR18,000 crore (net cash INR6,000 crore). Novelis gross debt INR75,000 crore, cash INR11,000 crore (net debt INR63,000 crore). Consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over the next 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is $600/t Novelis EBITDA assuming current scrap spreads and start-up costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management does not assume current spreads or metal prices; start-up costs sit below EBITDA. The $600/t target is seen as sustainable, not reliant on current tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How do coal captive mines change costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chakla and Bandha expected at similar cost to market coal; Meenakshi substantially lower. Captive mines expected to flatten the cost curve over 15-20 years; meaningful captive volumes only from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis avoid shipping to Canada given tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is mitigating tariffs by using US cold mill capacity, including additional capacity secured at Logan; Kingston (Ontario) mill longer-term planning still pending.

risks_watch: Oswego hot mill restart timing and the resulting Novelis volume recovery in Q1 FY27.
Tariff exposure (Midwest premium, US-Canada flows) and possible relief from governments.
Input cost inflation: Q1 FY27 cost guided about 5% higher, driven by furnace oil; CP coke and pitch also rising.
Sulfuric acid and TC/RC normalisation could reduce copper EBITDA from the current run-rate if Hormuz reopens.
Captive coal ramp-up delays (Bandha high strip ratio) and Aditya smelter timelines.
Net debt rising toward INR80,000-90,000 crore; net leverage target around 2x.
Battery-grade copper foil and battery demand in India slower than expected.
