500940|2026-06.headline: Finolex Q1 FY27: volume fell 27% YoY to ~68,000 MT, while EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin widened to 12%.
500940|2026-06.overview: Volumes fell 27% YoY to about 68,000 MT as PVC price volatility triggered channel destocking, with April the weakest month and May and June growing per management. Revenue fell 27% to INR884 crore from INR1,043 crore, but EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin improved from 9% to 12%, which management attributed mainly to top-line realization rather than cost. PAT was about INR107 crore and cash stood at INR2,636 crore. Management said July was the best month of the four, with a minimum price floor from the MIP and customs duty withdrawal, but declined to give full-year volume or margin guidance beyond reiterating the sub-15% margin view.

segments.name: Agri pipes
segments.commentary: Agri was 69% of volume; agri volume fell 27% YoY. Fittings were 5% of agri and 11% of total volume.

segments.name: Non-agri / plumbing
segments.commentary: Non-agri was about 25% of volume (fittings 25% within non-agri per management); volume fell ~24% YoY, versus ~18-20% industry peers per management.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC was about 7% of volume in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 volume guidance; management said it is too early and will revisit after Q2 trends.
Margin: reiterated the Q4 FY26 view of sub-15% EBITDA margin, with no revision.
Management expects a somewhat better Q2 on realizations after the MIP-driven price floor; said it was hopeful H1 volume could be flattish YoY, with a plus possible if July's pace holds.

Capex: capital outlay of INR125-200 crore per year for expansion and debottlenecking, unchanged. Installed capacity 520 (unit as stated), FY26 volume 333, headroom for 10-12% growth over roughly the next 1-1.5 years.
Other income of ~INR75 crore in the quarter is mark-to-market and driven by bond yields, so it is not guaranteed to recur at that level.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity stated as 520 (units not specified); FY26 volume 333. Management says there is headroom to grow 10-12% over the next 1-1.5 years.
Growth is coming through debottlenecking, replacing lower-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones, rather than large greenfield or brownfield projects.
Capex outlay remains INR125-200 crore, unchanged.

Ratnagiri PVC: EDC-based line running without interruption. VCM-based line does not run during the June-September monsoon months because the Ratnagiri jetty is fair-weather only. VCM availability is constrained by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints.
CPVC extrusion capacity is considered sufficient for near-term CPVC growth, according to management.
demand_pricing: Average PVC price in Q1 was about USD875/MT versus USD707/MT a year earlier (ICIS), carried over from elevated Q4 FY26 levels. A sharp intra-quarter correction in April triggered channel destocking.
Management cited INR96 to INR92 to INR82/kg as the PVC price path through April. Analyst cited a INR12-13/kg hike in the last 15-20 days after the MIP and duty changes.
Customs duty exemption on PVC resin was withdrawn in mid-July, and a minimum import price (MIP) was imposed. Management said these should support price stability and channel inventory.
Pass-through: management said almost all of the recent price increase (barring INR1-2) has been passed to customers.
Demand: July was the best month of the four, with a strong pickup; August to date was described as moving in the right direction.
Channel inventory is near normal, with some room left. A lot of stocking occurred in July in anticipation of price increases. Quantification in days was not given.
PVC-EDC spread was ~USD501/MT in Q1 FY27 versus ~USD522 a year earlier, and ~USD490 currently. PVC-VCM spread was INR122/kg in Q1 FY27 versus INR163 a year earlier.
Pricing: management said Finolex prices ~10-12% above Supreme-type peers in the market (ballpark only).
Market share: management said FY26 share of the top 5-6 reporting companies was about 22%, and it sees no change in Q1. An analyst cited FY23 share of about 27%.
JJM 2.0: management said the outlay is about INR67,000 crore, not higher than JJM 1.0. All sales go through channel partners, so there is no direct correlation to volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realization not rise QoQ when peers reported 7-9% jumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realization per kg was up ~15% vs the same quarter last year and was in line with peers. It said Q4 FY26 was an aberration with a sharp price rise, and that falling PVC prices in April drove the QoQ result. Discounts and incentives also affect net realization.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the volume decline was agri vs non-agri, and what were the monthly trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri fell 27% and non-agri fell ~24% YoY. April was the weakest month, May grew and June was normal. Management did not give monthly figures and said it would reach out separately.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion despite falling volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was largely top-line driven, with costs range-bound. It cited backward integration and the timing of raw material procurement as a cushion. It did not quantify inventory gains or losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year volume decline? Can H1 be flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide full-year volume. It said July was a good month and that flattish H1 YoY is possible, with a plus if July's pace holds, while August and September are still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy the INR2,636 crore cash into CPVC capacity and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CPVC extrusion capacity is sufficient and CPVC is about 7-8% of the PVC pipe market, which Finolex matches. It said the Board decides on cash deployment or returns and will announce when a decision is made.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin guidance sub-15% when Q1 delivered 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is holding the sub-15% guidance from Q4 because of volatility in Q1 and wants another quarter of data before revising it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM supply situation and the PVC plant utilization outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VCM availability is limited by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints. The VCM line does not run during monsoon months (about June to September) because of the fair-weather jetty. Management said efforts to secure supply are ongoing and H2 is uncertain.

501423|2026-03.headline: Shaily FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR991 crores and PAT 83% to INR170 crores, led by Healthcare revenue up 139% to INR393 crores.
501423|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR237 crores with EBITDA margin of 29.3% and PAT of INR40 crores (up 40%). Healthcare doubled in Q4 to INR113 crores on Semaglutide pen injector commercial launches in Canada and India, while Consumer fell 31% to INR102 crores on weak US and European home furnishing demand. Management announced a semiconductor tray supply agreement and first commercial supplies to a consumer electronics customer, and an INR500 crore enabling fundraise resolution (described as annual, with no specific raise planned). The pen capacity ramp is behind plan: the 25 million-unit line added in March runs at about 45% efficiency.

qa_highlights.answer: The March 25 million line runs at about 45% efficiency; the second 25 million line due July-August is purely Semaglutide. Target is 65-67 ppm per line, giving a combined 40-42 million pens by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 pen target still 36 million or higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reconfirmed about 36 million pens for FY27 (order book frozen); the August line is the main uncertainty and a better view will come around Sep-Oct earnings call.

qa_highlights.question: What are margin and capex implications for consumer electronics?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins will be thin until scale of roughly 15-20 million units; initial plant capex about INR100 crores; no segment margin numbers given as it is B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR500 crore enabling resolution signal a fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is an annual enabling resolution for flexibility; no capital is being raised now, and any future need would be a one-off large capex for device capacity outside India and Abu Dhabi.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the semiconductor tray opportunity and how competitive is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Shaily aims to supply all Indian chip manufacturers; management called it a volume consumable business and said it expects to be sole manufacturing partner in India for this customer on technical competence in conductive plastics.

qa_highlights.question: Why did UK subsidiary margins and growth weaken?
qa_highlights.answer: Longer-term, milestone-based projects delay revenue recognition; management asked investors to view UK and UAE margins combined and to judge margins on a year-on-year basis.

demand_pricing: Healthcare: Management estimates device volumes of ~9 million pens in Q1 (all delivery devices); mix roughly 50-60% GLP-1, remainder insulin and other molecules.
Pricing is volume and market-driven with annual price review, not cost-plus; index references include inflation and polymers, with contract longevity a key factor.
Chinese GLP-1 pens reportedly priced at $1.50-1.70 vs Shaily's above $2; management said some Chinese products infringe patents and it is considering a response.
Gross margin fell sequentially due to post-March commodity and freight cost spikes, premium airfreight, and delayed pass-throughs.
Consumer: softer home furnishing demand in Europe and US; India is ~2% of Consumer sales.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and pricing versus Chinese competition?

qa_highlights.question: Comfort with 36 million guidance given partner issues in Canada and Brazil?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap in supply must be filled and it still holds most approvals in various markets; it remains confident in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Time to reach $10 million revenue in Consumer Electronics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projected 24-30 months, explicitly not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Consumer Electronics plant and Semiconductor Trays?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial supply started; 5 components to be supplied before FY-end. Semiconductor Trays: INR5 crore initial investment; Consumer Electronics plant INR80-100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Development status of emergency use, reusable and on-body injectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Reusable auto-injector to be tested this month or next and shown at CPHI Milan. Emergency use program ~18 months in, targeted for closure by end-FY27. On-body injector via partnership, developed from the Mira prototype.

501455|2026-03.headline: Greaves Cotton Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 1,000 crores, with EBITDA up 49% to INR 68 crores.
501455|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR 1,000 crores (+22% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 68 crores (+49%) and PBT before exceptional items of INR 44 crores. Standalone Q4 revenue was INR 698 crores (+22%) but standalone EBITDA rose only 4% to INR 87 crores after a commodity-driven gross margin drop. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 3,437 crores (+18%), with EBITDA of INR 239 crores (+76%). Management took a ~INR 16 crore provision on an e-powertrain asset impairment and flagged rising input costs (aluminium, copper, platinum) as a near-term margin pressure.

segments.name: Energy Solutions (gensets, aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 18% and FY26 growth of 20%; aftermarket grew 23% in Q4 and 35% in FY26. Secured a single largest institutional order of INR 35 crores and launched a 650 kVA genset with in-house engine.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions (auto engines, aftermarket, Excel)
segments.commentary: Automotive business grew 48% YoY in Q4 on three-wheeler diesel demand and Euro V+ exports; FY26 segment growth was 16%. Non-3W diesel is 63% of mobility; exited two-wheeler parts, construction equipment and some battery/digital businesses.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions (special purpose engines)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 15% YoY; defence order (engines to repower army trucks) under execution. Macro described as mixed, with critical applications resilient.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (investee)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 786 crores (+19%), volumes +51%, market share 4.4% vs 3.6% in FY25. EBITDA loss narrowed from about -30% to about -20% of revenue (per management, standalone and consol). Targeted IPO deadline extended by SEBI to 30 September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Core businesses (Energy, Mobility, Industrial) medium-term organic growth of 16-18% YoY, reiterated.
Core business EBITDA margin maintained at 13-15% as the business scales.
Capex of INR 500-700 crores over the next 4-5 years across product development, capability/capacity enhancement, and international expansion; no year-wise split given.
Excel Controlinkage: remaining 20% stake to be acquired in Q2 FY27, taking ownership to 100%.
Retail aftermarket to grow 6-8%; industrial business to contribute to the 16-18% core target.
Input cost pass-through mechanism activated in Q1 FY27; management cautious on commodity cycle.
capex_capacity: Capex plan INR 500-700 crores over 4-5 years, split across product development, operations capability, and international market expansion (Middle East, Europe; North America under watch).
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant: dual conveyor for single-cylinder engines to increase capacity; robotic vision-based AI inspection system deployed.
Excel: conveyorised cable assembly line commissioned in Nagpur; automation investment made.
Launched 650 kVA genset based on in-house engine; new products expected to contribute from coming months.
Management stated the total capex envelope is static, with near-term capacity coming from extra shifts and working hours.
demand_pricing: Q4 Energy Solutions growth driven by integrated service model, retail annual maintenance contract launch, and expanded distributor presence in under-leveraged regions.
Commodity price increase (aluminium, copper, platinum) in Q4 compressed standalone gross margin YoY and sequentially; pass-through activated in Q1 FY27.
Auto industry grew 9% in FY26 per management; three-wheeler diesel holds 63% share of the diesel segment (industry split 40% electric, 40% CNG, 20% diesel).
International revenue rose to 13% of total in FY26 from about 9% in FY25, supported by Ligier micro-car Euro V+ engine exports.
Excel export business slowed due to Ukraine war headwinds; domestic business grew in double digits in FY26.
EV: strong Q4 volumes, March the best month ever; L5 3W volumes +31% YoY in Q4 and +17% in FY26; Hinduja Leyland Finance tie-up offers up to 95% on-road LTV.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13-15% EBITDA margin guidance for standalone/core or consolidated, and what is the path for Greaves Electric losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin guidance refers to core businesses (standalone plus Excel and Greaves Technologies), excluding investee GEML and GFL. Management cited GEML EBITDA improving from about -30% to -20%; it declined to quantify break-even or cash-loss timelines citing DRHP constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 a new base for core growth, and when will Excel reach 100% ownership?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 16-18% mid-term core growth. The final 20% of Excel is planned for Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin decline YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher RMC in Q4 from commodity cycle since March; aluminium, copper, platinum pressures. Pass-through activated in Q1, volume-led operating leverage and cost actions expected to offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving 20% Energy Solutions growth; is it outpacing the genset industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is keeping pace with industry growth; drivers are integrated sales and service teams, technician presence, retail AMC program, and distributor expansion in under-leveraged regions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 given only about INR 30-36 crores of PP&E spend?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual split given; the INR 500-700 crore envelope is over 4-5 years and the total is unchanged, with near-term focus on capability and capacity enhancement and new product development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there guidance on RoCE and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding about INR 900 crores (GEML/GFL capital and group cash of INR 500+ crores), core capital employed is about INR 700 crores with healthy returns; investee capital and cash to be deployed over 2-3 years. Incentives are tied to growth and capital discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Is a 3-wheeler low-speed or non-RTO EV scooter segment being addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the low-speed segment is a priority; Reo brand already sells in it and B2B demand is growing; looking at it closely.

risks_watch: Commodity cost inflation (aluminium, copper, platinum) and the pace of pass-through recovery in Q1 FY27; standalone EBITDA grew only 4% in Q4.
GEML losses and funding need: no break-even or cash-loss timeline given; IPO timing dependent on SEBI-extended DRHP validity to 30 September 2026.
Impairment of about INR 16 crores on an e-powertrain project that has not scaled; further write-downs possible.
Excel export slowdown from Ukraine war; Excel 100% buyout in Q2 FY27 is a cash outflow.
Capex execution: only about INR 30-36 crores of PP&E in FY26 vs INR 500-700 crore five-year plan.
Retail aftermarket growth guided only 6-8%; core growth target relies on Industrial and new Energy products.
Geopolitical volatility affecting exports and EV demand.

501455|2026-06.headline: Greaves Cotton Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% YoY to INR975 crores, but margins fell 2-2.5 percentage points on investments and commodity costs.
501455|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to INR975 crores and core businesses grew 16% to INR710 crores (19% like-for-like after portfolio exits). Margins came under pressure by 2 to 2.5 percentage points, which management attributed to about 1.5 points of deliberate Greaves.Next investments and commodity inflation (platinum, aluminium, steel, fuel) that pricing has only partly offset. Management said Q2 will be marginally better than Q1 and H2 better than H1, and that it remains committed to full-year FY27 margin targets. GEML revenue was about INR270 crores, roughly double last year, with market share reported at 5.6% in June.

segments.name: Energy Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY; medium-horsepower gensets grew 32% YoY. A pilot BESS facility was commissioned and a large institutional order covering supply, installation, commissioning and aftersales was executed.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY; automotive engines grew 36% YoY. Retail aftermarket pruning is complete (2-wheeler spares, lead-acid batteries, multi-brand EV retail, farm equipment exited). Excel grew 14% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions
segments.commentary: Reported revenue flat YoY and 9% growth after portfolio rationalisation. FM-UL compliant firefighting engine exports started and a large defence order was completed.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML)
segments.commentary: Record Q1 volume growth of 101% YoY vs industry 75%. Market share rose to 5.6% in June from 4.5% exit FY26; 2-wheeler revenue up ~120% and 3-wheeler up ~80% YoY. Dealer network expanded from ~300 to 600.

segments.name: Greaves Finance (GFL)
segments.commentary: AUM at INR560 crores, growing; Board approved an additional ~INR50 crores investment.

guidance_outlook: Greaves.Next target of 16-20% revenue CAGR for the next few years reiterated; management says it is on track for the 16% growth guided for the current period.
Price increases and cost-avoidance measures expected to show from Q2, with full benefit in H2 FY27.
Q2 margin expected marginally better than Q1; H2 expected to make up any H1 shortfall; full-year FY27 margin target reiterated.
GEML expected to move into positive EBITDA in 4 to 6 quarters; management declined to give specifics.
GEML double-digit national market share targeted in 4 to 8 quarters, based on roughly 1-1.5 points of share gain every 3 to 4 quarters.
Current capital infusion expected to fund GEML for about 2 years including capex, with burn rates now in single digits.
capex_capacity: GEML invested INR331 crores via rights issue (total INR530 crore issue, fully subscribed by GCL and Abdul Latif Jameel in proportion to holding).
GEML 2-wheeler production capacity is about 480,000 units.
Robotic gantry cell commissioned at CSN facility; Excel debottlenecking added 10-15% output; Excel pushpull cable utilisation at 70-75%, rubber line just starting.
Pilot Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) facility commissioned; commercial launch targeted in subsequent quarters.
Core business capex stated as on track; 650 kVA own engine launched last quarter.
demand_pricing: GEML 2-wheeler run rate roughly 9,000-10,000 units in the latest quarter; growing ~2,000 units per quarter.
Raw material price indexing for OEM contracts applies with a lag; aftermarket pricing passed through via distributors.

Strong demand for medium-horsepower gensets in industrial and commercial applications; AI data-centre demand described as strong, with a strategic supply agreement with a large global engine maker for larger sizes.
Excel: business restarted from Europe and expected from the US after a Russia-Ukraine-related export setback last year.
International business is about 13% of core revenue; Greaves International Trading FZE set up in Dubai for Middle East and Africa.

qa_highlights.question: How has margin erosion split between OEM and aftermarket/retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity costs hit all products. OEM contracts have indexing with a lag, while aftermarket pricing is easier to pass on; price increases have been taken in both.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin drop is investment versus commodity cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar attributed about 1.5 percentage points to additional investments; the rest is the inflation-price lag, which should narrow in Q2 and fully in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is GEML's growth sustainable and when does it turn EBITDA-positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said per-unit losses have fallen sharply and EBITDA could turn positive in 4 to 6 quarters, without committing to timing or scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why does GFL, an EV financing NBFC, exist in a pruned portfolio, and is it brand-agnostic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GFL is part of the EV ecosystem; its share of GEML financing is near double digits and rising. Vikas Singh said financing partners are brand-agnostic by nature.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough cash for the investee investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar said standalone liquidity as of March 2026 covers the INR50 crore GFL and INR331 crore GEML investments plus Q1-Q2 capex and dividends, and that the core business generates enough cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is motorcycle entry planned for GEML?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said motorcycle prototypes are underway; the scooter opportunity is also large and prioritisation is under leadership review with no timing decided.

risks_watch: Margins: Q1 margin down 2-2.5 pts; recovery depends on Q2-H2 pricing and cost savings, and the full-year target is contingent on H2 catch-up.
Commodity and geopolitical cost pressure (West Asia developments) may outlast the pricing actions.
GEML is still loss-making with a 4-6 quarter timeline to positive EBITDA; management gave no firm timing.
Excel revenue of about INR66-70 crores and export-led recovery depend on new Europe and US customers.
Greaves Technologies had earlier slippages; management said it is still stabilising and cited one pilot design-work order.
Unallocable expenses of INR25.82 crores in segment results; the company said these are now folded into core business P&L (slide 27).
key_quotes: Now our ability to mitigate those differs slightly by the segment of customers.
And to sum it up, we're absolutely on track with our commitment to Greaves.Next strategy and the margin targets that we have set for ourselves.
We're not in a position really to comment in terms of how soon and how much, but we are very confident and that's what the entire team is working towards.
At this stage, I don't want to reveal more detail because the discussions are still evolving.

502090|2026-03.headline: Sagar Cements guides FY27 volumes to about 7 million tonnes (FY26: 6.1 Mt) and Q4 EBITDA/tonne rose to ₹445 from ₹218.
502090|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 8% YoY and full-year volumes grew 11% to 6.1 million tonnes, with revenue up 20% in the quarter helped by non-trade pricing. Q4 EBITDA per tonne was ₹445 against ₹218 a year earlier, and quarterly PAT was ₹100 crore. Management flagged a fuel cost shock from the West Asia conflict (pet coke at $136-140 CIF versus about $120 earlier), with impact expected from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease. Management also announced a Superfine Building Materials division and in-principle approval for merging Andhra Cements into the parent.

segments.name: Plants (Q4 utilisation)
segments.commentary: Mattampally 59%, Gudipadu 84%, Bayyavaram 69%, Jeerabad 95%, Jajpur 44%, Dachepalli 38%. Jeerabad is cited as consistently running around 90%.

segments.name: Superfine Building Materials (new division)
segments.commentary: Approved by the board on 13 May 2026. It will use GGBS and fly ash to make superfine products (Blaine target 10,000-20,000) for UHPC, repairs and cladding. Management guides a minimum 30% margin; revenue and EBITDA numbers are deferred to next quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of about 7 million tonnes, relying on about 0.5 Mt from Jeerabad upgrade (expected by end-Q1), about 0.9 Mt from Andhra ramp-up and the balance from market growth of 12-15%.
FY27 EBITDA per tonne expected to be close to ₹600 if prices stay flat, with about ₹150/tonne from internal cost savings (WHRS, Andhra preheater, grinding units).

Pet coke and coal cost pressure: about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement on current blend, with impact from mid-Q2 if prices stay high. Management also pencilled in about ₹225-250/tonne in total fuel and miscellaneous cost increases, assumed to be passed through.
FY27 budget: ₹580 crore cost, about ₹100 crore lower than the prior year's cost base according to management's comments.

Capex: ₹190 crore pending on three ongoing projects (Andhra ₹140 crore, Gudipadu ₹17 crore, Jeerabad ₹33 crore). Maintenance capex about ₹50 crore per year. Some projects to be funded through lease or equipment finance.
Vizag land monetisation (about 100 acres, net about ₹3.5 crore per acre): ₹350 crore pencilled over 18-24 months, with ₹150 crore in year 1 after the government GO, and ₹150 crore assumed in FY27.
Net debt guidance for FY27 is to pay debt down from operating cash flow; year-end net debt was about ₹1,550 crore versus the earlier guidance of about ₹1,300 crore.
capex_capacity: WHRS: 2.8 MW of 4.35 MW (AQC boiler) commissioned on 12 May 2026; remaining 1.55 MW (preheater boiler) due by end-June 2026.
Jeerabad grinding expansion and Dachepalli expansion in progress; Jeerabad due before end of Q1 FY27.
Andhra Cements grinding expansion due by September 2026; new VRM for cement grinding due by September 2026.
Andhra clinker kcal consumption about 700 kcal/tonne of clinker versus about 775-780 earlier.
Madhya Pradesh incentives of about ₹171 crore over seven years; about ₹65 crore received so far, about ₹110 crore remaining over four years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand held up in the first two months of Q4 but slowed in late Q4 due to labour shortages, the festive season and unseasonal rains. Q4 volume growth was 8%, and Q1 FY27 to date is up about 7% YoY.
Price hike of about ₹25-30 per bag in second week of April (non-trade led) across regions; Hyderabad retail about ₹295 and wholesale about ₹268 after the hike.
Prices have been flat since mid-April, with some pressure in central and eastern markets (₹5 hike in Indore not sustained) and a slight negative bias there; south has held the April hike.
Demand outlook: AP and Telangana strong; Tamil Nadu 5-10%, Karnataka 5%, Odisha 5%, Madhya Pradesh 5-7.5%.
Management said bags cost fell about ₹2/bag, but the war impact on explosives and diesel (₹23.75/litre hike in commercial diesel) is expected to add about ₹100/tonne.
Superfine products priced around ₹30,000/tonne versus ₹2,500-3,000/tonne for low-Blaine GGBS, with low volumes expected initially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected cost impact from the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Pet coke has risen from around $120 to $136-140 CIF, adding about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement. Inventory cover runs to mid-Q2, and imported coal is being partly switched to domestic coal, with the outcome known by end-Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 28% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹11.5 crore was one-offs: about ₹7.5 crore mine bearing land (MBL) cess and about ₹3.24 crore DMF expense at a subsidiary, covering roughly 3-3.5 years of accrual. Promotional spend also rose. Excluding one-offs, growth is about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 volume of 7 Mt be achieved given past misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target relies on Jeerabad (+0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (+0.9 Mt) and market growth; it chooses not to chase share at the expense of cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jeerabad clinker sales continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some clinker sales are expected during the phased ramp-up, subject to clinker prices, with margin held at that location's level.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any cost reduction left after Andhra stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Andhra clinker cost is now in line; the new VRM (by September) should deliver the planned savings. Margins are expected to be better in FY27 than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter unsecured debt for the Andhra project was drawn after the planned rights issue became an OFS, and solar capex was accelerated for short payback. Debt is expected to fall from operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose sharply: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit days were extended in a difficult market, fuel prices were higher, and volumes grew. About ₹80 crore of US coal was bought in March on 180-day LC credit. Moderation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag land GO status and sale timing?
qa_highlights.answer: GVMC and UDA approvals are in place; the state GO is awaited, expected within six months. Management is assuming ₹350 crore over 18-24 months at the old reckoner rate of ₹4 crore per acre.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost gap between standalone and Andhra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is mainly logistics and market spread, with the Andhra cost gap closing after investments; detail to be discussed offline.

502090|2026-06.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
502090|2026-06.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7 million tonne FY27 volume target ex-clinker, and how much clinker will be sold in Q2 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The 7 mt target excludes clinker. Clinker is still sold to Andhra Cements' sister unit Bayyavaram and some outside, and some at Jeerabad until ramp-up; management would not quantify volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit volume growth possible in FY28, and what is the Q2 cost inflation and is the ~₹600/t EBITDA guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY27 and FY28 both see double-digit volume growth. Full-year cost pressure is about ₹100/t across fuel, raw material and miscellaneous, offset by savings; Q2 gets extra inventory and maintenance cost at three plants. Guidance is ₹500–550/t, assuming flat prices, not ~₹600.

qa_highlights.question: Are prices stable versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices have been flat from March exit to July and June to July; realisation was up about ₹50–60/t, with the cause unclear (mix or price hikes).

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vizag land sale and FY27 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Awaiting a generic Government GO after the government signalled it would replace a case-specific order; the ₹150 crore for FY27 is still seen as doable. Management said buyer engagement exists but timelines were the issue.

qa_highlights.question: Which regions drive incremental H2 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all incremental volume comes from the South (~80% of footprint). Madpradesh is also expected to rise after the 0.5 mt Jeerabad expansion, supporting the ~15% growth projected for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How does Andhra Cements' cost structure compare with Mattampally, and how should the three units be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable cost at Andhra is ₹100–125/t higher than Mattampally because it buys grid power without waste heat recovery; management says the kcal and unit metrics are at par. Andhra carries most of the debt, and management offered to share modelling details offline.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 EBITDA of ~₹425/t reach ₹600/t for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹550/t is 'definitely doable', citing Gudipadu WHR savings, Jeerabad expansion and the Andhra cement mill due end-September, assuming stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex going to rise, and what is the debt reduction path?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capex beyond ₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028. About ₹240 crore of ongoing capex spreads over FY27 and FY28; operating cash flow is not yet reflected in the gross debt path.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers to manage power and fuel costs if the West Asia crisis escalates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no control over prices and can only manage consumption, which it says is efficient. Inventory covers operations to mid-October; ₹100/t inflation is pencilled in (₹50 fuel, ₹50 other), and clinker is at its peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Tamil Nadu ban on rough stone and aggregate transport, and what limestone auction premiums are seen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no impact. Recent Telangana limestone auctions, about a year or 18 months old, went at 50–75% premiums; other auctions are pending in TN, AP and Telangana.

qa_highlights.answer: Parth Bhavsar asked about net debt trajectory. Management said the ₹150 crore land sale is in FY27 and about ₹200 crore in FY28.

502219|2026-03.headline: Borosil Renewables FY26 standalone sales rose 38% to INR1,534.83 crore and EBITDA margin hit 32% on higher solar glass realisations.
502219|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone sales were INR437.62 crore (up ~34% YoY, a record quarter) with EBITDA of INR144.61 crore at 33% of sales, helped by average ex-factory realisation of INR150.2/mm and about 15% higher volumes. Management attributed roughly half the quarterly sales jump to Ind AS revenue recognition timing (about 6% of Q4 sales), and said the run-rate is nearer INR400-410 crore a quarter. Fuel surcharges passed to customers during the West Asia-driven gas price spike had negligible net impact on realisation (under INR1/mm). The company wrote off its German exposure (Geosphere and GMB) with no additional P&L loss, as a provision was already made in Q1 FY26. Management also announced a rooftop solar branded-products venture, a 600 TPD furnace expansion targeted for Q4 FY27, and an enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crore in equity.

segments.name: Solar glass (standalone, Bharuch)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,534.83 crore with EBITDA margin 32%; Q4 volumes up 15% YoY and 14% QoQ, with production run at full capacity and no curtailment during the West Asia disruption.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 overseas net revenue INR2.3 crore and EBITDA INR0.82 crore, versus INR3.96 crore and INR1.90 crore in the prior quarter; German production shut from July 2025 and exposure to Geosphere and GMB written off.

segments.commentary: Early-stage branded rooftop solutions business sourcing modules, inverters and batteries from outside vendors; first sales booked in March 2026, with a first-year target of about INR75 crore and expected initial EBITDA margin below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management sees 30-33% EBITDA margin as achievable on a normal basis, barring unforeseen circumstances.
Run-rate quarterly sales of about INR400-410 crore after the roughly 6% Ind AS timing benefit in Q4 falls away.

600 TPD of new capacity (two 300 TPD furnaces) targeted for production within FY27; management said the first furnace is on track for around January 2027 and that sales contribution should come from Q1 FY28, with some sales possible in FY27.
Tax rate expected around 21% of PBT, with minimal cash tax while INR950 crore of expansion capex is capitalised.
SG1 and SG2 furnace rebuild capex of about INR100 crore expected in the next calendar year.
Customs notification for continuation of countervailing duty on Malaysian solar glass expected before the current duty expires on 6-8 June 2026.
capex_capacity: Expansion of 600 TPD (two 300 TPD furnaces) at the existing location is in full swing; nearly all orders placed and building construction on plan, taking capacity from about 1,000 TPD to about 1,600 TPD (around 60% uplift).
Management cited INR950 crore of capitalisation planned in the current financial year.

Domestic solar glass capacity is about 2,600 TPD (about 18 GW); about 33 GW of further capacity is expected by March 2027, mostly captive, taking the domestic total to about 51 GW against demand of about 65 GW.
Rooftop business: no capex for 1-1.5 years; the company may consider inverter assembly after 6-8 months to a year, but not module manufacturing.
Board approved an enabling resolution to raise equity up to INR750 crore, subject to shareholder approval; management said there are no current plans to raise capital.
demand_pricing: Realisation held near INR150/mm; management said pass-through of gas and fuel cost added less than INR1/mm, and that the price is tied to the landed cost of Chinese imports and near peak levels, with rupee depreciation providing only limited headroom.
Domestic solar installations were 44.6 GW in FY26 versus 23.8 GW in FY25, implying about 60-62 GW of glass consumption; imports still supply about 70% of demand.
ALMM-II (domestic solar cells) effective June 2026; solar cell capacity at 30 GW, expected to reach 75 GW by FY-end; ALMM-III for ingots and wafers from June 2028.

Indonesian Chinese-owned plant (about 1,500 TPD) has entered the market but has made limited impact so far; the Turkish producer's exports face high freight costs; the UAE plant is blocked by Strait of Hormuz conditions.
Export demand is low in major markets; the US may grow as customers seek non-Chinese origin glass, and Europe has niche demand for greenhouses and flat-plate collectors.

Cost pressure from oil-linked inputs is so far modest; vendors are seeking pass-through and the company is negotiating; gas quantities are secured under medium- and short-term contracts, but spot prices are high.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR150/mm realisation comes from fuel pass-through, and what would it be without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Jain said the pass-through contributed less than INR1/mm, about INR0.70-0.75, and a similar increase is visible in net realisation between Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisation or margins come under pressure as new domestic capacity arrives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no pressure for domestic producers; most upcoming capacity is captive, demand exceeds the 51 GW expected capacity, and Indonesian imports are not yet a price threat.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 13-15% sequential sales growth with flat realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly half was production gain (about 7%) and half was Ind AS timing: in-transit sales were lower at the end of Q3 and so were recognised in Q4, with the sales base reset to about INR400-410 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is gas supply secure given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantities are broadly secured under medium- and short-term contracts; the government gas cut is based on the past six-month average, and the rest is bought at market-related prices, so price rather than volume is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar roadmap, capex and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: No capex for 1-1.5 years; modules, inverters and batteries will be outsourced; first-year target is about INR75 crore, with margins expected below 10% initially and little or no profit in year one; working capital is kept low by negotiating terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the furnace expansion commissioning timeline hold, and what does it do to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing is as currently planned (first furnace around January 2027), with sales from Q1 FY28; operating leverage and higher yield are expected, but management did not commit to a specific margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and tax?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has fallen because older SG1 and SG2 assets are fully depreciated; current charge mainly reflects the 2023 expansion. Tax is around 21% of PBT, with deferred tax at a similar rate.

Fuel surcharge and gas price volatility from the West Asia conflict; management said the Q1 FY27 reset depends on the 30 June stock-take.
Ind AS timing effects could make quarterly sales lumpy; management flagged the INR400-410 crore run-rate as the base case.
Indonesian Chinese-owned capacity could pressure prices; management suggested BIS and quality-control measures as a mitigant.
Rooftop business faces competition from Tata Power, Havells and Luminous, and early margins are guided below 10%.
Furnace commissioning slippage (first furnace January 2027 target) and the planned INR100 crore SG1/SG2 rebuild capex.
Export demand remains weak in Europe; freight costs are high because of Red Sea and Hormuz disruptions.

Initially, we may expect less than 10%, just to give you a number.

rows.why: 600 TPD (two 300 TPD furnaces) is nearly fully ordered and under construction, lifting capacity from ~1,000 TPD to ~1,600 TPD (~60% uplift) on INR950 crore capitalisation, but management guided sales only from Q1 FY28, so within the window the capacity is mostly not yet selling.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: Standalone volumes were up ~15% YoY in Q4 FY26 with full utilisation and no curtailment, but the run-rate is reset to INR400-410 crore a quarter and new 600 TPD capacity only contributes from Q1 FY28, with some FY27 sales possible.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is effectively 100% with no curtailment, but the 600 TPD expansion is already under way; management was evasive beyond it and said there are no current plans to raise capital, so a further capex announcement is conditional rather than firm.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management explicitly reset the sales base to INR400-410 crore a quarter after the Q4 record of INR437.62 crore, which included ~6% Ind AS timing benefit, so a revenue guidance raise looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include CVD on Malaysian glass expiring 6-8 June 2026, gas and fuel price volatility tied to the 30 June stock-take, Indonesian capacity entering the market, and furnace slippage beyond January 2027, though management said realisation is near peak and demand of ~65 GW exceeds the 51 GW expected domestic capacity.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Rooftop solar branded products launched with first sales in March 2026 and a first-year target of ~INR75 crore, sourcing modules, inverters and batteries externally; inverter assembly may follow in 6-8 months to a year.

rows.why: Average ex-factory realisation was INR150.2/mm in Q4 FY26 versus INR127.6 in Q4 FY25, and management sees ~60-62 GW glass demand against 51 GW domestic capacity by March 2027, but imports still supply ~70% of demand and Indonesian capacity has entered.

rows.label: Customs continuation of CVD on Malaysian solar glass
rows.why: Management expects the notification before the current duty expires on 6-8 June 2026, and a delayed or diluted notification would weigh on pricing against imports that make up ~70% of demand.

rows.label: Enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crore equity
rows.why: Board approved an enabling resolution subject to shareholder approval, but management said there are no current plans to raise capital, so dilution is not expected in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic demand-supply gap and pricing and the 600 TPD build, but cautious on Q4 sequential sustainability (Ind AS timing) and evasive on expansion beyond 600 TPD; analysts pushed on realisation durability, fuel pass-through and the Q4 sales base.

502219|2026-06.headline: Borosil Renewables Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 53% YoY to INR405.69 crore and EBITDA to INR142 crore (35% margin), helped by a fuel surcharge.
502219|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales were INR405.69 crore, up 53% YoY from INR332.26 crore, while EBITDA rose to INR142 crore at 35% of sales versus 27.9% a year ago. Average ex-factory realisation rose to INR160.30 per sq m from INR150.20 in Q4 FY26, including a INR9.50 fuel surcharge introduced from 10 March 2026 after the West Asia war raised fuel costs. Management said the surcharge is now being cut as fuel prices ease, and that the 600 TPD furnace expansion is on track for commissioning in Q1 FY27-end (January to March 2027). Reported PAT of about INR169 crore in Q4 FY26 was inflated by a INR75 crore tax write-back, so the sequential PAT comparison is not like-for-like.

segments.name: Solar glass (core, standalone)
segments.commentary: Plants run at full capacity of 1,000 TPD; realisation INR160.30 per sq m, with EBITDA margin above 33% for the fourth straight quarter. Top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries (German step-downs)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27 and an EBITDA loss of INR0.84 crore, against INR14.32 crore revenue and INR23.24 crore loss a year earlier. Investment written off in the books after the court administrator indicated no recovery.

segments.name: Rooftop solar (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage on-grid residential kit (module, inverter, battery) sold as a system. Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore against an internal FY27 target of about INR36 crore; EBITDA margin expected in single digits, versus 30-35% for glass.

guidance_outlook: 600 TPD expansion at the existing site: construction targeted by December 2026, commissioning January to March 2027 (SG4 and SG5, about one month apart). Management says revenue should be modelled from 1 April 2027, though the internal target is 1 March.
Once the 600 TPD is commissioned, sales are expected to rise about 60%, adding about INR80-85 crore of quarterly EBITDA at current run-rate and prices.
Realisation to fall as the INR9.50 fuel surcharge is passed back to customers; management says cost declines should offset this, so profit is not expected to be affected.

Management declined to give a formal guidance but said it expects to continue at similar revenue and EBITDA levels if conditions hold; expects extra profitability this year because prices were at full levels all year.
Ambition to grow from about INR2,500 crore to at least INR4,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years after March 2027; next expansion decision expected within about 6 months.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 1,000 TPD; expansion of 600 TPD at existing location takes it to 1,600 TPD, with the expansion fully funded per management.

Furnace SG1 and SG2 refurbishment: timing not fixed, possibly Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28, likely after SG4/SG5 are commissioned. A rebuild needs about 75 days of shutdown plus 15 days to restart, so about 90 days with no output from the furnace being rebuilt.
Any further capacity beyond the 600 TPD expansion would be a new building and facility, sized at 600 or 1,200 TPD, and not an add-on to the current layout.
Domestic solar glass capacity expected to reach 7,700 TPD by March 2027 (about 51 GW), against about 2,600 TPD (18 GW) today and about 11,000 TPD demand for 62 GW of module requirement.

Module capacity in India is 203 GW; solar cell capacity is 30 GW, expected to rise to 75 GW by 2027 under ALMM-2 (effective 1 June 2026). ALMM-3 for ingot and wafer starts 28 June, with about 50 GW expected by 2029.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic industry supplies only about 25% of demand; even at 7,700 TPD, supply would cover only 75%, so pricing is expected to hold, with import-parity pricing as the reference.
Exports to the US are very small and in niche applications; the company is focused on the domestic market.
A significant portion of new domestic capacity is captive, so the open-market supply gain is limited, according to management.
Management expects module makers to consolidate over the next 1-1.5 years because module capacity far exceeds requirement; Mono PERC players and those without cell supply may drop volumes.
CVD of 9.71% on solar glass imports from Malaysia extended for five more years from 2 June 2026, on top of anti-dumping duties on China and Vietnam since December 2024.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall from INR169 crore in Q4 to INR87 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 PAT included a INR75 crore tax write-back tied to the write-off of the German subsidiary investment (INR325 crore provision). Excluding it, performance was not inferior.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose from 34 to 152; is that right?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 152-day figure, saying working capital is about 60 days, with a slight rise from stores inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic prices fall as capacity grows to 7,700 TPD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is robust, with domestic supply covering only about 25% now, and that pricing is anchored to import parity, so no pricing challenge is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar business worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal FY27 revenue target is about INR36 crore, Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore, with single-digit EBITDA margins because it is a trading-style solution business.

qa_highlights.question: Any equity raise or debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The current expansion is fully funded. Future projects will be funded from internal cash, with some debt if the project is large. No near-term equity raise is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin around 80% calculated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put gross margin at about 78% on a manufacturing-cost basis, with raw material at about 23-24% of sales, and said margin volatility is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of the SG1 patch repair and the volume effect of furnace rebuilds?
qa_highlights.answer: A four-day patch on one furnace cost about INR3 crore in lost output. A full rebuild would shut the furnace for about 90 days, causing a volume loss in the year it happens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 25.2% should be assumed for the full year.

risks_watch: Fuel-surcharge unwind: the INR9.50 per sq m surcharge is being reduced as fuel prices ease, so realisation could fall from INR160.30 even with stable costs. Management says the cost decline offsets it.
Commissioning risk: the 600 TPD expansion (SG4, SG5) must be commissioned by March 2027, with revenue only from April 2027. Any delay pushes the 60% volume uplift later.
Furnace SG1/SG2 rebuild: about 90 days of lost output per furnace, timing not fixed (Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28); this could reduce FY28 volumes against the 1,600 TPD capacity.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume, and module consolidation could affect volumes.
Capacity additions in domestic glass (to 7,700 TPD by March 2027) could pressure prices, though management expects supply to stay short.
Rooftop solar and the overseas subsidiaries are small and early, with unclear profitability; the call gave no segment-level data.
Management declined to comment on press reports of a strategic investment. Next-phase project choice (glass furnace or adjacent business) is due in about 5-6 months.

502355|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA was INR663 crore at 22.9% margin on record OHT volumes of 85,820 MT, while management flagged raw material inflation of 7-8% in Q1 FY27.
502355|2026-03.overview: Balkrishna posted its highest-ever quarterly and annual OHT volumes, with Q4 volume up 5% YoY to 85,820 MT and FY26 volume at 317,356 MT. Standalone Q4 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR2,894 crore, but EBITDA margin was hit late in the quarter by geopolitical supply-chain headwinds, and FY26 EBITDA fell 10% YoY to INR2,423 crore. The company has stopped giving volume guidance, is starting its on-highway push (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR), and has approved an additional INR2,000 crore capex. Management signalled raw material and margin pressure into FY27 with only partial price pass-through so far.

segments.name: Off-highway tyres (OHT)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume of 85,820 MT (+5% YoY) was a record; H2 clearly stronger than H1 with Europe recovering on easing channel inventories and Americas improving. US was just under 10% of FY26 volume, with a target of about 10% in FY27.

segments.name: Carbon black
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew marginally; third-party sales were about 9% of the business. Capacity is 265,000 MTPA after the December 2025 line, with the new lines fully utilised; about 30% of output is consumed internally and about 70% sold externally at industry-average margins.

segments.name: On-highway tyres (OHT-on-road)
segments.commentary: Entered truck-bus radial with launches in February 2026 and re-launched 2-wheeler tyres (capacity about 100,000 tyres a month). Phase 1 CV radial capex of INR750 crore added 800 tyres a day of fungible CVR/OHT capacity; PCR launch is targeted by end of calendar 2026 with first-phase capacity of 6,700 tyres a day. Long-term vision is INR5,000 crore revenue by 2030.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance for FY27 given the geopolitical uncertainty; management expects growth but declined to quantify it.
Raw material prices rose about 4-5% in Q4 FY26 and are expected to rise a further 7-8% in the June 2026 quarter.
Price hikes of 3-5% already taken across geographies, with a further roughly 2% targeted by end of May 2026; more hikes possible.
Freight was about 4.5-5% of revenue in Q4 and is expected to rise marginally absent further disruption.
FY27 total capex guided at INR1,500-1,800 crore; maintenance capex about INR200 crore a year on top of projects.
Management aims to sustain EBITDA margins of 23-25% at company level even as on-highway scales up; 5-year revenue growth vision of about 17% CAGR, with the jump back-ended as capacity comes on line.
EUR/INR realization about INR99 in Q4; FY27 hedge rate expected to be higher than this year, not yet quantified.
Final dividend of INR4 per share recommended, on top of INR12 paid over the previous three quarters.
risks_watch: Raw material inflation of 7-8% in the June 2026 quarter, with only partial pass-through through price hikes; management flagged likely near-term margin pressure in FY27.
Geopolitical supply-chain disruption affecting freight (about 4.5-5% of revenue) and margins.
Execution risk on the on-highway ramp (TBR, PCR, 2-wheeler) with no disclosed revenue targets for FY27 and PCR launch slated for end-2026.
Funding of the INR3,800 crore remaining capex is not finalised; the possible peak debt level was not confirmed (gross debt INR4,049 crore at March 2026).
Realisation of the US reciprocal tariff refund and how much will be passed to distributors.
Balance carbon black capacity (to 360,000 MTPA) and CV Phase 2 are due in Q1 FY27 and during FY27; any slippage would affect the ramp.
502355|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term vision and on the H2 recovery, but cautious and at times evasive on FY27: volume guidance was withheld, and funding, margin and hedge-rate questions drew "too volatile" or "can't assume anything" type answers.
key_quotes: So we stopped giving guidance due to the geopolitical scenarios and uncertainties.
At this moment, we may have some price pressures, margin pressures.
This was our highest ever quarter and best number.
We have positioned ourselves as a premium player in that category.

qa_highlights.question: Volume guidance for OHT in FY27 and CV radial sales expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stopped volume guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty; expects growth but will not quantify. CV radial business has just begun, with the 2030 vision still the target.

qa_highlights.question: Total FY27 capex and the INR2,000 crore additional capex: what it covers and whether it is incremental to the INR6,800 crore plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex guided at INR1,500-1,800 crore. The INR2,000 crore covers capacity expansion, infrastructure, AI automation and sustainability, staggered over several years. INR6,800 crore includes about INR3,000 crore already spent; maintenance capex about INR200 crore a year is extra.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material and price pass-through outlook; near-term margin pressure in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-5% in Q4 and may rise 7-8% in June quarter. Price hikes of 3-5% taken with about 2% more by end-May. Management said 'we may have some price pressures, margin pressures' and is evaluating pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Can company EBITDA margin of 23-25% be sustained with on-highway scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company as a whole aims to keep sustained EBITDA levels, which it is maintaining; the 23-25% range is the endeavour, applied at company level rather than by segment.

qa_highlights.question: Peak debt and funding of remaining capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding is a mix of sources and not yet finalised. Management said 'We can't assume anything. It's a volatile world' when asked if INR4,000 crore of gross debt is the peak.

qa_highlights.question: US reciprocal tariff refund: filed, and how much passes to distributors?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is importer on record and has filed; nothing received yet and quantum not disclosed. Management said it would be fair practice to pass back part of any amount recovered from customers.

502355|2026-06.headline: Balkrishna Q1 FY27 OHT volume rose 16% YoY to 93,770 MT, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 20.61% on raw-material inflation.
502355|2026-06.overview: Management reported record OHT sales volume of 93,770 MT (up 16% YoY) and standalone revenue of INR3,409 crores (up 24% YoY). Standalone EBITDA was INR703 crores at a 20.61% margin, pressured by raw-material costs linked to geopolitical disruption, partly offset by a ~5% price hike. PAT was INR432 crores. The On-Highway business (truck-bus radial and 2-wheeler) went live in Q1 and is being seeded, with a ramp expected from Q2; management declined to disclose its revenue or volume.

segments.name: On-Highway (TBR and 2-wheeler)
segments.commentary: Launched in Q1 through distributors set up in April; management calls it small and will not disclose revenue or volume. Target of INR5,000 crores On-Highway revenue by 2030 was reiterated; FY27 is described as a portfolio-building year and FY28 as the start of serious business.

502355|2026-09.headline: BKT signs Pirelli offtake deal to produce 800,000 Pirelli-branded premium car tires per year by 2030 at Bhuj PCR plant, starting CY2027.
502355|2026-09.overview: This was a short business update call on the Pirelli-BKT strategic offtake agreement, held at short notice, with Q2 FY27 performance explicitly off-limits under the silent-period policy. BKT will manufacture Pirelli-branded car tires (17-inch and above) at its newly built Bhuj PCR plant, ramping gradually from CY2027 to 800,000 tires per year by CY2030. A second phase contemplates a 50:50 JV and a dedicated plant for high-value passenger car tires, subject to preset conditions, with management saying the JV work must be announced by 2030. Management said the offtake fits within the existing expansion programme, with no additional capex for the offtake, and pricing is raw material at actuals plus conversion cost.

segments.commentary: Bulk of Phase 1 capacity (about 80% of 6,700 tires/day) stays on BKT brand, addressing the full Indian market from 13-inch upward. BKT is at an early stage of its on-highway journey.

502986|2026-03.headline: Vardhman sees industry spinning spreads near $0.90–0.95/kg versus ~$0.60–0.65 four months ago, but Q4 hit by ~INR57–58 crore forex mark-to-market loss.
502986|2026-03.overview: Management described a sharp turnaround in the Indian textile value chain over the past six months: US tariffs eased, cotton and yarn prices rose, and Chinese yarn demand lifted Indian exports. Q4 gross margin rose about 300 bps QoQ, but EBITDA was held back by an other-expense charge of about INR57–58 crore from mark-to-market on rupee forward cover after the rupee hit INR94.80 on 31 March. Management said fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, so Q4 did not fully reflect the improvement and Q1 FY27 should be better. The call gave no formal numeric guidance; most outlook comments were qualitative and tied to cotton, the dollar-rupee rate and the FTA pipeline.

segments.commentary: Management said fabric price hikes are being pushed selectively, with a 2–3 month lag to yarn. The new performance (100% synthetic) fabric plant, commissioned last fiscal year, is expected to reach full use in 6–9 months.

Remaining ~10% of spinning modernisation to finish in the next 6–8 months; biomass boilers and other green power projects to commission in 1–2 months, with cost benefits from June or July.

Performance fabric plant commissioned last fiscal year; 6–9 months needed to build order book. A fourth cotton and normal fabric line was also commissioned in FY26 but could not be fully used because of US tariffs; utilisation is expected in 6–9 months.
Open-end spinning project on hold to restart. New land in PM MITRA Park, Madhya Pradesh is expected by December or January, with plans to be finalised in 2–3 months.

Industry spindles: about 53 million rated; 11–12 million permanently stopped, leaving about 41–42 million working (industry estimate, not government data). Normal additions of 2–2.5 million per year were missed for three years.
Garment capacity expansion approved as a first step to viability; no decision on broader expansion.
demand_pricing: Chinese buying of Indian yarn rose to ~30 million kg per month over the last 4–5 months, against 7–8 million kg earlier. India's monthly yarn exports reached ~120 million kg-plus against a 100 million kg average.

Cotton: New York futures rose from ~$0.62–0.63/lb to ~$0.82–0.83/lb. Indian cotton moved from INR52,000–53,000/candy to INR67,000–68,000/candy; CCI selling price was INR67,000/candy after a ~INR5,000 rise in the last week.
Indian cotton is now priced around New York plus $0.05–0.08, close to the long-run relationship. Management said this removes the earlier disadvantage for spinners.

Pricing: fabric and garment price increases are being pushed across the chain. Brands are granting only small increases so far, with management expecting more clarity in 1–2 months. Yarn cost pass-through was described as comfortable given stronger demand.

Management noted US garment and home textile utilisation has recovered to roughly 90–100% after tariffs eased, from 50–60% earlier. Earlier, US tariffs reached 50%, which had forced discounting and loss-making orders.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn prices follow international cotton and that higher Indian cotton cost is absorbed by Indian producers. Demand and higher cotton costs have been passed on comfortably so far.

qa_highlights.question: Can the spread gains be quantified and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the spread at ~$0.90–0.95/kg against ~$0.60–0.65 four months earlier, about 40–50% higher. Sustainability depends on New York futures and China demand, which management could not predict.

qa_highlights.question: How long will spindle capacity take to return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects expansion decisions in 6–9 months if margins hold for 3–6 months. About 1,000 small mills have closed, so consolidation is structural.

qa_highlights.answer: Garment capacity expansion is an early viability step with no decision on broader expansion. Realisation was given as $7.5 per shirt.

502986|2026-06.headline: Vardhman Q1 FY27 margins rose on spinning yarn-size gains and raw-material trading gains; fabric utilisation remains weak as US orders slipped.
502986|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 numbers improved in both percentage and absolute terms, driven mainly by the spinning business through better yarn sizes and a partial trading gain on raw material bought before the cotton price rise. The fabric business lagged: absolute volumes were roughly flat YoY and 3-4% below Q4 FY26, because US orders were lost after a missed sampling season tied to US tariffs. Management expects the spinning margin to moderate as cheap inventory runs out, but sees a 13-14% margin as a reasonable direction. Capex is mostly complete, with biomass boilers starting and the Dhar (PM MITRA) site dependent on land and power by around December 2026 and June 2027.

segments.commentary: Weak utilisation after losing US season orders; management says prices pass-through on yarn is only 60-70%, leaving 20-30% unrecovered. 503101|2026-06.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q1 FY27 total income hit INR 217 crores, a multi-quarter high, with PAT of INR 52 crores and INR 900 crores of new redevelopment GDV added.
503101|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 217 crores (multi-quarter high), EBITDA of INR 66 crores and PAT of INR 52 crores. Sales on the existing portfolio were 38,000 sq ft with booking value of INR 86 crores and collections of INR 118 crores (MNRL's 40% share of Monte South); including the merged portfolio, sales were 46,000 sq ft, booking value INR 108 crores and collections INR 146 crores. Two redevelopment projects (Versova and Sewri, INR 450 crores GDV each) were added, and the company says it is debt-free with about INR 200 crores of acquisition capital after a INR 900 crore QIP. The merger with group entities is awaiting NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings in early September 2026.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, JV, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Sold ~35,000 sq ft with booking value INR 125 crores and collections INR 140 crores. Tower A has OC; Tower B has RCC to 65th floor and part OC to 45th floor, with balance OC expected this FY; Tower C RCC at 28th floor.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)
segments.commentary: Sold 14,000 sq ft with booking value INR 17 crores and collections INR 43 crores. Full OC received for Cedar and Daffodil towers, enabling handovers.

segments.name: Bhandup (NeoPark, NeoSquare)
segments.commentary: Sales of 8,000 sq ft with booking value INR 14 crores and collections INR 9 crores. NeoSquare has OC; NeoValley and NeoPark under construction per schedule.

segments.name: Commercial (Futurex and Millennium)
segments.commentary: Futurex combined sales ~4,000 sq ft, booking INR 19 crores, collections INR 23 crores; Futurex has OC. Millennium sold over 1,000 sq ft, booking INR 3 crores, collections INR 1 crore; under construction.

segments.commentary: Started after Kanjurmarg land acquisition in Q4 FY26, focused on Bhandup; no presales yet, but management expects some in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the launch timelines for the INR 900 crore redevelopment GDV, and how much more can be added in 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two new projects (Sewri and Versova, INR 450 crores each) add INR 900 crores in the quarter; no launch timeline or further 12-24 month addition was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 business outlook and which projects will drive acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers but said the outlook is positive and better than last year, citing Monte South, commercial, and new Bhandup and Panvel phases, with bookings flowing in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections trend over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ready-to-move sales at Futurex and Monte South convert to collections in about 3 months; Monte South Tower C is at the 28th slab, with about 40% collection on that basis. Collections expected to be heavier this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A Futurex investment-property floor was not sold in the quarter, so no rental/sale income was recognised from it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the amalgamation complete by December 2026 or slip into 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder and stakeholder meetings are planned for early September, followed by a second NCLT hearing; management said it is not sure of the timeline because NCLT benches are heavily loaded.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the redevelopment pipeline beyond INR 900 crores, and how are deals selected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Mumbai redevelopment opportunity is very large; selection focuses on prime locations and strict margin thresholds, and it avoids over-priced deals that can stall.

qa_highlights.question: How much capital will be deployed in FY27 and what return thresholds apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Target EBITDA margin 30-35% on acquisitions; about INR 200 crores of surplus capital to be fully deployed this FY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PTC vertical's pipeline and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC business started after the Q4 FY26 Kanjurmarg land acquisition; strong demand from neighbouring redevelopments; presales may start in next few quarters.

503722|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose to a record Rs1,370 crore-scale year with EBITDA up 22.5% to Rs144 crore; FY27 guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore.
503722|2026-03.overview: Banswara Syntex reported Q4 FY26 total income of Rs369.3 crore, with EBITDA up 46% YoY to Rs46 crore and PAT of Rs9.6 crore (up 87% YoY). For FY26, EBITDA was about Rs144 crore (margin near 11%) and PAT Rs28.4 crore (up 32.8%) after a one-time Rs9 crore labour code exceptional charge. Fabric and Garment grew, while Yarn volumes and revenue fell on labour shortages in spinning. Management guided to FY27 revenue of Rs1,450-1,500 crore and EBITDA margin of 10.5-11% over the medium term, with near-term margin pressure from raw material pass-through lag.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs456 crore a year earlier

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs113 crore (vs Rs123 crore; management corrected the gap to Rs10 crore), FY26 Rs449 crore vs Rs460 crore (about -2%). Volume 46 lakh kg in Q4 and 194 lakh kg in FY26; utilisation 78% in Q4 and 77% for FY26. Realisations up about Rs30-35/kg.

segments.name: Fabrics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs154 crore (vs Rs145 crore); FY26 record Rs569 crore, up 5%. Volume 62 lakh meters in Q4 and 230 lakh meters in FY26; utilisation 77% in Q4. Middle East exports affected.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs96 crore, up 40%; FY26 Rs324 crore, up 18%. Volume 11 lakh pieces in Q4 and 39 lakh pieces in FY26; FY26 utilisation 72% vs about 50% in FY25. Walmart added about Rs15 crore of Q4 revenue.

segments.commentary: Management said Tesca had turnover of about Rs100 crore and PAT of about Rs10 crore, with Banswara's share about Rs4 crore. No plan to raise stake.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore, led by Fabric and Garment; FY26 was about Rs1,370 crore.
Management targets about 20% revenue growth in both Fabric and Garment in FY27; Garment division projects 18-20%.
EBITDA margin expected at 10.5-11% over the medium term; near-term margins may dip as raw material costs are passed on.
FY27 capex planned at Rs135-140 crore (an analyst cited Rs130-150 crore); Garment capex only Rs3-5 crore.
Long-term debt expected to rise in FY27 on planned capex and reduce from FY28 onwards; no reduction in total borrowings this year.
Management expects H2 FY27 growth to exceed H1; Garment momentum to improve from Q2 after a subdued Q1.
capex_capacity: Yarn and Fabric capacity was reshaped toward finer counts, Siro Compact yarn (about 200 tons per month) and worsted finishing machines; management says installed capacity fell YoY partly due to mix shift.
Garment capacity: about 70,000 pieces per month available vs 40,000-50,000 jackets used; could go to 80,000 with long runs.
Surat SEZ garment capacity (about 40,000-50,000 jackets and about 100,000 pants) awaits approval; timeline not given, file under process with Industries Commissionerate and Kandla SEZ.
Management said Garment expansion could start mid-year (Q2/Q3 FY27) and that Rs2,000 crore revenue is possible without significant capex, with no firm timeline.
Capex items: zero water discharge project, a 132 KVA power line application, and other infrastructure and sustainability spend.
demand_pricing: Polyester raw material costs up about 25% due to the Middle East conflict; yarn prices raised but not fully passed on.
Wool prices rose sharply, from Australia and China; management says customers take 6 months to 1 year to accept new prices.
Rupee depreciation of about 6-7% helped export realisations without price increases.
Walmart added as a Garment customer; JC Penney (Fabric) and Mango (Garment) already customers; Celio and Marks & Spencer cited as large relationships.
Middle East exposure about Rs100 crore; Rs8-9 crore of Q4 product could not ship on time; management expects Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region in FY27.
US demand improving; company says it is more competitive than China in spun-synthetic segment.
D2C brand One Mile averages about Rs15 lakh per month; fundraising planned once it reaches about Rs1 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Have new export clients been added, such as Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Walmart is a new addition; it contributed about Rs15 crore of Q4 Garment revenue. Management aims for 20% growth in Garment and Fabric next year and sees no need for many more large clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why did installed capacity fall YoY despite investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Finer counts and worsted machines lower kg output; capacity is planned around realistic labour availability. Management says labour shortages persist into May.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour shortage transient or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says automation is not viable given many SKUs; focus is on scaling winning products and shifting from made-to-order to predictive analytics planning.

qa_highlights.question: How will the borrowings be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no reduction in FY27 as long-term debt rises on capex; long-term debt to reduce from FY28 on 5-7 year loan tenures. Working capital rise is linked to customer ready inventory; inventory above 90 days is watched.

qa_highlights.question: What are segment-wise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give exact segment margins due to internal transfers (about 33% of yarn and 25% of fabric is internal). Segment margins are said to be close to company level; Garment was previously at breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East impact and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said polyester costs rose about 25%; price increases partly accepted, and export pricing benefited from rupee weakness. Middle East exposure is about Rs100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will FTAs (UK, EU) matter, and can Rs1,800 crore be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: UK FTA expected around September and EU by December end per management, with no certainty. Management hopes for Rs1,800 crore in the year after FY27 and is willing to accept 11% EBITDA to keep 20% growth.

503811|2026-03.headline: Siyaram Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.1% YoY to INR 871 crores, PAT up 30.6% to INR 95 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12%.

504028|2026-03.headline: GEE Q4 FY26 turnover rose to INR112 crore and FY26 to about INR370 crore, with EBITDA margin near 9% and a 25-30% revenue CAGR target to FY29.

Q4 EBITDA was about INR33 crore at a 9% margin, and PAT about INR13 crore (3.5% margin). Management framed FY26 as a stabilisation year after the May 2025 promoter restructuring, and set targets of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29-30, FY27 revenue above INR500 crore and EBITDA margin above 10%. Growth is tied to defence, power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways and exports, with flux-cored wire production slated to start in July 2026.

segments.commentary: Export share is under 10% of revenue, down from earlier years. Approvals were obtained from ADNOC (UAE) and a Saudi breakthrough, with NAKS approval from Russia in trial. 504028|2026-06.headline: GEE Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR 103 crores, with EBITDA margin up 204 bps to 7.8%.
504028|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover grew 30% YoY to INR 103 crores from INR 79 crores, and EBITDA rose about 77% to INR 8 crores with margin at 7.8% versus 5.7%. PBT rose to INR 5.5 crores from INR 1 crore, and adjusted PAT rose to INR 3.2 crores from INR 1 crore. Management set a North Star of INR 1,000 crores revenue by FY29-30, with 10-13% EBITDA margin ambitions, supported by a NPCIL approval, new SAW wire, SAW flux and flux cored wire lines, and a Thane land monetisation. Management guided that Q1 and Q2 are seasonally weaker due to monsoons.
