504132|2026-03.headline: Permanent Magnets Q4 standalone revenue rose 47% YoY to INR 66 crores; FY26 revenue INR 225 crores (+13%), with Relays ramp pushed to H2 FY27.
504132|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 66 crores, up 47% YoY, while FY26 revenue was INR 225 crores, up 13%. FY26 EBITDA margin was 17% versus 14% a year earlier, helped by product mix and second-half scale-up; Q4 margin was 15%, up YoY but down sequentially. The new Alloys furnace was installed in January and commercialised in Q4, while the Relays project slipped to commercial ramp from H2 FY27 and no rare-earth revenue was booked in FY26 due to Chinese export restrictions. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-30% with EBITDA margin of roughly 15-18%.

504132|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 49% YoY to INR72.5 crore and EBITDA rose 159% to INR17.8 crore, led by EV demand.

EBITDA was INR17.8 crore (25% margin) versus 14% a year earlier and 19% in Q1, attributed to product mix and operating leverage. Alloys revenue grew in H1 but a new furnace ran below capacity due to teething issues, so FY27 alloys guidance was cut to INR40-50 crore. Relays commercial ramp-up slipped to FY28, and Quantum Magnetics product approvals have not started, so FY27 revenue from that segment is now expected to be nil.

504380|2026-06.headline: Flomic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps to 9.34%, but PAT fell to INR2.06 crore from INR2.98 crore.
504380|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore, with management attributing most of the growth to higher freight rates rather than volume (shipments up roughly 6-7%). EBITDA rose about 68% to INR11.21 crore and margin improved to 9.34% from 6.59%. PBT turned positive at INR2.73 crore from a loss of INR3.3 crore a year earlier, while PAT was INR2.06 crore versus INR2.98 crore last year. Management said a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit was included, and it cited branch closures, manpower cost reduction and an AI-based back-office system from 1 July as margin levers.

segments.name: Air Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR22 crore in Q1; management said some cargo has shifted from ocean to air, adding to this segment.

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore in Q1; around 15% of revenue now, with a stated gross margin of 15-16% (15-20% range), targeted at 17-18% and then about 20% of contribution.

504614|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 44% to INR2,025 crores and PAT 58% to INR1,109 crores, with Q4 PAT up 53% YoY to INR155 crores.
504614|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 thermal (4,155 MU ex-captive, +84% YoY) and hydro (661 MU, +31%) generation, with the energy segment contributing about two-thirds of EBITDA. Consolidated revenue rose 23% to INR5,928 crores, and net debt fell to INR215 crores from INR1,566 crores. Q4 was dented by a 30 MW captive unit shutdown, a 300 MW turbine maintenance outage in January, seasonal hydro slowdown and the coal mine hitting its 1.8 MTPA approved limit. Management outlined a doubling of energy capacity to 1,200 MW by FY30 after the Supreme Court dismissed appeals on the SKS Power acquisition, plus a Raipur pellet expansion to 2 MTPA.

segments.name: Thermal power (ex captive)
segments.commentary: Generation reached a record 4,155 MU in FY26 versus 2,238 MU in FY25 (+84%), helped by SKS Power integration. Around 400 crore sellable units are guided for FY27 versus about 375 crore units sold in FY26; FY26 realisation was above INR5/unit.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: Generation hit a record 661 MU in FY26 versus 508 MU in FY25 (+31%), helped by the 25 MW Rehar project. Management said the hydro segment EBITDA was about INR386 crores, and that two hydro projects have long-term PPAs.

segments.name: Steel, sponge iron and pellets
segments.commentary: Iron ore pellet output hit a record 826,293 MT and sponge iron 345,066 MT in FY26; HB wire record 40,425 MT. Steel realisation improved YoY and QoQ in Q4 but FY26 averaged below FY25.

segments.name: Coal mining (Gare Palma IV/7)
segments.commentary: FY26 output hit the 1.8 MTPA permissible limit after CECB consent for expansion from 1.68 MTPA; Q4 volumes were lower as the annual cap was exhausted. Domestic coal sales were about 150k MT, as most output is captively consumed.

guidance_outlook: SKS Power capacity to double to 1,200 MW by FY30; management now says commissioning is around 2030-31 because fresh environment clearance is being sought after the earlier one expired.
Acquisition of a majority stake in Adishankar Khuitam Power (66 MW, Arunachal Pradesh) approved; DPR being finalised, with the project expected to start by end-2026 and take 3-4 years.
Three small Chhattisgarh hydro projects (74 MW in total) may take 3-4 years to commission.
50 MW captive solar expected by end of Q1 FY27 (about September per later remarks); 30 MW TG set replacement to be back by end-June 2026.
Shahpur West high-grade coal mine targeted for commissioning before end-FY27; full-year operations expected in FY28.
Raipur pellet plant expansion from 0.9 to 2.0 MTPA, capex about INR500 crores, completion within 2.5 years; EC in place and DPR under preparation.

Annual hydro capex of about INR500-700 crores; the 600 MW IPP expansion to bring 'full blast' capex from next year, which will be substantially higher. Management did not give an investment figure for SKS expansion yet.
Management is evaluating separation of the renewable energy business (not the full power business); no conclusion yet.
Capex of about INR150 crores over the next two years at the Binjkot plant to improve PLF.

Mineral wool project installed to use industrial waste; management expects it to add to bottom line as it ramps up.
FY27 earnings drivers named: full-year Rehar hydro, efficiency gains at the IPP, 50 MW solar and the 30 MW TG set; FY28 driver is full-year Shahpur coal mine.
demand_pricing: Power exchange prices averaged INR3.75/unit in Q4 FY26, versus INR4.30 a year earlier and INR3.33 in Q3. Peak demand hit a record 270.8 GW.
Indian coal index rose 8% from March 2025 and 9% from December 2025 levels, due to import disruption from the West Asia conflict.

Steel prices recovered by about 10-15% in Q4 FY26 after reaching multi-year lows. Management expects long-product prices to rise once the conflict settles, but would not give Q1 FY27 realisation guidance.
Management said NMDC and OMC have cut iron ore prices, so end-product prices may fall.
India crude steel output grew over 11% in FY26; steel consumption about 164 million tonnes. Safeguard duties have reduced Chinese imports.

About 300 MW of the 600 MW IPP capacity is under PPA (medium/long term), with about 200 MW under PPA this year, rising to 300 MW next year. Management said PPA prices give more visibility than the volatile spot market.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited environment clearance and land/water already in place, and expected many Chhattisgarh iron ore mines to open within 2-2.5 years. The Raipur pellet expansion is designed to be ready when they do.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to improve IPP efficiency and EBITDA per unit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is scope to improve PLF at Binjkot, with about INR150 crores of capex planned over two years and spares and pending capex being completed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company demerge steel and power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only the renewable energy business is being examined for separation, with no conclusion yet; the full power business is not part of it.

qa_highlights.question: When will the SKS 600 MW doubling be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commissioning is now expected around 2030-31 because fresh environment clearance is being obtained, as the earlier clearance had expired. Capex amount will be given after configuration is frozen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-FY28 capex and growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual hydro capex is about INR500-700 crores, with the 600 MW expansion adding substantially higher capex from next year. FY27 growth comes from efficiency, full-year Rehar, the IPP, solar and TG set; FY28 from full-year Shahpur mine.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sellable units and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Previous-year sellable units were about 375 crore units and FY27 is guided to about 400 crore units. Average realisation was more than INR5 per unit.

qa_highlights.answer: Management called it normal treasury operations with no specific plans. Liquidity is about INR2,400 crores and the stake was about 1% of that.

504614|2026-06.headline: Sarda Energy Q1 FY27 total income INR 1,717 cr, EBITDA INR 762 cr and PAT INR 478 cr (+9.4% YoY), helped by a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit.
504614|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly EBITDA and PAT despite planned shutdowns, unplanned outages and weak small-hydro generation from delayed monsoon. Net profit included a one-time net benefit of INR 110 cr from regulatory approval of the final project cost of the 113 MW Sikkim hydro plant, which management said was worth about INR 162.6 cr of revenue and INR 18 cr of interest income. Energy contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA, and the company said it is now net debt-free with liquidity above INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026. Metals volumes fell QoQ because of captive power and furnace shutdowns at Raipur, Vizag and Siltara. Management declined to give numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Energy (IPP and captive power)
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA. Medium and long-term PPAs cover over 380 MW of 710 MW saleable capacity; about 330 MW of these are at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Small hydro output was hit by the delayed monsoon, and the company said it is roughly 1% below last year.

segments.name: Sikkim 113 MW hydro
segments.commentary: Shut from 18 June to 5 July 2026 after a transmission tower collapsed in heavy rain and landslide. Management said it is now running at full capacity, with about 5 days of July generation lost and the restoration cost covered by insurance apart from a minimal excess.

segments.name: Steel and ferro alloys (metals)
segments.commentary: Consolidated revenue fell QoQ on planned outages: a 30 MW captive unit replacement at Raipur (trial run now, commercial operation expected mid-August), a 23-day Vizag captive shutdown, and a 53-day Siltara ferro alloy furnace refurbishment. Steel prices were range-bound with a mild negative bias; ferro alloy prices improved modestly.

segments.name: Mineral wool (new)
segments.commentary: Running at about 60-65% of capacity, with production constrained by imported equipment held up by the West Asia crisis. Management said the project is not yet profitable, and it expects FY27 revenue of INR 90-110 cr.

segments.name: Mining (coal)
segments.commentary: Shahpur West is due to commission before end-FY27 (0.6 Mt). Bartunga Hill (2.1 Mt) is due by end-FY28. Gare Palma IV/5 (2.0 Mt), Gare Palma IV/7 (1.8 Mt) and Senduri (0.6 Mt, provisional) make up the mining plan; the target is 7.1 Mt capacity.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 PAT or EBITDA guidance; management said the company does not give forward profitability figures and that the market is volatile.
Q2 expected to be better than Q1, driven by hydro generation and higher power prices. July IEX prices were about INR 5/unit versus INR 4.19-4.20 a year earlier.
FY27 IPP generation expected to exceed last year's 415 crore units, with the captive plant utilisation also improving after the 30 MW unit restarts.
Steel and ferro alloy prices expected to remain stable. Ferro alloy margins may firm as raw material prices soften; steel may rise after a West Asia settlement and after monsoon.
Real power tariffs expected at INR 5-6/unit for the year, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

Full-year FY27 pipeline: 50 MW captive solar expected by end of next quarter (after a railway right-of-way delay); 74 MW Chhattisgarh small hydro approvals on schedule; Arunachal 66 MW hydro detailed engineering to begin this year.

SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW expansion: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant. The new unit is targeted for FY31 completion (per management, asked on the last call).
capex_capacity: SKS thermal expansion from 600 MW to 1,200 MW is awaiting regulatory approval, and the company describes the brownfield project as capital-efficient, using existing land, water and evacuation infrastructure.
Waste heat recovery power plant at Vizag, about INR 300 cr, for energy efficiency; all expansion projects funded through internal accruals.

Coal mining: Shahpur West commissioning before end-FY27; Bartunga Hill by end of next financial year; Gare Palma IV/5, IV/7 and Senduri approvals in progress. Management said the Gare Palma IV/7 expansion from 1.8 Mt to 5 Mt is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.
Shahpur West coal is high grade and is destined for sponge iron and ferro alloy plants, not the power plants.
Plans to quadruple mining capacity and double energy generation capacity, per management.
demand_pricing: India power generation grew 9.4% YoY to about 523 BU in the quarter; thermal grew 7.5%; solar generation rose about 45%; small hydro fell about 30% and large hydro about 7%.
Day-ahead market averaged INR 3.85/unit vs INR 3.92 a year earlier, but July prices rose to about INR 5/unit from INR 4.19. Management said peak hours have lengthened from 5 to 8-10 hours.
Indian coal index for June 2026 was about 21% above June 2025 and about 11% above March 2026.
India crude steel output grew over 7.5% in H1 CY26; imports exceeded exports again after two quarters. Management welcomed anti-dumping investigations.
West Asia conflict is raising input costs and creating supply chain issues. Management called the impact manageable but is in a wait-and-watch stance.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly EBITDA per management

financial_highlights.metric: One-time net benefit in PAT (Sikkim final project cost approval)
financial_highlights.change: Approx. INR 162.6 cr revenue and INR 18 cr other income pre-tax; about 25% of INR 110 cr at EBITDA level per CFO

financial_highlights.value: More than INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the back-calculated realisation is wrong because current income includes prior-year adjustments. Full-year power should be assumed at INR 5-6/unit, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

qa_highlights.answer: Revenue impact was about INR 162.64 cr and other income about INR 18 cr (interest awarded with tariff). EBITDA effect is about 25% of the INR 110 cr, net of tax.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 380 MW of PPAs is at SKS, what tariff applies, and what is the maximum SKS PPA quantity?
qa_highlights.answer: About 330 MW of the 380 MW is at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Maximum SKS quantity is 540 MW, and management said it still has to decide how far to commit.

qa_highlights.question: Which coal mines make up the 7.1 Mt target, and is Gare Palma IV/7 expansion to 5 Mt planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gare Palma IV/7 is 1.8 Mt, Shahpur West 0.6 Mt, Senduri about 0.6 Mt (provisional), and Gare Palma IV/5 about 2.0 Mt. Management said the 1.8 to 5 Mt expansion is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW environmental clearance timeline and construction start?
qa_highlights.answer: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant before procedures start. Management did not give a construction start date.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new SKS unit be completed, and will turnover more than double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated completion by FY31, as stated on the last call. On turnover doubling, management said it should be by that time.

qa_highlights.question: Has Sikkim hydro normalised, and is there residual Q2 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Sikkim is operating at full capacity. Management does not expect a residual impact in Q2, apart from about 5 days of July generation lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 PAT and EBITDA be guided numerically?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it does not give forward profitability guidance given the volatile market. It said Q2 should be better on hydro and July power prices, and FY27 IPP generation should exceed last year's 415 crore units.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mineral wool revenue, and what are the Q2 and FY27 sales and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant is at 60-65% of capacity and not yet profitable. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 90-110 cr, said Q2 is hard to comment on, and expects full production in about 6 months.

risks_watch: Delayed monsoon and hydro generation: small hydro was about 1% below last year in Q1, and Q2 depends on rainfall.

West Asia conflict: input cost inflation and supply chain disruption; steel prices hinge on a settlement. Solar daytime oversupply could weigh on day-time power prices, with BESS expected to offset.
Quality of earnings: Q1 PAT included a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit, and the company gave no numerical FY27 guidance.

504903|2026-03.headline: Rathi Steel FY26 total income rose ~41.7% to INR716 crore; Q4 PAT INR7.45 crore at 3% margin, with mills still only ~51-52% utilised.
504903|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of about INR716 crore (+41.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR28.9 crore (+18.8%) and PAT of INR12.87 crore (+39.24%, excluding prior-year exceptional items). Q4 total income was INR244.57 crore (+63.3% YoY, +52.7% QoQ), EBITDA INR9.89 crore (+22% YoY, +54% QoQ) and PAT INR7.45 crore, with PAT margin of about 3%. Growth was attributed to the restart of the idle TMT rolling mill in April 2025, which lifted rolling output about 117% to roughly 1,02,000 tons. Utilisation remains low at about 51-52% for both rolling and melting, which management sees as the main lever for margins.

segments.name: Rolling mill (TMT and stainless wire rod)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~2,00,000 tons per annum, utilisation ~51.4% in FY26; output grew ~117% YoY to ~1,02,000 tons after the TMT mill restart. Management did not split volumes between TMT and stainless.

segments.name: Steel melting shop (SMS)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~85,000 tons per annum, utilisation ~53% in FY26 (50-52% cited in opening remarks); about 40-45% backward integrated. Target is ~80% utilisation.

segments.name: Stainless steel vs TMT revenue mix
segments.commentary: Management estimated ~60% of FY26 revenue from B2B (mainly stainless) and ~40% from TMT bars, an approximate figure.

guidance_outlook: Rolling mill utilisation targeted at ~65-70% this year (fallback ~60-65%), up from ~51%.
Steel melting shop utilisation to move from ~50-52% towards ~80%.
Aspiration for ~20-25% average annual growth, using FY25 as base; earlier guidance was ~20% CAGR over three years.
Direct charging on the TMT mill expected to save ~INR3,000-4,000 per ton, or ~6-7% of TMT selling price including yield benefits, on the directly charged volume.
Capex of ~INR20 crore+ a year expected to continue for a few years, mainly replacement and debottlenecking; SMS expansion under study subject to approvals.
Refinancing talks under way with the existing lender at 16% cost of borrowing, with new lenders being explored at lower rates.
capex_capacity: Melting capacity ~85,000 tpa and rolling ~2,00,000 tpa at a ~12.5-acre NCR (Ghaziabad) site; FY26 utilisation ~51-52% for both divisions.
FY26 capex of INR20 crore+, mostly replacement and debottlenecking; the TMT restart cost ~INR5-7 crore in FY25.
Direct charging being implemented on the TMT mill, following its success in stainless wire rod.
SMS capacity expansion being evaluated at costs well below industry benchmarks; a larger melting unit is under consideration subject to demand visibility and statutory clearances.
Rooftop solar feasibility under study, indicatively 1-2 MW; open-access renewable power is over one-fourth of total power consumption.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic steel demand is healthy, with TMT and rebar pricing recovering after a prolonged soft patch.
Imports, mainly from Asia, are pressuring the industry; management says few rebar or stainless long products are imported into NCR, so the direct impact is limited.
Stainless steel pricing comes under pressure above a certain utilisation level; the company is shifting to a more balanced product mix to reduce reliance on any one category.
TMT sold mainly in NCR because freight limits longer-distance sales; stainless also sold in other states.
Institutional buyers are increasingly asking for GreenPro-certified products, which the company obtained for its Rathi Powertech 550 grade TMT bars (CII GreenPro Type-1 Ecolabel).
Fuel costs have roughly doubled over two to three months due to the Iran situation, which management cited as a margin headwind.

qa_highlights.question: What were TMT and stainless volume growth and spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no separate TMT and stainless volumes; overall rolled output grew ~117% to ~1,02,000 tons. Margins are expected to improve with higher utilisation, subject to fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of borrowing and the finance cost reduction target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Current cost of borrowing is 16% from a single lender. Talks are under way to refinance and secure additional need-based facilities at lower cost; no reduction target was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GST disputes and how much is under dispute?
qa_highlights.answer: Disputes relate to alleged input ITC issues at various adjudication stages; some are stayed by higher courts. Management does not expect any demand to crystallise. No amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the payment and inventory cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Average debtor period is ~25-30 days across products (receivables ~1 month). Payables ~60 days; inventory ~25-30 days (about one month overall).

qa_highlights.question: What are the key competitors and how does Rathi compete?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NCR proximity for delivery, brand recall and distribution network as edges; cost will be at par with peers once direct charging is in place on TMT.

qa_highlights.question: What are the challenges to reach 75-80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited establishing product acceptance for the restarted TMT mill and stainless supply pressure from IBC-driven acquisitions two years ago, with demand expected to catch up with supply.

risks_watch: Fuel cost spike (Iran-related) eroding the direct-charging saving and the margin recovery.
Stainless steel pricing pressure as utilisation rises, given new supply from IBC acquisitions.
Single-lender dependence at 16% cost of borrowing; refinancing outcome is pending.
Unquantified GST input-credit disputes with adjudication and stays still pending.
Management did not give a Q4 volume split between TMT and stainless, or Q4 raw material cost; key data gaps.
Slow utilisation ramp (51% to 65-70% target) and the 550D premium-grade product push.
Plant ageing; ongoing replacement capex needed.

504903|2026-06.headline: Rathi Steel & Power Q1 FY27 total income rose 24.6% to INR193.67 crores, PAT up 84.5% to INR3.48 crores, with volumes up ~30% to 28,372 MT.
504903|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong volume growth, driven by TMT bars, which more than doubled to about 18,677 MT from about 8,200 MT a year earlier. Total income reached INR193.67 crores (+24.6% YoY), EBITDA INR7.77 crores (+24.83%), and PAT INR3.48 crores (+84.5%), taking PAT margin to 1.8% (+58 bps). Stainless steel volumes were soft, down roughly 10-12% YoY to about 9,000 MT, mainly due to export-linked end-users hit by freight costs and West Asia disruption. Management reiterated a rolling mill utilisation target above 60% for FY27 and a 20% revenue CAGR aspiration, while the TMT 550D direct-charging integration is still in trial and expected to ramp post-monsoon.

vs ~8,200 MT in Q1 FY26, more than doubled
Q1 and Q4 respectively; not disputed by management

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: Volumes more than doubled to ~18,677 MT; roughly 47-48% of revenue, sold ~100% in NCR, largely to real estate. Brand portion is only 48-50% integrated; 550D integration trial runs done, full ramp expected post-monsoon.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Volumes ~9,000 MT, down 10-12% YoY on export-linked end-user weakness; roughly 52-53% of revenue. Management says it is more margin-accretive due to higher integration; 80-90% of range is 200 series.

Target of 20% revenue CAGR over the next two to three years, measured from FY25 base; management says achievable.
EBITDA margin improvement of 2-3 percentage points over about two years (FY27-FY28) cited as aspiration, from a range-bound 4-4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Stainless steel volumes and Q2 trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Stainless volumes were ~9,000 MT, down 10-12% YoY, due to export-linked end-users hit by freight costs and West Asia disruption; management aims to recover to last year's level.

qa_highlights.question: Rolling mill utilisation and exit rate for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Capex spent so far and full-year plan?

qa_highlights.question: Margin levers and EBITDA target?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital funding for the 30% volume increase?

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.

segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

505010|2026-06.headline: Automotive Axles Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 13.6% (from 12.4% QoQ) on revenue of Rs 5,168 mn and PAT of Rs 455 mn.
505010|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 5,168 million, EBITDA of Rs 702 million (about 13.6%), and profit for the year of Rs 455 million (about 8.7%, EPS about Rs 30). Management described EBITDA as one of the highest margins the company has achieved, helped by mix, a one-off, and lower employee costs versus the high-volume Q4. Management now sees the FY27 M&HCV industry down 5-10% versus last year, against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption, with Q4 expected to be a peak quarter. Capacity expansion (Phase-1 and Phase-1(a)) is about 40% complete.

segments.name: M&HCV on-highway axles (India)
segments.commentary: Management says demand is driven by replacement cycle and the shift from 6x2 to 10x2 or 4x2 tractor-trailers; heavy-duty (40 t and above) is the core focus. Overlap with American Axle described as minimal.

segments.name: Exports (to Meritor/CDBS global plants)
segments.commentary: Exports were about 13% of the quarter's revenue, versus a traditional 8-12% range; management guides to 8-12% for the year, with sea freight the main logistics challenge.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Defence contributes about 5-10% of revenue depending on tender timing; long gestation of 3-10 years from RFQ to SOP.

segments.name: Bus axles and new products
segments.commentary: Low-floor bus axle launch is still in validation, and is being reworked for upcoming pass-by noise norms. A 160 tandem axle is entering production with a large customer.

guidance_outlook: Management's FY27 industry view is a 5-10% decline versus last year (about 480,000 M&HCV units), against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption; best case is flat with last year.
Q2 expected to be reasonable, Q3 to see increasing demand, and Q4 to be another peak quarter, subject to geopolitical and monsoon risks.
Management guides to a steady-state PAT margin of 7.5-8.5% for the coming quarters and frames it as an overall band.
Capacity additions of roughly 25-30% are planned to cover the next two to three years of market growth, with Phase-1 and Phase-1(a) about 40% complete.
Management says it will not give specific volume guidance but expects better conversion and margins if volumes exceed the prior year.

Management says capacity must also be matched by supply chain readiness.
demand_pricing: Q1 M&HCV industry volume was about 110,000 units, down about 30% QoQ from the Q4 peak but among the highest Q1s in several years.
Steel and other commodity cost increases are fully passed through to customers on a back-to-back basis.
Conversion cost increases (LPG, tooling, consumables) were absorbed in Q1 with price negotiations ongoing with customers.
Management says the delayed monsoon is supporting freight and replacement demand.
Management says share of business with Ashok Leyland was maintained; the company confirmed it is a single source for some new products, with dual sourcing common at OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex breakup and growth versus replacement components of the Rs 120 crore programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split is hard to separate. Capex is for upgrades, automation and capacity for the next 2-3 years, roughly 25-30% capacity improvement.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and OEM opportunities split between Automotive Axles and American Axle (Bharat Forge)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two are competitors, that it cannot comment on the competitor's plans, and that exports go mainly to CDBS global entities.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company lost market share at Ashok Leyland?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a loss of share; the gap reflects product mix and seasonal/segment shifts. Confirmed Ashok Leyland share was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How was the cost of steel and gas handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel and other commodities are passed through fully. Conversion cost increases were absorbed in Q1 with recovery from customers being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised industry outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry down 5-10% versus the earlier 15-20%; best case is flat with last year, Q4 a peak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the regulatory outlook for bus axles and new product launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Bus axle product launch is in validation and is being reworked for pass-by noise regulations; a 160 tandem axle is entering production.

Defence revenue lumpy with tender timing (5-10% of revenue).

505160|2026-03.headline: Talbros Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR241 crore with record 18.7% EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to 15-20% growth.
505160|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest quarter by its account, with consolidated revenue of INR241 crore (up from INR211 crore) and EBITDA of INR45 crore at an 18.7% margin. FY26 revenue was INR1,383 crore (up 5%), EBITDA INR155 crore (17.5% margin) and PAT INR104 crore (up 10%). Management said the company is moving from order acquisition to execution, with several delayed orders (Stellantis, a European EV customer, Forging, Cummins, JLR) now starting in FY27. Forging margins were pressured in Q4 by pass-through of raw material and rupee-driven price resets.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth since FY24 lagged the order wins of about INR4,000 crore, and were there internal factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delays were largely customer-driven: a European EV order was delayed (now 50/50 EV mix, starting September), the Stellantis order starts June, and Forging orders slipped a year. Earlier 5-year order books of INR326 crore and INR431 crore delivered only partly in annual revenue terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the standalone business grow double digits in FY27, and what is the margin outlook given input cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, double-digit growth expected; at least INR60-70 crore of new billing from new part numbers. Management asked investors not to focus on quarterly margins, saying price increases are generally recovered in one to three months through proprietary products and metal/exchange-linked pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned by division and what is the outlook for the next year?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex of INR16 crore in Gasket and Heat Shield, INR60 crore in Forging, about INR20 crore Marelli, and about INR7 crore Marugo. FY27 capex to be worked out at end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18-20% aspirational growth purely organic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management referred to consolidated revenue of INR1,383 crore; new business of INR150-160 crore commercialising in June and October adds about 11-12%, with the balance from 6-7% market growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Forging margin compressed in Q4 with revenue up 11% and EBITDA up only 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a delayed price decrease pass-through in July-August and a price reset on 1 January after rupee depreciation; the benefit was passed on partly to customers. Margins expected to recover in one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Maruti at about 20% of revenue a concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers have 60-65% customer dependence, so 20% is comfortable; the share reflects strong passenger vehicle growth and high content per vehicle across all divisions except forgings. Exports expected to reach 30% in one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Marelli margins fall in Q1, and which segment will grow fastest in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower other income plus new manpower and shared rental costs; management expects margins to recover by year-end. Marelli is expected to grow 30-40% in FY27, forging about 20%, gaskets about 16-17%, and Talbros Marugo 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is data-centre gasket margin different from the rest of the gasket business, and what is the EV revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Same gasket product sold for a new application, with pricing unchanged; margins not split out. EV-related supply was INR12.5 crores in Q1 (about 3.27% of sales) versus INR10 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR9 crores a year ago; management targets around 5% in 2 years and a minimum of 5% over 5 years. JLR rubber EV components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. start in Q1/Q2 CY27.

risks_watch: Pass-through of steel, aluminium and labour inflation from OEMs has not yet happened; FY27 margin guide of about 17-17.5% depends on it.
Forging recovery depends on European demand, execution of the INR500 crores order book, and resolution of manpower and productivity issues; Q1 growth was only 4%.
Marelli JV: stake transaction still pending court proceedings with update expected by end-September; Q1 JV margin dip to be reversed by year-end.
Data-centre revenue (about 5% of gasket revenue) is concentrated in a single customer, Cummins, and depends on engine orders.
Lost Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.) and Cummins America ramp-up timing (slow starter) could weigh on the forging and gasket revenue trajectory.
Export share at about 25% against a 35% FY28 target; EV share at 3.27% of sales against a 5% goal.
key_quotes: Talbros has delivered yet another record quarter, achieving its highest ever quarterly revenue and surpassing the previous high recorded in quarter 4 of '26.
But we are very positive that we will get these increases from the OEMs in the coming quarters.
We are pretty much single source to Cummins for this particular engine component.
Plus, we are supplying bushes to BMW of EV vehicles, where sale has gone up a little bit there.
505160|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on growth, order wins and the record quarter, but cautious on margins, which it says are under temporary inflation pressure. On forging and Marelli it was more guarded, with several answers deferred to later updates such as the end-September Marelli stake update.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 17.6% in Q1 is under temporary steel, aluminium and labour pressure; FY27 guide is about 17-17.5%, dependent on OEM pass-through that has not yet happened, and Marelli margin is expected to recover by year-end.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Planned FY27 capex of about INR103 crores across gaskets, forgings and heat shields, but capacity is not quantified; Stellantis programme started production in Q1 FY27 and forging equipment is reportedly in place, and a Gujarat chassis plant with Tata Motors is only under discussion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Group revenue growth guided at 18-20% for FY27, gaskets about 17% to INR680-700 crores, forging 15-20% to INR340-350 crores with Q2 at double-digit growth, and Marelli 30-40%; Q1 forging was only +4%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was disclosed, so the capex call rests on the INR103 crore FY27 plan and a possible Gujarat chassis plant with Tata Motors, with a meeting due within 90 days.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Forging guidance was cut to INR340-350 crores from earlier expectations of around INR400 crores, and the margin guide of 17-17.5% rests on pass-through not yet achieved, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Forging Q1 grew only 4% after the loss of Meritor (INR30-40 crores p.a.), manpower shortages and weak European demand, and the INR17.5% margin depends on OEM pass-through that is not yet in place.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: JLR plastic EV components (about INR25 crores in orders) mature from next financial year, JLR EV rubber components (INR15-20 crores p.a.) start Q1/Q2 CY27, and data-centre gaskets are growing (INR25 crores Cummins sales in Q1 vs INR90 crores last year).

rows.label: Forging order book of about INR500 crores over 5 years
rows.when: Marelli and Dana/Carraro orders maturing Q3-Q4 FY27
rows.why: About INR100 crores p.a. of forging orders cited, which underpins the INR340-350 crores FY27 forging guide and the 15-20% growth expectation.

rows.label: Cummins America and data-centre gaskets
rows.why: Cummins America expected to contribute INR30-40 crores by FY27-28, but management calls it a slow starter and Cummins Q1 sales fell to INR25 crores from INR90 crores a year earlier.

rows.label: Marelli stake transaction
rows.why: Stake deal is in court proceedings with no firm update; management expects a clearer picture by end-September, so the outcome is unresolved.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record quarter, order wins and 18-20% group growth, but cautious on margins under inflation and guarded on forging and the pending Marelli stake deal; analysts pushed on forging guidance cut, Marelli margin dip and data-centre concentration.

505192|2026-03.headline: SML Mahindra FY26 revenue rose 18% and PAT 31%, but Q4 PAT grew only 2% on a 16% revenue rise as commodity inflation hit.
505192|2026-03.overview: This was the first investor call since Mahindra's 58.96% controlling acquisition completed on 1 August 2025, about eight months post-takeover. Management said FY26 volumes grew 28% in cargo and 12% in passenger vehicles, with market share up 20 bps in cargo and 80 bps in passenger for the full year. Q4 showed a cargo share dip, which management attributed to pre-poned institutional orders executed in Q3, while bus share gained 170 bps in the quarter. Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost (roughly 3.5-3.7% annualised), and a price increase of about 2-3% was taken from 15 April 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up two notches from AA minus

segments.name: Cargo (trucks)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 28% with market share up 20 bps for the year; Q4 cargo share declined, attributed by management to Q3 pre-ponement of institutional orders. Q4 cargo volume grew 10%.

segments.name: Passenger (buses)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 12% with market share up 80 bps; Q4 bus share gained 170 bps in the peak school-bus season. Q4 passenger volume grew 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a top-three position in India's ILCV trucks and buses segment, with focus on HCVs, and targets 10-12% combined market share by FY31 (currently about 6%).
Around FY31, the company targets about Rs 15,000 crore revenue, per the Global Investor Day, against a 3.5-tonne-plus revenue pool of about Rs 1.25 lakh crore last year.
Q1 FY27 plans are largely unchanged from original plans as of the call; management said a diesel price increase is the key swing factor.

Commodity inflation is expected to be partly temporary; management said price increases and commodity hedges should largely cover headwinds, and inflation is not expected to persist through FY27 if the Middle East situation eases.
First EV bus is to be launched in FY27; management gave no capex or volume figures for it.
A longer-format strategy session is planned for July 2026, close to the AGM.
capex_capacity: Service network: combined touchpoints to rise from about 300 to 450 by pooling 150 service setups across both brands; 70 are operational and 80 more are due by end of Q1 FY27.

Engineering and manufacturing synergies are being pursued to reduce product cost and capex outlay, including sharing engine (4-valve diesel and CNG 3.8-litre) and ADAS development with Mahindra teams.
ADAS regulation compliance (due in about 1.5 years) is a joint project with Mahindra, with cost detail deferred to launch.
EV bus development is underway; management said capex for scale-up will depend on market evolution.
demand_pricing: Industry grew about 2% in H1 FY26 and about 22% in H2 post-GST reform; ICV trucks +42%, LCV trucks +20%, MCV trucks +28%, ILCV +8% in that period.
Management sees no demand deferment yet and cites pent-up replacement demand, though a diesel price hike and Middle East disruption could moderate demand.
Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost; Q1 FY27 saw further increases in some commodities (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases), with some volatility.
Price increases of about 2% (some 3%) on SML products effective 15 April 2026; more may follow based on analysis.
Electric bus industry share is below 1% of the segment; private buyers are not yet buying e-buses beyond STU purchases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook, market share trajectory and synergy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry shifted from about 2% growth in H1 to about 22% in H2. Management said synergies come on both the back end (sourcing, engineering, manufacturing) and the front end (common dealers in unrepresented territories), with growth as the main thesis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to merge the two companies or delist SML?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delisting plan. On a merger, it is working on long-term strategy and will update at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the supply chain and cost impacts of the current crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: No vehicle production was lost through Q4 despite gas, aluminium and polymer shortages. Steel, aluminium, copper and polymers rose, and gases trade at a premium; management expects most increases to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called ADAS a significant development and said cost and detail would be shared at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand deferment seen in March or April?
qa_highlights.answer: No deferment as of now; peak school-bus season is underway and Q1 plans are largely as originally planned, but management flagged diesel price risk.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 margin headwind and what pricing offset is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 inflation was about 1.3% of cost (about 3.5-3.7% annualised). Price increases of about 2-3% began 15 April, and hedges will provide a partial offset, though steel cannot be hedged. Management said pricing should largely cover headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV bus and e-mobility strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EV bus launches in FY27 with product details to follow closer to launch. Capex scale-up will depend on market evolution, as private buyers are not yet buying e-buses.

risks_watch: Diesel price increase and Middle East disruption could moderate CV demand after Q1 FY27.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases) may persist; hedges do not cover steel, and pricing actions may lag.
Q4 PAT growth of 2% vs revenue growth of 16% indicates margin pressure that must be tracked in Q1 FY27.
Cargo market share dip in Q4 FY26 tied to order timing; watch whether share recovers in FY27.
Integration delivery: service network expansion to 450 touchpoints and cross-badging, plus dealer-channel sensitivity.
Timing and scope of the July 2026 strategy session and merger-related updates.
505192|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, integration progress and the demand tailwind, but cautious on the near-term outlook. Management was guarded on the diesel price, commodity inflation and EV timing, and avoided quantifying ADAS cost and merger plans.
key_quotes: We have outgrown the industry. We grew at 17% in the industry versus industry growth of 13%.
So, the main thesis behind this acquisition was growth.

We have not lost any vehicle production till quarter four in spite of several challenges, whether it is related to availability of gas or whether it is related to many other commodity availability, including aluminium, including polymers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: A 2-3% price increase from 15 April 2026 and hedges should largely offset commodity inflation, but steel cannot be hedged and Q4 PAT growth of 2% against 16% revenue growth shows margin pressure not yet recovered.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Service touchpoints pooled from about 300 to about 450, with 70 operational and 80 more due by end Q1 FY27, but no plant or line capacity was discussed and EV bus scale-up capex depends on market evolution given sub-1% e-bus share.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 cargo volume grew 28% and passenger 12% with share up 20 bps and 80 bps, Q4 cargo volume grew 10% and passenger 16%, and no demand deferment seen as of the call, with industry up about 22% in H2 post-GST.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation not quantified and management said no vehicle production was lost through Q4; capex is tied to synergies (shared engines, ADAS with Mahindra) and cautious EV scale-up, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance held (10-12% combined share and ~Rs 15,000 crore revenue by FY31) and Q1 FY27 plans are largely unchanged, with diesel price flagged as the key swing factor.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 PAT grew 2% on 16% revenue growth from roughly 1.3% of cost commodity inflation (about 3.5-3.7% annualised), and diesel price hike or Middle East disruption could moderate demand after Q1 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First EV bus is to be launched in FY27 with no capex or volume figures given, and product details to follow closer to launch.

rows.label: Price increase of 2-3% effective 15 April 2026
rows.why: Price increases of about 2% (some 3%) on SML products are already effective from 15 April 2026, against Q4 commodity inflation of about 1.3% of cost, with more increases possible.

rows.label: Strategy session and merger update in July 2026
rows.why: A longer-format strategy session is planned near the AGM, but management gave no delisting plan and no merger timeline, so scope is uncertain.

rows.label: Engineering and sourcing synergies with Mahindra
rows.why: Shared 4-valve diesel and CNG 3.8-litre engines and ADAS development are being pursued to cut product cost and capex outlay, though ADAS cost is not yet quantified and is due in about 1.5 years.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 growth, share gains, integration and the demand tailwind, but cautious on diesel prices, commodity inflation, EV timing and merger plans; analysts pressed on margins, demand after Q1 and the ADAS cost, which management deferred to launch.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.1 crore (1.5%) in Q1 FY26; 9.6% in Q4 FY26 per analyst
+223% YoY vs INR1.1 crore; margin up from 1.5%

segments.name: Standalone TIL (cranes, material handling, defence)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Tulip Compression (TCPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.name: Aftermarket / services
segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significant jump in FY27 turnover, but gave no numeric revenue guidance. Analyst's INR200 crore+ scenario was not confirmed.
Management expects no EBITDA margin harmonisation for the next six to eight quarters; medium-to-long-term TIL standalone EBITDA target 15-16%, timing 3-7 years.
Five-to-seven-year ambition to roughly triple turnover; no significant capex needed up to about INR700-750 crore turnover, beyond bridging capex of INR5-10 crore.
Debtor days target 60-75 days maximum; long-term aftermarket share target 40-45% of revenue.
Board approved up to INR50 crore equity infusion into Tulip; commitment to raise stake to 74% over a few years.
CarryKing 515 launch hoped for Q4 FY27, worst case Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Kharagpur plant loaded only 30-35% with about 150 acres free; Kamarhati plant is old and fully loaded.
Bridging capex of INR5-10 crore per instance, mainly for the old Kamarhati plant.
Target to localise 75-80% in every product and above 90% overall, with Cummins engines for ReachStacker a key dependency.
Pick and carry crane (CarryKing 515) launch targeted Q4 FY27 with 520 configuration to follow.
demand_pricing: ReachStacker market share 38-40% after a comeback; CONCOR order described as one-time, first such order since 2014-15.
Rough terrain crane market share about 50%+; truck crane share now below 5% from over 95% a decade ago, lost to Chinese competition.
Order delivery timelines range from 60-90 days (retail ReachStacker) to 6-9 months (defence), with the bulk of the order book typically exhausted within nine months.
Chinese competitors have pricing and credit advantages; management said TIL will not compete on extended credit terms.
Tulip's market share is about one-third in India in a three-player market; clients include city gas distributors such as IGL, MNGL and IGL-type CGD operators.

qa_highlights.question: ReachStacker market share, competitors and whether the Q1 order is CONCOR.
qa_highlights.answer: Share is 38-40%, and the CONCOR order is one-time. Management expects ReachStacker sales to scale to a sizable number this year via retail and niche buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix and localisation drive volatility; Q4 had Air Force cranes and ReachStackers. No harmonised margin for six to eight quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtor days.
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TIL competes on reliability, durability, and aftermarket uptime commitments, not on credit terms.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: management called the working capital cycle stressed; debtor days and debt reduction are the key items to track.
Margin volatility: EBITDA margins depend on product mix, and management gave no margin guidance for six to eight quarters.
Supply-chain dependence: localisation of European and US inputs (Cummins engines, gearboxes) depends on OEM and defence approvals and could take several quarters.
Execution: converting the INR211 crore standalone order book and the INR328 crore TCPL order book on time; the FY26 shortfall was attributed to geopolitics and logistics.
Governance and bandwidth: the Chairman plans to devote 40-50% of his time to TIL from next quarter, versus about 60% needed, and the Gainwell merger question was left open.
Tulip integration and TCPL full-quarter contribution in Q2 FY27.
505196|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term vision (tripling turnover, 15-16% margins, aftermarket targets) but cautious and explicit on near-term margins, which it said will not stabilise for six to eight quarters. It was candid on the stressed working capital cycle and declined to quantify FY27 revenue or Tulip profit projections.
key_quotes: Hence, we are looking at a few more quarters before we are really able to fix the margins.
You're right, working capital cycle at this stage in TIL looks stressed.

rows.why: Standalone order book is INR211 crore and TCPL order book INR328 crore, with nine ReachStackers delivered and a full-quarter TCPL contribution from Q2 FY27; management expects a significant jump in FY27 turnover, though no numeric guidance was given.

505200|2026-03.headline: Eicher Motors Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR8,280.6 mn? No: Q4 consolidated revenue INR6,080 crore? Transcript-stated EML Q4 revenue INR6,080, PAT INR1,520.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue (EML, as stated by Govind)
Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue (VECV, as stated by Srinivas)

segments.name: Royal Enfield (motorcycles)
segments.commentary: FY26 domestic motorcycle sales rose 23% to 1.1 million units; exports grew 20% to 120,634 units. Record FY26 total of 1.227 million motorcycles, with Brazil up 71% and now the largest international market. Apparel grew 21%, Genuine Motorcycle Accessories rose 32%, and spare parts grew 18%.

segments.name: VECV (commercial vehicles)
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes of 103,404 units, up 15%. Heavy-duty truck volumes were 25,155 with market share up to 9.1% from 8.4%... (stated as 14.1% growth with share improving to 9.1%); LMD trucks 46,195; buses 18,651; exports up 33.9% to 6,933 units; spare parts revenue up 13.9% to INR3,045.5 crore.

segments.name: Volvo Financial Services JV (proposed)
segments.commentary: Proposed 50:50 JV with Volvo Group for financing, leasing and other services, with EML investing up to INR750 crore for a 50% stake; the target company has assets under management of INR1,806 crore and has been operating for 10 years.

guidance_outlook: Management does not normally give numeric forward guidance; said the company is geared for a growth-led FY27.
Domestic motorcycle inquiry levels up 23% vs the previous period; booking rates at 7-8 days in May; bookings for 2025 vehicles described as strong.
Production capacity to be raised from 1.4 million to 1.6 million motorcycles per year by June-July 2026 via the 500 per day module, ahead of festive season.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion (INR958 crore capex) to add 2 million units of annual capacity by Q2 FY28.
Q1 FY27 material-cost headwind of 3% to 3.5% of material costs; 50% expected to be recovered via pricing and the rest via austerity and engineering savings, with projects kicking in by July-August.
Greenfield facility in Andhra Pradesh on 261 acres signed with the state government; typical 24-30 month window to become fully operational.
Medium-term: management expects the VECV trajectory to be upward; India's long-term drivers cited as infrastructure, logistics, e-commerce and cleaner mobility.
capex_capacity: Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu) brownfield expansion approved in February at INR958 crore, adding capacity from 1.6 million to 2 million units per year, targeted by Q2 FY28.
Current capacity of 1.4 million motorcycles per year, with a 500 per day module adding capacity to 1.6 million by June-July 2026.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield: 261 acres signed; MoU with state government; capacity to be planned beyond 2 million units.
JV investment capacity: up to INR750 crore for 50% of Volvo financing JV; target company net worth INR500 crore; management said it is adequately capitalised for the medium term.
Cheyyar land acquisition of 65 acres already in hand.
demand_pricing: Industry 250-750cc: management said FY26 domestic category sold 1.11 million motorcycles, up 23%; Q4 sales of 1.04 million, up 57% (as stated).
Inquiry levels up 23% vs previous period; no structural correction in demand per management.
Q4 price increase of 1.75% in April; Q4 margin pressure of 90 bps from costs, with 70 bps blended price increase taken in January and 20 bps offset by cost reduction and mix.
Premiumisation continuing; first-time buyers rising, with 30% of consumers under 25 years of age; GST reduction cited as a helper.
Europe continued to degrow; US tariff issues described as settled; US about 3% of total business.
VECV: entire FY26 broad-based growth; EV Pro X trucks delivered 2,452, incl. 726 EVs. Pro X named Debutant of the Year at Apollo CV Awards.
Supply disruptions in April-May from elections, manpower availability, LPG shortages and power issues described as temporary, lasting 1-2 weeks, with deliveries restarting.
Mid-size bike CAGR and inquiry momentum cited; no quantified category growth number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 retail outlook for the mid-size motorcycle category, and what are the expansion plans given thin dealer inventories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 industry sales were 1.11 million, up 23%, with no structural demand correction; bookings are 7-8 days, temporary supply issues are expected to clear in a week to 10 days, and capacity is going to 1.6 million units by June-July with the Cheyyar expansion by Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 3-3.5% material cost headwind is being passed on through pricing, and how much is being offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% of the 3-3.5% material cost headwind is recovered through the 1.75% April price increase, with the remaining 50% addressed through austerity measures and engineering savings; the Q4 margin hit was 90 bps, of which 70 bps was recovered in January pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Volvo financing JV see profit benefits and will it be a capital-hungry business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JV will run independently with its own risk profile and that EML will invest up to INR750 crore for 50%; the target has INR1,806 crore AUM; management expects to grow AUM to INR9,000-10,000 crore over 5 years with no hurry to scale.

qa_highlights.question: What are the product pipeline and timelines, including the Bullet 650 and any plans below 350cc?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project timelines shown at EICMA are on track; the Bullet 650 dispatch has started and the S6 was shown; the company focuses on 250-750cc, with platforms at 350cc, 450cc and 650cc.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Andhra Pradesh greenfield plant and its capacity ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the land MoU was signed this week, with the 261-acre parcel to be acquired; a plant is typically 24-30 months from land to full operation; no greenfield capacity timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MHCV outlook and how are fuel price hikes and labour shortages affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: VECV management said it took about 2% price increases from 1 April, with pass-through lagging due to time-bound transporter contracts; labour and LPG disruptions lasted 2-3 weeks and supply is improving.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: 3-3.5% material cost headwind in Q1 FY27 from the geopolitical situation, with only 50% expected to be recovered through pricing; watch Q1 gross margin.
Supply chain: elections, LPG availability, power issues and migrant labour movement disrupted production and deliveries in April-May; management expects normalisation within 1-2 weeks.
Fuel price hikes may hit transporter economics and the CV secondary market; VECV's pass-through is lagged by time-bound contracts.

505200|2026-06.headline: Eicher Motors Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 6,632 crore with record Royal Enfield volumes of 332,940 units.

Royal Enfield sold a record 332,940 motorcycles (up from 261,326), and VECV recorded its highest-ever Q1 sales of 24,815 units (up 14.8%). Management flagged a tight dealer inventory of 10-12 days ahead of festive season, with capacity ramp-up at Cheyyar and a greenfield Tada (Andhra Pradesh) plant approved. 505255|2026-03.headline: GMM Pfaudler FY26 revenue rose about 10% and EBITDA about 11% to INR 403 crore; Q4 gross margin fell, with no FY27 numeric guidance.
505255|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA rose from INR 361 crore to INR 403 crore, with full-year margin up about 1 percentage point. India was the standout, with revenue up about 12%, EBITDA up about 24% and PAT up about 40%. Q4 margins fell year-on-year and sequentially on a large HE (heavy engineering) shipment and higher gas and metal costs, which management called quarter-specific. FY26 order intake reached INR 3,714 crore (up about 20% from INR 3,100 crore) and opening backlog on April 1 was up about 34%. Management declined to give numeric FY27 guidance and said it would present a three-year plan to the market later.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 12%, EBITDA about 24% and PAT about 40% in FY26. Heavy engineering (Ahmedabad) did about INR 300+ crore revenue in FY26, and the Vatva facility (GMM Inox, Poland) grew double digits.

segments.commentary: Execution was slow; international EBITDA margin cited at about 10%. German restructuring is expected to save INR 45 crore a year once fully absorbed. Europe order intake was much stronger in FY26, including large systems orders.

segments.commentary: Edlon (semiconductor-linked high-purity linings) is now about USD 25 million revenue, which management called high margin. SEMCO (South America) won a USD 12-13 million agitator order in Q1 FY27; MixPro (Canada) is growing and profitable.

Q1 FY27 order intake continuing at a decent level, including an Edlon order of USD 8-9 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance for FY27, and what drives the growth and margin plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% order-intake rise includes systems orders that convert over 2-3 years, so it avoided a bullish number. It plans a three-year strategy to be presented to the capital markets once confidence improves, targeting at least double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the German restructuring saving and will exceptional items recur?
qa_highlights.answer: The German restructuring saves INR 45 crore a year, starting next year. No significant one-off cost is planned for FY27, though future restructurings would be reported as one-offs. FY26 exceptional items were about INR 65 crore, including German severance and the India labour code impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the finance cost high relative to a small net debt, and how does the company plan to reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FX on an intercompany loan between Germany and Luxembourg, and a financing agreement in place until 2028, which it intends to restructure within the next year. It said the high cash balance is partly customer prepayments needed to finance large systems orders.

qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to a 15% consolidated EBITDA margin in the medium term, as a minimum, versus about 11.4-11.5% today, and said it could come faster if initiatives work.

qa_highlights.question: Will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reporting format will change from next quarter (Q1 FY27), with a new organisation aligned by product, vertical and industry, rather than mid-year.

505255|2026-06.headline: GMM Pfaudler Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 925 crores, but EBITDA fell 7% YoY to INR 94 crores on pricing pressure and organisation-building costs.

The company moved to four global technology divisions (CRT, PPT, HET, PST) and disclosed segment results for the first time. segments.commentary: Revenue INR 466 crores (+10% YoY); order intake INR 502 crores (+23% YoY). Glass-lined pharma and chemical demand described as stable; large aftermarket and service base.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 255 crores (+23% YoY); order intake INR 367 crores (+64% YoY). Covers mixing, filtration, drying, and sealing; pharma and food & beverage adoption cited.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 74 crores (flat YoY); order intake INR 58 crores (up more than 700% YoY). India-led, oil and gas, petrochemicals, with nuclear and power entry and EIL approvals.

segments.name: PST (Process System Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 131 crores (+46% YoY); order intake INR 80 crores vs INR 363 crores in Q1 FY26, which included one large defence order. Skids and engineered systems for semiconductor, defence and pharma.

505283|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 21% to INR706 crore and FY26 PBT hit a record INR356 crore, but management flags 18-20% EBITDA as sustainable, not the 21.7% delivered.
505283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales were INR706 crore versus INR583 crore a year earlier, with raw material-to-sales falling to 50.06% from 56.35%. FY26 EBITDA was INR388 crore (21.7% of total income) and PBT INR356 crore (19.6%), supported by in-house backward integration and a selective order-acceptance stance. The unexecuted order board rose 15% to INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, including Precision Components, and the company remains debt-free with about INR460 crore net cash. Management called FY26's margin an exception and guided to 18-20% EBITDA going forward, while reaffirming a 20%+ growth aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR588 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: 600% of face value (INR12 per share), including final of INR8.50 and interim of INR3.50
About INR460 crore as on April 1, 2026

segments.name: Compression (only reportable segment)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 93.4% of total income; segment operating profit margin was 24.9% in FY26 versus 21.7% in FY25. Management said Q4 margin was a one-off and sustainable range is 18-20%.

segments.name: Air compression / ACD
segments.commentary: Roughly 18-20% of business. Tezcatlipoca centrifugal compressors gaining share (about 130 machines in field, 85 commissioned); reciprocating gas compressor orders at record highs; screw compressors lagged.

segments.name: Refrigeration (KC/KCX, Khione)
segments.commentary: Roughly 40-45% of business. Record KC/KCX volumes in FY26 and several large packages executed, some in Q4; Khione sales picking up.

segments.name: Process Gas Systems (PGS)
segments.commentary: Roughly 35-40% of business. Management described FY26 as lagging in oil and gas due to slower order finalisation; O&M base spans over 1,000 CNG stations; CNG order activity picking up in Q4.

segments.name: Precision Engineering (non-reportable in FY26)
segments.commentary: New division using Nashik and Hadapsar forgings, castings and machined components. Part of the INR1,863 crore order board; about INR500 crore executable beyond FY27. Will be reportable from Q1 FY27 per management.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin: 18-20% is the sustainable range; FY26's 21.7% is described as an exception, though management said it could reach 21% in good quarters.
Growth aspiration of 20%+ on top line and bottom line over a long period; management said it expects to deliver sales above order board conversion and reach 20%+ in FY27.
Equipment business (short-cycle, 4-12 weeks) targeted at 20-25% of revenue; new products targeted at 10-15% of sales.
Zephyros air conditioning package to be commercialised in Q1 FY27; A-800 centrifugal frame launch expected in about one month.

Continued capex to support growth and PLI-linked new product development; depreciation rose to INR31.1 crore in FY26 from INR28.9 crore.
Management said capacity is not a constraint at present; a subsidiary is being restructured and will take time to turn positive.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order board INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, up 15% from INR1,624 crore a year earlier; includes Precision Components. About INR500 crore executable beyond FY27.
Order inflow in the last two quarters about INR650 crore (per analyst); the order book is skewed toward products, which management said should shorten execution cycles.
Export about 6% of sales; MENA was a large share earlier but is slowing due to the Middle East conflict, with focus shifting to Southeast Asia and North Africa.
Management said price increases are passed to customers on short-cycle work, and large packages have had vendor pricing finalised, so no direct margin hit expected.
Gas package competition: specified vendor lists and lower-cost competitors make cost innovation difficult in Middle East gas packages.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book and what is the Precision Engineering share?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Birajdar said the INR1,863 crore book includes Precision Components; about INR500 crore is executable beyond FY27, and the equipment business brings in INR600-700 crore a year that is executed and dispatched within the year.

qa_highlights.question: Zephyros go-to-market and returns on the INR320 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target markets are small machine shops, restaurants and banquet halls, with channel build-out via dealers. Margins will be below the 25-30% sought, and returns will come from volume; INR60 crore has been spent so far.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East exposure and ability to win gas packages?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Kirloskar said the Middle East is a key market for packages but is not a large share of total business; near-term dispatch and new orders are difficult, and the company has won Middle East packages before.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 growth not follow a book-to-bill near 1 last year, and what changes now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed reliance on the gas business, where growth has been difficult, and said actions are being taken to improve competitiveness. Equipment and Precision Engineering are expected to carry growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is 21.5-21.7% EBITDA sustainable versus the 18-20% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Kirloskar said investors should not judge quarter to quarter; 18-20% is the base, with 21% possible. Ramesh Birajdar said Q4 gross margin crossed about 23% but 18-20% remains the sustainable core-business range.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the CNG and CGD demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said daughter stations are about 70% of new stations, with mother stations needed for long-haul supply, and demand should rise for both over time. Ramesh Birajdar pointed to ONGC's about INR200 billion investment over five to six years as an opportunity.

risks_watch: Margin normalisation: management guided to 18-20% EBITDA after a 21.7% FY26; watch whether Q1 FY27 holds above 20%.

Precision Engineering order sustainability is unclear; management declined to give a backlog split or say whether INR500 crore inflows will repeat.
Middle East conflict is slowing dispatches and new export gas orders, with MENA share of exports falling.
Zephyros commercial launch in Q1 FY27 with unproven demand; a subsidiary restructuring is under way with no timeline for positive results.
Equity sub-division from INR2 to INR1 face value and final dividend are subject to shareholder approval.

505533|2026-03.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q4 FY26 same-store sales grew 1.5% on mid-single-digit guest count growth; revenue up 9% to INR 6.6 billion.
505533|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 6.6 billion and same-store sales grew 1.5%, driven by mid-single-digit guest count growth, with positive footfall in all three months and momentum continuing into April. Full-year revenue grew 5% to INR 26.3 billion. Gross margin held near historic highs at 68.1% (up about 60 bps QoQ), and full-year cash PAT was INR 2.4 billion (9% of sales). Management said it is too early to call a sustained revival, and it guided to 60+ restaurant openings in FY27 versus a record 48 in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: About +60 bps QoQ; near historic highs

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: Management described West as the strongest growth driver, though it was affected by LPG disruptions; no specific West SSS figure was given.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Same-store sales ended the quarter nearly flat, a meaningful improvement on prior quarters, with guest count turning marginally positive after the company rolled back to everyday value (except Chennai, where it is a trial).

segments.name: Digital and delivery (McDelivery, app)
segments.commentary: Cumulative app downloads crossed 52 million with about 3.5 million monthly active users growing at double-digit YoY; delivery grew about 6% vs dine-in about 9%.

qa_highlights.answer: Supply chain initiatives and an internal cost project offset inflation; FY26 inflation was a tailwind that may not repeat. Pricing policy is 2-4% a year, but no price increase has been taken for four to five months and none is planned.

qa_highlights.answer: The 60+ number reflects Vision 2027 (580-630 restaurants) and penetration headroom; closures are portfolio management of about 6-7 a year and were not South-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion target hold if the LPG and raw material pressure persists for six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the store target holds, citing cost levers and industry-wide price increases as options if inflation rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the health and protein-led consumer read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mid-single-digit guest count growth shows no health-driven issue; it cited the Aloo Tikki balanced meal, lower sodium fries, reduced mayo fat, protein slice and millet bun as menu choices.

505533|2026-06.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 7.36 billion with SSSG of 4.3%, though operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable amid inflation.
505533|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR 7.36 billion, up 12% YoY, with same-store sales growth of 4.3% and positive SSSG in all three months. Growth was guest-count led, with double-digit footfall growth and the South turning SSSG-positive. Operating EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 946 million, but the operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable as over 200 bps of inflation (fuel, food, packaging, utilities, labour) was absorbed. Management said Q1 marks the peak of gross margin pressure and expects improvement from here, while restaurant additions were only 5 in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Positive in all three months; May and June mid-single-digit

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Management described West as continuing to deliver a very strong performance, with growth aided by a rollout of the value platform and expanded store clusters in Gujarat, Pune/rest of Maharashtra and Mumbai (each ~100 restaurants).

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: South ended the quarter with positive SSSG and double-digit guest count in all three months; management cited close to 4.5% SSSG this quarter. South has more than half of the store base per management, and Bangalore has 60+ restaurants, Hyderabad 35+ and Chennai 20+.

guidance_outlook: Over 60 new restaurants in FY27, reiterated as on track; 580 to 630 restaurants by December 2027 (Vision 2027).

Management expects some cost pressures to ease as geopolitical conditions improve; targets 100-150 bps YoY improvement in pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin as an internal long-term guidance, and aspires to 100+ bps expansion in FY27 (FY26 pre-Ind AS margin cited as 7.6%).
Mid-single-digit SSSG confidence for the year, with South expected to reach mid-single-digit; management declined to give high-single-digit targets.
G&A expected at 6% to 6.5% of sales for the remaining year.
Interim dividend of INR 0.40 per equity share approved by the Board.
No price increase taken yet in FY27; annual price increase guidance is around 3%, to be taken later after consumer research.

Lower historic store economics and margin trend questioned by analysts over five to seven years; management declined to engage on the data.
Sustainability of SSSG momentum beyond Q1, and the reliance on guest-count growth while ticket growth remains weak.
Management reliance on deferred price increases (none taken yet) to protect margins.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inflation was unbudgeted and largely from fuel, packaging and marketing spend, and it is not structural.
