qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 the peak of gross margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the highest level of impact and margins should improve from here, with operating margin being the focus. Inflation came from fuel, food, paper and distribution, utilities (gas) and labour (minimum wages), with diesel affecting distribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the G&A run-rate for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said G&A should be in the range of 6% to 6.5% of sales, and the focus should be on the bottom line rather than individual expense lines.

505533|2026-09.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR7.47 billion, with same-store sales up 10.1% on double-digit guest count growth.
505533|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter in 13 quarters, with revenue up 16% YoY to INR7.47 billion and same-store sales growth of 10.1%, driven mainly by guest count growth that was double-digit in each month. Operating EBITDA rose 29% YoY (management also cited about 26% in one answer), with margin up 130 bps to 13.1% despite about 190 bps of inflation across commodities, utilities and employee costs. The company opened 11 restaurants, taking the network to 492 across 80 cities, and reiterated its 580+ restaurant target by March 2028. Management said momentum continued into October, and guided to 100-150 bps of annual profitability improvement and 2-4% price increases over the year.

segments.commentary: Grew 15% YoY; company says delivery is broad-based and in double-digit growth, with own-channel delivery trial in Mumbai.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guest count momentum since December is the priority; check size is easier to lift, and price contributed little from Q1 to Q2.

505537|2026-03.headline: Zee Q4 FY26: digital revenue up 71% YoY to INR4,700 mn and ZEE5 EBITDA positive for FY26, but ad revenue fell 4% on a March West Asia hit and a INR4,084 mn one-off charge.
505537|2026-03.overview: Management reported that ZEE5 revenue grew 71% YoY to INR4,700 million in Q4 FY26, its highest ever, and that digital delivered positive EBITDA for FY26 versus a loss of INR5,480 million a year earlier. Linear advertising revenue declined 4% YoY as advertisers pulled spends in March amid the Middle East conflict; management said it would have been low single-digit growth excluding March. A one-off charge of INR4,084 million from a change in movie rights amortization (front-loaded to 50% over two years) and additional impairment was taken in the quarter, and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.9% on a 7% decline in operating revenue. Management gave no formal guidance, and the call was mainly Q&A on Zee Music, Bullet, live events, ad spend and manpower costs.

505700|2026-06.headline: Elecon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore, but management guided only low double-digit FY27 growth on raw-material-driven order conversion delays.
505700|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore over adjusted Q1 FY26 revenue of INR465 crore, with EBITDA up 3.9% to INR109 crore at a stated 21% margin and PAT of INR70 crore (13.5% margin, up 2.3%). Gear division drove growth, with revenue up 16.3% to INR416 crore, while MHE revenue fell 2.9% to INR105 crore on project execution delays and EBIT fell 25.3% to INR27 crore. Order intake rose 23% to INR755 crore and the consolidated open order book rose 36.8% to INR1,518 crore, yet management guided only low double-digit FY27 revenue growth, citing raw-material price spikes that slowed enquiry-to-order conversion and PSU-linked capex delays.

506222|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores and PAT rose 58.6% to INR84.3 crores, despite total income down 6.3%.

Management attributed the stronger profitability to product mix (lower GPPS volumes) and opportunistic pricing in tight segments, and said there was no significant inventory gain. Volumes fell 4.6% YoY to 46.1 KT, driven by GPPS weakness, while ABS and HIPS grew. Management declined to quantify the Thailand breakeven change or the power-savings benefit, citing short-term market distortion from the Middle East supply crisis, and reiterated that India ABS capacity additions remain on track for the second half of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 volume drop in India and the 20-30% drop in Thailand explained?
qa_highlights.answer: India dip was from GPPS only; ABS and HIPS grew YoY. Thailand comparison was distorted by prior-year pre-buying ahead of the INEOS-to-Styrenix brand switch, and Jan-Mar is seasonally weaker. Most business was retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread at spot prices better or worse in FY27 versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract and formula margins are similar or slightly better. Spot margins are better for specific grades where Korean suppliers' quality is weak, but this is opportunistic.

qa_highlights.question: Should capex be preponed for ABS given Korean import disruption?

qa_highlights.answer: ABS: 60-70% formula or contract. HIPS: well above 50% formula/OEM. GPPS: formula-based pricing above 70% for the business overall, with volumes dropping as the company avoids unformulated segments.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thailand ever reach breakeven given normalised spreads?

506222|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 133.9% to INR201.4 crore (26.1% margin) even as sales volume fell 26% to 38.9 KT.
506222|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 6.6% to INR770.5 crore and PAT rose 150.3% to INR137.3 crore, driven by a sharp margin jump, while volumes dropped 26% as non-OEM buyers held back amid Middle East-driven raw material price volatility. Consolidated (India plus Thailand) volume was 50.8 KT, EBITDA INR223.6 crore at 22% margin. Management described the margin gain as a snapshot of a volatile quarter, not a sustainable run rate, and gave no volume guidance. The ABS capacity expansion is said to be on track for completion in FY27 without a firm commissioning month, and Thailand volumes remain subdued.

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Demand fell in the quarter, with a smaller drop than polystyrene; OEM is about 70% or more of ABS sales. Management did not give a segment volume split.

segments.commentary: Hit harder than ABS, mainly in the non-OEM/unorganised segment; OEM is about 50% of PS sales. Management did not give volume numbers.

segments.name: SAN
segments.commentary: Merchant sales run at about 15,000-20,000 tonnes a year against roughly 100,000 tonnes of capacity; most output is used captively, and merchant sales will continue after the ABS expansion.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Running at low utilisation on specific products; volumes were broadly maintained quarter on quarter, but new business has not yet translated into meaningful volume growth. Validation cycles run 12-24 months.

SAN capacity of about 100,000 tonnes against merchant sales of 15-20 KT a year; expansions planned across rubber, SAN and compounding sites.
Thailand cost base is described as higher than India's; no reduction timeline was given.
demand_pricing: Demand fell in Q1 due to a Middle East-driven price spike from March and high volatility; buyers in the non-OEM/unorganised segment held back. Management put the volume decline at about 15-25% on total polymer.

Styrene monomer went from about $1,000/t pre-war to $1,600-1,700, then about $1,200, and has since traded in a $1,100-1,400 range. Acrylonitrile moved from $1,200 to about $1,800-1,900 and is now $1,400-1,600. Butadiene (bought locally) went from $1,000 to above $2,500 and has since eased.
Styrene monomer is now sourced from alternate suppliers with 10-15 days longer lead times; management said it is 'fully covered' and carried slightly higher raw material inventory at quarter end.

qa_highlights.answer: SAN merchant sales will continue. The ABS expansion will be completed in FY27, but exact timing was not disclosed because the project runs alongside an operating plant.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new plan; cash will go to planned capex with the rest returned to shareholders in line with existing policy. No specific dividend or buyback was announced.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Thailand sales strategy is to win validations in China, Japan, Vietnam, Korea and others; validations take 12-24 months. No volume guidance was given.

506395|2026-03.headline: Coromandel Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR 494 crore, but reported PAT fell to INR 115 crore on last year's land-sale gain.
506395|2026-03.overview: Q4 operations were strong: consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 494 crore, with the fertilizer plants run full after the annual turnaround. Reported PAT of INR 115 crore compared with INR 578 crore last year, which included a INR 347 crore land-sale exceptional gain; this year carried a INR 71 crore impairment on drone-business investments and goodwill. Fertilizer margins compressed sharply as Middle East disruption spiked ammonia and sulphur prices, while crop protection, specialty nutrients, retail and NACL performed well. Management gave no quantitative guidance on fertilizer margins or subsidy outcomes, pending government support.

SSP sales hit a record 8.4 lakh tons, and Nano DAP volumes grew 60% to about 42 lakh bottles.

segments.name: Crop protection (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 15% to INR 3,054 crore and profit 55% to INR 569 crore for FY26; FY26 revenue mix was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore. Q4 standalone crop protection growth was about 2%, attributed to export sales being moved into Q1 and a bio export order shipped earlier.

segments.name: NACL (Nagarjuna Agrichem, 53% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated crop protection with NACL reached about INR 4,000 crore; NACL FY26 revenue INR 1,585 crore (+28%) and EBITDA INR 103 crore, with margin at 6-7% and guided to 9-10% next year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew over 30% in FY26 with more than 300 new stores in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, and entry into Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

segments.name: Dhaksha (drones, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Impairment of INR 71 crore taken on investments and goodwill due to long lead times in order execution; management expects recovery after first large order executes this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year split of subsidy versus non-subsidy EBITDA and of crop protection revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidy share of EBITDA was 57% in Q4 and 66% for FY26. Standalone FY26 crop protection revenue was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore; NACL FY26 revenue was INR 1,584 crore and Q4 INR 361 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertilizer finished goods inventory and trading exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished fertilizer inventory is about 5.5 lakh tons, of which trading is about 60,000-70,000 tons. Trading margin is roughly 4-5%, and FY27 trading volume may fall in Q1 because of DAP import shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone crop protection growth only about 2% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is off-season, export sales were deliberately moderated to shift into April-May, and a bio export order was executed earlier in December; full-year crop protection growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sulphur and ammonia sourcing position, and is Q2 covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur has visibility up to June, with diversified spot sourcing from Canada, South Asia and Japan; ammonia and sulphur prices are about USD 800-850 per ton. Management said Q2 coverage depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping and a Middle East resolution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Dhaksha, the drone subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical gaps are fixed and a large order is awaiting execution, with the first order this year expected to build confidence; a larger facility is due around May 2026.

Raw material security: Q1 FY27 covered, Q2 depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping and a Middle East resolution; sulphur visibility only up to June; ammonia and sulphur around USD 800-850 per ton.

NACL margin recovery: 6-7% now, 9-10% guided next year, but management said restoring 7-8% is the limit without new active ingredients and formulations; 9(3) registrations take time.

There may be one or two challenging quarters, but it should get normalized and structurally the value gap what we originally envisaged will come through.

506395|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on crop protection, retail, specialty nutrients and volume execution, but cautious and largely non-committal on fertilizer margins, subsidy quantum and timing, and FY27 EBITDA per ton, repeatedly saying the situation is fluid and declining to give numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 fertilizer manufacturing EBITDA fell below INR 3,500/t vs over INR 5,000/t a year ago, but management is seeking June-September cost-to-cost subsidy reimbursement and crop protection margins are sustained near 19% while NACL moves from 6-7% toward 9-10%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kakinada phosphoric acid plant (~200,000 t/yr) is in trial runs with stable operations from April-May 2026, Sarigam adds 20,000 t around mid-2026, Dahej Mancozeb adds 10,000 t (commissioned), and granulation is firmly dated for December 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone crop protection revenue guided +20-25% for FY27 with six new launches, and rock phosphate volume to rise 30-40% from more than 3.5 lakh t; offset by trading volumes that management doubts will match FY26 and Q1 DAP shortages.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fertilizer and crop protection plants are running full (utilisation flagged as full), more than INR 3,000 crore invested in two years, and technical MAP plant, seaweed granulation and fluorination CDMO investments are under development, so further capex is likely to be disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no quantitative fertilizer margin or subsidy guidance and said conditions are fluid; upside is limited to crop protection and NACL margin progression.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ammonia and sulphur at USD 800-850/t, Q2 raw material cover depends on Middle East resolution, NBS rates raised only about 10% against sharp input inflation, and subsidy outstanding rose to INR 2,168 crore from INR 1,654 crore a year ago.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans six new crop protection product launches in FY27 alongside 20-25% domestic formulation growth, and fluorination CDMO small-scale capacity is due this year with production next year.

rows.label: Fertilizer MRP corrections and cost-to-cost subsidy
rows.why: Management is seeking extra subsidy and cost-to-cost reimbursement for June-September, size undisclosed, and industry has already made some MRP corrections in the last one to two months against raw material inflation.

rows.label: Dhaksha drone subsidiary recovery
rows.why: INR 71 crore impairment on investments and goodwill; recovery depends on executing a large pending order this year, with a larger facility due around May 2026.

rows.label: NACL margin recovery to 9-10%
rows.why: NACL FY26 revenue INR 1,585 crore (+28%) with EBITDA margin at 6-7%, guided to 9-10% next year on product mix; management said 7-8% needs no major investment but 9(3) registrations take time.

tone.note: Management was confident on crop protection (20-25% FY27 growth guide), NACL, retail and capacity commissioning, but cautious and non-committal on fertilizer margins, subsidy quantum and FY27 EBITDA per ton, declining to quantify; analysts pressed on margin squeeze and subsidy reimbursement.

506395|2026-06.headline: Coromandel Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 3% YoY to INR761 crores on West Asia input-cost spike, while revenue rose 15% to INR8,215 crores.
506395|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 15% YoY to INR8,215 crores, helped by higher fertilizer realisations and non-subsidy growth, with NACL now consolidated. EBITDA declined 3% to INR761 crores and net profit fell to INR382 crores from INR502 crores as ammonia and sulphur costs outran NBS subsidy rates. Management said phosphate production was deliberately cut to 6.9 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to protect inventory economics, while Crop Protection (revenue +20%, EBIT +44%) and Retail (revenue +85%) carried the quarter. Management is pressing the government for a kharif NBS revision and says no near-term fertilizer capacity additions are planned.

segments.name: Fertilizers (phosphatic)
segments.commentary: Production cut to 6.9 lakh tons from 8.4 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to optimise inventory; phos acid output 1.2 lakh tons, flat YoY. Sales volume fell 9-10% to 10 lakh tons, but primary market share rose to 22% from 18%; point-of-sale up 13% to 7.9 lakh tons, 16% share.

segments.name: Specialty nutrients and organics
segments.commentary: Described as strong, aided by higher organics and micronutrient offtake; launched 3 new products. Management says this business grows 25-30% with about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Record Q1: revenue +20% to INR870 crores, EBIT +44% to INR159 crores, with exports and B2B strong. New products are 32% of domestic B2C sales vs 23% last year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue +85% YoY; 76% of stores profitable vs 61% last year; 22 new stores take network above 1,200 outlets.

segments.name: Nano and bio products
segments.commentary: Nano business volumes +2% YoY with nearly 60% market share; UP and Maharashtra bans are restraining growth. Bio business steady, with 2 new products launched.

guidance_outlook: Phosphoric acid price for Q2 settled at $1,700/t vs $1,360/t in Q1, following higher DAP and raw-material prices.
Granulation project on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27; Crop Protection capacity expansion for key molecules expected by September 2026.

Management wants kharif NBS rates revised to the 6-month average policy formula; says the industry has taken a 25-30% price increase across grades, and that further price rises are not feasible without subsidy correction.
Sulphur expected to stay high for some time; management says the acid-backed production economics are unattractive until sulphur falls, with NACL-type steady-state EBITDA well below Coromandel.

No near-term fertilizer capacity additions planned; target is 4 million tons own fertilizer plus 1 million tons trading, with management citing 8-9 million tons of nutrient visibility for about 2 years.
Normal sustainable capex guided at about INR300 crores per year; ~INR7,000 crores invested over the last 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Phos acid and sulphuric acid plants commissioned; sulphuric acid at rated capacity and generating power; phos acid stabilising with a new rock-utilisation technology.
Granulation project on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning; new capacity is 750,000 tonnes, 50% to be sold via own retail and the balance into UP, Rajasthan, MP and Chhattisgarh.

Crop Protection key-molecule capacity to be commissioned by September 2026; further spending to focus on marketing and channel rather than assets; no new AI capacity planned given spare NACL capacity.
Senegal rock mining produced over 1.1 lakh tons in the quarter; BMCC operating close to 5 lakh tons/year target; evaluating a 100,000-150,000 ton SSP plant at $5-6 million.

Kakinada T-MAP plant and seaweed granulation plant progressing; Ankleshwar fluorination launch facility being set up; IIT Chennai research park planned; PA-SA plant gives about 60% acid self-sufficiency.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit was 23% through the quarter, moderating to 17% by late July; reservoirs at 34% of capacity vs 57% last year. Pulses acreage down 15%, oilseeds and cotton down 6%, and paddy back to normal.
Management says there is no fertilizer shortage; Urea and DAP stocks are comfortable for kharif, but industry production and imports must hold for two more months to build rabi carryover.
NP/NPK production and imports fell 21% and 38% respectively; management ties this to weak NBS subsidy for these grades.
Crop protection: domestic demand muted due to delayed sowing; export markets improving but cautious on price. Active ingredient prices are firmer than before because China keeps AIs low.
NACL export revenue hit by price moderation on molecules sold to global MNCs, while Coromandel passed input-cost increases through to exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a structural shift to NPK or a fertilizer shortage on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no shortage; the early-season pick-up of low-MRP packs was an advance purchase, and current uptake depends more on monsoon than on availability.

qa_highlights.question: How much did FX contribute to Crop Protection EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX is at most 5-6% of consolidated EBITDA, under a netting-based hedging policy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the depreciation spike and how much is from new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental depreciation from new capex is about INR16-18 crores; the rest is mining overburden amortisation (about INR30 crores) and NACL intangibles amortisation (about INR20-21 crores).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ask from government and how is the EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants the 6-month average NBS rate applied, and says NP/NPK rates need significant correction; the target is nutrient EBITDA of about INR6,500/t from INR5,000/t, but not in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided normal sustainable capex of about INR300 crores, but will consider higher spending for attractive-return projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dhaksha drone contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Coromandel bought 100-150 drones this quarter and targets a fleet of 500 during the year; management said Dhaksha is not a significant EBITDA drag.

risks_watch: Subsidy under-recovery on NP/NPK: sulphur and ammonia costs are not covered by NBS rates, and kharif revision is still pending.
Sulphur and phos acid pricing: phos acid up to $1,700/t in Q2; management says sulphur needs to fall to about $800/t for backward integration to pay.
Subsidy receivable of INR3,254 crores at June-end.
State bans on Nano fertilizers in UP and Maharashtra are holding back volumes.
Crop Protection export pricing: AI prices are firmer, but export demand is cautious and NACL revenue fell on price moderation.
Whether industry production and imports can hold through the next two months to build rabi carryover inventory.

Management was evasive on a few specifics (CP export/domestic mix, Dhaksha numbers, NACL stake increase), deferring them to follow-up.
key_quotes: Overall, we have delivered a resilient performance in a challenging operating environment marked by delayed monsoons, elevated raw material costs and pressure on fertilizer margins.
These rates do not fully compensate for the increase in global raw material costs, which happened subsequent to Middle East crisis.
Given the Phosphoric Acid price of $1,700, at least we want $800 of sulphur.
So I would put a normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores would be the number we'll look at.

rows.why: Phosphate sales volume fell 9-10% to 10 lakh tons and production was cut to 6.9 lakh tons (72% utilisation), while point-of-sale rose 13% to 7.9 lakh tons and Retail stores reach above 1,200 outlets; growth depends on monsoon (deficit moderating to 17%) and on industry imports holding for two more months.

rows.why: Normal sustainable capex is guided at about INR300 crores a year, a 100,000-150,000 t SSP plant at $5-6 million is under evaluation, and management will consider higher spend for attractive-return projects, but utilisation is only 72% and near-term fertilizer additions are ruled out.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is pressing for the kharif NBS revision to the 6-month average formula, citing a 25-30% industry price increase, and Crop Protection grew revenue 20% with EBIT up 44% to INR159 crores; an upgrade hinges on the government revising subsidy rates.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Subsidy receivable is INR3,254 crores at June-end, sulphur and ammonia costs are not covered by NBS rates, and NP/NPK production and imports fell 21% and 38%, so margins stay under pressure if kharif NBS is not revised.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Specialty nutrients launched 3 new products in Q1, Bio launched 2, and new products are now 32% of domestic Crop Protection B2C sales vs 23% a year ago.

rows.label: Kharif NBS rate revision to 6-month average formula
rows.why: Management is pressing for the revision; NP/NPK rates need significant correction and the EBITDA-per-tonne target of INR6,500/t from INR5,000/t depends on it, but it is not in the current quarter.

rows.label: NACL EBITDA margin recovery to 7-8% then 10-11%
rows.why: NACL EBITDA margin rose to 11% from 8% in Q1 (EBITDA INR41 crores, +9%), and management guides a path from 3-4% to 7-8% and then 10-11%.

rows.label: Nano fertilizer bans in UP and Maharashtra
rows.why: Nano volumes grew only 2% YoY despite nearly 60% market share, with the state bans restraining growth and no lifting signalled on the call.

tone.note: Management was confident on Crop Protection, Retail and Specialty, and cautious and repeatedly pressing government on NBS subsidy correction, while evasive on CP export/domestic mix, Dhaksha numbers and the NACL stake increase; analysts probed fertilizer shortage, FX contribution and depreciation.

506401|2026-03.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 13% YoY to INR383 crore, margin 18%, with PAT INR220 crore; management guides Q1 FY27 better than Q4.
506401|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,127 crore, down from INR2,202 crore a year earlier but up from INR1,983 crore in Q3, while EBITDA rose 74% QoQ and 13% YoY to INR383 crore. Phenolics EBIT reached INR287 crore at a 20% margin, and Advanced Intermediates EBIT rose to INR34 crore. Management attributed the gains to favourable pricing, feedstock bought on dips before the Middle East disruption, and integration benefits. The nitric acid plant ran at about 45% utilisation in Q4 because of technical issues, so the expected INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition is delayed.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs INR2,202 crore; +7% QoQ vs INR1,983 crore
+13% YoY vs INR339 crore; +74% QoQ vs INR219 crore

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR708 crore vs INR654 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR652 crore in Q3; EBIT INR34 crore vs INR15 crore in Q3. Gains came from stable volumes, end-product pricing and product mix, while exports slowed on logistics disruption.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,429 crore; EBIT INR287 crore vs INR239 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR145 crore in Q3, a 20% EBIT margin supported by spreads and downstream demand.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be better than Q4 FY26 on both standalone and consolidated basis, and better than Q1 FY26.
FY27 expected to show stronger margins for standalone business vs FY26, driven by new downstream products that management calls significantly margin accretive.
Feedstock inventory bought on dips expected to support costs until price stabilisation, perhaps end-Q2 FY27 or mid-Q2.
New products and fluorinated molecules expected on regularised commercial production from Q3 FY27, in time for export customers' CY2026 requirements.
MIBK/MIBC plant expected to be commissioned around end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27.
Polycarbonate project expected to be commissioned by June 2028; PC resin and Phenol expansion may be offset by about a quarter.
capex_capacity: Nitric acid plant ran at about 45% utilisation in Q4 FY26 due to technical issues; under repair with technology and equipment suppliers; the earlier INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition target is pending stable operations.

Multipurpose agrochemical intermediates and MIBK/MIBC projects: mechanical completion near; pre-commissioning next, commissioning around end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27.
Polycarbonate resin project (India's first fully integrated PC facility) targeted for June 2028 commissioning; total announced project around INR11,000 crore.
Praxair India to build, own and operate a dedicated on-site HyCO plant at Dahej under a build-own-operate model, reducing upfront capex for Deepak.
Funding: 60:40 debt-equity; bank debt tied up; equity contribution ongoing, with debt drawdown after 25% equity infusion.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as relatively stable across automotive, infrastructure, pharma, electronics and polymers; management says it is passing through raw material cost increases where possible, an ongoing exercise.
Advanced Intermediates realisations were lower than in earlier years, per management; capacity was reported as running full.
Phenol: domestic buyers' ordering pattern is mixed, with some back to normal buying and others still need-based. Management cited a China-India price spread but declined to comment on it.
China anti-involution and safety curbs on nitration chemistries seen as a structural tailwind for nitration products (DASDA, OBA-linked); management said this has already started on the ground.
Sulfur and sulfuric acid cost increases are a global headwind; management expects no significant net impact if India prices stay at par with international prices.
Management declined to give IPA or phenol production volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What was nitric acid utilisation in Q4 and is the INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant was at about 45% utilisation in Q4 due to technical issues; the balance was bought from the market. Target achievable once stable, but no timeline given. Concentrated nitric acid plant operating normally.

qa_highlights.question: Phenolics feedstock availability and China-India spread outlook for Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance was preponed by about 10-11 days in early April; intermediate stock covered supply. Management guided Q1 profitability higher than Q4 and expects no propylene constraint. Declined to comment on other companies' spreads.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new products and fluorinated molecule add to FY27 standalone performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Validation batches are supplied or in transit to customers; commercial production on a regular basis from Q3 FY27. Management did not anticipate customer approval concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved some customers to dealership and CSA models to secure outstanding amounts amid volatility, and said realisations, not capacity utilisation, are the lower metric in Advanced Intermediates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China nitration tailwind already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CCP-led safety and transport audit is a structural tailwind, not tied to a specific province or product, and that it has already started happening.

qa_highlights.question: How will the polycarbonate project (about INR11,000 crore) be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Upadhyay: debt tied up with banks at 60:40; equity is being infused, and debt will be drawn after 25% equity per the bank condition. Management said funding is not an issue and cash generation is sufficient.

risks_watch: Nitric acid plant reliability: utilisation was about 45% in Q4; repairs and the timing of stable operations remain open.
Feedstock cost volatility (benzene, xylene, toluene, propylene); inventory bought on dips is expected to support costs only until around mid-Q2 FY27.
Working capital: receivable days rose, and some customers have moved to dealership and CSA models.

Execution risk on MIBK/MIBC commissioning (around end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27), new products (Q3 FY27), and the polycarbonate project (June 2028, possible quarter mismatch between PC resin and phenol expansion).
Sulfur and sulfuric acid cost increases; pricing gap between India and international markets.
Geopolitical risks in the Middle East and the US tariff and China policy environment.

506401|2026-06.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q1 FY27: record consolidated EBITDA of INR 554 crore (21% margin) and PAT of INR 345 crore, up 207% YoY.
506401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and 22% QoQ to INR 2,592 crore, with EBITDA up 159% YoY to INR 554 crore and margin at 21% versus 11% a year ago. Phenolics delivered record EBIT of INR 418 crore at a 24% margin, while Advanced Intermediates EBIT was INR 67 crore at an 8% margin. Management said April was disrupted by a maintenance shutdown, propylene shortages and gas curtailment, so the phenol run rate of about 1 lakh tonnes applies to parts of the quarter rather than the full period. Debt funding for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project has been closed, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.27x.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,775 crore and EBIT of INR 418 crore (24% margin), supported by stronger realisations, sustained demand and high utilisation. Management said the business is almost entirely domestic.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates (AI)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 804 crore and EBIT of INR 67 crore (8% margin), helped by better realisations, higher operating rates and product mix. AI export mix is about 40-50%; raw material costs stayed high for some products.

guidance_outlook: MIBK and MIBC to be commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026; the remaining projects (multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility, etc.) are due in Q2 FY27, with commercial volumes from January.
Management aims to reach 4 lakh tonnes of phenol in the existing Deepak Phenolics asset in the short to medium term, with about INR 70-odd crore of debottlenecking capex.
Polycarbonate commissioning targeted for H2 FY28-29 and BPA a couple of months later; propylene from the PDH project is expected to support phenol volumes.

Capex: about INR 1,200 crore spent to date, another INR 1,000-1,600 crore in FY27 (figures varied in the call), and about INR 3,000 crore in FY28. Peak debt estimated at INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital, with D/E below 1.
capex_capacity: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain (nitric acid plant, nitration and reduction) completed and stabilised; the company says it now runs 8 products simultaneously.

Phenol capacity is about 3.5 lakh tonnes, and management says it is debottlenecking toward 4 lakh tonnes through advanced process controls. Run rate reached about 1 lakh tonnes per quarter in parts of Q1, but was not sustained through the full quarter.
MIBC pre-commissioning runs reportedly exceeded design capacity; management said it can ramp above 100% once demand comes in.
Debt for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project is closed, funded 60:40 debt to equity, with the 25% equity already contributed.

506405|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 177 crore from INR 150 crore QoQ, mostly raw-material pass-through; FY26 revenue INR 582 crore.

Working capital and short-term borrowings rose substantially on higher inventory, debtor and advance-payment requirements for boron, at about 8.75-9% interest. 506767|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue and profit were flat (within ±1% YoY); management sees margin improvement next year but guides only 5-10% volume growth.
506767|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as challenging, with both top line and bottom line roughly flat YoY, and volume down about 1% and prices down about 1%. The March 2026 ammonia sourcing disruption from the Middle East war was short-lived, with inventories bridging the gap and plants kept running at roughly 60-85% utilisation. Ammonia cost rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg, and the company passed through price increases, with aceto prices now above INR200/kg versus about INR140-150/kg last year. Management believes the margin trough has passed but cautioned that gains from price pass-through are temporary and that competition will settle margins later.

Price increases have been passed through, with customers absorbing them because the company's products are a minor (C-item) cost in their bill of materials. Management believes competition, not customers, is the main pricing pressure.

Peptides and acetonitrile demand expected to grow, but the company sees much of the optimistic peptide demand forecasts as unproven.

qa_highlights.question: How has user demand held up after raw material-driven price increases, and what is expected next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not yet seen demand destruction. Its products are a minor cost for customers, so pressure is expected from competition rather than customers. Prices are unlikely to revert to pre-February levels soon.

qa_highlights.question: Is ammonia available broadly across the industry, and how does this affect spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg. Government allocation is expected, as aliphatic industry needs only 10,000-15,000 tons per month. Stabilisation is expected in 3-6 months, and any spread gain is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for capacity utilisation and the Balaji and Aarti capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 60-85%. Methylamines are overcapacity after Aarti's entry, which is expected to take a long time to absorb. Ethylamines have adequate capacity for 4-5 years. Balaji's 18,000 ton ACN plant will add competition, but the company believes it is the lowest-cost producer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned capex for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR80-90 crore, mainly completing the Dahej plant and engineering projects. Apart from this, there is no major planned capex for existing products; maintenance capex is about INR20-30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company diversifying ammonia sourcing or looking at green ammonia?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia is bought mainly through distributors linked to fertiliser plants, with direct manufacturer links in only one or two cases. Green ammonia is still 3-5 years away from cost parity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin improvement is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some margin improvement next year. It noted that margins widen temporarily when raw material prices rise and fall, and that the company cannot predict whether it will keep growing.

506854|2026-03.headline: TANFAC FY26 revenue hit a record INR711 crore (+27% YoY), but operating EBITDA fell to INR112 crore (16% margin vs 23%) on sulphur costs and a plant outage.
506854|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations reached a record INR193 crore, up 11% QoQ from INR173 crore in Q3. FY26 operating EBITDA fell INR17 crore YoY to INR112 crore and PAT fell INR18 crore to INR70 crore, with management attributing this to normalising margins after an exceptional FY25, higher sulphur prices, an HF plant outage and higher depreciation. The company is building a INR495 crore downstream project (INR405 crore for HFC-32 refrigerant gas) targeted for Q3 FY27, with about 65% of its 20,000 MTPA capacity reportedly contracted. Management was evasive on HFC-32 production quotas, which are yet to be allocated by the government.

demand_pricing: Management says India HFC-32 demand is about 22-23 KT and could roughly double to 45-50 KT in 4-5 years, driven by room AC growth of about 16-17% CAGR. Global HFC-32 demand is about 380 KT (2025), going to about 485 KT by 2030.

Indian merchant AHF demand is about 40 KT in total: solar about 15 KT, surface treatment 15-18 KT, specialty 10 KT. Solar capacity in India is expected to rise from about 36 GW to about 216 GW in five years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quota will be decided in 2027 by the government. It cited an office memorandum of 1 April 2026 and said the 2027 calendar year is free for production. Quota applies from 1 January 2028, and management declined to comment further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the break-even and cost of production for HFC-32?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated cost of production at about INR240-280/kg, including operating expenses, and said it was not in a position to give break-even utilisation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no penalty for quota-related non-supply. Penalties are mutual and apply only once production starts. Management did not quantify any contingent liability.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a strong, unusual Q3 FY25, sulphur prices rising from about INR30/kg to INR38-40/kg, a Q4 M2M loss of INR2.5-3 crore, about INR70 crore of HF output lost to an outage, and INR7 crore of extra depreciation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product lists are fully distinct, with no overlap in fluorine downstream or other products.

507205|2026-06.headline: Tilaknagar Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 166% YoY to Rs 1,046 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.1% amid packaging inflation.
507205|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with Imperial Blue (IB) inside the combined business, with volumes up 172% YoY and 9% QoQ, led by IB at 5.4 million cases (+18% QoQ). NSR rose to Rs 1,183 per case (+1.5% QoQ, +5.3% YoY), but glass-led packaging inflation compressed gross margin to 42.1% (adjusted for subsidy) from 45.2% in Q4 FY26. Adjusted-for-subsidy EBITDA was Rs 148 crore at 14.5%, and net debt rose to Rs 2,100 crore on working-capital build. Management reiterated FY27 volume guidance and a net debt target of about Rs 1,700 crore by March 2027.

segments.name: Imperial Blue (IB)
segments.commentary: Volume 5.4 million cases in Q1, up 18% QoQ; June 2026 was the highest ever monthly volume at 3.4 million cases company-wide, with IB the largest-selling deluxe whisky. Reintroduced in Delhi in July 2026.

segments.name: MHB
segments.commentary: Volume grew 7% YoY in Q1 despite April disruptions.

segments.name: Super premium and luxury (House of TI / SSL)
segments.commentary: Spaceman Spirits (SSL) more than doubled sales YoY in Q1; growth led by Samsara Pink and new Indian-flavour launches. House:Pour Picante ready-to-pour launched late in Q1. Monarch Legacy Edition Brandy and Seven Islands Pure Malt are being expanded.

segments.name: Bartisans (associate)
segments.commentary: Stake increased from 36.2% to 41.5% to fund quick-commerce expansion and product innovation.

guidance_outlook: FY27: high single-digit to low double-digit volume growth for the combined business maintained; IB full-year volume expected to grow double digits from the ~21.5 million cases base at acquisition.
Beyond FY27: annual volume growth in mid-teens over the next couple of years; revenue growth at least ~300 bps above volume growth; new launches from FY28 onwards.

EBITDA margin for combined business 16%-18% by FY29 with upward bias; FY27 margin to improve from 15.5% base set in Q4 FY26. Q3 and Q4 expected to show significant margin uptick; Q2 similar to Q1 with extra A&SP spend.
Net debt target about Rs 1,700 crore by March 2027 (reduction of ~Rs 400 crore); net debt/EBITDA below 1.0x by March 2029 (earlier FY29 framing).
Supply chain and packaging optimisation expected to expand acquired-business margins by 250-400 bps and consolidated margins by ~250 bps.
Telangana price increase expected soon; management estimates 150-200 bps incremental annualised margin impact.
capex_capacity: IB manufacturing integration about 90% complete by April 2026; one state (of the TSMA-linked states) still under TSMA, with transition targeted by March 2027.
IB now transitioned from TSMA into Tilaknagar-operated units for 90% of the business.
Prag Distillery: around 60%-70% of the expected bottling-related savings already reflected in the numbers; full benefit not yet visible. Utilisation rate not disclosed.
Sales team scaled from about 350 pre-acquisition to 850+ as of March 31, 2026, across North, West, Central and East India.
demand_pricing: Glass and other packaging inputs inflated due to geopolitical tensions; partly offset by softer ENA prices.
Karnataka: volumes and operating-segment market share improved after price reduction and slab reduction.
Market share of IB improved in all states versus exit levels; South the easiest transition, and share gains in North, East and West (Maharashtra) as well.

Competition intensifying in IB's price segment (ICONiQ White, McDowell's scotch); management expects category activation to help growth. A&SP reinvestment rate being raised; activations in 28,000+ outlets in Q1.
Delhi: IB peak was about 0.5 million cases (around 2019-20); management expects return to those levels in 12-18 months.
Maharashtra-made liquor category around 6-7 lakh cases per month, flat; IB gaining share in the state.
Tamil Nadu business under 0.5 million cases annualised; possible policy change under new state government (imports or market opening) seen as upside.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka post-reform competition and pricing for IB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported good volume uptake and significantly improved operating-segment market share since the price reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Which states show more or less IB traction versus average?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined state-level detail; said share improved in every state versus exit levels, with South the smoothest transition.

qa_highlights.question: Are IB-related disruptions in Odisha, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Karnataka TSMA-related?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the disruptions were predominantly IB-specific and TSMA-related; details were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Trade spend and growth in the low-prestige IB segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said segment activity is rising after years of inactivity by leaders; company is increasing A&SP reinvestment and activating in 28,000+ outlets.

qa_highlights.question: Margin recovery timing to 15.5% and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumes inflation status quo; Q3 and Q4 to see significant margin uptick, Q2 similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Quarterly IB run-rate and separate IB NSR?
qa_highlights.answer: No bifurcated NSR given; IB full-year double-digit volume growth expected.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry in talks with government; last increase was three years ago; expected to add 150-200 bps to margin annualised.

qa_highlights.question: Tamil Nadu market size and route-to-market risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Current TN business under 0.5 million cases annualised; upside if imports or market opening allowed under new government.

507514|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore and EBITDA to INR89.7 crore after the Bhopal licence suspension; FY27 guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore.
507514|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore, EBITDA declined to INR89.7 crore and PAT was INR10.2 crore. Beer volumes dropped 20% to 187.19 lakh cases, driven by the temporary licence suspension at the Bhopal plant and weak demand in Karnataka and Odisha, while IMFL grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases. Management said the Bhopal licence renewal is pending with authorities, with no definite timeline; the UP greenfield brewery has begun trials and commercial production is expected from June 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR1,400-1,500 crore and FY27 EBITDA margin to close to 10%, with FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

segments.name: Beer
segments.commentary: Volumes fell 20% to 187.19 lakh cases in FY26 due to the Bhopal licence disruption and weak Karnataka and Odisha demand. Management said Karnataka is improving after excise rationalisation, and April-May industry growth was about 15-16%.

segments.name: IMFL / premium spirits
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases in FY26, led by premium portfolio penetration. Mahavat Whisky was launched in the mid-premium segment, and supply was halted when Bhopal stopped.

segments.name: Bhopal plant
segments.commentary: Management said roughly 50% of company volume historically came from Bhopal. Production has been halted since February and Delhi, UP and Jharkhand supplies from this plant stopped; finished goods were cleared and sold.

segments.name: UP greenfield brewery (subsidiary SDBL)
segments.commentary: About INR250 crore invested in FY26. Capacity is 1 crore cases per annum, with 15-20 lakh cases targeted in FY27 at about INR600 per case, roughly INR120 crore revenue at that realisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore (management called INR1,440-1,450 crore quite possible), assuming Bhopal resumes operations.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at close to 10%; FY28 guidance to be given in about six months due to inflation in glass bottles, cans and barley.
Q1 FY27 results expected to be better than Q4 FY26, helped by better utilisation at Hassan and Odisha and some one-off annual costs in Q4 not recurring.
Management expects Bhopal market share to return to earlier levels about six to seven months after the plant restarts.
UP plant expected to start commercial production in June 2026; full capacity ramp-up expected to take 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bhopal plant licence renewal is underway; management said it could be resolved in a couple of weeks, but later said a resolution could come within 7-10 days and gave no definite date.
UP brewery (1 crore cases per annum): trials under way, commercial operations expected from June 2026; Phase 1 is the brewery and no further capex is needed beyond working capital.
About INR400 crore of credit lines sanctioned but not drawn, which management will use only after Bhopal is operational.
Possible Phase 2 of the UP project could be the use of new promoter or warrant funds; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Karnataka (about 30-35% of business) is improving after the state's excise duty rationalisation, which lowered MRP on mainstream and economy beer; management says it is gaining share over the last 3-4 quarters.
Industry volume in April and May 2026 grew about 15-16% combined, with April at 51-52 lakh cases and May at about 50 lakh cases despite rain.
Delhi, Jharkhand and UP supplies from Bhopal have stopped; Jharkhand is partly served from Odisha, while some markets are not cost-effective to serve from other plants.
Andhra Pradesh business expected to start in the next 3-4 weeks; Tamil Nadu share is growing.
Input cost inflation in glass bottles, aluminium cans, barley and logistics is the main margin pressure; long-term supply contracts are not holding price.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA margin outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore, with the Bhopal licence assumed. FY27 EBITDA margin close to 10%; FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the UP plant contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: 15-20 lakh cases from UP in FY27 at roughly INR600 per case, about INR120 crore; plant capacity is 1 crore cases per annum with a 2-3 year ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 going to be as loss-making as Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects Q1 to be better than Q4 on higher Hassan and Odisha utilisation and lower annual costs booked in Q4. Only labour cost at Bhopal will fall; no salary cuts were made.

qa_highlights.question: How long to regain Bhopal and MP market share once the plant reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to recover the similar market share within about six months, though the main season makes it harder now. Management said the sales and distribution team is ready and waiting.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-time impact from Karnataka's excise cut?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-time impact. The MRP cut lowers consumer prices; management said revenue would rise slightly and margins would not suffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the licence lost and what internal steps are being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some matters are sub judice and cannot be discussed. It is appointing a dedicated compliance officer and improving compliance processes. The company said the rating downgrades stem only from the licence suspension.

risks_watch: Bhopal licence renewal timing is open-ended. Management's timelines have slipped from days to weeks to months, and the FY27 guidance depends on it.
Input cost inflation (glass, cans, barley) with no fixed-price contracts; FY28 margin guidance deferred.
Credit rating downgrades at parent and subsidiary; management says ratings will recover once the licence is restored. About INR400 crore of undrawn lines are available.
Governance: the Company Secretary resigned (personal reasons, per management) and an internal auditor left; a compliance officer is being appointed.
Market share loss in MP and Delhi may not be fully recovered, per management's own comments.

507514|2026-06.headline: Som Distilleries Q1 FY27 hit by Madhya Pradesh suspension: consolidated EBITDA INR15.2 crore on INR268.8 crore total income; FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore.
507514|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was described by management as an extremely difficult quarter, driven by the operational and regulatory disruption in Madhya Pradesh, where the Bhopal brewery remains suspended. Consolidated volume was 45.79 lakh cases, total income INR268.8 crore and EBITDA INR15.2 crore. Karnataka (cases up about 30%) and Odisha (up about 40%) recovered, and the UP brewery (about 10 million cases capacity) began commercial production around June 9, 2026. Gross debt rose only INR10 crore QoQ, with gross D/E moving from 0.3x to 0.31x, and operating cash generation was about INR28 crore. FY27 revenue guidance was lowered to INR1,000-1,100 crore from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore.

segments.commentary: Realisation up about 3% YoY to INR1,047 per case. Mahavat launched in Bhopal, Delhi and UP; supply resumption from Bhopal is a stated focus.

Hassan utilisation about 60%; Odisha about 70%; Bhopal (MP) suspended.

Raw material and packaging costs up about 7.5-8% YoY; cans rely on a single supplier (Ball Corporation) for the industry.
Excise duty paid rose because more volume was sold in Karnataka and Odisha, where excise is paid before dispatch unlike MP.

Receivables: most sales are to government wholesalers in the states where the company operates, and management sees no material receivable risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the MP closure in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR250-260 crore of revenue was lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhopal (MP) be restored, and what was the FY27 outlook if it is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is in courts and with authorities and is sub judice; it is hopeful of resolution this month. It declined to discuss a plan B or give numbers for a no-approval scenario, and reiterated FY27 revenue of INR1,000-1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Could Karnataka or other plants supply Bhopal to lift utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said importing from Odisha or UP to MP would be uneconomic because of MP's very high import fees, potentially leading to a loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Andhra Pradesh entry go live?
qa_highlights.answer: Excise and corporation permissions were delayed until end-July; export permissions from Karnataka are pending, and brands are expected in AP by first week of September.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company use contract manufacturing in states with overcapacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it compares local contract brewing against importing and chooses whichever is better on margin and quality, and that capacity is planned over five to 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Hassan plant not converted into a 100% subsidiary like UP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate and revert soon, with no commitment.

507526|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue INR239 crores, EBITDA up 13% to INR40 crores at 17% margin; proprietary IMFL volumes up 37% YoY.
507526|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net revenue was INR239 crores, with EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR40 crores (17% margin, up 200 bps) and PAT up 5% to INR24 crores (10% margin). Proprietary IMFL, the main growth driver, posted 37% volume growth and a record 22% segment EBITDA margin, while the Inbrew shift from licensing to contract manufacturing kept FY26 top-line growth flattish. Ethanol volumes fell 35% YoY on industry oversupply, and merchant ENA volumes rose 129%. Management guided to FY27 EBITDA margin of around 15% and double-digit consolidated revenue growth, and announced the acquisition of SDF Industries, a Kerala distillery-cum-bottling unit.

507552|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 mango production was good in quality and price, but export dispatches slowed due to vessel non-availability and sharply higher ocean freight, with customers delaying call-offs rather than cancelling. Exports are 35-40% of sales and domestic about 55%; management expects domestic demand, aided by an El Nino-driven juice and drinks season, to offset export softness. Frozen food is the growth engine: about USD3 million in Q1 (up ~20%) and USD12 million last year, with a target of USD30-plus million in three years. Realisations fell ~18.5% YoY in the quarter, and management flagged working-capital blockage from delayed shipments, with a CFO resignation pending replacement.

Biologicals, Bayer-acquired molecules and the Nagpur formulation plant (Rs 200 crore outlay, 23,000 MT) are the main forward-looking items.

507779|2026-06.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q1 FY27 standalone total income Rs 207.49 cr (first time above Rs 200 cr) and PAT up 112% YoY to Rs 12.14 cr, with EBITDA margin at 10.69%.

Average selling price rose 31% QoQ against an 18% rise in raw material prices, though management said employee cost increases of about Rs 3-3.5 crore per quarter absorbed part of the gain. FIBC volume fell to about 3,000 tonnes from 3,500 tonnes a year earlier, due to polymer and labour disruptions. The premium polypropylene Taslan yarn JV with Essegomma (Italy) started commercial production and sales, with volume ramp guided from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta (Trinetra Asset Managers): How is raw material volatility from the West Asia conflict progressing, and can raw material moves be passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer volatility has eased from about plus/minus 25% in March to plus/minus 10% now. Raw material changes are generally passed through with a lag of two weeks to one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta: What is the marginal differential and expected EBITDA from the B2C-linked premium segments, and what total EBITDA margin should be expected for the company?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN is expected to add about Rs 10 crore revenue in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA; non-woven B2C is guided to mid-double-digit EBITDA. Management would not give an exact company-wide margin guide but expects to sustain current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): What is ESSEKAN's peak revenue on current capacity and when would more capacity be added?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity can reach about Rs 30 crore revenue. More capacity will be added once utilisation hits 50-60%, as the capex is not high.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: Why did margins not expand more despite the 31% ASP rise versus 18% raw material rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing EBITDA margin was 12.6%. Employee cost rose about Rs 3-3.5 crore QoQ, FIBC manufactured volume fell due to supply chain and labour disruptions, and there were packing, oil, freight and one-time disruption costs. Energy costs were not a significant increase.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the factors ahead for the rest of the year, and what are the FIBC capacity and mix plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Two risks: ocean freight rising from about $2,000 to $5,000 per container could dent demand, and partial sharing of costs with customers could hit margins. Target is 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28; management declined to give a product mix percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What was the FIBC utilisation and is 3,000 tonnes the base for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were 3,800 tonnes in Q3 FY26, 3,500 in Q4 FY26 and 3,000 in Q1 FY27, with working-day seasonality. Management called 3,000 a damaged number that will build from here.

qa_highlights.question: Chaitrika (individual investor): What is the long-term revenue aspiration and what are the milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Current projects and installed capacity can take revenue to about Rs 900-950 crore in FY27-28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29, assuming current trading and polymer prices. Management will decide on deploying balance-sheet cash for further capacity next year.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker (individual investor): What tangible benefits have the UK (Valex) and Italian JV delivered, and when will financials show?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN sampling is under way with significant commercialisation expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27, with guidance on it by Q4. Valex has delivered no significant tangible benefit so far beyond brand awareness; its turnover is manufacturing-transferred, so profit sits within Kanpur Plastipack.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What annual savings come from renewable power, and what is the FIBC capacity ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable power is about 60% of energy and already at the planned level, saving about Rs 3-5 crore a year. Battery storage is a couple of years away. FIBC adds about 1,200 tonnes a year, so 4-5 years to reach the full 6,000 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What IRR and ROCE hurdles apply, and what working capital is needed as the business ramps?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-woven targets 15-20% IRR and ROCE above 20%; ESSEKAN returns are far higher given low capex. Working capital stays at similar levels for FIBC and raffia, while non-woven adds 30-40 days of working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Deeya Jain (Sapphire Capital): What are the realisation trends, and the ESSEKAN revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations track raw material and freight costs and should hold while raw material costs are steady. ESSEKAN is about Rs 10 crore in FY27, with an ultimate aim of Rs 100 crore in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What is the impairment, contract value and debt position?

507789|2026-03.headline: Jagsonpal Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR64 crores and PAT 31% to ~INR9 crores; MAT growth 12.2% vs IPM ~7-8%.

FY26 revenue grew about 7% to INR287 crores, while profit from operations grew 19% to about INR45 crores before the one-time labour code charge taken in Q3. The board announced a INR40 crore buyback at INR250 per share (no promoter participation) and a 200% dividend including a 75% special, together returning over INR66 crores. Management reiterated a target of 1.5x IPM growth, which it translates to 12-15% currently.

segments.commentary: Roughly 25% of business; overweight therapy, but management said in Q&A it is in line with IPM currently. A dedicated Ortho franchise is still being built.

segments.name: Dermatology
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-15% of business; second growth driver after Gynaecology. Ranked third on MR productivity.

guidance_outlook: Target growth of 1.5x IPM; management translated current IPM of 6-9% into 12-15% company growth and said it maintains this guidance for FY27.
Planned 9-10 product launches in FY27, of which about half are legacy brand extensions and 5-6 are new products in existing strength therapies.
Expects growth to get better over the next two quarters on Pharmarack-reflected numbers.

Management said it can raise over INR200 crores of fresh debt and has balance-sheet capacity for acquisitions up to ~INR400 crores; an acquisition announcement is not yet made.
capex_capacity: MR headcount unchanged; no new MRs added in the last quarter. Growth to come from productivity of existing field force and geographies.
Asset-light model using CMOs; management says cost pressure is mainly packaging material and insurance costs, passed on over time under longer-term CMO agreements.
Price increases are SKU-based and taken after 12 months; ~92% of portfolio is outside NLEM price control, allowing up to 9.9% increase per management.

508814|2026-06.headline: Cosmo First Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 46% to Rs 1,166 crore and EBITDA 26% to Rs 147 crore, though margin fell to 12.6%.

EBITDA rose 26% to Rs 147 crore, helped by better per-kg contribution across base, semi-specialty and specialty films, and management says all B2B businesses are now profitable. Export volumes fell 13% due to port congestion and a line maintenance outage, and BOPET margins compressed sharply sequentially. segments.name: US film business
segments.commentary: Export volumes down 13% due to port congestion and in-transit shipments. US subsidiary received about USD 7 million duty refund in July 2026, not yet appropriated. Management expects US revenue to grow 25-30% in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 34% YoY with 25% EBITDA margin, improved 2 percentage points QoQ. About 80% of business is backward integration into group films. FY27 growth guided at about 50%; Rs 400-500 crore FY30 target may be reached by FY29.

segments.commentary: Revenue up over 58% YoY and turned EBITDA positive. FY26 revenue about Rs 100 crore; FY27 guided Rs 150-160 crore and Rs 200+ crore next year, with capacity up 50% at minimal capex over next two quarters.

508954|2026-03.headline: Finkurve crossed INR 1,096 crore AUM (up 149% YoY) with gross NPA at a record-low 0.13% and CRAR at 30.96% in Q4 FY26.
508954|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 1,096 crore, up 149% YoY from INR 439 crore, with branches rising from 73 to 105. Quarterly total income grew 71% YoY to INR 69 crore and PAT grew 105%, per the CFO. Asset quality was described as a record low, with gross NPA at 0.13% and net NPA at 0.09%. Management also cited a rating upgrade to BBB+ (March 2026, from CARE and Infomerics), a co-lending start with Godrej (about INR 21 crore off-book AUM), and transition to a middle-layer NBFC. Guidance for FY27 is 40-50% AUM growth and about 50% branch expansion, with a cost-of-borrowing assumption of roughly 11.2%.

qa_highlights.answer: FY26 average cost of borrowing was 11.2%; FY27 is assumed at about the same. Moving from BBB+ to A- is a multi-factor journey, not expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR 102 crore of cash held, and is it a drag on ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash held as a buffer for April, a seasonally slack month for bank borrowings; management said the balance will be deployed into the loan book.

508954|2026-06.headline: Finkurve's Q1 FY27 AUM grew 135% YoY to a 118-branch network, with gross NPA at 0.54% and debt-to-equity up to 2.9x.

Reported AUM rose 135% YoY, revenue about 89% YoY and PAT about 65% YoY, with branches up from 83 to 118. Asset quality was stable (gross NPA 0.54%, net NPA 0.48%), while leverage rose sharply (debt-to-equity 0.7x to 2.9x) and ROA fell to 2.9%. Management reiterated 50-60% AUM growth guidance for FY27 and disclosed the first institutional NCD subscription (Rs 50 crore from Franklin Templeton).

segments.commentary: Co-lending share is about 3% currently; target is 15-20% of the book by end-FY27.

509079|2026-03.headline: Gufic Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR252 crore with EBITDA margin at 17.7%, while FY26 PAT fell to INR63.2 crore.

Indore reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 at about 30% capacity utilisation, as committed. Management guided to about 15% revenue growth in FY27, around 18% EBITDA margin for FY27, and gross debt held at about INR400 crore.

CMO traction is expected to build from Q2, with the main contribution in Q3; about 30% of capacity is for domestic CMO and about 70% for international use, where Hetero and Gufic have filed in more than 22 countries. No front-end role is planned in India or abroad.

qa_highlights.question: How does the shift in international model (distributor-led to own-registration, field-force led) change economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is moving to own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia once registrations and scale allow, aiming to lift margins from 40-50% under distributor models by 15-20% or more. A regional team was recruited in Q1 (one person in Mexico, one in the Philippines, two in Mumbai); the company also says it is building IP and trademarks in these markets.

qa_highlights.question: When will Indore get EU certification and does margin expansion follow, and is 18% the new normal margin?

Indore utilisation was 18-22% last year, 20-25% the year before, and close to 30-35% this year, targeted at 40-45% by year-end. Management said the 18% margin is the start of an improvement trend rather than a new normal, and that the earlier 18% period had Indore costs, depreciation and interest capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth conservative, and can growth go beyond 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% year-on-year company growth is a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond it. Some low-yielding product mix is being squeezed out, and it was not conservative in that guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from current capacity without further capex (analyst cited about INR2,700 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Roonghta first put FY27 expected revenue at about INR1,100 crore, with 15% annual growth taking it to about INR1,600 crore on existing facilities. Pranav Choksi said Navsari is capped at about INR800 crore, with toxin and penem not saturated, and Indore could add INR800-1,200 crore on about INR300 crore capex. The combined no-capex figure was cited as INR1,600-1,800 crore, and the total maximum as INR1,600-2,000 crore. The INR2,700 crore figure was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned employee addition strategy, and what productivity metrics are used?
qa_highlights.answer: Most additions are at Indore, with about 50-60 people for domestic expansion, while international headcount is capped at 20-25. The previous year's increase reflected contract staff moving to payroll in Indore and Navsari for quality roles, which management called a one-time step. Employee cost growth is in line with the company's overall growth.

Target mix is about 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation and 20-30% complex injectables, with the liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within 3 years.

509152|2026-03.headline: GRP Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 94 million (7% margin) from INR 331 million as EPR income, exports and raw-material costs weighed.

FY26 total income fell about 3% to INR 5,380 million and EBITDA dropped to INR 429 million from INR 694 million, with adjusted PAT of INR 46 million after a INR 14 million Labour Code charge. Export volumes fell about 15% while domestic volumes grew nearly 10%, and raw-material inflation reached 43% in certain SKUs. Management said the Pyrova (pyrolysis) and rCB platforms are still stabilising, and that the revised pricing from April 2026 passes through the full raw-material impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recovery trend in exports and order inflows, and have RM costs stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: North American direct volumes are largely recovered and the order book is stronger than most of FY26. Revised pricing from April 2026 captures the full raw-material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capex breakup, and what is the feedback on TPO and the new reclaim technology?
