rows.label: Pyrolysis EPR accrual on PCB approvals
rows.why: Management expects PCB approvals within weeks and retrospective EPR accrual by H1 FY27; EPR credits are priced near the INR 2.52/kg floor, so the catch-up accrual could lift H1 FY27 earnings.

rows.label: Order book stronger than most of FY26
rows.why: North American direct volumes largely recovered and the order book is stronger than most of FY26, though indirect volumes via Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia are only partly recovered and US tariffs still hit about 41% of RR revenues after February revisions.

rows.label: Revised April 2026 pricing passes through RM inflation
rows.why: Revised pricing from April 2026 is said to fully pass through raw-material inflation of up to 43% in some SKUs, after margin erosion in Q2 to part of Q4 FY26 under annual or half-yearly tyre contracts, subject to current conditions.

tone.note: Management was candid about a weak FY26 from tariffs, raw-material inflation and start-up costs, and confident on Pyrova and the reclaim expansion, but was evasive on forward margins and petchem pricing; analysts pushed on EPR accrual timing, pyrolysis oil realisations and capex funding.

509152|2026-06.headline: GRP Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 60% to INR174 million, margin 11% (+233 bps), PAT more than doubled to INR42 million on 26% total income growth.
509152|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 26% YoY to INR1,573 million, driven by Pyrova Energy utilisation, export recovery and better realisations. EBITDA grew 60% to INR174 million with margin up 233 bps to 11% despite sharp raw material inflation. Management re-segmented into Rubber Recycling and Others, and for the first time gave a directional FY27 outlook of close to 20%+ revenue growth. Pyrova cleared a 25-day monthly continuous run threshold in July 2026, and the rCB plant is slated for commissioning by October 2026.

segments.name: Rubber Recycling (Reclaim Rubber, Custom Die Forms, Pyrova Energy)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue grew 34% on a stand-alone basis with reclaim volumes +12%; margins expanded on realisations and efficiencies. Pyrova is still below stand-alone profitability; cumulative Pyrova investment is about INR91 crore.

segments.name: Others (Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefin, Windmill, residual polymer composite)
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly flat against a higher base that included polymer composite, which was permanently shut after the tariff hit. Engineering plastics volumes +27%; plastic verticals EBITDA margin up 14 pp YoY on a 10-pp gross margin improvement.

guidance_outlook: FY27: close to 20%+ overall revenue growth, driven by Pyrova, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling.
FY27: reclaim rubber volumes to grow close to 20%; management hopes to hold double-digit volume growth for the year.
Reclaim rubber, mid-term: mid-teen volume growth over 3 years, double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin from ~9-10% toward 10-14% after Pyrova synergies.
Pyrova: capacity to 45,000 tons, then +30,000 tons in FY28; EBITDA margin to 18-20% after rCB is mature (later described as 15-20%); FY28 seen as maturity year.
Plastics: over 20% growth in FY27, mid-teen growth through FY30, EBITDA margin 10-15%. Management said current margin is not one-time and should keep improving.
FY27 capex INR90-100 crore; FY28 capex decision in 2H FY27. Remaining ~INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan still to be deployed.
capex_capacity: Pyrova: two more pyrolysis lines to take capacity to 45 KTA; longest continuous reactor run achieved; July 2026 met threshold of 25-day monthly run with 4-day shutdown.
rCB (recovered carbon black) plant: commissioning starts next month (August 2026), target commissioning by October 2026; meaningful contribution expected by Q4 FY27.
Reclaim rubber debottlenecking capex included in FY27 plan.
Long-term: another 30,000 t pyrolysis and 12,000 t rCB capacity in Gujarat; Pyrova stand-alone revenue potential INR250-300 crore.
Renewable energy was ~48% of stand-alone power in FY26 (37% a year earlier); target 50% by FY28, expected to be reached in the current fiscal.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth ~30% YoY vs volume +12%; the balance is price, largely passed through to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually.
Management does not expect rubber prices to reverse soon; cited El Nino effects on natural rubber and oil-linked synthetic rubber pricing.
Reclaim is being pitched as a value alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches.
US exports recovered (export volumes +20%, mostly North America); Europe and other markets starting to contribute. Non-US indirect tariff-related volumes not fully recovered.
Domestic reclaim market share up ~1% YoY per management; export share flat overall but higher in focus geographies.
Engineering plastics growth driven mainly by automotive OE demand, with early appliance approvals contributing; polyolefin volumes flat as customer selection tightened.

financial_highlights.change: Gross margin moderated on higher raw material costs (management cited ~180 bps decline)
More than doubled; after prior period items
vs INR46 million in Q1 FY26

qa_highlights.question: Has the tariff disruption led to permanent changes in the competitive landscape, and did GRP win customers from global competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer composite was permanently shut, a real one-time loss. Reclaim and Custom Die Forms volumes are back to pre-tariff levels, with currency adding a margin benefit versus pre-February 2026. Some customers are starting to receive tariff credits, which may lift margins later, but visibility is limited. Indirect non-US export volumes are not fully recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Which business will be the largest contributor to earnings growth for the rest of FY27, and does management expect double-digit revenue growth and further margin expansion in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated close to 20%+ revenue growth for FY27, driven by Pyrova Energy, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling. It said the Q1 margin is not one-time and should keep improving, but it did not give a separate gross margin number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rCB project status, including customer trials, expected revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The first pyrolysis phase was commissioned in October 2025 and stabilised by March 2026. The rCB plant starts commissioning in August 2026 and is targeted for October 2026. Meaningful contribution is expected from Q4 FY27. Pyrova can reach 18-20% EBITDA margin once rCB is mature, subject to customer approvals; FY28 is seen as the maturity year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 27% growth in engineering plastics volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly automotive OE demand for nylon, with early appliance approvals from Q4 FY26 contributing some commercial volume. Polyolefin revenue grew but volumes were flat because customer selection was tightened, with a push into specialty polyolefin sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How much has rubber inflation risen over the past year, and when will prices stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict how long rubber inflation will last. Revenue grew about 30% against 12% volume growth, so the balance is price, largely passed to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually. Prices are not expected to reverse soon given El Nino and oil-linked synthetic rubber.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 capex plans, and what is the deleveraging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR90-100 crore, covering two more pyrolysis lines to reach 45 KTA, the rCB plant and reclaim debottlenecking. FY28 capex will be decided in 2H FY27. About INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan remains. Deleveraging timing is not in management's control, and there are no firm plans, though it would be needed to accelerate the Gujarat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers shifting toward sustainability-led material solutions rather than buying on price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a combination of value and sustainability. Reclaim is increasingly considered an alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches. In plastics, regulation drives conversion and cost drives adoption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recovery is demand normalisation versus share gains, and is the export order book back to pre-tariff levels? What is the sustainable EBITDA margin, and when does Pyrova become EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose 20%, mostly North America, with early Europe contribution. Domestic market share is up about 1% YoY, and export share is flat overall but higher in focus geographies. Pyrova crossed a 25-day monthly continuous run with a 4-day shutdown in July 2026. Management did not give a date for EBITDA breakeven. Stand-alone EBITDA margin targets are Reclaim 10-14%, Pyrova 15-20% and plastics 12-15%.

risks_watch: Rubber and raw material inflation: gross margin fell about 180 bps and management would not guide on gross margin; pass-through lags 1-4 quarters under quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts.

Pyrova execution: still below stand-alone profitability, with margins in single digits during ramp-up. rCB commissioning targeted October 2026, but several quarters may be needed for tire-industry product approval.
Indirect non-US export volumes not yet recovered; polymer composite closure is a permanent revenue and margin loss.
Capex and leverage: FY27 capex of INR90-100 crore, FY28 capex decision deferred to 2H FY27, and no firm deleveraging plan.
Plastics: polyolefin volumes flat on tighter customer selection; nylon growth depends on automotive demand; EPR enforcement and waste collection remain challenges.
Possible tariff credits to customers could affect margins, with timing and size not yet visible.
key_quotes: The threshold in the industry from a performance perspective is for a run of minimum of 25 days in a month and a 4 -day shutdown on the pyrolysis.
I do believe that this margin that we have generated in Q1 is not a onetime margin generation.
So, I wouldn't want to comment on the gross margin number.
At least as things stand now, we do expect these businesses to start generating cash flow.
509152|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the integrated platform, Pyrova milestones and the first-ever FY27 outlook, but cautious on near-term pricing, rCB timing and FY28 capex. Management declined to forecast rubber price direction or gross margin and framed several targets as conditional on customer approvals.

rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin rose 233 bps to 11% and management says it should keep improving, but gross margin fell ~180 bps on rubber inflation and pass-through lags 1-4 quarters, while Pyrova is still below stand-alone profitability in single digits.

rows.why: rCB commissioning starts August 2026 with target October 2026, and two more Pyrova pyrolysis lines to 45 KTA are under construction, with a further 30,000 t in FY28 planned; FY27 capex of INR90-100 crore is committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Reclaim volumes +12% in Q1 and guided to close to 20% for FY27, with reclaim export volumes +20% and engineering plastics volumes +27%, though polyolefin volumes are flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said the FY28 capex decision is due in 2H FY27 and ~INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan is still to be deployed, though utilisation was not disclosed so this is guided rather than strictly utilisation-driven.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at close to 20%+ growth versus Q1 revenue up 26% and reclaim volumes up 12%, and possible tariff credits could lift margins, but timing and size are not visible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin fell ~180 bps on raw material inflation, management would not guide on gross margin, pass-through lags 1-4 quarters, and rCB may need several quarters for tyre-industry approval.

rows.why: rCB commissioning Aug-Oct 2026 with meaningful contribution expected from Q4 FY27, though tyre-industry product approvals are still needed and timing is conditional.

rows.why: Export volumes +20% mostly North America with early Europe contribution, but indirect non-US export volumes are not yet recovered.

rows.why: Revenue grew ~30% against 12% volume growth so the ~18-point balance is price, passed through with a 1-4 quarter lag, and management does not expect rubber prices to reverse soon.

tone.note: Management was confident on the integrated platform, Pyrova's 25-day run milestone and the first FY27 outlook, but cautious on rubber pricing, rCB timing and FY28 capex; analysts probed the competitive landscape, plastics volume drivers, pricing pass-through, and leverage.

509480|2026-06.headline: Berger Paints Q1 FY27 standalone value growth 12.7% on ~8.4% volume; operating margin 17.4%, PAT up 25.5%.
509480|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 12.7% in value with volume up about 8.4%, driven by decorative (value +13.5%, operating profit up nearly 20%). Gross margin was 39.3%, held back by delayed and partial price pass-through in industrial and protective, GI and powder coatings, where price increases landed late in the quarter. Consolidated revenue rose 12%, PBDIT rose 12.6%-15% (management cited 15% operating profit growth) with margin up about 40 bps, and PAT rose 28.6%, with the Bolex and STP subsidiaries lagging on growth. Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth, a slightly better Q2 than Q1 on a year-on-year basis, and operating margin within the 15-17% range.

financial_highlights.change: Above 15-17% guided range; Q1 seasonally higher on value sales
Consolidated operating margin just short of 17%

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,424 crore as of end June 2026
financial_highlights.change: Up from Rs 992 crore (transcript reads 992 to 11.98 to 1424, likely a transcription error)

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth about 13.5%, the highest in 12 quarters, with operating profit up nearly 20% and margin expansion. Exterior emulsions outperformed; Color Plus premium interior emulsion gaining traction; Luxol metallics new range doing well.

segments.name: Protective, GI and powder coatings
segments.commentary: Relatively lower growth because price increases were taken late in the quarter after a prolonged battle in the field; expected to show up more in Q2.

segments.name: Automotive coatings
segments.commentary: Healthy double-digit value growth.

segments.name: Wood coatings and HomeShield
segments.commentary: Strong growth; wood coatings reported strong double-digit volume growth.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and waterproofing
segments.commentary: Robust volume and value growth; now about 10-12% of the paint business and growing well above paint. Roof pool and seal gaining momentum.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and JVs
segments.commentary: Bolex had flattest revenue on seasonality and UK remained subdued, though Bolex profitability improved. STP profitability improved on mix and price. BNPA and Becker JVs posted strong revenue and profit growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth expected to sustain, supported by full-quarter price increase impact in Q2 and festive demand.
Q2 revenue growth expected slightly ahead of Q1; Q2 volume growth around 7.5-8%, slightly below Q1's 8.5%.
Price increase contribution expected at about 7.5-8.5% in Q2 versus about 5% in Q1.
Operating margin to stay within the 15-17% guided range; Q2 year-on-year operating margin expected to improve, and Q2 should be slightly better than Q1 on that basis, though not sequentially.
Management expects good top-line and operating profit growth in Q3, with no firm margin call beyond that because of raw material volatility.
Capex for FY27 roughly Rs 600-800 crore; Panagar plant to start at end of this fiscal, plus a plant in Odisha near Jharsuguda.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex roughly Rs 600-800 crore, per management.
Panagar factory to start at end of FY27; second plant in Odisha near Jharsuguda, both funded partly from the cash surplus.
Tinting machine installations crossed 2,100 in the quarter; annual target about 10,000, mostly in under-indexed markets.
Store count above 1,900, with urban stores around 900+ and growing.
Backward integration: emulsions and most resins now made in-house; thickeners being produced in-house; a Dow-linked monomer to be made at Sandhila, Lucknow.
demand_pricing: Volume growth about 8.4%, value growth 12.7%, with price contribution about 5% in Q1 (mostly time-weighted) and mix improvement of roughly 2-3%, per management, which differs from management's normal 0.4-0.5% mix change.
Secondary sales were better than last year because rains were lighter; July growth described as reasonable, and August expected to be similar.
Dealers stocked up ahead of price increases; management expects this to be absorbed by stronger sell-out, with little Q2 destocking risk.
Competition intense: challenger brands aligned dealer price lists within about 5%, raised rebates to large dealers, and continue 10% free-material offers in most packs outside the economy segment.
East India muted; West Bengal government transition expected to take 3-4 months before government contracts restart. Northeast hit by floods in Assam. South and North grew faster.
Retail is the bulk of growth; project business 1-2% faster than retail.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 value growth came from price and mix, and what price increase is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 price impact about 5% (time-weighted, mostly industrial). Q2 price impact expected around 7.5-8.5%, depending on mix. Management said mix improved in Q1 and should improve further in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 margins expand year-on-year, and what about the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 operating profit growth to be decent and year-on-year margin to improve, helped by industrial price pass-through and operating leverage. Beyond that, margins depend on raw material prices, so no firm full-year call.

qa_highlights.question: Why is decorative growth below the industry leader's?
qa_highlights.answer: Base effect: the leader degrew last year while Berger grew. Management cited a 3.6% value growth differential and an 8.6% profit differential in the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth at risk from price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain high single-digit volume growth through network expansion, the branding campaign, new products and the price increase being absorbed, and sees no volume downside risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be post-Diwali price cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; it depends on crude and raw materials. If prices fall substantially, some price reduction in H2 is possible to avoid a price war.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand or pricing reason for the weak Bolex and STP subsidiary growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Bolex was seasonally weak in Q1; STP was disrupted by the Jamshedpur plant but has normalised. Corrective measures on less profitable lines in Bolex and STP are expected to lift profitability.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (crude oil, geopolitics): a sharp fall could widen margins, but could also trigger price cuts and discounting in H2.
Industrial and protective price pass-through still lagging; full effect expected in Q2 and August.
Competitive intensity remains elevated; challenger brands' rebates and free-material schemes could persist.
Mix shift toward low-value, high-volume construction chemicals could keep value growth below volume growth.
Eastern India and Northeast demand; West Bengal transition period.
Subsidiaries: UK operations subdued; Bolex and STP growth flat in Q1 with profitability turnaround still to be proven.
Monsoon and the timing of Diwali for festive-season sell-out.
509480|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on decorative momentum and the Q2 outlook, but noticeably cautious and hedged on raw material-driven margins, with repeated reference to volatility. Evasive on precise mix and price split and on market share figures.
key_quotes: Value growth, as you have seen already, is at 12.7%.
Operating margins are expected to remain within the guided range, which we have always said, that is between 15% and 17%.
The volume growth will be somewhere around similar levels as, quarter one, slightly below, maybe, you know, so we were at 8.5%, maybe it will be 7.5% to 8%, approximately.

rows.why: Bolex and STP growth was flat in Q1 and corrective measures on less profitable lines are expected to lift profitability, but this is not yet proven.

rows.why: East India remains muted and government contracts are expected to restart only after a 3-4 month transition period in West Bengal.

tone.note: Management was confident on decorative momentum (value +13.5%, highest in 12 quarters) and the Q2 price-led outlook, but cautious and hedged on raw-material-driven margins; analysts pressed on the price/mix split, market share and whether volumes are at risk from price increases.

509496|2026-03.headline: Cemindia FY26 revenue crossed INR10,000 crore (INR10,061 crore, +9%) and Q4 EBITDA margin hit 15.1%, helped by one-time claims and provision releases.
509496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income rose to INR2,973 crore for the full year and Q4 EBITDA jumped 66% YoY to INR450 crore at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the margin spike to one-time items: INR150 crore of claims realised (INR100 crore in Q4, partly booked as other income) and release of provisions held for metro jobs now completed. Management guided that the normal EBITDA margin is about 10-10.5%. Order book stands at INR29,000 crore, including L1 positions of about INR1,600 crore and an April win of about INR3,200 crore. FY27 guidance is revenue growth of at least 20-25%, with an order-inflow target of about INR25,000 crore.

segments.name: Group / captive EPC (Adani-linked) and data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre is a new division with 3-4 jobs secured from the group; cumulative data centre order book about INR3,000 crore. Management is keeping it within the group for now, with Vizag opportunities mentioned.

segments.name: Metro and tunnelling
segments.commentary: Bangalore and Mumbai metro jobs completed and contributed to Q4 margin. Chennai Metro has about 40% of value left, with completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028; the company owns 4 TBMs at Chennai and sold a Bangalore TBM. Tunnelling market (metro, road and other) is cited at about INR1 lakh crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to grow at least 25% per MD's opening answer; later answers say 20-25% is quite possible on top line.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR25,000 crore, against about INR19,000 crore secured in FY26 (including L1 and April wins).
Sustainable EBITDA margin excluding other income guided at about 10-10.5%; management says it will try for more than 10%.
FY27 capex planned at INR350-400 crore, against INR260 crore in FY26.
PAT margin: management aims to maintain the same momentum and margin.
Dividend was supposed to be declared but is delayed; management said it will be declared within a few weeks.
Revenue growth of 20-25% a year for up to about 3 years was stated as the aspiration; no fundraising planned.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR350-400 crore versus INR260 crore in FY26.
Chennai Metro TBMs have completed breakthrough; about 40% of value left, completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028 (stations included in scope).
New TBMs being bought for Pune Metro and Delhi Metro; large-diameter TBM would be needed for large diameter tunnel work.
No idle TBMs at present; a TBM is typically engaged for 3-4 years on a job.
demand_pricing: Work in hand (order book) stands at INR29,000 crore versus about INR20,000-21,000 crore a year earlier; management says no legacy jobs remain.
FY26 order wins about INR14,000 crore excluding L1 and April wins; with L1 and April wins, about INR19,000 crore versus about INR7,000 crore in prior years.
Pipeline of about INR70,000 crore, of which group is about 35-40%; roads and highways and tunnelling are the main segments, each about INR1 lakh crore market.

Vadhvan port: breakwater tender and dredging and reclamation tender out; company is L1 for the breakwater job and progress has stalled since technical bid opening in October with customer reasons unknown.
Mor Sagar (JV with group, 27% stake) is at early design stage; EPC award could go to the company or another party based on price.

Around 30% of jobs have fixed-price (star price) arrangements with commodity pass-through in both directions; about 80% of jobs have a clause protecting against normal inflation but not abnormal war-driven cost spikes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion to about 12% excluding other income, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited completed metro jobs, claims realised and release of provisions kept for metro jobs; it said this is not a regular phenomenon and guided 10-10.5% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin came from claims?
qa_highlights.answer: INR150 crore of claims were realised for the full year, of which INR100 crore in Q4; part was booked in other income (mainly interest) and part in revenue. The claim was described as one-time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mobilisation advance and how much is interest-bearing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mobilisation advance was INR1,400 crore at March 2026, with about 90% interest-free and about 10% interest-bearing; interest terms depend on the project and the promoter-group's contract with the client.

qa_highlights.question: How is the data centre business progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: A new division has 3-4 group jobs and about INR3,000 crore of data centre orders; the focus is on group opportunities for now, with Vizag opportunities mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Adani road-tunnel project and Vadhvan?
qa_highlights.answer: The group is L1 on the road tunnel job but has not yet received the order; the company will bid if it is awarded. Vadhvan is a slow-moving project and the company is waiting on customer decisions on the breakwater and dredging tenders.

qa_highlights.question: How much inflation risk is passed through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of jobs are fixed-price with commodity pass-through, about 80% have normal-inflation escalation clauses, and the remainder has no protection; management expects some margin impact that will be priced into future bids.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a dividend and fundraising plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The dividend was not declared this year due to a process delay and management said it will be declared within a few weeks. No fundraising is planned as the company has adequate funds.

risks_watch: Q4 margin of 15.1% included one-time claims and provision releases; normalised margin guided at about 10-10.5%, so Q1 FY27 margin is a key test.
Vadhvan port project is slow-moving with no clarity on the timing of the customer's release of the breakwater work.
Commodity and fuel inflation (crude, cement, steel) could squeeze margins on the about 70% of jobs without full pass-through, and this is not yet quantified.
Payment risk from some state governments; management says central government payments are fine but several states have weak treasuries and some bills remain uncertified.
Dependence on group orders: group is 35-40% of the INR70,000 crore pipeline; the road-tunnel award to the group is pending.
Management could not give Bangladesh receivables or the Q1 FY27 order details beyond L1 and April wins; the call reported the Bangladesh receivables as under control.
Dividend declaration pending; the company said it will be declared within a few weeks.

509496|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 operating income rose 6% YoY to Rs 2,721 crore, EBITDA margin 10.5%, while order inflow nearly tripled to Rs 8,519 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in other expenses from INR 95 crore to INR 106 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is not substantial, expense ratios are declining as a percentage of sales, and the one-offs include provision reversals and the INR 88 mn depreciation charge plus a property charge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 100 crore ECB repayment to the parent extended from Feb 2026 to June 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: The ECB loan from the parent follows RBI tenure guidelines; part has been repaid and the balance is payable by June 2027. Servicing cost is linked to FD returns, so no negative impact, per management.

509820|2026-06.headline: Huhtamaki India Q2 CY26 net sales rose 23.1% to INR723 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.3%, with PBT up 77%.
509820|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q2 net sales of INR723 crore, up about 23% YoY, with growth split roughly evenly across price, volume and product mix and broad-based across exports and domestic. EBITDA margin expanded to 10.5% from 8.3%, and PBT rose 77% to INR559 crore, with EPS up about 77%. H1 sales grew close to 12% and H1 EBIT margin was hit by a one-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge; excluding it, EBIT margin was 7.6%. Management attributed the quarter to pricing pass-through of Middle East-driven raw material inflation, a healthy portfolio mix and productivity, plus some customer inventory build-up that it said would partly reverse.

segments.commentary: Exports grew at roughly the same rate as domestic in Q2; exports are about 30% of sales volume. Management said duty-related challenges are stabilising.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic growth was almost identical to exports at about 23%; volume growth in liquid and home care categories was highlighted.

segments.commentary: Blueloop share of output is below 30% of material volume, up from the prior quarter; the balance of blueloop asset output (>70%) is used for products previously outsourced.

Customers valued supply reliability and contingency during the Middle East crisis; management said this drove share-of-wallet gains with same customer base.
Customer inventory build-up in anticipation of price increases is a tailwind; quantum not known to management.
Home care and liquid categories growing faster than food and beverage in India; late monsoon boosted beverage season.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q2 volume growth and export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was high single-digit, just short of double digit; exports and domestic grew at almost identical rates of about 23%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing volume growth again after sacrificing volume for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not moved away from profitable growth; product mix and customer base have largely settled and the focus is share-of-wallet and innovation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR750 crore quarterly revenue run-rate reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit; INR750 crore includes single-digit price pass-through, and outcome depends on product mix and customer growth. It could be INR650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is working capital and receivables trend (inventory and receivables roughly doubled; receivables ~50% of six-month turnover)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute values are higher due to price increases and higher volume; DSO and DIO are stable, and there are no realisation or ageing challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for acquisitions or monetising land such as Daman?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific non-organic plans disclosed; cash is directed to modernisation and capex. Thane land sale was completed a couple of years ago; other land monetisation will be disclosed in annual reports if it happens.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth rate be sustainable into next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to track market growth (around 3-5%) rather than repeat 23% every quarter.

509930|2026-03.headline: FY26 volume rose about 12% to 753,907 MT while consolidated PAT fell 1% to Rs 954 crore; FY27 volume guided at 12-13%.
509930|2026-03.overview: Supreme Industries reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 11,218 crore (up 7%) on volume growth of about 12%, with consolidated operating profit up 7% to Rs 1,654 crore and PAT down 1% to Rs 954 crore. Plastic piping volumes grew 14% while industrial products degrew 1% in volume and 3% in value. Management said the industry's plastic piping volume declined 9% in FY26 and guided FY27 piping volume growth of 15-17%, with overall growth of 12-13% and margins of 14-14.5%. PVC resin prices swung sharply in March (up about Rs 32-37/kg) and then fell about Rs 34/kg between 5 and 21 April, which management said was now corrected. Capex of about Rs 1,000 crore is planned, adding about 1.10 lakh MT of capacity to reach about 1.35 million MT per annum.

509930|2026-06.headline: Supreme Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% to INR2,718 crore on 14% volume decline, with standalone PAT up 17% to INR208 crore; FY27 guidance held.

Management attributed the weakness to April 2026 polymer price volatility and channel destocking, and said volumes recovered in May-July. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 12-13% overall volume growth, 15-17% piping volume growth and 14-14.5% EBITDA margin, plus about INR1,000 crore capex.

rows.why: Management says new facilities will be needed in the near future and Saudi manufacturing is planned but undated, though utilisation was not disclosed to confirm a capacity squeeze.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric FY27 guidance was given; management only said growth would be 'very, very good' and referred investors to quarterly results.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 revenue up 78% and PAT up 77%, with ₹365 crore order book; no cost or demand headwinds were flagged, though receivables ageing and lumpy quarters are watch items.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.why: Most of the ₹365 crore order book is expected to execute in FY27, equal to about 1.5x FY26 revenue of ₹240 crore.

511147|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 26% to about INR111 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR6.14 crore, while Q4 growth slowed on macro and war-related travel weakness.
511147|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with revenue crossing about INR111 crore for the first time, PBT of INR8.03 crore and PAT of INR6.14 crore, and the company stated it remains debt-free. Q4 was hit by macro volatility, especially in March, from the US-Israel-Iran conflict and lower US student travel, though management said Q4 revenue still grew 22% and GTO grew 16%. Management highlighted the FEMA 401/2026 RBI circular, which expands AD-II scope to trade remittances and family maintenance and allows Forex Correspondent (FXC) appointments, and said it has recommended a 15% dividend. Management also acknowledged that rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup have taken share from forex cards in leisure travel, and that leisure market volumes contracted about 25% from March.

segments.name: Student
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver per management; overall market contracted about 20% in the year while the company gained share. Loan-funded students growing while own-funds students contracted after TCS was cut to 2%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Over 900 corporates served; management cited a 95.62% CAGR. Named clients include Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra and, recently, Adani.

segments.name: Retail / leisure
segments.commentary: Card business declined in FY26 on lower US student traffic and competition from rupee credit cards; leisure market down about 25% since March. Management described this as a calibrated, value-led push with a minimum margin per transaction.

segments.name: Prepaid cards
segments.commentary: Four products (three plastics and one digital-only, Uni-Z launched last month). Switch Card supports 30 currencies; Xplorer Metal card is by invitation. Samsung Pay and Google Pay tokenisation planned this year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 to be a challenging, linear quarter with leisure travel down roughly 25% from March, and expects the next one to two months to remain tough.
Trade remittances expected to become a material business in 12 to 18 months; family maintenance (about $3 billion market) to be a growth area.
FXC network expected to expand through the model over the next 12 to 15 months, with Spice Money group network and NBFC/retail partners as possible distribution.
Trade remittance margins expected 20-30 bps, below current blended levels, as competition rises.
Target to raise digital/automated share of transactions from about 60% to 80% this year.
Management did not give numerical FY27 targets for cards or revenue; it said Q2 to Q4 are peak months and FY27 mix will change materially.
capex_capacity: Network kept lean at 21+ branches (down from 35 when the CEO took over, 16 in COVID); expansion planned mainly through FXC appointments rather than owned branches.
Company is evaluating whether to apply for a PA-CB licence.
Working on multiple payment rails for faster, holiday-enabled remittances and a student fee-remittance platform.
Smart Agent Platform, FPaaS, Smart Corporate Platform and consumer app run on a unified payments stack.
demand_pricing: Q4 traffic hit in March by the US-Israel-Iran conflict; leisure market contracted about 25% from March to May 2026 per management.
Rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup and lounge perks have taken a large share of international spend (management estimate about 60%), with credit card spend outside LRS and TCS.
Management says it will not price at a loss; pricing uses interbank rates with a small card fulfilment fee on the Switch card.
B2B and corporate make up about 80-85% of business; partner commissions and referral fees are a larger share of costs.
Retail customer lifetime value is quoted at about INR1,000 of annual income per traveller versus high digital CAC.
Management expects more competition after the RBI circular, with margin pressure; trade remittances may run at 20-30 bps margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new RBI circular affect volumes, revenue and margins over the next one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scope has expanded to trade and non-trade current account transactions, with no negative impact from the circular itself, but competition will pressure margins. Trade remittance margins are expected at 20-30 bps; current net margin is 0.6-0.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will be most affected by the new regulations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split out the impact by segment. It said the new trade and family maintenance categories open new growth areas, and that retail/leisure faces the most pressure from credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with low-priced small players on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay competitive but will not work at a loss per transaction, citing a minimum margin policy and a digital platform for each segment. It acknowledged its retail pricing may not be the lowest.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise FY26 revenue, volume, customer and new-product breakdown; agent commissions versus branch revenue; CAC; card KPIs and FY27 targets
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only broad-based answers: B2B and corporate are 80-85% of business, partner commissions are higher as a B2B company, and digital CAC is high. It declined to give specific numbers and said detailed data would be shared through the company's written channel.

qa_highlights.question: How does Scapia (bank-sponsored card) compare, and how are rupee credit cards affecting forex cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cards hold a regulatory arbitrage (no LRS or TCS), that around 60% of international spend has moved to credit cards, and that the association has represented to RBI for parity. Forex cards are positioned on rate certainty for multi-currency travel; corporate and student segments do not use credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TCS cut to 2% for education remittances doing to the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2% TCS mainly hit own-fund students, while loan-funded students are growing; it called the change a relief and said zero TCS would be better for the priority-sector segment.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and payables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Pooja Mishra said the rise in current assets and liabilities reflects card-program customer wallet balances on both sides of the balance sheet. Capital turnover improved to 4.4x from 3.8x, and short-term borrowings are fixed-deposit-backed working capital lines, not structural debt.

risks_watch: Leisure and card volumes down about 25% since March; Q1 FY27 expected to be linear and challenging.
Rupee credit cards eroding forex card share in leisure; RBI parity representation is pending with no timeline.
Margin pressure from new AD-II entrants and FFMC-licensed competitors; trade remittance margins guided at 20-30 bps.
Execution risk on FXC network rollout and trade/family maintenance scope, which management said still has open clarifications.
Management was evasive on FY27 numerical targets, segment-wise volumes, card KPIs and PA-CB licence decision.
Customer service complaint raised on a Delhi branch; management promised corrective action.
511147|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the regulatory opportunity and long-term structure, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: Q1 FY27 was flagged as challenging and specific FY27 targets and segment KPIs were withheld. Management was defensive when discussing credit card competition and pricing.
key_quotes: Revenue crossed around INR111 crores for the first time. Revenue grew 26% significantly ahead of GTO growth, good business profitable mix.
We are happy to say we are increasing our market share year-on-year while the business has -- overall market has contracted by 20%.
So, from our perspective, we are clearly focused on forex cards, how to bring out the merits of the forex card and it's up to the customer's choice to take a forex card or credit card.

rows.why: Net margin is stated at 0.6% to 0.8%, trade remittance margins are guided at 20-30 bps (below blended levels) as competition rises, and retail pricing is under pressure from rupee credit cards.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network kept lean at 21+ branches (down from 35); expansion is planned through FXC appointments rather than owned branches, with no capacity figures or timing given beyond the 12-15 month FXC rollout.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Leisure market volumes down about 25% since March 2026 and Q1 FY27 guided as challenging and linear, although Q4 GTO still grew 16% YoY and Q2-Q4 are described as peak months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as a line item and the company is asset-light; a PA-CB licence decision is under evaluation but there is no capex figure or utilisation signal.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 revenue or card targets were given, and management guided the next one to two months as tough.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged Q1 FY27 as challenging and linear with leisure travel down about 25% from March, and margins face pressure from AD-II entrants and trade remittance at 20-30 bps.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Samsung Pay and Google Pay tokenisation planned this year, FXC network expanding over 12-15 months, and trade remittance expected to become material in 12-18 months; Uni-Z was launched last month (before the window).

rows.why: The RBI circular expands AD-II scope to trade remittances and family maintenance, but management said open clarifications remain and trade margins will run at 20-30 bps.

rows.label: Rupee credit card share gain versus forex cards
rows.why: Rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup are estimated to hold about 60% of international spend; RBI parity representation is pending with no timeline.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet with 15% dividend recommended
rows.why: Management stated the company remains debt-free with PAT of INR6.14 crore and recommended a 15% dividend; short-term borrowings are FD-backed working capital lines.

tone.note: Management was confident on the RBI circular opportunity and the long-term structure, but cautious on Q1 FY27 and evasive on FY27 numbers, segment KPIs and card data; analysts pushed on margins, credit card competition and working capital.

511196|2026-03.headline: Can Fin Homes FY26 disbursements hit INR10,531 crore, just above guidance, with Q4 a record INR3,245 crore; FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore.
511196|2026-03.overview: FY26 disbursements of INR10,531 crore marginally beat the INR10,500 crore guidance, with each quarter setting a new peak and Q4 at INR3,245 crore. AUM growth was about 10.44% as rundown ran about INR600 crore above the INR6,000 crore assumption. Karnataka grew 7% in disbursements after e-khata issues, and Telangana ended roughly flat at INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore. Q4 included two one-offs: INR46 crore additional DTA provision on standard assets and INR13.5 crore tax refund gain; management says underlying FY26 profit was INR1,027 crore, up 20% from INR857 crore. Around 85% of the book has moved to quarterly reset, with the 50 bps pass-through and a 15 bps cut in January leaving an opening yield near 9.8% and spread of about 2.8%.

financial_highlights.change: all-time quarterly high; new peak in each quarter of FY26
after 50 bps quarterly-reset pass-through and 15 bps January cut

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursement growth of 7% after e-khata delays; Q4 averaged about INR290 crore per month; FY27 target is 15% growth. Delinquency is lowest among six zones.

segments.name: Telangana
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursements INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore in FY25, roughly flat; now running INR100 crore-plus per month and expected to be positive from day one of FY27.

segments.name: North and West zones
segments.commentary: Each running about INR150-160 crore per month; North and West together grew about 40%-plus in FY26 per management.

segments.name: Tamil Nadu
segments.commentary: Running INR180-200 crore per month; growing around 30%.

segments.name: East zone (mainly Andhra Pradesh)
segments.commentary: Running close to INR100 crore per month; grew about 40%-plus in FY26 per management.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: Share rose by about 2 percentage points in FY26 as a deliberate push, mainly in Karnataka.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore, about 25% growth, applied roughly uniformly across zones.
FY27 rundown (prepayments, BT outs, closures) assumed at about INR7,000 crore, giving net book addition of about INR6,000 crore and AUM growth of about 14%.
FY27 spread guidance 2.75% and NIM guidance 3.75%, kept conservative versus opening spread of about 2.8%.
FY27 credit cost guidance 15 bps, though management expects it to be well below that.
IT programme: about INR40 crore net incremental cost in FY27 (about INR60 crore of depreciation and opex against about INR20 crore current IT cost); cost-to-income ratio to rise slightly.
FY27 ROA target about 2.4%; ROE expected at 18%-plus, slightly diluted by IT costs.
28 new branches planned for the first half of FY27 (3 in Karnataka, 2 in Telangana); sales team to grow from about 80-90 to about 150.
Employee cost expected to rise about 10%-12% in FY27; other opex from INR134 crore to INR175-180 crore.
capex_capacity: IT transformation totals INR300 crore: INR100 crore capex and INR200 crore opex spread over 5 years; depreciation begins mainly in FY27.
Infrastructure and security modules are complete; deposit applications and HRMS are live; LOS and LMS go live in Q1 FY27 and are expected to drive the next stage of efficiency gains.
Branch network grew by 54 branches over FY23-FY25; 15 branches opened in the first half of FY26 contributed INR863 crore of disbursements versus INR128 crore from earlier branches in FY25.
Sales team of about 80-90 people contributed about INR868 crore in FY26 versus INR183 crore from a team of 30-35 in FY25.
demand_pricing: Demand inquiries remain good across branches; affordable segment has slowed to mid-single-digit growth, while mid and prime segments hold up better.
About 85% of the book is now on quarterly reset (from about 48% annual-reset-to-quarterly shift in Q4); about 15% remains on annual reset and would lag if rates rise.
About 62% of liabilities are bank loans linked to repo; NCDs carry a blended cost of about 7.66%-7.67%; CP rates fell to about 6.45% in April from above 7% in Q4.

Q4 BT outs were about INR400 crore, roughly 25% of the INR1,730 crore total rundown; main competitors for BT outs are LIC Housing and Bajaj Finance, with Bajaj winning mainly on takeover-plus-top-up offers.
Incremental yield is about 9.8% or higher; salaried share of new business fell from about 89% to about 83-84% (self-employed mix rising).
PMAY/CLSS traction is limited: about INR1 lakh crore of PMAY claims across all HFCs and NBFCs in six months, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BT-out and rundown rate peaking after the April quarterly-reset shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q4 to be the peak; BT outs were about INR380-400 crore in Q3 and Q4, nearly flat, and FY27 rundown is modelled at INR7,000 crore versus about INR6,600 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will disbursements reach INR13,000 crore given branch growth of about 6-7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are 28 new branches in H1 FY27, expanding the sales team from 80-90 to about 150, and recovery in Karnataka and Telangana; the company is also planning for elevated prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 state-wise disbursement run rates and opex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Current monthly run rates: Karnataka about INR275-290 crore, Tamil Nadu INR180-200 crore, North and West INR150-160 crore each, Telangana INR110-120 crore, East about INR100 crore. Employee cost is INR177 crore and other cost INR134 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Are the West Asia situation or LAP delinquencies showing stress, and is any management overlay planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No stress seen in bounce rates or delinquencies through March and April; no additional management overlay planned, but PCR rose from 49% to 56%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for spreads and margins after the reset and NHB repricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is expected at about 2.8%, with guidance kept at 2.75%; the only risk is a rate rise, which would affect the roughly 15% of the book still on annual reset.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company losing prepayments to LIC Housing and Bajaj?
qa_highlights.answer: LIC wins on price, offering rates such as 7.15% on new business; Bajaj wins on takeover-plus-top-up, where Can Fin is more conservative on LTV.

risks_watch: Rate-up cycle: about 15% of the book on annual reset would lag repricing, while about 62% of liabilities reprice quickly.
Prepayment pressure from LIC Housing and Bajaj; rundown assumed at INR7,000 crore, and a higher rundown would cut the 14% AUM growth outlook.
Affordable segment demand slowdown, which management acknowledged.
LOS and LMS go-live in Q1 FY27 and the IT cost ramp (about INR40 crore net) could weigh on cost-to-income ratio.
Karnataka e-khata rollout in gram panchayat rural areas is still delayed; Telangana needs to sustain INR100 crore-plus monthly run rate.
Borrowing cost trajectory: NCD refinancing at lower rates and NHB tranche repricing are expected benefits but not yet visible.
511196|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and spread retention, with the 2.8% spread and 15 bps credit cost stated as conservative guidance. Cautious on affordable-segment demand and on prepayment losses to LIC and Bajaj, and some answers were evasive on the exact disbursement and spread drivers.
key_quotes: So we are quite confident that the 2.8%, which is there is kind of is there.
the entire benefit of the quarterly reset, that 50 basis points, has been passed on at the time of the revision to all of them.
we have ended with a 7% disbursement growth in Karnataka.

rows.why: FY27 disbursement target of INR13,000 crore (about 25% growth over INR10,531 crore) with AUM growth about 14% on a INR7,000 crore rundown assumption, though affordable segment has slowed to mid-single-digit growth and prepayment losses to LIC and Bajaj are a risk.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex or utilisation not discussed; company is an NBFC, and the IT programme (INR100 crore capex over 5 years) is already in progress rather than a new announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls the 2.75% spread, 15 bps credit cost and 2.4% ROA guidance conservative but has not signalled a raise; FY26 disbursements only marginally beat the INR10,500 crore guide at INR10,531 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rate-up risk on the about 15% of book on annual reset, prepayment pressure (BT outs about INR400 crore in Q4, rundown assumed INR7,000 crore vs INR6,600 crore FY26), and LOS/LMS go-live in Q1 FY27 with IT cost ramp of about INR40 crore could weigh on cost-to-income.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: LOS and LMS systems go live in Q1 FY27 and are expected to drive the next stage of efficiency gains; no new loan product named.

rows.label: Disbursement run-rate build into FY27 target
rows.why: Current monthly run rates (Karnataka INR275-290 crore, Tamil Nadu INR180-200 crore, North and West INR150-160 crore each, Telangana INR110-120 crore, East about INR100 crore) sum to roughly INR1,000-1,100 crore per month, which would need to hold to reach INR13,000 crore (about INR1,083 crore per month).

rows.why: About 85% of book on quarterly reset, opening yield about 9.8%, borrowing cost 6.99% at start of April, CP rates down to about 6.45% from above 7%, and NCD cost about 7.66% with refinancing at lower rates not yet visible.

rows.label: Credit cost below 15 bps guidance
rows.why: FY26 credit cost about 10 bps against 15 bps guidance, GNPA down to 0.85% from 0.87%, and PCR up to 56% from 49%; management expects FY27 well below 15 bps but has not raised guidance.

511196|2026-06.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
511196|2026-06.overview: Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 1,650 crores, up 28% YoY; accounted for about 63% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Non-housing / LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 958 crores, up 32% YoY; about 37% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Self-employed (SENP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 44% YoY; current NPA around 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% in salaried, per management.

segments.name: Karnataka / Telangana
segments.commentary: All six zones grew; Karnataka grew 18% YoY (lowest zone), Telangana slightly higher. IT-sector exposure about 6% of customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crores with 14% AUM growth; management may push to INR 13,200-13,400 crores if needed to offset higher rundown.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target INR 3,000 crores; quarterly path then steps up to INR 3,500 crores and INR 4,000 crores in Q3 and Q4 per prior plan.
NIM to be maintained at 3.81% plus; Q2 incremental bank borrowing at 7.25-7.5% expected to add only marginal cost, on new loans only.
Credit cost guided at 10 bps for FY27; management sees no challenge to this.
Cost-to-income ratio around 19.5% for FY27, trending back toward 18% over about three years.
Remaining 245 branches to move to new IT platform by end of Q2, in tranches at month-end (July, August, September); update expected around September.
Opex: about INR 40 crores of further IT-related costs yet to come; no other major surprises expected.
capex_capacity: New LOS/LMS/report-generation platform live in 5 pilot branches from 8 July 2026, with sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS collections and closures processed.
Rollout to remaining 245 branches (250 total) planned within Q2 FY27, migrating month-end data in tranches.
Management expects about six months for new branches to stabilise on the new system; staffing benefits expected this year with sales additions from existing headcount.
APF (apartment finance) approvals up to 331 projects; per-project exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.
demand_pricing: No demand slowdown seen across geographies; partner banks willing to sanction, including a couple of large sanctions.
Bank borrowing rates for new loans now 7.25-7.5% vs about 6.95% last year; existing loans unchanged.
Special-rate threshold raised from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh loans, to offset higher incremental borrowing costs.
Customer pricing range about 8.4% (best, salaried, CIBIL above 725, INR 25 lakh+) to about 12.5% (non-salaried, non-housing, S3); blended yield 9.81%.
Competition: LIC and Bajaj Housing are the main rivals in branches; Bajaj growing around 25-30% per analyst comment, with its technology edge cited.
Best rate gap to banks widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps after repo cuts; management says it cannot close the gap cheaply.
82% of loans now have CIBIL score above 700 (vs about 75% earlier); 80% of business sourced via DSA.

qa_highlights.question: Macro, underwriting and asset quality outlook for next 3-6 months, and any changes to norms or customer filters (salaried vs self-employed rejections)?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand slowdown across geographies; 60 APF projects added in Q1 (271 to 331 approved). Rates for new bank loans are 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year. Special-rate threshold moved from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh, customer re-rating parameters and EWS/OTMS monitoring added, and 82% of loans now have CIBIL above 700 (vs about 75% earlier). Expect some indirect rise in rejection ratios; 80% of business comes via DSA.

qa_highlights.question: Status of IT rollout (LOS, LMS, report generation) and any impact on disbursement targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot in 5 branches went live on 8 July 2026 using 30 June data, processing sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS and closures with only minor teething issues. Remaining 245 branches to move in month-end tranches (July, August, September), with a further update around September; INR 3,000 crore Q2 target unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and blended yield by segment; are there trade-offs by ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended yield 9.81% (9.82% last year). Best rate about 8.4% for salaried, CIBIL above 725, loans of INR 25 lakh plus; highest about 12.5% for non-salaried, non-housing, S3 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Housing vs non-housing and salaried vs self-employed growth; number of loans; run-rate going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing disbursements INR 1,650 crore (+28% YoY) and LAP INR 958 crore (+32%); salaried +21%, SENP +44%. Management gave amounts only, not loan account counts. FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crore unchanged, with a possible push to INR 13,200-13,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IT-sector hiring slowdown in Bangalore affecting home loan offtake or policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No major impact seen so far: Karnataka grew 18% YoY and Telangana slightly more (partly base effect). IT-sector customers are about 6% of the base, with top IT employers barely represented. Karnataka NPA was lower in absolute terms at March 2026 vs March 2025, with only a marginal June increase.

qa_highlights.question: Any opex surprises in FY27 and how far is APF exposure per project capped?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40 crore of further IT-related cost to come, with AMCs and depreciation starting; salary, rent and other costs in line with last year. Cost-to-income about 19.5% for FY27, trending toward 18% in about three years. APF exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the book rundown elevated for four quarters, and is the 4% level the new normal? Also, how does the best-rate gap to banks affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crore (vs INR 976 crore) drove the rundown, as borrowers under change-in-tenure kept EMIs constant and paid down principal. BT-outs were INR 408 crore (vs INR 400 crore), and other closures INR 377 crore (vs INR 360 crore). Best rate gap widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps; management is exploring deposit conversion and bureau alerts for retention.

qa_highlights.question: Can ROA of about 2.4% and ROE of about 18% be achieved in FY27 given higher opex and the soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ROA was 2.39% (2.53% last year) and ROE 18%+. Management said the cost impact is already visible and expects to manage ROA, with NIM and spread on track and credit cost not a concern. Q1 NPA rise was only INR 17-18 crore vs INR 45 crore last Q1 FY26.

risks_watch: Book rundown: part-prepayments of INR 1,857 crore in Q1 (INR 1,072 crore part-prepay) mean FY27 disbursements may need to exceed INR 13,000 crore to hold 14% AUM growth; Q2 target is INR 3,000 crore.

IT rollout: 245 remaining branches migrate in month-end tranches through September; update expected around September. Management noted 50-100 branches will need more handholding than the 5-branch pilot.
Cost of funds: new bank loans priced at 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year; NIM guidance of 3.81%+ depends on incremental-only pass-through and yield mix shift.
Competitive pricing gap: best rate spread to banks/larger players widened to over 100 bps from 55 bps; LIC and Bajaj Housing (growing about 25-30% per analyst) are main rivals.
Asset quality: SENP current NPA about 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% for salaried; IT-sector and Karnataka exposure monitored with early-warning signals; credit cost guided at 10 bps.
Opex: cost-to-income moved from about 18% to 19%+ in Q1, FY27 guided near 19.5%; about INR 40 crore of further IT costs yet to come.
key_quotes: So against INR 2,500 crores, which was what was planned and what was projected, we have achieved INR2,609 crores.
So, we are confident that the NIM will be maintained at 3.81% plus and we should not have a problem in that.
And so the 10 bps that we have been talking about, definitely doesn't look to be a challenge this year.

The major challenge or the major portion from where our run down is happening is actually amortization and more importantly, part prepayment where customers are making more payments every month, and but the loans are still with us.
511196|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and the 14% AUM growth target, but cautious on the higher book rundown, the widened pricing gap to banks and the IT rollout's business impact. Management was candid about the rundown and competitive pressures, and it deferred on new product launches, saying the Board has not yet deliberated.

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview: Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.
25 of 28 branches planned for FY27 are already operational with staff; these are expected to contribute in Q3 and Q4.
Branch expansion: about 12 branches added in UP in the last year, per management.
About 129 staff who were deployed on the IT project are being redeployed to branches and departments, with some support retained for 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the liquidity coverage ratio rise well above the 100% regulatory minimum, and what is a steady level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to lower short-term borrowings, now about 12% of borrowings versus 26-27% in March 2023, plus smaller bulk borrowings. LCR range cited as 135% to 250%; HQLA held at roughly INR2,300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does a rising rate cycle affect home loan demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 25-50 bps move is a non-event for demand because EMI impact is limited on 15-year tenors. Rates of 7.15-8% are among the lowest seen, so customer behaviour is not expected to change much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk to FY27 disbursement target from the South monsoon or drought, and to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is early to assess; drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka, but the company lends mainly in Tier 1-2 areas. If industry slows, it could hit disbursement, and it may use LAP or construction top-ups as short-term levers.

qa_highlights.question: How will operational efficiency from Project Tejas play out in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited manual processes now automated, native AI features, auto form filling, and a digital sourcing channel expected to reach about 10% of business. Sales headcount to rise from about 90 to 150 this year without adding branch staff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate pass-through and prepayment outlook after the repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing rates rose 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 against a 25 bps repo hike, which translates to about 12-13 bps on the book. Management said a 100 bps rise could cut the rate gap by about 60 bps and reduce prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How reset timing works for bank borrowings and the loan book, and whether spread is at risk in a rising cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo-linked bank borrowings reprice from 1 November; T-bill-linked ones reset quarterly. About 87% of the floating book is on quarterly reset and 12-13% on annual, with roughly one-third repricing each on 1 November, 1 December and 1 January. Management said it will pass on hikes to protect spread and NIM.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in the H2 disbursement ramp (about INR3,500 crore per quarter) and the FY28 AUM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was INR2,600 crore against a planned INR2,500 crore, so the INR100 crore buffer was used; Q3 target is INR3,500 crore with about INR400 crore shortfall recovered in Q4. FY28 disbursement target of INR16,000 crore implies AUM growth of about 15-15.5%, with 15% described as a resultant figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity ramp for new branches and the pipeline status?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches take about 18 months (range 18-24) to reach 5 cases per staff per month. Management said sanctioned-but-not-disbursed rose about INR118 crore quarter on quarter, and that some pipeline was lost during the migration.

risks_watch: Q3 disbursement delivery against the INR3,500 crore target, and whether the INR400 crore shortfall is recovered in Q4 as guided.
Spread and NIM protection: liability cost rising about 12-13 bps on the full book against 10 bps passed on so far; management plans a next hike of about 15 bps.
Asset quality: SMA-0 uptick attributed to a daily versus month-end overdue computation change; gross NPA is expected to fall in H2 and credit cost is guided at 10 bps against about 9 bps in Q2.
Monsoon and drought risk to construction activity and demand in Maharashtra and Karnataka, plus Telangana Section 22 verification delays.
Sales channel ramp from about 90 to 150 staff (and 250 in FY28) to deliver INR1,500-1,600 crore in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1, and the digital channel target of 10%.
Liability mix: NCD pricing around 8.3-8.35% versus bank term loans at about 7.65%, and special-rate T-bill-linked borrowings that reset at varying times.
Prepayment trend (INR1,795 crore in Q2 versus INR1,857 crore in Q1) after the housing rate hike, and the NHB refinance draw (INR1,350 crore sanctioned, expected at about 6.6-6.7%).
key_quotes: The month in which the implementation has happened, the disbursements, they have dropped in that particular branches by about 70% to 75%, and then the next month, again, it pushes back and it comes back to almost 80% -90% of the old disbursement.

Basically, in terms of the demand or in terms of the business per se, there has been no change, but for the impact of the IT transformation, which is mainly on account of the understanding, or rather the change in the flow, the additional processes that have been incorporated.
We will be looking at a 20% plus growth in terms of the disbursement, which consequently should become a 13%- 14% AUM growth this year and a 15% plus AUM growth in the next year.
Basically, our endeavor will be to ensure that our NIM and spread and NIM stays protected.

Management was more hedged on the Telangana verification issue and monsoon risk ("it's a little early"), and it was evasive on the exact timing of the sales ramp and branch productivity.

511218|2026-03.headline: Shriram Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores; management guides 18% AUM growth for FY27 but will revisit after Q1.
511218|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered strong profitability, with PAT up 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores and NIM up to 8.61%, while AUM grew 14.85% YoY to INR3,02,273.75 crores. Gross Stage 3 edged up to 4.58% from 4.55% a year ago, and Stage 2 plus Stage 3 rose sequentially in CV, PV and MSME. MUFG Bank completed a preferential allotment on April 8, 2026, taking a 20% fully diluted stake, and the board recommended a final dividend of INR6 per share. Management budgets 18% AUM growth and 8.5% NIM for FY27, but said Q1 FY27 is hard to predict and it will revisit guidance after Q1, with credit cost unchanged for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is AUM growth of 18% for FY27 on AUM or disbursements, and what is the opex and credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: 18% refers to AUM growth; opex to stay around 26% to 27% cost-to-income; credit cost seen as manageable for now, to be revisited after Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 GS2 plus GS3 rise sequentially in CV, PV and MSME, and will credit cost rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail cash-flow fluctuations are normal and provisions are priced in; coverage was increased slightly; stress, if any, expected after November-December depending on fuel prices and monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the budgeted NIM and how much of the cost-of-funds benefit goes to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM budgeted at 8.5%; management aims to protect NIM and pass on benefit only if needed for growth; NIM will expand in practice, though the budget is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did used PV financing slow in Q4, and what is the PV growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the slowdown to focus on CV and expects PV growth above 20% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What share of disbursements is new vehicle financing and how will it scale?

qa_highlights.question: Will MUFG increase its stake before the 24-month lock-in ends?

511218|2026-06.headline: Shriram Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 59.79% YoY to INR3,444.56 crores, with NIM at 9.04% and disbursements up 19.51% YoY to INR49,974 crores.
511218|2026-06.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q1 FY27 numbers, with PAT of INR3,444.56 crores (up 59.79% YoY, up 14.3% QoQ) and NII up 33.67% YoY to INR8,055.70 crores. Growth was supported by fresh equity of about INR39,600 crores, which cut the leverage ratio to 2.14x from 3.82x in March and funded repayment of borrowings. Management reiterated the FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% but said it will reassess after Q2, and guided credit cost around 2% and operational NIM around 8.5% in the medium term. Asset quality was broadly stable, with gross Stage 3 at 4.64% against 4.58% in Q4 FY26. Management said the company will now deploy surplus liquidity into growth and return to borrowing, including securitisation, towards the end of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 18% FY27 growth guidance be raised?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for asset quality in gold and MSME?

511218|2026-09.headline: Shriram Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 59.37% YoY to INR3,677.03 crores, with NIM at 9.52% and gross Stage 3 at 4.65%.
511218|2026-09.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q2 FY27 earnings, with disbursements up 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crores and AUM up 16.96% YoY to INR3,29,021.72 crores. Net interest income rose to INR8,661.04 crores and NIM expanded to 9.52%, which management attributed partly to temporary capital-driven benefits. Asset quality weakened, with gross Stage 3 at 4.65% (4.64% in Q1) and credit cost at 2.03%, which management linked to weak monsoon and drought-prone geographies. Management trimmed AUM growth guidance to 15-17% from 18%, and said credit cost would be elevated by about 30-40 bps for one or two quarters.

segments.commentary: Gold disbursements were INR5,443 crores in Q2 versus INR5,153 crores in Q1. AUM is about INR9,000 crores, and LTV is about 72-73%.
