segments.commentary: Disbursements have rebounded, but Stage 2 and Stage 3 ratios rose. Management said absolute gross Stage 3 fell to INR862 crores from INR874 crores QoQ, and gross Stage 2 is INR963 crores versus INR953 crores, so the rise is a denominator effect.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Liability mix is public deposits 31%, NCDs 15.71%, ECB and bonds 16.5%, bank and institutional borrowing 21%, and securitisation 14%, out of total liabilities of INR2,36,271 crores. Management said about INR27,000 crores was raised in the quarter, and liquidity was brought down to about 3 months of future liabilities.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth for FY27 is now expected at 15-17%, down from the earlier 18% guidance; Q1 growth was about 15% and Q2 about 17%.
Credit cost guidance is about 2% long term. Management said it may run 30-40 bps higher in select geographies and products for one or two quarters, and the full-year figure would be lower than 2.3%.
NIM is expected to stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to around 9% in the medium term and about 8.5% in the long term.

Incremental cost of funds is expected to stay below 8%, potentially rising to about 8.35% if rates or capital market yields rise. Management does not expect the overall liability cost to rise from 8.4%.
Cost to income is guided to about 25% in the medium to long term, with technology spend likely to add to opex.
Gold loan target is unchanged: double the gold book in three years, from about 2.5% to about 5% of the book.

Insurance commission income of about INR350 crores in FY26 could fall by about INR100 crores if the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines are adopted, which management called immaterial to the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Liquidity has been drawn down to about 3 months of future liabilities, with cash plus investments falling from about INR38,000 crores to about INR31,000-32,000 crores. Future AUM growth will now largely need fresh borrowing rather than surplus liquidity.
Borrowing programme has resumed, with bonds and bank borrowing back to pre-March levels. Liquidity coverage ratio is 303%.
demand_pricing: Macro: Q1 FY27 GDP grew 7.8%, and the IMF raised its FY27 forecast to 7%. Retail CPI rose to 5.54% in September, and the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5% with a calibrated tightening stance.

Rural and auto demand: the Q2 passenger vehicle sales growth was 30.7%, two-wheelers 15.2%, and commercial vehicles 28.7%. The monsoon was 87% of LPA, and 51.2% of India's area was abnormally dry or worse as of September 23.
Stress is concentrated in drought-prone states such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana. Management said it is cautious there but sees no widespread problem.
New versus used vehicle yield differential is 200-400 bps, depending on the segment.
Management said fresh loans can be repriced, but the existing fixed-rate book cannot be repriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Stage 2 and Stage 3 increase across construction equipment, gold and MSME, and what credit cost is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonal weakness and certain geographies with lower rainfall, and said it is not widespread. Credit cost guidance stays at about 2%, with a possible 30 bps temporary increase in select areas. Loan-book Stage 3 is about 2.3%, not 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM and cost of funds evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM is elevated temporarily from capital infusion and will stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to about 9% medium term and about 8.5% long term. Incremental cost of funds is expected below 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AUM growth guidance lower, and are credit filters being tightened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided to 15-17% because of the West Asia war and weak monsoon, and said credit filters are unchanged unless the economy slows. Rural demand was strong in the last two quarters, and caution has only been applied to drought-prone areas in the last month.

qa_highlights.question: Are gold loan stress levels a sign of industry-level problems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is mainly from the new EMI and interest-servicing gold products, where customers used to bullet repayment are paying late, and it sees no industry-level challenge. The gold growth plan is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission was about INR350 crores in FY26, and the proposed guidelines could cut about INR100 crores. Management said this is not material to the balance sheet and expects IRDA to revise the rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex growth stay benign, and what is the medium-term cost-to-income target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included annual back-office bonuses, so Q2 staff costs normalised. The medium to long-term cost-to-income target is about 25%, with added technology spend as a risk.

511243|2026-06.headline: Chola Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR29,612 crore and AUM 23% to INR2,54,392 crore, with net credit cost down to 1.5% from 1.8%.
511243|2026-06.overview: Cholamandalam reported Q1 FY27 aggregate disbursements of INR29,612 crore (up 22% YoY) and AUM of INR2,54,392 crore (up 23%). Net credit cost fell to 1.5% from 1.8% a year ago, NIM rose 42 bps YoY and ROA reached 3.7% versus 3.1%. Gross Stage 3 rose QoQ seasonally (about 25 bps, per management), and the company changed its disbursement recognition to cheque debit date, which depresses reported disbursement growth this quarter. Management reiterated 22-23% growth and 1.5% credit cost guidance for FY27, and kept the INR200 crore management overlay intact.

511523|2026-09.headline: Veerhealth Care targets ~Rs 100 crore FY27 turnover and Rs 5-6 crore PAT after Q1 FY27 revenue of ~Rs 25 crore and PAT of Rs 1.25 crore.

511742|2026-03.headline: UGRO Capital says Q4 FY26 net total income rose 51% YoY to a figure not stated in the call, with GNPA at 2.5%, cost of borrowings at 10.16%, and FY27 opex guided to INR 490-500 crores.
511742|2026-03.overview: UGRO Capital's first full quarter of its February 2026 structural realignment saw AUM broadly flat QoQ as the non-focus intermediated (DSA-led Prime) book runs down and focus verticals (EM-LAP and embedded finance) grow; focus share rose from 33% to 38% of AUM. Net total income grew 51% YoY and 34% QoQ, and PAT grew 26% YoY, after a one-time restructuring cost of about INR 25 crores. Management reiterated five FY29 commitments (85% focus-vertical AUM, INR 220 crore cost takeout, 15-20% annual Prime run-down, no new equity, ROA of 3-3.5%), and said FY27 is a transition year with only marginal ROA improvement. Q&A focused on growth outlook, co-lending exit, embedded-finance credit quality and the Profectus acquisition economics. Note: the call's Q4 net total income level and total PAT were not stated in the transcript.

financial_highlights.change: down 45 bps YoY; fifth consecutive quarterly improvement
one-time restructuring cost INR 25 crores (INR 25.4 crores per slide)

financial_highlights.value: INR 72 crores, 1.9% of average AUM annualised

financial_highlights.change: GNPA up from 2.2% QoQ, attributed to denominator effect

segments.name: Emerging Market LAP
segments.commentary: AUM INR 3,581 crores in Q4 with GNPA 1.2%; 317-318 branches across 13 states (up from 127 in FY24); vintage branches (>12 months) at INR 68 lakh/month disbursement vs ~INR 80 lakh target, with ~156 sub-six-month branches queued.

segments.name: Embedded finance (MyShubhLife)
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,280 crores, up 27% QoQ and 6x in 15 months; GNPA 1.7%; ~2.5 lakh active merchants; yields 24-26%; average ticket ~INR 1 lakh, daily EMI, one-year tenor.

segments.name: Prime intermediated (DSA-led, run-down)
segments.commentary: Being run down at 15-20% annually; co-lending and DA income INR 155 crores in Q4 (about 25% of total income), expected to taper from FY28. Profectus school financing book (~13% yield) being replaced by smaller Tier 2-4 school loans at 16-17%.

segments.name: Secured book overall
segments.commentary: Secured portfolio including machinery loans about 67% of total AUM with GNPA ~1.5%; unsecured (embedded plus business loans) capped at 30-35% of portfolio per management.

guidance_outlook: Combined opex (UGRO plus Profectus) to fall from ~INR 750 crores to INR 490-500 crores in FY27, described as a one-time takeout of ~INR 220 crores with no further opex increases.
AUM expected flattish in FY27 with uptick thereafter; focus verticals growing ~25% CAGR while the Prime book runs down 15-20% annually.
FY27 is a transition year with marginally better ROA than FY26; step-up expected in FY28-FY29, targeting ROA of 3-3.5% by FY29.
Credit cost expected in the zone of just under 2%, not more.
Cost of borrowing to keep improving; each 25 bps reduction worth INR 35-40 crores annualised; more ECBs planned, which land at ~9.5-10% INR-equivalent after hedging.
No incremental equity required through FY29; growth funded by internal accruals. Internal assessment points to a likely credit rating upgrade next year (A+ outlook positive).
capex_capacity: EM-LAP network at 317-318 branches across 13 states; no new branch investment planned, with focus on productivity per branch (target INR 60-70 lakh per month per branch in FY27 per management).
Profectus overlap: present in about 28 locations; one branch retained per location, with some Profectus and some UGRO branches vacated.
Infrastructure build-out for EM-LAP complete; all opex for branch expansion already incurred over the last two-three years.
Profectus acquisition: paid ~INR 1,400 crores cash for ~INR 1,200 crores net worth company; management expects ~INR 150 crores profit in year one.
demand_pricing: EM-LAP targets micro-SMEs with turnover under INR 3 crores (median ~INR 1 crore), secured loans of INR 7.5-50 lakh in Tier 2-4 towns; prior intermediated Prime LAP yielded ~13-15% and business loans ~18-19%, versus ~26% on embedded.
Management expects yields to face downward pressure over time, especially in intermediated Prime; sees EM-LAP as less exposed due to a fragmented market and branch-network differentiation.

Co-lending exit rationale: bank-linked co-lending assets are lower-yielding; management cites a 1% margin example after cost of borrowing and credit cost. Co-lending will continue but shrink as a share of income.
Embedded-finance GNPA at 1.7% vs 4-4.5% projected at product design; 6 cohorts have completed lifecycle. Credit cost for embedded about 1.5-1.6%, roughly 70-80% of GNPA.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit the intermediated book, which was ~70% of AUM, and why stop co-lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower-yield DSA book lacked pricing advantage given cost of borrowing did not fall as expected; co-lending income is volatile and does not accrete to net worth; co-lending will continue but shrink. Secured EM-LAP has credit cost in the same band despite higher GNPA.

qa_highlights.question: Will AUM grow? Growth is slowing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 AUM is flattish with a pickup after; focus verticals grow ~25% CAGR (INR ~3,500 crores and ~INR 2,000 crores segments) while ~INR 10,000 crores runs down. Priority is bottom-line over scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Profectus given the planned shift to higher yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Profectus (INR ~180 crore cost base) was used to rationalise opex; the acquired portfolio generates cash profit that supports the new branch network, and the deal is ROE-accretive by ~10%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of rising NPAs and credit cost given flat AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cost will stay below ~2%. Repossessed asset resolution takes 12-15 months; 40-50% of cases settle after court order; recovery cost ~1%, with no principal loss so far.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex fall and how does the Profectus branch rationalisation flow through?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined opex falls to INR 490-500 crores from INR 750 crores; the INR 25 crore one-time cost has been fully provided this quarter, so savings should flow from Q1 and more from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fully diluted share count and are there remaining CCDs or warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total outstanding shares are 15.29 crore on a fully diluted basis, with 2 lakh shares pending conversion; all CCDs and warrants are matured or converted.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise ECBs when domestic borrowing is available, and is there an RBI limit?
qa_highlights.answer: No RBI cap on amount; ECBs are fully hedged and land at ~9.5-10%; DFIs are main lenders; more ECBs planned for cost and ALM benefits, with hedging cost currently higher.

risks_watch: Growth stalling: AUM flat in FY27; focus verticals must grow ~25% to offset the Prime run-down; GNPA may rise through denominator effect.
Embedded finance seasoning: management's 4-4.5% projected GNPA ceiling is well above current 1.7%, but only six cohorts have completed their lifecycle.
Yield compression in EM-LAP and embedded finance as competition emerges; management acknowledges downward pressure.
Execution of INR 490-500 crore opex target and whether savings flow from Q1-Q2 FY27 given notice-period costs.
Track the five FY29 commitments quarterly: focus share (38% now vs 85% target), opex ceiling, Prime run-down rate, no equity, ROA trajectory, and co-lending/DA income share (~25% of income now).

AUM is broadly flat quarter -on-quarter. That is intentional.
So total outstanding share should be INR 15.29 crores, yes.

511742|2026-06.headline: UGRO Q1 FY27: total AUM INR 15,013 crore and disbursements INR 2,551 crore (+59% YoY); opex cut to ~INR 119 crore from INR 217 crore in Q4.
511742|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 reflected the completed shift toward Emerging Market LAP and Embedded Merchant Finance (GROx), which together reached 46% of AUM versus 32% in Dec '25. Interest income fell 13% QoQ to INR 363 crore as co-lending and direct assignment income dropped to INR 75 crore from INR 155 crore, though it grew 19% YoY. Quarterly opex fell 42% QoQ to ~INR 119 crore, and reported PAT was lifted by a one-time deferred tax reversal from the move to the new tax regime (pre-tax ROA 2.6% vs reported 2.8%). Management guided AUM flat for FY27 with on-balance-sheet assets growing, and said growth can be funded without incremental equity through FY29. Q&A focused on runoff, GNPA trajectory, the Profectus merger and the weak share price.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked how much of the sequential interest income decline was old-book reversal versus disbursement timing, and when interest income would recover to Q4 levels.
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the decline on the call and promised to revert. It said Q1 is the base, interest income should rise sequentially as on-book assets grow, opex stays flat from Q1 run-rate, and co-lending/DA income stays in the current range during the transition year.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked whether the ROA path of 3-3.5% is on reported or normalised basis, given the tax reversal.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA adjusted for the one-time tax reversal is about 2.1%, and the 3-3.5% trajectory is built off that base.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked whether the EM LAP GNPA rise (1.2% to 2.1%) and Embedded GNPA rise (1.7% to 2.1%) were running ahead of the model, and whether the 1.5-2% EM LAP credit cost guidance holds.
qa_highlights.answer: Anuj Pandey said peak EM LAP delinquency is projected at 3.5-4% once average months on book pass 18 (currently ~15), settling at 3-3.5%; Embedded Finance peak should not exceed 3%. Shachindra Nath reiterated the 1.5-2% EM LAP credit cost guidance and said GNPA may rise to 3.5% without credit cost rising proportionately.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked about the Profectus merger timeline and post-merger capital adequacy.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said completion is targeted by end-Q3 FY27 if fortunate, and before Q4 FY27 at the latest. CFO said standalone CRAR is 21% and merged-basis CRAR should be about 23-24%, not the 27-28% suggested.

qa_highlights.question: Rishi asked whether the Prime/DSA book could be sold in one block, as Profectus was acquired.
qa_highlights.answer: Anuj Pandey said no: portfolio sales need 6 months' vintage, collection infrastructure would become uneconomic, negative carry on excess cash, and a large income reversal on the off-balance-sheet component. Run-off will remain the standard explanation for another 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Rishi asked about dividends and buybacks, given cash on hand and ~INR 300 crore expected FY27 profit.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buybacks are not possible for NBFCs under Companies Act leverage limits (2x). Dividend policy would need an RBI-compliant change and shareholder approval; FY27 profit includes assignment income, and the final call comes in Q3/Q4 FY27, with capital most likely retained for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Kamal asked about the main execution risks beyond the next two quarters, including the sub-2% GNPA thesis, opex and profitability.
qa_highlights.answer: Shachindra Nath pointed to Slide 21 productivity inflection and said the 145 branches under 6 months must reach INR 75-80 lakh monthly disbursement after 12 months. Other risks: larger-ticket, longer-tenure Embedded loans raising credit risk, and faster Prime runoff from competitors reducing income.

511754|2026-03.headline: Shalibhadra Finance FY26 AUM rose 25% to ₹220 crore and PAT grew 21.67% to ₹19.48 crore; FY29 target is ₹500 crore AUM.
511754|2026-03.overview: Management hosted its inaugural earnings call covering Q4 and FY26. AUM closed FY26 at ₹220 crore (up 25% from ₹176 crore), PAT rose 21.67% YoY to ₹19.48 crore, with ROA of 8.65% and ROE of 11.33%. GNPA stood at 2.94%, CRAR at 78.28%, and net worth at ₹172 crore. The company is moving from two-wheeler and vehicle finance into micro-LAP, LAP and home loans under its "Shalibhadra 2.0" strategy, with a branch expansion from 61 toward 100 branches. Management guided to lower ROA (about 7% within two to three years) and a rising share of nationalised bank borrowing to cut funding costs.

segments.commentary: Newer products cross-sold to existing customers; about 40% of new loans go to existing customers, drawn from roughly 5 lakh credit-worthy customers.

Technology investment in proprietary LOS and LMS platforms; management says underwriting is almost 100% automated.
Management says no branch has been closed; underperforming branches can take two to three years to mature.

Yield on advances fell from 25.4% (FY24) to 20.8% (FY26), attributed to competition from new entrants, a market-wide decline in lending rates and lower pricing for customers with good bureau scores.

Management sees large rural demand (about 70% of the population in rural areas) with few lenders.
Monthly OEM sales data is used to choose branch locations and to grow AUM at existing branches.

qa_highlights.answer: Current two-wheeler credit cost is about 2%; mortgage loans are expected at about 1% because property is immovable and easier to repossess.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the book comes from repeat borrowers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of new loans and about 40% of AUM are to existing customers, drawn from roughly 5 lakh credit-worthy customers.

qa_highlights.answer: ROA is 8.65% now and is expected to fall to about 7% in two to three years as higher-ticket products rise.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company bring down its cost of funds, given the 12% NCD?
qa_highlights.answer: The 12% coupon was the first NCD issue; costs are expected to fall as the company gains experience and the nationalised bank share rises (lending at about 10-10.5%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the branch rollout schedule and capex per branch?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 70 branches by calendar 2026, 75 by year-end, 85 next year, and 100 by FY29; capex is about ₹20 lakh per branch with breakeven in 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cites competition from new entrants, lower market lending rates, and discounted rates for customers with good credit bureau scores.

Spread compression from new entrants and falling yields; ROA guided down from 8.65% toward 7%.
Funding concentration and cost: borrowings are only about ₹50 crore, and the NCD was raised at 12% against a stated cost of funds of about 11%.
Execution of the branch ramp (61 to 100) into new states such as Karnataka and Goa where brand recall is absent.
New-product credit performance in LAP and home loans, which lack operating history at the company; management targets NNPA around 1% for the next two to three years.
Rate-cycle exposure: an RBI hike would raise borrowing costs while lending rates stay fixed.

512008|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹282.88 crore, up about 29% YoY, and EBITDA was ₹122.96 crore, up about 20% YoY at a 43.5% margin. PAT grew about 52% YoY to ₹70.85 crore, helped by lower finance cost, which management attributed to rationalised borrowing costs. Leasing remained the largest segment at ₹153.91 crore revenue, while Design & Build and Furniture grew strongly YoY but Design & Build fell sequentially from about ₹120 crore in Q4. Analysts pressed on sequential EBITDA decline (down about 14% QoQ), Furniture margin compression, and the planned demerger/restructuring.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY (from ₹219.62 crore); down about 3% QoQ per analyst
+20% YoY (from ₹102.16 crore); down about 14% QoQ per analyst

segments.name: Leasing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹153.91 crore (+26% YoY from ₹122.18 crore); segment result ₹64.33 crore. Managed workspace across 25 cities with over 84,000 total seats and over 68,000 billed seats.

segments.name: Design & Build
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹100.39 crore (vs ₹84.69 crore in Q1 FY26, about +19% YoY); segment result ₹33.84 crore. Order book above ₹228 crore, with management saying over 85% is external third-party work.

segments.name: Furniture (Ek Design)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹28.57 crore (+124% YoY from ₹12.75 crore); segment result only ₹2.10 crore, a thin margin of about 7%. Order book about ₹53 crore; over 2,200 SKUs and over 75,000 units delivered to date.

guidance_outlook: Management is 100% confident of adding 18,000-20,000 billable seats in Leasing this fiscal year.
Design & Build targeted at roughly 50% YoY growth for FY27, which management says is backed by the existing order book.
Furniture expected to deliver similar growth; management expects EBITDA above 25% in the vertical at optimal capacity utilisation (60-70%), targeted by end of this year.
Margins are described as stable to improving, with no specific consolidated margin guidance given.
Demerger/restructuring: all subsidiaries to consolidate under EFC (I) Ltd, with EFC Ltd merged in and an asset-holding company kept as a wholly owned subsidiary; no timeline given on the call.
capex_capacity: Managed workspace capacity: over 84,000 total seats and over 68,000 billed seats across 25 cities; more inventory under development without revenue commitment.
Asset monetisation model: acquires vacant assets (about 10 years old), refurbishes and leases them via managed office, capturing rental yield and grade-upgrade appreciation.
Fit-out payback is about 18-20 months per seat on a ₹50,000 per-seat cost, which management says is standard across cities and funded mainly by landlords.
Furniture plant is still scaling; management says optimal utilisation is 60-70% and expects to approach it by end of FY27.
Borrowings are mainly LAP and LRD facilities tied to acquired assets; management says borrowing costs have been rationalised.
demand_pricing: Average occupancy stated at 90%+ and enterprise retention at about 95%+ (churn 4-5%); average enterprise client tenure rose to 51 months.
Enterprise demand from GCCs, MNCs, BFSI, technology, consulting and outsourcing firms.

D&B order book rose to over ₹228 crore from ₹135 crore at end of Q4 FY26, with over ₹100 crore of Q4 orders already executed. Management says Q1 is seasonally slow and projects typically ramp in Q3-Q4.
Competition named on the call: Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India, IndiQube and large landlords; management cites price, speed of execution, design and fit-out cost optimisation as differentiators.
Management says supply-chain and material-price disruptions persist but have not stopped YoY growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the D&B (₹228 crore) and Furniture (₹53 crore) order books is third-party versus internal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 85% is from external clients, since most internal fit-out work is already done by landlords.

qa_highlights.question: Why did D&B revenue fall from about ₹120 crore in Q4 to about ₹100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said D&B is project-based with no seasonality; Q1 is typically slow, and projects ramp in Q3-Q4. It reiterated a roughly 50% YoY growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Furniture revenue rose 36% QoQ but segment margin fell from about 75% to about 7%; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing was wrong and that the business is still below optimal utilisation. It expects a stabilised EBITDA above 25% at 60-70% utilisation, and said QoQ margin comparison is not meaningful yet.

qa_highlights.question: Occupancy, retention and seat addition guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy is 90%+, retention about 95%+, and 18,000-20,000 billable seat additions are targeted with full confidence.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT rise while revenue and EBITDA fell QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the EBITDA dip to Ind AS accounting effects and pointed to PAT as the better measure. It cited lower borrowing costs, cost control, and Leasing performance.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates EFC against Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India and IndiQube, and what is the city mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the integrated real-estate-as-a-service model, three revenue streams, economies of scale, design and fit-out cost optimisation. It said the West is strongest; North and South are each above 15%; focus cities are 10 (3 North, 3 South, 3 West, plus Kolkata).

risks_watch: Sequential decline: revenue down about 3% and EBITDA down about 14% QoQ, with Design & Build lower than Q4; D&B growth depends on Q3-Q4 project ramp-up.
Furniture segment margin of about 7% in Q1 versus 25%+ target; sustainability depends on reaching 60-70% utilisation.
Reported PAT growth is driven partly by lower finance costs; watch interest cost and LAP/LRD leverage as asset-monetisation capex grows.
Demerger/restructuring details (timeline, tax treatment, accounting impact) were not specified and need follow-up.
Competitive intensity from Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India, IndiQube and landlords; supply-chain and material-price pressures on D&B.
key_quotes: There's nothing wrong in the Furniture segment.
The EBITDA reduction is primarily because of the way the Ind AS accounting works.
100% confident on kind of adding about 18,000 to 20,000 billable seats on the Leasing business.
There's no seasonality, which is kind of affecting this business.
512008|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book visibility and the 50% D&B and 18,000-20,000 seat targets, but defensive on the sequential decline, Furniture margin (about 7%) and the EBITDA dip, which management attributed to Ind AS effects and pointed to PAT instead. Restructuring answers were high-level, with no timeline or accounting detail given.

512068|2026-03.headline: Deccan Gold turned debt-free after Rs.315 Cr rights issue; Jonnagiri gold sales and Geomysore profit flowed in, but Kyrgyz project needs Rs.60-100 Cr more.
512068|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a defining quarter: Rs.315 Cr rights issue used to repay about Rs.219 Cr of debt, leaving the company debt-free by end-March. The associate Geomysore (26% stake, Jonnagiri gold project) began selling refined gold and reported profit, which management said flowed into Deccan's books. Kyrgyzstan (60%) gravity circuit is commissioned, with Merrill-Crowe/leach circuit targeted for June-July and full-scale commercial production in August 2026. Management disclosed a funding gap after Rs.55 Cr was diverted to Geomysore's rights issue, and said it is talking to promoter-linked investors for Rs.60-100 Cr; an EGM on related-party transactions is scheduled. Bhalukona nickel-copper-PGE drilling is showing wide mineralised intersections, with mining lease application targeted by April 2027.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.219 Cr (largely Hira Group and Godavari Power & Ispat)
About Rs.31 Cr: interest income Rs.18.3 Cr plus currency exchange gain balance

financial_highlights.metric: Jonnagiri gold production March and April 2026
Jonnagiri refined gold produced to end-March 2026

financial_highlights.value: About Rs.3,000 per gram vs market about Rs.16,000 per gram

segments.name: Jonnagiri (Geomysore, 26%)
segments.commentary: Open pit operating at 1,000 tpd licence capacity (about 300,000 tpa), recovery above 90%; FY27 production guided at about 600 kg, FY28 about 800 kg-1 t; FY27 revenue about Rs.900 Cr, EBITDA about Rs.630 Cr, PAT about Rs.470 Cr, with Deccan's 26% share about Rs.120 Cr, though management expects no dividend in FY27.

segments.name: Altyn Tor, Kyrgyzstan (60%, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Gravity concentrate production started; Merrill-Crowe and leach circuit to produce doré from June, full commercial production by August 2026. FY27 production guided at about 160 kg and FY28 at 300-350 kg; FY27 revenue about Rs.300 Cr, PAT about Rs.100 Cr (Deccan share about Rs.60 Cr). Processes about 1.6 Mt tailings and low-grade stockpiles (about 1-1.1 g/t) for about four years; 17% revenue share with Kyrgyzaltyn and 5% royalty to government.

segments.name: Bhalukona, Chhattisgarh (100%, nickel-copper-PGE)
segments.commentary: Seven diamond holes, 1,200 m drilled; first hole intersected about 30 m of sulphide mineralisation (about 0.4% Ni), including 2.6 m at 1.01% Ni, 0.29% Cu and 0.2 g/t Pd. Management's indicative resource is 75,000-80,000 t nickel-equivalent and about 7-8 t gold-equivalent, unverified.

segments.name: Ganajur (Karnataka)
segments.commentary: Gold deposit under litigation (High Court and Supreme Court, Indocil case); no ruling in the quarter. Management said timeline to production is about 2.5-3 years if the case is won.

segments.name: Gold-tungsten-tin, Spain (Logrosan)
segments.commentary: MoU to acquire 51% for EUR1.76 million with rights to go to 95%; 4 holes and about 1,500 m drilled, assays pending about 1-2 weeks. Earlier historic hole: 1 m at 96.2 g/t Au.

segments.name: Kalevala Gold, Finland
segments.commentary: Three projects (Syrjala about 2 Mt resource targeted to 4 t, Pahkalampi about 2 t at 3.5 g/t, 4P undrilled); company can go to 51%. Little work done this year due to funding constraints.

segments.name: Mozambique and Tanzania
segments.commentary: Mozambique lithium-tantalum surface targets identified, drilling deferred for lack of funds. Tanzania: three of five tenements relinquished, exploration focus reduced.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated targets (at current prices): Jonnagiri about 600 kg, Kyrgyzstan about 160 kg; FY28 Jonnagiri about 800 kg-1 t, Kyrgyzstan 300-350 kg.
Kyrgyzstan full-scale commercial production by August 2026; plant inauguration pencilled for 15 or 31 August.
Management funding need: at least Rs.60 Cr (outer limit Rs.100 Cr) for Kyrgyzstan; Rs.400-500 Cr for Bhalukona processing plant; Rs.800-1,000 Cr aggregate across projects in the next year or so.
Bhalukona mining lease application due by about April 2027; Spain mining lease application by October-November 2026.
2030 vision: Jonnagiri 1 tpa, Altyn Tor 700-800 kg, first Indian nickel-copper-PGE mine, and two to three gold mines plus critical minerals in production.
capex_capacity: Jonnagiri 1,000 tpd plant capex about Rs.350-400 Cr; Bhalukona processing plant about Rs.400 Cr; Spain about Rs.500 Cr (Finland underground would need more).
Kyrgyzstan underground development (decline) estimated at Rs.50-100 Cr, starting after three to four years, to be funded from internal accruals per management.
Jonnagiri expansion beyond 2,000 tpd needs public hearing and permits; clarity expected in 6-8 months, reflected in FY28 numbers.
Kyrgyzstan revised resource estimate to state reserve company by end-June; revised mine design and life-of-mine plan by August 2026.
Bhalukona: 2,000-3,000 tpd plant potentially, 15-year life, if resource is proven to 200 m depth.
demand_pricing: Model assumptions: gold about Rs.15,000/g for Jonnagiri and about $4,000/oz for Kyrgyzstan, a discount to spot. Management said there is no hedging policy.
Royalties: Jonnagiri pays 4% to Andhra Pradesh plus 1.28% (DMF and NMET), about 5.28% of top line; Kyrgyzstan 5% royalty plus 17% revenue share to Kyrgyzaltyn.
Jonnagiri refined 999 gold sold to bullion refiners and jewellers at IBJA price; Kyrgyz doré must be sold to National Bank (right of first refusal) at LBMA price less refining charges.
Bhalukona concentrate expected to be sold to smelters (Adani or Vedanta named); management said crude-price impact on Kyrgyz costs is under 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income so high and what is its breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs.18.3 Cr is interest income on the Kyrgyz loan at 15% and the balance is currency exchange gain, totalling about Rs.31 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the Rs.100 Cr needed in the next three months, and can it come from internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.100 Cr is an outer limit; actual need is about Rs.60 Cr over two to three years. Geomysore dividends may not come in FY27, so the company is talking to promoter-linked investors for debt or equity.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the promoters providing funds, and is any promoter selling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funding is from key promoter-group investors and an Australian promoter; Yandal Investments (about 10%) and Halcyon (about 5%) are not selling, with sales coming from retail promoter-group holders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Bhalukona mining lease and what could be the next production asset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mining lease application is due by about April 2027, with plant design then and production possibly around 2029; Bhalukona is the next candidate, with Spain also filing by Oct-Nov 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is an FPO or preferential issue planned and is the team ready?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has been in touch with merchant bankers and FPO planning would follow the present projects; it committed to nothing specific on timing.

risks_watch: Kyrgyz funding gap of Rs.60-100 Cr must close before winter construction; a bank transfer delay of a month would push completion months later.
Ganajur litigation outcome is unresolved; management is pursuing government policy routes.
Geomysore dividends not expected in FY27, so Deccan's Rs.120 Cr PAT share may not translate into cash; Kyrgyz loan repayments with 15% interest depend on production starting.
Bhalukona and Spain drill assays are pending and the Bhalukona resource figures are management's own geological estimates, not a JORC resource.
Gold price assumptions are below spot, but there is no hedging policy; a sharp fall in gold prices would hit revenue projections directly.
Management confirmed that Jonnagiri's FY27 revenue and profit forecasts assume about 600 kg; delays have occurred in past timelines.
512068|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on project potential (Bhalukona described as a personal favourite, Jonnagiri as transformational), but cautious on funding and timelines, repeatedly saying figures are indicative and not committing to dates. Evasive on several questions: no concrete answer on Geomysore IPO or reverse merger, and deferred the FPO question to after project milestones.
key_quotes: One of our associate companies that is Geomysore has recorded a profit and we could show some profit as a 26% shareholder of that Company.
We repaid all the debt that is about Rs.219 crores.
So we require up to Rs.100 Crores at least minimum Rs.60 Crores we require to complete that Kyrgyz project.
So by next April, we have to submit the mining lease application.
Rs.100 Crores is the completely outer limit that we are taking in case of any emergencies, but the actual requirement is around Rs.60 Crores.

512068|2026-06.headline: Deccan Gold Q1 FY27: Jonnagiri sold 59 kg gold for ~Rs87 Cr revenue, Rs6.35 Cr share of PAT; Rs137 Cr fundraise approved by Board.
512068|2026-06.overview: Management said the June quarter established the company as a producer, led by Jonnagiri (Geomysore Services) gold production and first dore output from Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan). Jonnagiri sold about 59 kg of gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT, of which Deccan's share was Rs6.35 Cr; about 80 kg of gold equivalent sits in inventory. Management framed the company as having two verticals, gold and battery-metal critical minerals, and said Rs137 Cr of CCDs, equity and warrants is pending shareholder approval. Management said the next quarter should be much bigger, but margins were low in Q1 and the company asked for another quarter before giving clearer guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Gold inventory at quarter end (incl. dore)
financial_highlights.value: About 80 kg gold equivalent (40 kg gold + 60 kg dore)
Rs137 Cr via CCDs, equity shares and warrants

segments.name: Jonnagiri (Geomysore, gold, India)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales of 59 kg gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT; Deccan's share Rs6.35 Cr. Production about 1 kg/day, with 2,500 tpd expansion planned, targeting up to 2 tonnes/yr around FY29-30.

segments.name: Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan, gold)
segments.commentary: Dore production started via Merrill-Crowe; gravity circuit and leach circuit added. Full-scale commissioning expected soon; tailings of about 0.6 Mt at about 1.3 g/t for first 4-5 years of output.

segments.name: Kalevala (Finland, gold)
segments.commentary: Drilling to start around Sept 15; about 1,500 m planned. Kuikka mining lease pending; feasibility targeted in 2027; production seen 2028-29 or later with about 800 tpd plant.

segments.name: Critical minerals (Chhattisgarh nickel-copper-PGE, Bhalukona)
segments.commentary: 2,500 m drilled, 1.3 km mineralised zone identified; resource estimate and mining lease application targeted next year; 3,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Logrosan tungsten (Spain)
segments.commentary: About 3,000 m drilled; full Dehesa results expected mid-September, resource model by early October; 1,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Mozambique lithium-tantalum
segments.commentary: About 150 sq km, three licences; 200 tpd concentrator targeted by end-2027 or Q1 2028 for concentrate.

guidance_outlook: Jonnagiri FY27 production 500-600 kg (earlier guidance retained); FY28 750-800 kg. Management will confirm after next quarter.
Altyn Tor: about 150-160 kg in FY27 and 300-350 kg thereafter, per management comments.
Jonnagiri EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters; Q1 margins were significantly lower.
Altyn Tor revised mine design and life-of-mine plan by October 2026; underground resource above 5 Mt could extend mine life by 6-7 years.
Dividend from Geomysore unlikely in FY27 per management; may come next year, not guaranteed.
Capex: about Rs400-500 Cr per 1,000 tpd plant; Bhalukona 3,000 tpd about Rs650-700 Cr; Altyn Tor underground Rs150-200 Cr in 3-4 years; Jonnagiri shaft work possibly above Rs400 Cr in 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Jonnagiri processing approvals of 1,010 tpd, with expansion to 2,500 tpd being sought; Bhumi Puja done for expansion.
Altyn Tor leach circuit and new tailings dam (10-year life) under construction; commissioning date to be announced after Chairman-level visit next week.
Finland: about 1,500 m drilling from mid-September; Kuikka pit targets about 70 kg gold; underground mines planned.
Chhattisgarh: 15th drill hole under way; plan 3,000 tpd plant; process flow sheet by mid-next-year.
Spain: Dehesa first-phase drilling complete; Maria drilling from end of this month; 40 sq km Maria licence plus 30 sq km pending.
Mozambique: 1,500-2,000 m drilling from September; 200 tpd concentrator by end-2027.
demand_pricing: Management said gold price in Q1 was about Rs1,50,000 per 10 grams and improved in the current quarter, supporting holding inventory.
Tungsten prices up 622% and tantalum up 196% over the last year; lithium up 108%; graphite up 5% (management figures).
Management plans to sell Jonnagiri stock in the coming quarter; Q1 sales lagged production because the inauguration was on June 24.
Dore from Jonnagiri is refined in-house at a small refinery (cost about Rs4-5 Cr); Altyn Tor dore must go to a government refinery at LBMA price.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Jonnagiri profit margin well below the expected ~65% EBITDA, and what is the outlook for Jonnagiri and Kyrgyzstan revenue and profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low Q1 sales (59 kg) and initial expenses explain the low margin; 65-70% EBITDA margin expected in one to two quarters. Further clarity expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex estimate and funding plan for the project pipeline (about Rs2,000 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than Rs1,000 Cr is needed for the next two or three projects; funding via offtake arrangements for critical minerals, combined debt and equity; gold projects possibly 50:50 or 40:60 equity to debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhalukona be funded by a rights issue like the earlier Rs80 per share issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm a specific route; said the Rs137 Cr raise is a bridge and a larger QIP may follow once drilling outcomes are clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hutti Gold and Ganajur progress, and what is the legal position?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganajur is a mining lease with court proceedings pending; management cited recent judgments on restoring pre-2015 rights. Hutti is a prospecting licence, so it is more tedious; focus remains on Ganajur.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be dividends from Jonnagiri, and is a strategic promoter being sought?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend depends on Geomysore board; management doubts dividends this financial year. No decision yet on a large strategic promoter; the company remains professionally run.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not refine dore in Kyrgyzstan?
qa_highlights.answer: Kyrgyz law requires dore to be sent to a government refinery, which settles at LBMA price; no in-house refinery is possible there.

risks_watch: Jonnagiri margin normalisation: management guided EBITDA to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters, versus Q1 margins well below that; Q1 PAT of about Rs25 Cr on Rs87 Cr revenue (about 29%) is the key test next quarter.

Inventory realisation: about 80 kg gold equivalent (40 kg gold + 60 kg dore) unsold at quarter end, plus about 90 kg expected in Q2; sales timing depends on gold price and the Q1 consolidated inventory line was unchanged in P&L.

Funding gap: management cited more than Rs1,000 Cr needed for the next two to three projects (about Rs2,000 Cr overall in analyst framing), with Rs137 Cr raise subject to shareholder approval; mix of offtake, debt and equity not finalised; QIP may follow.
Ganajur court case: no regular hearing yet; outcome depends on court and on mining lease status; Hutti remains a prospecting licence.

Altyn Tor commissioning date not yet fixed (to be announced after Chairman visit next week); revised mine design and life-of-mine plan due by October 2026; Jonnagiri dividend to Deccan unlikely in FY27 per management.

Exploration catalysts due next quarter: Dehesa full results by mid-September, resource model by early October; Kalevala drilling from about 15 September; Chhattisgarh resource estimate and mining lease application next year.

I think the next quarter is going to be much bigger than this.
So, to stabilize to about 65%, 70% of EBITDA, I believe it will take another quarter or two.
Hence, I honestly, I doubt whether we get dividends in this financial year.

qa_highlights.question: Sky Park new phase: area and GDV?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarified as higher floors on Towers 1-3 under new FSI, equivalent to one new tower; total GDV about INR750 crores, with about INR200 crores sold in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Which projects complete in FY27 to drive revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunteck One World Naigaon, ODC Avenue 1 higher floors, 4th Avenue, Sunteck Pinnacle commercial and ready BKC and other inventory; management expects H2 to be strong.

risks_watch: Dubai project removed from to-be-launched GDV, with no launch visibility in the next 1-2 quarters.
Presales growth depends on H2 launches of about INR7,000 crores; H1 presales growth was 19% against a 25% full-year target.
Nepean Sea Road RERA launch before end FY27 depends on demolition and approvals; a delay would hit the uber luxury ramp-up.
Collections lag as recent sales are weighted to early-stage projects with back-ended milestones.
Borivali West had a question on the older land parcel status and a prior-quarter Mira Road GDV reclassification; management's answers on these were not fully clear.
512179|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, launch pipeline and balance sheet, with firm assurances on the 25% presales target and the Nepean Sea Road timeline. Answers were sometimes repetitive or unclear on segment-mix figures, GDV reclassifications and the Borivali parcel history.
key_quotes: We have delivered a strong first half with growth across presales, collections, cash flows, revenue and profits, sustaining the CAGR of 25% across all major operational and financial parameters over the last 5 years.
Every new acquisition must clear the same filters we have always applied, a high IRR, a high equity multiple and a minimum project level EBITDA margins of 30% to 35%.
Reported margins will continue to converge towards the embedded EBITDA margin of our presales.
we are very, very confident that our guidance or our expectation of 25% year-on-year growth in the full year of FY '27, we will be able to maintain easily.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 embedded EBITDA margin is 30% (+160 bps YoY) and management says reported margins will converge towards that 30% as projects reach revenue recognition, with H1 EBITDA up 23% to INR1.6 billion on revenue up 16% to INR5.1 billion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Borivali West is now 11.5 acres (GDV INR80 billion) and Sky Park adds floors equal to one tower (GDV about INR750 crores), but these are land and density adds rather than new plants; completions in FY27 (Naigaon, ODC Avenue 1, 4th Avenue, Pinnacle) are named without quantified capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 presales growth of 25% is reiterated against H1 presales growth of 19% (INR1,611 crores), and the H2 launch pipeline of about INR7,000 crores ex-Dubai (Belvedere Park INR1,200-1,400 crores, Andheri INR1,250-1,500 crores) must carry the gap.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management spent about INR3.9 billion (INR400 crores) on business development in H1 after INR800 crores in FY26, bought 4.5 acres outright, and has 1-2 deals at advanced stage, so further land or project commitments are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Presales growth guidance of 25% was only held, with H1 at 19%, and no upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 presales growth of 19% against a 25% full-year target depends on about INR7,000 crores of H2 launches, and Nepean Sea Road (about INR3,000 crores GDV) RERA launch before end FY27 depends on demolition and approvals; Dubai is out for at least 1-2 quarters.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management guides H2 launches of Sunteck Belvedere Park (GDV INR1,200-1,400 crores), Andheri Western Express Highway redevelopment (INR1,250-1,500 crores), Altavia Tower 2 and Nepean Sea Road before end FY27, totalling about INR7,000 crores.

rows.label: Presales sustained by H2 launch pipeline
rows.why: Q2 presales were INR824 crores and H1 INR1,611 crores (+19% YoY); a 25% full-year outcome needs the H2 launch pipeline of about INR7,000 crores to convert, and Q2 collections of INR371 crores (H1 INR780 crores) lag because sales are weighted to early-stage projects.

rows.label: Balance sheet headroom for land buying
rows.why: Net debt to equity is 0.09 and trailing 12-month cash surplus is INR6.3 billion, which supports the continued INR400-800 crore annual BD spend while keeping the 30-35% project EBITDA margin filter.

rows.label: Dubai project pushed out
rows.why: Dubai was moved from to-be-launched GDV because launch visibility is not seen in the next 1-2 quarters, so it adds nothing to the FY27 pipeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25% presales target, the INR7,000 crore H2 launch pipeline, Nepean Sea Road timing and balance sheet, but answers on segment mix, GDV reclassification and the Borivali parcel history were repetitive or unclear, and analysts pressed on those.

512296|2026-03.headline: Bhagyanagar India crossed ₹2,000 crore revenue and ₹50 crore PAT in FY26; Q4 revenue ₹735 crore, PAT ₹18.5 crore, EBITDA margin ~5%.
512296|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as a record year: revenue above ₹2,000 crore, operational EBITDA above ₹100 crore and PAT above ₹50 crore for the first time. Q4 was the best quarter of the year, with revenue of about ₹735 crore, EBITDA of about ₹36 crore and PAT of about ₹18.5 crore. Volumes rose about 34% to 24,000 tonnes, and value-added share reached about 62% by Q4 (from 52% in Q1). Management guided to roughly 5% EBITDA margin, 20% volume growth and a 25% revenue CAGR, and said the demerger into copper and real estate verticals awaits NCLT hearing on 9 June.

financial_highlights.value: About ₹36 crore EBITDA; about ₹18.5 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PAT margin ~2.5% in Q4 (2.2% in Q3)

financial_highlights.value: About ₹43 for FY26; about ₹62 in Q4

financial_highlights.change: From ₹207 crore; increase via retained earnings, no dilution
From ₹157 crore; management says proportional to revenue

segments.name: Copper value-added products
segments.commentary: Value-added share was about 62% at end of Q4 versus 52% in Q1, with a target of 66% by end of FY27. Silver- and tin-plated bus bars for data centres are new, with exports to Canada and US; management expects them to reach 7-10% of revenue in 3-5 years and about 10% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Copper recycling (backward integration)
segments.commentary: Capacity reached 35,000 tonnes this year (up from 30,000 in March 2026). Scrap sourcing from the Gulf is under 5% of input; US is the largest single source at 35%.

segments.name: Plastic and aluminium recycling (planned)
segments.commentary: Plan to invest about ₹10 crore in plastic recycling, processing cable-linked plastic into granules and aluminium into ingots; management targets 12-15 month payback. Revenue contribution expected to be small.

segments.name: Real estate (land parcels)
segments.commentary: Book value of real estate about ₹29 crore; three parcels (Nacharam ~4 acres, Upal ~4.5 acres, Hardware Park ~5 acres). Only Upal is under active consideration for development or joint development.

guidance_outlook: Maintain ~5% EBITDA margin through FY27 on a higher top line; management said 4.5-5% is a good margin for this business.
Target revenue of ₹5,000 crore for the copper company in about 3 years (around 2030), i.e. a 20-25% CAGR; the 25% growth expectation for next year is split as ~20% volume and ~5% price.
Minimum 15-20% volume growth every year.
Q1 FY27: volume marginally below Q4 but well above Q1 FY26 (Q1 FY26 revenue about ₹486 crore); EBITDA margin expected to hold near 5%.
Planned capex of about ₹40 crore over the next two years, including the ₹10 crore plastic recycling project.
Fundraise of about ₹150 crore being considered; no final modality yet; management hopes to execute in FY27.
Working capital days expected to fall 2-3 days over the year.
capex_capacity: Copper capacity at 35,000 tonnes after increase from 30,000 tonnes in March 2026, in the new 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad.
Heat recovery systems on furnaces to improve fuel efficiency and cut cycle times, going live in FY27.
About ₹40 crore capex over the next two years on capacities and new ventures; ₹10 crore for plastic recycling, to be scaled up over the next year.
Plastic recycling capacity plan reportedly from 150 to 500 (management confirmed intent to increase, sourcing only cable-linked plastic).
demand_pricing: Management expects copper consumption growth driven by EV/auto, power electrification and renewables; said India could become the second-largest copper consumer.
Pass-through of copper price to finished products is in place; additional margin pass-on is not assured and needs more value-added mix.
Management sees primary copper shortage in 3-4 years, with recycled copper filling the gap; no shortage expected for 2-3 years.

Copper price: FY26 realisation about ₹963 per kg per an analyst's figure; current copper price cited at about ₹1,300 per kg by an analyst; management assumed about 5% annual copper price rise for guidance.
Scrap availability: Gulf-origin scrap dried up due to shipping transshipment disruption; management says BIL is less affected than the industry because Gulf exposure is under 5%.
Competition: Adani and Hindalco entering recycling; management believes sourcing relationships and 40-year history provide an edge.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 growth was about 35% volume and 10% price; FY27 target is about 20% volume and 5% price, with 15-20% minimum volume growth each year.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity size and margins for silver/tin bus bars?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% EBITDA margin; contribution still very small, expected 7-10% of revenue in 3-5 years with slow ramp.

qa_highlights.question: Is copper scrap availability a concern after the Gulf disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry is affected more than BIL; Gulf is under 5% of BIL's input and US is 35%. Management expects normalisation as shipping resumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the reported promoter pledge at 96%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge was about 5% of promoter holding given to MCX for hedging, and that the exchange data is wrong; no shares pledged to banks. It also acknowledged a small personal sale in the March quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per tonne hold at ~₹62 per kg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 5% margin, which equals about ₹60-65 per kg at current copper prices; not expected to grow much faster than copper prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5,000 crore target purely copper, and why demerge?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the ₹5,000 crore target is for the copper company alone; non-copper revenue is under ₹10 crore. Demerger separates land and windmills from the copper business.

qa_highlights.question: Market value split between real estate and copper after demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real estate book value is about ₹29 crore and could be worth 10-20 times that; did not expect a market cap reduction for the copper entity.

risks_watch: Scrap supply disruption from Gulf shipping transit delays; Q1 FY27 volume may be marginally below Q4.
Demerger depends on NOCs from ROC, Regional Director, Official Liquidator and income tax authorities before NCLT hearing on 9 June.
Rising working capital (₹230 crore) and borrowings tied to copper price; interest cost could erode PAT growth relative to EBITDA.
Entry of Adani and Hindalco into recycling could increase competition and sourcing pressure.

Reporting inaccuracies on screener and exchange sites (promoter pledge shown at 96%) and a ~5% promoter-holding change management attributed to pledge versus sale; management said it has sent multiple correction letters.
Proposed fundraise of about ₹150 crore has no final structure yet.
Plastic recycling ROI and 12-15 month payback to be verified on execution.
512296|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and long-term growth, but cautious on near-term margin (targeting only ~5% and declining to predict price-driven growth). Evasive on fundraise structure, EBITDA-per-tonne peer comparisons and pledge/shareholding data, which management attributed to exchange reporting errors.
key_quotes: We are hopeful of maintaining 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year, and on an increased top line.
Our capacity has now reached 35,000 metric tonne this year, with the new, 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad.
I'm not looking at it growing much faster than the copper prices.
The 5,000 crores guidance is for purely copper.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets ~5% EBITDA margin through FY27 (4.5-5% seen as good), Q4 EBITDA ~₹36 crore on ~₹735 crore revenue (~5%), and value-added share rising from 52% in Q1 to 62% in Q4 with a 66% target by end FY27, but it says additional pass-on is not assured and margin is not expected to expand much beyond copper price moves.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Copper recycling capacity already rose from 30,000 to 35,000 t (+16.7%) and is live, with ~₹40 crore capex over two years and a 60-acre integrated facility; ~20% volume growth in FY27 needs further capacity beyond 35,000 t, but no specific next-phase tonnage is named.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides minimum 15-20% volume growth every year and ~20% in FY27, after FY26 volume rose ~34% to 24,000 t, though Q1 FY27 volume is guided marginally below Q4 and scrap supply is a constraint.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has proposed ~₹40 crore capex over two years, including ₹10 crore for plastic recycling, and is considering a ~₹150 crore fundraise; utilisation was not disclosed, so the call rests on the stated plan rather than a utilisation read.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is already set at ~20% volume and ~5% price growth for FY27, and Q1 FY27 volume is guided marginally below Q4, which leaves little room for an upgrade near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gulf-origin scrap has dried up from shipping disruption (Gulf is under 5% of input, US 35%), Q1 FY27 volume is guided slightly below Q4, and working capital rose to ₹230 crore from ₹157 crore, with interest costs able to erode PAT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Silver- and tin-plated bus bars for data centres are already new with exports to Canada and US, but they are expected to reach only 7-10% of revenue in 3-5 years, and plastic/aluminium recycling (₹10 crore) is planned with a 12-15 month payback.

rows.label: Demerger into copper and real estate verticals
rows.why: NCLT hearing is set for 9 June, but the demerger still needs NOCs from ROC, Regional Director, Official Liquidator and income tax authorities; real estate book value is about ₹29 crore against a copper target of ₹5,000 crore in ~3 years.

rows.label: Silver/tin-plated bus bars for data centres
rows.why: Exports to Canada and US have started, with ~10% EBITDA margin expected, but contribution is still very small and the ramp is slow.

rows.label: Working capital days down 2-3 days
rows.why: Working capital rose to ₹230 crore from ₹157 crore, and management expects working capital days to fall 2-3 days over the year.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 records, 15-20% volume growth and the 5,000 crore copper target, but cautious on near-term margin and avoided fundraise structure and EBITDA-per-tonne peer comparisons; analysts probed volume versus price mix, scrap sourcing after the Gulf disruption, and the promote

512296|2026-06.headline: Bhagyanagar India Q1 FY27: revenue above ₹700 crore and EBITDA margin a record 5.43%, but volume fell to 5,200-5,278 tons on April-May supply disruption.
512296|2026-06.overview: Management reported revenue of over ₹700 crore, PAT of ₹20 crore (up 9.5% QoQ, 167% YoY), and a record 5.43% EBITDA margin. Volume fell to 5,278 tons (down 9.5% QoQ, 6.5% YoY) because trade-route disruption and material shortages hit April and May. Management said June volume alone was 2,200 tons and supply had normalised, and it cut FY27 volume growth guidance to 12-15% from about 15-20%. Margin gains in April-May came from shortage-driven realisations across commodity and value-added products, and management guided to 5-5.5% EBITDA margin for the rest of the year.

financial_highlights.change: Lower volume; no YoY figure stated
Commodity exports are the bulk of this
Relates to FY2022-23 supplier registration cancellation; company plans to contest in tribunal

segments.name: Commodity (copper scrap-based)
segments.commentary: Management said margins improved across commodity and value-added products during the shortage. Commodity exports are the main part of the 18% export share.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: 63% of Q1 sales, the highest so far. Target is 63-64% for FY27, rising about 1-2% a year toward 68-69% over 3-4 years. About 250 tons of tin-coated product sold in Q1, with about 600 tons estimated for data centers.

segments.name: Copper business restructuring (Tieramet)
segments.commentary: All copper business moves from Bhagyanagar Copper to new wholly-owned subsidiary Tieramet Limited, then Bhagyanagar Copper merges into the parent and Tieramet is demerged. Parent keeps three city land parcels and the windmill project. NCLT hearing is set for 7 August 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth cut to 12-15% (from about 15-20%), attributed to roughly 2 months of lost sales in April-May; June run-rate of 2,200 tons is cited as support.
FY27 average realisation expected about 30% higher YoY and above the ₹1,300/kg plan average.
EBITDA margin guided at 5-5.5% for FY27; management said 5.5% for the full year may be difficult.
FY27 exports guided at 12-15% of sales (minimum 10%).
Long-term target of ₹5,000 crore revenue by FY30 reiterated, with volume growth of about 15% from FY28 onward.
Capex of about ₹40 crore over FY27-FY28; 10,000 ton capacity addition (35,000 to 45,000 tons) expected around April-June 2027, more likely June 2027.
Debt projected at ₹300-350 crore by FY30 (about ₹325 crore cited later).
capex_capacity: 35,000 metric tons of capacity has been added and is online now.
A further 10,000 tons (35,000 to 45,000 tons) is planned, expected operational around April-June 2027, more likely June 2027.
CTC wire capacity is about 80 tons per month, moving to 150 tons per month after a new 48-conductor machine (earlier about 28 conductors).
Two Hyderabad units: a 4-acre and a 60-acre facility. Capex of ₹40 crore is planned over FY27-FY28.
demand_pricing: Management cites third-party data: India copper consumption about 2.4 million tons by 2030; secondary copper demand to double from 0.7 to 1.4 million tons in five years.
Recycled copper market in India said to grow at 12-13% CAGR by some estimates; overall copper market 5-6% (or about 8.5% in other reports). Company says it is growing at 2-2.5x the market rate.
Primary copper refining charges have turned negative; Indian primary producers (Vedanta, Hindalco, Adani) are buying recycled copper.
Margins are set as a percentage of LME: raw material purchases at 86-95% of LME. Management says percentage margin is more stable than rupees per kg.
Data center: 800V DC architecture could cut copper bus bar demand by about 50%; management said this would have no material impact on the company.

Customers added: Crompton Greaves, TMC and Atlanta (transformers); Blue Star, Micron, OBO and L&T (Al data center bus bars). More than 100 tons of bus bars exported to North America in the last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Has sourcing normalised, and is 15-20% volume growth still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June normalised supply, so FY27 volume growth is now guided at 12-15%. Average realisation is expected to be about 30% higher YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 EBITDA per kg so high, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to shortage-driven realisations in April-May across commodity and value-added products, not exports. From June, margins are back to a normal 5-5.5% range.

qa_highlights.question: What was the GST impact of ₹17-18 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Surendra Bhutoria said it relates to FY2022-23 scrap purchases from a supplier whose registration was cancelled retrospectively. ₹17 crore was deposited and the company is contesting the case at the tribunal, which it believes it will win.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company's value-added mix changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is targeted at 63-64% for FY27, rising gradually toward 68-69% over 3-4 years. Management said it will not jump as it did in the last two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 5,000 crore FY30 revenue target and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ₹5,000 crore by FY30 regardless of copper price. Debt is projected at ₹300-350 crore by 2030, and management says the 5% EBITDA margin cash flow will fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraise timing and purpose?
qa_highlights.answer: First tranche of ₹52 crore is finalised, with funds expected in August. A second tranche is expected around March after the demerger. Management said MCX margin funding depends on copper prices.

risks_watch: Volume: June run-rate of 2,200 tons must be sustained to reach 12-15% FY27 growth.
Margin sustainability: 5.43% Q1 margin was helped by April-May shortage pricing; management guides 5-5.5% for the rest of the year.
Restructuring: NCLT hearing on 7 August 2026 and the Tieramet demerger, with the second fundraise tranche tied to demerger completion.
GST: ₹17 crore deposit on FY2022-23 input credit reversal, pending tribunal outcome.
Data center demand risk from shift to 800V DC architecture, which management says would have no material impact.
MCX margin requirements could rise sharply if copper prices rise, per management.
key_quotes: So, we should be looking at between 12% to 15% growth in terms of volume for the whole year now.

Going forward in the year, we hope to maintain the EBITDA margin between 5% and 5.5%. I think maintaining 5.5% for the whole year might be a little difficult, but we will be able to maintain between 5% and 5.5%, as was earlier indicated.
But we are very confident of 5,000 crores by FY30, whatever the copper price.
So, we are very, very confident that we will win.
512296|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand, value-added scaling and the FY30 ₹5,000 crore target, but cautious and defensive on volume: guidance was cut to 12-15% and management pointed to the June run-rate. Evasive on the GST matter (confident of tribunal win), the real estate inquiries (dismissed as belonging to a separate company), and on whether Q1 margins are repeatable, where it said 5.5% for the full year may be difficult.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 5-5.5% EBITDA margin for the rest of FY27 versus record 5.43% in Q1, which was shortage-driven; from June margins are back to normal 5-5.5% range.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: June 2027 (Q1 FY28), within the 2-4 quarter window
rows.why: 10,000 t addition (35,000 to 45,000 t, +28.6%) backed by ₹40 crore capex over FY27-FY28, with management guiding April-June 2027 and more likely June 2027; 35,000 t already online.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 volume growth guided at 12-15% after Q1 volume of 5,278 t (-6.5% YoY); June alone was 2,200 t, so volume must recover sharply from the Q1 run-rate to meet guidance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A ₹40 crore capex programme over FY27-FY28 is already committed and under way, so no fresh capex announcement is signalled; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Volume guidance was cut and margin guidance was reset to 5-5.5% from the 5.43% Q1 peak, which was helped by April-May shortage pricing; no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 volume growth already cut to 12-15% from 15-20%, and management said 5.5% full-year EBITDA margin may be difficult versus 5-5.5% guidance; Q1 volume fell 6.5% YoY and June run-rate of 2,200 t must be sustained.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 250 t of tin-coated product sold in Q1 with about 600 t estimated for data centres, and value-added share targeted at 63-64% for FY27, but no specific launch date given.

rows.label: FY27 realisation about 30% higher YoY
rows.why: Management expects average realisation above ₹1,300/kg, about 30% higher YoY, supported by shortage-driven pricing and raw material at 86-95% of LME, though April-May premiums are fading from June.

rows.label: Tieramet copper demerger and second fundraise tranche
rows.when: NCLT hearing 7 Aug 2026; second tranche around March 2027
rows.why: First ₹52 crore tranche finalised with funds expected in August, second tranche tied to demerger completion; target debt ₹300-350 crore by FY30 (about ₹325 crore cited).

rows.label: GST input credit reversal ₹17-18 crore
rows.why: ₹17 crore already deposited on FY2022-23 supplier registration cancellation; company contesting at tribunal and expects to win, but outcome is open.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY30 ₹5,000 crore target, value-added scaling and copper demand, but cautious on volume (guidance cut to 12-15%) and on whether Q1 margins are repeatable; analysts pushed on sourcing normalisation, sustainability of EBITDA per kg, the GST matter and fundraise timing.

512329|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of INR56 crores, of which INR50 crores business EBITDA, with management reiterating FY27 annualised EBITDA of INR300-350 crores.
512329|2026-03.overview: SG Mart delivered its strongest quarter by revenue (above INR1,800 crores) and EBITDA of INR56 crores in Q4 FY26, despite a disrupted March from the Middle East crisis. Underlying business EBITDA was about INR50 crores, with INR6 crores of inventory gain; FY26 EBITDA rose 35% to INR137 crores. Working capital was cut to 20 days, operating cash flow was about INR300 crores, and net cash closed at INR750 crores. Steel shortages hit the B2B trading volume and renewable structures, while service centres and the new steel profile business ramped up. Management kept FY27 guidance of INR300-350 crores annualised EBITDA, subject to war-related disruption.

segments.name: B2B metal trading
segments.commentary: Volume fell versus Q3 on steel supply shortage that began in January and worsened with the war; April and May commitments described as slow. EBITDA of INR700-1,000 per ton, and management says it contributes little to earnings.

segments.name: Service centres (India and Dubai)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume about 190,000-191,000 tons vs 163,000 tons in Q3, with Dubai at 37,000 tons (about 10%). Per-ton EBITDA of INR1,700-2,000. Stock-and-sell is about 20-25% of volume; cut-to-length about 75%.

segments.name: Renewable structures
segments.commentary: Q4 volume slightly down on coated steel shortage; monthly average about 5,000 tons. Per-ton EBITDA of INR3,000-5,000. FY27 volume guided at 130,000-150,000 tons; capacity is about 150,000 tons a year with no further capex needed.

segments.name: Steel profiles (incl. puff panels)
segments.commentary: New line launched in Q4 with about 7,000 tons, sold under APL Apollo brand and group network. April run-rate 5,000-6,000 tons. Per-ton EBITDA of INR5,000-8,000; puff panel margins guided at 5-8%. Profile capacity about 120,000 tons per annum; FY27 volume guided at 100,000+ tons.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annualised EBITDA guidance of INR300-350 crores retained; management said it should be near that unless war-related losses in B2B or Middle East operations deepen.
Quarterly business EBITDA of about INR50 crores expected to keep rising through FY27; management sees no deterioration in per-ton EBITDA spreads in Q1 FY27.
Renewable structures FY27 volume of 130,000-150,000 tons, with monthly volume rising from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-9,000 tons once coated steel supply improves.
Service centre network to reach 11-12 by end of FY27 (three additions); FY27 renewable plus profile volumes expected above 230,000 tons combined.

Three-year targets: about 20 service centres at 8,000-10,000 tons per month each (about 2 million tons annualised exit run-rate), 250,000-300,000 tons renewables, 300,000 tons profiles; B2B volume not guided.
capex_capacity: Approved capex of about INR600 crores over FY27-FY28 described as the minimum; roughly one-third for service centre build-out, about half for land acquisition (at least four or five land parcels), and 15-20% for profile machines.
Land acquired in Ahmedabad, Indore and Kolkata; active scouting in Hyderabad, Chennai and Punjab, with more land acquisitions expected in the next two to three months.
Plan to add three service centres in FY27; a cut-to-length machine is being added at the Dubai centre.
