segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Q4 production 1.08 million tons; FY26 3.03 million tons. Q4 realisation INR9,590/t and EBITDA INR4,040/t. Second 2 million-ton-plus plant commissioned May 2026, taking capacity to 8 million tons per annum.

segments.name: DRI and power
segments.commentary: Q4 DRI sales 188,000 tons (+171% YoY); FY26 480,000 tons (+56%). Q4 DRI realisation INR27,306/t and EBITDA INR7,999/t. Power volumes up 48% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: VAP share of FY26 standalone revenue 32% (from 20% in FY25) and of EBIT 30% (from 11%).

segments.name: Thriveni (coal and iron ore mining)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA INR1,990 crore, margin about 25%. FY27 iron ore volumes in Odisha guided to 34-35 million tons (+39%); Gadchiroli volume growth guided above 75% including BHQ. Coal production 17.5 million tons in FY26.

segments.name: Copper (Surya, Congo)
segments.commentary: Surya copper plant (12,000 tpa cathode) commissioned March 2026; about 700-750 tons produced to date, running at 40-45 tons/day. FY26 copper guided at 9,000-10,000 tons per management's sentence.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone guidance: iron ore production 26 million tons, dispatches 27 million tons, pellets 7.75-8 million tons, DRI 825,000 tons, and wire rod production about 150,000 tons from the new steel plant.
Management said FY28 steel plant would run at about 1 million tons (75-80% of capacity) and pellets at 8-9 million tons.
Annual cost savings above INR2,000 crore expected, with logistics and sustainability initiatives maturing by March 2028.
Thriveni FY27 volume growth expected above 75% including BHQ; Odisha iron ore volume 34-35 million tons.
Thriveni FY27 EBITDA contribution from Geomysore gold MDO targeted at about INR60 crore.
Copper: Chemaf expected to produce meaningfully from July 2027; about 90,000 tons of copper targeted over 3-5 years across Chemaf and Surya; 30,000 tpa expansion pathway at Surya.

Capex: standalone INR10,000-11,000 crore in FY27 and INR12,500 crore-plus in FY28 per management; consolidated FY27 capex about INR15,000 crore including copper (about USD200-260 million) and Thriveni (about INR1,000 crore).
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR13,500 crore over FY24-FY26; FY26 standalone capex about INR8,100 crore. INR5,100 crore capitalised (mainly pellet plant 1, slurry pipeline, DRI); INR1,850 crore capital advances; balance CWIP.
Pellet capacity 8 million tons per annum after pellet plant 2 (May 2026); management targets about 10 million tons after debottlenecking, pending government approvals expected by FY27 year-end.
BHQ beneficiation first phase targeted for December 2027: 30 million tons input and about 12 million tons output; main equipment ordered from a European supplier.
Steel plant (blast furnace, arc furnace, coke oven, 1.2 million tpa wire rod mill) at Chandrapur in final commissioning stage, expected in Q4 FY27.
Hedri to Ghugus 195 km pipeline in advanced planning; expected to cut logistics cost by more than INR500/t for most iron ore output.

Chemaf plant capex initially about USD1.1 billion, over USD800 million spent; further USD200-260 million needed; plants 85-90% complete; Chemaf debt about USD800 million, of which USD475 million to be reduced via creditor settlements and about USD330 million non-recourse; further USD200 million asset-level borrowing planned.
demand_pricing: Management said iron ore pricing is driven by the market and Lloyds is in line with the rest of the market; steel demand described as strong, especially in India.
Pellet realisation fell sequentially as volumes rose: the company searched for new, more distant markets, lost some earlier tenders and increased exports.
Pricing parity with competition maintained while volume rose 120%.
Captive consumption of about 9 million tons of iron ore in FY27 (about 8.8 million for pellets and 0.2 million for DRI).

Receivables on consolidated basis rose to INR1,480 crore from INR171 crore; management said Thriveni was consolidated for only nine months and the company has no clear explanation yet and will revert.
Thriveni receivables cited at 15-30 days; Tata Steel slurry pipeline arrangement is take-or-pay with no exclusivity for other buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Economics of the Tata Steel slurry pipeline arrangement and whether other steel players can be served.
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a take-or-pay contract with low sustaining capex, with the entire capacity dedicated to Tata Steel near Kalinganagar. Rajesh Gupta said there is no exclusivity.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated FY27-FY28 capex, sustainable leverage and deleveraging plans.
qa_highlights.answer: Riyaz Shaikh said about INR14,500 crore remains to be spent over two years, with standalone FY27 at INR10,000-11,000 crore and FY28 at INR12,500 crore-plus. Consolidated FY27 is about INR15,000 crore including copper. Debt is to be raised at 1-1.5x EBITDA, with no equity planned; Thriveni RPS of about INR700 crore was paid in April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Ramp-up and revenue contribution from Congo copper and cobalt assets.
qa_highlights.answer: Surya is producing copper cathode at 40-45 tons/day, with 9,000-10,000 tons expected in FY27 per management. Chemaf will not produce this year and is expected to reach about 90,000 tons from July 2027, with sulfuric acid supply being solved in the next three months.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet capacity utilisation and target with two plants.
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Gupta said the first plant did 3 million tons in its first nine months, and the company targets 7.5-8 million tons in FY27 across both plants, with 10 million tons as a target after debottlenecking but no guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated receivables increase from INR171 crore to INR1,480 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the comparison is not like-for-like since Thriveni was consolidated for only nine months, and no clear reason was given for the movement; the company will revert.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the government iron ore ASP and royalty rules on BHQ economics.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said royalties at 50% for material below 45% grade and 75% below 35% reduce BHQ input cost, with cost upside of INR200-300/t and selling or internal usage upside of INR700-800/t for BHQ product at 66-67% grade.

financial_highlights.change: +498% YoY; margin up more than 1,000 bps YoY

key_quotes: The EBITDA margin has held steady at approximately 34% across both the last 2 quarters, demonstrating structural cost efficiency and not one-off gains.
Chemaf will not produce anything this year. It is expected to start production meaningfully by July of 2027 when the plants are expected to be commissioned.
We don't have a clear cut answer on why exactly that movement is there. We'll come back very shortly on that.

512455|2026-06.headline: Lloyds Metals Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 127% YoY to INR5,413 crore with record 39.2% EBITDA margin.
512455|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue reached INR5,413 crore (up 127% YoY, up 10% QoQ), EBITDA INR2,120 crore (up 172% YoY) and PAT INR1,527 crore (up 141% YoY). Management attributes the margin gain to the slurry pipeline cutting logistics costs, higher realisations and a richer value-added mix, with pellets now 41% of standalone revenue. Second pellet plant reached 100% utilisation within four months of its May 2026 commissioning. Thriveni (mining subsidiary) grew revenue 63% YoY but margins were hit by fuel costs, with pass-through negotiations ongoing. Management also outlined large capex (about INR11,000-11,500 crore per year for two years, rising to INR15,000-20,000 crore in year three) and Chemaf/copper JV financing that is still pending.

segments.name: Iron ore (standalone)
segments.commentary: Production 6.05 million tons (+53% YoY), sales 5.46 million tons (+58% YoY); realisation INR6,068/t and EBITDA INR2,230/t. Management said realisation was flat YoY; higher internal consumption reduced merchant sales.

segments.name: DRI and power
segments.commentary: DRI sales 1,83,920 tons (+133% YoY) at INR27,376/t realisation and INR6,273/t EBITDA; power volumes up 87% YoY.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Production 1.69 million tons, 100% utilisation within four months of second plant start in May 2026; realisation INR11,783/t, EBITDA INR5,803/t. Sales mix 75.3% domestic, 24.7% export.

segments.name: Thriveni (mining and logistics)
segments.commentary: Iron ore volumes including BHQ 19.09 million tons (nearly 2x from 9.87 million tons). Gadchiroli ROM handling capacity raised from 10 to 55 million tpa; 12.83 million tons produced in the quarter. Odisha volume guided to 34-35 million tons in FY27 (+39%).

segments.name: Copper (Chemaf / JV)
segments.commentary: Existing DRC asset running at about 800 tons per month (about 2,400 tons per quarter); larger JV asset carries about $800 million+ book size and needs about $300 million+ more capex, targeted for operation in Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Thriveni FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 28-30% reiterated, though the Q1 figure was impacted by fuel costs; pass-through talks are underway.
Thriveni logistics EBITDA margin expected to rise from 32% to 40% via EV/LNG fleet shift (200 more vehicles, 50 LNG and 150 EV).
Odisha iron ore volumes expected at 34-35 million tons in FY27; Laserda-Pacheri (1.5 mtpa) started in Q1 and Dalpahar (3 mtpa) expected Q2 FY27.
Steel plant (1.2 mtpa long products) targeted for commissioning by March 2027; BHQ beneficiation by March 2028 with recovery of 38% vs 35% originally planned.
Chemaf financial closure expected in 3-4 months; debt restructuring expected to cut consolidated debt by about 40-50% (roughly $700-800 million).
capex_capacity: Capex of INR13,513 crore in FY24-FY26 and INR3,005 crore in Q1 FY27; about INR8,500 crore planned for FY27 excluding the Konsari steel project, with INR11,000-11,500 crore over the next two years.
Capex guidance for year three is INR15,000-20,000 crore, with further increase once the steel plant is included; copper PNG (Panguna) project excluded and still at study stage.
Foreign (copper JV) capex of about $300 million+ to be spent over the next nine months, with financing (equity and debt) closure expected in about three months.
BHQ beneficiation: 30 million tpa throughput across 9 modules, about 16-17 million tons of saleable output in two phases.
Pellet conversion ratio about 1.07 t iron ore per t pellet; pellet to DRI about 1.5; about 2 t iron ore per t steel.
demand_pricing: Iron ore realisation flat at about INR6,000/t YoY; management said pricing is unpredictable and is not forecasting it.
Pellet export mix about 25%; export markets include Kenya, South Africa, South Korea, Indonesia and China; about 3/4 domestic and 1/4 export by volume.
Slurry pipeline saves about INR500-550/t on pellet cost.
About 2.4 million tons of iron ore and pellet to be consumed internally by FY28 (1.4 million additional for the steel plant), per management.
Thriveni external contracts: Tata Steel MDO volume 3-4 million tons; NTPC and OMC contracts growing 3-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did iron ore EBITDA per ton stay flat despite 58% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales price stayed around INR6,000/t and more ore was used internally, so merchant sales volume and per-ton margin in the reported figure did not rise; the margin shifted to value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the pellet margin structural or one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slurry pipeline saves about INR550/t, export share is expected to stay around 25%, and the margin gains are structural rather than cyclical.

qa_highlights.question: NTPC wage receivable of about INR300 crore: why no provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no provision is planned; the arbitration award was won, NTPC has not accepted it, the matter is sub judice, and resolution is hoped for in 2-3 months. Management also said NTPC relations remain sound with a new contract awarded.

qa_highlights.question: Chemaf debt restructuring: will consolidated debt fall by $700-800 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restructuring will complete in the next quarter before creditor deadlines, and debt will fall significantly, by about 40-50%, though some new debt may replace old debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR650 crore raised in Thriveni?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are to refinance high-cost debt, fund conversion of conventional equipment to electric equipment and fund overseas subsidiaries for mining; Thriveni's blended interest cost is about 9-9.5% and Q1 interest was about INR115 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What about the DRC copper export ban?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the DRC exports mainly cathode, and both assets will produce final cathodes, so there is no impact on them.

risks_watch: Iron ore pricing and pellet realisation are cyclical; management declined to guide on pricing and margins beyond FY27.
Thriveni margins fell due to higher fuel costs; pass-through agreements with clients are still under negotiation.
NTPC receivable of about INR300 crore is unprovided and under arbitration; outcome and timing uncertain.
Copper JV: $300 million+ capex and financing closure still pending; Chemaf debt restructuring not yet complete; management declined to disclose copper margins or timing of profitability.
Steel plant and Panguna (PNG) copper projects not board-approved; capex beyond FY27 is not finalised.
512455|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and celebratory on the quarter's results and margins, but evasive on forward pricing, copper margins, PNG and the larger steel plant, saying plans are not yet finalised or are too early to quantify.
key_quotes: I'm proud to say our pellets operations reached 100% capacity utilization within just 4 months.
This is a structural re-rating of the earnings base, not a cyclical spike.

We are confident that these margins can sustain in the cyclical commodity because we continue to actively pursue better and higher value markets for every product we make, chasing realization and not just volume.
Our teams are evaluating and making a plan on how we can increase the production capacity in these mines over the next 3 to 5 years.

512529|2026-03.headline: Viyash Q4 FY26 revenue INR920 crore (+19.1% YoY), adjusted EBITDA about INR200 crore at 21.7% margin; FY26 PAT INR225 crore.
512529|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was described by management as the strongest quarter in company history, the first full 12-month results of the combined Viyash-SeQuent entity. Revenue rose 19.1% YoY to INR920 crore, with formulations up 28% to INR499 crore and APIs up 5% to about INR384 crore. Adjusted EBITDA rose about 64% to INR200 crore and PBT swung from a INR37 crore loss to a INR125 crore profit. FY26 revenue was INR3,420 crore (+13.8%), adjusted EBITDA INR702 crore (+59.6%), and PAT INR225 crore versus INR16 crore in FY25. Management also cited a credit rating upgrade to AA- (long-term) and A1+ (short-term).

financial_highlights.value: INR125 crore PBT / INR66 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR37 crore PBT and loss of INR32 crore PAT in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR349 crore PBT / INR225 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PBT more than 26x; PAT more than 14x vs INR16 crore

segments.name: Animal Health formulations
segments.commentary: All regions growing strongly per management. Animal health business moved from a flat INR350 crore plus or minus INR10 crore over five years to a INR400 crore run rate this year. Companion animal platform build-out is planned for FY27 with a Boehringer Ingelheim distribution partnership.

segments.name: Human health formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 formulations up 28% YoY. Shift toward complex products and internalised APIs; a dedicated potent oncology lab in R&D is being readied this quarter or next. US subsidiary (60% owned) revenue about INR400-425 crore.

segments.name: API and CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 API revenue up 8% to INR1,491 crore; Q4 API up 5%. Management deliberately cut low-margin intermediates. Life cycle management CDMO business with 8-10 innovators is about INR200-225 crore and is expected to grow about 40% in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 life cycle management (innovator) CDMO business expected to grow about 40% from a base of about INR200-225 crore.
Management expects comfortable double-digit API growth next year, roughly in line with formulations growth.
Management sees 15% annual growth as possible over the next five years; a detailed strategy and investor meeting are planned, possibly in June.
Revenue target of INR1,000 crore EBITDA stated, with timing to be confirmed at the investor meeting; management earlier cited INR800 crore for FY27 or FY28.
Synergies accrued at about INR50-60 crore annualised, with a target of INR125-150 crore annualised over the next 12-18 months.
Tax rate to be modelled at about 27% for FY27 and FY28, moving to 26-27% after one-off merger-related adjustments roll off.
Goodwill amortisation to fall to about INR35 crore in FY27 from about INR100 crore in FY26; depreciation excluding this to stay similar to FY26.
EBITDA margins expected to be maintained, but FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs.
Management is evaluating selective inorganic opportunities and options to buy out minority stakes (Spain option by 2028).
capex_capacity: Manufacturing expansion in Spain and debottlenecking at the Turkey manufacturing site are underway.
Capex approved for R&D expansion; companion animal R&D to expand 5-6x, targeting 7-8 products per year, with R&D hiring starting over the next six months.
Capex for capacity increase in Viyash has been invested and is awaiting approval, which management expects to bring further synergies.
Two high-potent dedicated API facilities; API batch capability ranges from 0.5-1 kg up to 100 kg.
API R&D team of about 250 scientists including analytical and process; human health formulation R&D about 55-60 scientists.
demand_pricing: Animal health: about 70-80% of API volumes go to innovators; generics pricing falls to about 60-70% of innovator price versus 10-15% in human generics.
Companion animal addressable market in Europe about $1 billion (excluding vaccines); India companion animal market a few hundred crore.
Formulation model is partnership-based, with development paid by partners and profit share typically 50:50 (customers cited include Cipla and Dr. Reddy's).

Raw material and freight: impact in March was immaterial; freight added INR1-2 crore in Q4; solvent costs were the main pressure. Price increases are being used to offset, with key materials stocked for 1-2 quarters.
Commodity intermediate margins are about 30-35%; management is exiting these in favour of APIs and formulations.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the CDMO business and how will it scale over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the life cycle management CDMO business is about INR200 crore with 8-10 big innovators, and 90%-plus of relationships are existing. Ramp-up of NCE Phase III CDMO work takes years.

qa_highlights.question: Which subsidiaries drive minority interest, and how big are they?
qa_highlights.answer: Viyash owns 60% of the US formulations business (revenue about INR400-425 crore) and 60% of the Spain business (FY26 revenue about INR550 crore). Minorities account for about 20% of PAT; Spain buy-back option exists by 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Animal health growth priorities and Boehringer Ingelheim partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on API for patent expiries from 2028 onwards (15-20 products identified, 5-6 large), geography expansion for large animal products, and companion animals with the BI distribution deal and 7-8 new products per year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability versus pure-play API peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects gross margins to hold at current levels, plus or minus 1-2%, through forward and backward integration and dropping commodity products. Margin gains beyond that are expected only with CDMO scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables growth and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose mostly with revenue; days increased by only about 5-6 days in Q4. Focus is on converting EBITDA into PAT, with a tax regime shift for some subsidiaries from 34-35% to 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material and geopolitical impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Impact began in March and was not material; key materials are stocked for 1-2 quarters and price increases are being used to offset solvent and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is API growth single digit and when will it turn double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intermediates were cut deliberately; quality API and animal health APIs are growing double digit, and FY27 should see comfortable double-digit API growth with more approvals.

risks_watch: Investment year in FY27 (R&D, pre-operating costs) may dilute EBITDA margins despite management's margin-maintenance guidance.
Raw material cost volatility (solvents, freight) linked to geopolitical disruption; management says price increases can offset only for now.
Receivables growth outpacing revenue in some geographies (e.g. Turkey) with long credit periods; EBITDA-to-PAT conversion remains a stated focus.
Synergy realisation (INR50-60 crore run-rate versus INR125-150 crore target) depends on approvals taking 12-18 months.
US companion animal generic guidance is complex (BA/BE requirements), delaying the planned US entry.
Minority interest (about 20% of PAT) and the Spain buy-back timeline.

513097|2026-06.headline: Shivalik Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.4% YoY to ₹182.2 crore and PAT rose 44.9% to ₹33 crore, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-30%.
513097|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 33.4% YoY to ₹182.2 crore, EBITDA rose 35.2% to ₹43.2 crore and PAT rose 44.9% to ₹33 crore. Shunts grew 18.7% while bimetals grew 7.4%, and management attributed roughly half of the revenue growth to higher silver prices. Management said margin gains came mainly from shunt conversion from strip to finished parts, which it considers sustainable. The company also received consent to operate for Phase 1 of its Pune facility for cell connecting systems and bus bar assemblies, serving one two-wheeler OEM for now.

segments.name: Bimetals (thermostatic)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7.4% YoY; management says customers are signalling first quantity uptick in 4-5 quarters, mainly domestic. Expects about 44-45% of standalone revenue; utilisation about 40-45%.

segments.name: Contacts (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Expected to be 30-35% of consolidated revenue; about 60% of contacts revenue goes to switchgear. Silver price roughly doubled YoY, with about half of revenue growth attributed to silver.

segments.name: Cell connecting systems / bus bar and PCBA assemblies
segments.commentary: Minimal revenue in Q1 as full production began only in the last month of the quarter; expected 15-16% of total revenue in first year. Main Pune manufacturing becomes fully operational only in October.

Bimetal export opportunities with existing customers restarted after the US tariff pause; these are expected to add revenue in about 4 quarters.
Silver prices about double YoY and slightly lower QoQ; copper prices up substantially YoY.

qa_highlights.answer: Management gave overall revenue growth of about 20-30% and a segment mix: bimetal 44-45%, shunts 54-55% of standalone; contacts 30-35% and assemblies about 15-16% of consolidated revenue in year 1. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 33% growth is sustainable excluding commodity prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a 20-30% range going forward and said about half of the revenue growth came from silver, with shunt value-add conversion driving margin gains that are considered sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pune bus bar opportunity and incremental capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Potential business of ₹300-400 crore in about 3 years, with capex of about ₹20-25 crore since high-capex processes already exist at Solon; figures subject to change.

513228|2026-03.headline: Pennar Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14.91% to INR41.04 crores on total income of INR933.7 crores; management commits to 20% PAT growth in FY27.
513228|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 2.26% to INR933.7 crores while EBITDA grew 15.27% to INR114 crores and PAT grew 14.91% to INR41.04 crores, with PAT margin at 4.44% versus 3.9%. FY26 was a record year: total income INR3,666 crores (up 12.33%), PAT INR138.83 crores (up 16.22%), PAT margin 3.83% versus 3.7%. Management attributed the Q4 revenue slowdown to revenue slipping into Q1 and a solar hit in diversified engineering, and blamed labour shortages for PEB India underperformance in FY26. Working capital rose to 82 days, and gross debt-to-equity rose to 0.98x, both of which management is targeting to reduce.

segments.commentary: Revenue rose from INR460 crores to INR516 crores (+12.35%), mainly from the US, driven by the Telco acquisition, partly offset by PEB execution challenges.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR429.54 crores; fell due to steel order and BIW weakness, plus a solar revenue hit in Q4. Analyst computed segment margin rising to about 14% from 11.5%, which management attributed to engineering services revenue being booked gross with cost in employee benefits.

segments.commentary: Management reported healthy double-digit revenue and PBT growth in FY26; AI-assisted design and detailing now in use. Analysts were told the segment is not yet at INR100 crores scale.

segments.commentary: Order book increased to INR145 crores (press-stated) or INR128 crores (CFO-stated), with the highest-capacity 100 TPH AFBC and 80 TPH WHR boiler orders secured. Double-digit order backlog growth since March.

segments.commentary: Order backlog about INR34 crores, up from INR22 crores at the prior update; US tariff impact has moderated and orders are returning. European markets being explored.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix: higher value-add in BIW, ICD and boilers, and engineering services; margins guided at a similar 42% to 43% level.

qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to at least 20% PAT growth, not EPS growth, given possible equity dilution; it declined to guide revenue.

513228|2026-06.headline: Pennar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3.6% to INR884.55 crore while PBT grew 16% to INR46.8 crore, with PBT margin at 5.38%.

513262|2026-09.headline: Steel Strips Wheels Q2 FY27 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR1,930 crore and standalone EBITDA per wheel hit INR404, with management reiterating the figure as sustainable.
513262|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the strongest quarter in company history, with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT. Standalone EBITDA including other income rose 107% YoY to INR237 crore, margin 12.3% vs 9.6%, and PAT rose 209% to INR119 crore. Management attributed the gains to richer aluminium mix, cost optimisation, higher exports and customer price revisions for non-raw-material input costs. A supplementary invoicing of INR140 crore in Q2 (INR183 crore in H1) relating to raw-material pass-through was disputed by analysts as flattering EBITDA; management said it has no bearing on EBITDA. The board also approved a greenfield plant at Sambhajinagar (INR1,400 crore over 60 months) and an interim dividend of INR1.50 per share.

segments.commentary: Highest growth among segments in Q2 across domestic and export markets; domestic steel wheel demand up 28% in H1 per management. Management expects record CV sales in October.

513349|2026-03.headline: Ajmera Realty FY26 presales hit record INR 1,701 Cr (+57% YoY), beating INR 1,600 Cr guidance; FY27 presales target set at INR 2,200 Cr.

qa_highlights.answer: Mostly regulatory reasons; management is choosing to launch at plinth level for better demand and pricing, not at excavation stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sales weak at Ajmera One (Versova)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand for larger units appears only after RCC level; the project is at excavation, so management will not push desperate sales and expects a year before traction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated finance cost rise from ~INR21 crores to ~INR30 crores QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Solis entered revenue recognition, so accumulated interest on its high-cost PE-funded debt was charged to P&L. Cost is expected to normalise to about INR20 crores from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any P&L impact from the INR89 crores monetisation, and why was SV Concrete dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR89 crores is a balance-sheet financial asset realisation with no P&L impact. SV Concrete was swapped for Whitefield (INR389 crores GDV, Q4 FY27 target).

513375|2026-03.headline: Carborundum Universal FY26 standalone sales rose 8.6% to INR 3,024 crore, while consolidated PBIT fell 25.3% to INR 404 crore on subsidiary losses.
513375|2026-03.overview: Standalone performance rebounded through H2 FY26, with Q4 sales up 23.1% YoY to INR 845 crore and Q4 PAT more than doubling to INR 122 crore. Consolidated sales crossed INR 5,000 crore (INR 5,149 crore, +6.5%), but consolidated PBT before exceptions fell 27.2% to INR 416 crore, driven by VAW sanctions, Foskor, Awuko and Rhodius losses. Management decided to wind down Awuko and to close Foskor Zirconia, booking exceptional items of INR 135 crore in FY26. FY27 guidance is for about 4-4.5% consolidated sales growth, which falls to 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko, with capex of about INR 400 crore.

segments.name: Standalone Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,270 crore (+6.2%); H1 down 2.8% to INR 594 crore, H2 up 15.6% YoY to INR 675 crore. PBIT INR 195 crore (+0.9%), margin 15.3% vs 16.1%.

segments.name: Standalone Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 906 crore (+11.1%), with exports up 100% to over 33% of sales. PBIT rose 31.1% to INR 82 crore; management said growth was mainly volume with price roughly flat.

segments.name: Standalone Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,000 crore (+6.5%). PBIT fell 8% to INR 214 crore. Wear ceramics de-grew 9%; engineering ceramics grew 30% on SOFC demand; metallized cylinders grew 9% after a H1 production issue.

segments.name: Consolidated Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 2,271 crore (+5.1%); Q4 INR 610 crore (+13.4% YoY). PBIT margin 4.3% vs 7.0%, with Rhodius loss about INR 45 crore and Awuko loss about INR 75 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,632 crore (+3.7%), held back by VAW Russia sales down 35% in roubles. Foskor losses hit PBIT; consolidated segment PBIT INR 91 crore vs INR 177 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,268 crore (+9.3%); reported margin 20.2%. Industrial ceramics INR 569 crore (+7.8%); refractories and anti-corrosives INR 437 crore (+4.7%).

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales EUR 61 million, down 8.8% from EUR 67 million, after about EUR 5 million lost to a Q1 logistics transition. PAT loss EUR 2.6 million vs EUR 0.2 million in FY25.

segments.name: Awuko
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 10.5 million (+4.6%); loss before tax rose to EUR 7.7 million. Voluntary winding-up started in Germany.

segments.name: VAW Russia
segments.commentary: Sales about 6 billion roubles vs 9.4 billion (-35.3%) under US sanctions; profit before tax 617 million roubles vs 1.7 billion, but still profitable.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (South Africa)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 461 million (+11.2%); loss before tax ZAR 77 million vs ZAR 37 million. Operations being discontinued as not commercially viable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated sales growth of about 4-4.5%; about 11-12% excluding Foskor Zirconia and Awuko (together INR 343 crore of FY26 sales).
FY27 standalone Abrasives growth about 12% per management; consolidated Abrasives sales +5.5-6% (11-12% excluding Awuko).
FY27 consolidated Ceramics growth of 15-15.5%; consolidated Electrominerals sales -6.5% to -7% due to Foskor closure (8-9% excluding Foskor).
Margin guidance FY27: Abrasives 9.5-10% (FY26 comparable 7.9%), Ceramics 20.5-21% (reported 20.2%), Electrominerals 9-9.5% (comparable FY26 9.1%).
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore, mainly advanced ceramics for power electronics, brown-fused alumina expansion, a 110 kV substation and a tunnel kiln for refractories.
Rhodius expected to grow sales about 5% in FY27 with a very small loss; Aspiration 2030 targets were not formally quantified.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex FY26 INR 309 crore (standalone INR 235 crore) against INR 350 crore guided earlier.
Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components facility: first module commissioned in H1 FY26 at INR 66 crore; serial supplies start FY27, material revenue expected from 2029.
Aerospace and defence ceramics facility at INR 49 crore; STANAG 4 vehicle armour qualification secured; SCOMET approval awaited.
White fused alumina furnace upgrade from 2 MVA to 4.5 MVA at about INR 53 crore, adding up to INR 95 crore revenue potential; treatment facility INR 30 crore for up to INR 120 crore revenue.
Thin wheel capacity at Hosur using DRONCO-acquired assets: INR 83 crore outlay, 46 million wheels, peak revenue about INR 120 crore.
Refractories fired capacity to rise 75%; metallized cylinder capacity to be expanded in three phases over 18-24 months.
demand_pricing: Standalone H2 FY26 growth was broad-based, with Abrasives, Ceramics and Electrominerals each up double digits sequentially. Management attributed part of the rebound to GST rationalisation and festive demand.
China cut its abrasive export rebate from 9% to 0% from April 2026 (one analyst cited 13%). Management called it good for domestic industry but too recent to show in numbers.
Electrominerals growth was mainly volume; price roughly flat. Chinese import intensity has not declined.

Ceramics growth of 9.3% missed the 13-14% guided earlier, mainly due to deferred projects, especially in the glass segment. Management attributes the 15% FY27 outlook to backlog and customer forecasts.
Over 80% of Ceramics sales are exports; under 10% of Abrasives sales are exports.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the SOFC ceramics business become, and what is the wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give wallet share but said it is an important supplier, with customer visibility to about 2028, and it expects a meaningful share of revenue as the engineered segment grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Ceramics growth miss the 13-14% guidance, and does it signal structural competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed mainly deferred projects, not structural change, and expects the 15% FY27 growth to be backed by backlog and customer forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for semiconductor fab-equipment ceramics revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Material qualification takes four to six years; samples are tested and serial production starts, with material revenue expected from 2029 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to profitability at Rhodius?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects sales growth of 6-7% with the one-time EUR 5 million logistics loss not recurring, plus a special profitability programme, to return it to a small loss or breakeven in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there alternatives to Russian silicon carbide supply from VAW?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said replacing the capacity would be costly and difficult; it awaits sanctions relief and has no alternative for now.

risks_watch: Foskor Zirconia closure needs approvals in South Africa; the Awuko winding-up is ongoing in Germany.
VAW Russia sales are constrained by US sanctions, with no alternative supply route identified.
FY27 consolidated growth of 4-4.5% is low versus the 11-12% comparable figure, so the reported drop from exits needs watching.
Ceramics growth depends on the timing of deferred projects and on the US business, where exports fell 40% in FY26 for wear ceramics.
Rhodius returning to breakeven depends on recovering the lost EUR 5 million in sales and on cost actions.

513375|2026-06.headline: Carborundum Universal Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores; consolidated PAT up 23.4% to INR 76 crores, with Electrominerals up 33%.
513375|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores, broad-based across Electrominerals (+33%), Ceramics (+15.2%) and Abrasives (+14.7%), and were flat QoQ. Standalone PAT was INR 88 crores, up 14.3% on a like-to-like basis excluding a one-time INR 68 crore subsidiary dividend in Q1 FY26. Consolidated PAT of INR 76 crores was helped by a INR 25 crore gain on leasehold transfer at Sterling Abrasives, while Abrasives standalone margins were squeezed by an oil-linked and fuel cost push of about INR 16 crores. Management raised the consolidated Ceramics growth guidance to 23-25% and kept other segment guidance unchanged, while Foskor divestment and Awuko closure updates are now promised for Q2.

segments.name: Electrominerals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 282 crores, +33% YoY and +12.2% QoQ, mainly volume and export-led with very little price increase; PBIT rose to INR 39 crores from INR 7 crores. Exports rose to about 40% of segment sales from about 35% last year.

segments.name: Ceramics (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 274 crores, +15.2% YoY but -1.6% QoQ on refractories seasonality; PBIT INR 59 crores vs INR 62 crores YoY as IC gains were offset by fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.

segments.name: Abrasives (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 328 crores, +14.7% YoY, volume-driven; PBIT INR 34 crores with margin falling to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY, due to about INR 16 crores cost push (resins, oil, fuel) and INR 8-9 crores volume drop QoQ.

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany, Abrasives)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 15.6 million, +18% YoY and +1.1% QoQ (INR 172 crores, +33.9% YoY); loss after tax EUR 0.7 million vs EUR 1.6 million a year ago. FY27 guidance of about 5% growth and a small PAT loss is maintained.

segments.name: CUMI Awuko Abrasives (Germany, being wound up)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 2.89 million, +11.1% YoY; loss after tax EUR 1.69 million vs EUR 0.9 million a year ago. Voluntary winding up is in progress and management aims to complete it in about a quarter.

segments.name: VAW Russia (Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales RUB 1.58 billion, -14.1% YoY in roubles but INR 201 crores, +3.1% YoY in rupee terms; PAT RUB 52.1 million vs RUB 71.5 million a year ago. Business is domestic-focused.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (51% subsidiary, Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 107 million, -14.7% QoQ; deemed commercially unviable. Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed a INR 17 crore loss; divestment or exit options are being explored, targeted for Q2.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth: FY27 guidance of about 4-4.5% reported, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko; management says it could reach about 15% on a comparable basis given the order book.
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth: guidance of 5.5-6% retained; 11-12% excluding Awuko (about INR 108 crores).
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth: raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%; management expects the Ceramics margin to be at the higher end of the guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales: guidance of a 6.5-7% decline retained (reported basis); 8-9% growth excluding Foskor, and management says this could be 9-10%.

Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% retained, with Ceramics 20.5-21% maintained. Q1 consolidated Abrasives margin was about 2.5% excluding the Sterling gain, which management attributes to Awuko losses.
Capex of about INR 400 crores for FY27 retained. Rhodius guidance of about 5% growth with a small PAT loss is unchanged.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex was INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 against INR 64 crores a year earlier; the FY27 target of about INR 400 crores is unchanged, and management would not give project-wise splits.

FY27 capex covers expansion in advanced ceramics for power electronics (including substrates), metallized tubes, rings and brazed assemblies, brown-fused alumina expansion, an integrated furnace for thermal spray powders and a zirconia furnace.
Metallized substrate facility is being set up with one anchor customer and a technology tie-up; it should be commissioned in FY27, with revenue from FY28.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components: small in FY27, picking up in FY28, with a peak targeted for FY30. Aerospace and defence will improve in FY27 with the main ramp from FY28. Powder purity is moving from 5N to 6N.
Refractories capacity expansion is on track, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was volume-driven with very small price increases; management sees early easing of Chinese import competition but says exchange rates and China's export-rebate changes make the trend unclear.
Ceramics: growth was seen across segments; Wear Ceramics returned to growth this quarter after several quarters, and Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics are growing mainly through exports.

Electrominerals: volume-led, with treated-product mix helping margins; little or no price increase. Export share is rising toward 40%, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way.

Abrasives cost push: oil-linked inputs such as resins rose sharply in May and June, with oil reaching about $117 a barrel. Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5%. The US-Iran conflict that began end-February 2026 drove the cost pressure.
Management said it will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, and will decide one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi (Avendus): How much of standalone Abrasives growth is value vs volume, traction by sub-segment, and are Chinese import changes helping share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was predominantly volume-driven with very small price increases. Import competition from China has just started to ease, but management said exchange rates and China's export-benefit withdrawal make the trend unclear; it sees the trend as positive.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi: Where is Ceramics traction strongest across Wear, Technical, Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics, and is Metallized Cylinder/Engineered Ceramics growth domestic or export?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth optimism is across all segments except Wear, which is normal growth; Wear returned to growth this quarter after several quarters. Metallized Cylinder and Engineered Ceramics growth is predominantly export.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit (Equirus): How will semiconductor wafer fab, aerospace/defence and substrate revenues phase across FY27 and FY28, and does the Ceramics guidance upgrade come mainly from SOFC?
qa_highlights.answer: Substrate facility to be set up in FY27 with revenue from FY28; wafer fab components very small in FY27, picking up in FY28 and peaking in FY30; aerospace/defence slightly better in FY27 with main ramp from FY28. The upgrade is a combination of Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders and SOFC Ceramics, with no split given.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: What are plans for zirconia products and Foskor divestment progress, and what drove the Electrominerals volume vs price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has a couple of options after discussions with South African partners and aims to close the Foskor process by Q2; a fuller update is promised then. Electrominerals growth was mostly volume and product mix (treated products), with very little or no price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: Why was Abrasives margin under pressure if Electrominerals prices were not up significantly?
qa_highlights.answer: Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5% and were offset by normal price increases; the pressure came from oil-linked inputs such as resins, which rose sharply in May and June with oil reaching about $117 a barrel, plus fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: Amit Anwani (PL Capital): What is the strategic view on VAW Russia, its utilisation and sales update, and SOFC contribution and volume vs price in the 11-12% comparable guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in Russian business, which remains domestic-focused; management's aim is to stay put, comply with laws and serve the domestic market. Full-year growth is expected to be predominantly volume-driven with normal price increases; no individual SOFC split was shared, and pricing beyond normal will be decided one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Jain (Dolat): Excluding the Sterling gain, consolidated Abrasives margin is about 2.5% versus 9-10% guidance; what is the comment, and what is the CAPEX breakdown and unallocated expense run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is largely Awuko losses, which are still being incurred, so it holds the 9-10% guidance. Project-wise CAPEX split was not shared. Consolidated unallocable expense of INR 19 crores was mainly a forex loss versus a gain last year.

qa_highlights.question: Sajal Kapoor (Antifragile): How does the group distinguish a temporary setback from a signal to exit, and how does it make decisions in semiconductors and defence without operating history?
qa_highlights.answer: Awuko and Foskor were exited after management gave enough time; it waits at least four to eight quarters before deciding if a trend is temporary. For semicon, it is entering as a supplier of ceramics to fab equipment makers, building on 40-50 years of ceramics experience and working via anchor customers.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya (Kotak): How large are exports in standalone Electrominerals, and is European duty on Chinese imports a driver; what is the semicon 6N and substrate roadmap and any inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Export share has risen from about 20% earlier to 35% last year and is now on a path to 40%. Europe's duties are helping, with US and Asia efforts under way. 5N to 6N powder purity is being worked on; substrate benefits start FY28. Management said the focus is to remain a raw material supplier, with no inorganic plans stated.

risks_watch: Abrasives margin recovery: standalone Abrasives margin fell to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY; oil-linked resin and fuel cost push (about INR 16 crores) and whether normal price increases can offset it, given no further pricing is planned until the cost environment clears.
Awuko winding-up completion (guided within about a quarter) and the exceptional costs still to come; Q1 Abrasives losses from Awuko depress consolidated margins.
Foskor divestment or exit: options being explored, targeted to close by Q2; Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed about INR 17 crores of Foskor loss.

Consolidated Ceramics margin: management expects the high end of 20.5-21% guidance, but standalone Ceramics PBIT was flat YoY on fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.
Sustainability of Electrominerals export-led growth (33% standalone YoY) given that pricing was flat and the growth was mostly volume and mix.
VAW Russia: RUB sales down 14.1% YoY with geopolitical uncertainty; management says it is too difficult to predict and the aim is to stay put.
Unallocable costs: consolidated INR 19 crores in Q1 due to forex loss and lower interest income; forex swings may recur.
key_quotes: Growth at standalone level was broad-based and driven by all three segments.
So, it's going to be very tough and it's going to be tough for us to say that based on which we will start putting up price, etc., is also going to be tough.
We always wait at least four to eight quarters to see whether these are temporary trends or fundamentally things are changing.

513472|2026-03.headline: Simplex Castings FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 18% to Rs 202 crore and PAT 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore; FY27 target Rs 300 crore.
513472|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue up about 18% to Rs 202 crore, EBITDA up 20% to Rs 37.39 crore with margin expansion, and PAT up 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore. Q4 revenue was slightly below the prior-year Q4 (about Rs 67 crore cited by an analyst), which management attributed to customer site delays and LPG/gas supply disruptions that held back dispatches. The company received RDSO approval to restart wagon bogie manufacturing, with cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month now built. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs 300 crore and a FY28 aspiration of Rs 500 crore, contingent on execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders.

segments.name: Railways (cast and fabricated bogies)
segments.commentary: RDSO approval received to restart wagon bogies; 200-250 cast bogies a month capacity built. Cast bogie sale value about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Developmental order for fabricated loco bogies; FY27 target Rs 50 crore from cast railway business.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Management targets about Rs 50 crore from power in FY27, linked to BHEL and L&T orders for 32 and 16 coal-based thermal plants to be commissioned by 2032.

segments.name: Steel (coke oven doors and castings)
segments.commentary: Coke oven door segment estimated at Rs 50-60 crore of about Rs 200-220 crore revenue; management claims about 70% share of India's coke oven doors and expects growth toward Rs 100 crore over 2-3 years. Recent orders from SMS and Thyssen for SAIL stamp-charging batteries.

segments.name: Defence and shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Supplies A-brackets, B-brackets and stern boss castings to shipyards and components to Gun Carriage Factory Jabalpur (Dhanush). Management says margins above 10% but segment, with other rest-of-business, expected at only 15-20% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target Rs 300 crore: about Rs 200 crore from existing business (stated as already closed), Rs 50 crore from cast railway business and about Rs 50 crore from power.
FY27 margins guided similar to FY26; cost-reduction gains expected to show in Q3-Q4 FY27.

FY28 revenue aspiration of about Rs 500 crore, dependent on execution, acquisition and EPC, and railway orders.

capex_capacity: Cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month built under the first preferential issue; in CWIP until commercial production and prototype/first order.
Second preferential issue of about Rs 50 crore; about half earmarked for fabricated bogie facilities (Rs 25 crore capital and Rs 25 crore working capital).

Centrifugal rolls project (Rs 1.5-2 crore investment) dropped after market survey.
demand_pricing: Wagon bogies: wagon makers about 70-75% of market and railways spares about 20-25%; management targets both channels.
Possible wagon mega-order: management estimates 6,000 bogies (about 2 tonnes cast weight each) for 8,000-10,000 wagons over 3 years, with 20-30% typically outsourced.

Coke oven doors: India has an estimated 150-180 batteries; replacement demand about 3-4% a year; order flow of 2-3 batteries a year, plus about 70-80 batteries for planned 140 million tonne capacity expansion by 2030-2040.
Power and steel demand strong; management says it has become choosy on orders.
Gas (LPG) supply disruptions hit fabrication plants and top line in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue fall YoY versus last Q4 (about Rs 67 crore), and what drove margins higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dispatches slipped because customer site activity was delayed, leaving finished goods inventory that was expected to be realised in April-May. Gas (LPG) shortages also hit fabrication plants. Management said the margin goal is at least 8-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company supply full bogies or only parts, and what is the realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The company assembles bogies from its own castings plus outsourced springs, side bearers, brakes and pads. Cast bogie sale value is about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Couplers and draft gears are planned later.

qa_highlights.question: When will orders from RDSO approval arrive and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: An order of 100-200 bogies is expected in about a month. No further capex is needed for the cast bogie line; it is awaiting the prototype and first order.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 targets, margins, acquisitions and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue target is Rs 300 crore, with margins similar to FY26. Two acquisition talks remain open after one failed; they are in the same line of business. FY27 capex is Rs 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coke oven door market size and share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates 150-180 batteries in India, 3-4% annual replacement, and about 70% market share. Coke oven doors are about Rs 50-60 crore of revenue, with growth to about Rs 100 crore expected over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 Rs 500 crore target risk and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Risks are execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders. Management said acquisitions in India had prohibitive multiples, so it is looking abroad in steel, power or railways, size about Rs 20-100 crore. Funding may come from debt or equity; the second preferential issue is a Rs 50 crore part of that.

513472|2026-06.headline: Simplex Castings Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 35% YoY to ₹60.95 crore and PAT rose about 45% to ₹6.86 crore, with near-term order book at ~₹150 crore.

EBITDA rose about 25% YoY to ₹11.52 crore, with margin of 18.89%, and PAT rose about 45% YoY to ₹6.86 crore (PAT margin 11.25% vs 10.48%). Management said the near-term order book has expanded to roughly ₹150 crore+ from a historical ₹80–100 crore range. segments.commentary: No power/BHL orders in last year; management targets ~₹100 crore from power sector next year via orders secured through RXIL with BHL and L&T.

segments.name: Shipbuilding (Mazgaon Dock)
segments.commentary: First order of 5 sets about ₹4.5 crore; 3 sets already cast and first offered for inspection. A further pipeline order is about ₹8 crore.

segments.name: Steel and metallurgical
segments.commentary: Steel is the core market; management says ~₹300 crore of FY27 revenue will be fed by steel sector. Non-ferrous is about 20% of order book.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Target 5–10% of business in FY27 (with shipbuilding, 10–15%), working first with one ordnance factory (Khamaria, Jabalpur); not expected to grow 20–30%.

Non-ferrous and metallurgical (Balco, Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc, Nalco, Aditya Birla) about 20% of order book.

qa_highlights.answer: Running at roughly 50–60%; targeting at least 80% by end of next financial year, with gradual increase starting this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is ₹300 crore FY27 revenue guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹60 crore done in Q1, with ~₹150 crore order book to execute in FY27 and pipeline orders to come by March; management said ₹300 crore is in line.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital fall from 60–90 days (or 100–120 days) to target levels, and what is the margin cost of invoice discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Shift to railway bogies (30–45 day cycle, payment upfront from wagon builders) and RXIL/Invoice Mart (30–35 days post dispatch). Discounting costs about 5–5.5%. Management said ₹300 crore revenue would need only about ₹50 crore working capital at 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term opportunities beyond ₹500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to detail; areas mentioned include machine tool castings, defence and possible technology JVs or acquisitions; management reiterated no concrete plans yet.

513517|2026-03.headline: Steelcast FY26 revenue rose 13.33% to ₹423.17 crore and PAT 20.31% to ₹86.86 crore; management guides 20%+ volume growth for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin outlook 25-26% or 28-30%?

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution expected from GET in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is the company going to disclose a more detailed revenue breakup?

513517|2026-06.headline: Steelcast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR124.82 crores and PAT 19.26% to INR23.71 crores; management guides 25-30% FY27 volume growth.
513517|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR124.82 crores, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA of INR35.24 crores (28.23% margin vs 28.14%) and PAT of INR23.71 crores (19% margin vs 18.64%). Management said input-cost increases will be passed through via sales price variation formulas, with the bulk of the price correction effective 1 July. Capacity utilisation was 66% in April-June, and a greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes (about INR120 crores over two years) was approved, targeted for commissioning by 31 March FY28. The order book stood at INR140 crores, roughly 3-4 months of forward booking.

financial_highlights.change: Export share 60% by tonnage (management also cited 62% by value)
Not quantified vs last year; management said it is higher

segments.name: Sector mix (sales, current year guidance)
segments.commentary: Mining about 27%, earthmoving about 43%, construction about 15%, defense about 1%, with the remainder across other sectors. Ten years ago mining was about 84% of sales, earthmoving near zero and construction 15-16%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports have historically run at 45-50% of sales; FY27 guided at about 49-50% exports, and the next year at 47% exports and 53% domestic. Sales now go to about 16 countries; the US and Germany together are about 70% of exports.

segments.name: Ground engaging tools (GET)
segments.commentary: Under 1% of revenue today, with FY26 at about 1%; guided to about 3.5% of sales in FY27 and 4.5-5% by FY29 as new parts move into serial supply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at about 25% over FY26; in Q&A the chairman said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility, and FY27 volume was implied at about 18,000 tons at 63% utilisation.
Long-term growth target of about 20% CAGR over the coming years.
Sequential quarter-on-quarter top-line improvement expected for several quarters.
EBITDA margin guided to stay in range; in Q&A the chairman said a 150-200 bps rise to 28.5-29% for FY27 is theoretically achievable and is the aim. FY27 margin was about 27%.
Price correction for input costs (raw materials and natural gas) effective 1 July, passed through under the sales price variation formula with a one-quarter lag.
Capacity utilisation target of 63% for FY27 and 90% by FY29 on existing capacity; management said above 90% is not advisable.
New facility revenue potential at peak about INR300 crores; commissioning target 31 March FY28.
Two renewable power projects (2.4 MW wind-solar hybrid and 1.4 MW solar) expected to be commissioned before 31 December 2026.
capex_capacity: Greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes approved by the Board, steel castings from 5 kg to 1,000 kg, planned investment about INR120 crores over two years, with an internal commissioning target of 31 March FY28.
Land of about 100,000 sq m provided by the Gujarat government; the new site is 12 km from the existing facility.
Existing capacity is about 29,000 tonnes; FY27 utilisation target is 63% and 90% by FY29.
Plan to start recruiting around mid-year for FY28 readiness; staff currently adequate for FY27 targets.
Considering shifting some manufacturing fuel from natural gas to electricity over 2-3 years; natural gas is about 50-55% more expensive than at end-February prices.
demand_pricing: Pricing is pass-through under a sales price variation formula with customers; the chairman said all major raw material increases will be recovered, but declined to give a percentage range.
Over 100 new parts developed in the last 18-24 months; about 20% of revenue expected from new parts over the next 2-3 years, with 80% from existing parts.
Management said US railroad work has been deprioritised in favour of better-priced industrial markets, and defense is a low priority because pricing is better elsewhere.
Rupee movements are shared with customers, not hedged.
Management says all 9 end-user sectors are seeing demand increases, with automobile growing 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the input-cost increase will be passed to customers, and how much is done so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a minimal correction took effect 1 April; most comes from 1 July. All major raw materials are in the formula, so the chairman said all increases will be passed on, without quantifying a range.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 25% growth mean volume or volume plus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 25%, with price increases on top; the chairman later said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation reach 100% by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Target is 90% by FY29 on existing capacity, and new capacity starts adding volume afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and what is the new facility's peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly scale and operating leverage, with minimal price increase so far. Peak revenue potential from the new facility is about INR300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering a rights issue or bonus issue, and is it focusing on defense?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has about INR120 crores of reserves and will fund the capex from internal accruals; a rights issue is not needed because it would dilute EPS. A bonus issue will be taken to the next Board meeting. Defense is deprioritised because it is a single-customer, higher-risk business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split and how has it changed over 10 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining, earthmoving and construction together are about 70% of sales. Mining fell from about 84% to about 54% over 10 years, and earthmoving rose from near zero to about 36%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that exports are understated because of Tier 2 supply to OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: The chairman said 98-99% of sales are direct Tier 1 supply to OEMs, and OEMs may export part of what they buy, so total export share may be a little higher.

Recruitment plan from mid-year for FY28 capacity.

513519|2026-03.headline: Pitti Engineering FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR1,953 crore and adjusted EBITDA 20% to INR326 crore, with a new INR290 crore casting capex announced.
513519|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 7% YoY to INR506 crore, but export shipments slipped as roughly INR20 crore of sales (largely export laminations and machine components) could not be dispatched in March due to container and energy disruptions. Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 15.9%, though Q4 margins were hit by a mid-quarter energy and commodity spike. Management announced a greenfield casting facility in Hyderabad (INR290 crore, casting capacity to 36,000 tons by Q1 FY30) and said Q1 FY27 will not be worse than Q4 but will not see a sharp recovery. Net debt is about INR570 crore, with a working-capital release of about INR125 crore expected.

segments.name: Traction motor and railway components
segments.commentary: 33% of FY26 revenue, down from 38% per analyst; Q4 absolute sales about INR165 crore vs INR178 crore a year earlier, attributed to about INR20 crore of export shipments slipping (Wabtec, Siemens Mobility).

segments.name: Power generation
segments.commentary: 15% of FY26 revenue; management describes demand as stable across DG sets, thermal and hydro plants.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial motors
segments.commentary: 13% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Special purpose motors
segments.commentary: 7% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Mining, oil and gas
segments.commentary: 6% of FY26 revenue; cited as a growth area in new product development.

segments.name: Renewable energy (wind)
segments.commentary: 3% of FY26 revenue; growth moderated but offset by data centers and industrial motors.

segments.name: Data centers
segments.commentary: 3% of FY26 revenue; three new data-center programmes added, with commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Lamination and assemblies volume
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 18,400 tons (+7.3% YoY); FY26 volume 69,517 tons (+10% YoY), with assemblies growing faster than loose lamination.

segments.name: Raw casting and machine components volume
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 2,783 tons, with temporary year-end softness; FY26 volume 12,012 tons (+15.4% YoY).

guidance_outlook: FY27 targets: lamination sales of about 78,000 tons (about 72% of stated capacity) and machine components of about 16,000 tons; management estimates about INR2,300 crore top line at current commodity prices.
Consolidated lamination capacity is about 108,000 tons (no standalone/subsidiary split); no further lamination capex announced, and current capacity is sufficient to about FY28.
Q1 FY27 expected to be slightly slower than Q4 for both machine components and laminations, and not worse than Q4; no sharp recovery expected in Q1.

Working capital release of about INR125 crore expected as payables rise; net debt seen falling to about INR470 crore before current-year cash generation, and about INR250 crore by FY29 without further lamination capex.
Effective tax rate expected to remain around 33% for FY27 and FY28 due to ESOP, forex hedge accounting and depreciation differences; management did not give PAT guidance.

Maharashtra investment promotion subsidy (on about INR400 crore invested in Aurangabad over four years) may begin in FY27 under a 7-year recovery plan; company is seeking a 9-year plan or may defer accounting by one year.
ESOP cost of about INR10.3 crore per year continues in FY27 and then tapers off; a schedule is to be posted on the website.
capex_capacity: New greenfield casting and machine components facility in Hyderabad, adjacent to existing foundry, at INR290 crore; expected commissioning by Q1 FY30 (2 to 2.5 years), adding 11,400 tons and taking casting capacity to 36,000 tons.

Machine hour capacity to rise from 720,000 to 1.08 million hours, phased in from FY28 and FY29; about INR110-120 crore of the INR290 crore goes to the foundry and the rest to machining centres; allocation about 30% land and civil, 70% plant and machinery; asset turn about 1.2x.

Earlier capex (announced last year, INR150 crore): about INR100 crore spent as of 31 March 2026, with about INR50 crore pending; expected operational by end H1 FY27, debottlenecking casting capacity to 24,000 tons.
Capex funding: about INR100 crore from internal accruals, balance through net debt.
Q4 FY26 utilisation: sheet metal 80%, machining 87%, casting 64%; FY26 full year: sheet metal 76%, machining 81%, casting 71%.
demand_pricing: Quarterly price-change mechanism with international clients passes currency and commodity moves through; management says currency depreciation does not lift margins but helps India's cost competitiveness versus China.
Steel price exposure is managed by one month of raw material inventory and quarterly pricing offset; management says commodity hedging is not needed, while forex is 100% hedged.

Per-ton economics given: loose lamination about INR1.70-1.80 lakh/ton selling price; high value-added assembly about INR2.20-2.30 lakh/ton; raw casting EBITDA about INR30,000-35,000/ton; machined casting EBITDA about INR80,000-1 lakh/ton; loose lamination EBITDA about INR15,000-18,000/ton; high value-added assembly EBITDA about INR30,000-60,000/ton.
Mix: machine components about 80% export, 20% domestic; high value-added assemblies about one-third to 40% export; stator frame and rotor shaft assemblies roughly 50:50.
Management sees FY28 lamination volume of about 90,000 tons, of which about 60,000 tons loose and low value-added assemblies.

Export and new-customer pipeline: a competitor of an existing customer on a new export product from Q3 FY27; data-center casting and assemblies for Caterpillar, with commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27; Progress Rail added as a customer; Siemens Mobility served via Dakshin Foundry; Alstom is an existing Indian customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR290 crore greenfield capex for existing or new products, and what is the roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is for similar products (castings from 50 kg to 4 tons), targeting larger castings for mining, off-highway and data-center applications; machining expansion is modular from FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why did export revenue decline YoY in Q4, and when will the delayed sales be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: Foundry output fell from 1 March due to petroleum product (LPG) shortages, and containers were not moving in most of March, so about INR20 crore of mainly export sales slipped; recovery in Q1 will be a slog.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 outlook for volume, revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 targets of 78,000 tons lamination and 16,000 tons machine components, about INR2,300 crore revenue at current commodity prices; margins expected at similar percentages, with higher commodity prices lifting revenue but lowering percentage margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin fall about 100 bps despite the BCIPL ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore of higher-value sales were stuck in inventory without margin recognition, and a sharp mid-quarter energy-cost spike occurred after the quarterly price change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt trajectory and debt-free plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR570 crore now, falling to about INR470 crore after INR125 crore working-capital release, and about INR250 crore by FY29 without further lamination capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the effective tax rate about 30-33%, and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by non-deductible ESOP cost, uncrystallised forex losses on hedge accounting and depreciation differences; expected to persist for a couple of years, falling only slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not hedge commodities, and how does pricing work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says forex is 100% hedged and commodity hedging is unnecessary: one month of raw material inventory is consumed at prior-quarter cost, and customer prices reset one month later (1 May for Q1 FY27).

risks_watch: Energy (LPG) and West Asia disruptions; management says the energy situation is not fully normalised and Q1 FY27 will be slightly slower.
Export logistics: container movement and shipping constraints delayed about INR20 crore of sales in March 2026.
Timing and depreciation of machine-hour capex: machine delivery and ramp-up pace, lease-financed machines, and capitalisation dates are uncertain; no PAT guidance given.
Maharashtra subsidy recovery: 7-year plan may be too heavy versus Maharashtra sales; a 9-year plan or one-year deferral is under negotiation.
Working-capital release of INR125 crore depends on resuming inventory consumption and payables rising; inventory held near INR390-400 crore versus earlier INR300 crore target.
Data-center and Caterpillar programmes and the non-ferrous/ aerospace expansion are at development or sampling stage; commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27.

513519|2026-06.headline: Pitti Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹529 crores, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 16.8% and Lamination FY27 volume target raised to 82,000 tons.

Adjusted PAT was ₹32 crores versus ₹26 crores a year earlier. Lamination and assembly volume grew 19% to about 19,200 tons, and management raised its FY27 Lamination target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons. Management said the ₹150 crore capex (sheet metal capacity now 108,000 tons) has just commenced, while the ₹290 crore Hyderabad greenfield casting project is about ₹60 crores spent. Margins were flat YoY, which management attributed to pre-operating manpower and variable costs ahead of operating leverage.

Management said the call was mainly about the strategic transition to a multi-vertical model using existing assets: Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions have started and are ramping up, Apparel Solutions is due a couple of quarters out, and Home Textiles (especially Sheeting) will be rightsized. Net leverage was described as range-bound at about INR2,550 crores.

segments.commentary: Uses shared sheeting and knit processing capacity of about 90 million meters by year-end (vs 61 million meters earlier for home textiles, excluding knit). Full-capacity revenue potential about INR1,000 crores; revenue generation has started.

segments.commentary: Planned for Phase 2, expected to launch a couple of quarters later; no revenue contribution discussed yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise so much debt and how do tariffs affect the US business?
qa_highlights.answer: The recent NCD raise balances debt tenors and maturities and is not incremental capital. US tariff policy flip-flops created inflation and altered demand; tariff outlook has stabilised.

514183|2026-03.headline: Black Rose Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% and EBITDA about 90% YoY, with EBITDA margin up to 11% from 9.7%, helped by stock-and-sale model and price normalisation.
514183|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 showed a sharp jump, with revenue up 38% and EBITDA up about 90%, driven by the stock-and-sale model in distribution and growth in manufacturing. For the full year, standalone revenue dipped slightly as chemical prices corrected from the start of the year through March 2026, while volumes grew in domestic distribution and acrylamide liquid and NMA. The company stayed debt-free, inventories fell, and a 125% dividend was recommended. Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA or revenue numbers, saying only that top line is targeted to grow over FY26 at current prices.

financial_highlights.change: up from 9.7% in the prior year

financial_highlights.value: about 35% of prior-year revenue; balance from distribution

segments.name: Chemical distribution
segments.commentary: Backbone of the company; stock-and-sale model ensured uninterrupted supply through the Middle East disruption and supported Q4 revenue and margins. Merchant exports fell due to US tariffs and weaker US oil and gas offtake, though a strong export order pipeline is expected to convert in Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Capacity 32,000 MTPA, of which 20,000 MTPA is for merchant sales and the balance is captive. Volumes grew on new domestic and export customers after exiting the Morbi ceramic binder business; margins improved on raw material management. Export demand picked up in the second half of the current quarter.

segments.commentary: Capacity 3,600 MTPA. Volumes stable despite continued imports from China; management calls the business steady.

segments.commentary: Capacity 2,000 MTPA. Significant volume growth in FY26; company is the sole supplier to a key Indian customer. Volumes guided stable for the coming period, with new customer additions as the focus.

segments.commentary: In R&D and piloting; commercialisation targeted within FY27. Specialty amines project with Koei Chemicals is progressing, with an investment decision expected in the current year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was a mix of inventory gain and operating gain, with volumes rising. Only a 15-day period was affected by the war. No quarterly figure was confirmed.

qa_highlights.answer: The closure notice has been permanently revoked, so operations continue without interruption.

514211|2026-06.headline: Sumeet Industries Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 3.24% (EBITDA INR8.85 crore) on raw material volatility, while management guides ~6% margin and 30%+ revenue growth for FY27.
514211|2026-06.overview: Revenue (income) rose over 9% YoY to INR272.74 crore, but EBITDA was INR8.85 crore (3.24% margin) and PAT was INR1.14 crore, which management attributed to crude-driven PTA/MEG volatility, higher freight costs and a 15-day maintenance shutdown. Production fell 17% QoQ, with sales supported by inventory liquidation. Management said the rights issue (INR199.75 crore gross, net ~INR194.90 crore) is being deployed to working capital, the Nakoda CP plant, debt repayment (~INR23 crore) and a 6.5 MW solar plant. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 30%+ revenue growth, ~6% EBITDA margin and 3.5–4% PAT margin, with the Nakoda plant now guided for Q2 FY28.

segments.commentary: Management said value-added yarn is now 30–35% of yarn production. Demand described as good across POY, FDY and texturised yarn, with no demand issue if the Middle East conflict settles.

segments.commentary: Existing CP capacity cited as 300 tpd, with yarn drawing at 240 tpd. The acquired Nakoda CP plant (140,000 tpa) is expected to roughly double total capacity once commissioned.

Rights issue: 16.84 crore shares at INR11.86, raising INR199.75 crore; net ~INR194.90 crore allocated ~INR100 crore working capital, ~INR50 crore Nakoda operationalisation, ~INR23 crore debt repayment, ~INR22 crore solar captive plant.
