segments.commentary: Management guided Ashoka to grow about 30-35% in FY27; FY26 Ashoka revenue was about INR308 crore per an analyst's calculation that management did not dispute. Core markets are North America (incl. Canada), UK and Europe, with Australia and New Zealand also growing.

segments.name: Truly Indian (mainstream US brand)
segments.commentary: Management expects Truly Indian revenue of INR75-80 crore in FY27 if things go well. Listed in about 3,000 US stores including Costco, Raley's, Safeway-Albertsons and Whole Foods; repeat rotations are seen at some Costco divisions.

segments.name: B2B and private label
segments.commentary: B2B and private label make up about 20% of revenue. Distribution business added new regional brands and Ashoka SKUs (staples, oils, flour), with SKUs rising from about 440 to about 600.

segments.name: GCC / Middle East
segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue (described as under 15%). Shipments were nil in March and about 80-85% of GCC business was lost, with only 1-2 ports operating in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-1,000 crore, conditional on West Asia stabilising within about a month; management said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues.

Capex of INR20-25 crore in FY27 (pizza base line, Surat balance payments), plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking; a further US warehouse is planned around Q3 FY27.
Potential INR30 crore quarterly revenue risk from GCC on a run-rate basis, as an analyst framed it and management confirmed.
capex_capacity: Approximately INR124 crore capex over the last 2 years across Nadiad, Nashik brownfield and Surat greenfield; Surat total investment including Phase 2 is a little above INR100 crore.

Surat utilisation expected at about 35-40% in Phase 1 during FY27; Phase 2 contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27.
Average capacity utilisation across product lines was about 70-75% in FY26.

Debottlenecking at Nadiad and Nashik (flatbread and snack lines) drove most of the FY26 volume growth.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 growth was about 60-65% volume-driven, with the balance from product mix and rupee depreciation; management said prices were not increased.
Truly Indian initial traction is mainly distribution-led, with some repeats at Costco and other chains; management sees the Indian ethnic category at an inflection point in the US mainstream channel.
No impact seen from GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic) on demand; the whole range is vegetarian and vegan.
GCC shipments were nil in March 2026 because shipping lines were not taking containers. Other markets saw longer transit times and higher freight rates but no loss of sales.
Freight costs rose sharply in March 2026 as vessels were jammed and US routes lengthened; the company shares freight cost with GCC distributors 50:50 on those routes.
Tariff refund: applications filed for upwards of USD 1.5 million following a Supreme Court directive; nothing received in FY26, and any refund will be accrued in the year received.

qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR925-1,000 crore band, conditional on the Middle East reopening. Ashoka is expected to grow 30-35% and Truly Indian INR75-80 crore. With zero GCC, growth is 12-15% (about INR800-850 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East (GCC) impact and worst-case scenario?

qa_highlights.question: Surat plant ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Surat contribution is INR40-50 crore; full capacity implies INR200-250 crore once Phase 2 is complete. Full utilisation is targeted in year 3.

qa_highlights.answer: Freight rose by about 3-4% of revenue in March. The CFO said about 1 percentage point should be added to the base, with normalisation expected over about two months.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and total Surat spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat total is a little above INR100 crore. FY27 capex is INR20-25 crore (pizza line and balance payments) plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is the final year of the PLI scheme, expected at a similar level (about INR16 crore). The scheme covered 50% of marketing spend.

Freight and logistics costs: March spike of about 3-4% of revenue; management expects normalisation but this is unproven.
Loss of PLI incentive after FY27 (about INR16 crore per year) will remove a support to margins.
Surat ramp-up: Phase 2 starts in Q3 FY27 and contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27; execution risk.
Freezer capacity in the US warehouse is above 100%, which requires outside storage and a new distribution centre.

519183|2026-06.headline: ADF Foods Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, but EBITDA margin of 17.7% was flattered by INR19.69 crore tariff refund; freight cost ~3% of revenue.
519183|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with consolidated EBITDA up 26% to INR29.7 crore (17.7% margin) and PAT up 13.4% to INR17.3 crore. Management said the figures include tariff-refund benefit, and that adjusting for freight (~3% of revenue) the margin would be about 13.4% to 16.4% depending on the basis quoted on the call. Standalone revenue rose 20.5% to INR120.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 22.8%. Shipments were constrained by container and vessel shortages, with about 30% of ready goods unshipped in June, and management reiterated FY27 revenue above INR900 crore with high-teens EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore, up 28.5% YoY, with segment EBITDA of INR31.2 crore (21.6%). Management attributed the margin to product mix and frozen foods momentum.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.2 crore at 11.5% margin. Management said quarterly segment margins are seasonal and full-year margins will track historical ranges.

segments.name: Brands (Ashoka, Truly Indian, Soul)
segments.commentary: Ashoka growing above 30% in the latest quarter, with a 5-year revenue CAGR above 20%. Truly Indian is in 3,000+ US stores, with about 60% of growth from existing stores and 40% from new listings. Soul relaunch is still slow.

segments.name: B2B / private label
segments.commentary: Management put the sales split at about 75% own brands and 25% B2B and private label.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue upwards of INR900 crore, conditional on geopolitical and shipping conditions easing.
High-teens EBITDA margin guided for FY27 and beyond, excluding tariff refunds; management expects a return to 16-17% over about nine months as freight pass-through takes effect.
Freight pass-through began in Q1 FY27: about 75% in the US and 65-70% of total business overall, with some markets deliberately not passed on.
Surat revenue of about INR40-50 crore expected in FY27, with management saying the number is intact.
Surat full-scale utilisation expected in 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation this year and full utilisation around FY30.
Depreciation to rise by INR25-30 crore as Surat Phase 2 lines come in around Q3, with a further INR20-25 crore capex in FY27.
PLI scheme (about INR16 crore in FY26, about 2% of revenue) is in its final year; management hopes for an extension.
Q2 shipments expected to carry forward from Q1, but the carry-forward could slip into Q3 if container constraints persist.
Management said there are no further US tariff refunds expected; a USD2.8 million court award is under recovery discussion.
capex_capacity: Surat greenfield facility (frozen foods) began commercial deliveries and initial container shipments after commencing trial production in late March 2026; about 15 containers shipped in early Q1.
Surat at full capacity is expected to deliver a little under INR300 crore in revenue. Combined with brownfield capacity, total potential is about INR1,250 crore ex-agency at full ramp.
Phase 2 lines at Surat are expected in Q3, with residual capex of INR20-25 crore for FY27.
Management expects full utilisation of the combined capacity around FY30.
demand_pricing: Order book described as the strongest in company history for June, July and August, but about 30% of ready goods could not be shipped in June because of container and vessel shortages.
Management said consumer demand for ready-to-eat, frozen and shelf-stable Indian foods remains healthy across markets.
Pricing: freight costs passed through to customers from Q1 FY27 (about 3% of revenue impact). Tariff benefits will be passed back selectively by category to support market share.
Competition in Truly Indian is mainly from local US manufacturers of Indian-style foods, not Indian brands.
Management said the UK and Europe region should grow at high double digits, supported by a planned Ireland step-down subsidiary and FTAs.
West Asia disruption: March was very weak with no shipments; shipments resumed from end-April and are back near the 15% share of business previously affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and when will it reach the INR275 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full capacity will take 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight impact on margin and what is sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight impact about 3% of consolidated revenue; margin ex-freight was about 16.4% and about 13.4% after adjusting for tariff refund. Guidance is high-teens, with freight pass-through supporting recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR900 crore revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains cautiously optimistic, conditional on easing geopolitical and shipping conditions; the order book and demand support it.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment of the remaining tariff refund balance in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance will be evaluated against customer arrangements and recognised over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI contribution and its impact after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: PLI was about INR16 crore in FY26 (about 2% of margin). Final year is FY27; management expects brand investment as a % of sales to fall as brands scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 see catch-up from Q1 shipment shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Some carry-forward is expected in Q2, but it could slip into Q3 if container availability does not improve.

risks_watch: Container and vessel availability; a carry-forward of unshipped goods could push revenue from Q2 into Q3.
Freight costs and whether pass-through holds in the US, where roughly 75% of freight increase is being passed on.
Tariff: the 10% rate is still applicable, with no certainty on the future rate.
Margin dependence on the one-time tariff refund and on PLI, which ends after FY27.
Surat ramp-up is slow (about 30% utilisation this year), which limits near-term operating leverage.
Soul domestic brand is growing slowly, while brand investments in Truly Indian and Soul continue.

So, I think it's still continuing at 10% only at the moment. How it goes future is anyone's guess, Saurabh.
So basically, we have lot of structured programs in our manufacturing and supply chain operations.

519397|2026-03.headline: Sharat Industries FY26 revenue rose about 38% to Rs 524.7 crore and PAT about 60% to Rs 15.90 crore, while Q4 was hit by Middle East disruption and fishmeal costs.
519397|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a strong year on revenue and profit, with export revenue up about 23% and export volumes up about 8%. Q4 revenue grew about 25% YoY to Rs 117.24 crore, but margins were squeezed by the West Asia conflict, which forced rerouting of Middle East-bound shipments, higher logistics costs and inventory build-up, along with sharp fishmeal and soya price increases. US tariffs on Indian shrimp fell from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026, and management is targeting FY27-28 export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore. Management framed the Q4 margin pressure as largely external and event-driven rather than a change in the underlying business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: US and China make up roughly 40% of export portfolio; Russia, Southeast Asia, Europe and Middle East the remaining 60%. Value-added products were about 7-10% of export volume in FY26, with management hoping to double that share by volume if conditions normalise.

segments.name: Domestic / feed and farming
segments.commentary: Q4 is the start of stocking season in Andhra Pradesh farming, but sharp fishmeal and soya price increases hurt margins. Feed market share is sub 2%. Sales to Hyperpure began in Q4 FY26 with base products such as raw frozen shrimp.

segments.name: Processing
segments.commentary: Premium black tiger shrimp and new value-added products are a stated priority. A 1 MW captive solar plant is partly commissioned in Q4, with the balance due shortly.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term roadmap to FY27-28 targets annual export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore, via deeper Russia and China penetration, re-entry into the EU and a measured domestic and value-added build-out.
US exports expected to scale up significantly versus the last couple of years in FY27, but management is cautious and will revisit clarity around end of the quarter.
Value-added share of export volume hoped to double from 7-10% if export conditions normalise.
EU FTA expected to take effect over the rest of calendar 2026; benefits to accrue gradually.
Raw material prices and realisations expected to keep moving through the cycle; management hopes the fishmeal spike is temporary.
capex_capacity: 1 MW solar plant for captive consumption at processing division: partly commissioned in Q4 FY26, balance to be commissioned shortly.
Insect protein substitution for fishmeal in feed: pilot farming under way for over a year, with farm-level results described as encouraging.
Management aims to improve processing plant utilisation and unlock operating leverage via contract farming and asset-light merchant exports; slight utilisation improvement was seen in FY26.
No quantified capacity, utilisation percentage or capex amount was given.
demand_pricing: About 20 containers were planned for Middle East shipments in Q4; about half were rerouted on customer advice, about five were in transit and needed rescue by shipping liners, and the rest are held as inventory being reprocessed for alternate destinations.
US tariffs on Indian shrimp cut from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026; US is about 35-40% of export value. No new US clients were added in FY26 due to tariff turbulence.
Russia: two new clients added in FY26. China: new black tiger shrimp product, about five customers worked with so far.
PD Curl control product (launched in Russia) delivers incremental EBITDA margin of more than 5% up to about 10% over base EBITDA, but volumes are low.
Indian shrimp exports are about Rs 50,000-55,000 crore; company share is 0.5-0.75%.
Fishmeal price spike attributed to global demand and heavy Indian exports; industry has petitioned government for relief.

qa_highlights.question: How much business was hit by the West Asia conflict, and have deferred orders been recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20 containers were planned for Middle East in Q4; half were rerouted to other destinations, about five were in transit and needed safe handling at extra cost, and the remainder sit in inventory being reprocessed for other markets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key drivers of the ~60% PAT growth versus EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited export diversification (China black tiger shrimp via a partner processor), slightly higher capacity utilisation, and value-added products improving margins; geopolitical shocks would otherwise have allowed better margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PD Curl control product's potential and where can it go next?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental EBITDA margin of more than 5% up to about 10% over base; volumes are currently low, and management plans to add products to the Russian portfolio this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the company's market shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Share of Indian shrimp exports is about 0.5%, ranging 0.5-0.75%; feed market share is sub 2%, described as a minority position.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added share of exports and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added products were about 7-10% of export volume in FY26; the company hopes to double that share by volume if export conditions are normal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling the fishmeal price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Insect protein substitution is in pilot; some costs passed to contract farmers; the company aims for better export contracts with improved margins; industry has sought government relief.

risks_watch: Fishmeal and soya cost inflation, which hit Q4 margins and may persist.
Middle East conflict: inventory of rerouted cargo must be sold through alternate channels; logistics costs elevated.
Weather-related farm risk flagged for the rest of calendar 2026.
US demand normalisation and recession risk; tariff level sustainability.
EU FTA ratification timing across member states; benefit may take time.
Q4 seasonal softness and whether margins recover in the next quarter.

519552|2026-03.headline: Heritage Foods Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR 11,576 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.5% on procurement inflation of 8%.
519552|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 10% YoY to INR 11,576 million and FY26 revenue reached INR 45,260 million. 520057|2026-03.headline: JTEKT India FY26 sales grew 11% vs 9% PV market, but full-year EBITDA margin slipped to 7.5% from 7.6% on mix and forex.
520057|2026-03.overview: FY26 sales grew 11% against passenger vehicle market growth of 9%, helped by GST cuts and new Maruti Suzuki models (e Vitara, Victoris). Second-half EBITDA margin recovered to 8.48% from 7.71%, while H1 margin was 6.3%, leaving the full year at 7.5%. Management attributed the margin drag to product mix (Honda down about 33%, 0.33% impact), a forex accounting effect (0.23%) and US tariffs (0.24%), which it called largely temporary. New capacity (CVJ line 2, MS Gear line 5 and 6, CPS line 3) is still under-utilised, and management expects it to reach full utilisation over 1 to 1.5 years. A Brazil export order from the JTEKT group starts dispatch in May 2026.

segments.name: CVJ (driveline)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about INR 130 crore per management; line 2 (from Nov 2025, capacity about 370,000 units) is 27% utilised, line 1 about 83%. Full two-line volume targeted at about INR 250 crore with the Maruti EV MPV from October 2026.

segments.name: Manual gear (MS Gear)
segments.commentary: Line 5 at Dharuhera is at 106% utilisation; line 6 is at 21%, expected to reach 60% then 80-90%. Company holds 40-45% share of manual gear business.

segments.name: CPS
segments.commentary: Line 3 at Bawal is about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.

Brazil (Stellantis) order to start dispatch in May 2026, about 70,000 units in FY27 (management cited 70,000 this year and 100,000-150,000 next year), with potential to reach 5 lakh units per year.
Honda's EV SUV from Tapukara expected around December 2026, optimistically about 40,000 units and about INR 100 crore business for JTEKT.

Management expects the margin pressures from product mix and forex accounting to be temporary; US tariff reduced from 50% to 10% after the Supreme Court ruling, which management expects to lift US exports.
Capex for FY27 expected to be lower than the last two years; about INR 100 crore more for the Gujarat plant (total committed about INR 250 crore, INR 130 crore spent), plus normal capex.
capex_capacity: CVJ line 2 commissioned November 2025; capacity about 7.54 lakh units per annum (about 3.8 lakh vehicle sets); line 2 utilisation 27%, line 1 about 83%; work started on a third CVJ line.
MS Gear line 5 at Dharuhera 106% utilised; MS Gear line 6 at 21%; MS Gear line 4 at Chennai for export not yet started (SOP pending); capacity about 3.5-4 lakh per MS Gear line.
CPS line 3 at Bawal about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.
Chennai rack and pinion line for Brazil export with installed capacity about 4 lakh units.

CWIP of about INR 411 crore; management asked analysts to track CWIP as it will weigh on ratios for 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: PV market grew 9% in FY26, with 16.7% growth in H2 after GST cut (28% to 18% for small cars; 50% to 40% for larger ones); H1 growth was only 1.6%.
Honda's passenger vehicle business fell about 30%, reducing JTEKT's sales (almost 100% supplier to Honda); Renault-Nissan export models fell about 16%, Toyota about 4%.
Raw material cost pass-through to customers is back-to-back with a time lag, per management.
Competition in CVJ from GKN-linked and other suppliers, which hold over 60% of Maruti's business; management targets at least 15% CVJ share.
Management said it is not supplying Renault's Duster.

qa_highlights.question: Why have gross margins declined from 29% to 27% over two years, and how should they trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margin was 6.3% and H2 8.48%; net variable cost drag of 0.18% came from a 0.33% mix effect (Honda, Renault-Nissan, Toyota down; Maruti GST-driven models higher), 0.23% forex accounting effect and 0.24% US tariffs, offset by export gains and lower warranty. Management called these temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Has Toyota's Bidadi third line commenced, and what is Toyota's revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bidadi line had not commenced per its understanding; a new Maharashtra facility is expected in H1 FY29, lifting Toyota capacity to about 1 lakh vehicles. JTEKT is the only steering supplier to Toyota.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for other driveline products beyond CVJ and hub bearings for JTEKT's group?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan is finalised; management said it needs 1-1.5 years to stabilise CVJ first. It noted export opportunities for CVJ parts to group entities.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the INR 1,000 crore top-line addition by FY27 and whether revenue can double in 3-4 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 300 crore was added in FY26; with 10% market growth and INR 75-100 crore exports, about INR 500 crore more is possible in FY27 (about INR 800 crore total). It declined to share a formal business plan and said growth depends on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 capex and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex will be lower than the last two years, with about INR 100 crore for Gujarat plus normal capex. ROCE excluding CWIP is above 11%, and full utilisation should push it back toward earlier levels (about 16-17%).

qa_highlights.question: Driveline pipeline, CVJ margins and fixed asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: CVJ margins are better than most MS Gear products and it is 100% localised. Target fixed asset turnover is about 3x overall; CVJ is lower (about 1.5x), CPS 2.5-3x, manual gear 2-2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Potential for exports to US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brazil is the first step, with a Stellantis order, and that a further order could follow once quality and cost are established. No firm US or Europe plan was given.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and working capital status?

qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Lala said it is a SEBI LODR disclosure requirement for reporting lines one level below the CEO after recent promotions; no board induction planned.

522113|2026-03.headline: Timken India Q4 FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for first time, up 14.2% YoY to INR10,731 million; PBT margin 19.3%.
522113|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue from operations was INR10,731 million (up 14.2% YoY), the first quarter above INR1,000 crore, with PBT of INR2,074 million (19.3% margin) after a labour code impact. FY26 standalone revenue hit a record INR31,478 million (up 8.6%), with PBT of INR5,304 million (up about 3%) and PBT margin of 15.5%. The Board approved merging Timken GGB into Timken India. Management flagged input cost inflation entering FY27, with price pass-through only about 10% achieved so far, and said the new Bharuch plant is ramping slowly with about INR80 crore of FY26 revenue.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR205 crore (19%), up 22% QoQ. FY26 INR681 crore (20%).

segments.name: Distribution (industrial and aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR162 crore (15%). FY26 INR582 crore (17%).

segments.name: Process industry
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR200 crore (19%). FY26 INR651 crore (19%).

segments.name: Exports (intercompany)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR222 crore (21%), up about 40% QoQ from INR159 crore in Q3 and up about 66% YoY on the full year. FY26 INR707 crore (21%).

segments.name: GGB (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR16.6 crore and PBT INR4.6 crore, a PBT margin of about 30-32%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 top-line growth above market growth and says it will outgrow the market; no numerical revenue or margin guidance was given.

Price increases to offset raw material inflation (steel, grinding wheels, coolants, currency): about 10% achieved as of the call, with the aim of completing most of the pass-through over the current and next quarter.
Bharuch CRB/SRB plant expected to reach about 70% utilisation by July-August 2026, improving monthly after that.
Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR120 crore capex): first production targeted for November-December 2026, with asset turns of about 2x to start.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of revenue (management pegged last two years at about 8.5%), covering Jamshedpur rail, GGB plain bearings at Bharuch and some heat-treatment investment.
Management said the 65:35 domestic-manufactured to imported mix may hold for the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bharuch new plant: all lines capitalised; smaller lines and spherical lines running near full, large-line PPAPs under way, and CRB lines running close to two shifts. More than 100 new part introductions underway. FY26 revenue from the plant about INR80 crore (Q4 about INR60 crore, Q3 about INR12 crore). Management said the plant is still close to breakeven.

Bharuch total investment about INR720 crore including forex; buildings about INR350 crore; plant and machinery roughly INR310-320 crore by management's estimate. Peak revenue said to be close to 2x asset turns, but management ruled out INR1,000 crore.
Jamshedpur rail expansion: about INR120 crore capex, imported robotic machines from Europe, all approvals in place. Management said the building was built with spare capacity.
Plain bearing expansion at Bharuch and renewable energy investments are progressing; management said both are broadly on track.
Capital is debt-free; management said it will consider further expansion (0-8 inch range for CV and tractors, M&A) if the project is right.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is stable across most segments and is not among its top three concerns; cost escalation and pass-through, Bharuch ramp-up/PPAP, and expansion projects are the top three.
Steel MRO is slow and steel melt was lower in the quarter; cement MRO is good. OE sentiment is wait-and-watch because of geopolitics.
North America export demand is gaining momentum even without a signed US trade deal; the US is about 50% of exports, per the analyst.
CV demand described as robust with cyclicality; tractors okay; rail slow and steady; aftermarket okay.
Pricing: price increases began mid-April 2026 for both pass-through and recovery; about 10% realised, with automotive customers expected to delay. Management hopes for retrospective recovery.
Management said the Indian bearing market is about USD 2-2.5 billion (about 65% mobile, 35% stationary) and expects process and distribution to grow fastest.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken to offset raw material inflation, and will there be margin pressure in the next 1-2 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Price pass-through has only begun, at about 10%; management expects the rest over the current and next quarter, with the automotive OEM segment lagging. Management did not quantify the margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for domestic rail, CV, and US exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 exports were INR222 crore (up about 40% QoQ, up about 66% YoY for the full year); rail was INR278 crore in Q4 (slight YoY decline); CV described as robust.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch utilisation targets and FY26 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue about INR80 crore; utilisation expected to reach about 70% by July-August 2026, then improve monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Segment split for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4: rail 26%, mobile others 19%, distribution 15%, process 19%, exports 21% (total INR1,073 crore including intercompany). FY26 total INR3,419 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Jamshedpur capex timeline and asset turns; FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Production targeted for November-December 2026 at about 2x asset turns to start. FY27 capex expected at 8-10% of revenue; no formal capex guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend level?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY26 final dividend was INR2.5 per share on INR10 face value, down from INR36 previously. Management said it pays large dividends every 3-4 years and will consider the shareholder's request.

522113|2026-06.headline: Timken India Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~15% YoY to INR929 crore, with PBT of INR150 crore and PBT margin of 16.2%.
522113|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR929 crore, up almost 15% YoY, after a seasonally strong Q4 FY26 (highest standalone revenue of INR3,147 crore for FY26). PBT rose to INR150 crore from INR130 crore, with PBT margin at 16.2% versus 16.1% a year earlier, and EBITDA margin at 19.6%. Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to heavy-truck and off-highway price increases offsetting unfavourable Q1 mix. The Bharuch plant is ramping up quickly, with revenue of about INR50 crore in the quarter and near breakeven.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR200 crore, about 22% of Q1 revenue. Management described government railway buying as slow and sluggish, and said the year started with about 3% growth in rail.

segments.name: Mobile / others
segments.commentary: INR184 crore. Management said mobile (tractors, heavy trucks) is about 20% of the business and is where price increases are sticking.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR153.9 crore (about INR154 crore).

segments.name: Process
segments.commentary: INR186 crore, up about 28-30% YoY, driven by metals customers and wind (gearbox exports and domestic wind farms).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR200 crore, including about 1% export incentive. Intercompany push to America rose about 21%; Europe is down, China and ASEAN are down, and the US is up.

segments.name: Bharuch plant (within segments)
segments.commentary: About INR50 crore revenue in Q1, close to breakeven. Spherical roller bearing (SRB) line utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, targeted at about 70% by August-September; CRB line utilisation is lower, with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

guidance_outlook: Bharuch SRB line expected to reach about 70% utilisation in August-September 2026; CRB line ramp toward end of Q2 and Q3.
Rail expansion at Jamshedpur expected to start commercial production by calendar year-end 2026; management said it will ramp up immediately after that.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of sales, with project work described as on track; timing may spill some capex into FY28.
Further cost escalation seen as limited beyond the steel, carbide, coal and grinding increases already in the system; base oil described as the only volatile input.
Management said it will continue to pass on cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew; rail and PSU/ARC contracts are fixed and will reprice only at renewal.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramping up; three manufacturing lines; utilisation cannot be given at plant level but SRB demand is higher than CRB at this stage.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur on track; plain bearings investment at Bharuch on track.
Manufactured vs traded mix roughly 75/25, similar to prior quarters.
Gas conversion from LPG to natural gas completed across supply chain and plants.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven by resilient core-segment demand and both export and domestic execution.
Steel producers raised prices by about INR1,500-1,600 per tonne in January and about INR3,500 per tonne by April, around INR5,000 per tonne in total; most customers have started paying the increase.
Price pass-through is working in heavy truck and tractor/off-highway; rail, PSU and cement customers are on fixed annual rate contracts.
Process growth partly from metals projects (mills built in India for export) and wind.
Management said the US market is up, Europe and China are down, and ASEAN and Australia are flat to down.
No direct tariff figure given; management said the US landed tariff has moved over time and it would confirm the current rate.
Management said the parent's 80/20 portfolio review is aimed at performance improvement; no change in Indian strategy was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail INR200 crore (22%), mobile/others INR184 crore, distribution INR153.9 crore, process INR186 crore, exports about INR200 crore including 1% export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of parent's 80/20 strategy and belts divestment on India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80/20 is a Pareto-based performance tool that is being applied globally; it is not yet a change in strategy for India. The India focus stays on off-highway, rail and tractor/heavy-truck, with no two-wheeler, passenger car or washing-machine ball bearings.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch ramp-up and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Bharuch revenue was about INR50 crore, close to breakeven. SRB utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, expected to reach about 70% by August-September; CRB is lower with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of process and export growth and US outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Process grew about 30% YoY, from metals and wind. Exports to the US are growing, Europe is down, and the intercompany push to America is about 21%.

qa_highlights.question: Rail outlook and Jamshedpur ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Government railway procurement is slow due to funds diverted to infrastructure and defence; management expects this to be timing-related. Jamshedpur rail capacity is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation has been passed through to price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to give an exact percentage; heavy truck and tractor customers have largely passed through cost escalation, while rail and PSU contracts will reprice at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex plan and allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-wise split not given; capex directionally in line with the 8-10% of sales range, with some timing spillover into the next fiscal.

Slow government railway procurement due to fund diversion to infrastructure and defence; it could delay the Jamshedpur ramp-up benefit.
Bharuch ramp-up needs to reach about 70% SRB utilisation by August-September and CRB later; any slippage would weigh on margins.

Base oil price volatility affecting grease costs; the Brent outlook and the Middle East conflict affect energy and gas costs.
NCLT approval of the Timken GGB Technology merger is pending.

rows.why: Steel rose about INR5,000 per tonne in total and management said it will keep passing cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew, with most customers already paying.

522163|2026-06.headline: Diamond Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 129% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT rose 191% to INR58.5 crores, with FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crores.
522163|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR690 crores (up 129% YoY), EBITDA INR85 crores (12.3% margin, up ~200 bps) and PAT INR58.5 crores (8.5% margin). Management attributed the quarter's softness versus a normal Q1 to early, heavy monsoon flooding in Gujarat that hit medium and extra high voltage cable laying. The company completed a INR1,640 crore QIP (net INR1,614 crore), turning net worth positive at INR691 crore post-QIP from negative INR922 crore at June 30, 2026. Order book stood at INR3,688 crore as on August 11, 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore and FY28 of INR7,500 crore.

INR1,640 crore gross (INR1,614 crore net per Q&A)
INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 (~$445 mn), across 12 product lines
financial_highlights.change: ~2x FY26 revenue; >INR1,000 crore fresh wins since April

financial_highlights.value: Negligible in Q1 due to carried-forward losses; benefit expected for at least two years

segments.commentary: Largest order-book block; management targets moving mix up the voltage curve, with 66 kV and above EBITDA guided at 18–22%. A INR435 crore data center order sits in this band.

segments.name: Low voltage (1.1 kV) cables
segments.commentary: Q1 mix skewed toward LV and conductors because MV/EHV cannot be laid in flood conditions; LV EBITDA guided at 8–9%. New copper LV facility (brownfield, ~42,000 km capacity, revenue potential ~INR1,880 crore) targeted for FY28 commercial production.

segments.name: Conductors (incl. HTLS, AL-59)
segments.commentary: Conductor EBITDA guided at 9–10%. Management says AL-59 is now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped producing ACSR.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Currently negligible. Team being built; certifications for Europe and US in progress. Internal target of INR500 crore export order book by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the fourth rod mill, the incremental silane line and the CCV line, and sixth CCV line delivery.
qa_highlights.answer: Rod mill by 15 Oct, silane line by 15 Sep, CCV line in March 2027; sixth CCV line to be ordered this month, delivery assurance for August 2027 and commissioning by December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Net worth and use of QIP proceeds.
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth was negative INR922 crore at 30 June 2026 and is positive INR691 crore after the INR1,614 crore net QIP proceeds. Planned use: INR130 crore LV expansion, INR74 crore balancing equipment, INR325 crore general corporate purposes, INR350 crore promoter unsecured loan repayment, with about INR750 crore for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery expectation on the INR957 crore legacy receivables.
qa_highlights.answer: A special team is evaluating recovery; management expects about INR300 crore to be recovered over 12–18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation outlook after the audit qualification was resolved.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 depreciation will be the run-rate going forward, with pro-rata additions for new capex.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 phasing and utilisation for cables and conductors.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp will be gradual, with Q2 partly affected by rain and Q3–Q4 the strongest; utilisation is guided at ~40% for conductors and ~50–52% for cables in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin guidance and metal price sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 11–13% EBITDA margin, depending on metal prices; management cited aluminium moving from about $3,800 in May to about $3,000 by end-June. Mix is expected to improve as MV and EHV volumes rise in Q2–Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term debt and peak debt outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no substantial debt, the INR400 crore promoter unsecured loan has been repaid post-QIP and the INR1,900 crore promoter-held bonds are 0.01% payable after 30 years, with a net present value of INR47 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peer comparison given the flat Q-o-Q revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 softness to MV/EHV being laid at project sites that cannot be laid in rain, and said the peers' business is largely LV, so the cycle hits Diamond more.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration, including Adani.
qa_highlights.answer: Adani is about 40%+ of the order book, with a Board mandate to cut it to about 20% by year-end; the company is engaging about 670 active customers.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix at the INR14,000 crore peak and what could go wrong.
qa_highlights.answer: Conductors 30–35%, LV 10–15%, MV/EHV the remainder; data center target 20%, exports not yet sized beyond INR500 crore order target. Key risks are metal and polymer price moves requiring 20–30% more working capital, and execution capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crore, with management saying it is firmly on track and intends to hold the Q1 margin profile while delivering it.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 11–13%, dependent on metal prices; management said the absolute contribution stays steady under price-escalation contracts.
Q1 seasonality: management said an on-time monsoon would have added INR70–80 crore of top line and corresponding EBITDA in Q1.
FY28 revenue target of INR7,500 crore; management said the full-utilisation potential of INR14,000 crore is not expected in FY29.
Data center sales targeted at about INR750 crore in FY27 and INR1,500 crore in FY28 (about 20% of revenue); internal target of INR1,000 crore data center orders before 31 Mar 2027.
Export order book target of at least INR500 crore by year-end FY27; management said export guidance beyond this will be given after year-end.
Management said it expects around INR300 crore of legacy NCLT receivables (out of INR957 crore) to be recovered over 12–18 months.
capex_capacity: Two aluminium corrugation lines approved by the board for 66 kV and 132 kV cable capacity; capex about INR17 crore, achieved by converting one 33 kV line.

Sixth CCV line being ordered this month at an agreed price; delivery assurance for August 2027, commissioning expected by December 2027 with no additional civil or utility capex. Management said it triples capability in the target segment.

Two additional medium voltage cable lines under installation, said to be on schedule; one silane line expected by 15 Sep 2026, fourth rod mill by 15 Oct 2026, and one CCV line in March 2027 (per Q&A).

Copper LV and control cable facility converting old rod mill and legacy conductor plant (brownfield, no civil cost), about 42,000 km capacity and revenue potential about INR1,880 crore at full utilisation; commercial production FY28, commissioning before March 2027.

Capex per line per Q&A: silane line INR15–20 crore; CCV line about INR50 crore for the line plus about INR50 crore utilities and civil (about INR100 crore total), with revenue of about INR45–50 crore per line. Utilisation guided at conductors ~40% and cables ~50–52% in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.
demand_pricing: Order book INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 across 12 product lines, about 2x last year's revenue; over INR1,000 crore of fresh wins since April and about INR400 crore of orders in the last 6–7 days.
Order intake guided at INR275–325 crore per month; management said about INR2,800 crore of the book is to be executed before March 2027.
Adani Group share of the order book about 40%+, with a Board mandate to bring it to about 20% by year-end; around 670 active customers and 200+ in the current order book.

Gujarat disaster-management programme (Robust) estimated at INR22,000 crore over three years, of which INR16,000 crore is 11 kV and 33 kV MV cable; Rajesh Power 1,370 km order from Paschim Gujarat; management expects INR4,000–5,000 crore of Gujarat orders to be finalised by year-end.

Mix: management said MV and EHV cannot be laid in flooded sites, so Q1 skewed to LV and conductors; management said peers are mostly ~85% LV, whereas Diamond is ~70–80% MV/EHV. Conductor: AL-59 now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped making ACSR.
risks_watch: Phasing: FY27 guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore implies INR1,200–1,250 crore per quarter for Q2–Q4 against INR690 crore in Q1. Watch Q2 revenue.
Metal and polymer price volatility affecting gross margin and the pass-through lag; management's margin range is 11–13%.
Commissioning timelines: silane line (15 Sep 2026), rod mill (15 Oct 2026), CCV lines in March 2027 and December 2027; the new LV facility is due by March 2027 and commercial output in FY28.
Export certifications for Europe and the US; first export order targeted by Q3–Q4 FY27.
Working capital needs rising with metal and polymer costs and the need for vendor and dealer financing.
Customer concentration: Adani at 40%+ of the order book against the 20% target.
Monsoon and project-site disruption affecting MV/EHV laying in Q2 (described as partially affected).
key_quotes: We are completely back-to-back on passing the increases in metal and polymers to all our customers.
Our guidance is between 11% to 13%. This again depends upon the metal price.
The EBITDA guidance for the next year, we are confident we will maintain it between what I am telling you today, but we will work on how to improve upon it.
So, the rod mill should start by 15th of October. The incremental MV silane line should start somewhere by 15th of September, and the CCV line will start in March 2027.
522163|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, capacity and the FY27/FY28 targets, but measured on guidance specifics: the CEO-style speaker declined to give firm forward-looking assurances at the outset and repeatedly hedged margin and export numbers with metal-price and utilisation caveats. Tone was most defensive when addressing the Q-o-Q flatness versus peers and the Adani concentration.

rows.why: Utilisation is guided at only ~34% (conductors ~40%, cables ~50-52% in FY27), so capex is not needed for utilisation, but the board has already approved two aluminium corrugation lines (INR17 crore) and the sixth CCV line (~INR100 crore) is being ordered this month on demand, with further capex likely as the INR14,000 crore full-utilisation plan is scoped.

rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR4,300-4,500 crore while Q1 was INR690 crore, and margin guidance is hedged on metal prices, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Working capital needs and QIP-funded liquidity
rows.why: About INR750 crore of QIP proceeds is earmarked for working capital, and management flagged metal/polymer moves needing 20-30% more working capital as revenue ramps from INR690 crore to ~INR1,200 crore per quarter.

522195|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 39.22% to ₹322.06 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 26.80%, with management guiding ~30% growth to ₹500 crore gross revenue in FY27.
522195|2026-03.overview: Frontier Springs delivered FY26 revenue from operations of ₹322.06 crore (up 39.22%), EBITDA of ₹86.31 crore (up 73.80%) and PAT of ₹61.31 crore (up 76.88%). Q4 revenue was ₹82.54 crore (up 17.7% YoY, marginally above Q3) with EBITDA margin of 28.51%. Management guides FY27 gross revenue above ₹500 crore on an order book it put at ₹300-370 crore, and says it expects to hold margins at 23-24% or higher, while acknowledging steel-cost pressure could trim 1-2 points. Q&A centred on margin guidance, the FIBA product launch, air spring capacity and wagon tenders.

financial_highlights.change: up 17.7% YoY; marginally ahead of Q3 FY26
margin up 362 bps QoQ-stated as YoY in call and 462 bps YoY in call; call states both 362 bps and 462 bps

segments.name: Coil springs
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited by management as approximately ₹175 crore plus (analyst's recollection, confirmed as approximate gross figure). Management expects reasonable growth in FY27.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as ₹60 crore plus. A new 6-ton hammer was installed; it currently runs one 8-hour shift against 16 hours of available capacity. Management expects the strongest growth here in FY27.

segments.name: Air springs (coach sets)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as approximately ₹150 crore. Capacity is 300 coach sets per month; output is 180-200 per month. Realisation cited at about ₹1.25 lakh per air spring, described as slightly improved.

segments.name: FIBA (failure indication and brake application system)
segments.commentary: New product with RDSO basic approval and patent done; trials on trains start now, with about 6 months to regular supply. Management sizes the market at ₹40-50 crore and expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28. Margin said to be similar to air and coil springs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross revenue target above ₹500 crore, described as around 30% growth, backed by an order book of ₹300-370 crore disclosed on the call.
Margin target of 23-24% for the year, with management saying 26-28% is possible; management conceded 1-2 points could be lost on existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Medium-term growth of 25% per year beyond FY27 was stated; management also said 20-25% average growth is achievable across the three product lines.
FY27 capex planned at ₹20-25 crore across all three divisions, after about ₹20 crore in FY26; no term loans taken in several years.

Q4 FY27 is expected to be the strongest quarter, with the 6-ton hammer contributing from the third quarter onward; management expects the first-half revenue run-rate to break out of the ₹80-83 crore band.
capex_capacity: Air spring capacity 300 coach sets per month, utilisation 180-200 per month (about 60-67%); final testing is the bottleneck, and two more testing machines are planned.
Overall plant utilisation about 70% per management; a new automated coil spring line from China is under negotiation.
A 6-ton forging hammer was installed in FY26, joining 1-ton and 3-ton hammers; utilisation is one 8-hour shift out of 16 hours available.
FY27 capex of ₹20-25 crore across coil, air and forging divisions, focused on capacity and less manpower-intensive automation.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is ₹300-370 crore, mostly Railways. Orders come in daily, mainly small, and are not individually disclosed; the company agreed to post larger orders on the exchanges.
Railways' fixed-price contracts limit mid-contract price increases. Management is raising prices in new tenders to pass through steel and energy cost increases.
Railways' production plan for FY27 is about 6,000 passenger coaches and 1,200-1,400 locomotives, flat YoY; a large wagon tender is expected, with forging and springs supply.
Competition: no new spring or forging players, though more steel suppliers have been added by Railways, improving sourcing terms.
Q3 FY26 revenue was flagged as constrained by inspection delays, raw material delays and customer-side bottlenecks; the company is targeting a breakout above ₹82-83 crore per quarter.
Export: management said coil spring exports are not being pursued; forging exports to Europe and the US are being explored where margins are good.
Defence and non-rail forging (L&T, JCB, Caterpillar, cranes) are at sample or R&D stage; defence approvals are slow.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should be expected if steel prices stay high: 22-23% or 26-27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 23-24% for FY27 'if not 26-28%', citing negotiations with steel and energy suppliers and price increases in future tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between pass-through of commodity costs and the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing tenders at fixed prices may be lower; if the year completes, margin could fall by 1-2 points, but management aims to hold current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility for FY28-29 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific figure yet; management sees no order scarcity for 5-10 years and said growth of 25% is expected beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of FY26 revenue by division and air spring capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate gross figures: coil springs ₹175 crore plus, forging ₹60 crore plus, air springs ₹150 crore; air spring output 180-190 coach sets per month against 300 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue been stuck at ₹80-83 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks include delayed inspections by Railways inspectors and occasional raw material delays; management expects to break out in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FIBA opportunity and its FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Market of ₹40-50 crore; company is second indigenous source after imports, with 2-3 approved sources in total. Management expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28 once trials conclude.

risks_watch: Steel and energy costs: management concedes margin may fall 1-2 points on fixed-price existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Quarterly revenue has been stuck at ₹80-83 crore for three quarters; the FY27 ₹500 crore target depends on a sharp step-up.
Receivables are high at year end; management attributes this to high turnover and says there are zero bad debts. Next quarter's collections should be checked.
Timing of the large wagon tender and the FIBA trial and approval, both of which are needed for the second-half ramp-up.
Air spring testing bottleneck and whether two more testing machines are commissioned in time.
Defence and non-rail forging diversification is still at sample stage.

key_quotes: We enter FY26 with an order book of X300 crores which gives us good revenue visibility over guidance for FY26 as it crosses X500 crores in gross revenues to step up over 30% from what we delivered in FY26.

rows.why: The 6-ton hammer runs one 8-hour shift against 16 hours available, and management expects forging to grow fastest in FY27 with contribution from Q3 onward.

522205|2026-03.headline: Praj Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT before exceptionals fell to Rs 15.4 mn from Rs 582.5 mn; Q4 order intake Rs 6,580 mn, backlog Rs 43,050 mn.
522205|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 8,445 mn versus Rs 8,598 mn a year earlier, while PAT fell to Rs 116 mn from Rs 398 mn. FY26 revenue was Rs 31,679 mn (vs Rs 32,280 mn) and PAT was Rs 238 mn (vs Rs 289 mn). Management attributed margin pressure mainly to site execution cost escalation on delayed projects, continued investment in Praj GenX, and non-business one-time items, rather than raw material prices. Order intake was weak, with several engineering and GenX inquiries (about Rs 300 mn+ inquiry basket) deferred on raw material price uncertainty.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: 22% of FY26 revenue; 2% of Q4 order intake and 16% of backlog. Several opportunities deferred from Q4 on raw material uncertainty, now expected to reflect in FY27.

segments.name: PHS (ZLD/PHS businesses)
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue; 12% of Q4 order intake and 5% of backlog. One joint order closed with a semiconductor company in the current quarter.

Ordering expected to return to a Rs 800-900 crore band on a steady-state basis (management said this is a ballpark, not guidance).
First bio-IBA order expected in Q1 FY27.
GenX break-even targeted in FY27, contingent on booking orders over the next two to three quarters.

Blending mandates expected within about one year per management; E22/E25/E27/E30 BIS fuel specifications now notified.

CBG capacity ramp-up underway at a few plants using Napier grass and rice straw mixed feedstock.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins and profits declined over three years despite R&D investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBP-20 capacity build-out ended, reducing greenfield ethanol plant orders, while GenX investment over 2.5-3 years held back profits; order books are expected to benefit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much did raw material inflation hit Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said raw material costs rose about 3% in Q4 with other expenses down 2%, net impact 1-1.5%; the main driver was site execution cost escalation linked to project delays. YTD raw material costs were broadly flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deferred order quantum and GenX outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred inquiries were about Rs 300 mn+ (called an inquiry basket, not orders). GenX data centre order ranges Rs 50-150 crore; GenX fixed overhead run rate about Rs 10 crore per month; break-even targeted in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for mandates beyond E20 and what is the ethanol capacity impact?

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected steady-state order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline supports a Rs 800-900 crore range typically, but stopped short of formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the R&D spend and the synergy between bioenergy and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 R&D about Rs 65-66 crore (about Rs 20 crore capex, Rs 45-46 crore opex, about 100 scientists). Data centre work is cooling skids and modules; long term, bioenergy could power medium and large data centres.

522205|2026-06.headline: Praj Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 116.1 mn (vs INR 53.4 mn) on INR 7.16 bn revenue, with order intake of INR 10 bn and backlog of INR 45.9 bn.
522205|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations rose to INR 7.16 bn from INR 6.4 bn a year earlier, and PBT before exceptional items more than doubled to INR 210.5 mn. Order intake was INR 10 bn, with 57% domestic, and backlog stood at INR 45.9 bn at June 30, 2026. Management said execution remains slowed by first-generation ethanol funding issues and supply-demand imbalance, while new verticals (Praj GenX data-center work, Bio-IBA demo plant, Brazil corn-to-ethanol plant, ZLD/HiPurity for semiconductors) are starting to show orders. Margins were described as subdued on volume and mix, and management declined to give margin guidance.

segments.name: Bioenergy
segments.commentary: 66% of revenue and 62% of order intake; bioenergy revenue cited at INR 474 crore in the quarter. Domestic first-gen ethanol greenfield slowed; brownfield, DCO and ENA demand holding up.

segments.name: Engineering (incl. Praj GenX)
segments.commentary: 22% of revenue and 28% of order intake. Praj GenX won a hyperscale data-center modular supply framework with a minimum of about USD 50 mn over 2.5 years; management said booking is phased, not the full INR 500 crore headline.

segments.name: Praj HiPurity Systems
segments.commentary: 12% of revenue and 10% of order intake. First combined ultrapure water and ZLD contract for an Indian semiconductor company.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management declined to give margin or segment-level margin targets, citing ongoing investment in Praj GenX, R&D and new ventures.
Praj GenX expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27 (management said 'to start with, consider EBITDA breakeven'); PBT breakeven not confirmed.
International order share rose to about 40-43% of Q1 orders; management expects international revenue share to move up from about 25-30% in coming quarters, with export execution from Q3 FY27.
Bio-IBA commercial-scale demo plant construction expected to complete by December 2026.
Management expects new-vertical results (GenX, internationalisation, alternatives to ethanol) to show more clearly in the latter part of FY27, based on current order book.
Material cost upward pressure from geopolitical situation; management said it is using contracts and advance procurement to offset.
capex_capacity: Bio-IBA (bio-isobutanol) commercial-scale demo plant ordered in prior quarter; construction to complete by December 2026. Management cited 2% diesel blending mandate potential of over INR 3,000 crore project opportunity.
Brazil greenfield corn-to-ethanol plant of about 800 KLPD, executed end-to-end by Praj.
Ethanol-to-SAF detailed engineering order from an international customer, following a completed basic engineering order last quarter.

Ballpark capex for a 100 KLPD ethanol/isobutanol plant: INR 100-120 crore, depending on feedstock and product. Praj scope typically 50-60% of project value (process and critical equipment; installation/construction optional).
Mangaluru facility used for Praj GenX precision fabrication and modular manufacturing; first data-center project deliveries expected across Q2-Q4 FY27.
Dr. Pramod Chaudhari Centre of Excellence for Advanced Bioeconomy inaugurated at SPPU on August 10, 2026.
demand_pricing: Domestic first-gen ethanol greenfield inquiries limited to ethanol-deficit states (Tamil Nadu, Assam); management expects this to persist until higher blending mandates are announced.
Funding issues at end customers and ethanol supply-demand imbalance are extending first-gen project execution cycles.
Strong demand for ENA greenfield plants, where management claims a technology edge; brownfield demand driven by efficiency and co-products such as DCO.

CBG: GOBARdhan National Circular Bioenergy Scheme approved with outlay over INR 23,000 crore for FY27 to FY35-36; management expects better CBG margins as market opens, but noted many new CBG entrants.
Margin drag: material cost up about 10% YoY in Q1 on higher African export mix (lower margin); other expenses down about 7% YoY.
Q1 FY27 quarter-on-quarter: material cost down about 3% and other expenses up about 4%, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Collections and execution: why was bioenergy revenue (INR 474 crore) low versus the opening order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to slow conversion of domestic first-gen ethanol projects due to end-customer funding and ethanol supply-demand imbalance, partly offset by acceleration on other projects. Collections are lagging because of slow backlog conversion; management is working on it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin expand, and will RM and site expenses weigh on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said material cost and other expenses offset each other depending on the equipment vs site mix. YoY, material cost rose about 10% on African export mix, while other expenses fell 7%. Management expects steel-driven cost pressure to be managed with advance measures.

qa_highlights.question: Praj GenX breakeven timing and order book share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets EBITDA breakeven by end-FY27 and would not disclose GenX backlog share; engineering is still reported as one basket. Order-book buildup is improving with shorter delivery cycles on data-center orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports decline YoY while domestic revenue rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export revenue timing depends on order entry and execution cycles; a large export order batch was booked in Q1 with execution starting around Q3 after engineering. International share of orders was 40-43% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory over the next decade and service mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said services margins are higher than project margins and the mix shift (domestic/international, services/projects, new biofuels) is the route to better margins. Current investments in GenX, R&D and new ventures are absorbing margin.

qa_highlights.question: Bio-isobutanol mandate timing and biomaterials (bio-bitumen, PLA)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the timing of any diesel blending mandate is unknown, but Praj is technology-ready. Lactic acid technology for PLA exists; co-product progress is expected by fiscal year-end.

522215|2026-03.headline: HLE Glascoat FY26 consolidated revenue rose 31.7% to INR1,353 crore, but EBITDA grew only 5.4% to INR148.5 crore as Omeras losses weighed.
522215|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR391.7 crore (up 17.4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR43.9 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT of INR20.1 crore (5.1% margin). FY26 EBITDA margin was 11% against a previously guided 16%, with management attributing the gap to the Omeras (Germany) EBITDA loss of INR15.3 crore, a INR2.1 crore labour-code charge and INR4.6 crore of acquisition costs. Management says the ongoing business runs at about 13.5% adjusted EBITDA margin and expects margins to keep rising in FY27. The Board recommended a 55% dividend for FY26, and the order book stood at about INR681.6 crore on March 31, 2026.

segments.name: Filtration, drying and other equipment
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about INR122 crore vs INR109 crore in Q4 FY25 (+11.9%); FY26 revenue up 50.9%.

segments.name: Glass lined equipment (GLE)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about INR219.5 crore vs INR167.9 crore (+29.2%); FY26 up 15.2%. Management puts adjusted GLE EBIT margin near 10% for FY26 and 11.5-12% in Q4, excluding Omeras.

segments.name: Heat transfer equipment (Kinam)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 7.4% YoY; FY26 revenue up 64.6%, with utilisation at about 70-75%. Analyst put FY26 revenue near INR200 crore.

segments.name: Omeras (Germany)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about INR43-44 crore; FY26 EBITDA loss INR15.3 crore and PAT loss INR15.6 crore. Management says it is close to EBITDA breakeven, which it estimates at about INR200-225 crore annual revenue. Order book about INR78-79 crore.

segments.name: Thaletec (Germany)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about EUR34 million (roughly INR345-350 crore at average FX). Low double-digit EBITDA margin (about 11-11.5% at EBIT level); top line stagnant after a softer Q3.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the ongoing business to reach about 16% EBITDA margin in the next two years, excluding Omeras; consolidated margin guided at 14-15%, with Germany dragging the average.
Omeras expected to reach double-digit standalone EBITDA margin in FY27 and to exceed INR200 crore annual revenue in FY26-27.
Heat transfer equipment expected to grow 15-20% per year for the next couple of years.
Consolidated revenue ambition of about INR2,000 crore in roughly two years, including Omeras; management said below that would be disappointing.
Indian Omeras tank-manufacturing capex expected to be commercially operational by end of FY27; revenue contribution to show in next year's financials.
Board recommended 55% dividend for FY26.
capex_capacity: India GLE capacity utilisation now about 75%, up from the 60-65% previously cited; order inflow and pipeline described as improving.
Heat transfer (Kinam) utilisation about 70-75%; capacity creation planned from next year depending on how FY27 goes.
New Indian Omeras plant for tanks (biogas digesters, wastewater, ultra-pure water) expected commercially operational by end FY27; architectural products deferred in India for about 3 years.
Thaletec products now about 20% of Glass Lined India products in FY26.
demand_pricing: Pharma and API capex is the main demand driver in India; agrochemical and some specialty chemical customers deferred decisions after February 2026 because of the Iran-related geopolitical situation.
Gas prices for glass furnaces rose on the Iran conflict; management said most of the increase has been passed on to customers, with some impact.
Glass lined India value per equipment has fallen even as dispatch volumes rose 30-40%, so revenue has lagged output.
Exports from India were about 5-7% of India business revenue in FY26.
Expansion focus: Europe beyond Germany/Austria/Switzerland, US for Thaletec and Omeras, and Middle East for heat exchangers.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 16% FY26 EBITDA margin guidance from the Q2 call missed, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 guidance referred to H2 and FY27. Adjusted for Omeras, the ongoing business runs at about 13.5% EBITDA margin, and 16% is expected excluding Omeras in the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is Omeras on track to breakeven and double-digit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Omeras is close to breakeven. Its order book roughly doubled from Dec-25 to Mar-26. Management expects double-digit margins on a standalone basis in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY26 revenue of about INR1,250 crore (ex-Omeras) reach INR2,000 crore in two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said below INR2,000 crore including Omeras would be disappointing. Consolidated margin is expected at 14-15%, with India above 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Thaletec revenue for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately EUR34 million for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why has glass lined revenue been flat for several years?
qa_highlights.answer: Harsh Patel said equipment dispatch rose 30-40% but value per equipment fell sharply, so revenue has not grown in line with output.

risks_watch: Omeras turnaround: breakeven needs about INR200-225 crore annual revenue; quarterly EBITDA breakeven about INR45-50 crore.
Geopolitical deferrals in CDMO and agrochemical demand, and higher gas costs for glass furnaces.
Thaletec Germany top line flat in FY26; management expects a turnaround based on its order book.

522241|2026-06.headline: MM Forgings Q1 FY27 net sales rose to INR427 crore (+16% YoY) with EBITDA at 18% margin; management guides ~18% growth and ~INR1,800-1,900 crore FY27 turnover.

PBT grew about 30%, helped by a one-time land sale gain in Oragadam, Chennai (INR64 crore gross, INR58 crore net of tax), which management excluded from the EBITDA growth figures. Volumes were about 20,200 tonnes, with management saying April and May were hit by labour shortages and June and July recovered. Management expects Q2 onwards at 23,000-25,000 tonnes per quarter, targeting over 90,000 tonnes in FY27 and 1 lakh tonnes-plus run rate.

522249|2026-03.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% to INR 260.55 crore and PAT 73% to INR 60.71 crore, helped by export mix and FX gains.
522249|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 260.55 crore (up 22% YoY), PBT INR 82.59 crore (up 70%) and PAT INR 60.71 crore (up 73%). Consolidated revenue was INR 273.35 crore (up 9%), PBT INR 81.23 crore (up 54%) and PAT INR 59.43 crore (up 43%). Management attributed the margin jump to export mix, currency gains, lower freight and other expenses, better operating efficiency and some price pass-through in March. Raw material (paste PVC, yarn) prices rose sharply from early March but supply has normalised and prices have eased somewhat from March highs; automotive price increases are expected to flow through in Q1 FY27 with a 1-2 month lag.

financial_highlights.value: INR 55 crore, including FX gain of about INR 30 crore for the year
INR 290 crore vs INR 194 crore in FY25

segments.name: Export general
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 21 crore; general export market was temporarily hit by Middle East shipment hold and war-related logistics delays.

segments.name: Export OEM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 88 crore; Ford platform volumes increasing after new platforms were added.

segments.name: Auto OEM domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 55 crore.

segments.name: Replacement
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 41 crore.

segments.name: Footwear

segments.name: Furnishing
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 5 crore.

segments.name: PU
segments.commentary: Business described as muted; FY26 revenue about INR 27.08 crore. A large customer approved the company as vendor but no commercial price settlement yet.

guidance_outlook: Export growth guided at 15-20% (value) for the coming years; management said it could reach 20-25% depending on new platforms, with no firm timing.
Domestic growth guided at 8-10% (value), with a similar value growth expected over the next 2-3 years.
Export share of revenue expected at 40-45% in FY27 (value basis), with domestic the balance.
EBITDA margin guided at 25-26% as a base; management said 25-30% is possible in the long term, with 30% dependent on conditions.
Price increases on automotive customers expected to flow through in Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 with a 1-2 month lag; management said full-year margins should even out.

New coating line ordered for an existing India facility (not South India), expected to be commissioned by end of calendar 2026; capacity addition about 5 lakh meters per month, adding about INR 120-150 crore revenue. Management said FY27 cash outflow would be about INR 50 crore.

South India plant would have cost about INR 150-200 crore depending on land; the company chose the existing site instead.
US finished goods inventory held at about 8 weeks; transit times lengthened by the war.

Export prices are fixed in USD for automotive; general export pricing is case-by-case and traders react to currency moves.
Rupee depreciation gave an FX gain (about INR 30 crore for FY26) and improved export competitiveness.
Paste PVC and yarn prices rose sharply from early March 2026 after the war-related petroleum price spike; availability has since normalised.
Q4 FY26 gross margin about 50% and EBITDA margin about 31% (excluding other income), per analyst calculations on the call; management attributed this to export mix, productivity and cost control.

qa_highlights.question: How are paste PVC and yarn prices trending, and is there an availability risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose significantly as a petroleum by-product and softened somewhat from March highs; availability is no longer an issue. Short-term impact is about a month because pass-through lags, while inventory averages it out long term.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 domestic and export growth, and the volume?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 value growth was 15% overall, with exports about 35.5% and domestic about 4%. Volume sold was 31 million meters, up about 4.5-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins rise to about 30%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers cited were the export mix, currency gains, higher operating efficiency, cost control in other expenses and some March price pass-through. Management guided 25-26% as a base and said 25-30% is possible over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: Why was export growth guidance cut from 20%+ to 15-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 15-20% conservative and said export is running above that. Q4 general export was hit by a Middle East hold and US tariff effects, and the company is targeting new customers and platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise from INR 14 crore to INR 17 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a provisional impact of the new labour codes (effective 21 November 2025), booked in Q4 as a catch-up, plus some new hires.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and capacity addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Coating line in an existing India facility, completion by end of calendar 2026, about INR 50 crore in FY27 and about 5 lakh meters per month. Global plant capex about INR 300 crore, location still being evaluated.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (paste PVC, yarn) and the lag in passing on price increases to automotive customers.
Dependence on FX gains; the reported margin uplift includes FX gains, and management did not confirm Q4 margins can be held in Q1 FY27.
Export growth depends on OEM platform ramp-ups (Ford) and on the Middle East and US tariff situation.
Inventory build for the new export business and the 8-week US inventory requirement could weigh on working capital.
Scale and timing of the global plant (about INR 300 crore) remain undecided.
PU business is still muted and no commercial settlement has been reached despite vendor approval.
522249|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and margins, but evasive on quarter-to-quarter figures and the sustainability of Q4 margins. Management repeatedly referred to external factors (war, tariffs, raw material prices) and gave ranges rather than firm numbers.
key_quotes: And our volume with Ford was very low. So, we have added more platforms on Ford business.
So, in the long run, yes. If you look at the entire year as a whole, yes, we should be able to do that. I cannot comment on quarter-to-quarter basis right now.
So, we have given a very clear guidance of 25%-26% in the past. We should be able to maintain that for sure.

rows.why: Export OEM revenue was INR 88 cr in Q4 FY26 with Ford volumes rising after new platforms were added, and auto OEM exports reached INR 290 cr in FY26 vs INR 194 cr in FY25 (about +50%).

522249|2026-06.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 20% to INR247.03 crore and PAT 43% to INR58.95 crore, with growth mostly from price and mix, not volume.
522249|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue was INR247.03 crore (up 20% YoY), PBT INR77.79 crore (up 41%) and PAT INR58.95 crore (up 43%). Consolidated revenue was INR269.23 crore (up 25%), PAT INR56.12 crore (up 38%). Management said volume grew only about 2-3%, with the rest from price and mix, led by higher-value export sales. Raw material and freight cost inflation, linked to the West Asia conflict, were not passed on to export OEM customers; the company said it has sent price-increase requests to US customers but has not pushed them hard as markets softened.

financial_highlights.change: Export OEM INR73.56 crore; export general INR30.24 crore
Auto OEM INR56.08 crore; replacement INR36.52 crore; footwear INR41.16 crore; furnishing INR6.08 crore; other INR3.38 crore

segments.name: Export OEM
segments.commentary: INR73.56 crore in Q1 FY27 versus about INR53 crore in Q1 FY26 (analyst figure), roughly 39-40% growth; export volume up about 9% per management. Gross margin did not expand on this growth due to freight and raw material costs.

segments.name: Export general
segments.commentary: INR30.24 crore in Q1 FY27; no separate growth figure given.

segments.name: Domestic auto OEM
segments.commentary: INR56.08 crore; domestic volume growth overall about 1%. Management said four-wheeler volumes from Tata are at an early stage and Mahindra business should rise in coming years.

segments.commentary: INR36.52 crore in Q1 FY27; no growth figure given.
