guidance_outlook: Management guided to top-line growth of 10-15% per year over the next 3 years, with strong growth expected in exports and not strong growth in domestic.

Sustainable margin is guided at about 25% plus or minus 1-2%, with the Q4 FY26 margin described as an abnormally high one-time forex benefit; management asked analysts to view margin on a yearly basis.
US automotive business expected to grow substantially over the next 3 years, with Ford and Chrysler wallet share gains cited; management said growth would come from existing clients.
Freight and logistics cost increases expected to ease if the war situation improves, but management did not commit to a timeline.
Price increase for US export OEM customers under consideration; management said it would depend on how the market moves over the next two to three weeks.
capex_capacity: New line ordered for the existing Gujarat plant adds 5 lakh meters of capacity, with production targeted around February-March 2027 (end of FY27).
PVC installed capacity is 3.5 million meters per month (range 3.5-4.2 million depending on mix); utilisation is about 75-78% on current production of 2.7-2.8 million meters per month.
Capex for FY27 is around INR50 crore; a further capex of about INR250 crore over the next two years is possible if an overseas plant is finalised, and not yet confirmed.

Management estimated the new line adds about INR150 crore of annual revenue at INR300 per linear meter; total could reach INR250-400 crore including the additional facility, depending on mix.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 growth of 25% was about 2% volume and the rest price, driven by a higher-value export mix; management said raw material price was not the main cause.
Export volume growth of about 9% and domestic about 1%, with total volume growth about 2.77%.
Raw material prices softened a little in Q1 but remain above their early-March 2026 levels; prices were very volatile after March.
Shipping costs roughly quadrupled, and the company did not take a price increase on export OEM business, partly offset by about a 10% natural hedge from dollar appreciation.
Management said the company received a 10% price increase in US dollar terms on some business, though it said the US market is softening again.
Competition in PU is intense from China. Footwear demand was muted because sole prices rose two to three times.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth came from volume versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 2%; the rest came from price, mainly due to an export mix shift to higher-priced items rather than raw material pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall sequentially from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the previous quarter was abnormally high due to a one-time forex gain; the sustainable margin is about 25% plus or minus 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't gross margin improved despite a roughly 40% jump in export OEM?
qa_highlights.answer: The Gulf war raised raw material costs and shipping costs (about 4x). The company had requested price increases from export OEM customers but put them on hold when prices fell, and has not taken an increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR9 crore rise in other expenses QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mixed: higher export shipping/freight, travel, legal and professional, and risk coverage costs. Management said some of this will continue and some will ease; part relates to the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US OEM growth outlook and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects US business to grow substantially over three years, through wallet share gains with Ford and Chrysler and new Europe RFQs. It declined to give an order book figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% margin sustainable as a base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company should look at annual margin, which can move 1-2% either way quarter to quarter; it aims to maintain the margin level guided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is 65-66% on a 48 million meter total capacity basis (PVC 3.5-3.7 million meters per month); the new line lifts capacity to about 4-4.2 million meters per month and gives 25-30% headroom.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the PU plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The PU plant is underutilised with no change in three months. Sampling with top brands has been done but no business is confirmed, and management cannot make a strong recommendation this financial year.

risks_watch: Freight and raw material costs: shipping cost reportedly up about 4x and raw material prices volatile since March 2026; company has not taken a price increase on export OEM business, so the margin recovery depends on timing of price hikes and freight easing.
US export pricing: a price increase was requested from US customers but not pushed hard; outcome depends on market moves over the next two to three weeks, per management.
Capex and overseas plant: FY27 capex about INR50 crore; a further roughly INR250 crore over two years depends on an overseas plant location not yet finalised (Mexico, US or other NAFTA).

Other expenses: about INR9 crore QoQ rise in Q1 FY27 from freight, travel, legal, professional and risk cover costs; management could not split recurring versus one-time amounts.
key_quotes: So, we have not taken a price increase in the export market but you also have to look at one more thing in this 10% more or less natural hedge has happened.
So, we have a headroom to expand to 25%, 30% more capacity.
So anywhere between 10% to 15% growth, we are not looking very strong growth in the domestic market. But yes, we are looking at a very strong growth in the export market.
But this present quarter's margin will be sustainable and expected to continue.

522275|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 order intake of INR86.1bn (+188% YoY) lifted backlog to INR214.6bn; Q4 EBITDA margin hit a record 27.2%.
522275|2026-03.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported a strong Q4 and full FY26, with revenue up 42% YoY in Q4 to INR16.4bn and 45% for the year to INR62.1bn. Profit before tax and exceptional items for FY26 rose to INR17.1bn from INR8.2bn, and the company ended the year with zero debt and about INR25bn of cash. Order intake was lifted by a large HVDC turnkey order from Adani Energy (VSC technology), and management guided to a mid-20s EBITDA margin for FY27. Management also announced a INR550mn disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, and a INR10 per share dividend.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Export orders in FY26 were about INR12bn versus INR32bn in FY25, which included one large export order; excluding large orders, base export orders grew 15-20%. Export was about 30% of FY25 revenue and new orders were about 92% domestic.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Backlog is 98% private customers, central utilities and PSUs; state utility exposure is under 2%.

segments.name: HVDC and projects
segments.commentary: A large HVDC turnkey order (Adani Energy, VSC) was booked in Q4, with execution mainly from FY28-29 onwards. Management does not disclose project versus product split.

guidance_outlook: Management endeavours to deliver mid-20s EBITDA margin going forward, after earlier guiding to low-20s and then mid-20s/high-20s in FY26.
Base order inflow expected to be around INR70bn (INR7,000 crore) and management remains confident of achieving it.
Two pending export RPT orders: a large export order where the decision is expected in H2 FY27, and a U.S. data-centre high-voltage order (about INR14-15bn) expected to be decided in Q1 FY27.
U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group, feeding the Adani HVDC project) expected to be placed in the current quarter; it will not appear in the company's order book.
Capex of more than INR10bn to be phased from early FY27 through FY28, self-funded.
Management declined to give a split of Adani HVDC execution in early years; it said first two years would be lower than 30% and mostly engineering and supply-chain work.
capex_capacity: More than INR10bn of capex initiated across multiple product lines and facilities, to be phased through 2028.

INR550mn approved by the Board for new disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu; disconnectors are being restarted for the Indian market, and some products will be global feeder factory output.
Air core reactor facility and HVDC thyristor valves and controls facility planned in India to raise local content.
Management did not give a revenue ballpark for the expanded capacity, citing that HVDC revenue depends on bought-out equipment and manpower rather than in-house capacity.
demand_pricing: Management says the TBCB pipeline has about 33 packages bid out, 21 of them at 765 kV; the only live HVDC tender is Barmer, whose bid deadline is being extended.
Data centres in India are about 1.5 GW installed, mostly at 220 kV; management expects a meaningful contribution once 400 kV and 765 kV data centres scale.
Transformer contracts carry price escalation clauses; for other products, cost inflation is built into tender pricing.
Management said Q4 domestic order finalisation was slightly dull, which it described as a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are export orders weak after FY25, and how will the RPT approvals translate into orders in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding one large FY25 order, base export orders grew 15-20%. The pending RPT orders are a large export order (decision in H2 FY27), a U.S. data-centre order of about INR14-15bn (decision expected in Q1 FY27), and a U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and what was the INR50mn Q4 other expense item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintains an endeavour toward mid-20s EBITDA margin. The Q4 other expenses included about INR500mn of notional mark-to-market loss on foreign currency derivatives; management agreed EBITDA would have been better without it.

qa_highlights.question: Is Prolec's U.S. low-voltage distribution strategy relevant to the Indian entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India has no distribution-transformer manufacturing set-up, and entering would need organic or inorganic capacity; it said it does not see that as a current strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani HVDC execution profile and the Barmer/South Kalamb project share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said early-year execution would be lower than 30%, with most revenue from FY29. For Barmer-type projects, the supplier share depends on line length and scope, not a fixed rule of thumb.

qa_highlights.question: Will HVDC refurbishment projects move from LCC to VSC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCC-to-LCC refurbishment only requires valves and controls changes, whereas LCC-to-VSC is a wider scope with higher shutdown requirement and capex; it depends on customer choice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to sustain high margins and growth for longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is broader this time, covering the U.S., Europe, Middle East and Australia, and that export exposure is meaningful; it did not give a timeline for margin moderation.

risks_watch: Customer decision delays on large export RPT orders (H2 FY27 for one, Q1 FY27 for the U.S. order) and their conversion to revenue.
HVDC pipeline timing: Barmer bid deadline keeps being extended, and the next project after Barmer is not clearly scheduled.
Execution of the Adani HVDC turnkey order depends on securing a supply chain, with revenue weighted to FY29 onwards.
Imports of HVDC components (thyristor valves, controls hardware) remain, so local content is still limited until the new facility comes up.
Foreign-exchange derivative mark-to-market charges can affect other expenses and quarterly EBITDA.
522275|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, backlog and margins, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance on HVDC phasing, pipeline timing and export mix, and said quarterly order intake can be lumpy.
key_quotes: So, yes, we remain confident on achieving the base order number of INR7,000 crores.
Our order book remained strong in Q4, and we saw a booking of INR86.1 billion, up by 188% year-on-year compared to INR29.9 billion in quarter ended March '25.
During the fourth quarter, we achieved a record EBITDA margin of 27.2%.
So, this time, the cycle is different. The market is different and the longevity of the cycle looks to be more sustainable.

522275|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion, but order intake fell 30% to INR11.4 billion and gross margin slipped to 41.3%.
522275|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion and PBT rose to INR4.9 billion, with EBITDA margin at 25.1%, within the mid-20s guided band. Order intake fell 30% YoY to INR11.4 billion, mainly on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026, so backlog eased 2.5% QoQ to INR209.3 billion. Gross margin fell to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26, which management attributed to lower export mix, lower execution savings on elevated commodity prices, and HV business ramp-up. Two large related-party (RPT) orders, INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore, were delayed or on hold, and the company still has no firm plan for surplus cash of about INR16 billion beyond announced uses.

qa_highlights.question: Are the INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore RPT orders being booked, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: None of the INR1,300 crore order is booked; it is expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27. The INR3,000 crore project is on hold at the customer over budget issues and would need fresh shareholder approval after the September AGM. Management said both are not lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a jump in export orders, and what is the RPT pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export pipeline improved on US utility demand for instrument transformers and 400 kV GIS opportunities. Management declined to comment on the new RPT pipeline beyond saying it will go to shareholders when projects become live.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin bridge from 45.3% FY26 gross margin to 41.3% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2-2.5 points from ramp-up of lower-margin HV business (offset at EBITDA level); 1-1.5 points from lower export share and a high-margin export order in FY26; and the rest from lower execution savings due to elevated commodity prices. EBITDA was 25.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the mid-20s EBITDA guidance intact, and how are commodity costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-20s EBITDA guidance for FY27 is maintained. Transformers have formula-based escalation; other turnkey work relies on forecast costs, so cost pressure shows up in execution 1-2 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power Grid TBCB timeline stretching to 24-30 months a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not affect capacity utilisation; ordering cycles may lengthen by about 3-4 months for longer tenders.

qa_highlights.question: What will the company do with surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said options are under evaluation and nothing is firm; announced uses are INR10 billion capex and INR2.5 billion dividend, leaving about INR16 billion unallocated.

522295|2026-03.headline: Control Print FY26 consolidated operating revenue rose to INR482 crores from INR425 crores; CP Italy (V-Shapes) packaging losses remain the key concern.
522295|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR484 crores (vs INR431 crores) and standalone Q4 total revenue of about INR138 crores (vs INR114 crores). Standalone coding and marking drove growth, with management attributing most of the increase to volume and a small part to price, and a surcharge introduced to offset input cost pressure. The call was dominated by questions on losses at the Italian subsidiary V-Shapes (CP Italy), which management attributed almost entirely to the packaging business, and on the rationale for new IP and track-and-trace investments. Management said V-Shapes losses should fall in FY27 and could approach breakeven, though no firm timeline was given.

segments.commentary: Management calls it the main profit centre; Q4 revenue mix was printers 12%, consumables 62%, spares 9%, services 16%. FY26 mix was printers 14%, consumables 61%, spares 9%, services 15%. Management expects a reasonably good year in FY27.

segments.commentary: Management says the conventional business is at breakeven or slightly profitable; no figures disclosed. Two pilots with top 5-10 Indian pharma companies are nearing completion, with a possible scale-up if results succeed.

segments.name: Packaging (India and overseas)
segments.commentary: Management cited good traction in core packing, with a pipeline for laminates, food packing and new machines. A new UNNATI packaging-material plant is planned at Guwahati to lower material costs.

segments.commentary: Management says the subsidiary accounts for almost all consolidated overseas losses. Loss for FY26 was guided at about EUR1.5 million, down from EUR2-2.5 million in FY25. Machine quality issues and the inability to ship machines to Gulf customers have delayed revenue.

segments.commentary: Management says these are at breakeven or better, with 15-20% growth expected for each; CODEOLOGY is being restructured to a smaller core business, and MARKPRINT has contracts in hand. No subsidiary-level sales or profit figures were disclosed.

Gulf and Middle East customers of V-Shapes stopped buying as shipments to the Strait of Hormuz area were blocked.

Management said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores, and that pharma serialization (top 300 drugs, possibly extended to 946) is a driver, though there is no notification yet on the extension.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Garg: Are the international acquisition losses a repeat of past vanity acquisitions, and what are the cumulative loss and capital invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Shiva Kabra said the losses are almost entirely in the overseas packaging business (CP Italy) and that the programme has milestones; the investment cycle is longer than expected because the machines needed more stabilisation. He said the IP is now held by Control Print rather than CP Italy and could be licensed. No cumulative loss or investment figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Madhur Rathi: What drove the rise in standalone employee benefit expense from about INR21 crores to INR27-28 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Barve said the new wage code (effective November 2025) required a recast of leave-encashment and gratuity liabilities, about INR3.5 crores in impact. Provisions were also made for sales incentives and key management loyalty bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Thakur: When will V-Shapes break even, and will losses stop after FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said V-Shapes losses were about EUR2-2.5 million in FY25 and were guided to about EUR1.5 million this year; breakeven could come this year. He said little further funding is needed after current inventory ships, though some loans to V-Shapes will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the nature of the losses and the course correction for V-Shapes?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said about half of V-Shapes costs are R&D, and the rest is contract packaging plus manufacturing and sales. Fixed operating costs were estimated at about USD2-2.5 million per year, with total costs of about EUR2-3 million. Three to four non-productive staff have been let go; investment is going into sales.

qa_highlights.question: Saloni Arya: When do losses subside, what is the Track and Trace market size and margin, and what is the V-Shapes investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores; pilots are with two large pharma companies. He said margins are at least similar to the coding and marking gross margin, with no numerical margin disclosed. No cumulative V-Shapes investment was given.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Singh: Where are the quality issues at CP Italy, and what is the total cost base?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the first machines needed multiple engineering visits and the second was swapped for stock, so the company is aiming for 10 identical machines. Jaideep Barve said the CP Italy total cost is about EUR750,000 a year in direct wages, and Kabra said total fixed operating cost is about USD2-2.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Nikunj Bhanushali: What were the FY26 sales and P&L of CODEOLOGY, MARKPRINT and CP Italy, and what growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose subsidiary sales or profit figures; said the entire consolidated overseas loss is CP Italy. Kabra guided CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT to 15-20% growth and said CODEOLOGY will be scaled down for margin. FY26 printer sales were about 3,064.

522295|2026-06.headline: Control Print standalone operating revenue rose about 5% to ₹105 crore in Q1 FY27, with V-Shapes packaging still loss-making and breakeven pushed to H1 FY28.

Management attributed the slow quarter to extrusion and pipes demand softness, polymer price volatility linked to the Iran conflict, and a slower consumables pull-through. The packaging subsidiary (V-Shapes/CP Italy) remains a drag: management now expects the Packaging business to break even only in H1 FY28, and disclosed no new subsidiary cash infusion beyond a planned IP transfer purchase.

rows.why: Assam UNNATI plastic film facility is in limbo after the government suspended new units, and Guwahati expansion has stalled, so no new capacity has a commissioning date in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects Q2-Q4 to beat Q1 and guides core Coding & Marking growth of 10-15% by year-end, against 5% standalone operating revenue growth in Q1 and 574 printers sold.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and no new capex is guided; the only capex-related items are deferred (Assam) or being serviced from in-house co-packing lots, and CP Italy IP transfer is described as the last infusion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No upgrade signalled; management guides only 10-15% core growth by year-end, and the Q1 base was about 5% growth with consumables pull-through slowing (about ₹5 crore slipped out of Q1 at 85% margin).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone operating revenue grew only about 5% in Q1 (about ₹105 crore vs ~₹100 crore) against a 10-15% core guide for FY27, and packaging breakeven already slipped from H2 FY27 to H1 FY28.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Track & Trace innovative solutions are in pilot with three pharma customers with feedback expected by Q2, and disclosure of outcomes in the Q2 or Q3 presentation, but no launch date or revenue was given.

rows.label: Packaging (V-Shapes/CP Italy) breakeven in H1 FY28
rows.why: Management now guides breakeven only in H1 FY28 (slipped from H2 FY27), with no loss figure disclosed and machine reliability problems still unresolved.

rows.label: Track & Trace QR mandate expansion (2,000 to 25,000 SKUs)
rows.why: The TAM could expand from about ₹500-600 crore to ~₹1,500 crore, but it is still a discussion paper with no timing, and management would not predict enforcement.

rows.label: International subsidiaries break-even in FY27
rows.why: Management guided that international subsidiaries will break even this year, though sales are billed from India, so the subsidiary P&L is hard to verify.

tone.note: Management was confident on the standalone Coding & Marking core and its price increase, but defensive on V-Shapes and Track & Trace, declining to give timelines or loss figures; analysts pushed on the 4-5% growth against the historical ~10%, and on whether V-Shapes cash burn is ending.

523261|2026-03.headline: Venky's Q4 FY26 margins jumped on broiler realisation; poultry EBIT margin ~14% and Animal Health ~29%, but April–May broiler and chick prices softened.
523261|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 improved substantially, driven by better realisation on day-old chicks and broilers, with poultry margins near 14% and Animal Health EBIT margin around 29%. Oil Seed capacity utilisation rose to 65–70%, with a target of about 80% this year and a push to lift outside-group sales to roughly 60–65% of revenue. Management flagged that broiler realisation and chick prices fell from 10–11 May, and maize and soya prices are expected to stay volatile. Full-year FY26 volumes were mixed: commercial broiler birds fell to 8.69 crore from 9.17 crore, while layer chicks rose to 4.57 crore from 4.38 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 day-old broiler chick realisation

segments.name: Poultry
segments.commentary: Q4 operating margin ~14% on broiler realisation and input costs. Q1 FY27 to date (April) broiler ~INR97–100/kg, chicks INR38–39, layer chicks INR46; prices softening from mid-May. Cost of production ~INR89/kg for broilers, INR32–33 for broiler chicks, INR35–37 for layer chicks.

segments.name: Animal Health (AHP)
segments.commentary: Management said FY26 turnover was about INR100 crore and EBIT margin was around 29% in Q4; guidance is 22–23%+ for the full year FY27 and double-digit growth. Kesurdi plant runs at 75–80% utilisation and the new therapeutic plant at 35–40%. Exports are under 2–3% of turnover.

segments.name: Oil Seed
segments.commentary: Q4 EBIT margin ~5.3%. Capacity utilisation 65–70% now, targeted ~80% this year. Outside-group sales reached ~20% of production, with a target of one-third. Division is debt-free with no capex or working capital borrowings.

segments.name: SPF eggs
segments.commentary: Capacity 1.88 crore eggs/year, utilisation 48% in FY26 (45% prior year), production ~1 crore eggs, realisation INR80.22. Margin not disclosed; to be revisited.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Oil Seed to hold or beat Q4 performance through September, with the Q3 outlook dependent on the new crop and El Nino.
Animal Health expected to grow at double digits in FY27, with margins held at 22–23% or above for the full year.
Layer chick sales targeted above 5 crore in FY27, up from 4.57 crore; broiler chicks and contract broiler farming volumes targeted up 2–5%.
Q1 is seasonally weaker for poultry productivity (10–12% lower in open farms), so management expects softer Q1 volumes.
Management said the company would not add debt; working capital of about INR160 crore is sufficient.
Management said the company would concentrate on balanced yearly rather than quarterly performance.
capex_capacity: Oil Seed: four plants across three units; no new capex until the existing units are stable over the next year.
Animal Health: new therapeutic plant at 35–40% utilisation; Kesurdi plant at 75–80%.
SPF egg capacity 1.88 crore eggs; utilisation 48%.
Oil Seed capacity is counted on 300 working days, so utilisation can rise beyond the stated base.
demand_pricing: Layer prices stable at INR45–49 across Q4 FY26, April and May.
Broiler realisation was INR105–110 in the company's operating region in Q4 and stayed near INR110 in April; it fell from around 10–11 May, with management citing demand-supply factors.
Day-old chick prices reached about INR55 in Q4 and fell to about INR35 in the company's region, and to INR21–22 in parts of North India.
Management cited an industry poultry growth rate of 7–8% and said more than 75% of expansion comes from existing integrators.
Poultry share of the non-veg segment has reportedly risen above 55% from 35–40%.
Maize and soya prices are expected to stay volatile with crude oil and ethanol demand; India is currently priced above global levels, with Brazil and Argentina cheaper.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY26 volumes and realisations by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial broiler birds 8.69 crore (vs 9.17 crore), layer chicks 4.57 crore (vs 4.38 crore), broiler chicks 11.46 crore (vs 10.77 crore). Realisations: broiler INR89.59/kg, broiler chick INR34.94, layer chick INR45.15.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 and April–May pricing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 broiler INR102.67/kg, chick INR51.32, layer INR46.15. April broiler ~INR97–100, broiler chick INR38–39, layer chick INR46. Prices began falling from 10–11 May, with broilers near INR90–93 at one point.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Oil Seed margin sustainable and how is it growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity utilisation has risen over six months, outside-group sales reached 20% of production, and the target is one-third. Margins depend on conversion spread and inventory gains; the Q4 margin has been held.

qa_highlights.question: Will Animal Health margins hold and what drives them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins were driven by a new therapeutic plant, a natural-solutions product mix and wider distribution. It expects 22–23%+ for the full year, with raw material pressure in Q2–Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there interest in separately listing Animal Health or doing a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the portfolio complements the group and the model is working; the company will inform shareholders if anything is decided.

qa_highlights.question: Why has commercial broiler output been flat since FY20?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company can switch between chicks sold on to open-market farmers and birds grown in its own integration, so volumes shift year to year.

risks_watch: Broiler and chick price falls from mid-May could erode the Q4 margin uplift in Q1 FY27.
Maize and soya volatility, linked to crude oil and biofuel demand, could compress poultry and Oil Seed margins.
The CCI antitrust probe concerns parent breeding farms, but management said the listed entity was not affected for now.
El Nino and seasonal heat could lower Q1 broiler productivity; the Adhik Maas in May could weigh on demand.
Management did not disclose SPF egg margins and said it would revert on the matter.
Receivables remain high at INR544 crore, and related-party exposure is still significant.
523261|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Animal Health and Oil Seed trajectory, with specific numerical guidance. More guarded on poultry pricing, pointing to softer April–May realisations and raw material volatility; several questions were deflected (SPF margin, parent-bird competition, separate listing).
key_quotes: So definitely, the productivity will be less in quarter 1.
Now oil is already accounting around 40% of our outside production -- outside sales.
We are debt free. We are not using any money for the capex.
Capacity utilization today is around 65% to 70%. And this year, we expect to be around 80%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 poultry margin ~14% and Animal Health EBIT ~29%, but broiler realisation fell from INR110 to INR90-93 after 10-11 May and chick prices dropped from ~INR55 to ~INR35, so the Q4 uplift is at risk; Animal Health guided to 22-23%+ for FY27 against 29% in Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Oil Seed has four plants with no new capex until existing units stabilise over the next year; Animal Health new therapeutic plant is at 35-40% utilisation and SPF egg capacity is 1.88 crore eggs at 48% utilisation, so no new capacity is needed in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets layer chick sales above 5 crore in FY27 from 4.57 crore (about +9%), broiler chicks and contract broiler volumes up 2-5%, and Animal Health double-digit growth; Q1 volumes are seasonally softer by 10-12% in open farms.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Oil Seed utilisation is 65-70% and rising toward 80%, but management said no new Oil Seed capex until existing units are stable over the next year, and it will not add debt with working capital of about INR160 crore sufficient.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Oil Seed utilisation rising from 65-70% to ~80% and outside-group sales targeted at one-third, with Animal Health guided to double-digit growth, could support upside, but poultry price softness from mid-May limits near-term upgrades.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Broiler realisation fell from INR102.67/kg in Q4 to INR90-93 after 10-11 May, chick prices fell from ~INR55 to ~INR35, and maize/soya volatility plus El Nino and the Adhik Maas could weigh on Q1 productivity and margins.

rows.label: Broiler and chick price softness from mid-May
rows.why: Broiler realisation fell from INR105-110 in Q4 and April to around INR90-93 after 10-11 May, with day-old chicks down to about INR35 from about INR55, against cost of production of about INR89/kg for broilers and INR32-33 for chicks.

rows.label: Oil Seed outside-group sales to one-third
rows.why: Outside-group sales are about 20% of production today against a target of one-third, and utilisation is 65-70% against a target of about 80% this year, but margins depend on conversion spread and inventory gains.

rows.label: Debt-free operations continue
rows.why: Management said the company will not add debt, Oil Seed has no capex or working capital borrowings, and working capital of about INR160 crore is sufficient; receivables are INR544 crore against INR553 crore last year.

tone.note: Management was confident on Animal Health (double-digit growth, 22-23%+ margin) and Oil Seed utilisation rising to ~80%, but cautious on poultry pricing after the mid-May fall; analysts were pushed off on SPF egg margins, parent-bird CCI probe and separate listing.

523301|2026-03.headline: TCPL Packaging Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose over 9% YoY to INR 465 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.4% including forex-led other income.
523301|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income was INR 465 crore (over 9% YoY) and EBITDA including other income was INR 81 crore (17.4% margin), helped by operational export forex gains. FY26 revenue was about INR 1,836 crore (+3% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 318 crore (17.3%). Exports were hit in Q4 by Middle East disruptions, while domestic volumes grew ahead of consumer market trends. Management said margins were pressured by raw material inflation and a lag in passing on price hikes, and the company declined to give margin or export guidance beyond the near term. Finance cost rose on a INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on ECB, and deferred tax was higher due to capex-related timing differences.

segments.name: Flexible packaging
segments.commentary: Management called FY26 a strong year with healthy utilisation; the last commercialised line runs at optimum level. A fourth line at the unit is expected to be commercialised by year-end FY27, with management expecting its return on assets to beat lines 2 and 3.

segments.name: Folding cartons (consumer products, mainly FMCG and F&B)
segments.commentary: Management said this is more than half of the business. Carton utilisation is lower, with some double-digit scope for growth in existing capacity.

segments.name: Paperboard (Chennai greenfield)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is above 50% and rising on new customer approvals; management expects a good ramp-up ahead.

segments.name: Creative (Noida)
segments.commentary: Management said it just squeaked through to EBITDA break-even in FY25 and improved further in FY26, with a target of cash and net profit in FY27. Electronics demand weakness is a headwind.

segments.name: Recyclable films
segments.commentary: Domestic uptake is weak because EPR rules mandate recycled content, not recyclable packaging. Output is rising through export jobs, and machinery issues are resolved.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management expects margins to hold if raw material cost increases stop, and said a prolonged crisis would make further price pass-through difficult.

FY27 capex is guided at about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, with the bulk in flexible packaging and some building expansion; management said the plan is calibrated and could rise if demand picks up.
Exports expected to recover in FY27 if Middle East conditions normalise; management is optimistic about the UK, US, other North America, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia.
Domestic demand expected to be good for the year, but fuel price and rupee-driven inflation could hit consumer demand in coming quarters.
Utilisation at the Chennai and cylinder facilities is expected to improve over the next one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, mainly flexible packaging with some factory building expansion.
Fourth flexible packaging line at the unit expected to be commercialised by end FY27, with a temporary absorption-period drag on profitability.
Chennai greenfield paperboard facility above 50% utilised and ramping up on customer approvals.
Gravure cylinder facility at Silvassa commissioned recently and ramped up well, adding backward integration.
Management said capex intensity may rise as new initiatives materialise; the current plan is considered firm.
demand_pricing: Domestic volume growth ahead of underlying consumer market trends; management said momentum is okay with no demand problem currently, and it is broad-based across customers.
Exports were under pressure in Q4 due to Middle East disruptions; some vessels are sailing again after the ceasefire, but the outlook is highly uncertain.
Paper and board prices kept rising; virgin board increased sharply, and recycled board sees steady incremental increases that are harder to pass through.
Company adds more than one or two customers almost every month and is expanding its export team.
Electronics volumes are falling due to chip price increases; diversification into other packaging areas is offsetting this.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and which regions could scale beyond the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is fairly optimistic on export recovery if the Middle East normalises, citing scaling in the UK, US, other North America, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia. It gave no quantified target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost high despite debt levels, and is the ECB unhedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on the ECB raised interest cost. It is a notional, non-cash accounting item. Absolute debt grew on a standalone basis and fell marginally on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is deferred tax so high this year and is it linked to capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the actual tax outgo is already reflected, and the higher deferred tax is a timing difference from capex-driven tax vs accounting depreciation. It said the annual tax rate is in line.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give a domestic/export revenue split annually?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will consider providing the split, possibly offline, but did not commit.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pickup in recyclable film demand, and how is Creative progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic recyclable film demand is weak until the government mandates recyclable packaging. Creative reached EBITDA break-even in FY25, improved in FY26, and management aims for cash and net profit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and is there a plan to expand into new sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, and calibrated given uncertainty. Management said it adds one or two customers almost every month across sectors and is not sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 margins be higher with Chennai and cylinder ramp-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty. It said margins should improve with better utilisation if conditions are better.

qa_highlights.question: Is paper cost still rising, and what is the impact of the minimum import price on board?
qa_highlights.answer: Paper cost pressure continues, with virgin board up sharply and recycled board rising steadily. The MIP on board imports gives domestic mills some room, and management expects some price increase is inevitable.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and shipping disruption could keep export volumes weak and extend raw material inflation.
Continuing steady paper and board price increases could limit pass-through and compress margins.
ECB mark-to-market exposure to euro movements could keep adding to finance cost.
Deferred tax charges from capex timing differences could continue to weigh on reported PAT and EPS.
Monitor utilisation at Chennai, the cylinder facility and the fourth flexible line, plus the Creative break-even trajectory.
Fuel price and rupee-driven inflation could hit domestic consumer demand in coming quarters.
523301|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on domestic demand and long-term export growth, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, exports and FY28 outlook, citing the Middle East crisis and cost volatility. Management tended to defer specifics on guidance and deflected the finance cost and tax questions to accounting timing.
key_quotes: So, we do expect to have a good year for domestic as well.
I cannot tell you what is going to happen in 3 months. So, I am not going to speculate about 1.5 years down the line where anything can happen, as we have seen.
Just annualize it and see, do not go quarter-by-quarter, I think. Overall, it is fine.
But we add like more than one or two customers almost every month. So, that is a constant process.

rows.why: EBITDA margin was 17.4% in Q4 FY26 and 17.3% for FY26, but raw material inflation (virgin board up sharply) and a lag in price pass-through are pressuring margins, and management gave no margin guidance and said a prolonged crisis would make pass-through harder.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: Fourth flexible packaging line is under construction and expected to be commercialised by end FY27, and FY27 capex is guided at about INR 100 crore, with Chennai paperboard already commissioned and above 50% utilised.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic volumes grew ahead of consumer market trends and the company adds one or two customers almost every month, with Chennai and cylinder utilisation expected to improve over the next one to two quarters, though exports were hit in Q4 by Middle East disruption.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR 100 crore is already planned and management said it could rise if demand picks up and new initiatives materialise, but no new capex beyond the fourth line was announced; utilisation in flexible packaging is at optimum and folding cartons have double-digit headroom, so a further announcement is possible rather than certain.

rows.why: Management declined to give margin or export guidance beyond the near term, citing the Middle East crisis and cost volatility, so there is no basis for a raise.

rows.why: Management said a prolonged Middle East crisis would make price pass-through difficult and fuel and rupee inflation could hit consumer demand, with exports still weak in Q4 and recovery only if conditions normalise.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Creative targets cash and net profit in FY27 and the company is diversifying into other packaging areas to offset falling electronics volumes, but no specific new product launch date or name was given.

rows.label: Creative (Noida) reaches cash and net profit
rows.why: Creative reached EBITDA break-even in FY25, improved in FY26, and management targets cash and net profit in FY27, though electronics demand is falling due to chip price increases.

rows.label: Export recovery if Middle East normalises
rows.why: Management is optimistic on UK, US, other North America, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia and some vessels are sailing again after the ceasefire, but gave no quantified target and Q4 exports were hit.

rows.label: Deferred tax and ECB mark-to-market drag on PAT
rows.why: INR 18 crore notional ECB mark-to-market loss raised finance cost and deferred tax was higher from capex timing differences, both expected to keep weighing on reported PAT while capex continues at about INR 100 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic demand, customer additions and long-term export growth, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, exports and FY28 outlook; analysts pressed on finance cost, deferred tax and guidance, which management attributed to notional or timing items.

523301|2026-06.headline: TCPL Packaging Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~79% YoY to INR 40 crore on 16% total income growth, and the company announced a INR 125 crore lithium-ion battery separator film venture.
523301|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to INR 495 crore, EBITDA grew 17% to INR 88 crore, and EBITDA margin improved to 18%. Cash profit rose 56% to INR 76 crore and PAT rose nearly 79% to INR 40 crore, helped partly by a normalised interest cost versus a forex/mark-to-market hit in the prior-year quarter. Growth was domestic-led (good double-digit domestic growth, export growth positive but lower) with volumes up high single digits. Management announced a proposed subsidiary to enter lithium-ion battery separator films (INR 125 crore over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28) and a ~30% expansion of flexible packaging capacity (INR 50-60 crore).

financial_highlights.change: improved YoY (exact prior figure not stated)
domestic growth at good double-digit clip

segments.name: Flexible Packaging
segments.commentary: Existing facility at optimal utilisation; growing faster than carton business. Fourth line adding ~30% to existing capacity at INR 50-60 crore, expected operational January/February 2028. Management says flexible EBITDA margins are structurally lower than carton, though returns on capital are similar.

segments.name: Folding Cartons
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 70-plus%, varying by plant; some plants have headroom while others are full. Chennai plant ramping, management says 'getting there' toward ~70%. Expansion can be added within a quarter or 1.5 quarters' notice.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Growth positive YoY but below domestic; prior-year quarter was weak. Management is cautious on near-term global outlook. UK/EU FTAs give slight duty benefit mainly for flexibles.

segments.name: Battery separator films (proposed subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Proposed INR 125 crore investment over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28. Phase 1 capacity ~70 million sqm (~6-8 GWh), with a long-term plan of ~500 million sqm (~50 GWh). Phase 1 topline guided at INR 150-200 crore; management expects a 'good double-digit' margin and ROCE above company's 20% hurdle.

guidance_outlook: FY27 non-separator capex budget about INR 100 crore; with separator announcement, total could rise to INR 100-150 crore. Separator spend mostly in next year after land purchase this year.
FY28 capex expected to be at least similar to FY27 levels, possibly higher, depending on carton business.
Management declined to give formal FY27 growth or margin guidance, saying the historic trend is expected to continue and margins follow top line.
Separator revenue at full 500 million sqm scale was estimated at INR 1,100-1,300 crore, with the price environment uncertain.
Separator qualification and scale-up expected to take at least a year, with FY28-29 spent in qualification and early commercial supply.
capex_capacity: Flexible packaging: ~30% capacity addition, INR 50-60 crore, new line operational Jan/Feb 2028; existing facility at optimal utilisation.
Folding cartons: utilisation ~70-plus% overall; new space being developed in some factories for next year's capex; Chennai plant can add 2-3 lines quickly with space and infrastructure ready.
Battery separator: Phase 1 ~70 million sqm/yr (~6-8 GWh), starting with coating and conversion before backward integration into base film; long-term ~500 million sqm (~50 GWh).
Separator land purchase in FY27; majority of spend in FY28. Phase 1 lead times for machinery similar to packaging machinery; base film lines would take longer.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as recovering, with good double-digit domestic growth and improved customer volume growth.
Price increases pass through with a lag of over a quarter due to inventory and order-book timing; management says EBITDA margin could not be held without pass-through.
Competition in separators: no lithium-ion separator capacity online in India; lead-acid separator makers exist. Internationally, China leads with multiple players (SEMCORP cited as largest).
Brand owners' adoption of mono-material recyclable packaging in India is slower than expected because government has not mandated it; export demand for recyclable packaging is growing.
Management says the pan masala plastic ban notification is 'misleading' and the company is not a major supplier to that segment, so impact is marginal in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Flexible packaging capacity addition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise by ~30% at an investment of INR 50-60 crore; existing capacity is almost fully utilised.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost lower YoY, is it lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The prior-year quarter included a one-time forex/mark-to-market loss; this quarter is a normalised comparison. Debt figure not given.

qa_highlights.question: Separator Phase 1 topline and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 topline INR 150-200 crore; margin expected to be a good double-digit number; asset turns not comparable because of large land purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Separator technology: in-house or partner?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology developed through a mix of external sources and in-house R&D; management cites group experience across many specialised fields.

qa_highlights.question: Chennai folding carton ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is 'fairly satisfied'; utilisation is 'getting there' toward ~70%; room for 2-3 more lines with space in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the separator subsidiary be 100% owned, and what is capex per 70 million sqm?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 100% owned. Scaling is not linear; capex will be more than 8x Phase 1 because of base film backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Opex for the separator business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a top-heavy team would not be a significant drag at the group's INR 1,500-2,000 crore topline; separator opex is already budgeted.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory with flexible mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Flexible has lower EBITDA margins but similar return on capital; no structural margin direction given for the next 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Separator project: execution risk for a new technology in a 'very unforgiving' battery market; qualification and ramp depend on cell makers' factory timelines; PLI support not formalised.
Capex step-up: FY27-28 capex rising to INR 100-150 crore plus separator spend, with the separator's full-scale capex significantly larger than Phase 1.
Export outlook uncertain given geopolitics; management says 'if there is another war somewhere, we do not know'.
Flexible mix growth may dilute EBITDA margins; management did not explain why margins rose despite the mix shift.
Slow adoption of mono-material recyclable packaging by Indian brand owners in the absence of a government mandate.
Price pass-through lag of over a quarter on raw material costs.

key_quotes: During the first quarter, we delivered a record quarterly performance, with consolidated total income increasing by 16% year-on-year to INR 495 crore, while EBITDA grew by 17% to INR 88 crore with margins improving to 18%.

The project will be established through a subsidiary with a proposed investment of approximately INR 125 crore, to be deployed over the next 18 months, with commercial production targeted during Q4 FY28.
Margin will follow, let us see, but I think it will be a good double-digit number.
But basically, the EBITDA margin could not be maintained if we did not pass it through.

rows.when: Q4 FY28 for separator; Jan/Feb 2028 for flexible line

523329|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings rose 120% to INR 744 crores on Solano Gardens launch, while Q4 margins were hit by about INR 14 crores of one-off expenses.
523329|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 bookings of INR 744 crores (up 120% YoY) and collections of INR 352.1 crores (up ~39%), driven by the Solano Gardens launch where 343 of 433 units sold for over INR 384 crores. Q4 FY26 booking value was INR 382.7 crores and collections INR 96.5 crores. Q4 profitability was dented by about INR 14 crores of one-time items (GST input write-off of ~INR 11 crores plus earlier-project costs). The company added ~INR 2,000 crores GDV through three Lucknow land parcels, two via LDA auctions, and guided to ~INR 4,000 crores total GDV across ongoing, unsold and yet-to-launch projects over 5 to 7 years.

financial_highlights.value: INR 60-64 crores, of which Imperia Phase 2 ~INR 47 crores

segments.name: Eldeco Solano Gardens (Lucknow)
segments.commentary: Launch phase sold 343 of 433 units, booking over INR 384 crores; mix of plots (50-60% margin), villas and group housing, with weighted average margin of about 35-40% per management. Around 75-80% of horizontal component absorbed; first multi-storied project expected in a couple of quarters to year-end.

segments.name: Imperia Phase 2
segments.commentary: Total turnover about INR 300 crores; ~INR 47 crores recognised in Q4 FY26 (70-80% of Q4 revenue). Management guides INR 130-150 crores recognition in FY27. Project substantially complete with completion certificate obtained; possession offered ahead of schedule.

segments.name: Eldeco Latitude 27
segments.commentary: Project value about INR 270-280 crores. Official handover commitment November 2027, with management hinting at possible earlier delivery, potentially within FY27; 4 of 5 towers in first phase, one tower lagging 6-9 months.

segments.name: Eldeco Trinity
segments.commentary: Bookings declined slightly in the quarter; sample flat ready and relaunch planned in about 3 weeks. Recent launches priced at about INR 8,000-11,000 per sq ft, above weighted average.

guidance_outlook: FY27 construction spend expected up 15-20% from FY26 INR 177.7 crores, to about INR 200 crores.
FY27 recognition from Imperia Phase 2 guided at INR 130-150 crores; management called these conservative and said recognition could come earlier.
FY27 margin outlook: EBITDA margin about 30-35% and PAT margin about 25%, driven by Imperia 2 recognition.
Big launches expected towards end of FY27 after approvals and RERA; no major launch in the next quarter, only small launches.
Total GDV across ongoing, unsold and yet-to-launch projects about INR 4,000 crores, expected to be sold over 5-7 years.
Management said the one-off expenses are cleared and no further one-offs are expected in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Three Lucknow land parcels added in Q4 FY26 with GDV of about INR 2,000 crores and ~2 million sq ft saleable area, including two LDA auction parcels and a Shaheed Path parcel; launch expected towards end of FY27 subject to designs, approvals and RERA.
Solano Gardens has four parcels reserved for multi-storied group housing launches, to be rolled out over multiple years.
Management is considering replicating the Solano Gardens template at 2-3 more locations; Gorakhpur land talks ongoing with term sheets but nothing tied up.
Organic land aggregation continuing in 3-4 undisclosed locations; major business development deferred as hands are full for the next couple of quarters.
Latitude 27 has 5 towers; construction spend follows project timelines rather than sales pace.
demand_pricing: Management says demand in Lucknow is organic and not materially affected by geopolitics; a stock market slowdown could delay big purchases, and construction cost transmission is the bigger risk.
About 30-40% of collections are funded by home loans; management does not expect a rate reversal to change demand much.
Weighted average realisation per sq ft has risen sharply to around INR 6,500; management says new city-centric projects will push pricing higher, though prices are stagnating generally.

Recognised revenue can exceed delivered area: Q4 revenue of about INR 64 crores against 18,530 sq ft and 26 units delivered, because revenue is recognised on possession offered and collections completed under Ind AS 115.
Management sees supply, not demand, as the constraint in Lucknow, citing fragmented and disputed land.
Management said the UP urban development policy (February) eases FAR and approvals and is positive; it sees limited impact from possible entry of national players.

qa_highlights.question: What margins do plotted and villa projects carry versus the wider portfolio, and what margins are expected next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Plotted margins are 50-60%; Solano's weighted average including villas is about 35-40%. FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 30-35% and PAT about 25%, driven by Imperia 2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what was the one-off expense?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 14 crores one-time costs, including ~INR 11 crores GST input written off and earlier-project costs, hit EBITDA and PAT in Q4 and FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Imperia Phase 2 will be recognised in FY27 and what is unsold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projects INR 130-150 crores recognition in FY27; total project turnover about INR 300 crores, with the balance dependent on customer possession timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Imperia 2 recognition slow when the project is complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised only when control passes; customers who have not taken possession keep paying instalments, so recognition depends on their possession timing. Management said numbers are conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch plan and how much GDV can be monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Big launches are expected towards end-FY27 after approvals and RERA; no major launch in the next quarter. Management pointed to the ~INR 4,000 crores GDV over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the construction budget for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 spend was about INR 177 crores (vs INR 150-160 crores prior year); FY27 expected about INR 200 crores, up 15-20%, rising as more projects launch.

risks_watch: Q4 margin dilution from one-offs and reliance on Imperia Phase 2 recognition timing for FY27 earnings.
Revenue recognition depends on customer possession timing; Imperia 2 recognition could slip.
Big FY27 launches are dependent on approvals and RERA registration; no major launch expected in the next quarter.
Construction cost inflation is seen as the bigger macro risk than demand.
Competition from national players may rise after the UP urban development policy; Trinity bookings dipped and relaunch is pending.

523329|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose 63% YoY to INR 50.3 crores and PAT rose 382% to INR 15.1 crores, with collections up 68% to INR 131.2 crores.
523329|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong start, with collections outpacing bookings and profitability improving sharply year on year. Bookings normalised to INR 105.7 crores (1.26 lakh sq ft) after the exceptional Q4 FY26 launch quarter. Margin gains were driven mainly by the high-margin horizontal Imperia Phase 2 project, which accounted for about 85% of quarterly revenue. Management added a 50+ acre Lucknow land contract and about 15 acres of aggregated land, but gave no firm FY27 sales or booking guidance and was cautious on Faith (Trinity) launch traction.

segments.name: Eldeco Imperia Avenue
segments.commentary: Launched in Q1 with 44 units sold, booking value about INR 14.6 crores.

segments.commentary: Completion certificate scheduled for November 2027 across roughly 7-8 towers (GDV about INR 275-300 crores per analyst). Management aims to recognise completed towers from March to May 2027, about 15-20% of GDV, subject to execution and RERA extensions.

segments.name: Legacy ready inventory
segments.commentary: About INR 75 crores of unsold ready inventory in legacy projects. Management expects 40-60% to be liquidated in FY27.

Management says the strategy is to sell most inventory in the initial launch period; tail inventory is now being sold at current market prices.
Lucknow commercial rates described as steady with an upward trend, but management declined to quote figures.
Management says the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway is driving inbound migration and housing interest in Lucknow.
Management declined to give FY27 sales or booking guidance; it pointed to presentation data on average realisation for estimation.

qa_highlights.question: Why diversify into projects like Eldeco City Courtyard, and is commercial/mixed-use a larger opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Courtyard is a small commercial component of the integrated Eldeco City township, needed to meet development control norms; it is a very small share of salable area and Imperia Avenue shows good reception.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 37% EBITDA margin in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue mix shifted to Imperia Phase 2, a high-margin horizontal project (about 60% gross margin), while Q1 FY26 was dominated by a lower-margin vertical project; management expects horizontal projects to keep margins higher.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Imperia Phase 2 revenue is recognised, and how much is left?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 170-180 crores of the roughly INR 300 crores GDV is still to be recognised, predominantly in FY27 but timing depends on sales and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy ready inventory remains and how much can be sold in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 75 crores of legacy inventory remains; management expects 40-60% to be liquidated in the current year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Latitude 27 can be recognised in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Towers are targeted for revenue recognition within FY27 or by April-May 2027; management estimates 15-20% of GDV (about INR 275-300 crores) between March and May 2027, depending on execution and RERA extensions.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Faith tower bookings traction weak, and how is the booking figure reconciled with area?
qa_highlights.answer: Faith launched mid-June after war-related delays; the sample flat was ready 10-15 June, with 2-3 bookings and 20-25 in pipeline. Rajiv Khurana said the slides now show area allotted rather than area booked, since allotment follows booking, and the two are not directly comparable.

523367|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, but PBDIT fell to INR400 crore from INR426 crore on sugar cost pressure.
523367|2026-03.overview: DCM Shriram's Q4 FY26 net revenue (net of excise) grew 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, while PBDIT declined to INR400 crore from INR426 crore. Chemicals revenue rose 32% and Vinyl PBDIT jumped 68%, but Sugar and ethanol PBDIT fell 18% on higher cane prices and Fenesta's margin was diluted by costs. FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR13,538 crore and PBDIT rose 15% to INR1,694 crore, with net debt at INR1,767 crore and ROCE at 13%. Management flagged high PVC price volatility and an unresolved ethanol allocation problem as the main near-term concerns.

financial_highlights.metric: Net revenue (net of excise), Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: flat YoY; includes one-time INR19 crore Gujarat incentive

financial_highlights.metric: Sugar and ethanol PBDIT, Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: vs INR9 crore; includes one-time INR33 crore retention price gain

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 32% YoY; caustic volumes +2%, ECUs -4%. PBDIT flat at INR163 crore, held back by fixed costs from expansion, including a one-time INR19 crore government incentive. ECH plant fully commissioned in April 2026, running at 60-70% utilisation.

segments.name: Vinyl
segments.commentary: Revenue up 19% YoY, with PVC volumes +23% and carbide +5%. PBDIT rose 68% to INR39 crore on higher prices, lower energy costs and better efficiency. PVC prices are volatile, currently around INR81-82/kg per management.

segments.name: Sugar and ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue down 3% to INR991 crore; ethanol prices -15% on sales mix. PBDIT down 18% to INR207 crore as cane prices rose 8%. Crush fell to 473 lakh quintals with recovery of 10.8%; sugar inventory 32.2 lakh quintals vs 39.9 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Fenesta Building Systems
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,112 crore (+28%). Q4 revenue +34% YoY, but PBDIT up only 6% to INR37 crore given fixed costs and new platforms. Order book up 15%.

segments.name: Shriram Farm Solutions
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in FY26; research wheat sales +22% to a record. Q4 revenue +32% YoY in an off-season quarter. 13 new products launched in FY26, four from in-house R&D.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue down 11% on a maintenance shutdown. Outstanding subsidy INR189 crore vs INR161 crore last year. Gas supply risk from the West Asia conflict flagged.

segments.name: Bioseed
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue down 1% and PBDIT loss of INR8 crore. Management said the FY26 cotton seed environment was challenging; kharif placements are reasonable, with cotton inventory a concern.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR1,000-1,200 crore, including board-approved projects and pipeline.
INR217 crore capex for ~48 MW additional renewable power for Bharuch, taking RE provision from 50.4 MW to 98.4 MW; completion around Q1 FY28.
INR101 crore capex to expand formulated resins capacity by 36 KTPA to 50 KTPA; commissioning by Q2 FY28.
Management expects Epoxy/advanced materials unit to reach break-even in FY27 and be slightly better than break-even this year.
Management expects sugar margins to shrink versus last year but the shrinkage to be not significant, with prices expected to improve from record-low inventory.
Management expects caustic capacity utilisation to stay robust in FY27 and reasonable margins in ECH if raw material and product prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Pujan Shah (Molecule Ventures): outlook for PVC pricing given China property weakness and possible closures of inefficient Chinese PVC plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Shriram said pricing is very volatile and hard to forecast; hoped the rupee depreciation supports import parity and that the 11% import duty returns from 1 July 2026. Current PVC prices around INR81-82/kg; China capacity is so large that closures cannot be verified.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj (360 ONE): when will MIP be in place and is there accelerated Chinese dumping or domestic inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MIP is under dialogue with government, which has recommended a price considered too low; industry is pressing for a realistic MIP. China was ~50% of India's PVC imports last year, and no timeline can be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj: how will Middle East alumina capacity outages affect the global caustic balance and domestic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Shriram said regional balances matter and the impact of one demand region cannot be directly correlated to price; expects robust Indian demand long term with some short-term volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha (Unifi Capital): ECH utilisation and margin outlook, and epoxy break-even timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ECH running at 60-70% utilisation, ramp-up over one to two quarters; management expects healthy ECH margins if raw material and product prices hold. Epoxy/advanced materials expected to reach break-even in FY27, with Amit Agarwal saying slightly better than break-even this year.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: is ECH margin still in the 20-25% range and will chemicals EBITDA margin (about 20% in FY26) improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said Bharuch should be assessed as an integrated complex; complex revenue +38% and EBITDA +50% last year; new products rose from ~14% to ~34-35% of revenue. Aditya Shriram declined to give a margin number.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: will sugar margins be material in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said margins are lower than last year, but record-low industry inventory (~4 million tonnes) should lift prices; shrinkage expected but not significant. The export ban has only short-term sentiment impact.

qa_highlights.question: Riya Mehta (Aequitas): Fenesta cost pass-through, margins and demand after aluminium price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said retail customers are hard to pass cost to, while institutional contracts pass through costs beyond a tolerance level; margin is hit until then. Demand is good with a record order book.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: FY27 capex and Bioseed kharif trends?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR1,000-1,200 crore including board-approved projects and pipeline. Kharif placements are reasonable, with El Nino risk and cotton inventory as the main concern.

Management framed the quarter as the start of a domestic diversification phase, anchored by a newly operational Andheri (Mumbai) manufacturing facility outside the SEZ. This was the company's first formal earnings call, and management said near-term volumes from the domestic facility will be small.

financial_highlights.change: +22.7% YoY vs INR69.44 crore in Q1 FY26
up from INR230 crore two years earlier
up from INR16.9 crore two years earlier (about 35%)

segments.name: Export (Middle East, USA, Europe)
segments.commentary: Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain) contributes about 85-90% of total business; USA share has fallen to below 10% from 20-30% a year earlier due to tariffs. Management pegs current export run-rate at about INR280 crore.

segments.name: Domestic (Andheri, Mumbai facility)
segments.commentary: Facility covers about 5,360 sq ft with estimated capacity of 125-150 kg jewellery per annum, expected to lift overall capacity by 50-60%. Currently producing sample lines; management expects only INR15-20 crore revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Lab-grown diamond jewellery
segments.commentary: Management put lab-grown at less than 5-7% of current revenue, mainly from the US market. Domestic B2C lab-grown retail launch is targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of around 15-20%, predominantly from exports.
Domestic business targeted at about 50% of total revenue by 2030; implied revenue of INR550-600 crore on current export base.
Andheri facility peak revenue potential of around INR250-300 crore in about three years; revenue mix depends on gold carat mix (shift from 18k to 14k, 10k, 9k).
Five-year target of revenue more than double the current level.
Domestic EBITDA margin expected to be tighter initially, converging to export levels over time; B2C expected to be better margin than B2B but insignificant in FY27.
capex_capacity: Andheri, Mumbai facility (approx. 5,360 sq ft, three-storey; two storeys operational, third storey being built as a retail lounge for B2C) is up and running with 125-150 kg per annum estimated capacity.
Existing two facilities are in an SEZ and export-focused; the Andheri unit is the first outside SEZ for domestic operations.
Preferential allotment of convertible warrants (about INR27 crore) to fund facility expansion and working capital.
Inventory days cited at roughly 10-11 times for exports, with management expecting domestic to be similar or better.
demand_pricing: Retail customers are shifting from 18k to 14k, and in some cases 9k-10k gold jewellery, following gold price increases.
Top 10 customers account for approximately 60-65% of revenue (management could not give top-5 split).
Diamonds are hedged via forward contracts covering 4-6 months of receivables; gold has a natural hedge through matched import/export pricing.
Management said the Middle East revenue was not materially affected by the Hormuz disruption beyond roughly a month of air-freight stoppage from late February to March 2026.
Competition in domestic lab-grown is nascent; management named no specific head-to-head competitor and cited branded retailers and traditional jewellers as entrants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic expansion strategy given competition from organised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-pronged: manufacture for major Indian retail chains already served in the Middle East, and pursue B2C retail, especially lab-grown, over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US business exported or through a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: No subsidiary; sales are to wholesalers, distributors and retailers in Middle East, USA and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can the new capacity generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates INR250-300 crore of incremental revenue potential, subject to gold carat mix.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and 2030 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth of 15-20%, mainly exports; domestic to reach 50% of business by 2030, implying INR550-600 crore total on current export base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the lab-grown contribution and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab-grown is under 5-7% of revenue, mostly US; management hopes it will be a significant domestic contributor but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 revenue from the Mumbai facility and when does B2C start?
qa_highlights.answer: INR15-20 crore in FY27; B2C launch targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026), with B2C insignificant in FY27.

risks_watch: Domestic ramp is unproven: FY27 facility revenue guided at only INR15-20 crore against a 2030 target of about 50% domestic mix.
Heavy concentration: top 10 customers are about 60-65% of revenue, and Middle East is 85-90% of business.
Domestic EBITDA is expected to be thinner initially, which could dilute the 10.14% margin as B2B and B2C scale.
Gold price shifts toward lower carat jewellery and the 250-300 crore capacity estimate depend on mix assumptions.
Management said the company is still building a brand and retail experience for B2C; it gave no B2C target beyond the Diwali launch.
523676|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term domestic and lab-grown ambitions, but vague or deferential on specifics; several answers lacked numbers (e.g., competitors, B2C mix, margins) and the CEO had to look up top-10 customer share. Clear and specific on near-term FY27 guidance and the Middle East share.

So right now for the current year, our target is to have a growth of around 15 % to 20%.

rows.why: Preferential warrant raise of about INR27 crore is earmarked for facility expansion and working capital, and management targets domestic at 50% of revenue by 2030, which implies further capacity beyond the current 125-150 kg plant.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Domestic B2C lab-grown retail launch is targeted around Diwali 2026, though B2C is insignificant in FY27 and lab-grown is under 5-7% of revenue today.

rows.why: Retail customers are moving to lower-carat gold after gold price rises, and the INR250-300 crore Andheri revenue potential depends on this mix.
