523694|2026-03.headline: Apcotex Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 42% YoY to INR 55 crore at a 13.76% margin, with PAT up 107% to INR 35 crore.
523694|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR 398 crore (+14% YoY) on 10% volume growth, with EBITDA margin of 13.76% and PAT margin of 8.73%. FY26 delivered record sales volumes (+14% YoY) and record exports, but revenue grew only 4% to INR 1,442 crore while EBITDA hit a record INR 177 crore. Q4 included about INR 14 crore of employee-benefit provisions, INR 4 crore turbine impairment and INR 2 crore extra depreciation, which management called largely one-off. Management said the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure created short-term margin gains in Nitrile latex and some export disruption, and it did not give quarterly guidance.

financial_highlights.value: Cash and investments ~INR 160 crore vs total debt ~INR 92 crore; net cash ~INR 70 crore

segments.name: Nitrile latex
segments.commentary: Management estimates it is 15-20% of FY26 revenue. Margins were structurally below the base business in FY26 but improved every quarter, with March 2026 described as exceptional due to competitor supply issues. Utilisation was 90-100% across plants in Q4.

segments.name: NBR (nitrile butadiene rubber)
segments.commentary: Running at 100% utilisation for several quarters and expected to stay full for about four more quarters until new capacity arrives in Q1 of the following fiscal year (FY28). The expansion will almost double NBR capacity.

segments.name: ApcoBuild
segments.commentary: Management expects double-digit growth after a manpower issue early in FY26 was corrected and the distribution channel was reviewed; the division ended the year strong.

segments.name: Synthetic latex
segments.commentary: New capacity is being built and is expected to come on stream in FY28, with some headroom in the existing plants.

segments.name: Middle East exports
segments.commentary: About 12% of total revenue, covering UAE, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey. Management says the business is good but margins have been hit by freight and raw material cost increases.

segments.name: Europe and US
segments.commentary: About 2-4% of revenue combined.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly guidance. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than the FY26 average, though quarter-on-quarter progression is uncertain.
FY27 volume growth expected in low double digits for the full year, against capacity that is already running near full. Revenue growth depends on raw material prices and is not guided.
Nitrile latex: no capacity addition in FY27. Debottlenecking will add a little. Major capacity lands in Q1 FY28.
A possible step-up in Nitrile latex capacity at low cost has its plan ready. Equipment lead time is 8-9 months and a decision is expected in the next 3-6 months, so any capacity would arrive in FY28.
Raw material cover is in place through end-June 2026. The company is not taking a view on crude or petrochemical prices.
Management expects a 2026 new R&D centre spend of INR 20-25 crore; there is no stated timeline for ADD relief.
capex_capacity: NBR expansion will almost double NBR capacity, with new capacity due in Q1 of FY28.
Nitrile latex: new capacity expected in FY28 (by Q1). Quarter-4 utilisation was 90-100% across plants and it is expected to stay near 100%.
Synthetic latex: new capacity being built, expected in FY28, with headroom in existing plants.
New R&D centre approved by the board, with spend of INR 20-25 crore.
Co-gen turbine at Valia impaired by about INR 4 crore; the turbine is kept as backup and may be sold. Co-gen asset useful life cut from 40 years to 15 years.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume +10% YoY and FY26 volume +14% YoY, with record exports. FY26 revenue grew only 4%, so realisations were weak in FY26.
Raw material costs rose sharply in March 2026 with the West Asia crisis; management said the blended Q4 increase tracked a roughly 70% jump in crude over a couple of months.
Customers face pushback on price increases, particularly automotive-linked customers. Management called this a big concern for the long term.
In Middle East markets, Chinese latex has started entering Turkey and Egypt for the first time. Apcotex costs there have risen against Chinese competitors.
The Finance Ministry has not notified the DGTR-recommended anti-dumping duties, which the company wanted for five years on NBR. These were not in the plan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 13-14 crore employee benefit provision and why did depreciation change?
qa_highlights.answer: Three items: a new five-year long-term incentive plan (INR 2.7 crore for the year, now expensed quarterly), pending litigation provision on external legal advice, and a gratuity policy change tied to the new wage code. Depreciation on co-gen assets was cut from 40 to 15 years because the turbine is idle, and the Valia turbine was impaired by about INR 4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 EBITDA the new base for the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly guidance is given. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than the FY26 average at higher utilisation, but quarterly progression is uncertain given the war and raw material volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Jan and Feb were already good. March was an exceptional month because competitors could not supply reliably. Some of the gain will reverse in coming quarters, and the structural part is hard to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash position and non-recurring items?
qa_highlights.answer: At 31 March 2026, total debt was INR 92 crore and cash plus investments about INR 160 crore, so net cash was about INR 70 crore. Non-recurring items were the litigation provision, the gratuity change and the turbine impairment; the LTI is recurring and the depreciation change is mostly recurring, with INR 3-4 crore of it to recur.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material cost increase and customer resistance to price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended Q4 raw material cost rose broadly in line with crude. Customers in automotive are squeezed, and management called demand destruction a big concern. A sharp fall in prices would compress margins because the company has covered its raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nitrile latex contribution to FY26 revenue and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue share is about 15-20%, confirmed by the CFO. No EBITDA figure was given. Nitrile latex margins were structurally below the base business in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Low double-digit volume growth for the full year if demand holds and capacity allows. Revenue growth is not guided because pricing is unknown.

risks_watch: The Strait of Hormuz remains closed. Raw material cover runs to end-June 2026, with styrene now sourced from China.
Middle East exports are about 12% of revenue. Demand is falling there and Chinese latex is entering Turkey and Egypt.
Margin gains in March-April are partly temporary, and a fall in crude could compress margins as covered inventory is consumed.
Nitrile latex remains in oversupply long term. Margin recovery to pre-COVID levels is management's expectation but has no timeline.
Working capital will absorb cash as raw material prices rise, reversing the FY26 inflow of about INR 50 crore.
Anti-dumping duty on NBR is not notified, and a decision on the Nitrile latex expansion is due in the next 3-6 months.
523694|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet and operations, having run plants without any shutdown during the war. Cautious and openly uncertain on quarterly margins, pricing and Middle East demand, and avoids guidance on Nitrile latex margins.
key_quotes: Fortunately, we have been able to run our plant without one, even one day of shutdown because we were able to take some bold calls in early March.
Structurally, also, there was an improvement, right? Over the course of the year, every quarter, there has been a structural improvement in margins.
So, we expect it to only improve cash generation, on an annual basis.
We are running at almost full 100% capacity utilization now for Nitrile latex.

rows.why: NBR expansion under construction to almost double NBR capacity, with NBR at 100% utilisation for several quarters; synthetic latex capacity being built for FY28.

rows.why: Management guides low double-digit volume growth for FY27 after FY26 volume rose 14% and Q4 volume rose 10%, but capacity is already running near full (Q4 utilisation 90-100%) until new capacity lands in FY28.

rows.why: Nitrile latex utilisation at 90-100% in Q4 with no nitrile capacity add until Q1 FY28; a low-cost step-up plan is ready and the decision is expected within 3-6 months, with equipment lead time of 8-9 months.

rows.why: Management is running ahead on margins in March-April, but explicitly declines quarterly guidance and says some gains will reverse, so an upgrade is conditional on crude and nitrile supply.

rows.why: Management called customer pushback on price increases a big long-term concern, particularly in automotive-linked customers, while raw material costs rose sharply in March 2026.

523694|2026-06.headline: Apcotex Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 526 crore (+40% YoY) and PAT rose 311% to Rs 79 crore, helped by price realisations and inventory gains.
523694|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of Rs 526 crore, up 40% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 117 crore (22.3% margin vs 10.3%) and PAT of Rs 79 crore (15.01% margin vs 5.11%). Volumes fell 10-12% because exports to the MENA region were hit by West Asia disruption, freight costs and logistics issues, while domestic volumes rose about 10%. Management said inventory gains added roughly 2% to EBITDA margin. Working capital rose on higher raw material prices, and net cash fell to about Rs 40 crore from about Rs 70 crore at March 2026 (Q&A noted a figure of about Rs 30 crore).

segments.name: Nitrile latex (NBR/XNBR)
segments.commentary: Margins improved in Q1 versus prior years; management said they were above 15% in Q1 but did not reach that level through FY25-26. NBR is capacity-constrained with ~30% Indian market share, the rest met by imports.

segments.name: Synthetic latex / other products
segments.commentary: Management said margins expanded across all segments in Q1, not just nitrile latex. Company cites about 25 new products added and eight end-industries served.

segments.name: Apco build (small segment)
segments.commentary: Described as growing but still a small part of the business; no numbers given.

guidance_outlook: Average EBITDA margin guidance remains 15-16%; management declined to call Q1 margins sustainable and said it expects some quarters lower and some higher.
NBR capacity expansion expected on stream by Q1 FY28 (possibly April 2028); SB latex and other synthetic latex capex about a couple of months later (around June 2028).

Combined capex of about Rs 220 crore (Rs 130-140 crore for NBR debottlenecking/expansion adding roughly 100% of NBR capacity, rest for synthetic latex). Management expects about Rs 600 crore additional top line, roughly 40% uplift from announced projects.
Decision on a third (stage two) nitrile latex expansion expected in 3-4 months, after watching margins and Asian/Malaysian capacity.
Management expects volumes to rebound quickly once the West Asia conflict eases; said volumes in MENA may not grow near term while oil prices stay high.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 220 crore is in progress; only 15-20% spent so far, mainly advances and civil work. Major equipment deliveries are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
NBR debottlenecking/expansion costs Rs 130-140 crore and adds nearly 100% of current NBR capacity; original estimate was Rs 200-250 crore.
Plants run on dual fuel (gas and coal), and each raw material has multiple sources.
Capex so far is self-funded; management expects to take debt in the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Volumes fell 10-12% YoY and QoQ, entirely due to exports; MENA customers were hit by Strait of Hormuz disruption. Domestic volumes rose about 10%.

Realisations were higher in Q1, but management said they started falling late in the quarter as oil and raw material prices eased. It expects another price rise in August-September if crude rises again.
Domestic demand described as strong across paper, construction, rubber goods and others. Ocean freight costs were absorbed by the company on exports.

Competition: no anti-dumping duty in India currently. Management said Europe and the US have no NBR expansion announced; some Asian expansions are coming but expected to be absorbed in three to five years.
Working capital rose because of higher raw material values. Inventory days were unchanged; the increase came from price, not quantity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin came from inventory gains, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains added about 2% to EBITDA margin. Management now talks about average margins of 15-16%, not a sustainable level, and said the next few quarters may be lower or higher.

qa_highlights.question: What made the business resilient this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited deliberate investments in dual fuel, multiple raw material sources, quick procurement and inventory planning. It said these had been built over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Can throughput double in five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Announced projects should add about Rs 600 crore to top line, roughly 40%. Further doubling depends on market support, and management sees no reason it cannot happen.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the NBR expansion approved now?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex fell to Rs 130-140 crore for almost 100% NBR capacity via debottlenecking, from Rs 200-250 crore earlier. Margins had improved and there is no major NBR expansion globally, so returns were justified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and capex spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cash of about Rs 40 crore, down from about Rs 70 crore at March, partly due to higher working capital. Only 15-20% of the Rs 220 crore capex has been spent.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand or realisation rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations were higher on average in Q1 but are now falling with oil. Domestic demand is strong across sectors; exports are the main issue, mainly MENA.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz; management says volumes fall when exports are disrupted.
Q1 margins were lifted by inventory gains and supply tightness; management said the next 3-4 months will show whether margins hold.
Raw material and realisation swings with crude oil; management said net realisation is hard to predict.
Nitrile latex overcapacity in the glove supply chain and possible Asian expansions, including Malaysia (starting July-August 2026).
Working capital and inventory values rise with raw material prices; net cash has fallen.
Q2 seasonality: rains affect construction and footwear demand (the June-August quarter).
523694|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and the quarter, but cautious on sustainability of margins and timing of nitrile latex expansion. Management repeatedly declined to give normalised margin or volume numbers, saying oil and the war make the outlook hard to call.
key_quotes: We are quite confident of 15%, 16% average margins that I have mentioned before as well.
The NBR will be on stream by Q1 next year as per plan right now.
We have not taken any debt for it yet, but we will be in the next couple of quarters.

rows.why: EBITDA margin was 22.3% in Q1 vs 10.3% a year ago, but inventory gains added ~2 points and management guides average 15-16%, so margins are more likely to normalise than expand.

rows.why: NBR debottlenecking adds nearly 100% of current NBR capacity for Rs 130-140 crore and is under construction with major equipment due Q3-Q4 FY27, though only 15-20% of the ~Rs 220 crore capex is spent so far.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic volumes rose ~10% and demand is strong across paper, construction and rubber goods, but total volumes fell 10-12% as MENA exports were hit; export recovery depends on the West Asia conflict.

rows.when: next 3-4 months for stage-two nitrile latex decision
rows.why: Management approved NBR expansion and will decide a third (stage two) nitrile latex expansion in 3-4 months; NBR is capacity-constrained with ~30% Indian share and no major global NBR expansion announced.

rows.why: Management expects volumes to rebound quickly once West Asia eases and expects a price rise in August-September if crude rises again, but both depend on oil and the conflict.

rows.why: Company has added about 25 new products across eight end-industries, and Apco build is growing, but no specific new launch dates were given.

rows.why: Capex of ~Rs 220 crore is self-funded so far and net cash fell from ~Rs 70 crore to ~Rs 40 crore, with management expecting to take debt in the next couple of quarters.

rows.why: Working capital rose on higher raw material values while inventory days were unchanged, so net cash is under pressure until prices settle.

tone.note: Management was confident on operations, dual fuel and raw material sourcing, and on the NBR timeline, but cautious on margin sustainability, MENA export volumes and oil-linked realisations; analysts pushed on how much of margin came from inventory gains and what is sustainable.

523704|2026-03.headline: Mastek Q4 FY26 revenue rose 3.6% QoQ to INR938 crore with EBITDA steady at 16.1%; 12-month backlog up 13.5% YoY in USD.
523704|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was described by management as a stable quarter: USD revenue of $103.5 million was up 1.4% QoQ (flat in constant currency), and EBITDA held at 16.1% despite a $1.1 million salary increase. FY26 revenue grew 7% YoY in INR to INR3,699 crore, with EBITDA flat at 15.8%. Reported PAT was hit by a INR23.7 crore exceptional Labour Code true-up in Q4 (INR6.4 crore in Q3), which management moved below EBITDA and which restated Q3 EBITDA to 16.8%. Management guided to FY27 growth above FY26 but declined to give a numerical target.

-0.7% QoQ, affected by Labour Code true-up

segments.commentary: Grew ~11% in GBP and 21.8% in INR in FY26; UK EBITDA about 20% in Q4. Healthcare (NHS-led) grew ~24% in USD and 90%+ in INR in FY26. Q4 UK sequentially up, 12-month backlog up significantly.

segments.name: North America (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat QoQ on project ramp-downs; EBITDA margin down YoY and QoQ on revenue stabilisation and wage hikes. segments.commentary: Grew sequentially in Q4 and recognised ~$0.5 million of WAR-related revenue deferred from Q2. Margin down YoY and QoQ on flat revenue and wage hikes. Middle East faces short-term geopolitical headwinds; new decision-making has slowed.

segments.name: Financial services
segments.commentary: Described as the star of the quarter; ramp-up from large North American BFSI wins and UK/AMEA FS orders. Management said FCA deal reached 60+ onsite resources and will be fully ramped by end Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Sequential dip in Q4 from project timing gaps (live transitions in UK and US) with new projects yet to start; management expects recovery as new programmes ramp.

523704|2026-06.headline: Mastek Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% QoQ to INR 985 crore (1.8% cc), with 12-month backlog up 25% YoY to $310 million.

Middle East disruption raised bench costs and delayed collections, weighing on margin, while UK and North America both grew sequentially. Management highlighted a $25 million, five-year AI transformation deal in North America and a 12-month backlog of $310 million. Top-5 and top-10 client revenue declined QoQ due to a timing gap on NHS England projects, and ESOP expense starts from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Excluding the $25 million US deal, the order book looks flat QoQ; how does the funnel look, when will Middle East deals ramp, and will US and Middle East margins stay suppressed?

Margin pressure came from slower-than-expected ramp-ups causing bench cost and one-time collection slowdowns, expected to reverse later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting cost trend and ESOP impact going forward?

523704|2026-09.headline: Mastek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% QoQ cc to $107.3M, but 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M and EBITDA margin slipped to 14.4%.
523704|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 2.4% QoQ in constant currency to $107.3M (Rs 1,018.7 crore, up 8.3% YoY in INR), with PAT of Rs 105.7 crore. Operating EBITDA margin fell about 100 bps QoQ to 14.4%, mainly from increments and ESOPs (190 bps), partly offset by AI-led efficiency and extra working days. The 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M, attributed to a delayed US federal start and slower UK consumption, though it grew 2.3% YoY in USD. Management reiterated that FY27 should beat FY26, with North America turning around from H2 and UK Healthcare recovering after recontracting.

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and investments (net of debt)
financial_highlights.change: up about Rs 36 crore after Rs 50 crore dividend and Rs 55 crore loan repayment

segments.name: UK-Europe

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Total backlog rose 7.8% QoQ and 47.9% YoY. Management expects a meaningful growth turnaround from H2, though a $25M federal deal start has slipped to after the mid-term elections.

segments.name: APAC & Middle East
segments.commentary: Some older contracts were signed, giving a revenue bounce-back in Q2. Management said the Middle East outlook is uncertain and performance is well below plan, especially in Saudi Arabia.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Public sector grew 6.1% QoQ and Financial Services grew 15.3% QoQ. Healthcare & Life Sciences has been slow for two quarters, with management expecting recovery after beta-phase contract awards in Q3 or early Q4.

US and Middle East margins expected to improve from Q3, which should offset some of the UK mix-driven margin loss.

qa_highlights.answer: A $25M US federal deal start was delayed until after the mid-term elections, and a UK contract is consuming more slowly than planned, with pickup expected around Q4. Management still expects FY27 to beat FY26, citing H2 strength in UK and US and a Middle East dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI deals from new or existing clients, what are the deal sizes, and when will AI revenue be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: AI deals come from both new and existing clients, with at least two net-new wins in the examples shown. Typical AI deal size is $0.5M-$5M, and AI revenue figures will be presented from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline, and what is the bridge to the 160 bps recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments and ESOPs cost 190 bps. A UK mix shift from high-margin projects to lower-margin sovereignty and security-cleared work cost about 200 bps. AI-led efficiencies and restructuring recovered about 200 bps. Forex was a 20 bps tailwind. US and Middle East margins are expected to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America growth muted, and how do BFSI and healthcare trends differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a North America turnaround from H2. Healthcare & Life Sciences remains its strongest vertical, and BFSI growth is mainly UK-led. North America financial services is still early-stage.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI deals grow after the initial POC, and what margins do they earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI engagements typically expand into more process areas after the first win. Transformation and foundation deals earn 40%+ gross margin, while AI productivity deals carry compressed margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter energy and utilities, and what is the Top 5/Top 10 trend and subcon outlook?

523716|2026-03.headline: Ashiana Housing FY26 booking value hit record Rs 2,421 crore (+25% YoY); Q4 bookings Rs 1,290 crore driven by Gurugram Aaroham launch.
523716|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 bookings of Rs 1,290 crore rose 124% YoY, led by Ashiana Aaroham Phase-I and II in Gurugram (about Rs 833 crore at launch), with realisation up 71% YoY to Rs 11,566 per sq ft. Q4 total income rose 46% YoY to Rs 335 crore on handovers in Jaipur, Pune and Chennai, while PAT was flat at Rs 21 crore (6.26% margin). For FY26, total income more than doubled to Rs 1,187 crore, EBITDA rose 281% to Rs 176 crore (14.85% margin) and PAT reached Rs 118 crore versus Rs 18 crore in FY25. Management added about 2.9 lakh sq ft-equivalent of Senior Living land and reiterated a Rs 2,200 crore FY27 pre-sales target.

523754|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.8% to INR315.8 crores and PBT to INR16.99 crores, but Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores on a March raw-material spike.

Receivables built up sharply in a few key subsidy states, and operating free cash flow has been negative over multi-year periods, which an analyst pressed on. Management pointed to non-subsidy share rising to 35% in FY26 (from 3% in FY20 per the call) and to a projects pipeline of about INR54-55 crores for FY27.

523796|2026-03.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q4 FY26 revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 49.5 crore, with EBITDA margin up 183 bps to 31.4%, aided by the Marriott Executive Apartments acquisition.

Growth was driven mainly by consolidation of Marriott Executive Apartments (75 rooms, acquired 1 January 2026), which contributed its first quarter. Management said March was softer on geopolitical tensions and the West Asia conflict, with ADR and occupancy moderating at the existing hotels. PAT fell to about INR 6 crore, which management attributed to higher depreciation and finance costs from renovation and acquisition debt, and to a deferred-tax benefit booked in the prior year.

523796|2026-06.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 77% to INR44.9 crore and EBITDA rose 144% to INR11.8 crore, with PAT turning positive at INR1.4 crore.

523828|2026-03.headline: Menon Bearings FY26 consolidated PAT rose 53.41% to INR 38.25 crore; Q4 PAT up 108.55% YoY, with management guiding 20-22% EBITDA margin.

Management guided to 25% annual volume growth, 20-22% EBITDA margin for the next two years, and INR 500 crore revenue by FY28. Alkop (aluminium) growth was flagged as a key swing factor after a slow prior two years.

523828|2026-06.headline: Menon Bearings Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 36.57% to INR91.79 crores and PAT 67.35%, with management reiterating INR360 crore FY27 revenue as conservative.

524000|2026-03.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q4 FY26 PAT rose 69.6% QoQ to ₹255 crore, NIM recovered to 9.05% and ROA to 1.81%, with credit cost down to 2.51%.

PAT reached ₹255 crore (up 69.6% QoQ) and full-year PAT was ₹542 crore. Asset quality improved across Stages 1, 2 and 3, with GNPA at 1.44% and 6MoB30+ at 1.05%. segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: 400 gold branches operationalised as committed; Q4 disbursement about ₹819 crore; over 90% of branches in Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations.

segments.name: Consumer durables

segments.name: Commercial vehicles

segments.commentary: Launched a year ago; over 22,000 files processed and about ₹900 crore disbursed cumulatively; around 500+ consultants and partners; instant sanction about 20% of sanctions.

FY27 AUM growth guidance of 35-40% with commensurate disbursements; management said it could be a notch better.

Management said it is not doing micro-LAPs and has no exposure to small-ticket LAP segments, and cited the Middle East conflict as a watch item but no current stress.
Stage 1 assets 97.5% (97.4% in Q3 FY26); Stage 2 1.1%; Stage 3 1.44%; provisioning coverage 49%.

qa_highlights.question: What are disbursement yield and book yield for the quarter, and is the geopolitical situation a risk to asset quality or provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited disbursement yield of 15.96% (up 40 bps QoQ) and said portfolio yield will catch up gradually. qa_highlights.question: Guidance on fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical guidance was given. Management expects fee income strength in FY27 from processing fees, insurance and cross-sell, with growth now more calibrated after the launch phase.

qa_highlights.question: Status of technology and AI journey?
qa_highlights.answer: PL Prime is about 30% digital of a ₹480-500 crore monthly-scale business and expected to rise to 30-40%. Business loan digitisation is planned in 6-9 months. AI projects are cutting manpower needs, with no new PL underwriters hired.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROA and FY27 disbursement and AUM plans?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA expected to keep improving over the next few quarters, with no interim guidance. FY27 AUM growth guided at 35-40% with commensurate disbursements. Opex-to-AUM expected lower by March 2027, with 10-25 bps QoQ swings.

Management attributed margin gains to a ~50 bps rise in disbursement yield from product mix, and guided to a June 2028 exit ROA of 3-3.5%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no emerging stress: 6-MoB 30+ for the latest sourcing is 0.64% vs 1.05% in Q4; Stage 3 slippage improved ~13% and Stage 1 slippage ~5% QoQ; bounce rates are stable to lower; collection efficiency is ~99.6%.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal: Among the six newer businesses, which has surprised positively and which has scaled slower, and has strategy changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shopkeeper loans are the only product not being accelerated, given credit cost and ROA considerations. Gold has 460 branches with ~60 opened this fiscal. Education loans are around ₹144 crores monthly. CV and CD early vintages are performing better than historical data. Management also said agri and microfinance are not in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal: Cost of borrowing rose ~9 bps QoQ, so will it keep inching up?
qa_highlights.answer: Arvind Kapil said the increase is not a concern, citing NCDs at 25-30% of funding and a diversified borrowing mix. He said disbursement yield rose 50 bps this quarter after 40 bps last quarter, and the company should remain NIM accretive. No formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Pranay Mehta (Investec): What growth and profitability can be expected over the next 8-10 quarters, and are more new products coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the June 2028 exit ROA guidance of 3-3.5% from 1.98% today. It cited rising yields and better credit cost via calibration and collections. No specific new product launch was detailed.

qa_highlights.question: Pranay Mehta: Are NBFCs reporting stress in IT-sector distribution, and what is the company's view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the six-product mix spans different economic cycles. Business loans are held at ~10-16% growth versus over 40% in used cars, and it will slow products where calibration needs it. It is watchful of macro indicators, and agri and microfinance are not in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Is the quarterly write-off run-rate of about ₹275-280 crores recurring, or is there a legacy element?
qa_highlights.answer: Shriram Iyer said write-offs have declined QoQ, the legacy portfolio is now immaterial, and write-offs should not rise. He confirmed ₹275-280 crores as the run-rate for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint: Is the fall in PCR (Stage 2 coverage near 18%) normalised, and what is the cost of funding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PCR is range-bound and is driven by product mix; the legacy high-ECL book has run off, and gold and education loan share increases will lower PCR over time. Sanjay Miranka said a small cost-of-funds uptick is possible but disbursement yield gains should offset it, with no NIM challenge seen. Gold LTV is 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Trade-off between growth and profitability; sustainable ROA and the split of ROA gains between operating leverage and credit cost?

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality improvement from underwriting or benign credit conditions? Are AI/ML models reducing loss rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to proprietary models (30-35 models) and calibration. It cited bureau data showing consumer durable borrowers completing 9-month loans are about 40% better credit than industry.

qa_highlights.question: With most of the book under 12 months seasoned, why are write-offs still high, and what is the impact of the insurance commission regulation?

524164|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR619 crore (+17.4% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose 251 bps to 15.2%, helped by Ibuprofen demand recovery and higher prices.
524164|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR619 crore versus INR528 crore a year earlier, the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue. EBITDA rose about 40% to INR94 crore, with margin up 251 bps to 15.2%, and PAT rose 68% to about INR53 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 11.5% to INR2,319 crore, EBITDA grew about 29% to INR290 crore (margin 12.4% vs 10.7%), and PAT rose about 36% to INR138 crore. Management attributed the gains to utilisation, product mix, non-Ibuprofen traction and a late-quarter price uptick that was partly offset by raw material cost increases.

Management sees no supply problems on raw materials except for about one week in early March when crude-based chemicals and gas supply were disrupted.
Non-Ibu customers are mainly direct consumers rather than traders, which limits the upside from price moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 gross margin sustainable, or was it an inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to efficiency, product mix and capacity utilisation, plus a late-quarter price rise; it said there was no meaningful inventory gain and that quarter-to-quarter prediction is risky.

qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said Ibu is one of its best products, with 90-95% utilisation, and sees no issues for the next two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much R&D spend, and what products are in the launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 2-3% of revenue annually and is mainly process-related. Management did not name specific upcoming launches, saying products are announced when a decision is taken.

524200|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone net income including other income rose 17% QoQ to INR631 crores, EBITDA grew 20% QoQ to INR203 crores and PAT rose 27% QoQ to INR137 crores. For FY26, standalone net income was flat at INR2,281 crores while EBITDA and PAT grew 17% and 18%. Demand softened from October 2025 and management says it has since recovered. IBB volumes fell about 20% versus FY25 because of raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, which management says is now resolved. Management guides about 15% company-level volume growth in FY27 and FY27 capex of INR200-250 crores.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of FY26 revenue; management expects about 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next three years. Plant running at about 80% utilisation (about 75% post-expansion). Phase 2 of the expansion comes into effect by October 2026, with fuller utilisation in FY28.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Roughly 15-20% of FY26 revenue; revenue grew 15% in FY26. Management said FY26 AO volume was roughly flat-to-5% up, and the anti-dumping duty (ADD) application was rejected and reapplied, with a decision 6-9 months away.

segments.name: IB and HP-MTBE
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; stable in FY26, with management expecting double-digit growth in FY27.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; volume fell about 20% versus FY25 due to raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, now reported as resolved.

segments.name: Butyl phenols
segments.commentary: Capacity about 50,000 tonnes running at roughly 70-75% utilisation; management expects moderate growth in FY27 with no room for further expansion, so incremental demand goes first to captive use.

segments.name: Customised and others
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in FY26 on higher customer demand. Remainder of revenue mix.

segments.name: VOPL (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales were only about INR10 crores. Process reengineering of about 6 months to finish by September 2026, with production from October and revenue of about INR100-120 crores expected in FY27, from Q2/Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company-level volume growth guided at about 15%.
ATBS volume growth of about 15% YoY expected for at least the next three years.
FY27 capex earmarked at INR200-250 crores (about INR200 crores at Vinati Organics and INR40-50 crores at VOPL); management says about INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years.
AO and butyl phenol revenue targeted at INR800-900 crores in the next two years.
Long-term EBITDA margin of 26-27% considered achievable, given expansions, new products and raw material swings.
Gross block addition of about INR500 crores assumed at 1:1 asset turn.
Two to three new downstream products expected in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.
Company will continue to fund expansion from internal accruals and remain debt-free.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR270 crores, including VOPL capacity expansion, new product development and operational scalability. The ATBS capacity expansion was completed during FY26.

ATBS: a Phase 1 of 10,000 tonnes is commissioned. Total ATBS capacity is about 50,000 tonnes for lower molecular weight grades and about 40,000 tonnes for higher purity grades. Phase 2 (another 10,000 tonnes) expected by October 2026. Two-phase cost about INR250-300 crores.
CWIP was about INR210 crores at year-end, of which about INR60-70 crores is yet to be capitalised at VOPL. About INR120-125 crores of VOPL CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Pipeline products are downstream derivatives of MEHQ, butyl phenols and antioxidants, plus TAA, PTAP and 4-MAP at VOPL. Isoamylene derivatives were dropped. Monomers and polymers are under consideration but not confirmed.
Butyl phenol capacity of about 50,000 tonnes is at 70-75% utilisation with no space to expand.
demand_pricing: Demand softened from October 2025. Management says demand has since recovered, and ATBS is still growing at double-digit rates industry-wide.
ATBS pricing is stable and follows a formula-based mechanism. Management says it passes raw material and logistics price moves through to customers and holds margins.

AO faces undercutting and aggressive selling by Chinese producers. Management says ADD was not granted and has been reapplied, and it notes that 80-90% of ADD applications were rejected in the sector.
Raw material and logistics availability normalised after early disruption from the Iran war in Feb 2026. Logistics is described as stable.
ATBS end-use spans polymers for enhanced oil recovery, superabsorbents, personal care, detergents, mining and water treatment. Vinati sells to polymer makers, not directly to oilfield operators.

qa_highlights.question: What new products are in the pipeline, and when will they come online?
qa_highlights.answer: Most are downstream niche chemicals for fragrance, personal care, food-additive and plastics users. Two or three products are due in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue mix by product?
qa_highlights.answer: ATBS is about one-third and AO is 15-20%. IB is 10-12%, IBB is 10-12%, and customised and other products make up the rest, with overall ATBS and AO together around 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VOPL revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26. Management expects about INR100-120 crores in FY27 once reengineering finishes, with revenue from Q2/Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned in VOPL and how much CWIP is there?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40-50 crores of the FY27 capex goes to VOPL and about INR200 crores to the parent. VOPL CWIP of about INR120-125 crores is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATBS capacity and cost of the two expansion phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 50,000 tonnes (about 40,000 tonnes for higher-purity grades) with 10,000 tonnes per phase. The two phases cost about INR250-300 crores in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will AO and butyl phenol revenue reach the targeted INR700-800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is on track, with AO and butyl phenol revenue in the INR800-900 crore range within the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 26-27% EBITDA margin is a reasonable long-term level given expansions, new products and raw material swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AO growth lagged, and what is the status of the ADD?
qa_highlights.answer: AO growth was about 5% in FY26 because of aggressive Chinese undercutting. ADD was not granted, has been reapplied, and a decision could take 6-9 months.

risks_watch: AO margins and volumes depend on the anti-dumping duty decision, which could take another 6-9 months after reapplication, while Chinese players undercut prices.
VOPL revenue of INR100-120 crores in FY27 depends on finishing process reengineering by September 2026. The plant had teething troubles with its new process.
ATBS Phase 2 utilisation is expected to build mainly in FY28, and the plant is running at about 75-80% utilisation.
Butyl phenol capacity is at 70-75% utilisation with no room to expand, so growth may cut merchant sales.
Sector cyclicality has shortened, with sharp swings in raw material prices, logistics and customer destocking.
Management guidance rests on about 15% volume growth, a recovery from the October 2025 slowdown and IBB volumes resuming after the Iran war disruption.

So first of all, we did not hear back for the ADD on antioxidants, which means it was rejected. We have reapplied again for it because we have a strong case.

524200|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the balance sheet, ATBS demand, margins and the debt-free funding model, and openly acknowledges the slowdown from October 2025. Cautious and somewhat evasive on AO growth and the anti-dumping duty outcome, and on the VOPL timeline, which management said had hit teething troubles and was being re-engineered.

rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% in ATBS and butyl phenols are at 70-75% with no room to expand, and management has already guided INR200-250 crores for FY27 and INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years, so further capex plans are likely to be firmed up.

rows.why: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26; process reengineering of about 6 months must finish by September 2026 and the plant had teething troubles, so the ramp depends on that timeline.

rows.label: AO anti-dumping duty decision
rows.why: ADD was rejected and reapplied, with 80-90% of sector applications rejected historically, and AO revenue grew only about 15% in FY26 with volume roughly flat to 5% up under Chinese undercutting.

rows.label: IBB volume recovery after Iran-war disruption

524208|2026-03.headline: Aarti Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 2,422 crore and EBITDA 29% to INR 342 crore, with FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore.
524208|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,422 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 342 crore (up 29%) and PAT INR 137 crore (up 43%), helped by volume growth and higher utilisation. West Asia disruption raised benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene and methanol prices by over 60%, lifted freight costs and cut Middle East shipments, which are about 9-10% of revenue. Zone IV projects are delayed 3-4 months on contract labour shortages, with the bulk now expected in FY27. Management guided FY27 capex to INR 700-800 crore and aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite working-capital pressure.

segments.name: Energy applications
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue; volumes down 4% QoQ on lower Middle East exports. Expansion to 360 KTPA is on track and expected to commission soon. Middle East is about 9-10% of company revenue, mostly energy.

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Steady volume growth but margin pressure continues. A new $150 million multiyear agro intermediate contract runs to March 2030 with no incremental capex.

segments.name: Polymers
segments.commentary: Strong growth phase on EV-linked demand; MPDA continues to underperform due to Chinese competition.

segments.name: Dyes, pigments and paints
segments.commentary: Share of revenue about 10-11%. Demand pressure in 3,3'-DCBH globally, partly offset by domestic demand; some low-margin demand destruction possible in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Stable in the quarter; PNCB chain expected to benefit from China anti-involution from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore (about INR 150 crore a year is maintenance), funding Zone IV completion and a new INR 200-250 crore backward-integration contract.
Zone IV: calcium chloride and multipurpose plant to be commercialised within the quarter; remaining blocks commissioned through FY27 after a 3-4 month delay; initial revenue from Q2 FY27.
Management aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite higher working capital, as capex intensity falls and cash flow improves.
Tax rate guided at about 9-15% going forward.
Working capital target of 55-60 days, with the company currently above this level.
Augene (Superform JV) to commission around June-July 2026; recycling JV to commission in CY26.
Interest-cost and EBITDA potential from Zone IV and the UPL JV unchanged at INR 300-450 crore, but realisation may slip 6-7 months.
capex_capacity: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore; gross block expected at INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27.
Energy expansion to 360 KTPA on track for commissioning soon.
Contract labour availability in the capex region down 35%, delaying last-mile pipeline work.
Augene JV and recycling JV commissioning in 2026; DCB debottlenecking under way.
About 50% of the Bayer/Dicamba-linked asset is used for one intermediate, with steady volumes.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) rose over 60% in the quarter; some more than doubled.
Agro pricing is up sharply from January, but the company is holding spreads rather than absolute prices; full pass-through expected over 3-6 months.
NCB margins and pricing improved on China's anti-involution policy; DCB remains robust on EV demand.
MMA economics are volatile with gasoline-naphtha cracks ranging from negative to up $20/bbl; Middle East shipments physically halted, US shipments steady, Europe starting.
Physical supply of methanol (about a couple of months' cover) and sulfur (a few weeks' cover) is secure.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q4 margins, especially in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory impact was not significant; FX gain was about INR 10 crore in the quarter, and raw material costs also rose in March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9-10% of revenue on an annual average basis, mostly energy; product is being redirected elsewhere, with the full impact visible in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY27 capex fall and what is the breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore as guided, not reduced; FY27 guided at INR 700-800 crore mainly for Zone IV, the new long-term contract and about INR 150 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt high despite about INR 600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was a late-March term loan disbursement; net debt is about INR 4,300 crore, with bulk of cash used to repay debt in early April. Working capital rose INR 250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 freight and other-expense jump and inventory build?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rates rose from mid-February, exports were 57% of revenue, and US mix lengthened voyages; INR 409 crore stock build reflects goods in transit not yet recognised as revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Zone IV EBITDA and the net debt/EBITDA target at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost and operating-leverage initiatives are on track; the EBITDA potential is unchanged but may slip 6-7 months. Net debt/EBITDA was about 3.6x at year-end.

risks_watch: Middle East flows halted for 6-8 weeks; full Q1 FY27 impact on energy volumes depends on West Asia stabilisation.
Working capital and net debt rise if crude moves to USD 140-150/bbl.
Zone IV labour shortage and 3-4 month delay; check commissioning and first revenue in Q2 FY27.
Potential demand destruction in low-margin dyes and pigments over 3-6 months.
Unhedged USD 87 million FX loan; further rupee depreciation would add revaluation losses.
MPDA and agro margins remain under pressure from Chinese competition.

key_quotes: The overall demand environment for our basket of products remained largely stable.

rows.why: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore with gross block rising to INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27, energy expansion to 360 KTPA near commissioning, and Augene JV due June-July 2026, though labour shortage (down 35%) delays the last-mile work 3-4 months.

rows.why: Company is currently above the 55-60 day target after a INR 409 crore stock build (goods in transit), so release depends on freight and inventory normalising.

524208|2026-06.headline: Aarti Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 2,627 crore and EBITDA 79% to Rs 385 crore, with management refusing to guarantee the run rate.
524208|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 2,627 crore (+41% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) were lifted by raw-material price pass-through, product mix, and inventory and FX gains, which management sized at roughly Rs 50-60 crore. Volumes fell sequentially (energy -17% QoQ, non-energy -7%, overall about -12%) amid West Asia disruption and high raw-material prices. Zone IV commissioning is delayed by 3-6 months due to labour shortages, and management declined to commit to a forward EBITDA run rate. The Augene JV is near commissioning, and FY27 capex remains on track at Rs 700-800 crore.

segments.name: Energy (Fuel Additives)
segments.commentary: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; West Asia share fell to about 2% from about 15%, and volumes were redirected to US, Africa, Europe and India. Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged about $15-18/bbl, and management expects the capacity to reach high utilisation in Q1 itself.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Polymers
segments.commentary: Demand was soft in Q1 on weak downstream US and China demand, and low shipments followed heavy Q4 FY26 bulk shipments to the US. Management expects recovery in Q2 and full-year growth.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Dyes & Pigments
segments.commentary: Demand remained subdued amid high raw-material prices and seasonality. Price increases in dyes and pigments and pharma were partly linked to China's VAT removal on the NCB chain.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Pharma and Agro
segments.commentary: Pharma demand was stable. Agrochemical volumes were marginally lower as customers resisted elevated raw-material-linked prices; recovery is expected in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800 crore retained; the Augene JV is included in this guidance, but management said Zone IV ramp-up may be slower than originally assumed.
Management declined to guide to a sustainable quarterly EBITDA run rate, citing plus/minus 15-20% monthly price volatility; it expects volume growth to offset lost inventory gains.
Augene JV (50:50, consolidated at PAT level) expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, with steady-state revenue retained at Rs 300-400 crore.
FY27 capex on track at Rs 700-800 crore; capex intensity expected to fall significantly from FY28.

Zone IV commissioning is delayed 3-6 months; the MPP is expected to produce first product in August 2026 and commissioning will be announced thereafter. Management expects 5-10 products in FY27 and 25-30 by FY28.
Sabic-linked backward-integration project commissioning expected around Sep-Oct 2027.
capex_capacity: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; management said there is no fixed limit on further expansion, and it will first demonstrate utilisation over the next 12 months.
Zone IV: 97% of equipment erected and 85% of piping complete across the five chemistry blocks; full manpower restored, with commissioning expected in FY27 and ramp-up over FY28-FY29.
PEDA project in market seeding and expected to commercialise soon; DCB debottlenecking to 140 KTPA under evaluation.
NCB chain debottlenecking is being evaluated within existing assets given demand in India.
Aarti Circularity plastic recycling plant with Re Sustainability slated for commissioning in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inflation (benzene, sulphur, methanol, aniline) was passed through to customers; high prices reduced purchasing power in dyes, selected agro and polymer compounds.
Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/bbl, which management described as healthy, while the energy business remains volatile.
Exports were 59% of revenue; US-bound DAP shipments carry 2-3 month voyage times that delay revenue recognition.
China's suspension of export tax rebates is creating opportunities for the NCB value chain.
Non-energy volumes fell on delayed purchasing in a high-price environment, with some supply-chain effects; management said Middle East exposure in non-energy is low.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FX and inventory gains in Q1, and what is the impact on the EBITDA base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a Rs 50-60 crore impact but said it is hard to quantify because of intra-quarter volatility; the CFO said FX gains came from squaring off import positions as the rupee moved in a Rs 92-97 range, and management advised treating this as operating profit with no forward commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin lower sequentially despite the inventory and FX benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly gross margin is not a reliable steady-state indicator, citing timing of raw-material purchases and product placement, freight, lower volumes raising operating costs, and the chemical business running on absolute rupee deltas rather than percentage margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zone IV delay affect FY28 EBITDA visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MPP and calcium chloride unit are on track, but the five chemistry blocks face slower ramp-up than originally planned, and it will share ramp-up details once the blocks commission.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Augene JV affect reported EBITDA, and is it in the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that the Rs 1,800 crore FY28 guidance includes Augene EBITDA, while the Re Aarti JV is not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY28; reporting treatment for JVs is yet to be finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the energy business's volume, capacity and market share sustainable once West Asia normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business remains in a market-development phase; the portfolio is diversified across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India (Southeast Asia not yet penetrated), and it expects utilisation gains rather than volume shifts when West Asia reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing absolute sales volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it removed absolute sales numbers from slides because they were being used in an unfavourable way, and now gives energy/non-energy volume growth plus value-chain utilisation ranges.

risks_watch: Zone IV: five chemistry blocks face a 3-6 month delay and slower ramp-up; the MPP first product is expected in August 2026, and the FY28 Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance (which includes Augene) depends on this ramp-up.

Earnings quality: management said FX and inventory gains (Rs 50-60 crore, roughly Rs 47 crore per an analyst's figure) helped Q1, and it declined to commit to a forward quarterly EBITDA run rate given plus/minus 15-20% monthly price swings.

Energy seasonality and West Asia: management expects winter weakness from late October to December, and West Asia volumes (share down to about 2% from about 15%) are not yet restored; utilisation of the 360 KTPA fuel additives capacity is the key test over the next 12 months.
Working capital and leverage: management said working capital expanded and debt and finance costs rose in Q1; watch debt levels as imported-raw-material inventory (1-1.5 months) carries price risk.

Augene JV commissioning in Q2 FY27 and the Re Aarti JV reporting treatment, which management has yet to finalise; watch the Rs 300-400 crore steady-state revenue assumption and PAT-level consolidation.
key_quotes: In our guidance, we had given the numbers that will come from the capex-led programs and in capex-led, Zone IV was a significant contributor.
I would again hesitate to hazard a guess.
So we did not see the EBITDA run rate can be maintained.
The actual sales numbers is something that we have removed from the slides because they was getting utilized in a situation which was not favourable for the company.

524332|2026-06.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
524332|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

qa_highlights.question: At what price is ethanol sold to private players, and is it FCI rice or maize based?
qa_highlights.answer: Private ethanol buyers are mainly Reliance at an average ex-factory price of about INR 58/litre. Private buyers use damaged grain, while the company's own FCI-rice ethanol is tied to 40% of OMC allocation. Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Cause of the Bathinda fire and safeguards for other plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the likely cause was static charge, possibly from clothing of a nearby worker. The company has added facilities to prevent such incidents and called it rare.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for grain ethanol after E20 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is expected to improve only slightly next year because sugarcane ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel is a long-term driver, with isobutanol and SAF as additional sources, and cooking fuel use was also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics across FCI-rice, OMC maize and ENA/private ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: FCI-rice ethanol to OMCs is near cost. Maize-based ethanol to OMCs is quite profitable. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same, with blended EBITDA margin near 12%, or roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA on average.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Goyal bio-CNG, biodiesel and the 250 KLPD Goyal Distillery project?
qa_highlights.answer: Bio-CNG is under active evaluation after a favourable new policy, though paddy straw is tricky, mainly due to by-product sale. The company is not making biodiesel. The 250 KLPD Goyal project is on hold pending industry clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project on hold, and does maize oil locally sourced change this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biodiesel prices are not remunerative and biodiesel feedstock is largely imported, so government has focused less on it. Isobutanol is being tested to promote indigenous feedstock. Management said the government's view could not be commented on.

qa_highlights.question: Malt plant and IMFL entry timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Malt plant is still at conceptualisation with no timeline. IMFL entry is being worked on and is hoped for next year. Management views country liquor as more profitable than competitive IMFL.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the 250 KLPD Fatehabad project after the July statement about construction by August?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash against the ethanol policy. Machinery orders are finalised and the company is waiting before starting construction.

qa_highlights.question: Land sale timing, debt repayment and release of pledged shares?
qa_highlights.answer: No update on the land sale, as Bathinda real estate is slow and there is no rush. Working capital utilisation is low, some small loans were repaid, and banks released pledged shares. Working capital limit to be cut by INR 50 crore in August.

qa_highlights.question: Trend in DDGS realisations and Punjab country liquor market share?
qa_highlights.answer: DDGS prices eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for maize and rice based. Punjab country liquor market is about 1.25 crore cases a year, with a 30 lakh case target for this year.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook, total debt level and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes should stay about flat until the 200 KLPD unit restarts in about 15 days. Working capital utilisation is about INR 60 crore, with total debt around INR 360 crore including working capital. Debt rises only with a new capex project, and working capital is to be run towards zero over about 1.5 years. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol mixing in diesel, E20 damage, and government mandates beyond E20?
qa_highlights.answer: Management distinguished ethanol-in-diesel, which faces a flash point issue, from isobutanol, which it said is still under trial and not shelved. It said E20 has run 18 months without major vehicle damage, but further blending could be delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance cover and stock lost in the 200 KL tank, and expected restart?
qa_highlights.answer: The tank held about 90,000 litres at the time. The plant is being repaired and is expected to restart in about 15 days. Management said both stock loss and profit loss are covered by insurance, and the P&L impact is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of the Supreme Court-allowed OMC volume and the order book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is among the biggest gainers, with about 4.5 crore litres from both units under the Supreme Court order, covering until November. The order book is more than full for the next 3 months. Flex fuel demand will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Current maize price, margin outlook and state subsidy for CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize is about INR 25/kg now. ENA prices have been revised upwards, but raw material and fuel costs are rising. Management guided margins at about 10-12% with variation. Haryana has a CBG policy and the central policy is also favourable.

524342|2026-03.headline: Indo Borax Q4 FY26 revenue rose 25.7% to Rs 63.01 crore and PAT rose 41.9% to Rs 14.53 crore, with new promoter Zenrock in control.

FY26 revenue was Rs 215.45 crore (up 22.9%), EBITDA was flat at Rs 44.16 crore, and PAT was Rs 50.27 crore (up from Rs 42.51 crore). Management said the company changed control in January 2026 with Zenrock Chemicals as new promoter, and a new leadership team took over. A special dividend of Rs 30 per share plus a final dividend of Rs 10 per share (total Rs 40) was declared after monetising non-core assets. Management guided to Rs 250-plus crore revenue next year and 20-35% growth, but gave no formal numeric guidance, and no dividend policy has yet been declared.

Promoter group committed Rs 25 crore contingency; total funding Rs 432 crore vs about Rs 400 crore required.

Volume growth of 10-15% over the next two years is seen as achievable, and about 10% even if the salicylic acid derivatives do not pick up.
Volume growth in the remaining three quarters is expected to be better than June quarter, as demand recovers once prices stabilise.
Specialty Chemicals run-rate of Q1 is expected to repeat in the next three quarters and improve further.
Captive consumption from Sayakha is expected to reach 80-90% by December quarter, adding about 1% to gross contribution at peak utilisation.
Metformin capacity to rise from 1,400 to about 2,200 tpm, including 500-550 tpm USFDA-compliant capacity taking about 10-12 months.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 greenfield assets (Sayakha, Tarapur) cost about INR600 crore and are expected to yield about 1.5x asset turn; Phase 2 brownfield projects are expected at 3-4x.
Sayakha plant utilisation was about 65% in Q1 FY27 (versus 30% in Dec-quarter and 40% in Mar-quarter, per management), with about 50% of capacity used captively for antidiabetic intermediates.

demand_pricing: Metformin pricing up about 15-20% versus pre-war; the March-April peak was higher, and prices have since eased slightly.

Management says Chinese competition is not a concern for its product set, though some pressure exists from select players.
Salicylic acid prices were cut sharply by Chinese players, so derivatives (salicylates) are now more profitable than salicylic acid itself.
Europe is still a small, under-tapped market for Metformin; EU CEP approvals were obtained for 9 products.

qa_highlights.question: How did metformin realizations move QoQ and YoY, and how will backward integration support market share gains?

Metformin capacity is about 1,400 tpm at mid-80s% utilisation, scaling to about 2,200 tpm, including 500-550 tpm USFDA capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When can API supplies to the US market start, given the USFDA block timeline?

qa_highlights.question: Has the API industry entered a sustained recovery, and what is the asset turn on the INR600 crore capex?

Phase 1 greenfield assets are expected to give about 1.5x asset turn; Phase 2 brownfield about 3-4x, with Sayakha about 50% of capacity used captively.

524372|2026-03.headline: Orchid Pharma Q4 FY26 standalone revenue flat YoY at ~INR238 crore with EBITDA ~INR42.3 crore; FY26 EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore.
524372|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR238 crore, broadly flat versus about INR237 crore in Q4 FY25, and EBITDA rose to about INR42.3 crore from about INR40 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue fell to INR811 crore from INR922 crore and EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore, with management attributing this to cephalosporin price erosion and inventory write-downs in Q1 to Q3. Management said gross margins recovered in Q4 and that the worst of the pricing cycle may be behind, while remaining cautious on a full industry recovery. The call also covered the pending Dhanuka Laboratories merger, the 7ACA project, Enmetazobactam out-licensing (no definitive deal signed yet), and a planned US sterile cephalosporin fill-finish push.

segments.name: Base cephalosporin business
segments.commentary: Management is targeting 10-15% growth for FY27 and about 12% EBITDA margin for the base business. Growth is expected mainly from non-regulated markets such as Africa and South Asia.

segments.name: Enmetazobactam (Exblifep)
segments.commentary: Currently sold only in India and Europe; Europe Q1 sales were about 4x the prior quarter but not yet financially meaningful. Lifetime sales guided at $1-2 billion, with peak now expected in year 4-5 after launch.

segments.name: AMS (antimicrobial stewardship)
segments.commentary: Growing steadily and gaining hospital recognition. Currently an EBITDA drag of about INR8 crore a year.

segments.name: Dhanuka Laboratories (pending merger)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR450 crore, down from INR500 crore; EBITDA not yet available as audit is ongoing. Management estimates the merger could add 1-2% to combined EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Base business growth target of 10-15% in FY27, with about 12% EBITDA margin assumed for FY27.
7ACA project commissioning targeted for Q1 CY2027 at Chennai; first sales go internally, third-party sales after first few quarters.
Cefiderocol facility to be commissioned by end CY2026; product launch expected in Q2 or Q3 CY2027, subject to approvals.
Shionogi-linked plant commissioning in December 2026; India launch expected about six months after a clinical trial waiver, i.e. second half CY2027.
Enmetazobactam out-licensing: management hopes to sign at least one deal in the current quarter and about 50% of the identified markets within six months.
Merger with Dhanuka Laboratories: court order reserved in March; written order expected after court vacations.
capex_capacity: Cefiderocol facility: 1 million vial capacity; estimated first-few-years demand about 400,000 vials, with about one-third for India and the rest global; cost-plus agreement with guaranteed fixed PBT.
US sterile fill-finish and formulation capex about INR50 crore, mostly within the Cefiderocol project and largely filing and development expense.

7ACA: about 75% of output to be consumed in-house (25% existing consumption plus downstream intermediates); downstream capacity to be added by reengineering existing plants, with budget set aside; management guided about 5% additional EBITDA from downstream products.

US sterile FDF plan: five to six large sterile products over next few years, addressing about two-thirds of a ~$1.2 billion US cephalosporin opportunity; first ANDAs (Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Ceftaroline) to be filed via a CMO, with Orchid site as second site later.
demand_pricing: Cephalosporin pricing rose in April 2026 on war-related input cost increases (solvents and inputs); management reviews prices almost weekly and is unsure how much cost increases can be passed on.
7ACA price about $61/kg, versus about $55 a couple of quarters ago; long-term average about $60, with a range of $55-65.
Q2 and Q3 FY26 saw inventory bought at high prices sold at lower market prices, causing gross margin pressure; management said Q1 FY26 likely had the largest inventory loss but did not quantify it.
Cefiderocol price cited by analyst at about $150 per vial; management did not confirm the figure.
Enmetazobactam in Europe depends on formulary and government tender inclusion; South Europe inclusion is driving sales growth. Enmetazobactam treated about 30,000 patients in the last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has no Enmetazobactam out-licensing deal been signed despite the earlier one-per-quarter expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mridul Dhanuka said long-term agreements are taking longer than expected; term sheets are signed in some markets and definitive agreements are under negotiation in Japan, Russia, US, Latin America and Southeast Asia. Management hopes for one deal this quarter and expects about 50% of these to be signed within six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base business margin and growth outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting about 12% EBITDA margin and 10-15% sales growth in FY27, continuing a four-to-five-year trend. It noted that non-regulated market pricing will stay competitive as capacity expands.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Dhanuka merger a change in 7ACA in-house consumption (75%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mridul Dhanuka said 25% is existing consumption and the rest will be converted into downstream intermediates sold from Orchid Chennai. Only about 20-25% of 7ACA will be sold to third parties; some downstream capacity addition is needed, reengineering existing plants first.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak sales and timing for Enmetazobactam?
qa_highlights.answer: Lifetime sales are still held at $1-2 billion over the patent life. Peak sales are now expected in the fourth or fifth year after launch rather than the third.

qa_highlights.question: How will Cefiderocol capacity utilisation ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 million vials is sufficient and no near-term expansion is needed. About 400,000 vials are expected in the first few years, depending on geographies opened through GARDP licensing.

qa_highlights.question: Will US ANDAs be filed from a CMO first?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Ceftaroline will be filed through a CMO first to avoid delay from US FDA facility approval, with the Orchid site added later as an alternate manufacturing site.

risks_watch: Pending written order on the Dhanuka Laboratories merger; synergy of 1-2% EBITDA margin depends on completion.
FY26 EBITDA down about 35% YoY; sustainability of Q4 gross margin recovery and price increases amid war-related cost inflation.
Enmetazobactam out-licensing timing: no definitive agreement signed yet; deal flow repeatedly deferred.
7ACA commissioning in Q1 CY2027 described as a race against time; downstream capacity capex still unquantified.
Cefiderocol and US sterile launch timelines depend on regulatory approvals and registrations.
Chinese capacity additions and competitive pricing in non-regulated markets.

524372|2026-06.headline: Orchid Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 15% YoY to INR304 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR25 crore, on a merged Dhanuka basis.
524372|2026-06.overview: Orchid Pharma reported Q1 FY27 on a combined basis after the Dhanuka Laboratories merger (effective 10 July 2026, appointed date 1 April 2024), with FY25 and FY26 restated. Revenue from operations rose to INR304 crore from INR263 crore, and gross margin improved about 3 percentage points to 33%. EBITDA rose to INR25 crore from INR10 crore a year earlier. Management described the quarter as mediocre and said recovery would be gradual, with cephalosporin pricing still under pressure from overcapacity. Project milestones for 7-ACA (March 2027) and cefiderocol (commissioning December 2026) were reiterated.

segments.commentary: FY26 volumes and pricing fell 15-20% by product in a difficult cephalosporin year. Cefixime faces the most margin pressure, mainly in rest-of-world markets. 7-ACA pricing has been stable for about a year.

South Africa registration is done and GCC coverage is in place, but Middle East rollout is delayed by regional conflict.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR21 crore in Q1 FY27, against an earlier quarterly run-rate of INR20-25 crore. Management said it would not reach 25% of revenue in 3-4 years.

Merger synergies are expected to show initial benefits from FY28.

Jammu site chosen for low power costs, abundant water and cheap steam from agricultural waste, plus GST benefit. PLI incentive expected for 2 years, with extension to be sought after the plant starts.
demand_pricing: Management said the industry still has overcapacity and cutthroat competition in non-regulated markets.

Management expects regulated-market demand to improve over the next 2-3 quarters, with H2 seasonally stronger.
Ceftriaxone non-sterile supply from the new 7-ACA-linked capacity is planned for other Indian sterile manufacturers, which currently import from China.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover in H2 FY27 or only in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-regulated competition will persist and is hard to predict. It hopes regulated demand improves over the next two to three quarters, and called Q1 mediocre.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 7-ACA ramp-up and captive vs third-party split?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up to 80-100% by the end of year one, starting slowly. Long-term guidance is 80% in-house and 20% third-party. All output goes in-house until customer GMP approvals are obtained.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is budgeted for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant new capex beyond completing 7-ACA (INR750 crore) and cefiderocol (USD20-25 million).

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth reach about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not be prudent to give an annual growth number at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Exblifep partner pipeline and FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Advanced talks for South America, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand, Morocco and Australia. Management does not guide yearly numbers; the USD1-2 billion is lifetime potential. Management hopes for three or four more agreements by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of Chinese 7-ACA price cuts once the plant is running?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese producers have stable pricing and no cartel-like Pen G situation, so it sees little room for drastic cuts. It also acknowledged that Chinese pricing is unpredictable and that the company is working on yield and tighter concentration as its plan A.

524394|2026-03.headline: Vimta Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.6% YoY to INR1,120 million, with EBITDA margin of 37.6% and a net debt-free balance sheet.
524394|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR1,120 million, up 16.6% YoY, with EBITDA of INR421 million (37.6% margin) and PAT of INR211 million (18.9% margin). For FY26, total income reached INR4,163 million (up 19.5%), EBITDA INR1,489 million (35.8% margin) and PAT INR775 million (up 16.1%). Management said Q4 was helped by pre-clinical and seasonal food testing, but some expected growth did not materialise, and the company missed its earlier INR500 million annualised run-rate goal. The company entered biologics contract research (biologics and peptides) in FY26, with FY27 framed as a year of execution with no meaningful revenue expected yet.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook and whether 20-25% CAGR is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 20-25% CAGR a stretch but doable and the annual target. Visibility is good in pharma, food and electronics.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Indian testing market small relative to global?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said R&D is much smaller in India than in developed markets, and that low-value testing rarely justifies shipping samples overseas.

qa_highlights.question: Margins in the biologics business?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to be around the core level, a few percentage points either way; early projects are domestic and input costs are high, with better margins expected once overseas clients come on board.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the INR500 crore annualised revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: The target was originally to reach it by FY25; the company aims for Q4 run-rates in FY26 but missed due to external headwinds. Management remains hopeful but cautious.
