524394|2026-06.headline: Vimta Labs Q1 FY27 total income rose 13.7% YoY to INR1,129 million, EBITDA margin 36.4%, net debt-free balance sheet.
524394|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 total income was INR1,129 million, up 13.7% YoY but broadly flat QoQ, with EBITDA of INR411 million (up 16% YoY) and PAT of INR210 million (up 11.4% YoY). Operating margins moderated QoQ due to facility costs, new labour laws and rupee appreciation, though they improved YoY. Food testing hurt by lower import/export sample receipts from Middle East related disruption, while pharma CRO and clinical research showed recovery signs. The company secured its first Biologics order and onboarded a domestic client in Q1. Management said it was still on track for its growth momentum but acknowledged missing some business due to the Middle East situation.

524404|2026-03.headline: Marksans FY26 revenue rose 12.5% to INR2,951 crores with record PAT of INR420 crores; Q4 EBITDA margin hit 22.8%.
524404|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue grew 20.8% YoY to INR856 crores, with all three major regions growing and UK/EU posting its highest-ever quarter at INR308 crores. Q4 EBITDA rose 54% to INR195 crores, with margin up 491 bps to 22.8%, helped by mix, operating leverage and softer raw material costs in H2. Management flagged raw material inflation of 20-30% on petroleum-linked inputs for Q1 FY27, though it said inventory covers Q1 to a large extent. The company remains debt free with INR990 crores cash, a final dividend of INR0.90 per share was recommended, and FY27 guidance is 15-20% revenue growth with EBITDA margin in the 20-21% range.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin sustainable at current levels?

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan with over INR1,000 crore of cash?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise guidance upward?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin stands, given geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US strategy in light of tariff comments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not weight the tariff remarks heavily. US remains an important market, and local manufacturing is an option to keep open.

qa_highlights.question: Could ABCnow and QliniQ scale in the UK and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QliniQ is Rx-tilted, ABCnow has Rx and OTC, and Europe is about 80-85% Rx. Europe is targeted at about INR1,000 crore in five years, mostly through acquisitions.

524494|2026-03.headline: Ipca Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 20.52% from 18.24%; FY27 guided to 12-13% growth and 1-1.25pp margin expansion.
524494|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR2,388 crores (up 6% YoY per the call's stated figure) and FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR9,646 crores (up 8%). Standalone EBITDA margin was 25.27% in Q4 (vs 21.19%) and 25.18% for FY26 (vs 22.66%). Management guided FY27 consolidated growth of 12-13% and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 22-22.3%, but flagged rising input costs (solvents, packaging, APIs) and freight costs linked to the Iran-US/Strait of Hormuz disruption. Unichem margins fell to about 8% and are guided to 12-13% for FY27.

+6% vs INR2,274 crores (call figure; FY26 and Q4 comparatives appear mixed in the transcript)

segments.name: Export formulations
segments.commentary: FY26 INR2,083 crores (+9%). Promotional branded exports grew about 14% to INR664 crores; generics ex-tenders grew about 17% to INR1,149 crores.

segments.name: API

segments.name: Unichem (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin fell from about 12% to about 8% with flat turnover; Q4 other expenses rose by INR10-12 crores on tech transfers to third-party US manufacturers. Ireland facility closed; guided margin 12-13% in FY27.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and others
segments.commentary: Trophic Wellness (nutraceuticals) revenue about INR125 crores with profit about INR40 crores. Krebs Bio Nellore plant EBITDA positive; second plant has polishing issues. Onyx Scientific facing weak inquiry levels; UK formulation subsidiary lost INR2-3 million. Pisgah Labs formulation plant to be ready for commissioning around Q4 FY27, with meaningful turnover expected in FY28.

FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 22-22.3%, from 20.7% in FY26; standalone margin expansion guided at 1-1.25pp, below the earlier 1.5pp-plus norm due to material costs.

qa_highlights.question: How many launches per year are needed to grow 15-20%, and what is the Q1-Q2 FY27 pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic launches of about 18-20 products a year across 20 divisions, with 2-3 power brands per division. US generics: 6-8 launches in FY27 for Ipca; Unichem 5-6. Europe and other markets: 3-4 generic launches per market per year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the US revenue and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated US revenue was INR428 crores in Q4 (+10%) and INR1,567 crores in FY26 (+14%). Management guided FY27 Unichem US growth of about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone material cost fell about 2% against roughly 10% growth for most of FY26. Margin gains came mainly from mix: domestic, ROW, cardiac, generics and API. Unichem's margin decline partly offset gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material and price outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs have risen sharply since February. Management expects 10-12% material cost inflation if petroleum prices hold, offset by 6-7% price increases in decontrolled products. Generic pass-through is slower, with about 0.5-0.75% material cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Unichem margins and inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin guided at 12-13% for FY27, supported by closing Ireland, lower overheads and a US growth of about 10%. Inventory rose partly from a shift from air to sea freight (air fell from about 40% to 4-5%); management sees no concern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Lyka Labs, Krebs Bio and other subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Lyka is an associate; management said profitability is lower as new animal health and critical care teams mature. Trophic Wellness had about INR125 crores revenue and INR40 crores plus profit. Krebs Nellore is EBITDA positive; the second plant has polishing issues. Onyx Scientific has weak inquiry levels.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (solvents, packaging, APIs) at 10-12% if petroleum prices stay high, with partial offset from price increases.
Freight and air cargo disruption tied to the Iran-US conflict and Strait of Hormuz; freight up about 25% in Q4 and expected to affect Q1 FY27.
Unichem margin recovery to 12-13% and inventory levels, given its US share losses and higher transit inventory.
Pisgah Labs formulation plant commissioning slipping from Q4 FY27 and Onyx Scientific's weak inquiry levels.
Domestic institutional business declining on government funding constraints (FY26 down about 24%).
Lyka (associate) profitability pressure from field force expansion.

524494|2026-06.headline: Ipca Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 21% to INR2,788 crores and EBITDA margin reached 22.88%; FY27 growth guidance raised to 14-16%.
524494|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR2,788 crores, with consolidated EBITDA of INR638 crores (22.88% margin) versus INR425 crores (18.39%) a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA rose about 34% to INR557 crores. Management raised FY27 guidance: revenue growth to 14-16% (from 12-13%) and consolidated EBITDA margin to around 23% (from around 22%). Exports (+34%), domestic formulations (+13%) and institutional generics (+107%, helped by about INR40 crores of shipments slipping from March to April) drove the quarter. Management said margin gains came mainly from lower personnel and manufacturing costs as a share of sales, not material savings.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR425 crores, 18.39% in Q1 FY26 (+4.49 pp)

financial_highlights.value: about INR193 crores; zero short-term borrowings
financial_highlights.change: Dollar loans of about USD50 million fully repaid

segments.name: Unichem (subsidiary)

segments.name: Lyka Labs (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat and EBITDA reported negative. Management cited animal health, critical care and IVF as growth areas, with some divisions still below breakeven.

FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin raised to around 23% from around 22%.

Unichem guidance (10% portfolio growth, 13% EBITDA margin) not revised yet; to be reviewed after more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did acute underperform, and what is the India outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed underperformance, citing IPM growth of 4.5% vs Ipca's 8.9% acute growth. Antimalarials fell about 24%. Pain management grew about 13%, CV and diabetes about 17%, CNS about 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12-13% guidance hold, and what is the institutional outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was raised to 14-16%. Institutional growth is expected to be single digit, since the Q1 spike was largely about INR40 crores of delayed shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the US launch plans, and can growth reach 20-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3-4 Ipca launches and 7-8 combined Ipca and Unichem launches a year. Mid-teens growth (15-17%) is possible; source-change approvals are progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Will material cost pressure hit margins in the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: No margin pressure expected; material cost should fall slightly relative to sales. Q1 margin gains came mainly from personnel and manufacturing cost ratios.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation or price renegotiation affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices are rising, not being renegotiated down. FX adds to revenue and is partly offset by dollar-linked costs such as freight, testing, salaries and non-trading offices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about INR193 crores with a INR70 crore term loan at year-end, repaid next year. No short-term borrowings. Interest cost to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: Where will margins settle over 2-3 years, and what are the biotech plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years, with Ipca standalone up to about 30%. About 7 biosimilar candidates, mostly off-patent. Clinical revenue expected in FY29-30.

524558|2026-03.headline: Neuland Q4 FY26 revenue rose 134.9% YoY to INR788.7 crore and FY26 PAT reached INR363.1 crore, with management flagging lumpiness and weaker Q3.
524558|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR788.7 crore, up 134.9% YoY, led by CMS (commercial manufacturing) projects, which contributed over two-thirds of revenue. Gross margin was 62.1% and EBITDA INR319.4 crore (40.5% margin), which management said should not be read as a run-rate. FY26 revenue grew 37.1% to INR2,053.1 crore, EBITDA rose to INR603.4 crore (29.4% margin) and PAT to INR363.1 crore, but free cash flow was negative INR49.4 crore as working capital days rose to 137. Management said FX tailwinds helped and that the business remains lumpy, with Q3 FY26 muted.

524558|2026-06.headline: Neuland Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.3% YoY to INR650.1 crores, with EBITDA margin of 35.5% and PAT of INR147.4 crores.

EBITDA was INR231.1 crores (35.5% margin) and PAT rose to INR147.4 crores from INR13.7 crores a year earlier, helped by operating leverage, favourable mix and favourable exchange rates per management. Working capital days fell from 137 at end-FY26 to 84, and capex outflow was INR121.6 crores, mainly for R&D and peptide facilities. Management repeatedly stressed that quarterly performance is lumpy and declined to give FY27 numbers beyond reiterating a long-term ~20% growth aspiration.

524654|2026-03.headline: Natural Capsules posted FY26 EBITDA loss of Rs 1.56 crore (-0.83% margin) on revenue of Rs 187.20 crore; FY27 guidance targets Rs 274 crore consolidated revenue.
524654|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 55% QoQ and 30% YoY to Rs 58.45 crore, with EBITDA recovering to Rs 1.33 crore (2.28% margin), helped by about Rs 6 crore of deferred Puducherry dispatches. For FY26, revenue grew 11% to Rs 187.20 crore, but EBITDA turned negative and net loss reached Rs 24.66 crore, driven by the Puducherry shutdown and pre-commercial API subsidiary costs. Commercial API sales started at the Tumkur facility in Q4 FY26, and a contract manufacturing deal with Fermbox Bio was signed. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs 274 crore, with restoring capsule-segment profitability as the primary target, while balance-sheet and liquidity pressure remained a stated concern.

segments.name: Gelatin capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 gelatin revenue about Rs 163 crore, against a guidance of about Rs 171 crore; Puducherry shutdown cost about Rs 6 crore. Management cites a 12-13% EBITDA margin, with lines running above 93% utilisation.

segments.name: HPMC capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue only about Rs 8 crore against a Rs 25 crore target, with about Rs 3 crore from the US that stopped after July 2025. Installed capacity rose from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum with the new HPMC line; management cites about 18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: API (Natural Biogenetics / Natural Biogenex, Tumkur)
segments.commentary: Commercial API sales began in Q4 FY26, with about Rs 9 crore of API revenue in that quarter. Domestic API margins are guided at 2-3% gross and still negative at EBITDA; fixed cost is about Rs 15 crore a year. Utilisation is about 25-30%.

segments.name: Fermbox contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Contract manufacturing with revenue sharing; FY27 forecast about Rs 14 crore with about 20% EBITDA assumed. Fermbox plans about Rs 60 crore of downstream equipment on site, owned by them.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue of about Rs 274 crore: gelatin about Rs 170 crore, HPMC about Rs 20 crore, domestic API about Rs 70 crore, Fermbox about Rs 14 crore.
HPMC revenue expected only from H2 FY27, subject to US customer machine-suitability approvals; FY27 HPMC base case assumes utilisation below 50%.
Management expects a very low consolidated net margin in FY27 and said EBITDA at API level could still be negative; restoring capsule-segment profitability is the primary FY27 target.
PLI-linked minimum import price benefits excluded from guidance; prednisolone and dexamethasone commercial-scale production targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27, betamethasone for Q4 FY27 per the call.
WHO GMP certification targeted in the next quarter; CEP filing and WHO GMP inspection around Q2 FY27; USFDA around Q3/Q4 FY27. Management said USFDA timeline is about 24 months.
Total debt expected at Rs 100-110 crore in FY27 and FY28, with annual repayments of Rs 10-12 crore; possible additional borrowing of Rs 20 crore over two years.
Rs 240-250 crore API revenue target retained for FY29, needing an additional Rs 25-30 crore to complete two clean rooms.
capex_capacity: New HPMC line commissioned in FY26 takes installed capacity from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum; ready for double-zero production, with revenue expected from H2 FY27 subject to US approvals. Each HPMC line is about 750 million capsules a year, and two lines give about 1.5 billion.
Tumkur API facility: utilisation about 25-30%; management says the fixed cost burden is about Rs 15 crore a year.
Fermentation capacity freed up: about 40% spare after the enzymatic route, with Fermbox to use spare capacity under a no-compete clause.
Reaching the Rs 240-250 crore API target requires about Rs 25-30 crore to finish two clean rooms; infrastructure is already in place.
Pending HPMC approvals are machine-suitability checks: the new machine was installed in March 2026 and is in validation, with two to three months of customer stability testing.
demand_pricing: US Neutra/wellness demand is weak after the 2025 tariffs. Management expects improvement in 3-6 months, and HPMC exports to Mexico and Brazil are now the main export markets.

Steroidal API pricing in India is pressured by Chinese overcapacity. Management says Indian prices are much lower than Chinese export prices and sometimes below cost; generic-customer API margins are in the single digits.
Prednisolone and dexamethasone trial batches are about 10% above Chinese cost at kilo scale; the government's minimum import price on four products could close this gap.
Domestic API volumes are price-sensitive, and raw-material prices have risen after the Iran-US conflict hit petrochemical supply, per management.
Management said the company has about 36 days of order backlog across capsule types.

qa_highlights.question: How will management prioritise bandwidth and working capital across about five concurrent initiatives with near-zero cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Dedicated teams run each business; management said liquidity is a real pressure. Options under review include a BIRAC RDI application, preferential allotment (with promoter participation), and a rights issue, with limited promoter dilution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 HPMC revenue assumption, and what if approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case is about Rs 20 crore of HPMC revenue, against about Rs 8 crore in FY26. Management did not quantify the impact of a delay.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Natural Biogenex claw-back linked to FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the claw-back refers to FY29 figures, is already in the shareholders' agreement, and there is no current discussion on extending it.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are assumed for FY27 capsules?
qa_highlights.answer: HPMC is assumed at 18% EBITDA and gelatin at about 13%, the same as the Q4 FY26 level, with some upside from a weaker rupee.

qa_highlights.question: Was PLI income received in FY26, and what is assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI income was received in FY26, and none is included in FY27 forecasts because of timing uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the API guidance rely on Q4 run-rate, and what is the EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: API guidance is based on Q4 API revenue of about Rs 9 crore, growing gradually. Domestic API EBITDA is expected to be negative to low single-digit, and consolidated net margin very low.

qa_highlights.question: How big can the Fermbox contract become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could grow well beyond Rs 14 crore, with multiple products from Europe and the US and a better profit share; the Rs 50 crore scenario was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY26 API target missed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited yield gaps on PLI products, the failed Chinese technology support, and volatile intermediate prices; intermediate-based domestic sales started only in December 2025 and the Chinese yield consultant visa did not come through.

risks_watch: Liquidity and balance-sheet pressure: near-zero cash, a loss-making consolidated P&L, and fundraising options still open.
HPMC revenue depends on US machine-suitability and stability approvals, and US demand is still weak.
API PLI minimum import price benefit depends on commercial-scale production demonstrations expected in Q3/Q4 FY27, and betamethasone is slated for later.
Regulatory timelines (WHO GMP in Q2 FY27, USFDA in about 24 months) have slipped in the past, per analyst questions.
Steroidal API pricing and Chinese overcapacity; raw-material cost inflation from petrochemical disruptions.

capex_capacity: Fill-Finish and BSL-3 facilities capitalised during the year; Fill-Finish expands drug product capacity for domestic and export markets.
BSL-3 facility under optimisation to improve utilisation and operating cost; management said it is working to fully utilise the facility.
Received marketing and manufacturing licences for H9N2 Avian Influenza vaccine in Q4 FY26.

Nepal operations under close monitoring for operating stability.

Raw material costs rising due to global geopolitical developments and supply-chain disruptions; management may calibrate price actions.
Tender timing volatility continues to hit Animal Healthcare; non-tender business being pushed for penetration.
Africa: VITAL 2 participation; PPR eradication demand visibility strong but timing depends on country rollouts; political disturbances in parts of the region.
Tanzania: already supplying vaccines to the government; some requested vaccines may not be in pipeline; FMD not yet being discussed.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the Tanzania livestock vaccination opportunity and who are the competitors in Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: Hester Africa already supplies vaccines for Tanzania from its local plant and is in talks with government on further vaccines. FMD is not yet under discussion. Competition is three or four private animal vaccine producers, with most governments having small state-owned units and most vaccines imported.

qa_highlights.question: Are African sales invoiced in USD or local currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports to other African countries are invoiced in USD; local sales are in local currency. Management declined to give the local versus other-country split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the high Q4 poultry revenue and ~30% margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an endeavour to continue and that the level is a base to sustain, citing product mix and bottom-line focus, but could not predict external factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why were bad debt write-offs about INR 6.5 crore, and will they fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it reflects provisioning on debtors plus identification and write-off of some old unrecovered debts. Management expects the figure to reduce, though not to be alarming.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables of INR 92 crore look high versus revenue; what is being done on working capital and is the new BSL-3 facility being used?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 sales were over 33% higher than the prior quarter, and receivable days are being worked on. Management said BSL-3 optimisation is underway to align with current needs and it is working to fully utilise it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Animal Healthcare in FY27 and will subsidiaries break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged tender delays through FY26 that did not go to plan. It said Animal Healthcare picked up from Q4 and will recover from this quarter. No subsidiary breakeven timeline was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hester's share in pet vaccination?
qa_highlights.answer: None, as the company has no commercialised pet vaccines yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage come as debt falls and capacity is in place, and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant capacity is installed and utilisation will be optimised, but evolving regulatory requirements and new technologies mean future capital needs cannot be ruled out.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state revenue mix between poultry and animal healthcare and what net debt/equity level is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is around 50:50, as two years ago, and FY26 skewed toward poultry. CFO said debt is about INR 70 crore (down from INR 102 crore) and debt-to-equity of 0.19x is comfortable.

524669|2026-06.headline: Hester Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 88% and gross margin up to 78%, while consolidated revenue fell 8% on Nepal and Africa weakness.
524669|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14% YoY and EBITDA rose 95%, with gross margin improving from 69% to 78% on product mix and operational efficiencies. Consolidated revenue declined 8%, mainly on lower Nepal and Africa revenues. Consolidated profit included an exceptional gain from the Gates Foundation amendment that cut the Hester Africa soft loan from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, waived accrued interest and made the loan interest-free. Poultry grew 48% on institutional business and deeper penetration, while Animal Healthcare was held back by delayed government immunisation programmes (PPR, Lumpy Skin Disease / Goat Pox).

financial_highlights.metric: Hester Africa Gates Foundation soft loan
financial_highlights.value: Reduced from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, interest-free
financial_highlights.change: Exceptional accounting gain in consolidated profit

segments.name: Poultry Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Grew 48% YoY on higher institutional business and deeper market penetration. Management said the low pathogenic avian influenza vaccine, approved in March 2026, contributed to the jump. Management also cited early traction in poultry health products (feed supplements, disinfectants).

segments.name: Animal Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Impacted by timing of government immunisation programmes (PPR eradication, Lumpy Skin Disease Control Initiative, Goat Pox vaccine supply). Management described this as timing-related rather than a demand issue.

segments.name: International (Nepal and Africa)
segments.commentary: Revenues were low in the quarter and drove the consolidated decline. Management said strategic direction is unchanged, focused on registration, market development and commercial presence.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Emerging, not reported separately and included within animal health. Product categories are antibiotics, anti-parasites and grooming products sold under the Hester brand.

Management said the delayed government vaccine tender business is expected to come through in the next quarter.

Fixed assets rose by around Rs. 200 crore in FY26 (per analyst), with the new facilities cited as the driver. Management did not dispute the figure.
Pipeline products under development at the new facilities were not disclosed. Recombinant Brucella vaccine development is said to be progressing on timeline.
Regulatory dossiers were submitted in animal health during the quarter.

Management said the poultry distribution network is the same for vaccines and health products, with cross-selling of feed supplements and medicines under way.
Management said there was no material impact on the industry from the H5N1 culling compensation delay.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ministry's recent decision on HPAI vaccine imports for testing, and how does Hester benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Gandhi said it is premature to comment: the government still has to decide whether the vaccine will be imported or made in India.

qa_highlights.question: How does the poultry business's sharp growth compare with its historical track record? Is it cyclical or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said the division pushed sales where opportunities arose, while animal health sales slipped due to tender delays. No value or volume split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation, and can sales grow without new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said average utilisation is about 60% to 65%, but noted that this is subjective given the mix of batch sizes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the step-up in poultry revenue from about Rs. 45-48 crore to over Rs. 60 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi attributed it to better placement and more aggressive market penetration, with price increases contributing little.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash conversion weak, given that receivables are higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said operating cash flow is positive and conversion has improved. Rajiv Gandhi said higher receivables are seasonal and not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Africa operation's slow scale-up a natural gestation period or a tendering problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said it is a formative period in a new continent with economic and political strain. He declined to give directional guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa tax holiday timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said the tax-free status runs until 2030.

524715|2026-03.headline: Sun Pharma to acquire Organon at $14/share (EV $11.75B, equity $3.99B), funded by $2–2.5B cash plus bank debt; net debt/EBITDA rises to ~2.3x.
524715|2026-03.overview: Sun Pharma announced a definitive agreement to acquire Organon & Company at $14 per share, implying an equity value of $3.99 billion and an enterprise value of $11.75 billion. Management described Organon as a similar-sized company to Sun with similar profitability but no growth, and framed the deal as a growth-turnaround and innovative-platform play. Sun will move from net cash to net debt, with combined net debt/EBITDA of about 2.3x, and management said debt repayment is the priority. Closing is expected in six to nine months, subject to Organon shareholder and regulatory approvals; management said the deal is EPS accretive from day one and dividend policy is still under review.

segments.name: Organon – Innovative medicines
segments.commentary: About 33% of Organon revenue; women's health leader with #2 position in contraception and #3 in fertility. Key products cited include VTAMA (dermatology) and Emgality (migraine, Europe).

segments.name: Organon – Established brands
segments.commentary: About 55% of Organon revenue; 50+ brands with 15 brands above $100 million sales, including Zetia, Atozet, Arcoxia, Hyzaar and Cozaar. Organon's growth is about 1–2%.

segments.name: Organon – Biosimilars
segments.commentary: Portfolio of six products (including Renflexis and Hadlima), grown from about $400 million in 2021 to close to $700 million; biosimilar segment growing more than 13%.

segments.name: Sun – Innovative / branded generics
segments.commentary: Sun's innovative business is about 20% of sales. On a combined basis innovative rises to 27%, and established brands plus branded generics reach over 51%.

segments.name: Combined company
segments.commentary: Combined revenue of $12.4 billion; generics ~15% and biosimilars ~6% of combined revenue. Sales mix: US 27%, emerging markets 29%, India 17%, RoW 28%.

guidance_outlook: Synergies estimated at about $350 million, purely cost-side (procurement, people, supply chain), to be realised over two to four years.
Management said the deal is EPS accretive from day one, i.e. in the first 12 months after closing; no detailed EPS figures given.
Closing expected in six to nine months, subject to Organon shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.
Combined free cash flow of about $2–2.5 billion annually; priority is repaying acquisition debt from surplus cash flow.
Dividend payments post-deal not yet decided; management said cash flow planning has always assumed continued dividends and specifics will follow.
Management did not give organic growth targets for Organon; said the established-products business could show single-digit growth over time.
capex_capacity: Organon operates six sites across EU and emerging markets, with a manufacturing complex noted for complex product development.
Organon has about 10,000 employees, of which about 4,000 are in the field force.
Combined commercial front-end of about 24,000 people across more than 150 markets.
Management said Organon's R&D capability for long-acting products (e.g., Nexplanon, a contraceptive developed in-house) could be applied to other chronic-disease products.
Sun plans to enter 10 new markets (including China and South Korea) where it is not present today, via its own field force after closing.
demand_pricing: Organon's China sales are above $800 million across eight large brands growing at a single-digit rate; management said most of Organon's China established-brand portfolio has already undergone volume-based procurement (VBP).
Women's health global market is $35 billion, growing 6–10% CAGR; Organon has more than 100 women's health assets under development.
Management expects established brands to hold share and premium pricing despite generics, citing China examples of 20–30 generics with brands holding 20–30% share.
Biosimilar market opportunity: more than $320 billion of drugs losing exclusivity by 2035, which management sizes as a $70 billion biosimilar opportunity.
Management said the US biosimilar market has not settled, with ongoing change in approvals and interchangeability dialogue; no specific US channel claim made.
Negligible product overlap between Sun and Organon; only a small product divestment, which Organon has already done.

qa_highlights.question: How will Sun manage cultural fit and management bandwidth for the integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Shanghvi said the approach will be to learn from Organon's strengths, following the Taro and Ranbaxy playbook; an integration management office will be set up and senior management time is expected, with Organon talent seen as a strengthening of Sun's bench.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost synergy breakdown and Organon's cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayashree Satagopan said the $350 million is purely cost-side. Organon has gross debt of about $8.5 billion, cash of about $900 million and net debt interest of about 5.5%; Sun intends to work with lenders on swaps of bonds and to finance via its banks, expecting a higher credit rating than Organon.

qa_highlights.question: How will Sun grow innovative and biosimilar businesses, and what is the in-licensing roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar said in-licensing will be part of the strategy, citing women's health pipeline depth; Alok Shanghvi said the plan is to in-license pre-LOE biosimilars to use the combined commercial footprint, without specific numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a revenue synergy number, and how will Organon's established brands grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar gave no sales synergy number, citing early stage. Organon's established-brand business is expected to move from flat to single-digit growth through line extensions and bioequivalence-based products, a multi-year effort.

qa_highlights.question: Is EPS accretive, and does the deal require FTC divestments?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayashree Satagopan said the deal is EPS accretive from day one. Kirti Ganorkar said overlap is negligible and no major divestments are needed; the footnote refers to an Organon divestment already done.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Sun pursue a large acquisition now, and does it solve US commercial reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Shanghvi said the aim is to strengthen innovative capability and global reach, using a cash deal to avoid Ranbaxy-style dilution (about 15%). Alok Shanghvi said it is too early to claim a US channel breakthrough.

risks_watch: Leverage rises to ~2.3x net debt/EBITDA; repayment pace and any dividend decision are open.
Organon's flat-to-low growth; the turnaround depends on in-licensing and execution, with no quantified target yet.
Regulatory approvals and Organon shareholder vote within six to nine months; US tariff exposure for Organon was not addressed (deferred to Organon).
Nexplanon generic entry timing (around 2030 per analyst question) and commentary withheld until closing.
Undisclosed in-licensing milestone payments; management said these are in Organon's plan and valuation but gave no figure.
Amortisation post-deal not addressed; to be clarified at closing.
Organon attrition and employee cost issues were not addressed; management pointed to diligence.

524715|2026-06.headline: Sun Pharma Q1 FY27 sales rose 10.1% to INR151,836 million; EBITDA up 2.7% to INR44,177 million with 28.9% margin.
524715|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10.1% YoY to INR151,836 million, with gross margin at 80.5% on product mix. EBITDA rose 2.7% to INR44,177 million, and margin fell YoY because Q1 FY26 included Lenalidomide benefit. Reported PAT was INR28,948 million and adjusted PAT INR30,894 million, after a INR1,617 million Organon acquisition-related exceptional charge. India formulations grew 16% to INR54,749 million, while US sales fell 9.7% to USD427 million on Lenalidomide erosion and generic competition. Management held high single-digit full-year sales growth guidance and said the Organon deal is expected to close in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Global Innovative Medicines
segments.commentary: Sales USD351 million, up 12.8% YoY, 21.9% of consolidated sales; growth led by ILUMYA, ODOMZO and CEQUA across US and ex-US.

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Sales INR54,749 million, up 16%; market share 8.5% per Pharmarack MAT June 2026 (8.2% prior), ranked number 1; volume growth 5.4% vs IPM 2%. Five new products launched in Q1.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Sales USD427 million, down 9.7% YoY, driven by Lenalidomide erosion and added competition in generics; QoQ decline partly seasonal for Levulan. Five generic launches in the quarter.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Formulation revenues USD311 million, up 4.2% YoY, 19.4% of consolidated revenue; management cited geopolitics and macro conditions.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Formulation revenues USD218 million, marginally lower YoY and flat QoQ, about 13.6% of consolidated revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating costs ex-R&D rise 11% QoQ and 17% YoY, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly power and fuel for the Pen-G plant, which ramped in Q4. Costs will stay at this level, but captive 6-APA lowers raw material cost and lifts gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA loss came from new projects in FY26, and will they break even in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Biosimilar margins and price erosion assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin of 65-75% at portfolio level; US erosion capped at about 60%, Europe 75-85%. Yields of 4-6 g/L and 2,500-5,000 L bioreactors seen as the cost-competitiveness basis.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 21% FY27 EBITDA margin guidance include the rupee tailwind?

524804|2026-06.headline: Aurobindo Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 9,150 crore; operating EBITDA Rs 1,924 crore (21% margin) after a Rs 43 crore one-time charge; FY27 guidance reiterated.
524804|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to Rs 9,150 crore, with formulations at Rs 8,101 crore (89% of sales) growing 17%. Operating EBITDA was Rs 1,924 crore at a 21% margin, after a Rs 43 crore one-time loss on derecognition of leased residuals, and PAT was Rs 1,032 crore. The Lannett acquisition closed after FTC approval, and management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin above 21% and absolute EBITDA above Rs 8,000 crore. 524816|2026-06.headline: Natco Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR794.4 crores (from INR1,390.6 crores) on lower Lenalidomide, while Adcock associate profit share jumped to INR84.3 crores.
524816|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue declined sharply year-on-year to INR794.4 crores, mainly due to lower Lenalidomide sales, partly offset by double-digit growth in the base business. EBITDA including other income was INR245.7 crores (30.9% margin), improving quarter-on-quarter on international and domestic performance and lower operating costs. Consolidated PAT was INR206.5 crores versus INR269 crores in Q4 FY26, which included a one-time INR115 crore deferred tax benefit; management said normalised PAT grew 34% QoQ. Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of around INR750 crores and cautioned against annualising the flu-season-boosted Adcock contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR2,000 crore fundraise planned, given the existing cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cash is around INR1,400 crores after about INR3,000 crores of investments over the last year, mainly Adcock. Funds are needed for short-term loans, capex and two acquisition opportunities (one in India, one outside). QIP, rights issue or other options are being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PAT guidance of about INR750 crores still valid, given Adcock contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept guidance at around INR750 crores. It said the Q1 Adcock bump was seasonal, normal profit is around INR100 crores per quarter at the 100% level, and asked analysts not to annualise the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall sharply QoQ and YoY, and is this the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's Q1 had high R&D and legal costs. R&D spend is lumpy and tied to batches and trials, so this quarter is not the run-rate. Spend will be higher in future quarters, and management suggested an annual view.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India effective rate is about 25.16% under the new regime, about 27% after disallowances such as CSR. Q1 was higher because Brazil contributed more profit at above 35% tax rate.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Health reach breakeven and what is its revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects breakeven for the year and a much stronger Q2. Q1 revenue was about INR40 crores against INR138 crores in FY26; guidance was not updated beyond the existing FY27 targets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for South Africa, and can NATCO increase its stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites synergies: NATCO pipeline distribution through Adcock and Indian partner alliances, with value expected in 2-3 years. Bidvest holds 51% and is not selling; NATCO has a first right of refusal but no near-term opportunity.

526227|2026-03.headline: Filatex FY26 EBITDA rose 34.5% to INR 346.5 crore on flat volumes, but Q4 FY26 PAT fell 2.75% to INR 40.25 crore amid Middle East-driven crude volatility.
526227|2026-03.overview: Management compared Q4 FY26 against Q4 FY25 instead of Q3, arguing the sequential comparison was distorted by crude volatility. Q4 revenue was INR 985.5 crore (vs INR 1,080 crore) on 89,841 MT sales, with EBITDA up 13.86% to INR 86.26 crore while PAT fell 2.75% to INR 40.25 crore, partly due to a roughly INR 13 crore forex charge. For FY26, revenue slipped to INR 4,160 crore and volumes were flat, but EBITDA rose 34.5% and PAT rose 36.7%. Management said March was roughly EBITDA-neutral on a current-price basis and that Q1 FY27 utilisation could be 20-25% below the 1 lakh tonne quarterly run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 FY27 production be sub-optimal given continued volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said output will be 20-25% below the 1 lakh tonne quarterly level at minimum, with further visibility limited given daily changes.

qa_highlights.question: How will forex losses (about INR 13 crore in Q4) be mitigated as PTA self-sufficiency grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will hedge more; full hedging cost is about 3.5-4% per dollar on INR 500-550 crore exposure, i.e. INR 17.5-20 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure of the INR 690 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 335 crore is debt and the rest is internal accruals; FY27 year-end debt estimated at INR 350-360 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What ROE is the company targeting?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE reached about 12.96% vs 10.62% earlier, with a further 100-200 bps targeted this year if conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the steam and recycling projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Steam project delayed to mid-July due to a turbine delivery issue; recycling plant on track for end-September with no delay seen. Recycled chip to be sold, with yarn conversion mainly for existing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: Will PTA capacity additions create cost savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there will be negligible savings initially since imports are priced at landed cost; savings expected only once IOC and GAIL capacity creates surplus.

Chinese imports and labour migration disruptions; management expects the EU FTA to take effect around end CY2026 and remains uncertain on timing.

526247|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores with net profit up 78%, but FY26 revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores; FY27 guided at INR600-700 crores.
526247|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores, with EBIT up 35% to INR9.6 crores (10.8% margin) and PAT up 78% to INR6.6 crores. For full FY26, revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores as FY25's high-value chaffs and flares emergency orders were not repeated, while EBIT rose 42% to INR69.3 crores (17.8% margin) and PAT rose 61% to INR45.8 crores, helped by one-off other income. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin to 15-20%, with the order book at a record INR1,569 crores. Execution remains the central concern: raw material shortages (MIL, DRDO alternate materials), the Katepally plant accident, and pending free-issue material from BDL and DRDO all delayed deliveries.

Katepally: the RDX and HMX expansion is ongoing and not complete. A large planetary mixer and balancing equipment are in progress, and some items are expected to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27.

Katepally rocket motor facility (large motors for ISRO and DRDO strategic systems) was hit by an accident. Equipment is in fabrication and the building is under construction, with commissioning targeted for September 2026.
Peddakandukur flares plant: rebuilt after an accident about 1.5 years ago, recommissioned, and now producing in-house. Import dependence for flare components has reduced.

Odisha: the first land parcel was rejected and the state government is proposing new parcels. Management is in a video conference with Odisha officials. The three-phase plan has its second and third phases 4-5 years out.

Output is about 50 motors per month across LRSAM, MRSAM and Astra (per management's answer on domestic deliveries). About 40 motors were delivered to domestic customers in the current status described.
demand_pricing: Exports are about 54% of the order book and domestic about 46%. Management said export licences are held for most export orders, and that the INR400 crores of export orders still pending are development orders where invoicing follows milestones.
Newly won INR350.23 crore export order (April 2026) for defence products. Management expects an export licence decision in about 3 months.

A INR18.9 crore order received in February 2026 was cancelled in April because an export licence was not granted. Management said licence rejection risk depends on government policy and the destination country.
Domestic BDL and DRDO orders depend on free-issue materials (FIMs) from those agencies; management said these cannot be executed without them.

Management said alternate raw materials for land mines, loitering munitions and medium-calibre ammunition are in DRDO trials. MIL, the high-explosive supplier, could not meet requirements. Management expects approval within 1-2 months.

Pipeline: QRSAM is not included in the estimates. Some chaffs and flares orders are at negotiation stage and some RFPs are pending. Management expects the order book to stay at about INR1,000 crores-plus after current execution.
Other income: management said the Q4 and FY26 increase came from supplier discounts on delayed deliveries, paid in two parts, and that it is non-recurring.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and margin is targeted for FY27 given fewer emergency orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue target INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin 15-20%. Drivers are land mines, drone and loitering munition payloads, and medium-calibre ammunition, where alternate raw materials have been accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR500 crore guidance from February missed (about INR390 crores delivered)?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material shortages: MIL could not supply inputs for mines, loitering munitions and flares. Alternate materials are in DRDO trials, with production expected once approved in 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Katepally capex on track, and when does it finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Some items to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27. Full completion may slip to Q3 FY27 because plant and product qualification takes another 1-2 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export/domestic split of the order book, and how much export licence risk exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 54% and domestic about 46%. Management said licence approval depends on government policy and the country; the INR18.9 crore cancelled order shows the risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pending order book is stuck, and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic orders depend on free-issue materials from BDL and DRDO; about 40 motors delivered recently. Development-stage export orders are being executed against milestones.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the INR430 crore October 2025 order will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution has just started. About two-thirds is expected by end-FY27, with one-third in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Jagdalpur O&M contract lost, and is ISRO renewal possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagdalpur was lost in bidding because costs had risen. ISRO contract has about 2.5 years left, and renewal will be bid when the RFP is issued.

qa_highlights.question: Are there chances of similar accidents, and what mitigations are in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to automation, remote operations and safety control equipment in new plants. The Katepally rocket motor facility is due for commissioning in September 2026.

The ISRO contract (about INR18 crores per year) has about 2.5 years left, and the Jagdalpur O&M contract was lost in bidding.

526263|2026-03.headline: Mold-Tek Q4 FY26 PAT turned to INR 2.28 crore from a loss, but FY26 PAT fell 17% to INR 10 crore on a INR 4 crore FX MTM hit.
526263|2026-03.overview: Management reported a Q4 FY26 profit of INR 2.28 crore versus a loss of about INR 1.6 crore a year earlier, despite a roughly INR 4 crore MTM loss from rupee depreciation on forward contracts. Full-year PAT was about INR 10 crore against INR 12.16 crore in FY25, with management citing EBITDA of about INR 20 crore standalone (INR 19.64 crore consolidated) against INR 23 crore a year earlier. Beryl, acquired in November 2025, contributed five months of revenue, and the MES automobile (BIW) team was cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March. Management reiterated plans to move into structural design and targets of INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin for FY27. Analyst questions were pointed on EBITDA definition, the cancelled preferential issue, receivables and hedging, and several figures were disputed or left for follow-up with the CFO.

segments.name: Civil / Structural (steel detailing and design, India-based, US clients)
segments.commentary: Work on hand grew from about $4 million at start of FY26 to about $5 million at end-March 2026, which management described as growth of about 60-70% versus $2.84 million in June 2024. Structural design is about 10% of civil revenue, versus nearly 0% three to four years ago. Management targets 30-40% of revenue from design in three to four years.

segments.name: MES (Mechanical Engineering Services) - BIW automobile
segments.commentary: Team cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March; the team was closed from April 1. The segment lost about INR 7-8 crore a year and about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 FY26. Work on hand fell from about $0.5 million in Q1 to about $0.25 million.

segments.name: MES - Poles, towers and substation (US)
segments.commentary: Team grew from 45-50 to about 80 people. FY26 revenue was about $0.8 million; management expects FY27 to cross $1.5-2 million. Around 80-90% of this work comes from the USA.

segments.name: Beryl (US residential structural design, inspection and permitting; acquired Nov 2025)
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 80% permitting/inspection and 20% design. Team of about 40 in Tampa with no resignations in five months. Management guided Beryl margin at 8-10% for FY27 and said it can grow to about $5-7 million with India design support.

segments.name: PEMB (Pre-Engineering Metal Buildings)
segments.commentary: Now about 5% of revenue, down from being the core business before 2010.

segments.name: New MSA with Danieli Corus (Delhi, MES manpower)
segments.commentary: Mandate for 20 people; 3 fulfilled so far. Contract period 1-3 years, potential about $0.5 million per annum within a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 250 crore, with management saying INR 240 crore is 'easily feasible' from the Q4 run-rate of INR 59 crore (times four).
EBITDA margin to move from about 11% to at least 15%.
Standalone engineering business (MES plus civil from India) expected to grow at least 15-20%, with EBITDA margin in the 15-16% region.
MES cost cut expected to add about INR 7-8 crore back to profitability; productivity target improvement of at least 20% in FY27 (10-15% gain claimed in April).
Nashik office move expected to save about INR 2-2.5 crore per year from FY28; building targeted to be ready by end of FY27.
Hedging policy to be limited to 25-50% of turnover (previously up to 100%); operational EBITDA to be reported separately from MTM gains and losses from FY27.
Salary hike of 8.5-9% provided in Q4 for Indian teams; Beryl not yet covered.
capex_capacity: Team of 40-45 structural designers in India plus 2-3 in the USA; a 6-member Indian team was created for Beryl, with a plan for a 15-20 person India team, targeted by Q4 FY27.
Nashik owned building site acquired a couple of years ago; municipal approvals expected by end of May, ground work in June, completion by end FY27.
Management is in talks for an acquisition of a high-rise steel structural design company; one target is near the Atlanta office. No deal concluded.
Two PEs (professional engineers) certified in more than 20 US states; PE support needed for full member design.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand up to about $5 million at end-March 2026, against about $4 million at start of the year (per Q4 opening remarks); Q&A figure of $2.5 million at start of year.

Trade uncertainty between the US and India has stalled Interarch and Mold-Tek building orders in the US; no revenue progress from Interarch or Affordable Robotic Partnership.
BIW automobile demand fell as EV adoption and new model launches slowed; European work was over 50% of MES, while poles and towers are 80-90% US.
Beryl order book estimated at $0.2-0.3 million at any time, maximum about $0.5 million (per management; to be checked).

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 240 crore is easily feasible from Q4 revenue of INR 59 crore annualised, and that margin should rise from 11% to at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 2.9 lakh preferential issue at INR 164 cancelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the investor did not transfer funds because the share price had fallen to about INR 130, so the issue lapsed on 30 April against a 31 May deadline. The issue was independent of the Beryl stake purchase. About 30% of acquisition money is held as a three-year retention guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation hit P&L when costs are mainly wages, and what is the hedging policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Forwards booked at INR 85-92 led to about INR 4.9 crore MTM loss in Q4 as rupee moved to about INR 95. Management is cutting hedge cover to 25-50% of turnover and will show MTM separately from operational EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables doubled and revenue rose only about 40%; is the standalone business weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 turnover rose 81% YoY, that the rise in debtors reflects this growth, and that acquisitions are strategic rather than a response to weakness. It cited zero debt and INR 25-30 crore of deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MES loss and when does it end?
qa_highlights.answer: The MES loss was about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 and about INR 7-8 crore a year; management said the team was closed from 1 April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What were Beryl's revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl did INR 22.9 crore in the five months since acquisition, including INR 11 crore in Q4 with a loss of about INR 70 lakh. Management said Beryl's seasonal Q4 is typically weak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Danieli Corus MSA and its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: A manpower MSA in MES with a mandate for 20 people (3 deployed so far), a contract period of 1-3 years, and potential of about $0.5 million per year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 Florida SB 4-D inspection tailwind at Beryl ending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first inspection phase is complete and payments received; the second design phase was delayed by a government shutdown and is now restarting, so the tailwind is mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the threat from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI has a limited role in design and detailing, may cut headcount by 5-10% through checking tasks, and that back charges are zero.

526299|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was $463 Mn, up 2.5% QoQ and 7.1% YoY in constant currency, with full-year constant-currency growth of 6.7%. Direct revenue was $456 Mn (98.6% of total), growing 9.2% YoY in constant currency. EBIT margin rose 20 bps QoQ to 15.4% in Q4 and was stable at 15.3% for the year, within the 14.75%-15.75% band. Operating cash flow was $21 Mn, or about $38 Mn excluding roughly $17 Mn of delayed customer remittances collected in early April. Management guided FY27 to high single-digit to low double-digit growth and an approximately 80% OCF-to-net-income conversion.

qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no major cuts in pure tech budgets and urgency to act, with spend shifting to AI programs with clear ROI; business-funded programs are framed as revenue plays, not cost plays.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about DSO and OCF conversion, including the $16 Mn that slipped from FY25 into FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: DSO improved by one day; excluding the ~$17 Mn delayed remittance it would be about 86 days, or about 4-5 days better on that basis. OCF/net income is expected at about 80% on a consistent basis; the $16 Mn is roughly 7-8% of PAT.

526299|2026-06.headline: Mphasis Q1 FY27 revenue $471M, up 8.3% YoY constant currency; net new TCV $461M; FY27 guidance maintained at high-single to low-double-digit growth.
526299|2026-06.overview: Mphasis reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $471M, up 2.1% QoQ and 8.3% YoY in constant currency, with Direct revenue at $465M. Net new TCV was $461M, the fifth straight quarter above $400M, and three large deals were closed including one above $100M. EBIT margin fell 60 bps QoQ, absorbing ramp-up costs for new deals and TAP acquisition costs, and EPS declined 4% QoQ to INR 25.6. Management maintained FY27 guidance of high-single to low-double-digit constant currency growth and a 14.75%-15.75% EBIT margin band, and guided Q2 to its best sequential constant currency growth in three years.

qa_highlights.question: How much does the Red Oak consolidation add to FY27 growth, and is organic growth on track?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Red Oak is baked into the outlook but consummation is pending, with work expected to start around end-August. Payout is typically 1x-1.2x revenue, so the impact is within the existing guidance range and not separately quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline and how does the margin path look?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said TAP acquisition earn-out cost hit margin by about 0.35%, with two-thirds of potential consideration in earn-out flowing through the P&L. A steep utilization drop, made in anticipation of growth, is expected to reverse over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF soften and when does it normalize?

qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects hedge losses to trend down if the rupee stays near current levels, but the margin benefit will take a couple of quarters to show and will not fully disappear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of customer-contract acquisition deals?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said most upfront costs are expensed, and deals are assessed to be profitable in line with company average after that, with the first three months possibly lower or higher. Management said it does not buy low-margin businesses.

FY26 revenue was INR539 crore and PAT INR316 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR1.5 per share (15%). Million Minds Phase 1 was inaugurated on May 17, 2026, with about 60-65% of leasable area leased or in final stages as LOIs, and Malabar Retreat is about 79% complete. FY27 guidance on revenue and EBITDA was deferred to the Q1 FY27 results.

526371|2026-03.headline: NMDC guides FY27 production to 60 million tonnes and FY27 capex to about INR6,000 crore, with Q1 FY27 output up about 15% YoY.
526371|2026-03.overview: NMDC reported FY26 production above 50 million tonnes and an 11% PAT rise despite sluggish prices, with management citing a record capex of about INR3,300 crore. Management guided FY27 production to 60 million tonnes, with the first two months of Q1 FY27 about 15% higher YoY at roughly 10 million tonnes. New iron ore (Deposit 4, Deposit 13) and coal (Tokisud, Rohne) assets are being commissioned, and a INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag is sanctioned. The EBITDA margin was 33% group-level, down from 42%, due to a one-time HR coil trading arrangement with NMDC Steel; standalone iron ore EBITDA was stated at 42%.

segments.name: Iron ore (NMDC standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin at 42%, with FY27 guided at 42-43%. Kirandul FY26 about 21 million tonnes (to ~30 million by decade-end); Bacheli about 18-19 million tonnes (to ~35 million).

segments.name: NMDC Steel (NSL)
segments.commentary: NSL has turned profitable; the HR coil trading in the last quarter was a one-time cash-flow support and is not expected in Q1 FY27. NSL dues are being recovered at about INR100 crore per month, with full liquidation in 16-18 months (pre-demerger dues about INR2,500 crore, now about INR1,800 crore).

segments.name: Coal
segments.commentary: Tokisud (2.3 million tonnes peak, thermal, opened) targets 0.75-1 million tonnes in FY27 from Q2; Rohne (8 million tonnes peak coking coal) opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 production. Management expects INR500-600 crore revenue per 1 million tonnes at G10 grade, at 30-40% EBITDA (approximate).

segments.name: Pellets (KIOCL)
segments.commentary: KIOCL 3 million tonne job-work plant: FY26 about 2.4 million tonnes; FY27 target 3-3.3 million tonnes. Pellet grade achieved 66.5% Fe; targeting 67% DR-grade with a $20-30/t premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 60 million tonnes including NSL, built from Deposit 14 (+1 mt), NMZ (+1 mt), Kumaraswamy (+~3.3 mt), Deposit 5 (+2 mt to 12 mt), plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt).
Deposit 4 expected to start commercial mining in Q2 FY27: about 1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, and 7 mt peak rated capacity after 1.5-2 more years.
Deposit 13 start targeted around Q2 FY27 after pending clearances: under 0.5 mt in FY27, about 2 mt next year, 10 mt initial peak rising to 20-21 mt in 4-5 years.
Capex guidance: about INR6,000 crore in FY27 (range INR6,000-7,000 crore); INR7,000-10,000 crore per year over the next 2-3 years; INR40,000-50,000 crore over 3 years to reach 100 mt.
Overseas critical mineral and mineral asset acquisitions: INR2,000-3,000 crore expected in FY27; a couple of overseas assets targeted this year.
Management reiterated a 100 million tonne target by end of decade and said the 60 mt FY27 guidance is achievable without the railway doubling, but 100 mt requires it.
No immediate plans to leverage the balance sheet; internal accruals expected to fund capex and acquisitions, with debt possible late FY27 only for large global acquisitions.
Iron ore prices expected to stay range-bound in FY27; monthly price calls to be taken.
capex_capacity: Railway: 131 km doubling; two sections remaining, one by end of June 2026 and the Bhansi-Bacheli section by December 2026; evacuation capacity to rise from 28-30 mt to ~40 mt, with 60 mt+ after doubling beyond Jagdalpur.
Slurry pipeline (15 mt, Bacheli to Nagarnar), Nagarnar pellet plant and Bacheli grinding mill in pre-commissioning; commissioning expected by end-June or mid-July 2026.
EC capacity 64.8 mt vs CTO ~55.4 mt; CTO enhancement sought in three places to ~58.8 mt. All mines reached EC capacity as of 1 April 2026 (Deposit 5 the exception in FY26).
Deposit 5 downhill conveyor and bottleneck fix due June-July 2026, enabling 12 mt. New infrastructure at Deposit 14, NMZ, 11 and 11C takes about 1.5 years, adding 5-6 mt.
INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag (board sanctioned, ~2-2.5 year build); Vizag land parcel ~1,100 acres; pellet plant at Vizag on drawing board, pending slurry pipeline route decision.
Expansion works (~INR15,000-20,000 crore worth of major tenders) expected to be awarded by end-June or July 2026.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is not a constraint even at 100 mt, citing JSW, AMNS (10 mt plant near Vizag, 17 mt total), JSPL and NSL expansions; NMDC's phosphorus content of 0.05% is a claimed differentiator.

Iron ore prices expected range-bound in Q1 FY27 after steel prices peaked Dec-Feb and stabilised in March-April; the company sets prices monthly, citing international prices, competitor prices and logistics, not a direct steel-price link.
RINL consumes 7-8 mt per year; bills discounted at ~10% premium with a 45-day payment lag; no recourse to NMDC in FY25 or FY26.
Blended/branded iron ore (Vizag) planned as a premium product; exports unattractive given 30% export duty, so pellets are preferred for export.
Iron ore realisation slightly down ~2% per an analyst question; no quantified FY27 realisation guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Mine-wise bridge to 60 mt FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 14 +1 mt, NMZ +1 mt, Kumaraswamy +~3.3 mt (MPAP relief from 8.6 mt), Deposit 5 +2 mt (to 12 mt), totalling ~5.3 mt; plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt) gives ~60 mt including NSL.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mine economics and grade?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial volume mostly via auction at prices above CIL FSA; 1 mt is estimated at INR500-600 crore revenue with 30-40% EBITDA. Grade is G10; figures described as very preliminary.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery of NSL and RINL receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: NSL dues cut from ~INR2,500 crore to ~INR1,800 crore; recovery at ~INR100 crore per month, 16-18 months for NSL, about a year and a half to two for the rest. RINL is 100% government-owned, with timing slower but no risk assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and critical minerals spending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR6,000 crore (range 6,000-7,000), then INR7,000-10,000 crore per year. Overseas acquisitions INR2,000-3,000 crore in FY27; domestic rare earth via GMDC MoU in Gujarat, no firm profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Can 60 mt be reached without railway doubling?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 60 mt is achievable without it, but 100 mt is not possible without the doubling completing (Vizag/Bhansi-Bacheli section due December 2026).

qa_highlights.question: Deposit 4, Deposit 13 and Rohne ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 4 ~1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, 7 mt peak; Deposit 13 under 0.5 mt FY27, 2 mt next year, 10 mt initially rising to 20-21 mt; Rohne opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 output and 8 mt peak coking coal.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA guidance and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore EBITDA margin to be maintained at 42-43% for FY27; no specific per-tonne realisation or EBITDA-per-tonne figures were given.

526381|2026-03.headline: FY26 PBT crossed INR10 crore at INR10.30 crore (up ~34%), with PAT of INR9.58 crore and a 30% payout dividend of INR0.40 per share.
526381|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 total income from operations up 11.68% YoY to INR96.74 crore, with PBT up nearly 99% to INR3.70 crore and PAT up over 60% to INR2.98 crore. For FY26, total income from operations was INR357.25 crore, PBT INR10.30 crore (up over 34%) and PAT INR9.58 crore (up over 26%). The air freight segment profit rose to INR11.26 crore from INR8.53 crore, and finance cost fell by INR35 lakh to a lower level from INR1.18 crore. A new subsidiary, Rajpat Logistics Limited, was formed in the December 2025 quarter as an additional trucking-booking vertical.

financial_highlights.change: from INR1.18 crore in previous year

segments.name: Air freight logistics
segments.commentary: Segment profit rose to INR11.26 crore in FY26 from INR8.53 crore in FY25. The company says it operates from around 100 airports with more than 60 airlines, and serves pharma, auto parts, engineering, electronics, FMCG and documents.

segments.name: Rajpat Logistics Limited (new subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Formed in the December 2025 quarter; management says it is at a nascent stage. It will book trucking for top corporates on an asset-light basis, and management expects it to add about 25% to the INR400 crore revenue base and to earn ROCE above 15%.

Management is pursuing redevelopment of a non-core property with two adjacent property owners; a meeting was planned for the following week. No timeline or value was given.

demand_pricing: Management said industry rates are hardening, with international air rates up about 15% since March 2026, amid supply constraints linked to the geopolitical situation and higher crude and ATF prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add warehousing capacity?

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the mobile app and AI initiatives on revenue leakage?

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected value and structure of the non-core property redevelopment?

526423|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose to INR 18 crore (margin 12.91% vs 0.15%) on revenue of INR 142 crore, while FY26 volume fell 13% to 58,630 MT.
526423|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 recovered sharply from a weak prior year: revenue grew 3% YoY to INR 142 crore and EBITDA reached INR 18 crore versus INR 20 lakh a year earlier, with net profit of about INR 4 crore against a loss of INR 4 crore. For the full year, revenue fell 19% to INR 587 crore and volume fell 13%, attributed to heavy rains in operating areas, but EBITDA rose 23% to INR 35 crore and net profit was INR 1 crore versus a loss of INR 4 crore. Management linked Q4 inventory gains to PVC price volatility from the Middle East conflict, and said capex is on hold for two quarters. Several answers deferred to the CFO, reducing detail on freight, dealers and utilisation.

segments.name: Building products
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 2,683 MT (+7% YoY); FY26 volume 7,685 MT (-16%). Margins stated at 14-18%, higher than agriculture; management targets substantial growth in FY27 and CPVC expansion.

Building products are to be the main FY27 growth driver, with CPVC expansion; OPVC is not on the agenda.
Capex is on hold; the next decision on capex or a second plant will follow after the first two quarters of FY27.

demand_pricing: Demand for agri and building products was hit when the Middle East war pushed raw material and finished goods prices up sharply; management says demand is now back to near normal.
Management says PVC prices are volatile after the Iran-Iraq conflict; Q4 included inventory gains, and the company stocked up in March ahead of the April-June agri season.
The government withdrew import duty on PVC and other polymers until about 1 July; management said there is no anti-dumping duty.
Competition is aggressive with many national players present in MP; branded players are gaining share from unorganised ones.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses mainly comprise freight; the CFO would provide the breakdown offline. No figures were given on the call.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said building products revenue fell in FY26 due to rationalisation and will see a quantum jump in FY27, but gave no figure for the segment's FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are mostly from institutional customers, which the company cut in Q4 as planned.

526612|2026-03.headline: Blue Dart Q4 FY26 PAT fell to INR 43 crore on revenue of INR 1,533 crore; comparable PBT before exceptional items down about 17% YoY.
526612|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 6,141 crore versus INR 5,720 crore in FY25, with full-year PAT of INR 240 crore. Management said FY26 revenue and PBT before the Labour Code exceptional item each grew about 7%. Q4 revenue grew about 8%, but comparable PBT before exceptional items fell about 17%, with no exceptional item in the quarter. Management attributed the margin pressure to a mix shift toward heavier, lower-margin ground shipments, higher local vehicle hiring costs in March, and employee cost investments in sales and quality functions.

segments.commentary: About 60% of FY26 revenue by value; management said air is a transit-time product, not a mode, with about one-third of air load on commercial airlines and two-thirds on own aircraft. E-commerce air growth was described as steady with limited growth.

segments.name: Ground / surface
segments.commentary: About 40% of FY26 revenue by value and the stated growth engine; FY26 surface rate growth was 6.9% per management, and its share has risen from about 30-32% a few quarters ago.

Ground facility ramp-up (Gurugram) and fixed-cost absorption; management said ground is largely variable-cost.

526612|2026-06.headline: Blue Dart Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR1,658 crore (from INR1,442 crore) and PAT reached INR87 crore, driven mainly by yield and fuel surcharge rather than volume.
526612|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,658 crore against INR1,442 crore a year earlier, with PAT of INR87 crore. Management attributed growth mainly to pricing: GPI-led increases, targeted repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery after diesel and Brent prices rose from around March–May. Tonnage grew about 7% to 364,430 tons and shipments about 2% to 96.15 million, with air volume up about 2.6% and surface up about 9%. Management declined to quantify yield growth or give forward volume and margin guidance, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue but about 25% of kilos (1:3 air:surface by weight). Volume growth about 2.6%; growth is mainly yield-led. Freighter pallet utilisation 85–90%.

segments.name: Surface / Ground
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue and about 75% of kilos. Volume up about 9%; B2B revenue up about 14%. Management says surface is the faster-growing segment and is approaching air in size.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Revenue up more than 10% YoY. Management says about 50-plus million of the 96.15 million shipments are e-commerce, and Blue Dart holds about 12–13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 70% B2B and 30% B2C (plus or minus 2%).

segments.name: BFSI (documents and cards)
segments.commentary: BFSI alone is about 10–15% of total revenue; documents plus cards together, including small parcels, about 25–30%. Management says BFSI is no longer a growing segment.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not forecast volumes, citing seasonality, but expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward.
Typical GPI realisation is about 4–5%, with extra customer-specific corrections on top.

Standalone annualised capex guided at INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Aviation capex is driven by maintenance and engine cycles, with roughly 20–25% of depreciation as ongoing capex.
H2 is expected to bring higher volumes, but resourcing flex will determine margins; management aims for stable, consistent margin improvement.
No major expansion plans; growth is expected to be organic. Possible consolidation and expansion of southern hubs (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai, a few quarters away.
capex_capacity: Two major hubs added in North and a couple of medium-sized hubs in East in the prior period.
Freighter pallet utilisation at 85–90%; aircraft flown mainly at night and scheduled against available load.
Belly cargo is 30–40% of overall load in a typical month, and can reach 70–80% on lower-volume weekends. Blue Dart flies to 8 stations and carries belly cargo at 25–50 other locations.
The two aircraft acquired earlier are back to pre-acquisition pallet utilisation (as of 2024) and are integrated into the network.
demand_pricing: Growth came mainly from pricing: GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through. Management said yield was 'directionally' the main driver of revenue growth.
Fuel surcharge on surface is revised monthly based on local diesel prices, which rose in mid-May after about 5–6 years. Air fuel surcharge rose from April as Brent climbed from around mid-March.
Auto is a niche express vertical; management estimates it grows at about high-teens, in line with surface B2B. Market share is hard to quantify.
Management says e-commerce pricing remains competitive, with capacity still available in the market; Blue Dart positions itself as a premium player.
Management says it gained a very small but roughly stable market share in SME clients versus last year (informal assessment).

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue growth mainly from pricing, given volume growth was only about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed directionally. Pricing came from GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery (fuel surcharge offset fuel cost rises, which also lifted yield).

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-commerce growth lower than the industry, and is it a focus area?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce is a growth driver but not a mass-volume focus. It is prioritising premium, time-critical traffic that fits its capacity, and it is not targeting the largest e-commerce share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and new hubs?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone annualised capex is INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Two major northern hubs and some medium eastern hubs were added, and southern and Mumbai hub consolidation is being considered a few quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 brings volume opportunity but also resourcing challenges. It aims to keep or improve margins through efficiency and better realisation, without quantifying either.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 recently acquired aircraft stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said pallet utilisation was restored to pre-acquisition levels by 2024. The aircraft are part of the wider network, and capacity is not a constraint; yield is the main lever.
