Fuel: diesel and Brent rises were passed through with a lag; Q2 is expected to show the full surcharge effect, but any fall in fuel prices would reverse it.
Air volume growth of about 2.6% versus surface about 9% suggests air is stagnating in volume.
H2 resourcing: management flagged that peak-season flex will decide margins.
Competition in e-commerce pricing remains intense, with spare capacity in the market.
BFSI (documents and cards) is no longer growing, and the 25–30% documents-plus-parcels exposure needs monitoring.
Management declined to provide e-commerce split by air and surface, D2C share, or yield premium figures, limiting visibility.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand-level metrics fell because of new hotels with a wider base; Jadhavgadh had a mid-year slump, and a strategy change is under way. Management said the current EBITDA already reflects this, with gains expected next year as hotels mature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IRA Mumbai contribution, and how will it be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IRA Mumbai contributed about INR 50 crore revenue and about INR 20 crore EBITDA, and that the exit is roughly EBITDA-positive by INR 1-2 crore. Replacement will come from maturing hotels, new openings and tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 4% EBITDA compression, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wage code revisions add about INR 4 crore, which is permanent. About INR 2 crore is a one-time IRA closure payout, and newer hotels' payroll costs should be absorbed as they mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why are finance costs around INR 10 crore while borrowings fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not answer on the call and promised a follow-up. Other income of about INR 10 crore includes rent, interest from group companies, a INR 5 crore Ilex loan repayment and about INR 3 crore tax refund; a breakdown was promised.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 top line grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, but acknowledged the INR 50 crore IRA loss would reduce top line unless offset by other properties.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA drag from new properties and how many keys were added?
qa_highlights.answer: About 250-260 keys were added in FY26. The EBITDA drag is about INR 10 crore, of which about INR 6 crore should be absorbed into the gross operating profit (GOP) in the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold INR 40 crore of cash rather than prepay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers to hold cash as a contingency buffer rather than prepay the INR 86 crore loan at 9.75%, given the risk of shocks.

qa_highlights.question: Are the properties due to open this quarter on schedule, or have LPG, construction or supply shortages delayed them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no supply-chain impact from the war; Dwarka is due November-December, Gwalior around October-November, and Dehradun may slip about six months due to owner challenges.

qa_highlights.question: What occupancy trajectory is expected for Q2 and Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the Q1 occupancy growth trend to continue for the remaining three quarters, with business hotels typically above 75-80% and leisure properties seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a strategic pivot under the new CFO, and will the company move towards owned hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating various growth options and will combine asset-light leases or revenue share with owned hotels (brownfield or land parcels); debt capacity up to INR 300 crore at three times forward EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Are any hotels opened before FY26 loss-making, and what is the plan for loss-makers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hotels opened in FY24-FY25 are all profitable after lease charges; new hotels usually show losses in year one due to opening costs and take two to three years to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take price hikes given flat Orchid ARR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RevPAR is the key metric and that rates and occupancy are managed case by case depending on micro-market demand and competition.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA margin improvement, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the margin improvement long-term, with a 30% target in two to three years through revenue growth and cost control, including renewable energy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline and expected room additions in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 400 keys over the next 12-15 months across Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi, with possible delays.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for FY27 and FY28, and what was spent in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Most properties are leased, so capex is minimal; Mumbai and Pune renovation plans are being finalised, with guidance expected next quarter, and only normal repair and maintenance capex is planned for the next two years.

526797|2026-03.headline: Greenply Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit record INR776.2 crore (+19.6% YoY) with core EBITDA margin of 12%, up 150 bps YoY.
526797|2026-03.overview: Greenply reported its highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue of INR776.2 crore in Q4 FY26, with core EBITDA of INR93.2 crore at a 12% margin. MDF delivered its record quarter at INR189.4 crore revenue and 17% margin, while plywood volume grew 15.6% YoY. Management flagged a CEO/JMD resignation, a tax search operation, and a INR15.16 crore exceptional impairment linked to the Dubai entity, and guided to a 0.7-0.72 peak debt-to-equity during the MDF capex cycle. Part of Q4 volume growth was attributed to channel stocking in the second half of March, and chemical costs rose sharply, prompting price increases from April.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR588.5 crore, volume +15.6% and value +14.6% YoY, core EBITDA margin 10.4% (+120 bps YoY). FY26 revenue INR2,105.7 crore (+7.5%), volume +8.3%, margin 8.8%. Price hikes of 4-5% effective April 2026; management attributes gross margin dip to product mix.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 record revenue INR189.4 crore on 62,000 CBM (+45.3% volume YoY), margin 17%. FY26 revenue INR635.6 crore (+19.9%), margin 13.4%. Price increases of 5% and 10% effective April 2026 (15% total per analyst confirmation); FY27 volume guidance 25-30%.

segments.name: Furniture & fittings JV
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales INR12.99 crore; FY26 revenue INR44.27 crore with PAT loss INR50.8 crore (Greenply share INR25.4 crore). Management expects breakeven around the middle of next year.

guidance_outlook: Plywood volume growth target of 10% for the rest of FY27, with margins held at recent levels contingent on volume delivery.
MDF volume growth of 25-30% in FY27, using near-full capacity; EBITDA margins to be kept consistent with recent performance (Q4 FY26 MDF margin 17% described as sustainable).
Management expects the March 2026 quarter consolidated margin to be the new norm, with H2 FY27 plywood margin upside from new process technology.
Peak debt-to-equity expected at 0.7-0.72 during FY27 or the year after, reverting to 0.5-0.6 the following year.
Effective tax rate around 22% (standalone 22%, subsidiaries around 17%).

Odisha plywood plant capex about INR130 crore; other plywood technology improvements about INR45-50 crore; MDF capex about INR425 crore, of which about INR300 crore falls in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28.
capex_capacity: PVC and WPC plant commenced commercial production in April 2026 with installed capacity of 6 million kg for doors and 3 million kg for door frames; peak revenue potential INR75-80 crore.
New MDF facility: civil construction underway and key machinery ordered; management says on track. About INR10 crore paid as advance to main equipment supplier so far.
Plywood greenfield facility (Odisha) under construction at full pace with major orders placed.

Plywood process change (ContiRoll technology): implemented in 2 of 4 existing facilities, remaining 2 to be done in FY27. Management says it lowers cost, manpower and material use and improves quality.
Flooring line in MDF expected to be fully operational in early Q2 FY27, with annual top-line capacity of about INR70-75 crore at peak.
Management says investment per cubic metre on the new Conti capacity is lower, aiming to improve capex turnover and ROCE. Steady-state ROCE aspiration of 18-20% at peak utilisation.
demand_pricing: Chemical prices rose over 50% early in the quarter; chemicals are about 30% of MDF raw material cost. Price increases: MDF 5% and 10% (15% total per analyst question confirmed by management) and plywood 4-5%, effective April 2026. Management says chemical prices have stabilised.

Q4 volume growth partly reflected channel stocking in the second half of March, plus a shift from unorganised to organised players as small MDF and plywood players were disrupted by cash-tight supplier terms.
Industry MDF growth estimated at 15-20% annualised; plywood industry growth 3-4%. Management estimates Greenply MDF market share about 7% currently, peaking at 8-8.5%.
Timber prices stable in Q4 and expected flat for FY27. Imports of MDF largely wiped out due to BIS and dollar/freight conditions.
Receivable days rose by about 3 days from December 2025 (analyst cited 47 to 54 days YoY), attributed to OEM growth and furniture factory business; management says receivables are LC-protected.
Advertising spend in Q4 lower YoY; management says the annual amount is unchanged and it is timing of expense recognition.

qa_highlights.question: Is MDF margin sustainable and is plywood double-digit margin sustainable with quality issues in the lower-end brand fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says MDF margin is sustainable, driven by volume and operating leverage on fixed costs, with cost increases already passed on. Plywood margin is sustainable if volume targets are met; process changes have improved quality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet trajectory after capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity may peak at 0.7-0.72 in one year, then return to 0.5-0.6 the following year; management does not want substantially higher debt.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-offs (Dubai/GMEL, forex) behind the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no further challenges, with all potential liability on equity, corporate guarantees and loan advances provided for in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume growth inflated by channel inventory, and does Q1 FY27 continue the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management partly agreed, noting some stocking in the second half of March, and attributed growth mainly to a shift from unorganised to organised players; Q1 FY27 has started strongly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and split of growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR425 crore MDF capex, roughly INR300 crore in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28; Odisha plywood about INR130 crore; plywood technology upgrades INR45-50 crore. Analyst estimated about INR480 crore for FY27, which management said was almost right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDF gross margin volatile and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q2 and Q3 volatility to line extension disruption and trading mix; Q4 FY26 margin is the base to deliver going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the income tax search conducted and is there any liability?
qa_highlights.answer: Search covered Greenply, Greenlam and Greenpanel; management said the reason is not known, no order or demand has been received, and the auditor has noted no liability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the JMD and CEO Manoj Tulsian step down, and is there a change in strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: He stepped down to pursue personal commitments and will continue as an advisor; sales, plant, IT, HR and marketing heads are in place, and a full-time replacement at his level is not planned immediately.

526797|2026-06.headline: Greenply Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR724.9 crore, with core EBITDA margin of 10.8%, up 50 bps YoY.

Plywood and MDF both delivered double-digit volume growth, but management said Q1 sales were lost to election-related labour disruption, lower plant utilisation (92-93% vs ~98-99% in Q4) and weak outsourcing. Price increases of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood were taken, and the new MDF flooring line started commercial production on 20 July 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth, and a 10% plywood margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable MDF EBITDA margin, and the upside after the second line?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports 16-17% margin on a sustainable basis; the second line's operating leverage could add ~1% more, so 18% is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the MDF gross margin decline of ~300 bps QoQ?

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE targets for MDF and the path to them?

526807|2026-03.headline: Seamec Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to Rs330 crore and PAT more than doubled to Rs103 crore; FY27 growth guided at about 15%.
526807|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue and profitability, with consolidated revenue of Rs1,000 crore (up 47%) and PAT of Rs253 crore versus Rs88 crore. Q4 consolidated EBITDA reached Rs162 crore versus Rs91 crore a year earlier. Management guided FY27 revenue and profit growth of about 15% and a stable EBITDA margin of 40-42%, while flagging that vessel Seamec Paladin remains stuck in Dubai due to the West Asia conflict, which removes its revenue for April-May. The company added two ONGC O&M contracts with Supreme Hydro and SEAMEC AGASTYA, and is acquiring SEAMEC ANANT (about $70 million capex in FY27).

segments.name: Offshore vessel charter (DSV/MSV/OSV fleet)
segments.commentary: Management says fleet utilisation is almost 100% excluding off-hire from dry dock, breakdowns and seasonality. Diamond (OSV) on ONGC charter earns about $8,750/day per Vinay Agarwal; renewal expected at 10-15% higher.

segments.name: International (Saudi Arabia, Dubai)
segments.commentary: International markets contribute about 10-15% of revenue. Dubai operations have been pruned; one vessel is working for Saudi Aramco and one vessel (Paladin) is stuck in Dubai dry dock.

segments.name: O&M contracts (ONGC, consortium with Supreme Hydro)
segments.commentary: Samudra Sevak and Samudra Prabha contracts run to 31 March 2028 with values of Rs348 crore and Rs270 crore; Supreme Hydro holds about 10%. Billing is monthly. Samudra Prabha expected to start work around the first week of June 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and bottom-line growth of about 15%, per Sunil Gupta; management declined to go beyond 15%.
EBITDA margin guided to a stable 40-42%; quarterly margins may vary by 2-3 points with dry dock and contract mix.
Seamec Paladin not operating in Q4 or April-May; revenue expected from June only if geopolitical situation clears.
SEAMEC-II contracted only till August 2026, then a small dry dock; SEAMEC AGASTYA gives full-year revenue in FY27.

Competition persists in bidding; management denied pricing pressure in bids currently.

qa_highlights.answer: Supreme Hydro holds about 10% and provides technical know-how, manuals and personnel; billing is monthly to ONGC at month end.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 incremental revenue be about Rs500 crore from AGASTYA, SWORDFISH, ANANT and O&M contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the assumption was not right and would not go beyond 15% guidance, citing Paladin being idle and SEAMEC-II contracted only till August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 capex and FY27 plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about Rs300 crore; FY27 scheduled capex is about $70 million for ANANT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 margin one-off or should margins be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-off in Q4; Paladin idle for Q4 and April-May; margin guided stable at 40-42%, with 1-2% upside possible depending on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Diamond's rate far below spot OSV rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ocean and Emerald are larger vessels doing geotech and stimulation work, so comparison is not like-for-like; Diamond is an OSV, an aberration in a DSV-focused fleet.

qa_highlights.question: Is there impairment on UK subsidiary and any progress there?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment taken on prudence due to geopolitics, not abandonment; no accounting or execution impact; no new contract announced yet.

526807|2026-06.headline: Seamec Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41% YoY to INR 297 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124 crore (about 42% margin).
526807|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 297 crore against INR 211 crore a year ago, up 41%, and standalone revenue was INR 283 crore against INR 201 crore. Consolidated PAT rose to INR 81 crore from INR 76 crore, while standalone PAT was flat at about INR 81 crore versus INR 80 crore. Management attributed the quarter to higher vessel deployment, healthy utilisation and cost discipline, with Paladin's dry-dock and the Middle East conflict weighing on the onshore segment. The call focused on the Seamec ANANT acquisition (USD 70 million, expected by end-August), the 40-42% margin band and the 15-20% growth CAGR target.

segments.name: Offshore (IMR/EPC vessels)
segments.commentary: Margins materially better than onshore, attributed to higher vessel deployment. Management said the 40-42% margin band is sustainable on an annualised basis.

segments.name: Onshore / other (Paladin)
segments.commentary: Margins pulled down because Paladin was non-operational in Q1 (dry-dock in Dubai, stuck by Middle East conflict); it incurred cost with no revenue. Paladin has returned to India and resumed contract, with revenue expected from Q2.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over the next 3-5 years and says it is committed to that number.
Margins: management guides 40-42% EBITDA margin, sustainable on an annualised basis; quarterly figures not guided.

Seamec ANANT: acquisition (USD 70 million, funded about 50:50 internal equity and loans) expected to complete by end-August 2026; deployment on ONGC contract about one month after acquisition for statutory formalities, with start expected within Q2 FY27 per Naveen Mohta and in Q3 per Sunil Gupta; expected 95-98% utilisation once working.
Gallant vessel sale: expected to complete in September 2026 after shareholder approval.
Seamec Princess/III: monsoon idle period (May-October); Princess being dry-docked in this period; contract talks for October at an advanced stage, not yet announced.
Seamec II charter ends end-August 2026; intended for EPC work rather than IMR; no rate uplift confirmed.

Management expects FY27 and FY28 growth from newer vessels and higher deployment; Samudra Samrat-type ONGC O&M contracts (Samudra Sevak, Samudra Prabha) continue, with no vessel-wise revenue disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Seamec ANANT: timeline, consideration and financing?

rows.why: Management held the 15-20% CAGR and the 40-42% margin band, gave no rate outlook, and did not raise either, with off-hire and dry-dock periods cited as reasons to keep the margin band.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Seamec II charter ends end-August with no rate uplift confirmed, Princess October contract is not yet announced, and ANANT redeployment timing differs between Q2 and Q3 across management speakers.

rows.why: Princess October contract talks are at an advanced stage but not announced, and Seamec II charter ends end-August with intended EPC work and no rate uplift confirmed.

rows.label: Gallant vessel sale completion
rows.why: Sale expected to complete in September 2026 after shareholder approval; it is a divestment, so it reduces fleet rather than adding revenue.

rows.label: Middle East growth via Aramco qualification
rows.why: Management cites Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Abu Dhabi as key growth areas and Aramco qualification is lifting inquiry flow, but no contract count or revenue figure was disclosed.

526829|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 117% YoY to INR2,408 crore and PAT more than tripled to about INR62.6 crore, driven mainly by LPG volumes.
526829|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue (about INR2,408 crore), EBITDA (about INR147 crore) and PAT (about INR62.6 crore) for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with basic EPS of INR1.86. Management attributed the top-line jump largely to higher LPG prices during supply disruption from West Asia, while saying volumes also rose sharply (about doubled YoY) and that a portion of the growth came from new bulk and institutional customers on short- to medium-term contracts. Auto LPG volumes slowed temporarily on higher prices and have since recovered per management. Most company-specific numbers (segment revenue split, FY26 capex, LPG import volumes, Type 4 cylinder margins) were deferred to follow-up emails.

financial_highlights.change: +117% YoY (from INR1,112 crore); +98% QoQ (from INR1,216 crore)

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR62.6 crore (management also cited exceeding INR66 crore in one remark)
financial_highlights.change: More than tripled YoY (from INR20.5 crore); +82% QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: PAT margin (analyst-cited, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.change: Management said margins are 'intact' and that the drop is due to higher LPG prices

segments.name: Packed LPG (GoGas)
segments.commentary: Packed LPG sales of about 18,000-20,000 MT per month; management said it is more commercial than domestic and price-competitive on commercial. Packed LPG and Auto LPG were named as the highest-EBITDA-margin segments, but no margin figures were given.

segments.name: Bulk LPG / industrial
segments.commentary: About 300 industrial customers served; new accounts added in FMCG, food processing, glass and ceramics. Management said a meaningful part of Q1 was volume-led from new bulk and institutional customers.

segments.name: Auto LPG (ALDS)
segments.commentary: 315+ dispensing stations, all operational. Demand slowed temporarily in the quarter on higher LPG prices, and management said volumes have since recovered. Payback on a new station is said to be under 18 months.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: 50+ CNG stations completed, with a further 50 targeted in Bengaluru. Average station volume was said to be about 6,000-6,200 kg per day, and total volume about 3 lakh kg per day.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to 10-15% QoQ growth in revenue, PAT and EBITDA in coming quarters; it did not give a multi-year revenue number.
Auto LPG network target: 500 stations, with about 75 added in FY27 and about 100 in FY28, then a further evaluation toward 500.
CNG target to increase from 50 to 100 stations; talks with other CGD players for Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore, not finalised.
Management expects margins to rise as volumes grow and once prices normalise; no bps or percentage target was given.
Backward integration is under evaluation, including small coastal storage terminals (not finalised) and a 100% Dubai subsidiary for LPG import ease.
Type 4 high-pressure cylinder unit at Butibori (Nagpur): capex complete and machinery installed; production expected in 1-2 months, subject to order book. Margin not disclosed.
capex_capacity: Type 4 high-pressure cylinder plant (Butibori): capex complete and machinery installed; start awaits order book, with production expected in 1-2 months. Target customers are CGD players, car fleet owners and OEMs.
CNG: 50+ stations operational; 50 more planned in Bengaluru.

Fleet and infrastructure as stated: ships on time charter, 68+ bottling/blending plants, 478+ LPG road tankers, 225+ HCVs/LCVs, 82 CNG road vehicles, 15 cylinder plants and 3 high-pressure cylinder plants.
Total capacity was cited by an analyst as 608 TMT or 685 TMT; management did not confirm or answer on utilisation.
demand_pricing: India LPG market about 35.04 MMT, projected at about 40-42 MMT by FY2030; OMCs hold about 94% of sales and private marketers about 6%, with CPIL holding about 33% of the private segment (management claim).
During the West Asia disruption, the company diversified sourcing to North America, Africa and the Middle East, and said several marquee customers moved to longer-term contracts.
Management said Q1 revenue growth was mainly price-driven, but also volume-driven (volumes about doubled YoY per management).
Management said it is price-competitive against PSUs in industrial, HoReCa and commercial segments.
Gin Kar Lo, Gin Kar Do scheme (pay-for-actual-consumption cylinder weighing) introduced; direct financial impact not a stated objective.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Type 4 cylinder plant operational, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is complete and machinery is installed at Butibori. Production is expected within 1-2 months, but the start depends on receiving the order book. Management declined to give margin numbers until the first deliveries.

qa_highlights.question: Which cities are in CNG network talks?
qa_highlights.answer: Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore were named, but none is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue, EBITDA and PAT will grow QoQ, though revenue will move with LPG prices. It later quantified 10-15% QoQ growth.

qa_highlights.question: How is the PAT margin trending and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are intact and rising, and that the lower percentage reflects higher LPG prices. It gave no quantified margin target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 growth came from the West Asia disruption, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company had inventory when PSUs faced constraints, and that new customers signed longer-term agreements. Management said volumes are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation priority (organic, M&A, debt, dividends)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of new stations, JVs and acquiring infrastructure, plus bottling expansion and backward integration. No allocation split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging of LPG import currency exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payments are made on time and spot contracts are used, so no hedge is currently required; it would hedge in future if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BW exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BW, a strategic investor from 2023-24, exited in the secondary market to focus on its shipping business, with no impact on the company.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Income Tax search?
qa_highlights.answer: The search began 7 October 2025 and closed within 7 days. Assessment is open, no final demand has been received, and management does not expect a large payable.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of revenue by segment, FY26 capex, and LPG import data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred these to follow-up emails and gave no figures on the call.

Type 4 cylinder plant at Butibori: start depends on receiving an order book; no customer contracts were confirmed and no margin was disclosed.
Auto LPG volumes slowed on higher prices in Q1 and management says they have since recovered; watch monthly volume data and the 75 station additions in FY27.

Sustainability of West Asia-linked volume gains: management said several customers moved to longer-term contracts, but terms and volumes were not disclosed.

526861|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 7% to ₹160 crore while PAT fell 55% to ₹3.67 crore; management targets ₹60 crore from Malur in FY27.
526861|2026-03.overview: Management admitted missing its FY26 sales target, blaming delayed commissioning of Malur machinery and a workforce readiness gap. EBITDA margin slipped to 8.7% from 9.1%, and PAT fell 55% YoY to ₹3.67 crore. Management says Malur is now fully operational, the paint shop phase one went live in June 2026, and shipments to the largest customer have started. Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 8–11% and a ~20% revenue CAGR over three years. Analysts pressed on plant utilisation, idle capacity, cost structure and the gap between guidance and a 13–14% margin ambition.

segments.name: Construction equipment fabrication
segments.commentary: About 53% of FY26 revenue; management says customer capacity expansion is driving demand, and Malur was built for large, complex assemblies.

segments.name: Malur plant (Bangalore new facility)
segments.commentary: Management targets ~₹60 crore revenue in FY27 (analyst pencilled ₹50-60 crore), rising to ₹100 crore by FY29; ~₹25-30 crore of existing Bangalore business is being shifted there.

segments.name: Pune plant
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹36-38 crore in FY26; management targets at least ₹50 crore in FY27 (~80% utilisation), excluding new export trial orders.

segments.name: Vadodara plant
segments.commentary: Management sees flat volumes as a major customer's business declined; first small US export orders received recently.

segments.name: Power / electrical
segments.commentary: Largest electrical customer Schneider's offtake fell sharply from Q4 FY25; management sees little benefit from the power sector boom to its current customer mix.

segments.name: Robotics / automation
segments.commentary: FY26 business about ₹2 crore; inquiries up 300-400% since March; FY27 target ₹5-10 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Malur revenue ~₹60 crore; ₹100 crore by FY29, possibly earlier.
Overall revenue CAGR ~20% over next three years; FY26 base is ₹160 crore, and analysts cited ~₹190 crore as a plausible FY27 level.
EBITDA margin band 8-11%; management says it agrees double-digit EBITDA is needed and is aiming for it, but gave no 13-14% target.
Caterpillar business expected to grow at least 15-20% in FY27; management says talks are very positive.
Employee cost to be a key challenge, with Karnataka minimum wage hikes of up to 30% flagged; the goal is for employee cost as a percentage of sales to fall below FY26 levels.
Finance cost expected to stay around Q4 FY26 level; second paint shop phase capex ~₹2-3 crore still pending.
risks_watch: Execution risk: management admitted FY26 target miss; the Malur ramp-up depends on the largest customer's volumes.
Schneider (power switchgear) offtake decline from Q4 FY25 with no clear explanation.
Employee cost inflation, especially Karnataka minimum wage increases of up to 30%.
Overlap between Malur and Bangalore revenue means the net growth from Malur is ₹30-35 crore, not ₹60 crore.
Vadodara utilisation weak; Pune utilisation dependent on new export customers.
Freight cost and geopolitical or raw material volatility; pass-through lag of one quarter.
Lack of a quantified margin path beyond 8-11%; analyst pressure for 13-14%.
526861|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on FY26 execution, with management owning the miss; guidance is described as conservative, and the outlook for FY27 is cautiously optimistic. On margins and idle capacity, management was less specific and somewhat defensive when pressed by analysts.
key_quotes: As the company's MD, I take full responsibility for this shortfall.
We are still climbing the learning curve; we have n't climbed it.
So I think based on that , if we keep on , if we increase 20 -25% compounded as w e have been talking about, definitely a good part of that should flow downwards as EBITDA.
And if we don't do that, I would also treat it as a failure.

financial_highlights.change: stable over last three years per management

qa_highlights.question: Dhwanil Desai asked what FY27 Malur revenue to expect, whether product approvals are in place, and whether ₹50-60 crore is incremental to ₹160 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ₹60 crore from Malur in FY27 and ₹100 crore by FY29, with product approvals in place and shipments started to the largest customer. About ₹25-30 crore of the ₹160 crore base will move from Bommasandra to Malur, so the addition is not simply ₹160 + ₹60.

qa_highlights.question: Dhwanil Desai asked whether the margin path could move from 8-9% toward 13-15% as Malur utilisation ramps.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an EBITDA band of 8-11% for FY27 and declined to quantify beyond that. Harshad Patel said gross margin has held for three years and a good part of 20-25% compounded growth should flow to EBITDA, aided by automation.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta questioned why the company keeps adding plants while Pune and Vadodara run at low utilisation and whether consolidation is planned.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new Bangalore plant was needed because the old facility lacked space for Caterpillar growth, and no other new plants are planned. Harshad Patel said Pune will reach about 80% utilisation and that idle plants must improve or be closed, while citing skill and certification differences across plants.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta asked whether FY27 revenue should be closer to ₹190 crore or ₹210-225 crore, and how raw material price increases are passed through.
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Agrawal said the outlook is conservative given geopolitical and raw material volatility, while agreeing the projections could make the higher number achievable. Pass-through is quarterly when prices move more than ±5%, with a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Jain asked about Caterpillar growth and the power sector opportunity.
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Agrawal said Caterpillar talks are very positive, with at least 15-20% growth expected in FY27. Harshad Patel said power sector gains are mainly in transformers and not in the company's switchgear customers, and Schneider offtake fell sharply with no explanation.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Jain asked about Pune revenue potential, export margins and robotics targets, and employee cost trajectory.
qa_highlights.answer: Harshad Patel targets at least ₹50 crore from Pune in FY27 (from ₹36 crore) and robotics ₹5-10 crore. On employee cost, he said Karnataka wage rises of up to 30% are a major challenge and the target is employee cost as a % of sales below FY26, with the labour line affected by duplication across old and new plants last year.

qa_highlights.question: Manoj Dua asked how to reach 13-14% EBITDA margin in the long term and what the path is beyond ₹300 crore revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Harshad Patel agreed double-digit EBITDA is needed and said the company must aim for it, calling a failure to do so a failure. On growth beyond ₹300 crore, he said global earthmoving export demand is the focus and tube business is on hold for the next 12 months.

526951|2026-03.headline: Stylam's third laminate plant at Manak Tabra is due to start commercial production by end-June or early July 2026, with INR250-300 crore revenue targeted in FY27.
526951|2026-03.overview: Management said the third greenfield laminate plant at Manak Tabra is in testing and should begin commercial production in late June or early July 2026, delayed from earlier guidance by an environment clearance issue. Total capex to date is INR334 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 20-25% over FY26 and said Q4 gross margin was about 49% (which an analyst later cited as 39%, a discrepancy unresolved on the call). The call was dominated by the AICA Japan open offer and strategic partnership, the impact of the West Asia war on raw material costs, and management's answers were often vague or hard to hear.

segments.name: Laminates (existing plants)
segments.commentary: Laminate capacity utilisation was 74% in FY26; management said existing orders are being delayed due to capacity constraints. Export is about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: New third laminate plant (Manak Tabra)
segments.commentary: Management guided INR250-300 crore revenue in FY27 and INR600-700 crore in FY28 at about 80% utilisation; peak utilisation could yield INR900-1,000 crore. Operating margin guided at 22-24%.

segments.name: Acrylics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was about INR15 crore; FY27 target is INR50-70 crore, supported by AICA Japan purchasing acrylic, which management said is at a preliminary stage.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Management took over domestic handling about three months ago and does not report domestic EBITDA separately; the company reports consolidated EBITDA only.

guidance_outlook: Commercial production at new Manak Tabra plant expected end-June to early-July 2026; testing has started.
New plant revenue INR250-300 crore in FY27 (earlier stated INR300-400 crore in the next three quarters), INR600-700 crore in FY28 at about 80% utilisation.
Overall FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 20-25% over FY26; management declined to give an exact number.
EBITDA margin for new plant expected at 22-24%; an analyst's suggestion of about 22% company-level EBITDA by FY28 was answered with 'hopefully'.
Management expects EBITDA impact from West Asia-driven cost increases to be limited to about 1-3%, offset by price hikes, higher revenue absorbing fixed costs, and favourable USD/EUR exchange rates.
AICA deal (open offer completion and remaining stake tender of about 40%) expected to finish by mid-June, after which collaboration will be discussed.
capex_capacity: Third greenfield laminate plant at Manak Tabra: construction largely complete; delayed from November, then March, now June due to environment clearance (EC) needed from the Ministry of Environment in Delhi because Haryana had no CER at the time.
Capex incurred to date INR334 crore; management said fixed costs for the new plant are already in the P&L and staffing is about 150 workers with ~70-80% of wage costs already set.
New plant: three of four lines dedicated to export; compact laminates; some sizes to be produced in India for the first time.
Ramp-up: 30-40% utilisation expected from Q2 FY27; 80%+ utilisation targeted within two years.
Management said next quarter it would outline further expansion plans; a planned expansion was mentioned but not detailed.
demand_pricing: Management said new customers for the new plant's sizes are in discussion but gave no quantified PO book; existing orders are being delayed due to capacity constraint.

Raw materials: phenol and paper costs rose due to Middle East supply disruption; management said melamine has 5-6 months stock, phenol was bought 3-4 months ago at old prices, and some chemicals are under forward contracts.
Price hikes: 3-5% taken across customers; domestic in two tranches; export only where feasible, as management said Stylam competes with European players less affected by commodity costs.
Management said demand is not expected to fall with price increases, citing construction demand.
Export shipments are on FOB terms; transit time 45-60 days; no shipping delays reported. US tariff 10%.
Domestic brand visibility: management expects results in two to three quarters after restructuring of domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the new plant delayed and what is the commercial production date?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay was due to an environment clearance issue after a Supreme Court observation; EC was applied to the Ministry of Environment in Delhi, taking 2-3 months plus. Commercial production expected late June to early July; testing started.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue guidance for FY27 and what is the peak potential of the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: New plant FY27 revenue INR250-300 crore; FY28 INR600-700 crore at 80% utilisation; peak INR900-1,000 crore. Company-level FY27 growth 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will management structure or the AICA stake change after the open offer?
qa_highlights.answer: Manit Gupta said no change in management; AICA is a strategic partner with no operational role. Management said the aim is not to sell stake, though the SHA put option exists.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the West Asia war on costs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said impact limited to 1-3% of EBITDA, offset by price hikes, revenue scale, and favourable exchange rates (USD near INR96, EUR near INR112). Q4 gross margin cited as 49%, later referenced as 39% by an analyst.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and FY26 export vs domestic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex to date INR334 crore. FY26 revenue split 75% export and 25% domestic; management expects to keep the same split in FY27 while growing domestic.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AICA Japan opportunity for supply and acrylics?
qa_highlights.answer: AICA Global is not currently buying from India and has its own plant in Rudrapur; deal not yet finished, expected in about a month. Acrylics FY27 target INR50-70 crore.

527001|2026-06.headline: Ashapura Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR1,616 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR188.9 crore and margin fell to 11.7%.

PBT declined about 1.4% YoY to INR130.03 crore and EPS rose to INR12.07 from INR11.5. Guinea bauxite volumes fell to 2.34 million tons from 3.16 million tons in Q4, with bauxite EBITDA per ton rising to USD6.3 from USD5.9. India businesses were hit by fuel, freight and sulphuric acid costs, with the bleaching clay JV under the most pressure.

segments.commentary: Wholly owned; bentonite broadly stable with domestic growth offsetting weaker exports, while white performance minerals profitability was hit by higher sales and distribution costs. No segment figures given.

530005|2026-03.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated volume about 44 Mt, EBITDA of INR1,253/t, and a INR240/share FY26 dividend, with India Cements brand migration completed.
530005|2026-03.overview: The call was the UltraTech Q4 FY26 earnings call, transcript filed by India Cements Ltd as a subsidiary disclosure. UltraTech crossed 200 Mt India capacity and committed to 242.5 Mt by FY28. Q4 realisations rose about 2.5% on grey cement pricing, with consolidated EBITDA per tonne at INR1,253 (INR1,296 excluding acquired assets). Management flagged West Asia-linked cost pressure, mainly bags (about INR90 crore hit in March) and a mark-to-market forex loss (about INR120-130 crore), and said price hikes taken in April offset it. The Board recommended a INR240/share dividend for FY26, and India Cements' 100% brand migration to UltraTech was completed at end-March 2026.

530005|2026-06.headline: UltraTech Q1 FY27: domestic grey volume up 13.1% to 81% utilisation, EBITDA INR5,146 crore and PAT INR2,604 crore (+17.2%).

Domestic grey cement volume grew 13.1% YoY, with capacity utilisation at 81% versus 76%, and revenue rose 16%. Management flagged a fuel and packing cost shock during the quarter and guided to a further INR130-140 per ton cost increase in Q2 FY27. India Cements turnaround continued, with EBITDA per ton at INR603 versus roughly INR386 in Q2 FY26, and Cables and Wires remains on track for Q3 FY27 launch.

530005|2026-09.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; spot trade prices ~5% above Q2 average entering Q3.

Q2 average trade prices were flat to Q1 (down 1-1.5%), but prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in late September and kept rising in October, with management putting spot about 5% above the Q2 average. Fuel cost rose from INR 45 to INR 51.5 per bag, and management expects the cost pressure to largely persist through Q3-Q4 at roughly INR 2.2 per kcal. Capacity reached 204.7 Mt domestic after 4.6 Mt commissioning in September, and the Ultravolt wires and cables business launched on 3 September. Net debt rose to 1.26x net debt/EBITDA from 0.94x at March-end.

530007|2026-03.headline: JK Tyre Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 42% YoY to Rs.546 crore on 12.9% margin, with a further Rs.4,980 crore brownfield expansion approved.

Management said volume growth was broad-based, led by domestic OE and TBR, and margin expansion came from volumes, mix and cost control. Raw material costs are expected to rise 18-20% in Q1 FY27, which management is offsetting with staggered price hikes of 4-5% (replacement) and 5-7% (export), with a further 5-6% under way. The Board approved Rs.4,980 crore of additional PCR and TBR brownfield capacity to 2029, on top of the Rs.1,130 crore already under implementation.

segments.commentary: Q4 domestic volumes +21% YoY; OE +42%. TBR replacement +19%, TBR OE +53%. Passenger line +16% (replacement +10%, OE +26%). Farm volumes +58% (replacement +30%, OE nearly doubled, exports +44%). 2/3W OE +72%, 2/3W exports +31%.

qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds from the Dec-2023 QIP, held in fixed deposits, have been gradually withdrawn and deployed into expansion projects, reducing interest income.

qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Bajoria cited constrained inputs (bead wire from China, shipping disruption, container shortages, NR up about 18%) and productivity negotiations with workers; these are resolved and management expects better results in the remaining three quarters.

AUM reached Rs 1,448 crore (up 21% YoY) with the mix now 69% wholesale and 31% SME retail. Q4 PAT of Rs 19.4 crore was up 2% YoY but down 7% QoQ on higher ECL provisions and write-offs, and Gross NPA rose to 1.1%. qa_highlights.question: Why has SME share fallen and what is the strategy to rebuild it?
qa_highlights.answer: SME share fell from a 48% peak in FY23-24 to 31%. Causes cited: senior team changes, branch attrition, tighter policies, and a cautious stance over the last 3-4 months. 530117|2026-03.headline: Privi FY26 revenue rose 21.7% to INR2,582.9 crore and PAT 75% to INR327.5 crore, with a 25.76% EBITDA margin.

For FY26, income grew 21.73% to INR2,582.92 crore, driven by about 6.5% volume growth, roughly 8% price increases and product mix. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target and 20%+ EBITDA margins, with the first capex phase due by 30 June 2026 taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA. The PRIGIV JV turned profitable for the first time in Q4, and the merger with PFSPL and PBPL awaits NCLT approval.

segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q4 FY26 for the first time. Revenue is expected at about INR130 crore in FY27 versus INR55 crore last year, with an additional INR50 crore capex. It manufactures high-end specialty chemicals exclusively for Givaudan.

segments.name: Downstream / new specialty molecules
segments.commentary: Silver Amber, Amber Silk, Privilege and Privitolide are in commissioning, with one already commissioned. Ethyl maltol, maltol and cyclopentanone projects target mechanical completion by June 2027, with revenue expected over the next 18 months. Furfural backward integration is about 2 years away, and the vertical is said to reach about INR1,000 crore revenue.

guidance_outlook: Targets 20%+ revenue growth for the coming year on a standalone basis; the 20% excludes merged entities until the scheme is effective.
Expects to sustain 20%+ EBITDA margins going forward; one answer referenced a 24% margin and another 25%.
Long-term target of about INR5,000 crore revenue and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA in 3 to 4 years, roughly 2x.
Post all three capex phases, standalone capacity is expected at about 72,000 MT, around mid-to-late 2028.
Expects the NCLT approval for the merger of PFSPL and PBPL into the parent during FY27, internally targeted for Q3 FY27.

A biomass-to-value-added-products demonstration plant with capex of about INR70-75 crore is in basic and detailed engineering, expected in about 12 months.
Furfural backward integration is expected around FY28-29, after first establishing the finished goods and sourcing furfural from outside in the meantime.

530365|2026-03.headline: Orient Bell Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 66% YoY to INR16.4 crores, with margin up 270 bps, after ~20% cumulative price hikes in March-April.
530365|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 7% and revenue rose 7.5% YoY, with FY26 volumes up 4.4% and revenue up 3.1%. Consolidated EBITDA for Q4 was INR16.4 crores (up 66% YoY, margin up 270 bps) and PBT was INR8.4 crores versus INR3.6 crores a year earlier. Management took roughly 20% cumulative price increases in March and April to offset a roughly 30% rise in gas prices, and said the company is debt free with surplus cash. Management declined to give forward guidance on volumes, margins or capacity utilisation, citing gas-supply uncertainty in Morbi.

vs INR3.8 crores in FY25; after INR1.3 crores one-time labour code cost

segments.commentary: Retail was about 78% of FY26 revenue, with institutional the balance. Management said retail grew faster while the enterprise business did not do well in FY26.

segments.name: Vitrified vs non-vitrified
segments.commentary: Vitrified utilisation was about 80% per management's estimate; non-vitrified was not quantified but was described as higher, possibly around 90% in Q4.

segments.commentary: Still in pilot-stage expansion in select North and East India geographies; epoxy, grout and spatula added in the last 2-3 months. Management expects decent volumes in FY27 but gave no figures.

Management expects Q1 FY27 to see the remaining part of the gas/energy cost increase, since cost increases began around 9-10 March and part was covered in Q3 and Q4.
Management said there is no downward price movement likely in the next few months, and definitely not in Q1, as Gujarat gas June pricing is expected to rise about INR5 per cubic metre.
Management expects FY26 margins to be better than FY25, and said margins have improved year-on-year for the last three quarters.
Capex: no major capacity capex needed in FY27; maintenance capex is about INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores versus about INR6-7 crores in FY26.
Marketing spend is expected to rise from 3.6% of revenue toward about 4% in FY27, though this is not yet decided.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 60-65% in Q4 FY26, and management said it is better than in Q3 and April-May is better than Q4.
No major capacity capex needed; capex limited to maintenance, about INR6-7 crores in FY26 and about INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores in FY27.
Company has three factories outside the Morbi cluster, which supply the bulk of sales and helped stock availability.

Gas allocation was cut to about 50% at one point roughly 10 weeks before the call, leading management to consider shutting some lines; the company uses biofuels in spray dryers at Sikandrabad for 7-8 years.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increase of about 20% in March and April 2026 (about 15-16% in March, 5-6% in April); the company said it was among the first to raise prices around 10 March.

Dealers are cautious and reducing stock to avoid high-priced inventory; a dealer working-capital squeeze and wait-and-watch behaviour in large projects were cited.

Morbi: over 500 units reopened from 1 May, mostly GVT; ceramic output is lower, with labour shortages constraining polishing and packing. Management said Morbi design-level stocks have run down after no production in late March and April.
Management said Morbi oversupply has been cut by the crisis; exports were flat in FY26 and the unorganised sector did poorly.
Digital initiatives: 50,000 new designs added monthly by dealers via AI room visualisation; online lead generation contributing sales for 350-plus dealers monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins sustain around Q4 levels given gas price pressure, and have price hikes been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the margin trajectory to continue; Q4 margin was 7.7% versus about 6% in Q3 (per management's description). Price hikes of about 20% were taken in March-April and further gradual increases are expected depending on gas and diesel prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are gas prices and the Q4 blended INR per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas pricing is formula-linked and changes every few days, with the mix moving from 80% formula to 55% normal and 45% spot. Overall gas prices are up about 30%, and Q4 blended cost averaged about INR45 per SCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company undertake capex now that debt is repaid?

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue goes to marketing?

qa_highlights.question: How are price hikes expected to play out, and is there demand slowdown?

530365|2026-06.headline: Orient Bell Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores, with EBITDA margin at 8.7% and a record 39.7% gross margin.
530365|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores on 22.9% volume growth and about 15.9% higher ASP, with EBITDA up to INR17.6 crores from INR5.6 crores. Management attributed the quarter to Morbi shutdowns (late March to mid-May) that opened a supply gap, plus its own demand-generation push and dealer sell-out support. The company remains debt-free, reports a working capital cycle of 18 days, and is weighing deployment of its cash. Management declined to give any revenue or margin guidance.

segments.commentary: GVT was about 47% of Q1 sales by value; about 15-20% of GVT came from Dora plant, bulk from SKD, and a low single-digit share from Morbi.

segments.name: Tile adhesives (Masterbond)
segments.commentary: Early-stage, cash-and-carry business with INR2.5 crores of sales in Q1, currently scaling in North and part of East India.

Dealers are adding suppliers in other geographies to reduce dependence on Morbi.

Gas: Q1 average about INR60 per unit; Sikandrabad (North) moved from INR44-45 pre-war to INR60-62. Morbi exports fell to about INR800 crores a month average in April-May versus INR1,500-1,600 crores earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase was taken in Q1 and are prices sustainable as gas prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increase of about 18-19% versus pre-war, almost fully realised; no cuts yet, with management watching gas and Morbi pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% volume growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi supply gap during the shutdown plus OBL's demand generation, with about 40% sell-out support to dealers and 24/7 TV advertising; management pointed to input KPIs rather than guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Company policy is no guidance on revenue or margins; management cited positive quarter-on-quarter KPIs only.

qa_highlights.question: Use of about INR75 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15 crores of internally financed capex over four to five months; the larger part is to be invested in the business, with a decision in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Tile adhesives progress and bathware plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhesives generated INR2.5 crores in Q1 on a cash-and-carry basis, expanding from North to East; no bathware plans.

530367|2026-03.headline: NRB Bearings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to INR372 crores, EBITDA margin 19.5%, and FY26 PAT up 77% to INR146 crores.
530367|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR372 crores, with EBITDA up 17% to INR74 crores (19.5% margin) and PAT of INR42 crores. For FY26, revenue rose 11% to INR1,335 crores, EBITDA rose 19% to INR267 crores, and margin expanded to 19.5% from 18.3%. Management attributed margin gains to solar power, automation, yield improvement and renegotiated vendor costs, and flagged a quarter-end forex anomaly that pulled down Q4 gross margin. Management leaned on an FY-level lens, declined to disclose standalone export, aftermarket, and segment splits, and guided to brownfield capacity commissioning from June-July 2026.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Management says NRB is in transmission, driveline, chassis and steering, with limited engine exposure beyond two- and three-wheelers and little wheel-end content. Replacement market grew about 4%, and the company said it shifted focus toward OEMs in Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial business is about 14-15% of revenue per management, including tractors and farm equipment. Target is 20-25% of revenue over time; named focus areas are construction equipment, off-highway, gearboxes, switchgear, power generation and electric grid.

segments.name: Aerospace (Mahant Toolroom, acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mahant Toolroom order book is close to INR50 crores, up from INR25 crores at announcement, with all orders from HAL across divisions. Management expects full operational control between mid-April and May 2026 and a business plan in about six months.

guidance_outlook: International business expected to grow 10-14% in FY27 per current business plan, with management saying maybe up to 15%.

FY27 capex guided at about INR120 crores (including land), against a total announced INR200 crore capex over 18 months plus up to INR40 crores for land; split is 90% machines and 10% infrastructure and building.
Brownfield capacity enhancements to commission from June-July 2026 through FY27 and up to Q1 2028, with partial benefits from the current quarter.
Management aims to sustain EBITDA margins of 18-21% over time; industrial products expected to be as profitable as the core, with individual products ranging from 14% to 30%.
Five-year aspirational revenue target of about INR2,500 crores, which management said is increasingly becoming a concrete goal.
Mahant Toolroom business plan to be shared in about six months; AS9100-linked aerospace certification expected in about six months.
capex_capacity: Reported capacity utilisation about 85%; management says effective utilisation at several plants is much closer to full after adjusting for demand variation, maintenance, shifts and changeovers.
Bottlenecks identified at specific plants; machinery orders placed and first machines arrived, with major enhancement commissioning from June-July 2026.
Capex split: about 90% machines and 10% infrastructure/building/plant; maintenance, quality, new product and small balancing capex is part of normal capex at about 10% of turnover.
Joint venture declaration allows up to 20% of JV capacity to be used for automotive; about 20-25% of current automotive capacity is being used for industrial products.
Mahant Toolroom acquisition gives people, design and certification capability; the company had INR100 crores of aerospace RFQs but lacked an AS9100 plan.
demand_pricing: Management says growth came from volume, market share gains, capacity utilisation, product mix and efficiency, not one-offs.
Export demand was affected by geopolitics and logistics; India faced gas shortages, and customers changed product mix during Q4, which reduced the quarter's original plan.
Management says it prices to maintain margin profile; EV-specific bearings priced to keep existing margins and bearing content per vehicle is largely value neutral.
Company does not give export, aftermarket or standalone splits; it says the replacement market grew about 4% and that it deprioritised replacement given discount structures.
New wins include Siemens (details withheld under confidentiality), and aerospace platforms for HAL and NAL.

530367|2026-06.headline: NRB Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR370 crore and PAT 15% to INR38 crore; standalone PAT up 31.7%.
530367|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR370 crore (vs INR310 crore) and PAT of INR38 crore (vs INR33 crore). Standalone sales grew 14.7% YoY, PAT 31.7% and EBITDA 21.7%. The call focused on the diversification push into aerospace (via the MTR/Mahant Tool acquisition), electrification, off-highway, and robotics, plus a revised FY31 revenue outlook. Management declined to give quarterly or specific FY27 guidance and repeatedly redirected questions to the longer-term track.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 growth guidance and said it is conservative on guidance. It pointed to trailing 12-month growth of 14.38%, which would reach about INR2,730 crore by FY31, leaving the INR3,000 crore figure for investors to compute.

qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is set for April 2027. The site moved from Hyderabad to Aurangabad (Shendra) over logistics and cost concerns, and a partly ready facility has already been bought. INR110 crore is the investment, with INR130 crore of capacity.

qa_highlights.answer: Data-centre bearings are NRB's own product in development, not part of the JV, with no announcement yet. For the CAGR, management pointed to the trailing 12-month average of 14.28% and said the INR2,500 crore target was too low.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the INR10 crore QoQ rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Power, logistics and petroleum-linked cost escalation. Management said it is offsetting this through value engineering (VAVE), plant cost reduction and price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return above 20% as in the past, and has the core team of Mahant Tool Room been retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin guidance is kept at 18-20% on an annual basis; quarters may vary. On retention, management said MTR's leader Mr. Mallappa now heads the aerospace defence segment and that talent retention was a reason for the deal.

qa_highlights.question: Has the lifetime nominated business risen from INR800 crore, which new platforms were won, and will MTR contribute revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Lifetime nominated business is now about INR1,100 crore, driven by the US Corvette win (about 300,000 peak volume). On FY27 MTR revenue, management said yes but declined to quantify, citing difficulty predicting aerospace timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to merge SNL Bearings into NRB?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan to merge. SNL is described as a strong contributor with a lower price point, serving the replacement market and industrial, two-wheeler and agricultural applications.

530475|2026-03.headline: Tinna Rubber Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to over 18% on revenue of INR157 crores, up 22% YoY, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25%.
530475|2026-03.overview: Management reported record tire processing volumes in FY26 and a standalone EBITDA margin of 17.2%, up 286 bps. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY and 13% QoQ to INR157 crores, with EBITDA up 63% YoY to INR29 crores. Subsidiaries and new projects (Oman, South Africa, Saudi, TP Buildtech, PCMB, pyrolysis and rCB) carried start-up costs and geopolitical drag that management expects to normalise through FY27. Infra segment softened on bitumen shortages, which management expects to be temporary.

TP Buildtech Kolkata plant commissioned, running under 25% utilisation, with three new construction system product lines launched.
Micronized rubber powder capacity being increased at at least two plants. PCMB capacity moving from a 6,000 tpa pilot to an 18,000 tpa polymer compounding facility in Haryana.
demand_pricing: Raw material economics: virgin rubber about INR240-260/kg vs recycled rubber about INR50/kg, roughly one-fifth the cost.

Bitumen prices have almost doubled, driving stronger crumb-rubber-modified bitumen (CRMB) demand, though India's bitumen supply constraint (imports of 3-3.5 million tons) hit road-work volumes in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP improved on demand; management said realisation volatility currently favours the company.
Freight rates and elevated polymer prices from the Middle East crisis raised import costs; management says the company offset these by sourcing from multiple geographies and feedstock types.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants: management cites a moat from raw material, product, customer and geographic diversity, plus 2-5 year approval cycles with tire majors.

qa_highlights.question: Vision FY29 revenue breakup by segment, and EPR outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Will the infra slowdown hit blended margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects better realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP to offset any infra softness, and says the bitumen-driven slowdown is temporary.

qa_highlights.answer: Combined FY27 revenue of about INR50-55 crores. EBITDA margins of 15-19% are expected once the plants are fully running, with payback in line with the existing business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 42 to 55?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly due to PCMB, where industry practice carries longer credit days. Core rubber-products credit days have not changed materially, and working capital days are expected to stay at current levels.

qa_highlights.answer: Most of it from internal accruals, with FY27 EBITDA projected above INR100 crores. Management may take up to about INR20 crores of debt if needed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling bitumen supply and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company holds no bitumen and does not trade it. It supplies modifier to IOC and to contractors who source their own bitumen, which the company says is assured business for the next couple of years.

segments.name: Tire recycling (India and Oman)

segments.name: PCMB / PP Buildtech

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR670-700 crores (INR675-700 crores cited in later reply).
EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20% for FY27, described as sustainable despite Q1 at ~22%; management declined to confirm either 18% or 22%.
Vision 2029: INR1,000 crores revenue by FY29, 25%+ revenue CAGR, 33%+ profitability CAGR, EBITDA margin above 18%, ROCE above 30%, presence in 10 locations.
Capex of ~INR100 crores across FY27-FY28; INR27 crores spent in Q1 FY27; ~INR60 crores to be capitalised in FY27. Capex could rise if demand stays strong.
TPO/rCB (pyrolysis oil and recovered carbon black) contribution of 7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 crores). TPO sales from Q2 FY27; rCB production from Q3 FY27.

South Africa breakeven expected Q2 FY27; Phase 2 tyre crumb production expected Q2 or Q3 FY27. Saudi Arabia (24,000 tpa) construction targeted toward end of calendar 2026, subject to Middle East normalisation.

capex_capacity: India tyre crushing capacity 185,000 tpa, rising to 235,000 tpa by FY27 (+27%).
MRP capacity: 3,500 tpa expansion commissioning by Q3 FY27, taking total to 20,000 tpa.

Management is exploring de-bottlenecking and possibly a greenfield India plant; India utilisation cited at 80-85% by analyst. Blended utilisation target 75-80% by year-end across geographies.
demand_pricing: Industrial demand supported by rising raw material costs and ESG-driven tyre-maker demand; MRP and reclaimed rubber volumes growing fast.
Rubberized bitumen demand rose as bitumen supply tightened and prices rose due to the West Asia conflict; government push to reduce import dependence.
Consumer turfing demand hit by binder and synthetic grass price spikes; management says the market is intact and will recover once prices stabilise.
EPR credits: ~100,000 units monetised in Q1 at a floor price of ~INR2,500 per unit (~INR25 crores cash). Management says EPR contributes ~INR25-30 crores a year at PBT level.
Margin gain attributed to raw material optionality and value-added product mix. Management said inventory gains were very marginal.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin rise is due to inventory gains, and is there margin normalisation ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains were very marginal. Management said the changes are systemic (raw material optionality, value-added mix), and expects some front-ended costs from new projects, so 18-20% is the sustainable range.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the 400-500 bps margin expansion; material plus inventory cost fell to 46% of sales.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main contribution came at gross margin, from cheaper raw material and higher realisation from value-added products, plus scale efficiencies. Overall EBITDA margin expanded about 4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How is EPR monetisation accounted for, and what is its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accrued EPR credits from prior years were monetised against unbilled revenue. Q1 P&L impact was already booked in FY26. Annual EPR contribution is about INR25-30 crores at PBT level. Analysts' questions on clean PAT were not fully resolved on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Chile and Saudi Arabia, and will overseas investment scale up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Oman's limited scope and similar operating parameters for Saudi Arabia, and end-of-life tyre sourcing and hedging for South Africa and Chile. India remains the core investment focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for infrastructure given the West Asia situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bitumen shortages hit some projects, but rubberized asphalt demand rose as contractors sought cheaper alternatives. Infrastructure revenue grew 7% in Q1, and Q1 is the peak road-work season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores was reiterated; margin should sustain at 18-20% even though Q1 was 22%.

Other expenses rose ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst; company promised an email clarification.
Geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) affecting bitumen and binder supply, Oman utilisation (78%), and the Saudi project timeline.

530475|2026-09.headline: Tinna Rubber Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% to INR157 crores and PAT 45% to INR17 crores; H1 PAT up 60% to INR38 crores.
530475|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR157 crores (up from INR120 crores), with EBITDA of INR29 crores (18.8% margin) and PAT of INR17 crores (10.9% margin). H1 revenue rose 25% to INR313 crores, EBITDA 50% to INR63 crores (20.4% margin) and PAT 60% to INR38 crores (12.2% margin). Management said profitability moderated from Q1 due to start-up costs, geopolitical uncertainty and subsidiary performance, and reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue, INR126 crores EBITDA and INR70 crores PAT. Expansion moved forward with a 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site (INR250 crores over 3 years), while the Saudi Arabia tyre recycling plant has been delayed by the West Asia conflict.

segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 38% to INR112 crores despite bitumen supply constraints; management cites it as a main growth driver with Industrial, and notes monsoon and cold-weather seasonality in Q2 and Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 37% to INR85 crores; exports were about 6% of total revenue with export volume growth of about 15%.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: H1 revenue rose to INR21 crores from INR19 crores, driven by price correction with stable volumes.

segments.name: Steel (by-product)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR57 crores from INR53 crores, mainly on price correction with stable volumes; management describes it as a by-product of tyre recycling.

segments.name: PCMB (Polymer Composites & Masterbatch)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue more than tripled to INR27 crores after 12,000 tpa added at Gannaur; capacity now 18,000 tpa, targeted at 8-10% of FY27 revenue and about INR70 crores top line. Management said this business runs at lower EBITDA margin than the core.

segments.name: TP Buildtech (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR41 crores with EBITDA INR4.7 crores, contributing INR1 crore at consolidated level; best-case target of INR100 crores revenue by FY27.

segments.name: Oman subsidiary
segments.commentary: Ran at 90% utilisation in H1; EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 6.4% in FY26; PAT of INR1.3 crores in H1.

segments.name: South Africa and Saudi Arabia (start-up)
segments.commentary: Combined start-up loss of about INR94 lakhs in H1; South Africa Phase 1 complete with semi-processed exports begun, and 9,000 tpa crumb line delayed 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin (about 16% per analyst) come off versus prior quarters, and what about PCMB mix and steel price trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin was 18%-plus in Q2 (reported 18.8%), Q1 was an aberration with raw material and inventory benefits, and PCMB runs at lower margin than core as a new business still stabilising with R&D spend.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company's sourcing and margin stability differentiated versus peers hit by geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited diversity of geography, raw material base and customer base, pan-India presence, and multiple tyre origins, without commenting on competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Where is India capacity being added to reach 235,000 tpa, and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 10-15k tpa comes from debottlenecking, South Africa adds about 10k tpa this year, and Saudi (24k tpa) is delayed; the 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site is needed as existing land is largely exhausted.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR250 crores Andhra Pradesh capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding options are open over the next 6 to 12 months given a strong balance sheet; the INR250 crores is exclusively Tinna Rubber and spread over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Saudi plant and the Panipat land acquisition risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi land is allotted and contractors identified, but no advances released pending local stabilisation; Panipat is a fully depreciated plant of under 2 acres that could be moved within 3-4 months, and management is making representations to the state government.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential from Andhra Pradesh and what is Vision 2029 INR1,000 crores implication?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex to sales of 2.5-3x implies INR250-300 crores revenue from INR100 crores capex; INR1,000 crores by FY29 is reachable with Andhra and Saudi, with 5-10% variance possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited front-ended hiring ahead of projects (growth of 20-30% annually), start-up costs, and provision for performance bonus in Q2.

530517|2026-03.headline: Relaxo Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.1% YoY to INR 751 crore, with EBITDA margin at 16.5%, aided partly by GST cut-driven channel restocking.
530517|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 751 crore (+8.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 124 crore (+10.6%) and PAT INR 68 crore (+20.4%), with PAT margin at 9.0%. Management attributed the volume recovery to GST cut from 12% to 5%, channel restocking by distributors and better consumer demand, and said the underlying growth is closer to 5-6% over the last two quarters. FY26 revenue fell to INR 2,702 crore from INR 2,790 crore, while PAT rose 5.3% to INR 179 crore. Management has taken 2-3 price increases of roughly 15-18% at consumer level to offset input cost and wage inflation linked to West Asia tensions and Haryana labour costs.

Management said the company cut trade discounts and lifted contribution on higher volumes, with some benefit from back-end cost work; there was a small price increase in Q4.
Management stated the industry (footwear) is seeing price hikes across players, not only Relaxo; Bata, Red Tape and Metro were cited by analysts as not yet having raised prices.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth was a one-off channel restock after the GST cut, and what is underlying growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full impact started after December and underlying growth was about 5-6% over the last two quarters, as distributors' stock was liquidated in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: By how much have input costs risen and how much price has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended consumer price increase of about 15-18%; cost increase estimated at 15-20% including labour, with margins expected to be protected.

qa_highlights.question: Why take price hikes early when competitors have not, and what is the volume risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the April raw material spike and a more than 30% wage increase in Haryana; said the price hike cannot be taken back and gave no volume guidance beyond the 4-5% target.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 capex of INR 180-200 crore include the EBO rollout, and will 100 EBOs dilute margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the EBO capex (INR 30-35 lakh per store, about INR 30-35 crore for 100) is part of the INR 200 crore; management said EBO margins are already accretive and company-level margin is expected to rise about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the high Q4 margin, and is there any inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited back-end plant cost reduction, higher volume against fixed costs, lower trade discounts and a small Q4 price increase; denied any inventory gain.

FY26 revenue declined year on year, so the Q4 recovery must be sustained to show full-year growth.
Geopolitical and inflation uncertainty affecting consumer sentiment, which management flagged as not fully visible.

530521|2026-06.headline: Virat plans Rs 95 crore primary investment in Brahm Lifestyle for 70.2% stake, pivoting toward lifestyle brands; socks contract sales ~6 million pairs.
530521|2026-06.overview: The investor call, hosted by the Brahm Group (promoter, ~75% owner), centred on a strategic pivot rather than Q1 FY27 operating results. Management said Virat will be renamed Brahm Virat Industries Corporation Limited (pending ROC approval) and will invest Rs 95 crore via preferential allotment for a 70.2% controlling stake in Brahm Lifestyle Products Private Limited. Virat's core business is contract manufacturing of socks (9 million pairs capacity, 145 machines), with a nascent branded push (Lord Walker). No audited Q1 FY27 financials, margins or segment numbers were presented; forward figures were management projections and were explicitly labelled forward-looking.

segments.commentary: Management cited ~6-6.5 million pairs contract volume at ~Rs 60 per pair (~Rs 36 crore revenue, 10-12% operating margin); branded target of 2 million pairs in two years at Rs 200-250 per pair.

segments.commentary: About 600 bags sold this year at ~$1,200 retail; target of 2,000 bags at ~$2,000 in two years (~$2 million sales).

segments.commentary: Run-rate ~Rs 1 crore per month; management targets ~Rs 100 million FY-end sales at ~10% EBITDA margin; app launch mid-September.

segments.name: Skill by Brahm (fitness/wellness, Pune)
segments.commentary: Targeting Rs 5 crore sales in first year via memberships; online launch planned November in Pune.
