segments.commentary: Pune Club restaurant breaking even; three spas in Bengaluru operated under Unwind by Brahm. Described as small-scale with no significant capital need.

guidance_outlook: Socks: branded plus contract revenue of ~Rs 100 crore and EBITDA of Rs 20-40 crore in two years (management's own projection).
Brahm Lifestyle: management said it would be disappointed if Rs 400-500 crore sales with ~20% EBITDA were not reached in three to four years; cited a Rs 1,000-3,000 crore market cap as achievable.
Lord Walker: target of ~1 million pairs in calendar 2027, with 5-year plan toward a global lifestyle brand.
Management aims for a 50-60% CAGR on deployed capital; this was described as a personal track record, not a guarantee.
Inorganic acquisitions: 5-6 LOIs under NDA, to be brought to the Virat board when appropriate; no specifics disclosed.
capex_capacity: Capacity: 9 million pairs per year from 145 machines (up from 33 machines and 2 million pairs in 1995); current output ~6 million pairs.
Spare capacity cited as the rationale for branded and DTC expansion, with contract manufacturers in the Gujarat ecosystem available for support.
Brahm Fresh app launch mid-September; Skill by Brahm online in Pune in November.
Handbag production: leather sourced from Indonesia, assembly in India; apparel tie-ups in Kolkata, Coimbatore and Bengaluru.
No explicit Virat capex figure or commissioning timeline was disclosed.
demand_pricing: Virat exports to UK and Switzerland; UK FTA operational from 15 July 2026 removes 11% import duty on Indian socks, per management.
Customers include John Lewis, Waitrose, Barbour, FootAsylum, Umbro, Castore, Sudu, Kukri, Migros (~300 stores) and Galaxus (Switzerland).
Lord Walker launched domestically on Amazon, Myntra, Nykaa, Instamart and Blinkit; first year is focused on brand awareness.
Management said it has zero sales so far in North America, Far East and Middle East, and named these as future targets.
Competition: management referenced China and Turkey sock production and cotton prices, without quantification.

qa_highlights.question: How mature is each business and how will management bandwidth be handled across multiple businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the socks business is mature and cash generative. Other businesses were described as self-sufficient, with funding and teams in place and shared Brahm platform services for technology, HR and admin.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the Rs 95 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no major need for money in socks or handbags. Funds are earmarked for Skill by Brahm, possible acquisitions (5-6 LOIs under NDA), international distribution and marketing, with no specific allocation given.

qa_highlights.question: Can management provide revenue, EBITDA or ROCE guidance for 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave two-year socks projections (Rs 100 crore revenue, Rs 20-40 crore EBITDA) and a handbag target (~$2 million sales), and said a Rs 3,000 crore market cap was achievable. Caveated as forward-looking.

qa_highlights.question: Will Virat expand into products beyond socks, such as gloves or knitwear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said apparel for men, women and kids is planned under Lord Walker, including undergarments, t-shirts and kidswear (Little Walker), with knitwear for kids a future option. Emphasis remains on getting socks right first.

530549|2026-03.headline: Shilpa Medicare Q4 FY26 revenue hit record INR439 crore (+30% YoY) with EBITDA INR121 crore (28% margin); FY26 revenue INR1,549 crore (+18%).
530549|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR439 crore, up 30% YoY, with EBITDA of INR121 crore (+40% YoY, 28% margin). Full-year FY26 revenue was INR1,549 crore (+18%) and EBITDA INR445 crore (+30%, 29% margin), with gross margin at 70%. Adjusted PAT before exceptionals was INR87 crore for Q4 and INR232 crore for FY26 (about +135%). Q4 also included a INR30 crore exceptional gain from selling 31% of Sravathi Advance (JV now an associate, 34% held) and an INR18 crore associate share of profit tied to Maaia. Management gave no formal FY27 guidance, and most FY27 commentary was qualitative.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR985 crore, up 16%; Q4 revenue INR259 crore, up 16% YoY, driven by newly expanded capacity uptake and captive demand from formulations.

segments.name: Formulations (FDF)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR205 crore, up 54% YoY; FY26 INR618 crore, up 30%. Excluding licensing income, base business grew 64% in Q4 and 75% for FY26. European formulation revenue exceeded INR200 crore, up over 100%.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR150 crore, up roughly 100% YoY, driven by CDMO deal momentum; includes a prior-year-type milestone component (Orion albumin milestone referenced by analyst, not quantified).

segments.commentary: Around INR200 crore per analyst question; management said licensing is lumpy but expects it to remain in a similar range at least in FY27.

Recombinant albumin: IMPD batches ongoing at new facility; IMPD submission planned in H1 FY27; India Phase III study approval already received from CDSCO.
demand_pricing: US formulation revenue rose from INR54 crore in FY25 to INR80 crore in FY26 but ran flat at about INR28 crore per quarter over the last 2-3 quarters; azacitidine generic was discontinued in the US.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said US revenue is rising and will continue to in FY27, but azacitidine generic was discontinued; focus is shifting to super-specialty products. Azacitidine FY25 revenue was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin rise toward 35% and will service/licensing income hold near INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 35% is an ambitious target that will not be reached immediately because growth requires spending; licensing income is lumpy but expected to remain in a similar range at least.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR18 crore associate profit (Maaia) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Maaia (35% stake) had previously taken share of losses to zero the investment; improved performance reinstated the carrying value and share of profit was booked. Recurrence cannot be predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Europe FY27 growth and Nilotinib generic timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Generic Nilotinib competition expected in FY27 but tender contracts of 1-2 years mean limited value impact until FY28. Tadalafil ODF and Axitinib launches planned; CFO gave no growth guidance but expects healthy growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of OLC PDUFA and FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not project any meaningful OLC contribution in FY27; filing details are confidential.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the albumin IMPD submission pushed to H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Batches for the IMPD are being produced at the new facility and must finish first; regulator review of a trial application typically takes 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the USFDA status at the Jadcherla site?
qa_highlights.answer: A USFDA audit observed issues; compliance was addressed and a re-audit is awaited. Management says US sales now come mainly from third-party CMOs, so there is no revenue impact.

530549|2026-06.headline: Shilpa Medicare Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR469 crore with EBITDA margin of 30% and reported PAT of INR101 crore, helped by a negative tax rate.

Reported PAT of INR101 crore (up 115%) was flattered by a negative tax rate from reversal of deferred tax liability as the company moves to the new tax regime; the tax rate is guided to normalise to about 25%. Credit rating was upgraded from A+ to AA-, and ROCE improved to 12.5% from 8.8% in FY25. Management declined to give numerical guidance, repeatedly pointing to pipeline launches in FY27 and FY28.

530555|2026-03.headline: Paramount Communications Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24.5% QoQ to INR 573 crore, but FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 117.5 crore (6% margin) on US tariff disruption.
530555|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sequential recovery: revenue INR 573 crore (+13.6% YoY, +24.5% QoQ), EBITDA incl. other income INR 38.8 crore at 6.7% margin, and PAT INR 20.5 crore. FY26 revenue rose about 23% to INR 1,912 crore, but absolute EBITDA and PAT declined YoY due to US tariffs escalating from 10% to 50% during 2025. Management redirected volumes to domestic demand, which grew about 27%, and retained a US presence at sub-economic margins. The Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore, Phase 1) is the main growth lever, with a stated INR 5,000 crore revenue ambition by FY31.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Grew 37.3% to INR 1,001 crore in FY26, led by power cables; domestic order book at INR 508 crore (87% of order book).

segments.name: Domestic B2C and distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 10.6% to INR 179 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Domestic B2G (government/PSU)
segments.commentary: Stable at about INR 182 crore in FY26, so its share of revenue fell.

segments.name: Exports (USA-led)
segments.commentary: Grew 13.9% to INR 550 crore in FY26 despite tariffs; eight active US distributors versus two in FY22.

guidance_outlook: FY27 (informal, assuming current metal prices hold): top-line growth of 15-20% and at least 10% volume growth; no formal guidance given.
Margins expected to return to FY25 levels as a first milestone, with pre-tariff margin levels targeted by end of FY27.

Narmadapuram Phase 1: investment about INR 300 crore by FY28; partial operations from Q1 FY28; sales target about INR 500 crore in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore in FY29; expected 9-10% margin and 3-4 year payback.

Long-term aspiration: INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31, implying doubling every 3-4 years; Phase 1 capacity alone seen at INR 3,600-4,000 crore, with Phase 2 (INR 200-300 crore capex) to exceed INR 5,000 crore.
Working capital expected to normalise within Q1 FY27 after receivables rose on Q4 back-ended dispatches.
capex_capacity: Two existing plants at Dharuhera (Haryana) and Kushkhera (Rajasthan) described as running at optimal utilisation for three to four years; physical space constraint reached.
Existing-plant capex of about INR 50-55 crore a year, over INR 160 crore across the past three years.

Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh): about 31 acres allotted by MPIDC and possession taken; civil works underway; long-lead machinery ordered; building construction to start shortly; commissioning from FY28.

Narmadapuram products: EHV cables up to 132 kV (starting with 33 kV, then 66 kV and 132 kV), transmission conductors, elastomeric EBeam and EPR cables, lead-sheathed rubber cables; EHV approvals expected by FY28.

Funding: about INR 122 crore of equity raised (about INR 92 crore from investors, about INR 30 crore from promoters), plus internal accruals and modest debt; current debt only about INR 110 crore of working capital limits.
demand_pricing: Management cites six demand drivers: India T&D capex of INR 3.35 lakh crore (FY26-30), renewables (210-220 GW solar and 50-60 GW wind by FY30), data centres (about 70% higher cable density for AI facilities), US grid capex above USD 1 trillion, construction capex of INR 18-19 lakh crore, and railways (FY27 budget INR 3 lakh crore).

US tariffs: 10% reciprocal tariff from 2 Apr 2025, raised to 25% in August and 50% by end-August 2025; IEEPA tariffs invalidated by US Supreme Court (Feb-Apr 2026), which management says restored India's competitiveness.
Management says it kept US presence at sub-economic margins at lower volumes; competitors from Vietnam, South Korea, Cambodia, Ecuador and Egypt had a tariff advantage in FY26.
Pricing policy: no firm-price orders with delivery beyond 3-4 months; metal is bought the next working day after order receipt; price-variation formulas increasingly accepted by customers.
Management expects Q2 FY27 onwards to see stronger US demand pull, with one or two new products to be launched in the US next quarter.
Middle East, Europe, Australia and Africa flagged as opportunistic markets, with the Middle East a focus area in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new plant reach optimum utilisation, and what is the payback and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 (INR 300 crore) targets INR 1,200 crore revenue by FY29; payback 3-4 years; margin 9-10%. No formal guidance, but 15-20% top-line growth and at least 10% volume growth assumed if metal prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the domestic market not scaled up the top line or bottom line over the past year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is capacity, not demand; the plants have run at full utilisation for four years, and the company diverted US volume to domestic. FY24 precedent: US sales fell from INR 400 crore to INR 280 crore while domestic doubled from INR 400 crore to INR 800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables roughly double, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 65% of Q4 sales were dispatched in the second half of the quarter; over three-quarters had been realised by 15 May 2026. Working capital cycle moved only from 99 to 101 days; CFO said most dispatches are against LCs.

qa_highlights.question: Can Paramount return to FY25 margins, and what drives margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 EBITDA margin is the first milestone. Drivers: new products, US tariff normalisation, power, renewable and data-centre demand, and operating leverage on volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will EHV lead times exceed 5-6 months, and how is raw material risk handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids long-delivery firm-price orders and prefers 3-4 month horizons or price-variation clauses; EHV would follow the same policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the longer-term aspirational revenue and margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore by FY31; Phase 1 capacity can reach about INR 3,600-4,000 crore, and Phase 2 to exceed INR 5,000 crore. Margins expected to move towards peer range as scale grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when the balance sheet has low leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity was about INR 122 crore of the INR 300 crore project; management said it diversifies the funding mix, with working capital needs still to be bank-funded and current debt about INR 110 crore.

risks_watch: Receivables: working capital cycle at 101 days; management says receivables normalise in Q1 FY27 with over three-quarters of Q4 receivables already collected. Watch the Q1 FY27 receivable run-rate.
US tariff regime and recovery: margins in the US remain below pre-tariff levels; watch whether volumes and margins improve each quarter from Q2 FY27.
Narmadapuram execution: commissioning slated for Q1 FY28 with EHV approvals expected by FY28; the 9-10% margin and INR 1,200 crore FY29 target depend on it.
Raw material (copper and aluminium) pass-through: policy is to avoid long firm-price orders, but EHV and longer-cycle orders may test this.
Management's FY31 INR 5,000 crore target and the FY27 guidance are informal and conditional on metal prices holding.

530555|2026-06.headline: Paramount Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore; operating margin (ex other income) expanded 320 bps YoY to 6.6%.
530555|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore but fell 7.7% QoQ, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4-to-Q1 pattern. Operating profit excluding other income rose 129.2% YoY to INR 34.7 crore, with margin up 320 bps YoY and 136 bps QoQ to 6.6%. The US export recovery after the IEEPA tariff invalidation drove exports to INR 155 crore (29%+ of revenue, up about 77% QoQ), while domestic revenue reached INR 374 crore. Order book rose to INR 615 crore from INR 583 crore, and a fresh equity raise of about INR 122 crore lifted net worth to INR 894 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is in line with expectations and FY25-level margins are targeted by at least Q4 FY27. Drivers cited: normalisation of US exports after the IEEPA duties were struck down (expected to add 300+ bps), and a higher-margin domestic power cable mix (~57% of Q1 revenue). Exports were 29%+ of revenue vs 15% in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Narmadapuram, and are there cost or time overruns?
qa_highlights.answer: Most critical machinery is ordered, with delivery lead times long but expected on time. Civil construction has started and major works are expected to take 6-7 months. Management does not expect major overruns. About INR 30 crore+ has been spent, plus more than INR 155 crore over three to four years on existing plants.

qa_highlights.question: How is Narmadapuram capex funded, and what utilisation supports the INR 1,200 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt drawn yet; funding is from equity raised, internal accruals and planned term loan. Post phase 1, debt-equity is targeted below 0.3x. INR 1,200 crore is at 75% utilisation (the CFO-level comment referred to FY29). Approvals up to 66 kV are in place; 132 kV approvals are expected to start within about a year of manufacturing, with some possibly in 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export order book only INR 97 crore despite strong export revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is deliberately keeping export orders low: firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months delivery, and most customers now bear tariff changes. Management still expects INR 700-800 crore of US exports this year, versus INR 155 crore in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation, and what growth is possible in FY27 versus FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants run at practically 100% utilisation, and the constraint is manufacturing capacity rather than demand. FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%. FY28 growth is expected to be much faster once Narmadapuram starts. The INR 5,000 crore FY31 target is seen as a floor to beat.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin progress at risk if H2 export mix falls, and how do export margins compare with domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export EBITDA was negative in FY26, about -4% to -4.5% at EBITDA level. Pre-FY26 export margins were about 1.5% above domestic. It said the company can pivot quickly between domestic and export, citing FY23 and FY25 shifts, and expects export margins to keep improving each quarter.

Metal price and aluminium exposure: management says firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months, but variable-price and +/- pass-through still carry some variation risk. Metal throughput was only disclosed as up about 4% YoY.

The 6.6% operating margin which excludes other income is quite a meaningful step for us to achieve the FY25 levels that we hope to close with in the current financial year, by atleast the last quarter of FY27.
Because, for Paramount the problem in is not selling, the problem is manufacturing, because our capacity has been constrained.
We do not expect to cross the level of 0.3x at best by the time we complete the first phase of our Narmadapuram project.

530655|2026-03.headline: Goodluck India Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin above 10% and PAT up 34% YoY to over INR56 crore, while FY27 growth guidance was trimmed to 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: PAT grew about 25% against 4% revenue growth: how much is from finance costs or tax, and what is the normalized PAT growth trajectory?

qa_highlights.question: Can the existing order book support double-digit growth without material new wins, and what is its execution timeline?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company have any exceptional items in FY27, after about Rs 150 crore in the last two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect exceptional items this year. Last year's items were mainly Vivaad-se-Vishwas settlements and some investment write-downs.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the Telangana land sale and further monetization?
qa_highlights.answer: The sale was 27 acres for Rs 26-27 crore, leaving about 400 acres in Telangana. Other parcels are under discussion. Non-core monetization target is Rs 150-200 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge reduction timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters and the company are in talks with lenders and expect a substantial reduction this year. Management said around 85-90% of shares are pledged and expects at least a 15-20% reduction, without a specific timeline.

qa_highlights.answer: OC is expected this financial year after a pending litigation closes. The third tower is a service apartment tower, ready to occupy once OC comes. Some buyers have taken possession for fit-outs.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 15%, and are buybacks or ESOPs being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm 15% margins because competition has risen and a large project was lost last year. Margins are targeted at 13-14%. Buybacks will be considered after debt reduction, which may take two to three years. ESOPs will be handled through the existing ESOP trust.

qa_highlights.question: How much working capital and capex will execution need, and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Client advances against bank guarantees or surety bonds should cover most needs. Working capital borrowing of Rs 100-200 crore may be needed in between. The 14.02% margin is mostly project mix, with an average of 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging, and the arbitration awards above Rs 1,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is looking at dredging work, alone or with partners. Arbitrations are being followed up, and settlements are explored where possible. PSUs usually litigate through all courts.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and Q2 revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 40-45, and this continues in new contracts. Q2 is seasonally slower because of monsoon, with some ups and downs but no major disruption expected.

qa_highlights.question: Hydro bids under evaluation and outcome timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Bids under evaluation total about Rs 9,000 crore, mostly Arunachal and North-East hydro, with a Rs 60,000 crore pipeline. Management said outcomes are hoped for by Diwali, which the CEO called hopeful.

qa_highlights.question: Retention money and release timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention is about 5% of each contract, around Rs 200-250 crore on the balance sheet. It is mostly released at project end, though some projects allow withdrawal against bank guarantees.

Q4 operating EBITDA margin improved 41 bps YoY to 12.9% (INR17.78 crore), while FY26 EBITDA margin fell 89 bps to 11% (INR59.49 crore). 531241|2026-06.headline: Linc Q1 FY27 operating income rose 1.4% to INR13,895 lakhs, but EBITDA margin fell 89 bps to 8.7% on polymer costs; no guidance given.
531241|2026-06.overview: Linc delivered a stable Q1 FY27 with operating income of INR13,895 lakhs (+1.4% YoY) despite geopolitical uncertainty and elevated input costs. Corporate sales fell 14% against a high base, exports fell 3%, general trade grew 8% and e-commerce grew 32%. Operating EBITDA was INR1,209 lakhs (8.7% margin, down 89 bps YoY) and PAT was INR581 lakhs (4.2% margin, down 93 bps YoY), both hit by polymer price increases from supply constraints and higher crude. Management said polymer prices are easing, but deferred formal guidance to the Q2 call.

segments.commentary: Operationally stable; exports were more than 50% of its revenue in the quarter.

531266|2026-03.headline: VST Tillers FY26 revenue rose 25% to INR1,240 crore; Q4 revenue up 9% to INR328 crore, operational EBITDA margin 14.2%.
531266|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 25% year on year to about INR1,240 crore (transcript also cites INR1,248 crore), led by power tillers, which grew 35% to 50,332 units. Q4 revenue rose 9% to INR328 crore, with operational EBITDA margin of 14.2% versus 13.4% a year earlier, and operational PAT (excluding fair value gains/losses) up 36% to about INR39 crore. Management declined to guide FY27 growth, citing fuel and commodity inflation, a monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA, and fertiliser availability concerns; it said April and May demand was good and expects Q1 growth over the prior year. Price hikes were taken across tillers and tractors at the end of April.

segments.commentary: FY26 volume 11,346 units vs 7,458 (about 52% growth); Q4 volume 2,947 units, up 27%. Front and rear rotary weeders launched in Q4.

segments.commentary: FY26 volume 3,464 units, up 44%; seasonal, so minimal Q4 volume.

segments.commentary: Single 8+2 variant (3.5 litre engine) currently; FY26 target is about 1,000 units; target 5,000-6,000 units by FY30. Sold through a few dealerships with month-on-month volume increases.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; it is tracking month by month and quarter by quarter, expects Q1 growth over the prior year, and targets 25% but said specifics are difficult to call given uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins be maintained with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance moved to a 12% to 14% operational EBITDA margin range, up from 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up plan for the Zetor brand and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about 1,000 Zetor units in FY27 and 5,000 to 6,000 by FY30, with more variants and a 4WD variant to come.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and the European business shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 export momentum was better; Netherlands-based operation to launch in June/July 2026 as planned, and management is confident of export growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory held at about 36 days; receivables cut from about 75 days to 51 days, with further reduction targeted over the next 2 to 3 years via the TOC supply chain model and SRM digitisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large investment balance be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Three areas: technology and products, global expansion (US re-entry with launch by end-2027), and inorganic opportunities in adjacencies; no specific deal announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the electric tractor investment in Zimeno Inc (US)?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment already provisioned for; US subsidy removal and tariffs halted drivetrain exports. Expertise gained is being used to launch electric weeders and tillers first, with an all-India launch planned for early Q2 FY27.

531266|2026-06.headline: VST Tillers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR313.4 crores, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 45 bps to 12.85% on raw material inflation.
531266|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR313.4 crores from INR282.4 crores, and PAT rose to INR48.7 crores from INR44.6 crores. Operational EBITDA margin (excluding other income and fair value gains) was 12.85%, versus 13.3% a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to commodity and raw material inflation. Power tillers grew about 18% and power weeders about 56% in volume, while domestic tractors grew 4.5% and tractor exports were 275 units. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 outlook, saying it would be clearer in about a month, and said the July volume softness reflected a high base.

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA (excl. other income and fair value gain)

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Volume grew about 18% in Q1; management cites 16-20% tiller growth over recent quarters and expects 15-20% to continue. Bajaj Finance retail financing volume roughly doubled to about 1,000 units from about 400 a year earlier, but still only 8-9% of retail sales versus a 15-20% target.

segments.name: Power weeders (SFM)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 56% in Q1 and management has been clocking 50-60% growth for several quarters. Retail counters added more than 500 in three months, taking the network toward a target of about 2,000 counters by year-end, on top of 750-800 SFM dealers.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 4.5% in Q1 but supply lagged demand during ramp-up of the new variant, per management. Management expects Q2 growth, with substantial volume increases in Q3 and Q4; 40-50 HP is described as a crowded segment.

segments.name: Tractors (exports)
segments.commentary: 275 tractors sold in Q1. Europe: about 1,400-1,500 tractors per management, with entry into Turkey and the Nordics planned. Africa: 75 HP tractor shipments started. US expansion described as unclear.

segments.name: Reapers
segments.commentary: Seasonal product; volumes expected to pick up in Q2 with the harvest season. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 outlook given; management said it is too early and will comment in about a month, since H2 depends on monsoon and rabi sowing.
Management said demand outlook is positive through September, with the next 15-20 days critical for kharif crop survival.
Long-term target of about 20,000 tractors by FY30 (including 5,000-6,000 international units); revenue vision of INR3,000 crores by 2030.
More than 30 tractor variants planned over the next three years; three global platforms (A, B, C) to launch over 12-36 months.
Tractor dealer additions targeted at 50-60 in FY27, versus 40-50 last year.
capex_capacity: A new production facility will need investment in roughly the next two years, per the CEO.
Tiller-tractor hybrid product (geared, with differential) to roll out from the factory starting this month, with substantial volume in Q3 and Q4.
International distributor logistics infrastructure delayed from Q1 but expected operational in Q3.
Hydrostatic transmission tractor being seeded for export markets, not sold in India.
Bangalore land of about 19 acres; manufacturing already moved out, only administrative office remains; no monetisation decision yet.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand issue in tillers; July volumes declined YoY against a very high base.
Tractor 40-50 HP segment is crowded and highly competitive; company is acquiring market share through product breadth.
Commodity inflation (steel, forgings, castings, aluminium, copper), elevated and volatile natural rubber prices, and high crude and freight costs weighed on margins.

Emission norm: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026, which management says will not create a big cost increase for end customers. Stage 5 for all tractors in 2032 could add 25-30% to tractor technology cost today, though this may fall over time.
Possible 100% US tariff under a bill in Congress is a risk to US expansion plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tractor growth lagging the industry despite new launches, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 supply did not fully meet demand during the new-variant ramp-up; management expects Q2 growth and substantial increases in Q3-Q4. Strategy includes more than 30 variants over three years and state-by-state rollout of the FENTM series, starting with Gujarat, then Maharashtra.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the Bajaj Finance tie-up and other financing partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail financing reached about 1,000 units versus about 400 a year earlier, but only 8-9% of retail, against a 15-20% target. Other partners include Chola, TVS and nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is tiller export viable, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 300 units last year. A geared tiller with differential for Europe and India and an electric tiller/weeder are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any moderation in demand given July volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed July to a high base in tillers. It sees growth continuing at least through September, with tillers at 16-20% growth and weeders at 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation policy and non-core asset plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the policy is to maximise shareholder value and it expects to deploy capital over the next 18-24 months. No development on non-core assets yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the implications of upcoming emission norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026 is already ready. TREM 3A from April 2028 is covered. Full Stage 5 for tractors in 2032 may add 25-30% to technology cost at current prices.

Monsoon uncertainty over the next 15-20 days affects kharif output and rabi sowing.
Tariff risk to US expansion, and the possible 100% tariff bill in Congress.

Management has not given a FY27 outlook; next update expected in about one month.

rows.why: About INR 370 crore of the INR 400 crore FY25-27 programme is already deployed (over 90% complete), with INR 90-95 crore ex-GST CWIP machines due for deployment in Q3 and about INR 125 crore of wind energy capex arriving from early November.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fleet utilisation is about 100% and ARR is expected to reach about INR 120 crore from December 2026 to FY28 Q3 as CWIP machines deploy, against current ARR of about INR 72-78 crore, with the order book at about INR 78 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 100% for three years against an industry figure of about 80%, and Mission 2030 implies about INR 600-700 crore of incremental capex over three years, so further capex is guided with a plan behind it.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects to surpass the INR 60-65 crore FY27 guidance, citing the INR 78 crore order book, current ARR of about INR 72-78 crore and H2 seasonality, after H1 revenue of INR 2,989 lakh.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR 2,989 lakh is about half of the INR 60-65 crore guidance, the executable order book is about INR 78 crore, and management expects to surpass guidance; the main watch item is receivable days, which management says normalise to 60-65 days by year end.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 80-ton tower cranes for data centre work are in transit for October-November, and wind energy and crawler fleet additions of about INR 125 crore plus INR 90-95 crore CWIP arrive in Q3, with management citing 150-tonne+ crawler demand.

rows.label: Net debt capped at INR 400-500 crore until FY30; deleveraging after FY28
rows.why: Net debt is guided at INR 400-500 crore until FY30 and debt-to-equity under 2 for 1-1.5 years, with most FY24-25 machines free of bank financing by FY28, but Mission 2030 capex of about INR 600-700 crore keeps leverage high.

rows.label: Receivable days normalise to 60-65 by year end
rows.why: Management blames a family settlement and about INR 75 lakh provision this quarter, says about INR 3 crore is over one year old, and expects cycle normalisation, but this is not yet visible in the numbers.

rows.why: Management deferred UAE and KSA expansion until deleveraging, with paperwork 60-70% complete and funding dependent on internal accruals or equity.

531335|2026-03.headline: Zydus Wellness Q4 FY26 net sales grew 62.1% on Comfort Click, but net profit fell 5.8% as seasonal brands dropped 9.8% in the domestic business.
531335|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales rose 62.1% YoY, driven by the Comfort Click acquisition, with international like-to-like growth of 31.4% and domestic growth of only 1.7%. Domestic seasonal brands fell 9.8% as a delayed summer and rain in March and mid-April left retail and wholesale pipelines unfilled, while skin and hair care rose 39.7% and food and nutrition rose 9.4%. EBITDA grew 42.2% to INR 2,701 million, but net profit fell 5.8% due to higher finance costs from the acquisition debt, higher amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items. Management said operating leverage and the 17-18% EBITDA margin goal remain intact, while the seasonal recovery is expected from May onwards.

financial_highlights.metric: International incl. Comfort Click like-to-like growth (Q4)

Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +2.3%

segments.commentary: Q4 grew 9.4% and FY26 grew 15.5%. RiteBite Max Protein grew at roughly 50% in FY26 (about INR 244 crore per analyst), and management said actual branded growth is higher than reported due to contract manufacturing optimization.

capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.

Complan NutriGro was relaunched and moved to direct supply in the kids segment; VieMax by Complan launched in adult nutrition.
Channel expansion: Boots.com (UK) for WeightWorld and MaxMedix; Amazon UAE for vitamins and supplements.

Sugar Free Green reported its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; sweetener market share rose 24 bps (MAT March 2026); Nutralite grew at double digits despite gas supply headwinds.
Management said supply disruption from the Middle East conflict has been limited, affecting only a very small part of the business.
Gross margins were in line with plan; management cited brand-level margin improvements and exits from low-margin products.

qa_highlights.question: What weighed on seasonal growth and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak North and East markets, March/April rains, and a missing retailer pipeline build ahead of summer. It expects a recovery from May onwards but declined to forecast the season.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be expected to move toward the 17-18% aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins are in line with plan and the miss was driven by mix from weak seasonal sales. Umesh Parikh said operating leverage will play out across the business excluding Comfort Click.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce changing the innovation and channel approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said the portfolio is designed for quick commerce consumers while keeping the traditional channel SKUs. Quick commerce is about 7-8% of domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Comfort Click margin trajectory and is it EPS accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Umesh Parikh said Comfort Click is in line with or slightly ahead of expectations, and it became EPS accretive in Q4. The currency tailwind is about 3%, the gap between reported and constant-currency growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company divest slow-growing categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said there are no plans to divest any category and no major change in capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cuticolor gaining traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Cuticolor is positioned as a derma-backed, Korean-origin safe hair colour sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce, with repeat buying and early traction, after about six months in the portfolio.

risks_watch: Seasonal recovery depends on May-June temperatures and rainfall; a further weak season would hit the margin mix and FY27 growth.

rows.why: Boots.com (UK) listing for WeightWorld and MaxMedix and Amazon UAE for vitamins and supplements are live channel expansions, though management called the US and UAE early-stage bets.

531335|2026-06.headline: Zydus Wellness Q1 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million, while reported net profit fell 7%.

Reported net profit declined 7%, but profit excluding amortisation of acquired brands grew 26.5%. The domestic business grew 4.6%, with Skin & Hair Care up 34.5% and Food & Nutrition up 16%, while seasonal brands fell 12% due to unseasonal rains in the East and North. International (including Comfort Click) grew 24.8% like-to-like, and management said the summer weakness was recovering in the second half of the quarter.

capex_capacity: Comfort Click costs: an analyst cited about INR 80-85 crore a quarter of interest and depreciation, which management did not dispute.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no specific constraints; 25% is a good growth rate, but it will keep guiding to double-digit growth and does not give forward-looking numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ETR was near 27% (about 25% underlying, distorted by UK thin-cap disallowances). For FY27, 12-15 points of the 25% are cash; from FY28 it is expected to be fully cash.

qa_highlights.answer: The GBP loan was refinanced into a euro loan at a much lower rate; the finance cost run-rate should hold unless the euro benchmark moves materially.

qa_highlights.answer: East (continuous April-May rain) and North were the main drags. Glucon-D's gains in North, West and South were offset by East. Nycil was hit by North and East plus retailer stock. Growth recovered in the second half of the quarter but not enough to offset the full-quarter drag.

qa_highlights.question: Will Comfort Click be EBITDA-positive in the seasonally weak September and December quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Comfort Click has been EPS accretive since Q4 FY26 and expects net margin, EBITDA and PBT to rise if momentum continues. Comfort Click's US presence is 'very small' but growing well and is too early to judge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Complan's growth despite category degrowth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from the core kids segment (better nutrition, advertising, distribution), celebrity endorsement, toddler (NutriGro), adult nutrition (VieMax, VieMax Diabetes Care) and RTD entry (Complan Power Play). Kids nutrition is the core driver.

qa_highlights.question: What were A&P spends and digital mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported A&P was 18.2% of total sales, including Comfort Click, which spends heavily on advertising. Like-for-like core A&P was similar to last year. Digital's share of spend is rising.

531344|2026-03.headline: CONCOR posted record FY26 throughput of 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), but PAT fell 4.5% and Q4 domestic EBIT margin collapsed to 0.2%.
531344|2026-03.overview: FY26 handling hit a record 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), with EXIM at 8% and domestic at 14.6% growth, and rail freight margin rose to 27.16% from 25.65%. PAT declined 4.5% on weaker domestic traffic (gunny bags and Morbi tiles hit by West Asia-related supply disruptions) and tank container shortages. Q4 domestic segment EBIT margin fell to 0.2%, driven by higher empty running and a sharp rise in other expenses. Management guided FY27 handling growth of 9.5% (EXIM 8%, domestic 15%), kept EBITDA margin at 24-25%, and cited the DFC connection to JNPT from 1 June 2026 as a major driver.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 domestic segment EBIT margin
financial_highlights.change: Q4 domestic revenue down 4% YoY per analyst question; management did not dispute

financial_highlights.change: well above INR70-80 crore quarterly run-rate per CFO

segments.commentary: FY26 EXIM handling 4.21 million TEUs (record), growth 8%; market share fell to 53.9% from 55.2%. Lead distance dropped about 3 km, so revenue grew only about 2.5% against originating volume growth of about 4.5-5%.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 segment EBIT margin 0.2%, with revenue down about 4% YoY. Gunny bag (jute) and Morbi tile traffic collapsed, forcing empty container repositioning; Q4 domestic empty running rose 11.3% to INR76.76 crore. Market share fell to 55.9% from 57.6%.

segments.name: Rail and port share
segments.commentary: FY26 rail coefficient: JNPT 15.12% (CONCOR share 60%), Mundra 24.6% (share 35.4%), Pipavav 57.5% (share 48.3%). Overall market share 54.5% vs 55.9% last year.

EBITDA margin to be maintained at 24-25% in FY27 and beyond.

531431|2026-06.headline: Shakti Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37.9% YoY to INR859 crores, but EBITDA margin stayed near 9.6% on raw material and realisation pressure.

531508|2026-03.headline: Eveready FY26 revenue grew 8.2% and EBITDA margin held at 11.5%; Jammu alkaline plant (INR200 crore, 360 mn units peak) inaugurated 22 April 2026.
531508|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 8.2% and EBITDA grew 8.9%, with full-year EBITDA margin at 11.5% despite steep zinc cost increases in H2. Batteries grew 9.3%, flashlights 3% and lighting about 8.1%, with calibrated price hikes in carbon zinc and alkaline. The Jammu alkaline battery plant was inaugurated on 22 April 2026 and commercial production is expected within weeks. Management guided to holding margins near 11.5% in FY27, and debt was reduced by over INR100 crore in FY26 with further reduction targeted, helped by Noida leasehold sales.

financial_highlights.value: about INR116 crore (leasehold transfer completed 30 March 2026)
about INR136 crore (INR44 crore advance received)

segments.name: Batteries
segments.commentary: Grew 9.3% in FY26 and make up about two-thirds of business. Alkaline is nearly 10% of battery business (about 15% of category saliency per management) with volume growth over 20% CAGR; company alkaline share about 16%, up from under 10% a year ago.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Grew 3% in FY26 on a mature battery-operated base; rechargeables and new power bank and charger launches are the focus. BIS mandate fully implemented by end-January 2026 is seen favouring branded players.

segments.name: Lighting and electrical accessories
segments.commentary: Grew about 8.1% in FY26; management called the recent double-digit quarter-on-quarter growth sustainable. Flashlights and lighting with adjacencies make up about one-third of business.

segments.name: Mosquito racquets and mobile accessories
segments.commentary: Mosquito racquets, launched about 1.5 years ago, now hold a leadership position in urban markets; mobile accessories launched in FY26 via e-commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be held around the FY26 level of 11.5%, with headwinds stronger than last year.
Zinc prices expected to keep rising into subsequent quarters; a further price increase may be needed in Q2 if cost volatility persists.
Jammu plant: commercial production in a few weeks, more than 100 million units in year one, phased ramp-up; operational breakeven from year one per CFO, payback 5-6 years.
Alkaline saliency expected to reach 20-25% of batteries in about 3 years, with zinc at 75%; company aims to exit with about 20% alkaline share.
Debt reduction to continue in FY27; no capex planned beyond routine capex; Plot B2 proceeds of about INR90 crore expected in FY27.
Tax: company expects to transition to Section 115BAA (22%) from FY27, subject to utilisation of carried-forward business losses.
A&P spend to stay at about 10% of sales.
capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline battery plant: investment about INR200 crore, peak capacity 360 million alkaline batteries per year, phased ramp-up; inaugurated 22 April 2026 by the J&K Lieutenant Governor.
Jammu also has lines for zinc batteries, flashlights and lighting products, enabling backward and forward integration.

Noida plant: exited, with Plot B1 leasehold transfer completed 30 March 2026 and Plot B2 pending; Noida plant closure is part of the manufacturing realignment begun in Q2 FY26 (November board meeting).
Jammu incentive (GST-linked) not yet approved; company is awaiting approval.
Depreciation impact of Jammu capitalisation not quantified; company will share details offline.
demand_pricing: Rural demand resilient through FY26; urban demand improved in the latter part of the year in value and everyday categories, but discretionary spending remains selective.
Zinc costs rose steeply and sustainedly in H2 FY26; calibrated price increases taken in carbon zinc and alkaline batteries.
INR ranged INR83 to INR91+ in FY26 and has moved to about INR94-95 recently; the company hedged FX and secured zinc positioning ahead of the market.
Flashlight market about 70% unbranded and China-dependent; BIS compliance expected to raise costs for unorganised importers in H2 CY26.
Management said H1 revenue is typically a few percentage points better than H2.
Urban revival may be at risk if West Asia-related disruption persists beyond Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the business for INR94.5-95/USD and crude above $100, and what is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX hedging and zinc procurement positioning, plus pricing, delivered FY26. Management expects to hold margins around the 11.5% level in FY27, though headwinds are stronger than last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the alkaline plant cannibalise carbon zinc, and will carbon zinc prices be raised to narrow the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects alkaline at 20-25% and zinc at 75% of batteries in about 3 years, with some cannibalisation. The price gap in India is currently narrow, and further zinc price increases are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 tax rate 22%, and why was there no tax on the Noida land sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition to 115BAA in FY27 is confirmed, subject to carried-forward business losses. The Noida gain was set off against about INR500 crore of business losses from the write-off of old ICD provisions; MAT credit not yet used.

qa_highlights.question: Is commercial production at Jammu starting in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production has not started yet; it is expected in a few weeks and within the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target market share and export plan for Jammu?
qa_highlights.answer: Current alkaline share is about 16%, with a target of about 20% exit. Jammu output is for domestic sale for now, with white-label export possible later.

qa_highlights.question: Noida land sale proceeds versus the INR250 crore ballpark?
qa_highlights.answer: Plot B1 sold for about INR116 crore, with profit booked net of WDV and charges. Plot B2 is expected at about INR136 crore, with total about INR251 crore.

531508|2026-06.headline: Eveready Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR407.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 15.1% and PAT up 22.3%, driven by alkaline batteries and price actions.
531508|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR407.7 crore, up 9% YoY, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth. EBITDA was INR61.5 crore at a 15.1% margin and PAT was INR37 crore, up 22.3%. Management attributed margin protection to calibrated price increases and operational efficiencies, and stated there were no one-off gains. The Jammu alkaline plant began commercial production on 29 May 2026, while flashlights were soft on delayed monsoon and the lighting business reached breakeven.

segments.name: Batteries - Alkaline
segments.commentary: Key growth driver with close to 48% volume growth; premium alkaline market share reached 18%, with management targeting an exit share of 25-30% in two years. Alkaline is about 6-7% of company portfolio.

segments.name: Batteries - Carbon zinc
segments.commentary: Volume growth in line with industry (zinc market volumes roughly flat, -1% to +1%); company holds about 58% share of carbon zinc, described as broadly flattish. Legacy manufacturing costs reduced.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Revenue down 6.7% on delayed monsoon and lower conventional battery-operated volumes; rechargeable flashlights grew over 20%.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13.7%; pricing stabilising after 18-20 months of erosion; company says segment broke even in Q1, with emergency LED bulbs and electrical accessories growing.

segments.name: Electrical accessories / wires
segments.commentary: Insulation tapes growing; wires and MCBs started about 6 months ago, with plans to more than double sales in FY27. Wires are sourced, not manufactured.

guidance_outlook: Management expects roughly 10% gross margin uplift on alkaline products from Jammu plant once fully stabilised (after about one year); operating margin not guided.
Alkaline market share target of 25-30% exit share in two years.
Debt expected to turn positive/like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters.
Lighting expected to grow in Q2 and Q3 FY27, with cost softening uncertain.
Management said another round of price or margin corrections may be needed to manage zinc inflation.
Long-term plan and M&A strategy to be presented in 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline plant commenced commercial production on 29 May 2026; company describes it as the only alkaline battery plant in India.
Jammu plant plant and machinery investment about INR90-95 crore; total Jammu investment INR200 crore-plus, yet to yield results.
Pre-operating expenses of Jammu plant capitalised; expenses after 29 May charged to P&L.
Jammu GST/incentive approval (NCSS scheme, 3x eligible plant and machinery refund over 10 years) still pending formal approval.
Noida plant closed and sold; one plot executed, second expected to close shortly. CCI matter: next hearing around late September 2026.
Solar power installed at Jammu and other plants; company moving toward leasing/rental model for assets.
demand_pricing: Zinc prices around $3,500/ton versus below $3,000 for most of last year; electrolytic manganese dioxide, electrodes, acetylene black and lighting components also inflated.
Alkaline market about INR550 crore (within a battery market of about INR4,100 crore at MRP); alkaline volume growth +19% to +23% over last 7-8 quarters, versus zinc flat.
Alkaline share of dry cell about 13-15%; Duracell is the largest alkaline competitor, Panasonic and Nippo are close followers in zinc.
Digital channels (quick commerce, e-commerce) showed strong growth.
Employee cost up only 2-3% YoY, reflecting the Noida closure.
Management flagged no immediate cannibalisation of zinc by alkaline; may emerge when alkaline exceeds about 20% of the battery market.

qa_highlights.question: Share gains in dry cell (58%) and whether Amazon Basics entry or BIS/EPR compliance is a risk.
qa_highlights.answer: 58% share refers to carbon zinc only. BIS on flashlights is on paper complete, with compliance to be driven across unbranded players over 2-3 quarters. EPR pricing and compliance are under discussion with MoEFCC and the Pollution Control Board, and no cost estimate was given.

qa_highlights.question: What operating margin will Jammu alkaline deliver versus imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 10% gross margin uplift on the product once stabilised, not operating margin. Alkaline is 6-7% of revenue, so the impact is modest for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an one-off in the margin, and how is zinc hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; margin came from calibrated price actions. Zinc is monitored weekly and further price or margin corrections may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Consultancy fees to a director and timing of the GST subsidy.
qa_highlights.answer: NRC and Board approved a whole-time director's compensation; quantum not disclosed. GST incentive has no formal approval yet, with discussions advancing.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company be debt free and what is the Jammu fixed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt around INR165 crore; company expects to be like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters. Jammu costs are absorbed into product cost, not separately disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Size of CCI matter and potential cash outgo.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cannot estimate the outcome; next hearing is in late September.

risks_watch: Zinc and commodity inflation; possible further price hikes could affect volumes.
Unresolved EPR compliance cost and pricing framework.
CCI matter with a potential INR150 crore outgo flagged by an analyst; management could not estimate it.
Pending GST incentive approval for Jammu.
Monsoon-dependent flashlight demand and structural decline in conventional flashlights.
Lighting margins at breakeven and dependent on price stability.
Emerging cannibalisation of carbon zinc by alkaline once alkaline crosses about 20% of the market.

531548|2026-03.headline: Somany Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin rose to 11.4% and FY26 to 9.3%; management guides at least 150 bps more margin improvement in FY27 despite gas-price shock.
531548|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales grew about 6% and FY26 about 5%, with EBITDA margin up in both periods (11.4% in Q4, 9.3% for FY26). Capacity utilisation was broadly flat at about 79% for the year, rising to 82% in Q4, and Somany Max reached near breakeven versus a loss of about INR 9 crore in Q4 FY25. Gas prices jumped from about 9 March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation, and Morbi capacity was disrupted, which management sees as a share-gain opportunity for organised players. Working capital improved sharply, with receivable days at 40 (from 51) and working capital lower by 4 days to 9 days. Management passed through about 16-17% tile price hikes and about 8% bathware and sanitaryware hikes, and said input cost increases are being fully recovered in retail but only about 85-90% in projects.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: GVT volumes up 3% while ceramic and PVT volumes fell 3%; average tile price increase of about 16-17% since March 2026. Company-wide utilisation around 79% for the year.

segments.name: Sanitaryware and bathware
segments.commentary: Sanitaryware grew 8% in FY26 to INR 320 crore; management targets double-digit growth in FY27. Bathware price hike of about 18% taken in February on brass costs, and a blended 8% hike in April. Only 25% of dealers currently stock sanitaryware.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Management expects healthy double-digit volume growth in FY27 for sanitaryware and adhesives combined; no separate adhesive figures were given.

segments.name: Outsourced / JV production
segments.commentary: Outsourced sales about 35-36% of volume after Acer and Amora moved from JV to outsourced status (about 30% excluding those). Total FY26 sales volume about 72 million sq m; capacity about 75 million sq m.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by at least 150 bps from the 9.3% FY26 base, to about 10.5-11% or better; management reiterated 10.8% or better when asked.
FY27 volume growth guided to decent single digits for tiles and double digits for sanitaryware and adhesives.
FY27 revenue growth of about 20-25% if current prices hold, per management, which would be driven by about 15% price hikes plus high single-digit volume growth; value outcome depends on gas prices.
Brand spend to rise slightly in absolute terms, while staying around 2% of sales as a percentage.
Capex limited to about INR 70-80 crore of routine capex and balancing equipment, mainly for the vintage plant and to add value at bathware plant.
South plant to move to a long-term gas contract from next month, expected to cut gas cost by at least INR 17-18 per SCM versus the current INR 78.
capex_capacity: Current gas price in Morbi is about INR 74 per SCM plus 6% (about INR 78) for May, sourced from GSPC; North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper.
Morbi restarting after gas supply from 1 May: about 60-65% of Morbi running in mid-May, with management expecting about 85% by month-end; labour shortage is the constraint.
Company plants running at about 100% of operating capacity across India, excluding a couple of kilns shut for product-mix reasons.
INR 30 crore invested in a new press at Somany Max to improve utilisation.
Vintage plant balancing equipment being added to turn it profitable; bathware capacity being augmented.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand improved in January and February with single-digit growth; March was disrupted as exports stalled. Industry exports were about INR 17,000+ crore versus about INR 18,000 crore potential.
April was a slow but growing month: Morbi supply shortfall, higher prices (company about 15-17%, Morbi about 30-35%), and dealer destocking caused slower volumes.
Gas cost increase is about INR 5.5-6 per sq ft; other input costs (transport, labour, packaging) add about INR 1-1.5 per sq ft; total cost pressure about INR 6.5-7 per sq ft.
Management says the price hike covers the full cost in retail, while about 15% of business (projects) recovers about 85-90%.
Sanitaryware and bathware blended price hike of about 8% in April 2026.
Stock levels at Q4 end reduced by about 2.5 million sq m (about 15 days) over the year; old stock over 180 days cleared in March.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are the receivable days and negative working capital, and what is the outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects receivable days to stay near current levels, possibly up 1-2 days. Working capital gains came from lower outsourced-vendor stock and clearance of old stock in March. Sustainability is uncertain given the delayed response to price hikes in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a tipping point where gas costs make running plants unviable?
qa_highlights.answer: Tile prices are about 15-20% below two years ago and current hikes bring prices back to historic levels. Management does not see plant shutdown even with a further 10-15% rise, excluding a severe oil shock (about USD 200/bbl).

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only about 2% in Q4 versus double digits for peers, and realisation lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume was focused on non-JV and outsourced material to clear inventory before April price increases. It said realisation was up INR 6 per sq m YoY, with the mix shifting toward cheaper outsourced product.

qa_highlights.question: Gas price differential between Morbi and North, and South plant pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi is about INR 74 plus 6% (about INR 78) per SCM for May; the North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper. South is INR 78 per SCM currently, but a long-term contract from next month should cut it by at least INR 17-18.

qa_highlights.question: Is the share buyback possible given the market leader's INR 300 crore buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for the next 6-8 months, due to an SEBI embargo tied to consolidation of wholly owned subsidiaries. Promoters bought shares before the trading window closed.

qa_highlights.question: Will Morbi's recovery affect outsourced volumes and FY27 supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outsourced OEM plants for large organised players should keep running. Four or five supplier plants had short-term material gaps in April, expected to normalise in May. Full material availability is expected by June.

risks_watch: Gas prices and any further geopolitical escalation; management said price cuts would follow if gas prices fall.
Morbi restart pace (85% target by end-May) and labour availability; a 10-15% Morbi capacity may not restart.
Demand response to 15-17% tile price hikes; management expects pent-up demand but April was slow.
Transport and fuel costs, which had not yet been quantified after diesel and petrol price hikes.
Sustainability of working capital release and debtor days, and the 4-day rise in receivables risk.
Somany Max path to positive EBITDA in FY27, and Acer and Amora now sitting in the outsourced bucket.

Answers on gas pricing and April volumes were less precise and some figures were corrected or restated during Q&A.

So we are to gain from this disruption because a lot of the capacity in Morbi shut down, and everybody is now buying from the same source of gas.
Tile still being the most cheapest material for the flooring and wall, like I mentioned, there is no alternative to a tile.

531548|2026-06.headline: Somany Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin up 3.6 pts YoY to 11.6% on standalone utilisation of 83% (vs 72%), with volume growth only ~3%.

Sales grew about 3% while value grew about 24%, with a few percent of sales lost in April when Morbi supply was shut for roughly 1.5 months. Price hikes of about 16-17% were passed through to the market, and gas costs rose 16-18% in the current period. Management guided to single-digit to mid-single-digit volume growth, maintained margins of 11%+, and announced a 9-plus million sq m South plant (about INR220 crore capex) due around end-Q3 FY28.

531569|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell YoY as March 2026 exports stalled on Middle East disruption; consolidated revenue INR 132.1 mn, EBITDA margin 15.74%.
531569|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined year-on-year because exports could not be executed in March 2026 after Iran-related conflict disrupted Middle East shipping and logistics. Input costs also rose in March, compressing gross margins. Consolidated revenue was INR 132.1 mn with EBITDA of INR 21.73 mn (15.74% margin) and PAT of INR 5.5 mn (3.97% margin). Management says alternative routes via Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Southeast Asia have restarted shipments and expects a broader export recovery in Q1 FY27. The Pune IV facility, commercial since December 2025, contributed INR 2.7 mn in Q4 versus INR 1.2 mn in Q3.

Asset quality improved, with consolidated gross Stage 3 at 0.9% (down 61 bps QoQ) and net Stage 3 at 0.5%. Management reiterated FY28 targets of INR55,000 crore AUM (revised FY28 AUM guidance cited as INR57,000 crore in Q&A, with FY27 at INR46,000 crore), ROA 4-4.5% and ROE 16-18%.

531768|2026-03.headline: Poly Medicure Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 21% YoY to INR534 crore; FY27 consolidated guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore with margin pressure from raw-material costs.
531768|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR443 crore (up 5.2% YoY, a record quarter) with standalone EBITDA margin of 27.3%, and consolidated revenue was INR534 crore (up about 21% YoY) with consolidated EBITDA of INR112 crore. FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12.3% to INR1,875 crore, while standalone grew about 4% to INR1,662 crore and standalone EBITDA margin came in at 26.8%. Management flagged a raw-material cost increase of about 20% linked to crude, plus freight and wage pressure, and said gross margin could fall to roughly 66% (200-300 bps lower) on current conditions. FY27 guidance calls for consolidated revenue of INR2,300-2,400 crore and standalone of INR1,900-1,950 crore, with capex of INR200-225 crore.

segments.name: Standalone business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,662 crore (up about 4%) with 60-70% export-driven; Q4 standalone revenue INR443 crore. Standalone gross margin 68.1% for FY26.

segments.name: Infusion Therapy
segments.commentary: Share of Q4 FY26 revenue fell to 50% from 57% a year earlier; management says it will stay around 50% as the core business, with IV catheter global market share of about 11%.

segments.name: Renal
segments.commentary: About 450 dialysis machines placed in FY26, taking installed base to about 1,000; Renal is about 11% of revenue and Q4 Renal revenue grew about 25% QoQ per an analyst. FY27 Renal growth target is over 20%, versus earlier 30-35%.

segments.name: Cardiology and critical care
segments.commentary: About 11,000 stents deployed in FY26. Stent business is only about INR10-12 crore of revenue; focus is on drug-eluting balloons and other higher-value devices. Management did not disclose cardio and onco revenue.

segments.name: Acquired subsidiaries (Citieffe and PendraCare)
segments.commentary: Combined FY25 revenue about EUR25.5 million (Citieffe about EUR17.5 million, PendraCare about EUR8 million). Citieffe FY27 growth guided at 10-12% in EUR; PendraCare guidance restricted due to Middle East exposure. Steady-state EBITDA margin expected mid-teens, rising to 18-20% over 2-3 years.

segments.name: Brazil (Medyneo acquisition)
segments.commentary: Small acquisition of a company with ANVISA and import licences, about USD40,000 cash outlay; saves an estimated 18-24 months of approval time. The company has no current operations.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore (vs INR1,875 crore in FY26), including full-year consolidation of PendraCare and Citieffe.
FY27 standalone revenue guidance INR1,900-1,950 crore: domestic growth above 20% and international growth above 15%.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guidance 25-27%; consolidated EBITDA margin guidance 23-25% because subsidiaries run at lower margins.
Gross margin may erode from about 68% toward about 66% (200-300 bps lower) on current crude and freight conditions; management expects this to ease if crude softens and cost-saving projects deliver.
FY27 capex guidance INR200-225 crore, lower than FY26 INR296 crore.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR296 crore across Haridwar, Faridabad, Mitrol and YEIDA Medical Park; FY27 capex guided at INR200-225 crore with more spend on automation to offset wage increases.
Gamma plant established this year and now fully operational, contributing savings.
Capacity utilisation after QIP-1 capacity expansion is about 65-70%.
Renal installed base about 1,000 dialysis machines after about 450 placements in FY26; management expects about 20% sequential growth in machine sales in FY27.
Clinical registry for a 2,000-patient study: over 650 enrolled; full enrolment targeted by end of FY27 across India and abroad.
demand_pricing: Standalone price increases of 3-5% already taken with customers to offset freight and wage costs.
Raw material costs up about 20% in aggregate (crude-linked, including plastic packaging); raw materials are about 32-33% of revenue. Inventory of 2.5-3 months cushioned Q4 impact.
West Asia disruption: about 6-8% of revenue from the region; demand described as intact, but shipments are delayed by logistics bottlenecks.

Europe: management says demand has recovered over the last 3-4 months after over-inventory and slowdown; distributors added in Northern Europe, UK and Germany. Management targets about 15% growth in Europe.
US: business is recovering after a tariff-related setback that delayed launches by about a year; some new FDA-approved products are in the pipeline.

Chinese dumping in renal and other segments continues; the company is seeking government action (counter-duties and ASEAN duty-free imports). Management says 20-25% growth is still attainable in renal.
Export receivables rose because the company extended better credit terms to international customers to support volumes; management expects receivable cycle similar in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Brazil acquisition's category, revenue and cost, and what is the EU vs RoW split of PendraCare and Citieffe?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil target is a small, non-operating medical-device storage and distribution company acquired for about USD40,000, saving 18-24 months. Citieffe and PendraCare are each about 50% Europe and 50% RoW; Citieffe also has about 35-40% in North America and Mexico.

qa_highlights.question: Is the renal segment facing Chinese or domestic competition, and what growth is targeted for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition is from imports, not domestic players. Renal growth target for FY27 is about 20%, versus an earlier 30-35%, because of Chinese competition and cost inversion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone inventory and receivables rise sharply, and will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone inventory rose about INR30 crore, with finished goods around INR30-35 crore (5-6 days). Receivable days rose from 68 to 86 mainly because of international customers, and management expects a similar cycle in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin dip QoQ despite growth in higher-margin products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q4 dip to product mix, with some lower-margin products in the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time INR9 crore cost and what was the acquired businesses' EBITDA impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR9 crore was transaction-related adviser costs and regulatory and employee provisions booked at year-end at international entities; no manpower rationalisation. The acquired entities had a negative EBITDA impact of about INR2.6 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable organic growth rate and the long-term revenue mix target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FY27 guidance of over 25% consolidated growth and 15-16% standalone growth. Long-term target is about one-third India and two-thirds RoW.

risks_watch: Raw-material inflation (about 20%) and possible standalone gross margin erosion to about 66% if crude stays at $100-110; management will review at end of Q1 FY27.
West Asia disruption affecting about 6-8% of revenue and shipping, with pending orders not yet executed.
Export receivable days (86) and inventory days (58) elevated; management expects no near-term normalisation.
Chinese import dumping in renal and other segments; Government response (counter-duties, ASEAN duty-free imports) is pending.
Acquired-entity integration: PendraCare exposed to the Middle East; Citieffe lost a Latam tender in CY25; consolidated EBITDA guided lower than standalone.
Brazil entry and US product launches depend on regulatory approvals; import registrations take 6-9 months.
key_quotes: So on the current situation based on where we are today as on today, we may see some erosion on gross margin going from, let's say, 68% to maybe around 66% or maybe in that region, maybe lower by 200 bps, 300 bps.
I can say that absolutely for the moment, yes, but we don't know what can happen tomorrow. That is my worry.
I think we have to see that last year was more or less for us also a lot of transition year because there was a lot of focus on high technology, building new technology products.
Export, in fact, were negative, not flattish also. We were, I think, minus 3% or 4% on the export side.
531768|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand recovery in Europe, US and India, and on FY27 guidance, while cautious on raw-material and crude-linked margin risk, West Asia logistics and Chinese dumping in renal. Management repeatedly hedged margin outlook as "very fluid" and dependent on crude softening.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided to erode from about 68% to about 66% (200-300 bps) on crude-linked raw material costs up about 20%, and consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 23-25% because subsidiaries run at lower margins; standalone EBITDA guide 25-27% vs FY26 26.8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gamma plant is already fully operational, and FY26 capex of INR296 crore went into Haridwar, Faridabad, Mitrol and YEIDA; but utilisation is only 65-70% after QIP-1, so no major new capacity is firmly dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone FY27 revenue guided at INR1,900-1,950 crore vs INR1,662 crore in FY26 (about 14-17%), with domestic growth above 20% and international above 15%; consolidated guide INR2,300-2,400 crore vs INR1,875 crore, helped by full-year acquisitions; Renal FY27 growth target cut to over 20% from 30-35%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR200-225 crore, lower than FY26's INR296 crore, with utilisation at 65-70% giving headroom, so no new capex wave is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious that margin outlook is 'very fluid' and will review at end of Q1 FY27 with crude at $100-110; the guide was just set with gross margin cut risk, so a raise looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin could fall to about 66% if crude stays at $100-110, West Asia (6-8% of revenue) shipments are delayed, and Chinese renal dumping persists; management will review at end of Q1 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Some new FDA-approved products are in the US pipeline and drug-eluting balloons are a focus, but timing depends on approvals and import registrations that take 6-9 months, and no firm launch dates were given.

rows.label: Europe recovery and distributor additions
rows.why: Demand has recovered over the last 3-4 months with distributors added in Northern Europe, UK and Germany, and management targets about 15% European growth.

rows.label: Standalone price increases of 3-5%
rows.why: Price increases of 3-5% are already taken with customers to offset freight and wage costs, which partly cushions the 20% raw-material inflation.

rows.label: Receivable and inventory days elevated
rows.why: Receivable days rose from 68 to 86 and inventory days from 50 to 58, and management expects no near-term normalisation of the export receivable cycle.

tone.note: Management was confident on Europe, US and India demand recovery and FY27 revenue guidance, but cautious on crude-linked raw-material margin erosion, West Asia logistics, Chinese renal dumping and receivable days; analysts pressed on margins, renal growth cut and working capital.
